articles.title: Metabolic phenotypes and female reproductive impairment: cross-sectional associations with infertility and impaired fecundity.
articles.journal: Gynecological endocrinology : the official journal of the International Society of Gynecological Endocrinology
articles.authors: Hu X, Zhang Y, Wu J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The joint role of adiposity and metabolic dysfunction in female reproductive impairment remains uncertain. We examined cross-sectional associations of metabolic phenotypes with infertility and impaired fecundity in women of reproductive age.
METHODS: We analyzed 4,862 women from pooled 2011-2019 survey data. Normal weight was defined as BMI 18.5-24.9 kg/m2 and overweight/obesity as BMI ≥ 25 kg/m2. Metabolic unhealth was defined by the presence of at least one of three survey indicators: hypertension, diabetes/prediabetes, or dyslipidemia. Survey-weighted logistic regression, sensitivity analyzes, subgroup interaction tests, and restricted cubic spline models were used.
RESULTS: Among 4,862 women, 575 (11.8%) met the infertility outcome and 774 (15.9%) met the impaired-fecundity outcome. Relative to metabolically healthy normal weight (MHNW), fully adjusted odds ratios for infertility were 1.28 (95% CI 1.04-1.58) for MUNW, 1.32 (1.00-1.75) for MHO, and 1.43 (1.16-1.76) for MUO. For impaired fecundity, the corresponding estimates were 1.24 (0.95-1.60), 1.28 (1.00-1.65), and 1.40 (1.13-1.74). Exploratory subgroup analyzes did not support a robust age-specific interaction after multiplicity control, and spline analyzes provided mixed evidence for continuous adiposity measures.
CONCLUSIONS: The metabolically unhealthy overweight/obesity phenotype showed the most consistent association with infertility and impaired fecundity. These cross-sectional findings support an association between combined adiposity and metabolic abnormalities and reproductive impairment, but they do not establish causality and require confirmation in prospective studies.

articles.title: Guidance documents for the conduct of vaccine clinical trials in pregnant and lactating women: A tool from the CEPI-SPEAC-Brighton Collaboration project.
articles.authors: Munoz FM, Lindgren AL, Sevene E et al.
articles.abstract: As infectious diseases continue to pose risks globally, the inclusion of pregnant and lactating women in vaccine clinical trials is crucial to ensure that mothers and newborns have the option to benefit from potentially life-saving vaccinations. Pregnant and lactating women face unique risks from some infectious diseases and the potential benefits of vaccinating them during pregnancy or lactation can extend to newborns through the transfer of maternal antibodies. Vaccination during lactation raises a distinct set of scientific questions, including transfer of vaccine components and of antigen-specific antibody into milk, the isotype and functional profile of that antibody, and its contribution to infant mucosal protection. Conducting vaccine clinical trials in these populations requires careful attention to regulatory and ethical considerations, study design, data collection and analysis, safety monitoring, and the assessment of efficacy and effectiveness throughout the life cycle of the vaccine. Unique challenges exist, such as distinguishing vaccine-associated adverse events from background pregnancy- and obstetric-related events, fear of harming the fetus, and addressing real and perceived risks to mitigate study recruitment hesitancy and ensure the safety of participants and their unborn infants and the success of the clinical trial. With the exception of first-trimester studies, substantial progress has been made over the last three decades to ensure pregnant and lactating women are included in vaccine studies. Collaboration with experts in vaccine research and ethics, obstetric and maternal-fetal medicine specialists, pediatricians, neonatologists, and other pertinent experts is essential to ensure these studies are properly and successfully conducted. This document compiles published global guidelines and relevant literature concerning the conduct of interventional or observational vaccine studies in pregnant and lactating women.

articles.title: Pregnancy and Childbirth for Asian American Adoptees: Navigating Relationships With Adoptive Mothers Impacted by Infertility.
articles.authors: Hayashi Y, Donnelly EY, Hexter LJ et al.
articles.abstract: With over 200,000 international adoptees of Asian descent in the United States, many of whom are now adults, there remains a significant gap in understanding how they navigate critical life transitions such as pregnancy and childbirth. This research explores, from the perspective of Asian American adoptees, how their relationships with their adoptive mothers are impacted during this transformative period. Drawing from a subsample of 28 participants from a larger study exploring Asian American adoptees' experiences of pregnancy and childbirth, researchers utilized thematic analysis of interviews to identify main themes. Three key themes emerged: adoptees' (1) (dis)connection with their adoptive mothers; (2) hypervigilance and protectiveness of their adoptive mothers' feelings; and (3) desire to give their child what their adoptive mother could not. These findings highlight the intricate dynamics of adoptive identities and family relationships during pregnancy, underscoring the need for more attention to adult adoptee voices in both research and clinical practice. Finally, this study offers crucial insights for practitioners working with adoptees and adoptive families, emphasizing the need to address the emotional and relational intersections of adoption, infertility, grief, and loss.

articles.title: Indoor air pollution and health outcomes in women in developing Asian countries: a systematic review.
articles.authors: Rahmadina F, Pratiningsih WA, Fitriani D
articles.abstract: Indoor air pollution (IAP), primarily from the combustion of solid fuels like wood and charcoal, is a critical public health challenge. This exposure disproportionately affects women in developing countries due to their traditional domestic roles. However, a comprehensive synthesis of the wide-ranging health outcomes specifically for women in developing Asia remains limited. Therefore, the main objective of this review is to summarize the available evidence on the association between IAP exposure and various health outcomes in this vulnerable population. For this, a systematic review was conducted following the PRISMA guidelines. A search in Cochrane Library, PubMed, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and Scopus was performed. The methodological quality and risk of bias of included studies were verified through the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS), AXIS tool, and the OHAT framework. All selection and data extraction processes were carried out independently by two reviewers. Strong and consistent evidence was found across the 28 included studies. IAP exposure was significantly associated with multi-systemic health damage, including increased respiratory symptoms (aOR=3.0), decreased lung function, and adverse reproductive outcomes such as a higher risk of birth defects (aOR up to 7.09) and stillbirth (aOR=1.34). Furthermore, exposure was linked to increased cardio-metabolic disease risk, genotoxicity, and significant cognitive decline. Thus, future policies and interventions are urgently needed to mitigate this preventable burden of disease.

articles.title: Feasibility of Intraoperative Indocyanine Green Fluorescence Angiography for Perfusion Assessment in Pediatric Adnexal Mass-Associated Torsion.
articles.authors: Liu S, Ren Q, Yang S et al.
articles.abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility of intraoperative indocyanine green (ICG) fluorescence angiography for perfusion assessment in children with adnexal mass-associated torsion and to explore its potential clinical value using a historical comparison cohort.
DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study with a historical comparison cohort.
SETTING: A single tertiary pediatric surgical center.
PARTICIPANTS: Thirty-eight children who underwent surgery with intraoperative ICG fluorescence angiography for adnexal mass-associated torsion between January 2022 and September 2024 were retrospectively compared with a historical cohort of 58 children treated without ICG between January 2020 and January 2022.
INTERVENTIONS: Serial ICG fluorescence angiography was performed before detorsion and after lesion enucleation with adnexal reconstruction. Qualitative perfusion patterns, signal-to-background ratio (SBR), postoperative ultrasound findings, and propensity score-matched clinical outcomes were evaluated.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: All 38 patients successfully underwent intraoperative ICG fluorescence angiography, with no ICG-related adverse events observed. Qualitative perfusion patterns changed from Type A/B/C in 3/16/19 patients before detorsion to 13/17/8 after adnexal reconstruction. The median signal-to-background ratio (SBR) increased from 0.841 (interquartile range [IQR], 0.569-0.979) before detorsion to 0.920 (IQR, 0.696-1.046) after reconstruction (P = .038). Among 16 patients with absent preoperative Doppler flow on the torsed side, 12 demonstrated Type A or B perfusion after reconstruction. Among the 36 patients with at least 3 months of postoperative ultrasound follow-up, 33 (91.7%) had a Good outcome, 2 (5.6%) had an Intermediate outcome, and 1 (2.8%) had a Poor outcome. Given the small numbers of Intermediate and Poor outcomes, associations between intraoperative ICG findings and postoperative ultrasound outcomes were evaluated descriptively. After 1:1 propensity score matching of patients with at least 3 months of postoperative ultrasound…
CONCLUSION: Intraoperative ICG fluorescence angiography is a feasible adjunct for real-time perfusion assessment during organ-preserving surgery in children with adnexal mass-associated torsion. It provides additional information on tissue perfusion that may support intraoperative organ-preserving decision-making. Further prospective multicenter studies are warranted to establish its role in clinical practice.

articles.title: Patient-centered perioperative pain management in hysterectomy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Micussi M, Gabriel I, Platte R et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate evidence-based perioperative pain management strategies and their effects on postoperative pain during the first 24 hours after hysterectomy.
DATA SOURCES: A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library to identify studies published in English up to April 2025. The review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA recommendations, with its protocol registered in the Open Science Framework.
METHODS OF STUDY SELECTION: Eligible studies comprised randomized controlled trials investigating perioperative analgesic interventions in women undergoing hysterectomy, with postoperative pain intensity assessed using the Visual Analog Scale or Numeric Rating Scale. A total of 32 studies fulfilled the eligibility criteria for qualitative synthesis, of which 25 contributed data to the meta-analysis.
TABULATION, INTEGRATION, AND RESULTS: Data on patient characteristics, surgical approach, analgesic interventions, and pain outcomes were extracted. Mean differences (MD) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated using random-effects models. Muscle plane blocks using ropivacaine (MD = -2.37; 95% CI, -3.34 to -1.40), pelvic floor infiltration with ropivacaine or bupivacaine (MD = -1.36; 95% CI, -2.14 to -0.59), and intravenous lidocaine combined with dexmedetomidine (MD = -1.78; 95% CI, -2.35 to -1.22) demonstrated significant improvements in early pain scores. However, no significant differences were observed at 24 hours.
CONCLUSION: Perioperative analgesic strategies may reduce early postoperative pain after hysterectomy, although consistent benefits were not demonstrated at 24 hours. High-quality studies are warranted to establish standardized multimodal protocols and assess longer-term pain outcomes.

articles.title: NEOADJUVANT BRACHYTHERAPY AND CONCURRENT CHEMORADIOTHERAPY IN CERVICAL CANCER- A REVIEW FROM THE FRENCH CERVICAL CANCER GUIDELINES GROUP.
articles.journal: Journal of gynecology obstetrics and human reproduction
articles.authors: Cordoba A, Kerbage Y, Carcopino X et al.
articles.abstract: Cervical cancer remains a major global health challenge, particularly when diagnosed at a locally advanced stage. This narrative review examines the respective roles of neoadjuvant brachytherapy (NBT), concurrent CRT, and image-guided adaptive brachytherapy (IGABT), together with recent advances in systemic treatment. For locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC), concurrent CISPLATIN-based CRT followed by IGABT remains the standard of care. IGABT enables dose escalation to the primary tumour while limiting exposure of adjacent organs at risk and cannot be adequately replaced by external-beam boost techniques. NBT may be considered for selected patients with node-negative, early-stage disease when treatment de-escalation is appropriate. Although retrospective studies suggest that NBT can facilitate less radical surgery and reduce the need for postoperative radiotherapy, it has not demonstrated a survival advantage over standard treatments. Systemic intensification is reshaping LACC management: the INTERLACE trial demonstrated improved survival with short-course induction chemotherapy before CRT, while KEYNOTE-A18 established PEMBROLIZUMAB administered concurrently with CRT and continued as maintenance therapy as a new option for high-risk disease. Conversely, OUTBACK and CALLA did not support routine adjuvant chemotherapy or DURVALUMAB-based treatment. Optimal outcomes depend on careful patient selection, timely treatment completion, access to high-quality IGABT and interstitial techniques, and multidisciplinary expertise. Expanding access to prevention and evidence-based treatment remains essential to reducing global disparities in cervical cancer outcomes.

articles.title: Platelet-neutrophil immunothrombosis in obstetric antiphospholipid syndrome and non-APS pregnancy morbidity during low-molecular-weight heparin-based prophylaxis.
articles.authors: Manfredi AA, Canti V, Castiglioni MT et al.
articles.abstract: We prospectively studied 21 women receiving low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) for APS or non-APS pregnancy morbidity and 21 healthy pregnant controls. Ten women were reassessed two years after LMWH discontinuation. Reference groups comprised 21 age-matched healthy non-pregnant women and five non-pregnant patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Blood was collected at 10-12, 20-22 and 30-34 weeks of gestation. Platelet and neutrophil activation, platelet-neutrophil aggregates and myeloperoxidase (MPO)-DNA complexes were quantified. Longitudinal biomarkers were analysed using participant-level mixed-effects models including study group, gestational stage and their interaction. LMWH effects were examined in vitro, and ex vivo NET generation was assessed in neutrophils from treated high-risk and untreated healthy pregnancies. Healthy pregnancy was associated with increased platelet P-selectin expression and MPO-DNA complexes, without broad neutrophil activation. Women reassessed off LMWH showed substantially higher platelet HMGB1, platelet-neutrophil aggregates, neutrophil tissue factor expression and MPO-DNA complexes than non-pregnant controls, with exploratory within-participant analyses supporting increases from pregnancy to postpartum. During LMWH treatment, most markers fell within the distributions observed in healthy pregnancy. Mixed-effects models provided no multiplicity-adjusted evidence of differences in gestational trajectories between healthy and treated pregnancies. In vitro, LMWH attenuated platelet activation and platelet-driven neutrophil responses, while neutrophils from LMWH-treated patients showed reduced ex vivo responsiveness. All index pregnancies resulted in live births. These findings indicate that platelet activation characterises healthy pregnancy. During LMWH treatment, most markers of platelet-neutrophil activation show distributions close to those observed in healthy pregnancy.Top of Form.

articles.title: Spatial Immunometabolic Context of Tertiary Lymphoid Structures in Ovarian Cancer: Evidence, Hypotheses, and Pharmacological Considerations.
articles.authors: Wang Y, Wang P, Wang X et al.
articles.abstract: Ovarian cancer, particularly high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC), is characterized by marked spatial heterogeneity and limited benefit from immune-checkpoint inhibitor monotherapy. Tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS) are organized lymphoid niches associated with immune-active tumor states, but their biological and clinical implications depend on maturation, anatomical site, cellular composition, and treatment context. This review evaluates how spatial metabolic conditions may be associated with TLS organization and B-cell function in ovarian cancer. To prevent overinterpretation, the evidence is classified into four levels: direct evidence from ovarian-cancer TLS, indirect evidence from ovarian-cancer immune or metabolic studies, evidence from other tumors or lymphoid systems, and author-generated hypotheses requiring validation. We distinguish TLS morphology from germinal-center activity, somatic hypermutation (SHM), class-switch recombination (CSR), B-cell receptor (BCR) clonality, antibody affinity, antigen specificity, and effector function. We further discuss the context-dependent roles of lactate transport and hypoxia, including evidence that physiological germinal-center hypoxia and MCT1-dependent pyruvate metabolism can support selected B-cell functions. Spatial metabolomics and imaging mass cytometry may help test these relationships, but they do not by themselves establish causality or therapeutic predictiveness. Accordingly, pharmacological strategies are presented as mechanistically relevant candidates rather than validated TLS-directed treatments.

articles.title: Physical Intimate Partner Violence Before and During Pregnancy and Adverse Birth Outcomes Using PRAMS 2016-2020 Data.
articles.authors: Eapen DJ, Matthews K, Manikonda L et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe the prevalence of physical intimate partner violence (IPV) in the 12 months before and during pregnancy and its association with adverse birth outcomes using 2016-2020 Pregnancy Risk Assessment Monitoring System (PRAMS) data.
DESIGN: Secondary analysis of PRAMS data.
SETTING: PRAMS Phase 8 surveillance data were collected by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention from 2016 to 2020 across multiple states.
PARTICIPANTS: Annual sample sizes per state range from about 1,000 to 3,000 women.
METHODS: Analysis of deidentified PRAMS Phase 8 data and weighted logistic regression to examine adjusted odds ratios (aOR) of each outcome.
RESULTS: The prevalence of physical IPV was 2.8% before pregnancy and 1.96% during pregnancy. Physical IPV, in both periods, was consistently associated with increased odds of adverse birth outcomes. Those who experienced physical IPV before pregnancy had increased odds of low birth weight (LBW; aOR = 1.3; 95% confidence interval [CI] [1.2, 1.5]), preterm birth (PTB; aOR = 1.2; 95% CI [1.1, 1.4]), and small for gestational age (SGA; aOR = 1.2; 95% CI [1.1, 1.4]). Similarly, those who experienced physical IPV during pregnancy had increased odds of LBW (aOR = 1.2; 95% CI [1.0, 1.3]), PTB (aOR = 1.2; 95% CI [1.0, 1.4]), and SGA (aOR = 1.2; 95% CI [1.0, 1.4]).
CONCLUSION: Physical IPV before and during pregnancy are distinct yet related exposures, each associated with increased odds of LBW, PTB, and SGA. These findings support the importance of identifying women experiencing IPV during the preconception and prenatal periods. Consistent with existing clinical recommendations, health care professionals should provide IPV screening and use a trauma-informed approach to care for women who are at risk for experiencing IPV. Preventing and reducing IPV among women has significant implications for improving maternal and fetal health. Providing access to comprehensive services that meet the physical, health care, emotional, social, legal, and economic needs of women and children is crucial.

articles.title: Trends and Risk Factors for Postpartum Readmission due to De Novo Endometritis: A National Historical Cohort Study.
articles.journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.authors: Noonan G, Wiley R, Katlaps I et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess national temporal trends and timing of 60-day postpartum readmission for de novo endometritis from 2010 to 2022, identify patient-, delivery- and hospital-level risk factors, and determine readmission risk following term caesarean delivery categorized by labouring status.
DESIGN: Retrospective historical cohort study.
SETTING: All-payer inpatient hospitalizations using the Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project Nationwide Readmissions Database (NRD) from 2010 to 2022.
POPULATION: An estimated 38.7 million delivery hospitalizations among individuals aged 15-54 years. Delivery admissions with diagnoses of sepsis/shock, chorioamnionitis, endometritis or peripartum hysterectomy were excluded to capture de novo readmissions, as were November and December deliveries due to incomplete 60-day follow-up.
METHODS: Joinpoint regression was utilized to assess temporal trends and calculate average annual percentage changes (AAPCs) across the study period and stratified by coding eras (ICD-9-CM vs. ICD-10-CM). Multivariable logistic regression models evaluated demographic, clinical, and hospital factors associated with 60-day readmission for de novo endometritis, adjusting for potential confounders. A secondary subgroup analysis among term caesarean deliveries (2016-2022) compared labouring caesarean delivery (CD-L) to non-labouring caesarean delivery (CD-NL). Sensitivity analyses evaluated cases where endometritis was the first-listed readmission diagnosis.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: 60-day postpartum readmission with a diagnosis of de novo endometritis, and 60-day readmission with de novo endometritis as the primary (first-listed) diagnosis.
RESULTS: Between 2010 and 2022, 73 664 delivery hospitalizations (0.2%) were complicated by a 60-day readmission for de novo endometritis. Readmissions decreased from 23.8 to 14.1 per 10 000 deliveries (AAPC: -5.2%, 95% CI: -6.7% to -3.7%), with the sharpest decline occurring between 2014 and 2017 (AAPC: -12.8%, 95% CI: -16.0% to -8.1%). Most readmissions occurred rapidly, with…
CONCLUSIONS: Postpartum readmissions for de novo endometritis are uncommon, occur primarily within 10 days of hospital discharge, and have decreased substantially over the past decade. The risk is concentrated among patients experiencing substantial intrauterine manipulation, labouring caesarean delivery, haemorrhage, or operative interventions, highlighting key targets for risk-stratified surveillance and infection prevention strategies.

articles.title: Incidence and risk factors of preterm birth in women with polycystic ovary syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Wang L, Liu K, Wang G et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a highly heterogeneous syndrome. While it is established that PCOS increases preterm birth risk, it remains unclear which specific phenotype drives this risk. This study aimed to systematically evaluate the pooled incidence and identify risk factors for preterm birth in women with PCOS.
METHODS: A systematic search of nine databases was conducted from database inception to December 2025. Study quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS). Data were synthesised using a random-effects model to address heterogeneity.
RESULTS: A total of 79 studies involving 154,786 participants were included. According to the NOS, 63 included studies were rated as high quality and 16 as moderate quality. The pooled incidence of preterm birth in women with PCOS was 13.3 % (95 % CI 0.120, 0.145), which notably exceeds the estimated global average (∼10 %). Significant risk factors identified included advanced maternal age (OR 1.05, 95 % CI 1.00, 1.10), elevated fasting glucose (OR 1.54, 95 % CI 1.33, 1.79), higher total testosterone levels (OR 1.49, 95 % CI 1.25, 1.77), pre-pregnancy hyperandrogenism (OR 1.60, 95 % CI 1.23, 2.08), multiple gestation (OR 9.85, 95 % CI 6.52, 14.88), and conception via in vitro fertilization (OR 2.30, 95 % CI 1.32, 4.00).
CONCLUSIONS: Women with PCOS face a substantial risk of preterm birth, driven by a dual pathway of intrinsic metabolic/androgenic dysfunction and extrinsic factors like assisted reproductive technology. Routine screening for pre-pregnancy metabolic and androgenic profiles, coupled with strict adherence to single-embryo transfer policies during assisted reproductive technology, is imperative to mitigate preterm birth risks in this population.

articles.title: RNAi-mediated suppression of HPV16/18 E6 oncogene induces downregulation of HERV-K (Env and Np9) expression.
articles.authors: Soleimani-Jelodar R, Arashkia A, Shoja Z et al.
articles.abstract: Our recent study indicated increased expression levels of HERV-K Env, Np9, and Rec in cervical cancer. However, the relationship between the physical status of the viral genome or E6/E7 expression levels and HERV-K reactivation remains poorly defined. To address this gap, 95 HPV16- or 18-positive cervical samples were investigated in this study. The physical status of the viral genome and the expression levels of viral E6/E7 and HERV-K transcripts were measured using qRT-PCR. An RNA interference (RNAi) transfection system was also used to silence E6 expression in HPV-positive cell lines and assess subsequent changes in HERV-K transcripts. HERV-K Env and were significantly greater in the integrated group versus the mix-form group. A positive correlation was observed between Np9 expression and HPV16/18 E6. Correspondingly, after using RNAi molecules to silence E6 of HPV16/18, the expression levels of HERV-K Env and Np9 were substantially reduced in both CaSki and HeLa cells. In conclusion, the integrated HPV with persistent E6/E7 expression likely plays a role in HERV-K reactivation, implying that HERV-K may exacerbate HPV-driven pathogenesis. RNAi-mediated E6 suppression reduces HERV-K transcripts, suggesting potential intersecting molecular pathways between HPV and HERV-K in cervical cancer tumorigenesis. Further mechanistic studies are needed to assess whether targeting HERV-K or shared pathways could offer therapeutic benefits.

articles.journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.authors: Farren J, Jurkovic D, Memtsa M et al.
articles.abstract: Complications in early pregnancy include miscarriage, ectopic pregnancy (when the pregnancy develops in the wrong place, usually in the fallopian tube) and molar pregnancy (when the pregnancy develops abnormally). If women have pain or bleeding in early pregnancy, it can be a symptom of one of these complications, so they are usually offered an ultrasound scan. If the pregnancy cannot be seen on the scan (this is known as a pregnancy of unknown location or PUL), or the pregnancy is ectopic or molar, blood tests from the pregnant woman are taken to measure substances known as biomarkers. This can give more information about the status of pregnancy, and help plan any follow-up, or decide which treatment might be best. Common biomarkers already in daily use include human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG, the hormone tested in pregnancy tests) and progesterone. For women with PUL, measuring these hormones in blood tests can help determine whether further monitoring is needed and when it should take place. In ectopic pregnancy, these hormone levels can help show whether the pregnancy is continuing to grow or is resolving naturally, and whether surgery may be needed. hCG levels are also used to monitor women after a molar pregnancy and to determine whether further treatment is required. However, these biomarkers cannot be used on their own to diagnose an ectopic pregnancy or miscarriage, because hormone levels can sometimes look similar in healthy pregnancies. For this reason, they are used alongside other tests and clinical information. Many other biomarkers, such as PAPP-A, which is also used for screening in later pregnancy, have been found to be different in miscarriage or ectopic pregnancy compared with a normal pregnancy, but they are not used routinely. This is because, by themselves, they do not seem to be good enough at predicting the outcome of the pregnancy or what treatment is needed, and because they may not be widely available. In the future, it is hoped that other markers will be found to help predict and diagnose miscarriage and ectopic pregnancy more accurately. It may also be possible to combine the results of a few biomarkers to create better tests. This paper aims to summarise the current value of biomarkers in early pregnancy and how they can be used safely. This is important because if these tests are used in the wrong way, it could result in harm to a healthy pregnancy or unnecessary surgery.

articles.title: Prevalence and Risk Factors of Excessive Daytime Sleepiness in Older Adults: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Medical Directors Association
articles.authors: Xiong Y, Tao S, Meng X et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS) is a common but often overlooked condition in older adults, and it is associated with a variety of adverse outcomes. This study aimed to explore the pooled prevalence of EDS and its risk factors among older adults.
DESIGN: Systematic review and meta-analysis.
SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: Adults aged 60 years and older in any setting.
METHODS: A systematic search was conducted in 8 databases, including CNKI, VIP, CBM, WanFang Data, Web of Science, PubMed, Embase, and The Cochrane Library from inception to October 2025. Two researchers independently screened the literature and extracted the information. Pooled prevalence estimates and odds ratios for the prevalence of EDS in older adults and its risk factors were calculated using fixed- or random-effects models.
RESULTS: Forty-three eligible studies were included; the overall pooled prevalence of EDS in older adults was 16.9%. Subgroup analyses revealed significant variations in prevalence across geographic regions (P < .001), with the lowest rate observed in East Asia (13.0%) and the highest in Western Asia (21.8%). Furthermore, the use of different Epworth Sleepiness Scale cutoff values resulted in significant differences. Several factors were significantly associated with an increased risk of EDS, including male sex, obesity, malnutrition, urinary incontinence, and various comorbidities (eg, dementia, Parkinson's disease, cerebrovascular disease, depression, diabetes, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, insomnia, and obstructive sleep apnea). Conversely, the use of hypnotic medications may serve as a protective factor.
CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: EDS is common among older adults, although prevalence estimates vary across geographic regions and according to the Epworth Sleepiness Scale cutoff used. Several demographic, nutritional, and health-related factors were associated with EDS. These findings support greater clinical attention to EDS and targeted early screening, particularly among older adults with relevant comorbidities or other associated factors, to facilitate timely evaluation and appropriate intervention.

articles.title: Improving the Letrozole Induced Polycystic Ovary Syndrome in Rat Model: Effect of Vitamin D on Hyperandrogenism, Insulin Resistance, Inflammation and Adipokines.
articles.journal: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology
articles.authors: Korkmaz GE, Yaman M, Ak TP et al.
articles.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a chronic systemic disease progressing. Vitamin D deficiency may contribute to the pathophysiology of PCOS by affecting multiple mechanisms. In this study, the effects of Vit D on altered biochemistry and ovarian histopathology and adipokine immunoreactivities in PCOS rats were investigated. Forty female Sprague Dawley rats were divided into 5 groups as control, Dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), Vit D, PCOS and PCOS+ Vit D experimental groups. DMSO group was applied 2% DMSO (1 mL/kg/day, by gavage). Vit D group was applied Vit D (200 IU/day, orally). PCOS group was applied letrozole dissolved in 2% DMSO (1 mg/kg/day, by gavage). PCOS+ Vit D group was applied letrozole and Vit D simultaneously. In the PCOS group, luteinizing hormone/follicle stimulating hormone (LH/FSH) ratio and LH, testosterone, interleukin-1 (IL-1), tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNF-α) and homeostatic model assessment for insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) values increased significantly, unlike the FSH value. In this group, the number of all follicles decreased significantly, while cystic follicles increased. Morever, the granulosa layer in the secondary and tertiary follicles decreased significantly, while the thecal thickness increased. Also it was observed disorganized zona pellucida, degenerated oocytes, thecal and hilar cell hyperplasia. All these changes were significantly improved in the PCOS+ Vit D group. Changes in omentin, visfatin and resistin immunoreactivity in PCOS were ameliorated by Vit D administration. This study determined the ameliorative effects of vitamin D supplementation on the biochemical and histopathological changes and regulation of adipokine distribution in PCOS.

articles.title: Psychometric validation of the french endometriosis health profile-5 (EHP-5): structural validity, measurement invariance and recommendations for clinical interpretation.
articles.journal: Quality of life research : an international journal of quality of life aspects of treatment, care and rehabilitation
articles.authors: Dodeur-Delangre P, Pouytes C, Le Borgne M et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The Endometriosis Health Profile-5 (EHP-5) is a widely used disease-specific instrument for assessing endometriosis-related quality of life. Despite its growing use, evidence regarding its structural validity and measurement invariance remains limited. This study examined the psychometric properties of the French EHP-5.
METHODS: A total of 1,439 French-speaking women with medically diagnosed endometriosis completed an online survey. Preliminary item analyses included difficulty and discrimination indices, floor and ceiling effects, and Ferguson's delta coefficient. Internal consistency was evaluated using Cronbach's alpha and McDonald's omega. Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) was conducted using robust weighted least squares estimation (WLSMV). Hypothesis testing for construct validity was conducted using 0-10 numerical rating scales for pain intensity and frequency and dichotomous indicators of fatigue and constant pelvic pain. Measurement invariance was tested across infertility, parenthood, and comorbidity groups.
RESULTS: The five core items demonstrated satisfactory item functioning and internal consistency (α = 0.71; ω = 0.71). CFA generally supported a unidimensional structure of the core scale (CFI = 0.956, TLI = 0.912, SRMR = 0.047), although RMSEA (= 0.111) exceeded conventional recommendations. EHP-5 scores were significantly associated with pain intensity, pain frequency, fatigue, and constant pelvic pain, consistent with the predefined hypotheses for construct validity. Measurement invariance was generally supported across infertility, parenthood, and comorbidity groups.
CONCLUSIONS: The French EHP-5 core scale appears to be a brief measure of endometriosis-related quality of life with satisfactory psychometric properties. Clinical implications and recommendations are discussed, particularly regarding the complementary roles of the core and modular components of the instrument and their implications for score interpretation.

articles.title: The impact of heterozygous BRCA1 mutations on ovarian angiogenesis.
articles.authors: Pegoraro S, Fogar B, Spazzapan M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: BRCA1/2 mutations are classically associated with hereditary breast and ovarian cancer, yet growing evidence indicates that even heterozygous BRCA1 status may alter ovarian physiology before malignant transformation. Carriers of BRCA1 mutations display reduced ovarian reserve and accelerated reproductive ageing, although the underlying cellular and molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. Given the fundamental role of angiogenesis in follicle survival and stromal homeostasis, we investigated whether BRCA1 haploinsufficiency disrupts the ovarian microvascular environment, thereby predisposing to both impaired ovarian function and the establishment of a pro-tumorigenic niche.
METHODS: Ovary specimens were obtained from healthy women (n = 20, WT) or from women carrying BRCA1 mutations undergoing preventive oophorectomy (n = 20, mut). Vascular density was assessed by immunohistochemistry and quantified using QuPath software. Ovarian endothelial cells (OVECs) were isolated from biopsies and used to perform transcriptomic and functional assays, with a focus on endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition. The involvement of BRCA1 mutations in altered endothelial behavior was confirmed in BRCA1-silenced HUVECs. To investigate tissue-specificity, parallel experiments were conducted using endothelial cells isolated from the skin of women carrying or non-carrying BRCA1 mutations.
RESULTS: Mut OVECs exhibited distinct in vitro growth behaviors, including altered morphology (i.e. elongated and fusiform shape) and replication rate. Transcriptomic analysis revealed a distinct gene expression profile in mut compared to WT OVECs. Mut cells exhibited an enrichment of gene signatures associated with vascular remodeling, such as migration, proliferation, and sensitivity to endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition. Functionally, mut OVECs showed increased angiogenic behavior and a shift toward mesenchymal traits. Histological analysis of ovarian…
CONCLUSIONS: In conclusion, this study provides the first evidence that heterozygous BRCA1 mutations induce a tissue-specific endothelial dysfunction in the ovarian microenvironment, characterized by aberrant angiogenesis and increased susceptibility to endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition, suggesting that the ovarian vascular niche is remodeled towards a pro-tumorigenic state prior to malignant transformation. These findings identify a potential target for early detection and preventive strategies in BRCA1 mutation carriers.

articles.title: Health-related quality of life with PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors added to standard therapy for endometrial and cervical cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.journal: Quality of life research : an international journal of quality of life aspects of treatment, care and rehabilitation
articles.authors: Lemos MJ, Queiroz LF, Ayesha A et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether adding programmed cell death protein 1 or programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-1/PD-L1) inhibitors to standard therapy affects health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in patients with endometrial or cervical cancer.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from inception through September 2025 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing a PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor plus standard therapy with the identical treatment backbone, with or without placebo. Mean differences (MDs) in change from baseline were pooled using random-effects models with the Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2, and certainty of evidence was evaluated with GRADE.
RESULTS: Nine RCTs involving 5,933 patients were included, of which seven trials comprising 4,995 patients contributed to the meta-analysis. Adding PD-1/PD-L1 inhibition did not significantly affect EORTC QLQ-C30 global health status/quality of life (MD -0.07; 95% CI -1.50 to 1.35; I²=0%; 7 studies; 4,995 patients). Results were also non-significant for physical, role, emotional, cognitive, and social functioning; lymphedema; menopausal symptoms; peripheral neuropathy; sexual worry; symptom experience; and EQ-5D health status. Certainty of evidence was moderate for global health status/quality of life and low for the remaining outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Adding PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors to standard therapy did not detectably change global HRQoL, and the pooled confidence interval excluded clinically important deterioration. No functional or symptom domain differed significantly, although small effects cannot be excluded for domains informed by few trials.

articles.title: Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices of Pregnant Women and Health Care Workers Regarding Antenatal Testing for HIV, Hepatitis B Virus, and Syphilis in Vietnam: Protocol for a Multicenter Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.authors: Nguyen TK, Bui MT, Bui TTT et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mother-to-child transmission (MTCT) of HIV, hepatitis B virus, and syphilis remains a preventable cause of fetal loss, neonatal morbidity, and long-term disability. In Vietnam (Viet Nam), although antenatal care coverage is high, gaps persist in the timing, uptake, and completion of screening and follow-up services for these infections.
OBJECTIVE: This study has 2 parallel population-specific objectives. Among women who recently gave birth, we will estimate completion of antenatal testing for HIV, hepatitis B virus, and syphilis and its associated factors with study-defined optimal testing (completion of all 3 tests during the first trimester). Among health care workers (HCWs), we will assess knowledge, attitudes, and reported practices and identify professional factors associated with good practice regarding antenatal screening and MTCT prevention.
METHODS: This multicenter, hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted from June to September 2026 in 4 provincial hospitals in northern Vietnam. Women completed an interviewer-administered questionnaire after delivery, once clinically stable and before discharge. Antenatal testing was verified from maternal records, laboratory reports, or electronic records whenever available. HCWs completed a separate anonymous self-administered questionnaire during the same study period. The 2 participant groups were not matched. The primary outcome for women is completion of all 3 antenatal tests during the first trimester (study-defined optimal testing). The primary outcome for HCWs is good practice regarding the prevention of MTCT. The minimum target sample sizes were 601 women and 601 HCWs. Data will be analyzed separately for each group. Descriptive analyses will summarize knowledge, attitudes, and practices indicators and service uptake. Modified Poisson regression with robust variance will be used to identify factors independently associated with the primary outcomes.
RESULTS: The protocol received ethics approval on February 9, 2026. The study is funded by Thai Binh University of Medicine and Pharmacy, Hung Yen, Vietnam. Recruitment was conducted from June to September 2026. As of manuscript…
CONCLUSIONS: The study will provide hospital-based evidence on completion of antenatal triple screening and provider practices. By prespecifying distinct outcomes for women and HCWs, the study is designed to identify actionable gaps while avoiding causal interpretation of cross-sectional associations.

articles.title: Racial and Ethnic Differences in Long-Term Ocular Outcomes Among Individuals With Gestational Diabetes.
articles.authors: Nelson EM, Homa S, Ho E et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) disproportionately affects Black and Hispanic or Latino birthing populations, but racial and ethnic differences in long-term ocular complications after GDM are not well characterized. We compared the risk of diabetic retinopathy (DR) and diabetic cataracts (DC) among individuals with GDM across racial and ethnic groups over 10 years.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using de-identified electronic health record data from the TriNetX US Collaborative Network (N = 182,086 with GDM across 67 healthcare organizations). Individuals with pre-existing type 1 or type 2 diabetes or prior GDM were excluded. We calculated cumulative incidence and incidence rates of DR and DC by race and ethnicity between January 2000 and July 2026. We then performed 1:1 propensity score matching for Black or African American vs. White patients and for Hispanic or Latino vs. White patients, balancing demographics, body mass index (BMI), blood pressure, laboratory values, and medications (standardized mean difference < 0.10). Outcomes were compared using risk ratios (RR), Kaplan-Meier analysis, and hazard ratios (HR).
RESULTS: Overall, 1,078 individuals developed DR (0.593%), and 505 developed DC (0.278%). Crude cumulative incidence was highest among Black patients for DC (0.70%) and among Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander (1.32%), Black (1.23%), and American Indian or Alaska Native (1.18%) patients for DR. In matched cohorts of 24,121 patients per group, Black patients had a higher risk than White patients of both DR (RR, 1.62; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.21-2.18) and DC (RR, 2.26; 95% CI, 1.44-3.56). Time-to-event analyses were consistent (DR HR, 0.68 for White vs. Black patients; 95% CI, 0.50-0.91; DC HR, 0.47; 95% CI, 0.30-0.75). In matched cohorts of 17,600 patients per group, Hispanic or Latino and White patients did not differ significantly in DR (RR, 1.21; 95% CI, 0.77-1.90) or DC (RR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.46-1.90).
CONCLUSIONS: Among individuals with GDM, Black patients had a higher risk of DR and DC than matched White patients, although absolute risks were low. We found no significant difference between Hispanic or Latino and White patients, but power was limited by rare outcomes and shorter follow-up. These findings are hypothesis-generating and support further study of ocular outcomes after GDM, including studies with a non-GDM comparison group and longer follow-up.

articles.title: Intradetrusor Botulinum Toxin A at Doses of 100 and 200 Units for Urinary Incontinence in Women: A Single-Center Retrospective Study From Saudi Arabia.
articles.authors: AlShomrani H
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intradetrusor botulinum toxin type A (BoNT-A) is an effective treatment for refractory urgency urinary incontinence (UUI), but real-world data from the Middle East are limited, and clinical practice varies between 100-unit and 200-unit doses. This case series describes outcomes and safety of intradetrusor BoNT-A, by dose administered, in women with UI at a Saudi tertiary center.
METHODS: The study population comprised female patients diagnosed with UI, including urge, mixed, and idiopathic overactive bladder (OAB)-related incontinence, who had received at least one intravesical BoNT-A injection during the defined study period at King Abdulaziz University Hospital (KAUH). The primary outcome was documented clinical improvement in incontinence. Secondary outcomes were time to improvement, percentage reduction in incontinence episodes, retreatment, patient satisfaction, and adverse events. Analysis was descriptive because of the small cohort and unequal dose groups.
RESULTS: Ten female patients were identified, and one, with multiple sclerosis, was excluded; nine (mean age 68.7 ± 8.9 years) were included. Seven (78%) received 100 units, and two (22%) received 200 units of BoNT-A administered under cystoscopic guidance. Clinical improvement was documented in 3/9 (33%) patients (2/7 at 100 units; 1/2 at 200 units), while the other six (67%) had no meaningful response. Responders had 70% to 95% reductions in incontinence episodes, beginning at six to 24 weeks (median eight weeks) and lasting about four months to two years. Mean reduction across the cohort was 28.3%. Seven patients (n=7, 78%) were recorded as needing further treatment: six (67%) non-responders and one (11%) responder whose effect lasted about four months and was reinjected, the only repeat injection in the series. Three patients (33%), all in the 100-unit group, developed transient urinary retention with urinary tract infection (UTI) and dysuria; none needed catheterization. Satisfaction followed response:…
CONCLUSIONS: In this small case series, intradetrusor BoNT-A had an acceptable short-term safety profile. The response was all-or-nothing: three of nine women improved substantially, and six did not, and no dose-related difference could be assessed given the numbers. These descriptive findings are hypothesis-generating and support larger prospective multicenter studies to optimize BoNT-A dosing protocols in diverse populations, particularly within Middle Eastern healthcare contexts.

articles.title: Differential serum proteome profiling and electrochemical biosensing of leucine-rich alpha-2-glycoprotein (LRG1) and lipopolysaccharide-binding protein (LBP) as subtype-specific biomarkers for HPV-negative cervical cancer.
articles.authors: Watcharatanyatip K, Chokchaichamnankit D, Weeraphan C et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer (CC) is still a major global health concern. Specifically, human papillomavirus (HPV) - negative CC (HPV-neg CC) has a poorer prognosis than HPV-positive cases (HPV-pos CC). Distinguishing between HPV-pos and HPV-neg CC is the focus of this study, using proteomics and electrochemical biosensors.
METHODS: Pooled serum samples from healthy individuals, HPV-pos CC, and HPV-neg CC patients were analyzed using label-free quantitative proteomics. Differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) were analyzed using PEAKS® Studio software (≤1% False Discovery Rate, FDR; 1.5-fold change threshold). STRING and Metascape databases were used for protein-protein interaction analysis and functional clustering. An electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) biosensor was developed to quantify potential candidate biomarkers including lipopolysaccharide-binding protein (LBP) and leucine-rich alpha-2-glycoprotein (LRG1).
RESULTS: Proteomics revealed distinct signatures, associating HPV-pos and HPV-neg CC with humoral immune response impairment and systemic inflammatory response, respectively. Concurrently, inflammatory mediators, LBP and LRG1 were top DEPs across all groups, with 3.99 and 2.89-fold increases in HPV-neg CC vs. healthy control, respectively. The EIS-based biosensor verified that LBP had remarkable discriminatory power in separating HPV-pos CC cases from HPV-neg CC cases (AUC = 0.9815), whereas LRG1 successfully separated cancer cases from healthy controls (AUC = 1.000).
CONCLUSIONS: Proteomics and EIS biosensor techniques identified LBP as a potential biomarker linked to systemic inflammatory responses in HPV-neg CC. Therefore, this pilot study links the gap between proteomic discovery and clinical application, eventually providing exploratory insights into subtype characterization for HPV-neg CC. Further investigations in a larger cohort based on our findings are necessary for a better understanding of the role of LBP and LRG1 in all CC subtypes.

articles.title: iNGR-Modified Brucine-Loaded Liposomes Enhance Tumor Penetration and Suppress Ovarian Cancer Peritoneal Metastasis.
articles.authors: Zhao M, Li W, Wu M et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To develop an iNGR peptide-modified PEGylated liposomal brucine formulation (iNGR-Bru-lip) for targeted treatment of ovarian cancer peritoneal metastasis and to evaluate its tumor targeting, penetration, antitumor activity, underlying mechanism, and biosafety.
METHODS: The iNGR peptide was conjugated to DSPE-PEG-NHS and incorporated into brucine-loaded liposomes. The formulation was characterized using cryogenic transmission electron microscopy, dynamic light scattering, zeta-potential analysis, encapsulation-efficiency measurement, stability testing, and in vitro drug-release assays. Cellular uptake and targeting specificity were evaluated using confocal microscopy, flow cytometry, competition assays, and receptor-blocking experiments. Antitumor activity, autophagy-related changes, and apoptosis were investigated using cellular assays, MDC staining, transmission electron microscopy, Western blotting, and EBSS-mediated autophagy activation. Biodistribution, tumor penetration, therapeutic efficacy, and systemic safety were assessed in an ES-2 peritoneal xenograft model.
RESULTS: iNGR-Bru-lip displayed a uniform spherical morphology, an average diameter of 140.43 ± 0.64 nm, a polydispersity index below 0.15, negative surface charge, high brucine encapsulation efficiency (89.81 ± 2.50%), and stability for 30 days. The formulation exhibited sustained brucine release over 48 h. iNGR functionalization enhanced cellular uptake in CD13/NRP-1-high ES-2 cells, while competition with free iNGR peptide and CD13/NRP-1 blockade reduced cellular fluorescence. Compared with free brucine and non-targeted liposomes, iNGR-Bru-lip produced greater cytotoxicity, suppressed colony formation, migration, and invasion, and increased apoptosis. These effects were accompanied by autophagy-related changes, while EBSS-mediated autophagy activation attenuated the pro-apoptotic response. Intraperitoneal administration produced greater tumor accumulation than intravenous administration. In vivo, iNGR-Bru-lip penetrated peritoneal tumor tissues and significantly reduced abdominal circumference progression and tumor burden. Hematological, biochemical, and histopathological assessments revealed no evident systemic toxicity.
CONCLUSION: iNGR-Bru-lip integrates combines receptor-associated targeting, enhanced tumor penetration, and autophagy-associated apoptosis induction, providing a promising nanomedicine strategy for ovarian cancer peritoneal metastasis.

articles.title: Association of First Trimester Maternal Prognostic Nutritional Index and Hemoglobin-Albumin-Lymphocyte-Platelet Score with Preterm Birth and Low Birth Weight: A Retrospective Cohort Study of 6780 Pregnant Women.
articles.authors: Lan L, Li Z, Zhong J et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the associations between first trimester maternal prognostic nutritional index (PNI) and hemoglobin-albumin-lymphocyte-platelet (HALP) score with preterm birth and low birth weight.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study enrolled 6780 pregnant women, with PNI and HALP calculated using laboratory indicators obtained in the first trimester. Baseline clinical data and perinatal outcomes were extracted from the electronic medical records. Group comparisons were conducted using the χ2 test and Mann-Whitney U-test. Logistic regression analyses were conducted to identify independent associated factors. Receiver-operating characteristic (ROC) curves were plotted to evaluate the predictive performance of PNI.
RESULTS: Of the 6780 pregnancies, 841 (12.4%) were preterm births and 922 (13.6%) were low birth weight infants. For low birth weight subgroup analyses, 137 cases with macrosomic infants (birth weight ≥4000 g) were excluded, yielding a sample of 6643 for this sub-analysis. Maternal PNI and HALP levels were significantly lower in fetuses with preterm birth and low birth weight than in term birth and normal birth weight fetuses (all p<0.001). Logistic regression analysis showed that lower PNI was independently associated with preterm birth (adjusted odds ratios (OR) = 0.873, 95% confidence intervals (CI): 0.854-0.893, p<0.001) and low birth weight (adjusted OR = 0.882, 95% CI: 0.863-0.902, p<0.001), whereas HALP was not statistically significant. The area under the ROC curve (AUC) values of PNI for predicting preterm birth and low birth weight were 0.622 (95% CI: 0.600-0.644) and 0.608 (95% CI: 0.586-0.629), indicating modest discriminatory ability, with optimal cut off values of 39.65 and 39.45, respectively.
CONCLUSION: Low PNI was an independent factor associated with preterm birth and low birth weight, while HALP showed no independent association. Given its modest AUC values, PNI may serve only as an economical auxiliary complementary biomarker, rather than a standalone predictive tool, for antenatal risk stratification of preterm birth and low birth weight.

articles.title: Menstrual Phase-Dependent Changes in Heart Rate Variability in Healthy Young Women: A Longitudinal Observational Study.
articles.authors: Dhopeshwarkar R, Choudhary K, Chowdhary T et al.
articles.abstract: Background Cyclical changes in estrogen and progesterone across the menstrual cycle may modulate cardiac autonomic control, but the heart rate variability (HRV) changes reported in healthy women are inconsistent. This study examined short-term HRV in the menstrual, follicular, and luteal phases of the cycle in healthy young women. Methodology This longitudinal observational study was conducted in the Department of Physiology, Dr. S. N. Medical College, Jodhpur. Twenty healthy women aged 18-25 years with regular cycles (26-32 days) who were not using hormonal contraceptives underwent five-minute resting electrocardiographic recordings in the menstrual (days 1-3), follicular (days 8-10), and luteal (days 20-22) phases of a single cycle. Time- and frequency-domain HRV indices were compared using repeated-measures analysis of variance with Bonferroni-adjusted post hoc tests. Results The mean age was 20.15 ± 1.72 years. Mean heart rate differed across phases (84.47 ± 7.82, 84.74 ± 7.37, and 89.99 ± 11.24 bpm; p = 0.04). The root mean square of successive differences (RMSSD) declined from 40.77 ± 9.28 ms in the menstrual phase to 34.33 ± 8.55 ms in the follicular phase and 31.07 ± 7.52 ms in the luteal phase (p < 0.001), and pRR50 declined from 28.33 ± 4.68% to 17.03 ± 3.44% (p < 0.001). Very low frequency (LF) power was highest in the luteal phase (439.43 ± 130.33 ms²; p < 0.001), and normalized LF power rose from 53.29 ± 7.17 in the follicular phase to 62.34 ± 12.64 in the luteal phase (p = 0.03). High-frequency (HF) power, normalized high-frequency power, LF power, the LF/HF ratio, and standard deviation of RR intervals (SDRR) did not differ significantly between phases. Conclusion In this small sample, beat-to-beat vagally mediated indices (RMSSD and pRR50) were lowest, and heart rate was highest in the luteal phase, whereas spectral high-frequency power and the LF/HF ratio were unchanged. Hormone levels were not measured, so the findings cannot be attributed to specific hormones. The menstrual phase should be recorded, and ideally standardized, when HRV is measured in women.

articles.title: MRI Accuracy for Detecting Deep Myometrial Invasion in Low-Grade Endometrial Cancer: Insights From a Seven-Year UK Experience.
articles.authors: Jabbar A, Kodiathodi S, George M
articles.abstract: Background Endometrial cancer is the most common gynaecological malignancy in high-income countries, with approximately 10,200 new cases each year in the United Kingdom, around 34% of which are attributable to overweight and obesity. Depth of myometrial invasion determines International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) stage IA versus IB and therefore both the extent of surgical staging and whether surgery is undertaken locally or at a cancer centre. Pelvic magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is widely used for this assessment, although diagnostic performance in routine practice varies and the influence of body mass index (BMI) remains uncertain. Methods This retrospective single-centre diagnostic accuracy study included consecutive women with biopsy-proven grade 1-2 endometrioid endometrial carcinoma who underwent preoperative pelvic MRI followed by hysterectomy within a UK NHS pathway between January 2017 and July 2025. Women whose MRI demonstrated radiological stage greater than IB were excluded, so these estimates apply to women with radiologically presumed stage I disease. Final histopathology was the reference standard, with deep myometrial invasion (DMI) defined as invasion of 50% or more of the myometrial thickness. Diagnostic performance measures were calculated with 95% confidence intervals. A post hoc subgroup analysis compared performance by BMI category. Results A total of 204 patients were included. Median age was 65 years (range: 26 to 88), and median BMI was 34 kg/m² (range: 21 to 62; mean: 34.4 kg/m²); of 189 women with recorded BMI, 46 (24.3%) had a BMI below 30 kg/m² and 143 (75.7%) had a BMI of 30 kg/m² or above. MRI demonstrated sensitivity of 63.33% (95% CI: 49.90% to 75.41%), specificity of 82.64% (75.45% to 88.44%), positive predictive value of 60.32% (50.34% to 69.50%), negative predictive value of 84.40% (79.37% to 88.38%), and accuracy of 76.96% (70.57% to 82.55%) for detecting DMI. MRI stage and final histopathology were concordant in 157 of 204 cases (77.0%); MRI over-staged 25 women and under-staged 22. Direct between-group comparison showed higher diagnostic accuracy among women with BMI ≥30 kg/m² than among those below, but this comparison was unadjusted; the subgroups were unequal in size, and the prevalence of deep invasion also differed between them (26.6% versus 34.8%). Conclusion In this single-centre NHS cohort, preoperative MRI demonstrated moderate diagnostic accuracy for detecting DMI in women with…

articles.title: Effectiveness of Prenatal Screening for Gestational Diabetes: A Narrative Review.
articles.authors: Mohammad Altowijri A, Dhaifallah Alanazi M, Abdullah Albalawi S et al.
articles.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is a common metabolic disorder of pregnancy associated with adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes. Despite its clinical importance, considerable variation remains in approaches to prenatal screening, including the timing, diagnostic strategy, and criteria used to identify affected pregnancies. The expansion of screening also raises concerns regarding unnecessary diagnosis, healthcare utilization, and patient burden. This narrative review of the available literature was conducted to examine different approaches to prenatal GDM screening. The review considered variations in screening timing, screening strategies, diagnostic thresholds, and their associations with maternal and neonatal outcomes. Particular attention was given to the clinical implications of identifying milder degrees of dysglycemia and to the economic and practical consequences of different screening approaches. This review concluded that prenatal GDM screening should aim to achieve clinically meaningful detection while minimizing unnecessary intervention and patient burden. Future research should focus on standardized outcomes, simplified and accessible screening approaches, and context-specific strategies that integrate clinical effectiveness, economic considerations, and healthcare resources.

articles.title: Mild Abdominal Pain During the 14-Day Post-Embryo Transfer Waiting Period and Pregnancy Outcomes: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Gao L, Ren Y, Ding M et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate the association between mild abdominal pain during the 14-day post-embryo transfer (ET) waiting period and the pregnancy outcomes.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted involving patients who underwent embryo transfer between January and July 2019. Overall, 4256 ET cycles were included, consisting of 1497 fresh and 2759 frozen-thawed cycles. Abdominal pain was self-assessed using the Numerical Rating Scale (NRS) on day 7 and on day 14 of the 14-day post-ET waiting period. Scores of 1-3, 4-6, and 7-10 correspond to mild, moderate and severe abdominal pain respectively. Key variables included patient demographics, cycle characteristics, and pregnancy outcomes. Independent predictors of abdominal pain during the 14-day waiting period after ET were identified using multivariable logistic regression analysis.
RESULTS: The overall incidence of mild abdominal pain during the 14-day waiting period was 25.09%, comprising 24.79% mild and 0.31% severe cases. Patients who reported mild abdominal pain during the 14-day post-ET waiting period had significantly higher rates of clinical pregnancy (66.54% vs 56.40%, p < 0.001) and live birth (57.06% vs 46.99%, p < 0.001) compared with those who did not. Conversely, in the small subgroup of patients with moderate-to-severe abdominal pain (n=13), the pregnancy rate was notably lower. On multivariate logistic regression analysis, mild abdominal pain was associated with higher occurrence of clinical pregnancy and live birth during the 14-day post-ET waiting period.
CONCLUSIONS: Mild abdominal pain during the 14-day post-ET waiting period was not associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes but was associated with a higher clinical pregnancy rate, although further research is needed to clarify the potential mechanisms. In contrast, moderate-to-severe abdominal pain was associated with a lower clinical pregnancy rate; however, this finding should be interpreted cautiously given the small sample size of this subgroup.

articles.title: Clinical effect of tranexamic acid combined with carbetocin on reducing postpartum hemorrhage in high-risk pregnant women.
articles.authors: Sun W, Ji D, Sa R et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of tranexamic acid combined with carbetocin for postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) in high-risk parturients.
METHODS: A total of 200 high-risk parturients were divided into an observation group (tranexamic acid combined with carbetocin, n=118) and a control group (carbetocin alone, n=82). Postpartum blood loss, PPH incidence, blood transfusion rate, hysterectomy rate, hemoglobin level, hemoglobin decrease, length of hospital stay, lochia duration, adverse drug reactions, and postpartum recovery were compared.
RESULTS: The observation group had significantly lower 2-h blood loss, 24-h blood loss, PPH incidence, blood transfusion rate, and hysterectomy rate (all P<0.05). Hemoglobin at 24 h was higher and hemoglobin decrease was smaller in the observation group (both P<0.05). No significant differences were observed in length of hospital stay, lochia duration, adverse drug reactions, or postpartum recovery indicators between the two groups (all P>0.05).
CONCLUSION: Tranexamic acid combined with carbetocin effectively reduces postpartum blood loss and the incidence of PPH, lowers the blood transfusion and hysterectomy rates, improves hemoglobin levels, and does not increase adverse drug reactions or affect postpartum recovery, demonstrating good efficacy and safety in high-risk parturients.

articles.title: Maternal hair glucocorticoids as indicators of HPA axis dysregulation in early preterm birth.
articles.authors: Rawat M, Mallick LM, Künzel RG et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preterm birth (PTB) is a leading cause of neonatal morbidity and mortality, yet its biological mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis dysregulation is implicated in PTB, and maternal hair glucocorticoids may reflect chronic HPA axis activity. The purpose of this study was to evaluate whether hair cortisone (HCNC) and cortisol (HCC) concentrations measured during pregnancy were associated with early preterm birth (ePTB), birth after 20 weeks and at or before 34 weeks of gestation.
METHODS: This analysis used data (N = 309) from the Placental Abruption Genetic Epidemiology study in Peru. Maternal hair collected at birth was divided into two 3-cm segments representing later pregnancy (0-12 weeks before birth) and earlier pregnancy (12-24 weeks before birth) to estimate HCNC and HCC. To address variation in glucocorticoid concentrations by gestational age at birth and differences in exposure windows between ePTB and term births, we used gestational age-standardized residuals as outcomes. Multivariable logistic regression procedures were used to estimate odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals for ePTB.
RESULTS: Higher HCNC in later pregnancy was associated with lower odds of ePTB, corresponding to 20% (OR = 0.79, 95% CI: 0.63-0.99) lower odds of ePTB per-one standard deviation increase in gestational-age standardized HCNC. In contrast, higher HCC in earlier pregnancy was associated with higher odds of ePTB (OR = 1.58, 95% CI: 1.29-1.94).
CONCLUSIONS: Hair glucocorticoids may reflect HPA axis dysregulation during pregnancy, but imprecise temporal resolution and wash-out effects warrant further study of their predictive value for ePTB.

articles.title: Association between the triglyceride-glucose index and severity of abnormal uterine bleeding in perimenopausal women: a retrospective single-center study.
articles.authors: Ye Y, Yuan M, Zhang S
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index, a surrogate marker of insulin resistance (IR), and the severity of abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB) in perimenopausal women.
METHODS: A single-center retrospective observational study was conducted from January 1, 2024 to December 31, 2025 on perimenopausal women diagnosed with AUB. The TyG index was calculated as ln (fasting triglycerides [mg/dL] × fasting glucose [mg/dL]/2) and was analyzed both as a continuous variable and in tertiles. AUB severity was graded using a composite measure of bleeding pattern, hemoglobin (Hb) level, and endometrial findings. Multivariable logistic regression and ordinal regression were used to assess the association, with adjustment for demographic, reproductive, and metabolic covariates. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis evaluated discrimination.
RESULTS: A total of 246 women were included (mean age 48.3 years). Eighty-eight women (35.8%) had severe AUB. The mean TyG index increased across severity strata (mild 8.41 ± 0.39, moderate 8.69 ± 0.41, severe 8.97 ± 0.44; P for trend <0.001). Each one-unit increase in TyG index conferred increased odds of severe AUB (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 3.94; 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.18-7.12; P<0.001). Compared to the lowest tertile, the highest TyG tertile had an adjusted OR of 4.62 (95% CI 2.21-9.66; P for trend <0.001). The area under the ROC curve (AUC) for the TyG index was 0.74 (95% CI 0.68-0.81), with an optimal cut-off of 8.71.
CONCLUSIONS: A higher TyG index is independently associated with increasing severity of AUB in perimenopausal women in a dose-dependent manner. The TyG index may serve as a valuable, low-cost tool for risk stratification and supports the observation that perimenopausal AUB is associated with metabolic dysregulation.

articles.title: Construction of a management model based on traditional Chinese medicine comprehensive health management for a high-risk gestational diabetes mellitus population and its impact on postpartum diabetes.
articles.authors: Niu Y, Liu H, Sun D et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop a Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) comprehensive health management program for high-risk pregnant women with gestational diabetes and evaluate its impact on postpartum diabetes.
METHODS: This prospective randomized controlled trial enrolled 248 pregnant women from August 2024 to July 2025 (registration: ITMCTR2026000970). Participants were assigned to a control group (routine management, n=123) or an experimental group (TCM comprehensive health management, n=123). Glycemic parameters, islet function indicators, and lipid parameters, psychological scores, maternal-infant outcomes, and risk factors for postpartum diabetes were compared.
RESULTS: At baseline, no significant differences were observed between the groups in any indicator (P > 0.05). Repeated-measures ANOVA revealed significant main effects of time and group and significant time × group interaction effects (P < 0.05). After the intervention, FPG, 2hPG, and HbA1c significantly decreased in both groups (P < 0.05), with greater reductions in the experimental group (P < 0.05). Islet function indicators (FINS, C-P, and HOMA-IR) also declined significantly, with larger decrements observed in the experimental group (P < 0.05). Concurrently, TC, TG, and LDL-C decreased while HDL-C increased in both groups, all favoring the experimental group (P < 0.05). SAS and SDS scores decreased significantly, with more pronounced improvements in the experimental group (P < 0.05). Subgroup analyses revealed a significant treatment-by-age interaction (P=0.034), with participants aged ≥ 35 years showing more pronounced glycemic improvements than those < 35 years. Among TCM constitution types, the Yin-deficiency subgroup exhibited significant between-group differences in glycemic benefits (P < 0.001), although the overall interaction across constitution types did not reach statistical significance (P=0.416). The experimental group further exhibited lower rates of cesarean section, pregnancy complications, and perinatal adverse outcomes (P < 0.05). At 6-month postpartum follow-up,…
CONCLUSION: TCM comprehensive health management effectively improves glucose and lipid metabolism, enhances islet function, alleviates anxiety and depression, reduces maternal-infant complications, and lowers the risk of postpartum diabetes, with potential greater benefits observed in older pregnant women and those with Yin-deficiency constitution, although the age-related finding requires confirmation in future studies.

articles.title: Bariatric surgery and risk of cervical shortening and spontaneous preterm birth.
articles.authors: Abelman SH, Keller NA, Jackson FI et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Previous studies have shown that, on average, pregnant patients with obesity have longer cervical length measurements at screening than patients with normal weight. However, little is known about how bariatric surgery modifies this effect.
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the incidence of cervical shortening, preterm birth, and cerclage placement in patients with and without a history of bariatric surgery.
STUDY DESIGN: This was a retrospective cohort study within a large healthcare system in New York between January 2019 and December 2024. Patients with screening cervical length measurements between 16 weeks 0 days and 23 weeks 6 days of gestation were included in the analysis. Short and very short cervical lengths were defined as <25 mm and <10 mm, respectively. Bariatric surgery status was determined, including gastric sleeve, gastric band, Roux-en-Y gastric bypass, and other documented types of bariatric surgery. The shortest measured cervical length was used to determine the presence of a short or very short cervical length. Patients with multiple gestations, a history of preterm birth, cerclage placed before 16 weeks' gestation, missing prepregnancy body mass index data, or no record of an ultrasound between 16 weeks 0 days and 23 weeks 6 days were excluded. Multivariate logistic regression models were used to compare the incidence of short and very short cervix, cerclage placement, and preterm and spontaneous preterm birth at <37 and at<34 weeks' gestation by history of bariatric surgery, adjusting for prepregnancy body mass index class, race and ethnicity group, and nulliparity.
RESULTS: In total, outcomes were analyzed for 69,296 patients: 68,476 (98.8%) without and 820 (1.2%) with a history of bariatric surgery. Among patients with a history of bariatric surgery, 27 (3.3%) had short, and 5 (0.6%) had very short cervices with 6 (0.7%) subsequently receiving a cerclage. Among patients without a history of bariatric surgery 1072 (1.6%) had short, and 246 (0.4%)…
CONCLUSION: Bariatric surgery is associated with an increased risk of midtrimester cervical shortening and spontaneous preterm birth, independent of prepregnancy body mass index and history of preterm birth. These findings support recognition of patients with prior bariatric surgery as a distinct obstetrical risk group and suggest that incorporating bariatric surgery history into risk assessment may improve identification of patients at risk for spontaneous preterm birth.

articles.title: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and long-term risk of chronic hypertension and cardiovascular disease: A national claims-based cohort study.
articles.authors: Ayyash M, Huang Y, Kishkovich T et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) are increasingly recognized as important predictors of future cardiovascular disease. Although individuals with HDP are known to be at increased risk of subsequent chronic hypertension and cardiovascular morbidity, the association between antihypertensive treatment and long-term outcomes is not well characterized. This study aims to evaluate the association between new-onset HDP and long-term risk of chronic hypertension and cardiovascular disease outcome, and to assess the impact of disease severity and need for antihypertensive treatment on long-term outcomes.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the 2016-2022 Merative™ MarketScan® Commercial Claims and Encounters and Multi-State Medicaid databases. Individuals with a delivery hospitalization and continuous enrollment during the entire pregnancy through 90 days postpartum were included. HDP exposure was defined as gestational hypertension or preeclampsia, excluding those with chronic hypertension during pregnancy. Secondary exposure included antihypertensive medication use from >20 weeks' gestation through 12 weeks postpartum. The primary outcome was incident chronic hypertension beyond 90 days postpartum. Secondary outcomes were cardiovascular conditions including heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, unspecified heart failure, atrial fibrillation, stroke, coronary artery disease, aortic aneurysm, and a composite cardiovascular outcome-defined as the occurrence of any of these cardiac conditions. Cumulative incidence function with Gray's test and Cox proportional hazard models were used.
RESULTS: Among 1,010,658 deliveries, 13.0% had HDP, including 3.0% who received antihypertensive medications. Chronic hypertension occurred in 1.4% of those without HDP, 4.9% with HDP without medications, and 12.6% with HDP receiving medications (p < 0.001). Composite cardiovascular outcome occurred in 0.35%,…
CONCLUSION: HDP is strongly associated with long-term risk of chronic hypertension and cardiovascular outcomes, with the highest risk observed among individuals requiring antihypertensive therapy. Antihypertensive medication use remained associated with subsequent outcomes after accounting for HDP subtype, suggesting its potential role as a marker of elevated cardiovascular risk. These findings support targeted postpartum cardiovascular surveillance and early risk-reduction strategies.

articles.title: Urinary miRNAs for non-invasive detection of gynecological cancers: opportunities and challenges in liquid biopsy applications.
articles.authors: Fuchs T, Passerini G, Liebau C et al.
articles.abstract: Gynecological cancers, including cervical, ovarian, and endometrial cancers, are major contributors to morbidity and mortality among women worldwide, with early detection being essential for improving diagnostic accuracy and survival rates.
