This review explores the potential of urinary microRNAs (miRNAs) as non-invasive biomarkers for diagnosing and monitoring these cancers, highlighting advancements in detection technologies such as digital PCR and next-generation sequencing (NGS). Dysregulated urinary miRNA profiles have been associated with these cancers and often reflect those observed in tissue biopsies, underscoring their diagnostic potential. However, overlapping miRNA alterations across malignancies can limit cancer-type discrimination, while variability in sample collection, extracellular vesicle (EV) separation, analytical methods, and data normalization impedes reproducibility and clinical translation. Advances in NGS have enhanced the sensitivity and precision of miRNA analysis, and the integration of multiple miRNA biomarkers may improve diagnostic accuracy and cancer-type discrimination, although these applications require clinical validation. Future research should focus on standardizing methodologies, characterizing miRNA-tumor interactions, and addressing tumor heterogeneity to fully realize the clinical utility of urinary miRNAs in gynecological oncology.

articles.title: Real-world determinants of bone mineral density loss and osteoporotic fractures in primary hyperparathyroidism: a retrospective cohort and nested case-control study.
articles.authors: Zeng M, Zhang B, Yu L et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To identify real-world determinants of osteoporosis and fragility fractures in primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT) and to quantify bone mineral density (BMD) recovery after parathyroidectomy (PTX).
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study with a nested case-control analysis included PHPT patients diagnosed during 2015-2024 who had undergone DXA. The primary endpoint was osteoporosis; the secondary endpoint was fragility fracture. Determinants of osteoporosis were analyzed using propensity-score matching (1:2) followed by multivariable logistic regression; fractures were analyzed using risk-set matched conditional logistic regression. BMD changes after PTX were assessed by paired t-tests.
RESULTS: Overall, 300 patients (100 osteoporosis/200 normal bone mass) were included. Older age [adjusted odds ratio (aOR) = 1.28], postmenopausal status (aOR = 1.44), higher corrected calcium (aOR = 1.30), higher parathyroid hormone (PTH) (aOR = 1.95), and vitamin D deficiency (aOR = 2.05) were independently associated with osteoporosis, while higher body mass index (BMI) (aOR = 0.93) and prior PTX (≥ 12 months, aOR = 0.63) were protective. In fracture analysis (92 cases/184 controls), risk increased with age (aOR = 1.45), lower BMD T-score (aOR = 1.62), corrected calcium (aOR = 1.18), PTH (aOR = 1.70), and vitamin D deficiency (aOR = 1.52), whereas higher BMI (aOR = 0.94) and PTX ≥ 6 months (aOR = 0.58) reduced risk. Among 146 PTX patients, BMD increased by 7.7% at lumbar spine, 5.6% at femoral neck, and 5.0% at total hip at 12-24 months post-surgery. Subgroup analyses indicated stronger surgical benefits in vitamin D-sufficient patients; sensitivity analyses confirmed robustness.
CONCLUSIONS: Skeletal complications in PHPT are driven by metabolic activity, vitamin D status, age, menopausal status, and BMI. PTX is associated with reduced risk and significant BMD recovery.

articles.title: Construction and validation of a cross-sectional classification model for identifying adverse metabolic status in patients with polycystic ovary syndrome based on serum amino acids and lipid metabolic characteristics.
articles.authors: Zhao Y, Wang H, Zhang C et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To develop and externally validate a cross-sectional classification model for identifying adverse metabolic status at diagnosis in patients with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) based on serum amino acid and lipid metabolic profiles.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 442 PCOS patients, comprising a training set (n=309; June 2022-December 2024) and an external validation set (n=133; January 2025-December 2025). Within each dataset, patients were classified into an adverse metabolic status group or a metabolically normal group according to the presence of at least one of the following conditions at baseline: metabolic syndrome, insulin resistance (IR), non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, impaired glucose tolerance, or type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). At enrollment, serum concentrations of branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs), aromatic amino acids (AAAs), glucogenic amino acids, lysophosphatidylcholine (LPC) species, and free fatty acids (FFAs) were measured using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Routine biochemical and hormonal parameters were also collected.
RESULTS: Multivariable logistic regression identified BMI ≥ 28.215 kg/m2 (OR=11.27), HOMA-IR ≥ 3.42 (OR=4.61), TyG index ≥ 4.84 (OR=5.44), valine ≥ 270.125 nmol/mL (OR=5.68), glutamate ≥ 63.185 nmol/mL (OR=8.87) and arachidonic acid ≥ 21.535 μmol/L (OR=10.85) as independent positive predictors of adverse metabolic status. In contrast, higher SHBG (OR=0.31), BCAA/AAA ratio ≥ 3.215 (OR=0.20), LPC(16:0) ≥ 142.06 μmol/L (OR=0.22), and LPC(18:1) ≥ 30.515 μmol/L (OR=0.28) were protective factors. The nomogram achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.965 in the training set and 0.939 in the external validation set.
CONCLUSION: The nomogram integrating serum amino acids and lipid profiles with routine clinical measures may provide a reliable tool for classifying adverse metabolic status in PCOS patients at initial assessment.

articles.title: Burden, etiology, and risk factors of diarrheal diseases among neonates in Eastern sub-Saharan Africa from 1990 to 2023.
articles.authors: Korma W, Asefa L, Gelchu M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diarrheal disease is the leading cause of child morbidity and mortality. However, there are only limited studies available in Africa. This study determined magnitude, burden, etiology, and risk factors of diarrheal disease among neonates (aged 0-27 days) in the Eastern Sub-Saharan African (ESSA) region from 1990 to 2023.
METHOD: The Global burden of Diseases 2023 estimates and methods were used. The incidence rate estimated was the cumulative incidence over the entire neonatal period (0-28 days), representing the total number of diarrheal episodes per 100,000 neonates during this period.
RESULTS: There were an estimated 215,343 cumulative new cases of diarrheal disease per 100,000 neonates (95% UI: 186,566-240,723) in 2023. The highest incidence and prevalence rates were estimated in South Sudan, Madagascar, and Malawi, whereas the lowest prevalence rate was estimated in Mozambique. The highest years of life lost and disability-adjusted life years rates were estimated in Somalia, whereas the lowest were estimated in Uganda and Tanzania. Rotavirus, adenovirus, and shigella were the common causes of diarrheal disease, whereas unsafe water, poor sanitation, no access to hand-washing facilities, low birth weight, short gestation, and suboptimal breastfeeding were the leading risk factors.
CONCLUSION: This study has revealed that there was substantial reduction in the burden of diarrheal diseases among neonates in the ESSA region in 2023 compared to 1990. However, the rates remain high and heterogeneous across the region. Therefore, prevention activities should target high-risk populations, improving water, sanitation, and hygiene, infant nutrition, and vaccination.

articles.title: Targeting tumor antigen Mesothelin by CAR-NK-92 cells as an effective therapy against ovarian cancer cells.
articles.authors: Stalp JL, Kutle I, Hachenberg J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ovarian cancer is typically diagnosed at an advanced stage with peritoneal metastases and remains associated with high relapse rates and limited therapeutic options. While chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-based immunotherapies have demonstrated remarkable success in hematologic malignancies, their implementation against solid tumors remains challenging due to tumor heterogeneity and an immunosuppressive microenvironment. Mesothelin, a cell-surface glycoprotein overexpressed in ovarian cancer and largely absent in healthy tissues, represents a promising therapeutic target.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: Third-generation anti-Mesothelin CAR constructs containing CD28, 4-1BB, and CD3ζ signaling domains were introduced into NK-92 cells using self-inactivating (SIN) alpharetroviral or lentiviral vectors. CAR expression, vector copy numbers, and cytotoxic activity were evaluated in 2D and 3D co-culture models employing ovarian cancer cell lines (OVCAR3, A2780) and primary patient-derived tumor cells. Cytotoxicity was assessed through live-cell imaging and flow cytometry.
RESULTS: Mesothelin was highly expressed in ovarian cancer cell lines and patient tumor samples, but minimally detected in healthy ovarian tissues. Alpharetroviral anti-Mesothelin CAR-NK-92 cells exhibited potent, antigen-dependent cytotoxicity against Mesothelin-high OVCAR3 and primary ovarian cancer cells in 2D models and pronounced tumor reduction in 3D spheroid assays. Additionally, alpharetroviral CAR-NK-92 cells demonstrated greater cytotoxic activity compared to lentiviral counterparts.
CONCLUSION: Our findings demonstrate significant antitumor activity of alpharetroviral anti-Mesothelin CAR-NK-92 cells in vitro, underscoring Mesothelin as a promising therapeutic target in ovarian cancer. The favorable safety profile and high performance of alpharetroviral vectors support their further development as a platform for next-generation CAR-NK cell therapies against solid malignancies.

articles.title: En Bloc Pelvic Lymph Node Dissection Using the da Vinci SP System for Endometrial Cancer.
articles.authors: Kanno K, Iwata T, Sawada M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although sentinel lymph node mapping has become the standard approach for surgical staging in early-stage endometrial cancer, systematic pelvic lymph node dissection (PLND) continues to play an important role in selected patients with intermediate- and high-risk disease.1 Furthermore, PLND is a fundamental surgical procedure, performed not only for gynecologic oncology procedures, but also for colorectal and urologic oncology procedures.2,3 This video demonstrates the key anatomical landmarks and our standardized anatomy-based concept for en bloc PLND, followed by its implementation using the da Vinci SP surgical system (SP), a newer single-port robotic platform.
METHODS: A 66-year-old woman with preoperatively diagnosed early-stage uterine serous carcinoma (p53-positive) underwent single-port robotic staging surgery, including simple hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, pelvic and para-aortic lymph node dissection, and partial omentectomy.
RESULTS: The procedure was completed without intraoperative complications. A standardized, anatomy-based approach using reproducible anatomical landmarks facilitated safe and systematic en bloc PLND. Suspension of the vesicohypogastric fascia (umbilical artery) provided stable exposure of the retroperitoneal space, while the articulating snake-like instruments of the SP platform enabled precise traction and countertraction, facilitating meticulous dissection throughout the procedure. Final histopathological examination confirmed stage IIC uterine serous carcinoma. The patient subsequently received adjuvant paclitaxel-carboplatin chemotherapy and remains disease-free at the latest follow-up.
CONCLUSIONS: The SP platform enables standardized, anatomy-based, en bloc PLND while adhering to fundamental oncologic principles. The anatomical concepts and technical strategies may facilitate reproducible surgical practice and may be applicable across multiple specialties in pelvic oncology.

articles.title: Impact of ARRIVE (A Randomized Trial of Induction versus Expectant Management) publication on severe maternal morbidity: national time-series analysis.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
articles.authors: Baucom AM, Miltenberger E, Czarny HN et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe maternal morbidity (SMM) has more than doubled in the United States over the past two decades. The ARRIVE trial (A Randomized Trial of Induction versus Expectant Management), published in August 2018, found that elective 39-week induction in low-risk nulliparous women reduced cesarean delivery rates and hypertensive disorders compared to expectant management. However, whether these trial benefits translate to population-level improvements in maternal safety remains unknown.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether publication of ARRIVE (A Randomized Trial of Induction versus Expectant Management) was associated with changes in SMM, induction of labor, and cesarean delivery rates among low-risk pregnant individuals in the United States.
STUDY DESIGN: We conducted a national interrupted time-series analysis using the Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project National Inpatient Sample from October 2015 to December 2021. We identified term (≥39-week), singleton, cephalic, low-risk delivery hospitalizations without prior cesarean. The intervention date was November 2018, after exclusion of a three-month dissemination period following ARRIVE publication. Primary outcomes were SMM excluding transfusion, SMM including transfusion, induction of labor, and cesarean delivery. Secondary outcomes included hypertensive disorders and SMM among individuals with hypertensive disorders. Outcomes were modeled using survey-weighted segmented Poisson regression to estimate immediate level changes and post-intervention slope changes, adjusted for maternal age, race and ethnicity, seasonality, COVID-19 pandemic effects, and temporal trends. Age-stratified analyses examined effect modification.
RESULTS: The cohort included 1,740,895 delivery hospitalizations representing 8,699,980 weighted deliveries. ARRIVE publication was not associated with immediate or slope changes in SMM (level change adjusted relative risk (aRR) 1.007, 95% CI 0.881-1.150; slope change aRR per month 1.001, 95% CI 0.995-1.008) or transfusion SMM (level change aRR 0.964, 95% CI 0.880-1.056; slope…
CONCLUSION: ARRIVE publication was associated with increased induction and initial cesarean decreases, but no detectable changes in SMM or hypertensive disorders. The divergence between changed practices and unchanged maternal safety outcomes highlights the complexity of translating trial evidence to population benefit and warrants careful monitoring of ARRIVE implementation and long-term maternal outcomes.

articles.title: Large Language Model-Based Clinical Decision Support Tool for Insulin Dosing in Gestational Diabetes: A Simulation Model.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
articles.authors: Murphy LM, Allshouse AA, Theilen LH et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUNDS: Gestational diabetes (GDM) is a major contributor to maternal and neonatal morbidity, healthcare costs and a growing healthcare burden for clinicians. Artificial intelligence (AI) applications are increasingly used in healthcare, but data are lacking on their use in GDM management.
OBJECTIVE: To demonstrate the proof of concept of utilizing a large language model (LLM) clinical decision support tool (CDST) in GDM care we conducted a study with an objective to compare ChatGPT management of insulin dependent GDM to clinician management. Our primary hypothesis was that ChatGPT would suggest starting insulin at a higher dose than the clinicians. Our secondary hypothesis was that clinician-prescribed doses would converge with the initially recommended ChatGPT dose by the first visit occurring more than 2 weeks after insulin initiation.
STUDY DESIGN: In a retrospective cohort of patients with insulin-dependent GDM, we compared a model using ChatGPT as a simulated CDST to traditional clinician-prescribed insulin. Gestational age (GA), weight, and glucose values were entered into ChatGPT with a request to create an initial insulin regimen, and subsequent log values were entered with a request to alter the regimen as appropriate. The primary outcome was total daily insulin dose (TDD) and the exposure was regimen source (ChatGPT vs clinician). We compared TDD at the initial visit and the first subsequent visit occurring 2 weeks after insulin initiation.
RESULTS: A total of 60 patients were included. The initial clinician TDD of insulin was 13.3 units lower than the ChatGPT recommendation (95% CI: 7.7-18.9, p < 0.001). At the first subsequent visit occurring 2 weeks after insulin initiation, clinicians increased their prescribed TDD by an average of 11.1 units (95%CI: 7.4-14.4, p< 0.001). At this subsequent time point clinician prescribed TDD was similar to the initial ChatGPT prescription (mean: [ChatGPT-CP]: 2.2 units (95%CI: -3.2-7.7), p=0.42), and concurrent visit (mean [ChatGPT-CP]: 1.6 units…
CONCLUSION: Clinicians initiate insulin at lower doses than recommended by ChatGPT. However, 2-3 weeks after insulin initiation, recommended doses were similar. These findings suggest the feasibility of prospective studies assessing the use of an AI-CDST in GDM management. This approach may complement clinicians as a co-management tool and expand access to earlier medical intervention, particularly in areas with limited access to high-risk obstetricians.

articles.title: Multiparameter continuous fetal monitoring for early detection of physiologic derangement in a lamb model of fetal surgery.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
articles.authors: Papastefan ST, Liesman DR, Zhou J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fetal echocardiography is the gold standard for intraoperative monitoring during fetal surgery but hinges on fetal bradycardia as the primary indicator for fetal distress. However, fetal bradycardia likely represents a terminal stage of physiologic decompensation when encountered in fetal surgery.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the relationship between fetal heart rate changes and fetal physiologic derangement during stressors relevant to fetal surgery and to assess the potential contribution of continuous multiparameter fetal monitoring in the early detection of fetal distress.
STUDY DESIGN: To challenge this hypothesis, we utilized a novel, integrated fetal monitoring probe to provide real-time core measurements of fetal oxygen saturation (SpO2), temperature, and FHR. Maternal (pre-placental) hypoxia, umbilical cord occlusion (post-placental hypoxia), and fetal hypothermia were induced to simulate clinically relevant perturbations in fetal surgery in a large animal model.
RESULTS: Fetal bradycardia (defined as FHR<110) most often occurred in the setting of FPD, with positive-predictive value of 100% for fetal hypoxia, 83.3% for acidosis, and 91.7% for hypercarbia. However, the negative-predictive value of bradycardia was 41.5% for hypoxia, 62.5% for acidosis, 37.2% for hypercarbia, and 37.8% for acidosis. Time from the onset of FPD to detection of FHR changes was significantly longer than fetal SpO2 changes in the case of pre-placental hypoxia. Distinct patterns of fetal SpO2 and FHR changes were present between pre-placental hypoxia, post-placental hypoxia, and fetal hypothermia that were detectable via multiparameter fetal monitoring probe tracings.
CONCLUSIONS: In conclusion, profound fetal hypoxia, acidosis, and hypothermia occur frequently in the absence of fetal bradycardia. The novel multiparameter continuous probe detected FHR changes with minimal latency after clinically relevant fetal hypoxic stressors.

articles.title: Severe maternal morbidity in patients with cardiovascular disease and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
articles.authors: Pullins MJ, Quist-Nelson J, Fuller M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) are independently associated with increased risk of severe maternal morbidity (SMM). While prior studies have characterized adverse pregnancy outcomes among patients with CVD, limited data have evaluated how the development of HDP influences non-transfusion SMM across specific cardiac subtypes, particularly through the postpartum period, in large contemporary U.S. cohorts.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the impact of HDP on non-transfusion SMM among patients with CVD during delivery and within 90 days postpartum.
STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study using the Premier Healthcare Database of pregnant patients ≥18 years delivering between 2015 and 2020. Patients without CVD were compared to those with six CVD subtypes present on admission (aortic, ischemic, congenital, pulmonary hypertension, cardiomyopathy, and valvular). The primary outcome was non-transfusion SMM during delivery hospitalization and within 90 days postpartum, stratified by CVD and HDP subtype (gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, and preeclampsia with severe features), estimated as covariate-adjusted predicted rates (%). Secondary outcomes included SMM subtypes, ICU admission, and all-cause readmission within 30 and 90 days, reported as crude rates and adjusted odds ratios (aORs).
RESULTS: Of 4,606,247 births, 18,771 (0.4%) had CVD, and 12.0% had HDP. HDP was associated with higher adjusted predicted non-transfusion SMM rates, independent of CVD, with increasing risk across HDP severity and marked heterogeneity by CVD subtype. Patients with CVD had consistently higher SMM across all HDP subtypes. The highest delivery hospitalization SMM rates occurred among patients with cardiomyopathy (25.6%) and pulmonary hypertension (33.2%) with preeclampsia with severe features; this pattern persisted through 90 days postpartum. Acute respiratory distress syndrome and mechanical ventilation were the most common SMM types during delivery, while heart failure/pulmonary edema predominated postpartum. Cardiomyopathy (aOR 9.02) and pulmonary hypertension (aOR 4.37) had the highest odds of ICU admission; readmission risk was also highest in pulmonary hypertension (30-day aOR 1.77; 90-day aOR 1.76) and cardiomyopathy (30-day aOR…
CONCLUSION: HDP significantly increases risk of non-transfusion SMM in patients with CVD, particularly in pulmonary hypertension and cardiomyopathy, and in those with preeclampsia with severe features.

articles.title: Reproductive Outcomes After Tubal Sterilization Reversal by Surgical Approach: A Systematic Review and Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Lemos MJ, Curi-Pesantes B, da Silva DBP et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare laparotomy, conventional laparoscopy, and robotic surgery, and separately evaluate open macrosurgical versus microsurgical reanastomosis.
DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched from inception through August 2026.
METHODS OF STUDY SELECTION: Comparative studies reporting reproductive outcomes after tubal reanastomosis for reversal of prior tubal sterilization were eligible. Two reviewers independently selected studies and extracted data. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I, certainty using GRADE, and confidence in network estimates using CINeMA.
TABULATION, INTEGRATION, AND RESULTS: Random-effects pairwise meta-analyses and an exploratory Bayesian network meta-analysis were performed. Thirteen nonrandomized studies were included, with 1,106 women represented in the baseline extraction; denominators varied by outcome. For overall pregnancy, laparotomy versus laparoscopy yielded a risk ratio (RR) of 0.89 (95% CI 0.68 to 1.16; 6 studies, 468 women). Pairwise analysis suggested fewer live births after laparotomy (RR 0.69; 95% CI 0.53 to 0.91; 4 studies, 310 women), but this association was sensitive to omission of individual studies. Network comparisons did not establish differences between approaches. Pairwise evidence was of very low certainty; confidence in network estimates was low to very low.
CONCLUSION: Available comparative evidence does not identify a reliably superior surgical approach. The studies were sparse, heterogeneous, and susceptible to confounding; clinically important benefits or harms remain possible. Prospective studies with standardized outcomes and adjustment for fertility predictors are needed.
REGISTRATION NUMBER: PROSPERO CRD420261481874.

articles.title: Using placental biomarkers to guide delivery in late preterm preeclampsia.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics and gynecology
articles.authors: Villalaín C, Peguero A, Delgado A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In women with late preterm preeclampsia without severe features, the optimal timing of delivery remains uncertain. Earlier delivery may reduce progression to severe maternal disease, whereas expectant management may limit neonatal morbidity related to late preterm birth. Because conventional clinical criteria have limited ability to predict short-term deterioration, angiogenic biomarkers may provide additional risk stratification. A randomized clinical trial showed that biomarker-guided timing of delivery reduced progression to preeclampsia with severe features; however, its effectiveness in routine clinical practice has not been established.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether angiogenic biomarker-guided timing of delivery, when implemented in routine clinical practice, was associated with lower progression to preeclampsia with severe features and to compare short-term neonatal outcomes between study periods.
STUDY DESIGN: Before-after cohort study at the two principal recruiting centers of the previous trial, including singleton pregnancies with preeclampsia without severe features between 34+0 and 36+6 weeks. Women managed expectantly from 2014 to 2017 were compared with women managed according to angiogenic biomarkers from 2022 to 2025. Delivery was recommended for an abnormal angiogenic profile, defined according to the center-specific protocol as PlGF <60 pg/mL in Center 1 or an sFlt-1/PlGF ratio >110 in Center 2. The primary maternal outcome was progression to preeclampsia with severe features. The coprimary neonatal outcome was composite neonatal morbidity, including respiratory distress, hypoglycemia, jaundice, 5-minute Apgar score <7, umbilical arterial pH <7.00, or neonatal admission. Confounding was addressed with propensity-score weighting and…
CONCLUSION: Angiogenic biomarker-guided delivery timing was associated with lower progression to preeclampsia with severe features, without earlier delivery at the cohort level. No between-period difference was observed in short-term neonatal morbidity excluding neonatal admission; because the study was not designed or powered to establish neonatal noninferiority, clinically important differences in neonatal morbidity could not be excluded. By supporting earlier delivery in women with an abnormal biomarker profile and continued surveillance in those with a reassuring profile, angiogenic testing may help individualize delivery-timing decisions in late preterm preeclampsia without severe features.

articles.title: Vaginal and Scrotal Rejuvenation and Adult Acquired Buried Penis: Nonsurgical Care and the Hidden Burden in Men With Obesity.
articles.authors: Arruda S, Khan AI, Chanani D et al.
articles.abstract: Vaginal and scrotal rejuvenation encompasses concerns about appearance, comfort, and sexual function, with substantial differences in anatomy and supporting evidence. We examine nonsurgical treatment mechanisms, clinical outcomes, and the dermatologic management of adult acquired buried penis in men with obesity. Selected clinical studies and professional guidance were examined, with attention to anatomic targets, study design, patient-reported outcomes, and follow-up. Established medical treatment and pelvic floor assessment address many vaginal and vulvar symptoms. Sham-controlled trials have generally not demonstrated additional benefit from vaginal carbon dioxide laser for menopausal symptoms. Evidence for external labial augmentation and regenerative procedures remains preliminary. Scrotal angiokeratomas provide a defined indication for laser or locally destructive treatment, whereas cosmetic botulinum toxin has limited clinical evidence and unresolved reproductive safety. In adult acquired buried penis, hygiene measures, treatment of inflammation, and obesity care may lessen signs and symptoms, but they cannot reliably correct fixed anatomic entrapment. Nonsurgical genital care requires a specific diagnosis and a defined outcome goal. Dermatologists may contribute through established medical care, appropriately selected office procedures, and timely gynecologic or urologic assessment when findings or anatomy exceed the scope of conservative treatment.

articles.title: In an age of expanding reproductive horizons, a deeper mechanistic understanding of myoma-related infertility is essential.
articles.authors: Donnez J, Dolmans MM
articles.abstract: Fibroids are the most commonly encountered benign tumours and their association with infertility has long been a source of controversy. Indeed, fibroids are increasingly observed in women seeking medical treatment for infertility due to extended reproductive horizons and the current trend for women to postpone childbearing. Growing numbers of studies and reviews are now highlighting the possible negative effects of fibroids on fertility and reproductive outcomes. The aim of this opinion paper is to provide an overview of mechanisms by which uterine fibroids could impair fertility, looking to open potential avenues for the development of targeted therapy.

articles.title: Prevalence of rare autosomal aneuploidies in pregnancies following assisted reproduction: a retrospective study.
articles.authors: Debeuckelaere A, Tsuiko O, Vancoillie L et al.
articles.abstract:
RESEARCH QUESTION: Is there a higher relative risk of rare autosomal aneuploidies in assisted reproductive technology (ART) pregnancies compared with naturally conceived pregnancies?
DESIGN: This retrospective study was undertaken at a tertiary IVF centre between 1 July 2017 and 5 December 2024 to determine whether ART increases the risk for aneuploid conception. All successive ART and naturally conceived pregnancies undergoing non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT) were examined. Pregnancies were stratified into preimplantation genetic testing (PGT) (n = 331) and non-PGT (n = 1179). The prevalence rates of common trisomies (21, 18, 13), monosomies, rare autosomal trisomies (RAT), and other chromosomal abnormalities were compared with nationwide Belgian NIPT data.
RESULTS: The prevalence of RAT in the ART population was less than 1% and comparable with the rate for the general obstetric population (P = 0.84). Detected RAT were suggestive of confined placental mosaicism, and none were associated with confirmed fetal abnormalities. No significant differences were observed for monosomies (P = 0.92) or other chromosomal abnormalities (P = 0.16). The borderline increase in common trisomies in the non-PGT group (P = 0.06) likely reflects higher maternal age.
CONCLUSION: The results indicate that ART pregnancies, regardless of the use of PGT for aneuploidy, do not carry increased risk of chromosomal abnormalities compared with naturally conceived pregnancies. Many abnormalities observed at the preimplantation stage appear to be eliminated during early development, and low-level mosaicism generally has limited clinical relevance once a pregnancy is established.

articles.title: Oral-transdermal versus oral oestrogen: outcomes and live birth predictive model for artificial cycle suboptimal endometrial response.
articles.authors: Song X, Zhu S, Li J et al.
articles.abstract:
RESEARCH QUESTION: In patients with suboptimal endometrial response during artificial cycle, do reproductive outcomes differ with the use of combined oral and transdermal oestrogen versus oral oestrogen alone?
DESIGN: Single-centre retrospective cohort of 1380 patients undergoing first single vitrified‒warmed blastocyst transfer (2017-2023) after oral oestrogen endometrial preparation. Suboptimal response was defined as endometrial thickness ≤8 mm on ultrasound after 10‒12 days. Patients then received either continued oral oestrogen or combined oral and transdermal oestrogen. After 1:1 propensity score matching, 395 patients per group were included. Logistic regression was adjusted for confounders. The primary outcome was live birth. Machine learning was used to develop and validate the LOTS model in the pre-matching oral and transdermal group (n = 653), with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve as the primary evaluation metric.
RESULTS: Unadjusted logistic regression analysis showed that the oral and transdermal group had significantly lower odds of preterm birth (OR 0.39, 95% CI 0.20 to 0.76, P = 0.006) and greater endometrial thickness before conversion (P < 0.001), with no significant differences in odds of biochemical pregnancy, clinical pregnancy or live birth. Adjusted regression analysis confirmed reduced odds of preterm birth (adjusted OR 0.44 95% CI 0.22 to 0.87, P = 0.018). The XGBoost algorithm, adopted in the LOTS model with all pre-specified baseline variables as predictors, showed acceptable performance for predicting live birth in the combined group, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.716 (95% CI 0.670 to 0.762) in the training cohort and 0.682 (95% CI 0.598 to 0.766) in the validation cohort.
CONCLUSIONS: For patients with suboptimal endometrial response, combined oral and transdermal oestrogen increases endometrial thickness and reduces preterm birth risk. The LOTS model supports individualized clinical management.

articles.title: Hypoxia reprograms tRNA cleavage toward 5'-halves in trophoblasts: convergent Glu-tRF enrichment in syncytiotrophoblast vesicles during preeclampsia.
articles.authors: Knyazev E, Antipenko I, Pirogov A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preeclampsia (PE) is characterized by placental ischaemia and a massive release of syncytiotrophoblast extracellular vesicles (STB-EVs). Transfer RNA-derived fragments (tRFs) form a substantial fraction of STB-EV RNA, but the mechanisms of their biogenesis and selective sorting under hypoxia remain unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To profile the tRF pool in placental tissue and STB-EVs in PE, alongside in vitro hypoxia in BeWo b30 cells, and to validate specific stress-induced tRFs.
METHODS: We re-analysed small RNA-seq from placental tissue and STB-EV fractions from normotensive and PE pregnancies, and from BeWo b30 treated with CoCl2 or a selective HIF-1α stabiliser (the oxyquinoline derivative neuradapt). Candidate tRFs were validated by RT-qPCR in cells and EVs.
RESULTS: In vitro hypoxia reprogrammed small RNA processing in trophoblasts: Dicer-dependent microRNAs decreased, angiogenin (ANG) was strongly induced, and 32-33-nt 5' tRNA halves accumulated. In clinical samples, PE was associated with compartment-specific tRF changes: placental tissue showed modest remodelling, whereas STB-EVs displayed increased 5'-halves and altered tRF cleavage positions. Specific glutamate tRFs (Glu-tRFs) were consistently enriched in STB-EVs. RT-qPCR confirmed that chemical hypoxia induces 32-33-nt Glu-tRF 5'-halves in cells and promotes their selective loading into EVs. Rank-based analysis indicated that Glu-tRF sorting into STB-EVs depends on fragment structural features and is associated with stress-induced changes in the RNA-binding protein YBX1.
CONCLUSION: Placental hypoxia triggers ANG-dependent biogenesis of 5' Glu-tRNA halves and their selective export in STB-EVs. The convergent fragments identified here, particularly 10_GluTTC_33 and 13_GluTTC_33, are promising non-invasive biomarkers of placental ischaemia and candidate paracrine effectors in PE.

articles.title: Novel ICT-based fluorescent probes for β-galactosidase detection and imaging in ovarian cancer cells.
articles.journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
articles.ta: Spectrochim Acta A Mol Biomol Spectrosc
articles.authors: Gao J, Cao J, Liang S et al.
articles.abstract: Two novel near-infrared (NIR) fluorescent probes, Nap-gal and Nap-TPA-gal, were rationally designed and synthesized for the rapid and sensitive detection of β-galactosidase (β-gal), a key biomarker of cellular senescence and ovarian cancer. Both probes adopt a modular design incorporating a naphthalimide fluorophore, a galactosyl recognition unit, and a linker. The introduction of a triphenylamine (TPA) unit in Nap-TPA-gal significantly enhances the intramolecular charge transfer (ICT) effect, as confirmed by density functional theory (DFT) calculations, resulting in a narrower HOMO-LUMO gap and red-shifted emission. Upon enzymatic cleavage of the galactosyl moiety by β-gal, both probes exhibit a pronounced "turn-on" fluorescence response. Nap-TPA-gal demonstrates superior performance, including a lower detection limit (0.144 U/mL), faster response kinetics (10-15 min), and excellent selectivity over various interferents. Molecular docking simulations reveal that Nap-TPA-gal adopts a more extended binding conformation within the active pocket of β-gal, forming multiple hydrogen bonds and π-π stacking interactions, which account for its higher binding affinity and catalytic efficiency. Moreover, Nap-TPA-gal was successfully applied to image endogenous β-gal activity in living SKOV-3 (ovarian cancer) cells, showing a strong fluorescence signal that was effectively suppressed by the inhibitor D-galactose. Collectively, Nap-TPA-gal represents a promising NIR fluorescent probe for real-time detection of β-gal in complex biological systems.

articles.title: Reproductive health practices and access to preconception care among women with epilepsy in Cameroon.
articles.authors: Njohjam MN, Nongse EM, Nji SS
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pregnancy is a critical period for women with epilepsy (WWE), which requires careful planning, preconception care, and specialized care. In many low-resource settings, access to reproductive health information and epilepsy-specific pregnancy care remains limited. This study aimed to assess knowledge, reproductive health practices, and access to preconception care among women with epilepsy in the North West of Cameroon.
METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study of WWE who had been pregnant at least once following epilepsy diagnosis. Using a structured questionnaire, we assessed sociodemographic characteristics, epilepsy history, contraceptive use, preconception counseling, pregnancy planning, antenatal care utilization, and knowledge regarding epilepsy and pregnancy.
RESULTS: We included 100 WWE participants with a mean age of 30.6 ± 8.8 years. The total number of pregnancies after epilepsy diagnosis was 245, with a mean number of 2.45 ± 1.65. Prior to pregnancy, 86% were not receiving follow-up care for epilepsy. Preconception counseling on the effects of epilepsy on pregnancy, the effects of pregnancy on epilepsy, and pregnancy-related precautions had never been received by 88%, 92%, and 92% of participants, respectively. Sixty percent reported unplanned pregnancies, while only 4% informed a healthcare provider before conception. During pregnancy, 52% were not followed by any healthcare professional.
CONCLUSIONS: There were substantial gaps in reproductive health knowledge, preconception counseling, and specialist pregnancy care among WWE in this study. Integration of epilepsy services into reproductive and maternal healthcare programs is urgently needed.

articles.title: Maternal exposure to lacosamide and zonisamide during pregnancy and risk of major congenital malformations: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Rehan ST, Looti AL, Ssentongo P et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Effective seizure control is critical during pregnancy but established first-line antiseizure medications (ASMs) carry variable teratogenic risks, and alternative options are needed. Newer ASMs like lacosamide and zonisamide are increasingly prescribed, yet their comparative safety regarding major congenital malformations (MCMs) remains incompletely characterized.
OBJECTIVES: To systematically evaluate and synthesize the risk of MCMs associated with maternal exposure to zonisamide or lacosamide monotherapy during pregnancy.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and ScienceDirect were searched from inception to January 2026. Data on MCMs were synthesized using random-effects meta-analysis of proportions for zonisamide and aggregate event rates for lacosamide.
RESULTS: Ten studies encompassing registry and observational cohorts met the inclusion criteria. The primary random effects meta-analysis of five registries with 303 patients demonstrated a pooled MCM rate for zonisamide of 1.3% (95% CI: 0.5-3.5%;I2 = 1.2%). Out of a total of 142 pregnancies exposed to lacosamide, there were zero reported cases of MCM. Thus, a conventional meta-analysis could not be performed. However, the pooled estimate based on the aggregate data was 0% (exact 95% CI 0.0-2.6%).
CONCLUSION: Current evidence on zonisamide and lacosamide in pregnancy is constrained by small numbers of exposed pregnancies and imprecise estimates. Although observed malformation rates were low, the data do not permit reliable exclusion of a clinically meaningful increase in risk. Further large, prospective registry data are required before the safety of these agents can be considered established.

articles.title: Determinants of discordance between spot urine protein-to-creatinine ratio and 24-hour proteinuria during pregnancy.
articles.authors: Geçici NA, Demir FN, Kayıkçı U
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of the spot urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR) for detecting significant proteinuria during pregnancy, investigate factors associated with diagnostic discordance between spot UPCR and 24-h urine protein measurement, and identify predictors of false-negative UPCR results.
STUDY DESIGN: This retrospective study included 145 pregnant women who underwent both spot UPCR and 24-h urine protein measurement during the same clinical evaluation. Patients were classified into four groups according to concordance between the two methods (true positive, true negative, false positive, and false negative).
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Diagnostic performance of spot UPCR was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Clinical and laboratory characteristics were compared between concordance groups, and multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify independent predictors of diagnostic discordance and false-negative UPCR results.
RESULTS: Spot UPCR showed moderate diagnostic performance for detecting significant proteinuria, with an AUC of 0.728, sensitivity of 57.1%, and specificity of 81.7%. Diagnostic discordance occurred in 29.0% of patients, with false-negative results accounting for most discordant cases. Among women with significant proteinuria confirmed by 24-h urine collection, 42.9% had UPCR values below the conventional diagnostic threshold. Urine sampling after 12:00 PM was independently associated with both diagnostic discordance and false-negative UPCR results.
CONCLUSIONS: Although spot UPCR provides a practical alternative to 24-h urine collection, its diagnostic performance was only moderate, with a substantial proportion of false-negative results. Spot UPCR should be interpreted alongside the clinical presentation, and urine collection timing should be considered when interpreting results and planning clinical management.

articles.title: Cognitive trajectories across the menopausal transition in women with multiple sclerosis: an exploratory longitudinal cohort study.
articles.authors: Bridge F, Sanfilippo PG, Darby D et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Women with multiple sclerosis (MS) may be disproportionately vulnerable to cognitive symptoms during menopause because cognitive impairment is common in MS and sex hormone fluctuations may influence cognition and MS disease activity. The impact of menopause on cognition in the MS population is unknown.
METHODS: Retrospective analysis of prospectively collected cognitive data from five Australian MS centers (2016-2026). Menopause status was determined through retrospective surveys (2018-2026). MSReactor cognitive assessments and Women's Health survey responses were linked with prospective clinical data from the MSBase registry. The primary analysis included 28 participants (336 assessments) and a secondary exploratory analysis included 50 participants (493 assessments). Linear mixed-effects models assessed changes in cognitive trajectories across visual attention, processing speed, and working memory using Simple Reaction Time (SIRT), Choice Reaction Time (CHRT), and One Back Test (OBK) tasks. Models examined changes in slope anchored at menopause (primary analysis) and age 50 (secondary analysis).
RESULTS: In the primary analysis, no evidence of a change in cognitive trajectory at menopause was observed (slope change: SIRT: β=10, 95% CI -14,34; CHRT: β=17, 95% CI -25,60; OBK: β=30, 95% CI -17,77). In the secondary analysis, CHRT and OBK showed evidence of a change in slope at age 50, with worsening reaction times before age 50 and relative stabilization thereafter (slope change: CHRT: β=-22, 95% CI -42,-2.7; OBK: β=-28, 95% CI -55,-0.91).
DISCUSSION: This exploratory study did not identify a change in cognitive trajectory associated with menopause. However, the small sample size and wide confidence intervals mean clinically relevant effects cannot be excluded.

articles.title: In-field vs. out-of-field recurrence after radiotherapy and outcomes of pembrolizumab combined with chemotherapy in recurrent cervical cancer.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Nakagawa S, Suzuki Y, Matsumoto S et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between recurrence patterns after prior radiotherapy and survival outcomes in patients with metastatic, persistent, or recurrent cervical cancer treated with pembrolizumab combined with chemotherapy.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study included patients with metastatic, persistent, or recurrent cervical cancer who received pembrolizumab combined with chemotherapy at our institution between September 2022 and September 2026. The primary analysis compared survival outcomes between patients with in-field and out-of-field recurrences after prior radiotherapy. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were used to evaluate the association between recurrence patterns and survival outcomes. For the sensitivity analysis, the cohort was stratified according to bevacizumab use, and progression-free survival and overall survival were compared between the recurrence groups within each subgroup.
RESULTS: Among the 84 patients treated with pembrolizumab combined with chemotherapy, 59 patients with a history of prior radiotherapy were included in the primary analysis. Of these, 13 (22 %) had in-field only recurrence, 19 (32 %) had both in-field and out-of-field recurrence, and 27 (46 %) had out-of-field only recurrence. In the multivariable Cox regression analyses, neither in-field only recurrence nor both in-field and out-of-field recurrence was significantly associated with overall survival or progression-free survival compared with out-of-field only recurrence. Additional Kaplan-Meier analyses stratified according to bevacizumab use showed no significant differences in survival outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with metastatic, persistent, or recurrent cervical cancer treated with pembrolizumab combined with chemotherapy, no statistically significant differences in progression-free survival or overall survival were detected between in-field and out-of-field recurrence after prior radiotherapy.

articles.title: Does fetal head station affect maternal and neonatal outcomes in second-stage cesarean delivery?
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Sokolik K, Matot R, Romano A et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between digitally assessed fetal head station (FHS) and outcomes of second-stage cesarean delivery (CD).
METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 418 term singleton second-stage CDs at a tertiary center (2012-2023). FHS was categorized as ≤ 0 or ≥+1 and was assessed before vacuum extraction when attempted. The maternal composite comprised vaginal push assistance, uterine incision extension, hemoglobin decrease > 3 g/dL, transfusion, endometritis, postpartum fever, or rehospitalization; the neonatal composite comprised 5-minute Apgar score < 7 or neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission. Complete-case models adjusted for maternal age, second-stage duration, and fetal head position, with and without failed vacuum.
RESULTS: FHS was ≤ 0 in 276 women and ≥+1 in 142; failed vacuum rates were 13.0 % and 50.7 %, respectively. Maternal composite rates were 71.0 % and 73.2 %; neonatal composite rates were 9.8 % and 16.9 %. With failed vacuum adjustment, adjusted odds ratios (95 % confidence intervals) for FHS ≥+1 were 1.15 (0.62-2.12) for the maternal composite and 1.21 (0.55-2.68) for the neonatal composite. Without failed vacuum adjustment, associations were observed for transfusion (2.46, 1.18-5.12) and cord pH < 7.2 (2.39, 1.19-4.82).
CONCLUSION: Digitally assessed FHS was not significantly associated with the assessed outcomes in full-cohort models including failed vacuum extraction. These findings suggest that the complexity and outcomes of second-stage CD may be influenced by multiple intrapartum factors beyond clinical assessment of FHS alone.

articles.title: Clinical significance of ovarian metastasis in gastric-type cervical adenocarcinoma: a retrospective study.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology : the journal of the Institute of Obstetrics and Gynaecology
articles.authors: Wang Z, Qiu J, Zeng Z et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gastric-type cervical adenocarcinoma (GCA) is a rare and aggressive subtype of cervical carcinoma characterised by a relatively high propensity for ovarian metastasis. Nevertheless, the risk factors, metastatic pathway and prognostic implications of ovarian metastasis in GCA remain poorly elucidated. This study aimed to characterise the clinicopathological profiles of GCA patients and clarify the clinical prognostic value of ovarian metastasis in GCA.
METHODS: Clinicopathological and follow-up data of 71 patients with GCA at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Centre from 2011 to 2023 were retrospectively analysed. The chi-square test and Kaplan-Meier's survival analysis were adopted to compare intergroup differences. Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to screen independent prognostic factors, while logistic regression analysis was performed to identify risk factors associated with ovarian metastasis.
RESULTS: In this cohort, 66.2% patients presented with FIGO stage III-IV disease. Histologically, most tumours were well-differentiated (43.8%) and exhibited low Ki-67 proliferation index (68.4%). The incidence of ovarian metastasis was 38.3% (23/60), among which 78.3% of cases presented with bilateral ovarian involvement and 52.2% were complicated by synchronous fallopian tube metastasis. Multivariate Cox regression confirmed that ovarian metastasis was an independent adverse prognostic factor for overall survival (OS) (HR = 4.144, 95% CI: 1.539-11.158, p = 0.005). Patients with ovarian metastasis had a significantly lower 3-year OS rate than those without metastasis (20.5% vs. 80.4%, p < 0.001). Furthermore, multivariate logistic regression identified uterine corpus invasion as an independent risk factor for ovarian metastasis in GCA patients (OR = 4.314, 95% CI: 1.264-14.726, p = 0.020).
CONCLUSIONS: Despite the typical well-differentiated histology and low proliferative activity, ovarian metastasis occurs frequently and is strongly correlated with poor survival outcomes. Uterine corpus invasion serves as a valuable predictive indicator for elevated ovarian metastasis risk in GCA, which can facilitate clinical risk stratification and individualised treatment decision-making.

articles.title: Global Reproductive Carrier Screening Guidelines: A Scoping Review.
articles.authors: Ellis E, Parobek CM, Spector A et al.
articles.abstract: Reproductive carrier screening (RCS) evaluates the risk of having a pregnancy with autosomal recessive or X-linked genetic diseases. However, professional organizations and governmental agencies often disagree on which diseases to include on RCS screening panels. In this scoping review, we evaluate the content and quality of worldwide RCS recommendations. We screened abstracts from Medline OVID, Web of Science, CINAHL, Embase, and PsycInfo for the following criteria: (1) RCS guidance document; (2) produced by governmental body or professional organization; and (3) published between January 1st, 2010 and November 24th, 2025. Two reviewers extracted, characterized, and evaluated recommendations with the AGREE II criteria. From 1851 citations, 54 documents were selected, predominantly from North American and European WHO regions. Documents were split between single-condition, targeted, and expanded carrier screening recommendations and focused on indications for RCS among preconception populations. Domain 5 ("Applicability") and Domain 3 ("Rigor of Development") had the lowest AGREE II scaled scores, at 23.7% and 30.3% respectively. This review highlights the inconsistencies among RCS guidelines, which likely contribute to observed disparities in what is offered by clinicians and healthcare systems. The poor methodological rigor of existing documents calls for a commitment to standardizing a framework for developing recommendations and promoting evidence-based care.

articles.title: The Global Landscape of Liquid Biopsy Technology in Oncology: From Biological Foundations to Commercial and Clinical Frontiers.
articles.authors: Tavakkoli Yaraki M
articles.abstract: Liquid biopsy has developed rapidly over the past decade and now contributes to several defined areas of oncology practice. Here, we offer an expert opinion on the biological foundations, technological platforms, clinical evidence base, commercial ecosystem and market trajectory of blood-based cancer diagnostics as of mid-2026. We critically evaluate the four principal circulating analytes, cell-free DNA (cfDNA) and its tumour-shed fraction circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA), circulating tumour cells (CTCs), extracellular vesicles (EVs) and tumour-educated platelets (TEPs), alongside the analytical platforms that extract clinically actionable signals from them, including high-sensitivity next-generation sequencing, digital droplet polymerase chain reaction, enzymatic and immunoprecipitation-based methylome profiling, genome-wide fragmentomics, long-read sequencing platforms and the increasingly central role of artificial intelligence in multi-omic signal integration. The principal prospective trials are appraised with attention to both their findings and their limitations, including DYNAMIC, TRACERx, IMvigor011, PATHFINDER 2, the National Health Service (NHS)-Galleri and ECLIPSE. The full spectrum of Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved companion diagnostics is reviewed in conjunction with the rapidly maturing startup ecosystem, which spans multi-cancer early detection, minimal residual disease monitoring and circulating-tumour-cell-based multi-omics, alongside the consolidating mergers and acquisitions landscape, with explicit reference to announcements made at the 2026 meetings of the American Society of Clinical Oncology and the American Association for Cancer Research. Non-plasma biofluid substrates including cerebrospinal fluid, urine, saliva and pleural fluid are also discussed for tumour-type-specific applications. The global liquid biopsy market, projected to grow from US$6.17 billion in 2024 to approximately US$22.69 billion by 2034, is analysed by technology, application and geography. We argue that, despite the technical progress documented herein, three structural barriers, namely reimbursement fragmentation, clonal-haematopoiesis-driven biological noise and the persistent absence of prospective mortality data for multi-cancer early detection, together with the fundamental biological limits on ctDNA shedding in low-shedding tumour types and in early-stage disease, must be resolved before liquid biopsy can be applied effectively at the…

articles.title: Serum IL-33/sST2 is associated with polymyositis/dermatomyositis complicated with interstitial lung disease.
articles.authors: Li W, Yang J, Lv Y et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate serum levels of interleukin-33 (IL-33) and soluble ST2 (sST2) in patients with polymyositis/dermatomyositis (PM/DM), and analyze their correlation with clinical indicators.
METHODS: Serum IL-33, sST2, and neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) marker cell-free DNA (cfDNA) were measured in 60 PM/DM patients and 20 healthy controls. The correlations between these indicators and their relationships with clinical data were analyzed. IL-33 expression in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) was detected by Western blot, and its effect on NETs formation was observed via high-content live-cell imaging.
RESULTS: PM/DM patients showed significantly elevated serum IL-33, sST2, and cfDNA levels compared with controls (all p < 0.01). ELISA-detected serum IL-33 levels showed no significant difference between PM/DM patients with and without ILD, while Western blot analysis revealed significantly higher IL-33 protein expression in PBMCs from the ILD group than from the non-ILD group. Of note, IL-33 expression at the cellular (PBMCs) level, but not serum IL-33, was associated with ILD in PM/DM patients. sST2 levels were also higher in PM/DM patients with ILD. IL-33 induced NETs formation in neutrophils. IL-33 and sST2 levels positively correlated with cfDNA and lung CT scores in PM/DM-ILD patients. Multiple linear regression identified IL-33, sST2, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) as independent factors for cfDNA. ROC analysis showed that the combination of sST2, ESR, and CRP yielded an AUC of 0.911 for diagnosing ILD, which was superior to any single indicator.
CONCLUSION: Elevated IL-33 and sST2 in PM/DM correlate with inflammation, muscle injury, ILD, and NETs formation, suggesting the IL-33/ST2 pathway may contribute to PM/DM-ILD pathogenesis by promoting NETs formation. Key Points • Serum IL-33 and sST2 levels are significantly elevated in PM/DM patients, and correlate with inflammation, muscle injury, and disease activity. • IL-33 promotes NETs formation in neutrophils, and serum cfDNA positively correlates with IL-33 and sST2, suggesting the IL-33/ST2 axis may contribute to PM/DM-ILD pathogenesis through inducing NETs. • sST2 has discriminative value for ILD in PM/DM, and its combination with ESR and CRP improves diagnostic accuracy (AUC = 0.911), supporting its potential as a clinical biomarker panel.

articles.title: Surveillance strategies for the early detection of malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors in neurofibromatosis type 1: a systematic review.
articles.authors: Damodharan S, Tonsgard J
articles.abstract: Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor (MPNST) is the leading cause of cancer-related death in neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1), with a lifetime risk of 8-15% and five-year survival below 50% in most series. Imaging surveillance, most often whole-body magnetic resonance imaging (WB-MRI), is offered on the premise that earlier detection of premalignant or early malignant lesions permits curative resection, but the supporting evidence has not been formally synthesized. Following the PRISMA 2020 statement, we searched MEDLINE, EMBASE, Cochrane CENTRAL, trial registries, and conference proceedings from 2000 to July 2026 for studies of structured surveillance or lesion characterization in people with NF1. Two reviewers screened and extracted data independently, risk of bias was assessed with design-specific tools, and certainty was graded with GRADE. Sixteen records were included: six surveillance-impact or natural-history cohorts, five imaging diagnostic-accuracy studies, two investigational cell-free DNA studies, and three contextual records (a guideline, a prognostic meta-analysis, and a registered protocol). Because the data were few and heterogeneous, no meta-analysis was possible and the primary objectives could not be addressed quantitatively. The only comparative incidence estimate came from one retrospective cohort compared with expected population-based rates. One retrospective imaging study traced 91% of MPNSTs to a pre-existing distinct nodular lesion. Diffusion-weighted MRI and FDG-PET discriminated benign from malignant tumors with high sensitivity in symptomatic referral cohorts, with threshold-dependent specificity. Harms were inconsistently reported. Certainty was very low for surveillance impact and harms and low for diagnostic accuracy. Current evidence is insufficient to establish whether surveillance improves outcomes; this review informs the design of prospective trials and the next revision of international surveillance guidelines.

articles.title: Women's experiences of gynaecological surveillance in Lynch syndrome.
articles.authors: Johnson JE, Dore M, Saso S et al.
articles.abstract: Gynaecological surveillance is offered in Lynch syndrome despite limited evidence for its clinical effectiveness. Invasive gynaecological investigations often cause pain and distress, but experiences vary and little is known about the psychological burden of repeated testing. We evaluated the lived experiences of annual gynaecological surveillance in women with and at risk of Lynch syndrome. Recruitment occurred via hospital clinics, social media, and Lynch Syndrome UK. Participants completed a semi-structured questionnaire by telephone. Quantitative data were summarised descriptively. Free-text responses were recorded verbatim, coded inductively and grouped thematically, with outputs reviewed by a second researcher. Overall, 104 women participated: 93 had confirmed Lynch syndrome and 11 had a strong family history of Lynch syndrome cancers (median age: 41 years). Median pain scores were 7/10 for outpatient hysteroscopy (IQR 6-9) and endometrial biopsy (IQR 6-10), versus 3/10 for pelvic examination and transvaginal ultrasound scan (both IQR 2-4). Among participants undergoing annual surveillance (75/104), 74 (98.6%) found surveillance reassuring, but 44 (58.6%) reported surveillance-related anxiety. 51 (68%) said they attended all scheduled surveillance visits. Free-text responses identified anticipatory procedural distress and cancer worry, particularly fear of adverse findings. Participants described surveillance as necessary given the limited non-surgical alternatives. Although regular gynaecological surveillance provides reassurance, it imposes considerable physical, psychological and practical burdens. Addressing this requires a dual approach: immediate optimisation of pain management and psychological support within current clinics, alongside a long-term shift toward non-invasive diagnostic innovations to fundamentally transform the healthcare experiences of high-risk cohorts.

articles.title: LINC01232 is associated with an unfavorable prognosis in cervical cancer and promotes malignant progression via miR-34a-5p.
articles.authors: Pang X, Luo Y, Liu M et al.
articles.abstract: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) have emerged as promising biomarkers and key regulators in the malignant progression of cancer. This study mainly delves into the clinical significance and the underlying mechanisms of LINC01232 in cervical cancer (CC). Differentially expressed lncRNAs (DElncRNAs) in CC were identified using the GSE167362 dataset. Tumor and adjacent non-cancerous tissues from 138 CC patients were collected, and LINC01232 expression was quantified by RT-qPCR. The Chi-square test linked clinical pathological parameters to LINC01232. Kaplan-Meier curves assessed its 5-year prognostic correlation, and Cox regression identified poor-outcome risk factors. Cell function (viability, apoptosis, migration, and invasion) was assessed via CCK-8, flow cytometry, and Transwell assays. EMT marker levels were measured by RT-qPCR and Western blot. DLR and RIP assays validated LncRNA or mRNA-miRNA binding. LNC01232 was upregulated 4.93-fold in the GSE167362 dataset. Both it and Histone deacetylase 1 (HDAC1) were overexpressed in tumor tissues and cell lines, while miR-34a-5p expression dropped notably. LINC01232 expression was notably associated with lymph node metastasis, advanced FIGO stage, and HPV positivity. Patients with high LINC01232 levels had worse prognoses, and it emerged as a risk factor for poor outcomes. Notably, miR-34a-5p directly targets LINC01232 and HDAC1. Inhibition of miR-34a-5p counteracted LINC01232 silencing-induced suppression of cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and EMT, while HDAC1 knockdown abolished the tumor suppressive effects of the miR-34a-5p mimic. LINC01232 is associated with poor prognosis in CC and may promote malignant phenotypes, potentially through miR-34a-5p/HDAC1 axis.

articles.title: Immunoblot analysis as a helpful adjunct to determine the time of a CMV infection in pregnancy.
articles.authors: Bissinger AL, Schmid L, Hoopmann M et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To evaluate the utility of immunoblot analysis for determining the timing of maternal CMV infection in pregnancy.
METHODS: Retrospective study including 151 pregnant women referred for suspected primary CMV infection or unclear serological results at the University Hospital Tübingen between July 2023 and November 2025. CMV-specific IgG, IgM, and IgG avidity were measured using standard chemiluminescence immunoassays (CLIA), and corresponding CMV immunoblot assays were performed. Associations between immunoblot band reactivity and CLIA IgG avidity, used as the reference test, were analyzed by Firth's penalized logistic regression. Detection and false-positive rates for identifying low IgG avidity (< 15%) were calculated for individual bands and their combinations.
RESULTS: With increasing IgG avidity, the probability of a positive reaction decreased for the IgM IE1 and p150 bands, the IgG IE1, CM2, and p65 bands, and the IgG avidity IE1 band, and increased for the IgG gB1 and gB2 bands and the IgG avidity p150 and gB2 bands. Among cases with low IgG avidity (< 15%; n = 56), absence of the IgG avidity gB2 band achieved the highest detection rate (92.9%) but at a false-positive rate of 54.7%. The lowest false-positive rate (1.1%) was observed when both the IgG gB1 and IgG avidity p150 bands were absent, at a detection rate of 23.2%. The presence of IgM IE1 or the absence of IgG gB1 detected 58.9% of low-avidity cases at a false-positive rate of 10.5%.
CONCLUSION: Immunoblot band patterns are systematically associated with CLIA IgG avidity and may serve as a helpful adjunct in determining the timing of a CMV infection in pregnancy.

articles.title: Autologous Fascia Lata Pubovaginal Sling Versus Synthetic Retropubic Midurethral Sling: A Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Vereeck S, Buckley VA, Kashyap AJ et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: Midurethral slings (MUS) and autologous pubovaginal slings (PVS) are treatment options for stress urinary incontinence (SUI). The aim of this study was to compare the outcomes of autologous fascia lata (FL) PVS and MUS.
METHODS: Cohort study of patients undergoing FL PVS or TVT MUS between 2018 and 2024. A retrospective medical record review and prospective standardised telephone interview in 2025 was performed. The primary outcome was subjective success, defined as Patient Global Impression of Improvement (PGI-I) score of 1 or 2. Secondary outcomes included Australian Pelvic Floor Questionnaire (APFQ) bladder score, recurrent SUI, de novo lower urinary tract symptoms, de novo dyspareunia, pelvic pain, complications, and reintervention. Multivariable logistic regression was used, adjusting for age, BMI, surgery type (primary vs recurrent), concomitant prolapse surgery, and follow-up duration.
RESULTS: A sling procedure was performed in 299 women, 107 were excluded (nonresponders), leaving 192 for analysis. Of those, 69 (35.9%) underwent FL PVS. Median follow-up was 24.5 (IQR 16.0-46.5) months. Mean age and median BMI were 60.3 (SD 13.3) years and 27.0 (IQR 25.0-31.0) kg/m2, respectively. Most patients reported subjective success, with no difference between groups (FL 73.9% vs TVT 78.0%, p = 0.516). While improvement in APFQ bladder score was significantly higher after FL PVS (p = 0.042), there was no significant difference in the number who reached the minimally important difference (FL 75.4% vs TVT 67.5%, p = 0.251). On multivariable logistic regression, there was no significant difference in the odds of PGI-I success, reintervention, or recurrent SUI between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Fascia lata pubovaginal sling and retropubic midurethral sling are associated with comparably high success rates for the treatment of SUI.

articles.title: Patient Versus Provider Priorities in Stress Urinary Incontinence Surgery: A Cross-Sectional Ranking Survey.
articles.authors: Manji I, Kani AS, Zhang WM et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: Informed consent for stress urinary incontinence (SUI) surgery requires clinicians to understand patient priorities. We hypothesized that clinically meaningful divergences would exist between patient and provider priorities, alongside specific points of agreement.
METHODS: Through two parallel cross-sectional surveys, we enrolled: (1) female patients with bothersome SUI at a single tertiary center; (2) members of the Canadian Society for Pelvic Medicine. Participants were asked to rank 16 surgical outcomes and complications. We generated consensus rankings using Borda Count analysis (N-1 scoring) and compared them between groups using Spearman's rank correlation and Fisher's exact test.
RESULTS: We obtained complete rankings from 25/34 patients (73.5%) and 28/40 providers (70.0%). Consensus hierarchies showed a moderate, significant correlation (rho = 0.543, p = 0.03). Divergences were bidirectional. Patients prioritized acute procedure-related injury to bladder, bowel, and nerves as top three. Providers agreed with bowel and nerve injury in top three but prioritized prolonged pain in second place. The largest divergence was for bladder infection, which was ranked significantly higher by patients than providers. Both groups ranked logistical factors, such as delay in return to daily activities, among the lowest. Minimum persistent pain difference influencing procedure preference did not differ, with approximately half of patients and providers expressing that 10% difference in pain outcomes would influence their choice (p = 0.318).
CONCLUSIONS: Patient and provider priorities are moderately aligned in SUI surgical informed consent discussions. Counseling could contextualize the risks patients may overestimate, validate common complications they fear, and proactively raise the long-term outcomes they may omit to appreciate.

articles.title: Outpatient Referral After Adolescent Sexual Health Emergency Department Visits Improves Follow-Up.
articles.journal: The Journal of adolescent health : official publication of the Society for Adolescent Medicine
articles.authors: Recto M, Mullins TLK, Zhang Y et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate which methods of outpatient referral during pediatric emergency department (ED) visits for sexual health are associated with increased follow-up among adolescents otherwise at risk of being lost to care.
METHODS: A single-institution retrospective cohort study was conducted among patients 14-20 years-old who underwent testing for any sexually transmitted infection during ED visits between 1/1/2018 and 12/31/2018 and were discharged home, excluding pregnant patients or those presenting following sexual assault. The primary outcome was any follow-up within 6 months of the index ED visit. The primary independent variable was referral at discharge. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to assess associations.
RESULTS: Among 1,152 patients (median age 17 years; 76% female), 73% received a referral, and 36.5% were seen in follow-up within 6 months of the index visit. Referrals specifying time frame for follow-up were associated with increased follow-up (odds ratio [OR] 5.9, 95% confidence interval [CI] 4.2-8.4), whereas "as needed" referrals were not. In multivariable modeling, attending a follow-up visit was associated with referral (adjusted OR [AOR] 3.6, 95% CI 2.5-5.2), female sex (2.74, 95% CI: 1.90-3.95), and prior preventive care (4.42, 95% CI: 3.36-5.81). Although associated with having follow-up visits, referrals were not associated with contraception initiation or decreased return to the ED within 6 months of the index visit.
DISCUSSION: Referral to outpatient care was associated with increased follow-up among adolescents with sexual health needs, particularly when referrals specified a follow-up time frame. Pediatric EDs should standardize discharge processes to include specific and consistent outpatient referrals.

articles.title: The Role of the cGAS-STING Pathway in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Systematic Review of Molecular Mechanisms and Therapeutic Implications.
articles.journal: American journal of reproductive immunology (New York, N.Y. : 1989)
articles.authors: Dehghanian A, Rasekh Jahromi A, Safavi Jahromi H et al.
articles.abstract: Polyendocrine metabolic syndrome (PMOS), previously and widely referred to as polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), is a common reproductive and metabolic disorder characterized by hyperandrogenism, mitochondrial dysfunction, and chronic low-grade inflammation. The cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) pathway may link mitochondrial injury to inflammatory responses in PCOS. We systematically searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science from inception to August 21, 2026, for studies investigating STING or the cGAS-STING pathway in women with PCOS or experimental PCOS models. Five studies published between 2021 and 2026 met the inclusion criteria. Human evidence demonstrated increased endometrial STING protein abundance in women with PCOS, while experimental studies consistently implicated mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) leakage and cGAS-STING activation in PCOS-associated inflammation. Hyperandrogenism-induced mitochondrial injury and permeability transition pore opening promoted mtDNA release, STING activation, granulosa-cell inflammation and apoptosis, and follicular dysfunction. Additional upstream mechanisms included gut microbiota-associated metabolic disruption and lead-induced SOD2 dysfunction. STING inhibition or knockout and interventions targeting mitochondrial homeostasis, including ketogenic diet, β-hydroxybutyrate, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, and SOD2 enhancement, attenuated inflammatory or PCOS-like phenotypes. Overall, STING may represent a molecular link between mitochondrial damage and inflammation in PCOS, although predominantly preclinical evidence warrants further clinical investigation.

articles.title: Molecular Diagnostics-Guided Immunosuppression Minimization to Belatacept Monotherapy in Kidney Transplant Recipients.
articles.authors: Salcedo-Betancourt JD, Feizpour C, Marsh M et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Minimally invasive molecular diagnostics, including donor-derived cell-free DNA (dd-cfDNA) and gene expression profiling, reliably distinguish immune quiescence from allograft injury; however, their utility in guiding immunosuppression minimization has not been fully evaluated.
METHODS: We conducted a 12-month prospective, single-arm observational proof of concept study to determine whether integration of dd-cfDNA (AlloSure), gene expression profiling (AlloMap), and conventional clinical biomarkers could facilitate immunosuppression reduction toward belatacept monotherapy in kidney transplant recipients. Adult recipients ≥9 months post-transplant receiving belatacept-based immunosuppression with stable renal function (eGFR >40 mL/min/1.73 m2), AlloSure ≤1%, and no donor-specific antibodies were enrolled. A three-month lead-in period confirmed immune quiescence prior to stepwise immunosuppression reduction.
RESULTS: Of 25 consented participants, 23 completed the lead-in period. Median dd-cfDNA remained <0.2% throughout follow-up, renal function remained stable, and no episodes of biopsy-proven acute rejection or de novo donor-specific antibodies occurred. One for-cause biopsy performed for transient creatinine elevation demonstrated no rejection. Overall, 52% of participants underwent immunosuppression reduction and 17% achieved belatacept monotherapy. Elevated AlloMap scores were the primary barrier to further reduction despite reassuring clinical and dd-cfDNA markers.
CONCLUSION: Molecular diagnostics-guided immunosuppression minimization was safe in carefully selected belatacept-treated kidney transplant recipients, supporting further evaluation of biomarker-guided strategies to individualize long-term immunosuppression.

articles.title: Knowledge and Counselling Gaps Among Women with Epilepsy: A Single-Centre Cross-sectional Study.
articles.authors: Alotaibi FG
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Effective care for women with epilepsy depends on structured counselling and informed decision-making covering drug-induced teratogenicity, periconceptional seizure control, the effects of uncontrolled seizures on maternal and fetal outcomes, folic acid supplementation, breastfeeding, and family planning. This study assessed knowledge of these domains among these women and examined its association with educational level and epilepsy duration.
METHODS: A single-centre, cross-sectional survey was conducted in the epilepsy clinics of King Khalid University Hospital, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, between November 2025 and February 2026. Consecutively attending women with epilepsy aged 15 years or older completed a self-administered, Arabic-language electronic questionnaire comprising 14 guideline-derived knowledge items, each corresponding to a counselling point considered essential to routine care. Responses to each knowledge item and their association with educational level and epilepsy duration were tested using the chi-square test.
RESULTS: Of 452 eligible women invited, 379 (83.8%) completed the survey. The largest proportion of participants, 49%, were aged 25-44 years; 68% had had epilepsy for 11 years or longer, and 97.6% were taking anti-seizure medications. Across the 14 knowledge items, 46.4% to 82.3% of participants responded "I don't know", indicating substantial knowledge gaps; uncertainty was greatest for the teratogenicity of anti-seizure medications, the safety of breastfeeding during treatment, and the effects of seizures during pregnancy on maternal and fetal health. Knowledge was significantly associated with educational level, being lower among women with general education or less.
