Participants with epilepsy duration of more than 15 years showed better knowledge in a few domains included the adverse effects of seizures on fetal health, the importance of close follow-up with an epileptologist during pregnancy, folic acid supplementation, breastfeeding and its safety during treatment, and family planning.
CONCLUSION: Substantial information gaps persist among women with epilepsy, indicating a need for structured, individualised counselling. Further studies are required to identify the factors underlying these gaps, including the content and frequency of counselling, consultation duration, and coordination of care between health care providers.

articles.title: Prenatal Genetics and Investigational in Utero Gene Therapy for Sickle Cell Disease: Clinical, Ethical, and Justice Considerations.
articles.authors: Massih AA, Riolini A, Rai S et al.
articles.abstract: Sickle cell disease (SCD) is a monogenic hemoglobinopathy with inequities in morbidity and care within and between countries. Prenatal somatic gene therapy is proposed but remains preclinical for SCD. This critical narrative review examines how such an intervention would interact with existing disparities and evaluates it in terms of autonomy, beneficence, non-maleficence, and justice. SCD differs from conditions for which fetal intervention is established: fetal hemoglobin is protective, clinical manifestations generally arise after its postnatal decline, and newborn screening permits early preventive care. A prenatal intervention must therefore demonstrate a material advantage over timely postnatal management while exposing neither the pregnant person nor fetus to disproportionate procedural or product risk. Intended somatic treatment is not equivalent to heritable genome editing or embryo selection, although off-target effects, mosaicism and unintended germline exposure require explicit investigation. There is currently no evidence that prenatal somatic gene therapy is cost-effective or would overcome access barriers. Its reliance on fetal medicine, molecular, and manufacturing infrastructure could initially widen disparities. Clinical translation would be ethically defensible only after disease-specific comparative evidence, independent oversight, non-directive consent, lifelong follow-up and a credible equitable-access plan. Strengthening newborn screening and proven care remains the immediate justice priority.

articles.title: Outcomes After Fetoscopic Myelomeningocele Repair With Preoperative BMI ≥ 35.
articles.authors: Burnett BA, Parobek CM, Johnson RM et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether preoperative BMI ≥ 35 kg/m2 is associated with preterm birth and adverse maternal outcomes following fetoscopic myelomeningocele (MMC) repair.
METHOD: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients undergoing fetoscopic MMC repair from 2014 to 2026. Patients with preoperative BMI ≥ 35 kg/m2 were compared with BMI < 35 kg/m2. The primary outcome was preterm birth before 37 weeks' gestation. Secondary outcomes included gestational age at delivery, maternal complications, and procedure-related risks. Comparisons were performed using bivariate analyses and multivariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: Among 209 patients, 21 (10%) had preoperative BMI ≥ 35 kg/m2. Rates of preterm birth before 37 weeks were similar in patients with BMI ≥ 35 versus < 35 kg/m2 (52% vs. 49%, p = 0.80), as was gestational age at delivery (35.9 vs. 37.0 weeks, p = 0.70). BMI ≥ 35 kg/m2 was not associated with preterm birth after multivariable adjustment (aOR 0.99, 95% CI 0.37-2.62). Skin-to-skin operative time, CO2 insufflation time, and total fetoscopic time were comparable between the groups. No differences were observed in the rates of PPROM, placental abruption, intraamniotic infection, or maternal perioperative complications.
CONCLUSIONS: Pre-operative BMI ≥ 35 kg/m2 was not associated with differences in preterm birth, gestational age at delivery, operative characteristics, or maternal perioperative morbidity following fetoscopic MMC repair.

articles.title: Neuroinflammation as a Unifying Mechanism in Major Psychiatric Disorders: From Molecular Pathways to Clinical Implications: A Systematic Search and Review.
articles.authors: Alammar MA
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine whether neuroinflammation can be understood as a unifying mechanism in major psychiatric disorders and summarized its molecular and clinical relevance. Major psychiatric disorders, including major depressive disorder (MDD), bipolar disorder (BD), and schizophrenia, are increasingly linked with immune dysregulation and inflammatory signaling. Neuroinflammation may help explain shared biological mechanisms across these disorders, but the available evidence remains diverse and clinically heterogeneous.
METHODS: This review followed PRISMA 2020 guidance. Electronic searches were conducted in PubMed, ScienceDirect, Cochrane Library, PubMed Central, and Embase for studies published between 2021 and 2026. Only English-language, human studies published between 2021 and 2026 were included. Studies had to address neuroinflammation or related neuroimmune mechanisms in depression, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, or psychosis. Methodological quality was assessed using design-specific appraisal tools.
RESULTS: All 2288 records were identified. 52 duplicates were removed; 2236 records were screened. Twenty-one full text reports were assessed for eligibility, and 15 studies were included in the final synthesis after exclusion of six full-text reports, including one study with high risk of bias. The included studies covered major depressive disorder, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, first-episode psychosis, perinatal depression, perimenopausal depression, and cross-diagnostic postmortem datasets. Across these studies, neuroinflammatory involvement was reported through altered cytokines, complement proteins, matrix metalloproteinases, kynurenine-pathway metabolites, immune-cell changes, viral immune associations, and transcriptomic immune pathways. Some intervention studies also showed that symptom improvement was accompanied by favorable changes in inflammatory measures.
CONCLUSION: The available evidence supports an important but heterogeneous role of neuroinflammation across major psychiatric disorders. Current findings suggest shared immune-related mechanisms, but no single biomarker is sufficient as a universal diagnostic marker. Larger and better-designed studies are needed to clarify clinical relevance and therapeutic potential.

articles.title: Fetal fraction in pregnancy loss reflects maternal-fetal physiologic integration: a prospective cohort study in the Copenhagen Pregnancy Loss Cohort.
articles.authors: Tummoszeit I, Banasik K, Bliddal S et al.
articles.abstract:
STUDY QUESTION: Can maternal biomarkers of maternal-fetal physiologic integration predict the fetal fraction of cell-free DNA in pregnancy loss?
SUMMARY ANSWER: Maternal organ system biomarkers, including cardiometabolic, hepatic, renal, and thyroid markers, substantially predict fetal fraction in pregnancy loss (Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristics Curve (AUC-ROC) 0.77-0.80), indicating that fetal fraction may reflect integrated maternal-fetal physiology.
WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY: Fetal fraction, which is the proportion of cell-free DNA in maternal plasma derived from the placenta, increases with gestational age and decreases with higher maternal BMI. Existing prediction models on fetal fraction rely mainly on demographics and placental hormones, and the contribution of broader maternal organ-system biomarkers remains unclear.
STUDY DESIGN SIZE DURATION: Prospective multi-center cohort study within the Copenhagen Pregnancy Loss study with development cohort (n = 992) from a tertiary university hospital and external validation cohorts from two secondary university hospitals (n = 275 and n = 241). Enrollment was from November 2020 to February 2023.
PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS SETTING METHODS: Women ≥18 years with confirmed intrauterine pregnancy loss before 22 weeks at three Danish university hospitals were included. Fetal fraction was estimated from cfDNA sequencing using SeqFF. Six clinical characteristics and 36 biochemistry measurements, selected to reflect physiological domains implicated in placentation including thyroid, renal, lipid, and inflammatory markers, were analyzed using Bayesian Hurdle lognormal regression and gradient boosting models with external validation.
MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE: In adjusted hurdle models, higher total thyroid hormone levels were associated with adequate fetal fraction (e.g. total triiodothyronine (TT3) Odds Ratio (OR) 2.76 (95% CI 1.31-5.87); total thyroxine (TT4) OR 2.42 (95% CI 1.43-4.29)), while higher levels of creatinine and uric acid were inversely associated (e.g. creatinine OR 0.39 (95% CI 0.17-0.91); uric acid OR 0.47 (95% CI 0.26-0.90)). The magnitude of fetal fraction was additionally associated with HDL cholesterol/total cholesterol ratio, uric acid, and creatinine. A gradient-boosting model achieved AUC-ROC 0.77 in internal cross-validation and 0.80/0.78 in external validation (two secondary university hospitals), with aspartate transaminase (AST)/alanine…
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: N/A.

articles.title: Does Child Marriage Mediate the Relationship Between Experiencing Pre-Marital Sexual Intercourse and the Discontinuation of Education or Employment?
articles.journal: International journal of sexual health : official journal of the World Association for Sexual Health
articles.authors: Islam MM
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: In low- and middle-income countries, girls are more likely than boys to drop out of school when they become sexually mature and particularly when they engage in or experience premarital sexual intercourse. This study aims to examine whether child marriage mediates the relationship between premarital sexual intercourse and the discontinuation of education or employment among women.
METHOD: Data on ever-married women aged 15-49 years were extracted from the Bangladesh Demographic and Health Survey 2022. Data were available for 13,778 ever-married women, enabling an assessment of whether they experienced premarital sexual intercourse and whether they continued their education or employment after marriage. The mediating effect of child marriage was examined by using the "mediate" command available in Stata software.
RESULTS: Overall, child marriage was significantly more prevalent among those who had sexual intercourse before marriage than among those who reported it after marriage (81% vs 59%). Approximately 81% of women who were engaged or experienced premarital sexual intercourse were married before the age of 18, and 17.02% reported that they continued their education or employment after marriage. Among the women who experienced sexual intercourse during or after marriage (n = 9,640), nearly 59% got married before the age of 18, and 16.72% of these women continued their education or employment after getting married.
CONCLUSIONS: Child marriage is a significant mediator in the relationship between premarital sexual intercourse and the cessation of education or employment. Premarital sexual intercourse substantially influences child marriage, which then affects cessation of education and employment. Since educational achievements for girls have broader positive effects, raising awareness of the impacts of child marriage, enhancing sexual health literacy, and improving access to contraception for adolescents are urgently needed.

articles.title: Age at menarche and osteoporosis: the China osteoporosis prevalence study.
articles.authors: Wang Y, Wang Z, Sun Q et al.
articles.abstract: Menarche marks the onset of high estrogen exposure, yet the relationship between age at menarche (AAM) and osteoporosis is not fully understood. This study aimed to investigate the associations of AAM with BMD, osteoporosis, and fractures across different age decades. In this cross-sectional study using data from the China Osteoporosis Prevalence Study (COPS), we examined the correlations between AAM and BMD at the FN, TH, and LS in women aged 20-29 to ≥70 yr. Peak bone mass was determined based on BMD trends across age groups. Among postmenopausal women, we also assessed the associations of AAM with osteoporosis, vertebral fractures, and clinical fractures within the past 5 yr. This cross-sectional analysis is exploratory and intended to generate hypotheses about the life-course association between AAM and bone health. Later AAM was associated with a cross-sectional pattern of peak bone mass estimates occurring in older age groups at the FN and TH; however, no significant difference in peak bone mass magnitude was observed between AAM groups. In postmenopausal women, later AAM correlated with lower BMD at the LS and TH, and higher odds of osteoporosis. No significant association with fractures was observed. Later AAM was associated with estimates of peak bone mass timing at older age groups at the FN and TH without altering its magnitude. In postmenopausal women, later AAM was associated with modestly lower LS and TH BMD and higher odds of osteoporosis. Therefore, earlier osteoporosis screening is warranted for these women after menopause, and BMD assessment should include sites beyond the FN.

articles.title: A Narrative Review of Intravesical OnabotulinumtoxinA for the Treatment of Overactive Bladder and Practical Implications for UK-Based Practice: Do Injection Distribution and Site Matter?
articles.authors: Stimler B, Attwell-Heap A, Stewart H
articles.abstract: Intravesical onabotulinumtoxinA (OnabotA) is an established third-line treatment for overactive bladder. UK practice typically delivers 100 units as 20 separate 0.5 mL detrusor injections, sparing the trigone; this technique was inherited from the trials that established the licensed dose, rather than shown to be the optimal way of delivering it. This narrative review considers what the current literature on injection number, distribution and depth means for UK outpatient practice, and whether the conventional technique remains the best-supported approach or whether alternative, simpler techniques could make the procedure quicker and more tolerable without loss of effectiveness. We conclude that total dose, rather than how it is distributed, appears to be the main determinant of clinical response, and we consider the practical implications of this for UK services, along with the gaps in the evidence that UK-generated research could address.

articles.title: Hypermethylation of HIST1H4F in Tao Brush Samples as a Complementary Biomarker for Triaging Patients at Risk of Endometrial Carcinoma.
articles.authors: Lu Q, Duan X, Huang Y et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Endometrial carcinoma (EC) is a prevalent gynecological malignancy with a favorable prognosis when diagnosed at an early stage; however, effective minimally invasive triage tools for symptomatic or clinically selected patients with suspected endometrial lesions remain lacking. This study aimed to evaluate the methylation level of HIST1H4F in endometrial brush samples as a potential complementary biomarker for triaging patients at risk of EC who may benefit from confirmatory hysteroscopy.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: We analyzed methylation profiles from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) databases to identify HIST1H4F as a candidate biomarker. Quantitative methylation-specific PCR (qMSP) was employed to detect HIST1H4F methylation in 121 endometrial tissue samples and 118 Tao brush samples. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using sensitivity, specificity, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC).
RESULTS: HIST1H4F methylation levels were significantly higher in EC tissues than in normal controls, with AUC values of 0.993 (TCGA) and 0.975 (GEO). Clinical validation confirmed significantly elevated HIST1H4F methylation in EC and precancerous lesions versus normal tissues (p < 0.001). In Tao brush samples, the sensitivity and specificity for EC detection were 84.00% and 88.64%, respectively (AUC = 0.907). For stage I EC, the AUC reached 0.922, suggesting potential diagnostic value for early-stage disease.
CONCLUSION: HIST1H4F hypermethylation is a promising complementary triage biomarker for EC and its precancerous lesions in symptomatic or clinically selected patients. When combined with Tao brush sampling, this biomarker offers a novel, minimally invasive triage strategy for identifying patients at risk of EC who may benefit from confirmatory hysteroscopy. However, as an exploratory validation study, further validation in larger, prospective cohorts is warranted.

articles.title: Development and Internal Validation of the Triglyceride-Glucose Index for Metabolic Syndrome in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.authors: Chen Y, Xiao F, Yan Y
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and metabolic syndrome (MetS) in Chinese women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), and to develop and internally assess a TyG-based model for concurrent MetS identification.
METHODS: A single-centre, retrospective, cross-sectional study included 317 women with PCOS diagnosed by the 2003 Rotterdam criteria. MetS was defined by the 2004 Chinese Diabetes Society criteria. The TyG index was calculated as Ln[fasting triglycerides (mg/dL) x fasting plasma glucose (mg/dL)/2]. Multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic spline and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyses were performed. A nomogram was constructed and internally assessed, and decision curve analysis explored its clinical utility. Models were developed and evaluated in one cohort, without external validation.
RESULTS: MetS was present in 74 of 317 participants (23.34%). The TyG index was independently associated with MetS (adjusted OR for each 1-unit increase 3.97, 95% CI 1.74-9.06), with a dose-response gradient across tertiles (P for trend < 0.001). Restricted cubic spline analysis indicated a non-linear association, with a threshold at a TyG index of 8.6; above this value the likelihood of MetS increased markedly (OR 5.87, 95% CI 2.10-16.36). The TyG index discriminated MetS better than triglycerides, fasting blood glucose or HOMA-IR (AUC 0.84 versus 0.75, 0.70 and 0.71). The optimal study-specific cutoff was 8.76, with a sensitivity of 93.2% and a specificity of 67.0%. A nomogram incorporating the TyG index, age and body mass index reached a concordance index of 0.87, and decision curve analysis indicated a positive net benefit across threshold probabilities of approximately 14% to 70%.
CONCLUSION: The TyG index was independently associated with the concurrent presence of MetS in Chinese women with PCOS and showed a non-linear, threshold-like pattern. Because the predictors overlap with components of the MetS definition and no external validation was available, the reported discrimination and study-specific cutoff should be regarded as exploratory rather than clinically established. External validation is required before routine use.

articles.title: Policy mechanism matters: state-level pharmacist prescriptive authority and contraception prescribing.
articles.authors: Strasser J, Luckenbill S, Griffin R et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: State policies that authorize pharmacists to prescribe contraception could make contraceptive care more accessible in the US. Over half of states have implemented such a policy, either via: collaborative practice agreement (most restrictive), standing order, statewide protocol, or prescriptive authority (least restrictive).
METHODS: We used national prescription claims to measure variation in pharmacist-prescribed contraception by state policy type and by pharmacy affiliation in the thirty-one states that had a relevant policy in place as of 2024.
RESULTS: We identified a total of 3447 pharmacists, or 3.3% of all retail pharmacists in the US, prescribing contraception. Pharmacists prescribing contraception were most commonly affiliated with Walmart (17.4%), CVS (15.7%), Rite Aid (10.1%), and Safeway (9.4%). States with prescriptive authority or statewide protocols had significantly higher rates of pharmacist-prescribed contraception (11.6% and 5.9% of retail pharmacists, respectively), compared with states with standing orders (1.0%) or collaborative practice agreements (2.3%).
CONCLUSION: This study found that the type of policy mechanism authorizing pharmacists to prescribe contraception plays a key role in determining uptake of this practice. State policies must be considered as part of a broader set of factors, including retail pharmacies' policies, pharmacist training, and reimbursement.

articles.title: Perinatal outcomes of minimally invasive fetal procedures for the treatment of sacrococcygeal teratoma: a systematic review.
articles.authors: Bartasevicius VT, Callado GY, das Chagas LA et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Sacrococcygeal teratomas are the most common fetal teratoma. When ultrasonographic parameters deteriorate at early gestational ages at which preterm delivery is not feasible, intrauterine treatment methods have been indicated. This study aimed to assess the perinatal outcomes of minimally invasive fetal procedures for the treatment of sacrococcygeal teratoma.
METHODS: This systematic review followed PRISMA guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251238039). We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL for studies published from January 2000 through November 2025, with four or more participants reporting minimally invasive intrauterine interventions for sacrococcygeal teratoma. The primary outcome was fetal death; secondary outcomes included perinatal mortality and preterm birth. Risk of bias was assessed using Downs and Black.
RESULTS: Five studies met inclusion criteria (three retrospective cohorts and two case series; n=4-22 participants) across six countries. Procedures included radiofrequency ablation, percutaneous and fetoscopic laser ablation, cyst aspiration, and shunting. Fetal hydrops and cardiac compromise were the main indications for intervention. Among studies with a comparator group, survival ranged from 40.0-75.0 % in intervention groups vs. 12.5-100 % in expectant management. Neonatal mortality reached 50.0 % in two studies, and preterm birth before 32 weeks occurred in 25.0-100 % of intervention cases across the five studies.
CONCLUSIONS: Minimally invasive fetal procedures are a feasible option for fetuses with sacrococcygeal teratoma complicated by hydrops or cardiac compromise, but the available evidence is limited to small retrospective studies subject to severity-based selection bias and does not allow conclusions regarding their effect on survival. Preterm birth was frequent after intervention.

articles.title: Atypical Presentation of Acute Groin Pain, Two Surgical Pathologies in One, Acute Appendicitis in an Amyand's Hernia.
articles.authors: Nassar M, Salem W, Devries M
articles.abstract: Amyand's hernia (AH), described as the presence of the appendix within an inguinal hernia sac, accounts for ~1% of groin hernias. Appendicitis within an AH is even rarer, posing challenges in diagnosis and management. We report the case of a 65-year-old female with a history of hypertension and prior hysterectomy who presented with 3 days of worsening abdominal pain. Computed tomography (CT) of the abdomen and pelvis demonstrated a right inguinal hernia containing an inflamed appendix with surrounding free fluid. The patient underwent open right inguinal hernia repair with laparoscopic appendectomy. Intraoperatively, the appendix was reduced from the hernia sac and found to be necrotic without perforation. The postoperative course was uncomplicated, and the patient was discharged on postoperative day one. She later underwent elective definitive bilateral inguinal hernia repair with mesh. Management of AH depends on the condition of the appendix and degree of contamination. In cases of complicated appendicitis, primary tissue repair is preferred to reduce the risk of mesh infection. This case highlights the feasibility of a staged approach in patients with appendicitis associated with AHs. Although rare, AH with appendicitis should be considered in patients presenting with groin hernias and abdominal pain and subsequently confirmed on CT. Individualized surgical management can lead to favorable outcomes.

articles.title: Projected clinical utility of polygenic risk score-stratified cancer screening: a systematic review.
articles.authors: Pascucci E, Lentini N, Russo L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer screening programmes apply uniform criteria irrespective of inherited risk. Polygenic risk scores (PRSs) have been proposed as a promising tool to stratify individual cancer risk and tailor screening strategies. However, whether PRS-informed strategies improve health outcomes compared with current practices remains uncertain. We aimed to synthesise the available evidence on the projected clinical utility of PRS-stratified cancer screening across six malignancies.
METHODS: We searched PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science from inception to March 15, 2026, for studies evaluating PRS-stratified screening for breast, colorectal, prostate, lung, gastric, or cervical cancer. Eligible outcomes included cancer-specific mortality, life-years gained (LYG), quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), overdiagnosis, and false-positive rates. Risk of bias was assessed using the ISPOR-AMCP-NPC questionnaire for modelling studies and ROBINS-I for observational studies. Certainty of evidence was appraised using the GRADE framework.
FINDINGS: Of 20,Simulated 100 million 058 records identified, 25 studies were included (22 decision-analytic modelling studies, 3 observational studies) covering five malignancies; no eligible studies were identified for cervical cancer. Modelled PRS-stratified strategies were projected to improve QALYs for breast, colorectal, gastric, and lung cancer, whereas results for prostate cancer were heterogeneous. Modelled mortality reductions were projected for colorectal, gastric, and lung cancer, although evidence for the latter two rested on single studies. For breast cancer, modelled mortality outcomes were inconsistent and dependent on comparator intensity. For prostate cancer, modelling studies primarily projected reductions in overdiagnosis rather than mortality improvement. Across all cancer sites, the absolute magnitude of incremental benefit over non-stratified screening was modest. Harms increased in high-risk groups receiving intensified surveillance. The certainty of evidence was rated very low for all outcomes across all cancer types, driven by serious risk of bias and very serious indirectness, reflecting limited transferability across populations and healthcare systems.
INTERPRETATION: PRS-stratified screening shows consistent but modest potential to improve the efficiency of cancer screening, particularly for…
FUNDING: This study was funded by the European Union under Grant Agreement No. 101183265 (Joint Action JANE-2).

articles.title: Spatial variation and associated factors of cervical cancer screening uptake among women aged 25-49 in Sub-Saharan Africa: a cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Alemu EA, Animut Y, Lakew AM
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cervical cancer is the third most common cancer in developing countries. In Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), it is the leading cause of cancer-related death among women. It is a late-onset disease with an incubation period of up to 20 years. This makes it preventable with early screening and treatment of precancerous lesions. However, the uptake of cervical cancer screening is very low in this region. Previous studies have not assessed the spatial variation in cervical cancer screening and there is limited evidence on associated factors.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the spatial variation and associated factors of cervical cancer screening uptake among women aged 25-49 in SSA, 2017-2023.
METHOD: A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted across 10 SSA countries between 2017 and 2023. A weighted sample of 75 360 participants was included in the analysis. Spatial analysis was performed on ArcGIS 10.7 to detect spatial autocorrelation and identify hotspot areas with a high proportion of cervical screening non-uptake. Spatial multilevel logistic regression was performed in R V.4.3 to identify associated factors of cervical cancer screening uptake.
RESULT: Cervical cancer screening uptake among 25-49 year-old women in the SSA region was 11.6% (95% CI 11.3% to 11.7%). The screening non-uptake was clustered (Global Moran's I=0.62). The hot spots in the 10 countries studied were located in most parts of Madagascar, Mauritania, Benin and Côte d'Ivoire. Age, educational status, employment status, wealth, marital status, sex of household head, media exposure, parity, HIV testing, health insurance, modern contraceptive use, early sexual initiation, multiple sexual partners and sub-region of SSA were statistically significant factors associated with cervical cancer screening uptake.
CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDATION: Cervical cancer screening uptake in the SSA region is low compared with the WHO target. It varies geographically in the SSA region. Therefore, stakeholders in the SSA region should implement spatially targeted interventions to enhance cervical cancer screening uptake. Individual and community-level factors were identified as associated with cervical cancer screening uptake.

articles.title: Building Demand for Human Papillomavirus (HPV) Vaccination in India: A Review of the Behavioural and Social Drivers of Parental and Community Acceptance.
articles.authors: Zanwar A, Sahni P, Arti A et al.
articles.abstract: India launched its National HPV Vaccination Campaign in February 2026, offering free, voluntary, single-dose vaccination to 14-year-old girls with parental consent. By September 2026, more than 80 lakh doses had been administered against an estimated annual cohort of about 1.2 crore girls, with wide variation across states. Because uptake depends on parental decisions, understanding what drives acceptance is now a programme priority rather than an academic question. This narrative review synthesises Indian evidence on parental and community acceptance of human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination, identified through a structured PubMed search and organised by the World Health Organization (WHO) Behavioural and Social Drivers (BeSD) framework, and considers how the shift to a free, nationally endorsed, single-dose programme changes the relevance of earlier findings. Indian studies consistently report low awareness, fears about safety and infertility, and concerns that the vaccine may encourage early sexual activity. Decisions are shaped by the wider family, with fathers and elders often having the final say, and by the recommendations of doctors and frontline workers. Most studies measure stated willingness rather than actual vaccination, and the evidence is concentrated in a few southern districts. Before 2026, cost was a dominant practical barrier; with free provision, the remaining practical barriers are mostly access, consent processes, and reaching girls outside school. The national campaign removes the cost barrier but not the belief-based and social barriers. Demand generation should prioritise equipping trusted health workers and teachers to recommend vaccination, engaging extended families and community leaders, pre-empting misinformation, and making consent and access easy. Standardised measurement of behavioural drivers, using tools such as the WHO BeSD surveys, should be built into campaign monitoring.

articles.title: Immune cell mediated fibrosis after kidney transplantation: mechanisms and emerging immunomodulatory therapies.
articles.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
articles.authors: Chen H, Chen X, Yan Y et al.
articles.abstract: Renal allograft fibrosis is a common histological endpoint after multiple injuries, rather than an independent disease entity. Despite modern immunosuppression, recurrent alloimmune injury, ischemia reperfusion injury, infection, donor and recipient related factors, and drug toxicity can converge on interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy. This review examines how innate and adaptive immune responses contribute to the transition from early graft injury to chronic remodeling, with particular emphasis on cellular plasticity and intercellular communication. Human single cell and spatial studies show that immune, tubular epithelial, endothelial, and stromal cells form heterogeneous, stage dependent networks rather than fixed pathogenic populations. We prioritize evidence from human kidney allografts while clearly identifying mechanisms inferred from experimental models. Established immunosuppression remains essential for preventing immune mediated graft injury, whereas regulatory T cell therapies, macrophage state modulation, cytokine blockade, and CD38 directed therapy remain investigational. None has been proven to reverse established allograft fibrosis. Future diagnosis and treatment should integrate Banff histology, donor specific antibodies, donor derived cell free DNA, urinary chemokines, and biopsy-based transcriptomics. Clinical trials should determine whether targeted immunomodulation can slow the progression of allograft fibrosis and preserve long-term graft function and survival.

articles.title: Association of Cervical Low-Risk HPV Infection with Ovarian Response and Early Embryo Outcomes in Women Aged ≥35 Years Undergoing a First IVF Cycle: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Song J, He Y, Hu X et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Low-risk human papillomavirus (LR-HPV) infection is highly prevalent in women of advanced reproductive age, yet its association with ovarian response and embryo quality during in vitro fertilization (IVF) remains unclear. This study is exploratory, with only 12 LR-HPV-positive patients included.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 145 infertile women aged ≥35 years undergoing their first IVF cycle (12 LR-HPV-positive, 133 LR-HPV-negative) after strict exclusion of high-risk HPV (HR-HPV). Ovarian stimulation parameters, oocyte yield and embryo outcomes were compared between groups. Non-parametric tests with bias-corrected and accelerated (BCa) bootstrap were used for unadjusted analysis. Quade rank-covariance analysis was applied to adjust for age and anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH). Three outcomes were prespecified as primary endpoints: number of retrieved oocytes, number of MII oocytes, and patient-level D3 high-quality embryo status. The binary primary endpoint was defined as the presence of at least one high-quality D3 embryo. For this binary endpoint, Firth logistic regression and E-value sensitivity analysis for unmeasured confounding were performed. Analyses for D5 blastocyst outcomes were unadjusted and underpowered. All primary statistical analyses were performed in R; annotated analysis code is provided as.
RESULTS: The LR-HPV positivity rate was 8.3% (95% CI: 4.3-14.2%). After Quade adjustment, the LR-HPV-positive group had fewer retrieved oocytes (F = 8.341, P = 0.004, partial η2 = 0.06) and fewer MII oocytes (F = 10.393, P = 0.002, partial η2 = 0.07). The median patient-level D3 high-quality embryo rate was lower in the LR-HPV-positive group (50.0% vs 79.9%, P = 0.031), and this difference remained present after Quade adjustment (F = 5.832, P = 0.017, partial η2 = 0.04). Firth logistic regression showed reduced odds of obtaining ≥1 high-quality D3 embryo (adjusted OR = 0.24, 95% CI 0.07-0.85, P = 0.027). The E-value for the point-estimate was 3.2, whereas the…
CONCLUSIONS: In this small single-center retrospective exploratory cohort, cervical LR-HPV positivity was associated with lower oocyte yield and reduced patient-level D3 high-quality embryo rate. No statistically detectable difference was observed for D5 blastocyst outcomes. These findings are hypothesis-generating and vulnerable to residual confounding and selection bias, and cannot support changes in clinical screening or intervention practice.

articles.title: Innate Immune Activation as a Shared BMI-Independent Pathway Linking Polycystic Ovary Syndrome and Obstructive Sleep Apnea: Distinct Myeloid Signatures and Suggestive Genetic Signals for EIF2AK2.
articles.authors: Cao Y, Li Z, Wen Q et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) exhibit a much higher prevalence of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) compared with those without PCOS. Moreover, PCOS women with OSA present poorer metabolic profiles, higher BMI, and greater psychiatric burden. In addition, OSA overlaps with PCOS in its associated comorbidity spectrum. Given that, shared elements were assumed underpin the pathogenesis of PCOS and OSA.
METHODS: Data from the UK Biobank and Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) databases were integrated and analyzed using bioinformatic approaches, single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) analysis, PCA, Firth's penalized logistic regression, interaction, mediation, and stratified analyses.
RESULTS: Innate immune activation was observed as a shared BMI-independent pathway linking PCOS and OSA. BMI appeared as a mediator, rather than an effect modifier, in the association between innate immune activation and the two disorders. Disease-specific immune divergence masked by elevated BMI was further observed: neutrophils showed positive associations with PCOS but not OSA, whereas monocytes were positively correlated with OSA but not PCOS. Suggestive genetic signals for EIF2AK2 were detected without robust statistical support from gene-based analyses. We proposed an evolutionary immunological hypothesis for the comorbidity of PCOS and OSA: ancient viral selective pressures might have shaped a hyperreactive innate immune baseline beneficial for ancestral survival, yet such adaptive traits could become maladaptive under modern lifestyles, potentially contributing to chronic low-grade inflammation and increasing PCOS and OSA susceptibility.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings might clarify the pathological correlation between PCOS and OSA and offer new insights to clinical preventive and therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Clonal hematopoiesis in solid tumors: mutant hematopoietic cells as a tumor-microenvironment component across source, lineage and treatment.
articles.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
articles.authors: Su H, Tang J, Li L
articles.abstract: Clonal hematopoiesis (CH) introduces a hematopoietic component into the molecular and immune landscape of solid tumors. Its interpretation depends on whether a variant is measured in blood, plasma or tumor tissue, which cells carry it, and when sampling occurs relative to treatment. Existing reviews have examined cancer-associated inflammation, therapy-related clonal selection and clinical outcomes; a less developed question is how these observations can be compared when they measure different aspects of the same clone. This focused narrative review connects source attribution with immune-cell state, tissue localization and longitudinal change, separating human associations from cellular localization and experimental perturbation. Paired leukocyte analysis can identify hematopoietic variants that would otherwise be assigned to cancer cells. Mutation-resolved tissue measurements add information about local immune interactions, whereas serial blood measurements help distinguish clonal selection from the relative prominence of CH when tumor-derived plasma DNA declines. Genotype-specific findings, particularly involving TET2 and myeloid function, provide mechanistic explanations for some treatment associations, but aggregate CH has shown inconsistent relationships with immune-checkpoint efficacy and toxicity. The resulting framework links each measurement to its appropriate biological or clinical use: source correction is already actionable, while treatment prediction and organ-specific risk assessment require evidence that CH adds information beyond established tumor and patient characteristics.

articles.title: Genetic insights into lipoprotein(a) lowering and reproductive and offspring health outcomes.
articles.authors: Hu S, Perez Alcantara M, Zhang L et al.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)]-lowering therapies are being investigated to reduce atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk. However, their implications on women's reproductive health are unknown, and pre-clinical models offer limited insight towards understanding such effects. We evaluated potential causal effects of genetically proxied Lp(a) lowering on reproductive and offspring health outcomes.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We analysed common and rare variants in the LPA region using two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR), genetic risk scores (GRSs), and gene-based tests. Additionally, performing individual-level analyses using UK Biobank and All of Us cohorts, with genome sequencing linked to biomarkers and electronic health records, we investigated outcomes spanning maternal health during pregnancy, labour and delivery complications, pregnancy outcomes, and congenital malformations in 236 228 UK Biobank and 122 038 All of Us women and recorded female infertility in 102 549 All of Us women. In summary-level analyses, no significant adverse associations of genetically predicted low Lp(a) with reproductive and offspring health outcomes were detected. Nominal associations were present across MR, GRS, and gene-based analyses, but no adverse reproductive findings survived the multiple-testing corrections. Confidence intervals for all fertility and reproductive-count estimates included the null. Controls showed expected associations for higher Lp(a) with LDL cholesterol (P = 2 × 10-19) and triglycerides (P = 4 × 10-9).
CONCLUSION: In summary, we found no robust or multiplicity-adjusted evidence of adverse reproductive or offspring health effects related to genetically proxied Lp(a) lowering. These findings provide genetic evidence relevant to assessing the reproductive and offspring health implications of targeting Lp(a).

articles.title: Modernizing reporting and communication of isolated echogenic intracardiac foci and choroid plexus cysts in the cell-free DNA era.
articles.authors: Oyelese Y, Wang M, O'Brien B et al.
articles.abstract: Echogenic intracardiac foci and choroid plexus cysts are among the most common findings on second-trimester prenatal ultrasound. Historically classified as "soft markers," they were incorporated into aneuploidy risk assessment in an era when screening relied on maternal age and serum analytes with limited performance. The widespread adoption of cell-free DNA (cfDNA) screening has fundamentally altered this paradigm. With detection rates exceeding 99% for trisomy 21, the modest likelihood ratios associated with isolated EIF and CPC no longer meaningfully alter post-test probability or clinical management. These findings are therefore best regarded as common normal variants rather than clinically significant markers of aneuploidy. Despite this transformation in prenatal screening, reporting and communication practices have changed little and remain highly variable, often influenced by historical practice patterns and medicolegal concerns rather than contemporary evidence. Numerous studies demonstrate that disclosure of isolated EIF and CPC may result in maternal anxiety, persistent concern despite reassurance, unnecessary diagnostic testing, and disruption of maternal-fetal bonding. These effects may be amplified by immediate patient access to ultrasound reports and terminology that continues to imply pathology where none exists. This review examines the historical and contemporary evidence supporting a modernized approach to the reporting and communication of isolated EIF and CPC in the era of cfDNA screening and proposes an evidence-based framework for clinical practice. In pregnancies with low-risk cfDNA results and a normal detailed fetal anatomic survey, isolated EIF and CPCs should be regarded as benign findings without clinical significance. Contemporary evidence no longer supports the routine reporting and communication of these findings in the context of aneuploidy risk. When disclosure occurs, communication should be non-alarmist, emphasize that these are normal variants, and avoid terminology suggesting increased risk for chromosomal abnormalities. Aligning reporting and communication with current evidence has the potential to reduce patient harm while promoting patient-centered prenatal care.

articles.title: An analysis of the mechanisms of phlegm-stasis and subthreshold lactate and lactate-modified levels in polycystic ovary syndrome, and research progress.
articles.authors: Cheng X, Zhang M, Sun C et al.
articles.abstract: Lactic acid, as a novel epigenetic regulator, participates in the regulation of gene transcription through lactylation. In the pathological context of PCOS, its core TCM pathogenesis-"the mutual entanglement of phlegm and blood stasis"-aligns closely with metabolic disorders and chronic low-grade inflammation in modern medicine. These conditions collectively drive the abnormal accumulation of lactate, which in turn acts as a substrate to drive lactylation, thereby continuously influencing the expression of genes related to ovarian granulosa cell function, follicular development, and endometrial receptivity. Abnormally accumulated lactate may not only represent the microscopic manifestation of "phlegm-dampness" but may also act as a signalling molecule that exacerbates the "blood stasis" state characterised by inflammation and tissue damage. Therefore, from the perspective of TCM's phlegm-blood stasis framework, it is essential to thoroughly investigate whether abnormalities in lactate metabolism and dysregulation of lactylation serve as common molecular nodes for key pathological processes in PCOS-such as insulin resistance (IR), chronic inflammation, and impaired follicular development. We also aim to explore the potential value of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) and integrated Chinese-Western medicine strategies-guided by the therapeutic principle of "resolving phlegm and removing stasis"-in targeting the lactate metabolic network, with the goal of providing molecular-level evidence and new insights for the prevention and treatment of PCOS through integrated Chinese-Western medicine.

articles.title: Laparoscopic versus robot-assisted radical prostatectomy: trifecta outcomes in prostate cancer surgery.
articles.authors: Nadeem F, Motiwala ZY, Misra S et al.
articles.abstract: The trifecta outcome in prostate cancer surgery is a core measure for the assessment of prostatectomy techniques which constitutes oncological control, preservation of urinary continence, and erectile function preservation. Interpretation of trifecta outcomes is complex due to variation in patient selection, definitions, and follow-up protocols. This study aims to compare LRP (laparoscopic radical prostatectomy) and RARP (robot-assisted radical prostatectomy) in the management of prostate cancer, especially trifecta outcomes. A literature search was conducted using PubMed, Embase, and CINAHL databases to identify studies relevant to the topic from 2005 to May 2025. Studies that compared RARP and LRP in prostate cancer patients and reported at least one of the trifecta outcomes were included in this narrative review. Functional outcomes, patient satisfaction, and cost-effectiveness were the different themes for which data was synthesized. Early outcomes in urinary incontinence and erectile function showed better recovery with RARP when compared to LRP, specifically within the first 12 months postoperatively. Within the two approaches, oncological outcomes such as positive surgical margin and biochemical recurrence were comparable. There was reduced postoperative pain, faster recovery, and higher satisfaction scores associated with RARP. However, there are significant barriers to adoption of RARP like high cost and limited access particularly in low- and middle-income countries. The choice between RARP and LRP should be individualized. Further research should focus on integrating AI, AR and ePROMSs to improve surgical care. RARP offers advantages in early functional recovery, while long-term oncological outcomes remain comparable between techniques.

articles.title: The 'Three-Groove and Two-Arc' technique for modified Thulium laser enucleation of the prostate: a retrospective study on efficacy and safety.
articles.authors: Chao W, Zhang J, Wang M et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate the efficacy, safety, and urinary continence outcomes of the 'Three-Groove and Two-Arc' modified ThuLEP technique for the treatment of large prostate.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 1,325 patients with benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) who underwent surgery at our center. Parameters were measured before and after the procedure: prostate-specific antigen (PSA), prostate volume, International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS), maximum flow rate (Qmax), and post-void residual urine (PVR). Additionally, enucleation time, morcellation time, operation time, catheterization time, and presence of transient urinary incontinence were recorded. Follow-up assessments of IPSS, Qmax, and PVR were conducted 1, 3, and 6 months after the operation.
RESULTS: The mean age of the patients was 73.2 ± 10.4 years. The mean prostate volume was 115.6 ± 24.5 mL, and the mean PSA was 3.8 ± 1.4 ng/mL. The mean preoperative IPSS was 28.5 ± 3.7, which decreased to 11.6 ± 2.8 at one month postoperatively. The mean preoperative PVR was 88.2 ± 43.5 mL, compared to 29.3 ± 12.3 mL at one month postoperatively. The mean enucleation time was 45.6 ± 9.2 min, and the mean morcellation time was 9.8 ± 2.1 min. Transient urinary incontinence was documented in 65 patients (4.9%).
CONCLUSION: The "Three-Groove and Two-Arc" technique showed a favorable safety profile and early functional outcomes in patients with large-volume BPH (>80 mL), with a low documented rate of transient urinary incontinence.

articles.title: Multi-platform social media use and trust, health beliefs, and HPV vaccination willingness among Chinese university students.
articles.authors: Pan H, Wu Z, Li M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination coverage among Chinese university students remains low despite effective vaccines and national elimination targets. How multi-channel social media shapes vaccination decisions in China's digital environment is not well understood. This study investigated determinants of HPV vaccination willingness among university students using the Health Belief Model (HBM), focusing on media exposure, trust, and gender-specific barriers.
METHODS: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 250 university students in Guangdong, China. The survey measured sociodemographic factors, HPV knowledge, HBM constructs (perceived susceptibility, severity, benefits, barriers), perceived vaccine safety, browsing and active search frequency on five social media platforms, trust in different information sources, and vaccination willingness. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression identified independent predictors. Gender-stratified analyses examined specific barriers.
RESULTS: Of the 250 students, 78.0% (195/250) expressed willingness to get the HPV vaccine. Greater HPV vaccination willingness was associated with being female (aOR = 10.24, 95% CI: 4.05-25.92), age 18-26 years (aOR = 4.83, 95% CI: 1.41-16.50), higher HPV knowledge (aOR = 1.18, 95% CI: 1.03-1.35), greater perceived vaccine safety (aOR = 4.50, 95% CI: 2.01-10.09), greater perceived susceptibility (aOR = 4.48, 95% CI: 2.08-9.64), and greater social media trust (aOR = 2.12, 95% CI: 1.20-3.75). Passive browsing and active information searching were not retained in the final multivariable model. Social media platforms (WeChat, Xiaohongshu, Weibo) were the most frequently used information channels but received the lowest trust ratings; healthcare providers were trusted most. Willing students reported higher browsing frequencies on WeChat, Xiaohongshu, and Weibo than unwilling students (p < 0.05), but these differences did not persist in the multivariate model. Male and female students had different barrier profiles: infertility myths were more common among males (14.7 vs. 4.5%, p <…
CONCLUSIONS: Social media was frequently used but received lower average trust than healthcare providers; social media use frequency was not independently associated with willingness. Instead of just putting more content on social media, efforts should focus on building knowledge, using trusted sources such as healthcare providers, and on correcting gender-specific misunderstandings.

articles.title: Long-term multisystem organ damage following hypertensive disorders of pregnancy across clinical risk subgroups: a UK Biobank study.
articles.authors: Hmimas M, Angarita-Fonseca A, Sharma A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) are associated with increased long-term cardiovascular, cerebrovascular, and renal risk, yet pathways linking HDP to later organ damage remain poorly understood. Persistent vascular dysfunction after HDP and subsequent cardiovascular risk factors may contribute to long-term hypertension-mediated organ damage (HMOD). We evaluated associations between HDP and long-term cerebral, cardiac, vascular, and renal HMOD across clinically relevant risk subgroups.
METHODS: In this UK Biobank matched cohort study, parous females with a history of HDP were matched 1:4 to females without HDP by age at first delivery and parity. HMOD was assessed using white matter hyperintensity volume, left ventricular ejection fraction, pulse wave arterial stiffness index, and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio. Multivariate linear regression models adjusted for cardiovascular risk factors assessed associations between HDP and each HMOD marker. Analyses were stratified by subsequent hypertension, menopausal status, age ≥50 years, antihypertensive medication use, and time since HDP ≥10 years.
RESULTS: Among participants (mean age 50 ± 7 years), HDP was not associated with white matter hyperintensity volume (β = -0.31, 95% CI -1.04 to 0.41, p = 0.401), left ventricular ejection fraction (β = 0.76, 95% CI -0.38 to 1.90, p = 0.193), pulse wave arterial stiffness index (β = 0.14, 95% CI -0.36 to 0.64, p = 0.595), or urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (β = -0.12, 95% CI -0.51 to 0.26, p = 0.535) after multivariate adjustment. Subgroup analyses revealed an isolated significant adjusted association with lower log-transformed white matter hyperintensity volume among participants with subsequent hypertension (β = -0.41, 95% CI -0.79 to -0.03, p = 0.033), while other associations were not consistently significant.
DISCUSSION: HDP was not consistently associated with selected measures of long-term subclinical HMOD across clinically relevant subgroups. Established long-term cardiovascular and renal risks following HDP may not be uniformly reflected by HMOD markers assessed at a single time point later in life. Future longitudinal studies using repeated assessments are needed to identify which HMOD phenotypes emerge following HDP and whether they predict or mediate subsequent cardiovascular, cerebrovascular, and renal outcomes.

articles.title: Plasmacytoid dendritic cells and M2 macrophages are associated with clinical outcomes in human papillomavirus-independent vulvar squamous cell carcinoma.
articles.authors: Peñuelas N, Sisuashvili L, Marimón L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vulvar squamous cell carcinoma (VSCC) is a rare malignancy comprising HPV-associated (HPV-A) and HPV-independent (HPV-I) subtypes. HPV-I is associated with high recurrence rates and poor survival, yet lacks validated prognostic biomarkers and therapeutic stratification tools. Although immunotherapy has transformed cancer care and highlighted the tumor microenvironment (TME) as an important determinant of clinical outcome, the rarity of VSCC has limited its molecular characterization, and the TME remains poorly understood. We therefore aimed to define the VSCC TME in an HPV-specific context and identify immune features associated with clinical outcomes.
METHODS: We analyzed 70 surgically treated VSCC (18 HPV-A and 52 HPV-I) using targeted transcriptomic profiling (HTG EdgeSeq). Immune and stromal cell composition was inferred by computational deconvolution, primarily with xCell and supported by EPIC, quanTIseq and MCPcounter. TME composition was compared by HPV status and, within HPV-I VSCC, by p53 and PD-L1 immunohistochemical status. Associations with recurrence-free and disease-specific survival were assessed using Firth-penalized Cox regression adjusted for FIGO stage and p53 status, and candidate populations were evaluated by CD123 and CD163 immunohistochemistry.
RESULTS: HPV-A tumors showed higher immune and overall microenvironment scores, with enrichment of diverse lymphoid and myeloid populations, whereas HPV-I tumors showed lower immune-cell enrichment. Within HPV-I VSCC, plasmacytoid dendritic cell (pDC) enrichment showed the most consistent association with favorable survival across deconvolution-based analyses, with immunohistochemistry confirming CD123+ cell infiltration as an independent favorable prognostic factor. PD-L1 positivity occurred in 44% of HPV-I tumors and was associated with CD163+ macrophage infiltration, which, in turn, was independently associated with poor outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: TME profiling identified two clinically relevant immune populations within HPV-I VSCC: CD123+ cell infiltration was associated with favorable outcomes, whereas CD163+ macrophage infiltration was associated with PD-L1 positivity and poorer outcomes. These findings provide a rationale for further investigation of the TME as a source of prognostic and potentially therapeutic biomarkers. Validation in larger, independent cohorts is required before clinical utility can be established.

articles.title: Response-equivalent dosing of follitropin alfa and follitropin delta in Japanese women: a cross-fitted retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Kobanawa M, Sato K
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To develop a Japanese population-specific empirical conversion between follitropin alfa IU and follitropin delta µg based on comparable ovarian response and to evaluate its response and clinical consistency.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort included 231 first cycles with follitropin alfa and 154 with follitropin delta. Overlap weighting balanced age, body weight, antral follicle count, anti-Müllerian hormone, basal FSH, and basal LH. Inverse response calibration incorporated oocyte yield, follicle-to-oocyte index (FOI), and follicular output rate (FORT). Five-fold cross-fitting assessed coefficient stability and held-out response equivalence. Follicular, endocrine, embryological, and reproductive outcomes were additionally compared at cross-fitted response-equivalent doses.
RESULTS: The conversion was follitropin delta (µg/day) = 4.581 + 0.02244 ×follitropin alfa (IU/day) (R2 = 0.704), corresponding to 7.95, 9.63, and 11.31 µg for 150, 225, and 300 IU. Fold-specific slopes ranged from 0.02144 to 0.02327 µg/IU. In held-out observations, FOI (difference -0.033; 90% CI, -0.097 to 0.031) and FORT (0.001; -0.097 to 0.100) met ±0.10 equivalence margins, whereas oocyte yield (-1.40; -2.65 to -0.15) did not meet the ±2-oocyte margin. Follicular, embryological, and cumulative reproductive outcomes were broadly consistent between preparations across response-equivalent dose levels.
CONCLUSION: This Japanese population-specific conversion was stable across cross-fitting and supported response equivalence for FOI and FORT. Clinical outcome analyses further supported the consistency of the proposed response-equivalent dose relationship.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://jrct.mhlw.go.jp/en-latest-detail/jRCT1031260453, This observational study was registered in the Japan Registry of Clinical Trials jRCT1031260453.

articles.title: Subclinical hypothyroidism, autoimmunity, and late obstetric outcomes: a population-based cohort study.
articles.authors: Eshkoli T, Elhayani Y, Fraenkel M et al.
articles.abstract: The 2026 American Thyroid Association guidelines no longer use thyroid-antibody status to guide levothyroxine treatment in subclinical hypothyroidism (SCH), yet the relevance of SCH and thyroid autoimmunity to obstetric outcomes beyond early pregnancy has rarely been examined at population scale. We evaluated the association between maternal thyroid function, thyroid autoimmunity, and a composite of late obstetric complications in a population-based cohort. We conducted a retrospective, population-based cohort study of 23,499 singleton pregnancies among Clalit Health Services members in Israel (2013-2022) with at least one gestational thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) measurement and documented thyroid-autoantibody testing; pregnancies with persistently suppressed TSH (maximum <0.4 mIU/L) were excluded. Pregnancies were classified by gestational TSH (euthyroid, maximum 0.4-4 mIU/L; SCH, mean ≥4 and maximum <10 mIU/L) and antibody status, yielding four groups, and assessed for a prespecified composite of 14 obstetric complications. Inverse-probability weighting (IPW) balanced baseline covariates, and rate ratios (RRs; ratio of mean complication counts) were estimated using IPW-weighted quasi-Poisson regression; "any complication" was analyzed as a secondary binary outcome. After weighting, neither SCH nor thyroid autoimmunity was associated with an increased rate of composite complications. Antibody-positive euthyroid women had a modestly lower composite rate than antibody-negative euthyroid women (RR 0.92; 95% CI 0.88-0.96), as did SCH antibody-positive women versus euthyroid antibody-negative women (RR 0.93; 95% CI 0.87-0.98), although the latter attenuated after additional adjustment for parity and obstetric history. Within SCH, antibody status was not associated with the composite (RR 0.99; 95% CI 0.88-1.11), a finding stable after adjustment for recorded levothyroxine treatment, and among antibody-negative women SCH was not associated with an increased composite rate (RR 0.93; 95% CI 0.87-0.99). Healthcare-utilization patterns were consistent with, but did not establish, a surveillance effect. In this clinically detected and managed cohort, we did not observe an increased burden of late composite obstetric complications associated with SCH or thyroid autoimmunity; the modestly lower rates observed in some comparisons may reflect surveillance, survivor effects or residual confounding. These findings are consistent with current TSH-guided,…

articles.title: DDX3X and DDX3Y in human reproduction and development: from molecular mechanisms to clinical implications.
articles.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
articles.authors: Chen Y, Liu H, Hu X et al.
articles.abstract: DDX3X and DDX3Y are paralogous DEAD-box RNA helicases on the human sex chromosomes that share over 90% sequence identity yet act in different tissues. They have been treated as two unrelated disease genes-DDX3Y an azoospermia factor, DDX3X a neurodevelopmental one-but here we read them as paralogs that share one RNA-regulatory activity, redeployed at successive points in reproduction and development. Their shared activity is the selective translation of structured transcripts, including G-quadruplex-bearing   5 '    leaders, organised within RNA-protein condensates whose material state the two paralogs set differently. We follow this activity across gametogenesis and early development: DDX3Y in the early male germline, where loss in complete AZFa deletion gives Sertoli cell only syndrome; maternal DDX3X through oocyte maturation, the oocyte-to-embryo transition, the placenta, and corticogenesis, where loss causes the DDX3X neurodevelopmental disorder. Which paralog becomes limiting in a given tissue reflects the local balance between them, set against a shared requirement to keep their combined output within a narrow range. The narrow, near-categorical male phenotype and the graded, multisystem female one may reflect this shared activity acting at different developmental moments. What the two phenotypes share is that activity, not a common causal lesion.

articles.title: Pathophysiological mechanisms and next-generation therapeutic opportunities in endometriosis.
articles.authors: Hou HT, Wu MH, Tsai SJ
articles.abstract: Endometriosis is a chronic, inflammatory, and heterogeneous disease affecting approximately 10% of women of reproductive age and is a major cause of pelvic pain and infertility. Despite its substantial clinical burden, diagnosis is frequently delayed, and current hormonal and surgical treatments remain non-curative, with recurrence and variable treatment responses being common. These clinical challenges reflect the complex and multifactorial nature of endometriosis, in which hormonal dysregulation, immune dysfunction, hypoxic and metabolic adaptation, and vascular remodeling interact to drive ectopic lesion establishment, persistence, and progression. This review integrates current understanding of the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying endometriosis pathogenesis. We discuss how enhanced adhesion and invasion facilitate lesion establishment, how dysregulated innate and adaptive immune responses impair the clearance of ectopic endometrial cells and sustain chronic inflammation, and how hypoxia-driven signaling and metabolic reprogramming promote lesion survival. We further examine the roles of aberrant steroid hormone signaling, angiogenesis, and lymphangiogenesis in lesion maintenance and progression, as well as how these interconnected processes contribute to lesion heterogeneity and treatment resistance. Finally, we highlight how emerging multi-omics approaches and patient-derived organoid and assembloid models may facilitate mechanistic validation, biomarker discovery, and therapeutic development. By connecting the mechanisms of lesion initiation and progression with current therapeutic limitations, this review provides a framework for developing more precise, mechanism-based diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Explainable machine learning models for endometriosis diagnosis: a retrospective development and validation study.
articles.authors: Chen L, Chen X
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to develop and validate machine learning (ML) models for diagnosing endometriosis based on common clinical characteristics, aiming to offer guidance for clinical screening and early diagnosis of endometriosis.
METHODS: We retrospectively collected data on female patients aged 18 years and older from a tertiary hospital in China. The data were randomly split into a training set and a validation set in a 7:3 ratio. Patients were divided into an endometriosis group and a non-endometriosis group. In the training set, nivariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent risk factors for endometriosis. (logistic regression [LR, a traditional statistical inference model with a linear baseline], random forest [RF, bagging ensemble of decision trees], support vector machine [SVM, radial-basis-function kernel], and XGBoost [gradient-boosted trees]) were constructed. These four algorithms were selected because they cover complementary learning paradigms, encompassing interpretable linear models and nonlinear ensemble methods.The optimal Youden index was used to select the cutoff probability, thereby determining the sensitivity and specificity of each model.
RESULTS: A total of 233 patients were included. Among them, 120 patients had endometriosis. Our analysis showed that a history of uterine fibroids, menopausal status, dysmenorrhea, white blood cell count, CA125, and CA199 were independent influencing factors for endometriosis. Results revealed that in the validation set, the AUC, sensitivity, and specificity were 0.878 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.793-0.962), 0.944, and 0.706 for LR; 0.878 (95% CI: 0.795-0.960), 0.694, and 0.912 for RF; 0.853 (95% CI: 0.764-0.941), 0.667, and 0.853 for SVM; 0.860 (95% CI: 0.777-0.943), 0.722, and 0.794 for XGBoost. The detection performance of the LR model was not significantly inferior to that of the other models.
CONCLUSION: Building ML models to detect endometriosis based on basic demographic information, clinical characteristics, and laboratory indicators is a feasible approach with desirable performance. The sample size in this study was limited, and internal validation was performed using a random split of the dataset. Therefore, caution is still warranted regarding the validation performance and interpretation of this model.

articles.title: Stress Biology, Vaginal Microbiome Dynamics, and Diagnostic Outcomes After Abnormal Cervical Cancer Screening: Protocol for a Digitally Enabled Multimodal Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Tossas K, Owens BD, Sayeed S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer risk is shaped by interacting psychosocial, biological, microbial, and clinical processes; however, few prospective studies integrate repeated biospecimens, ecological momentary assessment, wearable data, and electronic health record information within the same cohort. This gap is especially important in populations disproportionately affected by cervical cancer inequities.
OBJECTIVE: This paper describes the protocol and the current implementation of a digitally enabled prospective cohort study designed to examine how psychosocial stress, cortisol regulation, vaginal microbiome dynamics, human papillomavirus-related factors, and clinical follow-up jointly influence the resolution or persistence of abnormal cervical cancer screening findings at diagnostic evaluation.
METHODS: The study is recruiting women aged 21 to 65 years after an abnormal cervical cancer screening result and before diagnostic colposcopy. The target sample is 270 women (90 Latina, 90 non-Latina Black, and 90 non-Latina White). Study procedures include electronic health record-based prescreening; in-person consent and onboarding; baseline surveys; twice-daily ecological momentary assessment for 14 days; home salivary cortisol collection; passive Fitbit monitoring; retrieval of residual Pap (Papanicolaou) material from the index abnormal screen (T0); blood, urine, saliva, vaginal pH, and a self-collected vaginal swab at baseline (T1); and provider-collected vaginal and cervical sampling at follow-up colposcopy (T2). Data are integrated across Epic, REDCap, participant-facing digital tools, biospecimen workflows, and pathology-linked outcomes. The 2 coprimary confirmatory analyses use Firth bias-reduced logistic regression to estimate the adjusted odds of persistence associated with a standardized baseline 10-item Perceived Stress Scale score and a standardized participant-level mean diurnal cortisol slope, controlling for age, race or ethnicity, and index…
CONCLUSIONS: This prospective cohort study provides a protocol model for equity-focused, prospective cohort research to examine multilevel drivers of women's health. By integrating psychosocial, biological, digital, and clinical data across multiple time points, the study is positioned to inform both mechanistic research on pathways underlying the resolution or persistence of abnormal cervical cancer screening results and implementation strategies for complex, participant-centered longitudinal studies.

articles.title: Genetic Mutations and Fertility Challenges: from Acrosome Biogenesis to Assisted Reproductive Technologie, A Review.
articles.authors: Emami M, Tavalaee M, Naderi N et al.
articles.abstract: Acrosome biogenesis is a highly coordinated process of spermatid differentiation, involving Golgi-derived vesicle trafficking, endoplasmic reticulum-associated protein processing, acrosome-nucleus anchoring, manchette-dependent sperm-head shaping, acrosomal matrix maturation and acquisition of oocyte-activation competence. Disruption of these pathways may cause severe sperm-head abnormalities, including globozoospermia, teratozoospermia, impaired zona pellucida interaction, failed oocyte activation, and fertilization failure after conventional in vitro fertilization (IVF) or, in selected cases, intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI). This review summarizes available evidence on acrosomerelated genes and interprets their reproductive significance within a clinically oriented genotype-phenotype-assisted reproductive technology (ART) framework. Genes involved in endoplasmic reticulum (ER)/Golgi proteostasis and glycosylation, proacrosomal vesicle formation and fusion, acrosome-nucleus anchoring, acroplaxome-manchette integrity, acrosomal matrix function, and oocyte activation are reviewed according to developmental role, sperm phenotype, evidence level, predicted fertilization defect and potential ART implications. Particular emphasis is placed on clinically relevant genes, including DPY19L2, SPACA1, ACR, ACTL7A, ACTL9 and PLCZ1, which may differentially affect zona penetration, sperm-oocyte interaction, early embryo development or calcium oscillation-mediated oocyte activation. The review highlights that ART strategies should not be generalized across the acrosome-related defects. Although ICSI can bypass zona binding and penetration, it may not overcome oocyte-activation deficiency. Therefore, assisted oocyte activation (AOA) should be only considered in the selected cases, such as previous low or total fertilization failure, globozoospermia, abnormal PLCζ expression or localization, or variants strongly associated with activation failure. Integrating molecular diagnosis, sperm phenotype recognition, genetic counseling, evidence-based ART selection and long-term outcome monitoring may improve management of genetically determined male infertility.

articles.title: Physiologic subtypes of gestational glucose intolerance and risk of future maternal prediabetes or diabetes.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.authors: Selen DJ, Pant D, Thaweethai T et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gestational glucose intolerance (GGI), an abnormal initial gestational diabetes (GDM) screening test, conveys an increased risk of future diabetes, even when GDM is not present. We aimed to determine if GGI subtypes, classified according to the underlying mechanism of hyperglycemia, are at differential risk for future prediabetes or diabetes.
METHODS: We defined GGI as glucose loading test 1-hour glucose ≥ 140 mg/dL at > 22 weeks' gestation with a subsequent oral glucose tolerance test that did not meet criteria for GDM diagnosis. We applied homeostasis model assessment (HOMA-2) to fasting glucose and insulin at 16-20 weeks' gestation and classified pregnancies with GGI into subtypes based on whether they had insulin resistance (HOMA-2S <50th percentile), insulin deficiency (HOMA-2B <50th percentile), or both (mixed). We assessed the future risk of prediabetes/diabetes (HbA1c ≥ 5.7% at ≥ 3 months after delivery) in each GGI subtype, compared to pregnancies with normal glucose tolerance, using covariate-adjusted Cox proportional hazards models.
RESULTS: Of 747 pregnancies, there were 123 with GGI: 51.2% insulin resistant, 26.8% insulin deficient, 17.9% mixed, and 4.1% uncategorized. Over a median of 15.9 years of follow-up, 36.4% (N=272) developed prediabetes or diabetes. All GGI subtypes were associated with an increased risk of future prediabetes/diabetes compared to normal glucose tolerance controls: insulin resistant adjusted hazard ratio (aHR)=1.80 (95% confidence interval: 1.22-2.65, p=0.003), insulin deficient aHR=2.15 (1.35-3.42, p=0.001) and mixed aHR=2.07 (1.02-4.20, p=0.045).
CONCLUSIONS: GGI confers an increased risk of future maternal prediabetes/diabetes, regardless of the mechanism underlying glucose intolerance during pregnancy.

articles.title: Past, present and future of Estetrol (E4); a natural fetal estrogen for human use.
articles.authors: Coelingh Bennink HJT, Afors K, Douxfils J et al.
articles.abstract: Estetrol (E4) is a natural estrogen produced by the fetal liver with a distinctive pharmacologic profile separating it from other natural and synthetic estrogens. Encompassing 25 years of research and development, this review summarizes the history, biochemistry, pharmacology, clinical development, and potential future applications of E4. Essential features of E4 are (1) its high oral bioavailability, long half-life and minimal binding to sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG), enabling once-daily oral use, and (2) the limited effects on liver function, especially on hemostatic factors, resulting in a lower risk of venous thromboembolism compared to other natural and synthetic estrogens. Estetrol is further characterized as a natural estrogen with selective tissue activity, with a limited impact on breast tissue and cardiovascular and metabolic parameters, while preserving efficacy including bone mass protection. Estetrol therefore has the potential for a markedly improved safety profile. Clinically, the E4/drospirenone (DRSP) combined oral contraceptive (COC) is available worldwide since 2022 and provides effective contraception, a predictable bleeding profile, and a favorable tolerability profile. In phase 2 and 3 studies in postmenopausal women, oral E4 improves vasomotor symptoms, vaginal and urogenital complaints, and quality of life and wellbeing. Ongoing research is exploring wider uses, including combination with the oral GnRH antagonist relugolix for a COC with a focus on the perimenopausal transition and possible applications of E4 in gynecology, endocrinology, obstetrics, neurology and oncology, especially the treatment of advanced breast and prostate cancer.

articles.title: Clinical and Hormonal Factors Associated With Sperm Retrieval and the Role of Preoperative Medical Treatment in Non-Mosaic Klinefelter Syndrome Patients Undergoing Microdissection Testicular Sperm Extraction.
articles.authors: Turgut NE, Boynukalin K, Avci AE et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-mosaic Klinefelter syndrome (KS) is a major genetic cause of non-obstructive azoospermia, with testicular sperm extraction (TESE) serving as the principal option for biological paternity; however, factors associated with sperm retrieval (SR) and the benefit of preoperative medical treatment remain unclear.
OBJECTIVES: To identify clinical and hormonal factors associated with SR and evaluate the impact of preoperative medical treatment.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 227 non-mosaic KS patients undergoing first m-TESE between 2020 and 2025. Clinical, demographic, and hormonal variables were analyzed, and SR outcomes were compared according to the preoperative hormonal treatment with recombinant hCG and/or anastrozole. Associations with SR were assessed using prespecified multivariable logistic regression, inverse probability of treatment weights (IPTW)-based sensitivity analysis stratified by basal total testosterone (TT), and receiver operating characteristics (ROC) analysis.
