RESULTS: The overall SR rate was 48%. Treatment showed a nonsignificant increase in SR compared with no treatment (52.9% vs. 43.9%; p = 0.177). Among patients with basal TT <2.5 ng/mL, SR rates were similar in treated and untreated patients (48.6% vs. 47.7%; p = 0.914). Among patients with basal TT ≥ 2.5 ng/mL, SR was higher in those treated with anastrozole (62.5% vs. 39.7%; p = 0.038). However, the treatment-by-TT interaction was not significant (p = 0.116), and the IPTW analysis was limited by poor overlap between treated and untreated groups. In multivariable analysis, basal FSH (adjusted OR per 5 mIU/mL increase, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.82-0.99) and current smoking (p = 0.02) were independently associated with lower odds of SR. However, basal follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) showed limited discriminatory ability on ROC analysis (AUC = 0.584, 95% CI: 0.51-0.66; p = 0.029).
DISCUSSION: Basal FSH showed a modest association with SR, and current smoking was significantly associated with lower odds of SR, whereas preoperative medical treatment was not significantly associated with SR in non-mosaic KS.
CONCLUSION: Conventional clinical and hormonal factors, as well as preoperative medical treatment, showed limited associations with SR, indicating the need for more informative biomarkers.

articles.title: Single Versus Combined Standard Sperm Separation Techniques for Assisted Reproduction: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analyses.
articles.authors: Weber I, Barth G, Golbach R et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In assisted reproduction, different conventional sperm preparation techniques are in use in order to enhance the relative amount and quality of sperms in the specimen. Despite numerous experimental studies, there is no comprehensive evidence for the specific use of standard separation techniques.
OBJECTIVES: We aimed to examine the differences between pellet swim-up (P-SU), direct swim-up (D-SU), and discontinuous density gradient centrifugation (DGC), each compared to the combination of both (DGC/P-SU) in terms of total sperm count, sperm concentration, motility, morphology, DNA fragmentation, fertilization, pregnancy, and live birth rate.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: PubMed, Cochrane Library, Embase, and OSF Preprints were systematically searched. We included studies comparing the combination of DGC and SU in any order with at least one of the single separation techniques. Multi-level meta-analyses of the pre- and post-treatment differences were performed. Subsamples included motility classes, DNA fragmentation detection methods, baseline sperm quality, and prospective study design.
RESULTS: Fifteen studies (n > 1369 participants) were included. DGC/P-SU, DGC, and P-SU showed egal decreases of the sperm concentration. DGC/P-SU significantly increased progressively motile sperm compared to P-SU with an estimated difference of -4.5 percentage points (PP; 95% CI [-8.14; -0.86], p ≤ 0.015; n = 2 independent studies). DGC/P-SU also significantly increased normal morphology compared to P-SU with a difference of -5.3 PP (95% CI [-8.98; -1.62], p < 0.001; n = 3 independent studies), although a potential damaging effect cannot be excluded. In contrast, P-SU resulted in a significantly greater increase in rapid progressive motility than DGC/P-SU (difference 3.58 PP; 95% CI [2.15; 5.02], p < 0.001; n = 2 independent studies). Regarding DNA fragmentation, DGC/P-SU reduced it significantly more than DGC (difference 3.54 PP; 95% CI [0.82; 6.26], p = 0.01) and P-SU (difference 3.31 PP; 95% CI [0.21; 6.41], p = 0.04; n = 7 independent studies). Included studies reported no differences regarding the fertilization rate, pregnancy rate, and live birth rate.
DISCUSSION: This work could identify small differences of the techniques. Limiting factors were the limited…
CONCLUSION: Based on the present data, no robust clinical recommendations are possible yet. Further comparative research regarding the single sperm separation techniques and their combination is necessary.

articles.title: Functional Endocrine and Histological Characterization of Leydig Cell Micronodules in Infertile Men Undergoing Intratesticular Surgery.
articles.authors: Naiki T, Nozaki S, Naiki-Ito A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Leydig cell micronodules (LCM) are occasionally observed in testicular biopsies from infertile men, but their functional significance remains unclear.
OBJECTIVES: To characterize the endocrine, histological, and functional Leydig-cell phenotype associated with LCM.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 290 infertile men who underwent intratesticular surgery with biopsy at two Japanese institutions. Patients were classified as obstructive azoospermia (OA), non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA) without LCM, or LCM. Endocrine profiles, pathological findings, and exploratory follow-up for testicular germ cell tumors were assessed. Additional INSL3 immunohistochemistry was performed in LCM cases and randomly selected non-LCM cases stratified by Johnsen score.
RESULTS: The LCM group had smaller bilateral testicular volume, lower total testosterone, higher LH and FSH, and lower inhibin B than the OA and/or non-LCM groups. Free testosterone was reduced compared with OA. In the INSL3 subanalysis, LCM showed a lower TT/LH ratio and markedly reduced relative INSL3 intensity compared with Johnsen score-stratified non-LCM groups. Bayesian posterior predictive analysis supported that reduced INSL3 intensity in LCM was not explained solely by spermatogenic impairment.
DISCUSSION: LCM was associated with endocrine disruption involving both Leydig-cell and seminiferous tubular compartments.
CONCLUSION: LCM may represent a functionally altered Leydig-cell phenotype rather than an isolated tumor-risk lesion.

articles.title: Total Laparoscopic Hysterectomy in Solid-Organ Transplant Recipients: Single-Center Experience.
articles.journal: Experimental and clinical transplantation : official journal of the Middle East Society for Organ Transplantation
articles.authors: Özek MA, Akıllı H, Tunç M et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The safety of laparoscopic hysterectomy in solid-organ transplant recipients remains to be elucidated. Here, we analyzed the surgical outcomes of total laparoscopic hysterectomies in solid-organ transplant recipients. We compared results with total laparoscopic hysterectomy cases without history of organ transplant as control.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We included laparoscopic hysterectomies performed between January 2020 and December 2025. We divided our study cohort into 2 groups: (1) solid-organ transplant recipients and (2) control cases. We retrospectively analyzed and compared demographic characteristics, medical records, and intraoperative and postoperative outcomes.
RESULTS: We analyzed 5 solid-organ transplant recipients and 25 control cases. Two of the solid-organ transplant recipients had liver transplants. Mean age at operation, body mass index, and previous history of abdominal surgery were similar between the transplant group and the control group. Mean duration of laparoscopy was 130 minutes in the transplant group and 111 minutes in the control group (P = .363). The uterine volumes were not significantly different between the 2 groups (P=.865). Hemoglobin drop and length of hospital stay were also similar in the transplant and control groups. There were no cases of organ dysfunction or infectious complication in the transplant group.
CONCLUSIONS: Laparoscopic hysterectomy after abdominal solid-organ transplant generally seems safe, with some caveats. Care should be taken to avoid injury to the transplanted organ. When preoperative factors like body mass index, previous history of abdominal surgery, and uterine volume are similar, blood loss or increased length of hospital stay showed no increased risk to transplant recipients.

articles.title: Cost effectiveness of exome and chromosomal microarray analysis in cases of severe central nervous system structural anomalies.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Rosenberg-Friedman M, Maslovitz S, Dominsky O et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The central nervous system (CNS) is affected in 9% of fetal malformations but accounts for as much as one-third of all pregnancy terminations due to fetal anomaly. When applying chromosomal microarray (CMA) to the diagnosis of fetal CNS anomalies, the estimated diagnostic yield remains low. Recent study demonstrated that, in fetuses with major CNS anomalies, exome sequencing (ES) had an additional diagnostic yield of 44% over the 10% provided by CMA. We aimed to determine the cost effectiveness of the added value of ES in major CNS structural anomalies.
METHODS: We modeled costs, utility, and quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs) for CMA versus CMA + ES in prenatal testing. Two strategies were compared using the Markovian process decision analysis model: (1) CMA only, abnormal result culminating in termination of pregnancy (TOP); (2) ES after a negative CMA, where for positive result a TOP is conducted. The outcomes included health quality of life after TOP or having a disabled child, the costs of the CMA test, the ES test, and the health expenses of a disabled child. The time horizon of the model was 20 years. Sensitivity analysis including probabilistic sensitivity analysis of all parameters was conducted.
RESULTS: In the base-case model, the total expected cost per pregnancy was $US 91 059 for the CMA-alone strategy (driven largely by the expected long-term cost of raising a child with an undiagnosed disability) and $US 3101 for the CMA + ES strategy. The QALYs with a time horizon of 20 years were 11.84 and 13.84 for CMA and CMA + ES strategies, respectively, so CMA + ES dominated CMA alone (higher QALY value and cost saving). Sensitivity analysis revealed that the results were robust, and CMA + ES dominated the CMA with cost savings for all sensitivity analysis.
CONCLUSIONS: We suggest that ES has the potential to be cost effective and should be considered as a first-tier test in the prenatal diagnosis of major CNS anomalies. The substantial increase in diagnostic yield offered by ES not only provides valuable information for the current pregnancy but also holds significant relevance for future pregnancies. These findings are pivotal in facilitating timely and evidence-based decision-making.

articles.title: Increased Gross Umbilical Cord Abnormalities and Histologic Placenta Accreta Spectrum in Assisted Reproductive Technology Pregnancies: A Comparison With Spontaneous Conceptions.
articles.journal: Pediatric and developmental pathology : the official journal of the Society for Pediatric Pathology and the Paediatric Pathology Society
articles.authors: Felicelli C, Vadasz B, Goldstein JA et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Assisted reproductive technologies (ART) have revolutionized the management of infertility, providing a pathway to parenthood for millions of individuals. The affect of ART on placental pathology is poorly understood, as it may influence placental development leading to alterations in placental pathology and potentially affecting maternal and fetal outcomes. We aimed to assess how the pathologic findings in placentas from patients who underwent ART conception differ compared to non-ART conception.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis of ART versus non-ART placentas that underwent full pathologic examination was performed over a 4 year period. Pathologic reports from ART placentas were compared to non-ART placentas, with a focus on singleton gestation. Clinical and pathologic data was collected and compared between groups.
RESULTS: A total of 649 placentas were initially identified within both case cohorts. After case exclusions and sequestrations, 541 ART singleton placentas were compared to 568 non-ART placentas. Placentas from ART patients were smaller (P = .0202), had a higher rate of umbilical cord insertional abnormalities (P = .0135), were more likely to have accelerated villous maturation (P = .0295), and had higher rates of histologic Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS; P < .0001). The rates of maternal vascular malperfusion, fetal vascular malperfusion, and chronic inflammation were similar between groups.
CONCLUSION: Placentas that are the result of ART conception show significant pathologic differences from their non-ART counterparts, which have the potential to impact maternal and fetal outcomes. The risks associated with ART should be conveyed to patients to provide adequate counseling, especially in assessment for the risk of abnormal placentation.

articles.title: Cerebral redistribution in late-onset fetal growth restriction: relation between abnormalities of individual Doppler components and adverse outcomes.
articles.journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
articles.authors: Dall'Asta A, Valentini B, Sorrentino S et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Cerebral redistribution consists of the preferential redirection of the arterial and well-oxygenated blood flow to the fetal brain and is commonly associated with fetal growth restriction (FGR) secondary to placental insufficiency. In this study, we aimed to evaluate the perinatal outcomes of fetuses with late-onset FGR and cerebral redistribution, examining whether outcomes differed according to the normality or abnormality of the individual Doppler components that determine a reduction in the cerebroplacental ratio (CPR).
METHODS: This was a retrospective, multicenter cohort study conducted across four tertiary maternity units in Italy (University of Parma, Parma; Fondazione Policlinico Universitario 'A. Gemelli' IRCCS, Rome; IRCCS Materno Infantile Burlo Garofolo, Trieste; and University of Brescia, Brescia), including non-anomalous singleton pregnancies complicated by late-onset FGR associated with cerebral redistribution (defined as CPR < 5th percentile according to the Fetal Medicine Foundation reference charts). The study included cases collected at the four participating units between January 2019 and December 2024. Cases were categorized according to umbilical artery (UA) and middle cerebral artery (MCA) Doppler data (Group 1: normal UA-pulsatility index (PI) (≤ 95th percentile for gestational age) and MCA-PI (≥ 5th percentile); Group 2: abnormal UA-PI (> 95th percentile) and normal MCA-PI; Group 3: normal UA-PI and abnormal MCA-PI (< 5th percentile); and Group 4: abnormal UA-PI and MCA-PI), and perinatal outcomes were compared and evaluated using univariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses.
RESULTS: In total, 352 cases were included, of which 117 (33.2%) were assigned to Group 1, 84 (23.9%) to Group 2, 85 (24.1%) to Group 3 and 66 (18.8%) to Group 4. In the univariate logistic regression analysis, Group 4 showed…
CONCLUSIONS: In cases of late-onset FGR associated with cerebral redistribution, isolated abnormalities of the UA-PI or MCA-PI could not identify fetuses at increased risk of perinatal complications. However, the coexistence of both abnormal UA-PI and abnormal MCA-PI, indicating the highest extent of cerebral redistribution, was independently associated with perinatal complications including neonatal hypoglycemia and birth weight < 3rd percentile. In such cases, birth weight was also independently associated with perinatal complications. © 2026 International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology.

articles.title: 'I Had Been Told I Couldn't [Become a Parent]': Variations of Sex Characteristics and Intersex Family-Building Between Bodily and Reproductive Autonomy.
articles.authors: Crocetti D, Danon LM, Brink M
articles.abstract: Family building is widely understood as a socially meaningful aspiration and a dimension of human rights. For intersex people, or people born with variations of sex characteristics (VSC), pathways to parenthood may be impacted by sociomedical factors that extend beyond those experienced by endosex individuals with infertility. This article explores family-building experiences among adults with VSC by analysing how participants re-imagine reproductive futures in the context of medical power, informational gaps and restrictive reproductive citizenship regimes. Drawing on 64 qualitative interviews with people with VSC, partners and clinicians, alongside a review of reproductive policy frameworks, we examine how biomedical infrastructures, legal regulations and childhood medical experiences overlap with family-building experiences. By foregrounding themes of hermeneutical injustice, embodied agency and reproductive citizenship, this article investigates how participants navigate reproductive futures while mobilising peer expertise and family-building strategies. Ultimately, this paper argues for healthcare and policy frameworks that affirm bodily autonomy and ensure equitable family-building support for people with VSC.

articles.title: Data-driven clustering of atrophy patterns in Alzheimer's disease.
articles.authors: Winzell F, Raket LL, Overgaard NC et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To enable early detection and treatment of Alzheimer's disease, a better understanding of the heterogeneous disease progression is needed. Longitudinal MRI data has been utilized by previous studies to uncover patterns of brain atrophy. In this work, we aimed to improve upon previous methods by combining a continuous modeling of disease stages with a data-driven clustering algorithm.
METHODS: We developed an algorithm that primarily stages subjects on a continuous latent-time disease scale and subsequently finds clusters of atrophy patterns in a completely data-driven manner. The core of the algorithm is a set of non-linear mixed-effects models, which includes both subject-specific random effects and cluster-specific fixed effects. We applied our algorithm to longitudinal MRI data from the ADNI and OASIS databases and analyzed the found clusters rigorously by studying biomarkers, indicators of co-pathologies, and connections with previously established subtypes. We also utilized the BioFINDER-2 cohort as an independent validation dataset.
RESULTS: We found four clusters of longitudinal atrophy patterns; A: Progressive atrophy, B: Slow progression, C: Delayed atrophy and D: High atrophy. The D (High atrophy) exhibited higher amounts of atrophy, primarily in the typical regions affected in AD. The delayed atrophy group C remained relatively spared until the final stages of the disease, where we saw rapid neurodegeneration. The B (Slow progression) group displayed the least atrophy, and the A (Progressive atrophy) group showed a typical AD-like progression. However, the clusters could only be somewhat reproduced in perturbations of the discovery cohort. In the validation cohort, two clusters were found, which to a certain degree resembled some characteristics of the ADNI/OASIS clusters.
CONCLUSION: Our method combines a continuous disease staging model with a data-driven clustering algorithm, which mitigates some limitations of previous attempts at modeling brain atrophy patterns in Alzheimer's disease. We found four clusters of atrophy patterns, which expressed different clinical profiles. However, the clusters are likely mixes of previously found AD subtypes, and are produced from continuous progression patterns rather than discrete subtypes.

articles.title: Association between the ratio of serum uric acid to high-density lipoprotein cholesterol in early pregnancy and the incidence of gestational diabetes mellitus: a prospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Xiao M, Wu Z, Liu Z et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the ratio of uric acid (UA) to high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) (UHR) in early pregnancy and the risk of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), and to evaluate its potential predictive value as a risk indicator for early identification of GDM among pregnant women in Xinjiang.
METHODS: The prospective cohort study was conducted at the First Affiliated Hospital of Shihezi University from May 2022 to December 2024. A total of 1424 women with singleton pregnancies in the first trimester were enrolled from the Perinatal Clinic and Department of Obstetrics. A questionnaire survey was administered to collect basic information, and participants were followed up from the second trimester to the third trimester. Fasting venous blood samples were collected from all participants before 14 weeks of gestation to measure UA and HDL-C levels and calculate UHR. GDM was diagnosed based on the oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) performed at 24-28 weeks of gestation. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) model and multivariate logistic regression were used to analyze the dose-response relationship and the association between UHR and GDM. Subgroup analyses were conducted to explore the relationship within different subgroups. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to evaluate the predictive value of UHR for GDM.
RESULTS: The incidence of GDM in this study was 7.16%. The median UHR of pregnant women with GDM 15.88 (12.42, 19.36) was significantly higher than that of pregnant women without GDM 12.45 (10.17, 15.54) (p < 0. 001). The RCS model revealed a significant positive association between rising UHR levels and GDM risk (P for overall = 0.002). Multivariate logistic regression analysis revealed that women in the highest quartile (Q4) of UHR had a significantly increased probability of developing GDM compared with those in the lowest quartile (Q1) (OR = 3.717, 95% CI: 1.710 - 8.081, p = 0.001). The test for linear trend indicated a progressively increasing risk of GDM with higher first-trimester UHR levels (P for trend < 0.001). Subgroup analyses suggested that among…
CONCLUSION: Elevated first-trimester UHR was found to be independently associated with an increased risk of GDM in this cohort and may serve as a promising candidate biomarker for early risk prediction of GDM. Moreover, combining UHR with traditional risk factors may enhance predictive accuracy, supporting its potential utility in early GDM risk assessment.

articles.title: Association between toileting behaviors and overactive bladder symptoms among female university students in Lebanon and Armenia: a comparative study.
articles.authors: Darwich K, Affan R, Jarrouge G et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Overactive bladder (OAB) is a prevalent lower urinary tract symptom syndrome among young women, with potentially modifiable behavioral risk factors including toileting behaviors. This cross-sectional study investigated the association between toileting behaviors and OAB symptoms among female university students in Lebanon and Armenia.
METHODS: A total of 812 female university students (402 from Lebanon and 410 from Armenia) completed an online survey including the Toileting Behaviors-Women's Elimination Behaviors Scale (TB-WEB) and the 8-item Overactive Bladder Questionnaire (OAB-V8). Spearman correlation, chi-square tests, Mann-Whitney U tests, and descriptive statistics were used to analyze the data. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors independently associated with screening-positive for probable OAB symptoms. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05.
RESULTS: 52.5% of Lebanese and 39.0% of Armenian participants screened positive for probable OAB symptoms based on the OAB-V8 cutoff. Lebanese students had higher TB-WEB scores (49.26 ± 8.77 vs. 44.82 ± 6.50) and OAB scores (8.01 ± 4.16 vs. 7.02 ± 5.48) (both p < 0.001). Total TB-WEB scores were positively correlated with OAB scores in both Lebanon (ρ = 0.680, p < 0.001) and Armenia (ρ = 0.312, p < 0.001). Delayed voiding showed the strongest association with OAB in Lebanon (ρ = 0.687, p < 0.001), whereas premature voiding was significantly associated with OAB only in Armenia (ρ = 0.264, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Unhealthy toileting behaviors were significantly associated with OAB symptoms in both countries, with notable differences in behavioral patterns. These findings suggest that toileting behaviors may represent a potentially modifiable factor worth exploring in future interventional studies on bladder health in young women.

articles.title: Association between internet use and unmet need for family planning among currently pregnant women in Bangladesh: evidence from BDHS 2022.
articles.authors: Miah MS, Uddin MJ
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine the association between internet use and unmet need for family planning among currently pregnant women in Bangladesh and to assess disparities by residence, administrative division, and key socio-demographic characteristics.
METHODS: This study has used cross-sectional nationally representative Bangladesh Demographic and Health Survey (BDHS) 2022 data, including 4,370 currently pregnant women aged 15-49 years covering urban and rural areas of Bangladesh. Stepwise survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression models were estimated to evaluate the association between internet use and unmet need for family planning. Additionally, stratified analyses were performed by place of residence, administrative division, maternal age, age at first birth, maternal education, and media exposure.
RESULTS: Overall, 41% of currently pregnant women had an unmet need for family planning. Women who used the internet had 1.83 times higher odds of unmet need for family planning than women who did not use the internet (aOR = 1.83, 95% CI: 1.52-2.20). Stratified analyses showed stronger associations among women with an early age at first birth (10-17 years) (aOR = 2.70, 95% CI: 1.91-3.82), those aged 25-34 years (aOR = 2.41, 95% CI: 1.82-3.17), women with no formal education (aOR = 5.34, 95% CI: 1.70-16.71), and women residing in Barishal (aOR = 3.24, 95% CI: 1.99-5.28), Rajshahi (aOR = 3.30, 95% CI: 1.62-6.72), and Sylhet (aOR = 2.98, 95% CI: 1.96-4.53). Descriptive spatial analysis revealed geographic disparities in the prevalence of unmet need for family planning, with comparatively higher prevalence observed in Chattogram.
CONCLUSIONS: Internet use was significantly associated with a higher unmet need for family planning among currently pregnant women in Bangladesh. The association diverse across selected socio-demographic and regional subgroup. These findings may help inform the progress of targeted family planning programs for population groups with a higher burden of unmet need while providing evidence for future research on digital engagement and reproductive health.

articles.title: Fertility support needs of reproductive-age women based on the Kano model and ERG theory: a cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Wang G, Yang L, Tu A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Amidst the declining fertility rate and population aging, providing effective fertility supports for reproductive-age women is urgently needed. Hence, understanding their fertility support needs is paramount.
METHODS: An observational design was implemented and the STROBE Checklist was adhered to ensure the study's reporting met high-quality standards. The demographic characteristics questionnaire, fertility questionnaire and the questionnaire on fertility support needs based on Kano model and ERG theory were used. A convenience sample of 381 reproductive-age women was recruited from the First Affiliated Hospital of Hainan Medical University and Sanya Maternal and Child Healthcare Hospital in Hainan Province, China. The collected data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and the Kano model.
RESULTS: Among the 31 fertility support needs, 3 were classified as Indifferent attributes, 18 were classified as One-dimensional attributes, and 10 were classified as Attractive attributes. In the Predominance Zone, seven needs were identified, all of which belonged to the "Relatedness Needs" dimension and were classified as One-dimensional attributes. The Secondary Improving Zone contained one need from the "Existence Needs" dimension, which was classified as an Indifferent attribute. The Reserving Zone comprised 23 needs, including two classified as Indifferent attributes, 11 classified as One-dimensional attributes, and 10 classified as Attractive attributes. Based on the sensitivity index, the top five needs were Item 16, Item 11, Item 18, Item 19, and Item 15.
CONCLUSION: This study clarified the attributes of 31 distinct needs, analyzed their attribute distributions and sensitivity rankings. The findings offer evidence to support the development of more responsive and person-centred fertility support measures for reproductive-age women.

articles.title: U.S. preterm birth rates reduced nationwide, particularly among medically-induced deliveries, during the COVID-19 pandemic lockdown period.
articles.authors: Leal Hernandez ZP, Rejzek LC, Oliner J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: During the early months of the COVID-19 pandemic, many studies-particularly from wealthy nations-reported a drop in preterm birth rates. Our goal was to examine nationwide changes in U.S. preterm births in relation to a range of sociodemographic, perinatal conditions, and obstetric care factors.
METHODS: Using data from the publicly available natality files from the National Center for Health Statistics, we examined 25,767,850 observations of all U.S. registered singleton births during the months of April to June (i.e. early pandemic lockdown months) for the years 2015 to 2021. To control for seasonal shifts and focus on the early onset of the pandemic, we calculated average annual preterm birth rates (< 37 weeks gestation) between the months of April to June. We used these observed rates to generate predicted rates for 2020 and 2021, and stratified by sociodemographic and medical characteristics of interest.
RESULTS: The nationwide preterm birth rate has been increasing since 2015, but this trend was temporarily interrupted by a significant decrease in the early months of the pandemic. Preterm birth rates dropped for nearly everyone regardless of their sociodemographic characteristics. Additionally, there was a significant and steeper drop for late compared to early preterm births, for preterm home births compared to preterm hospital births, and significantly lower rates of preterm birth among those with induced births (c-section or vaginal). The average number of prenatal visits decreased in these months, and preterm birth rates significantly decreased among those with low (0-10) and average (11-15) number of prenatal visits. The decrease in preterm birth rates during this period was also accompanied by a decrease in fetal death rates, and decreases in neonatal and maternal intensive care admissions.
CONCLUSION: Our analyses indicate a potentially unintended interim health benefit of the pandemic across nearly all sociodemographic groups, with significant decreases particularly among induced preterm births. These findings, paired with reduced rates of fetal deaths and maternal and neonatal ICU admissions, suggest that in some cases, less intervention may have served as a benefit to reproductive outcomes. These results support the reduction in prenatal visits recommended by the 2025 national obstetric guidelines.

articles.title: Elevated classical soluble HLA class I molecules in breast cancer patients are associated with favorable disease outcome.
articles.authors: Tegeler CM, Rieth J, Koch A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: T cell recognition of human leukocyte antigen (HLA)-presented peptides plays a central role in immunosurveillance of malignant disease. Besides HLA molecules on cell surfaces, soluble HLA molecules (sHLA) are released in the blood and suggested to impact cellular immune responses.
METHODS: Here, we investigate classical sHLA class I (HLA-A, -B, -C) molecules in pretreatment serum from 191 patients, either with invasive breast cancer (BC, n = 140) or with ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS, n = 51), in relation to clinical parameters and survival with a follow-up time of up to 10 years.
RESULTS: Classical sHLA class I serum levels were significantly elevated in patients with DCIS and invasive BC compared to a healthy control cohort. sHLA levels did not differ across molecular subtypes or menopausal status. Of note, higher sHLA class I levels at time of diagnosis were associated with prolonged overall survival independent of age and metastatic status.
CONCLUSIONS: The findings of this study reveal first insights on classical sHLA class I molecules in BC patients suggesting an association of higher sHLA class I levels with favorable overall survival that warrants mechanistic investigation and identify sHLA as a potential candidate biomarker for further validation.

articles.title: Novel truncated variants in HFM1 cause ovarian dysfunction and female infertility.
articles.journal: Journal of assisted reproduction and genetics
articles.authors: Qiu S, Liu R, Gao H et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: HFM1 encodes a meiosis-related DNA helicase required for homologous recombination and crossover formation. HFM1 variants have been associated with POI and ovarian dysfunction, but their functional consequences remain incompletely characterized. This study aimed to identify pathogenic variants in two ovarian dysfunction patients with poor ART outcomes.
METHODS: Whole-exome sequencing and Sanger sequencing were performed to identify candidate variants and evaluate familial segregation. The identified variants were analyzed by in silico prediction and structural mapping. Wild-type and mutant HFM1 constructs were expressed in HeLa cells and mouse germinal vesicle oocytes to assess functional effects.
RESULTS: Two nearby truncated HFM1 variants were identified: HFM1 c.2899delA (p.Ile967Phefs*2) in a patient with diminished ovarian reserve and HFM1 c.2994T > G (p.Tyr998*) in a patient with premature ovarian insufficiency. Both variants were predicted to affect the C-terminal region of HFM1. Functional assays showed lower apparent molecular weights, reduced protein expression, and abnormal cytoplasmic localization of both mutant proteins in HeLa cells and mouse oocytes.
CONCLUSION: These findings support the deleterious effects of patient-derived HFM1 variants and suggest that C-terminal disruption of HFM1 may contribute to ovarian dysfunction and poor ART outcomes. These findings also expand the mutational spectrum of HFM1 associated with ovarian dysfunction.

articles.title: Placental abnormalities in congenital diaphragmatic hernia: A systematic review of experimental and clinical studies.
articles.authors: Pistone M, Antounians L, Lauriti G et al.
articles.abstract: The placenta is essential for fetal organ development, and its dysfunction is implicated in several congenital anomalies. However, little is known about the status and role of the placenta in congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). Herein, we aimed to define the incidence of placental abnormalities in CDH and characterize gross morphology, histology, molecular pathways, and vascular function. Using a predefined search strategy, we performed a systematic review following PRISMA guidelines. Human and animal studies reporting on placental and/or umbilical cord abnormalities in CDH were analyzed. Of 2,820 records identified, 14 articles were included. Human studies reported no consistent macroscopic placental phenotype. Cord abnormalities included hypercoiling, abnormal insertion, and single umbilical artery. Fetal vascular malperfusion, thrombotic lesions, and chronic inflammation were reported at histology. Ex-vivo CDH fetoplacental arteries showed impaired function with excessive constriction and inadequate relaxation. Animal studies reported reduced placental weight, trophoblast injury and apoptosis, and altered retinoid metabolism. Despite extensive literature on CDH, the status of the placenta remains understudied. Available evidence indicates that CDH is associated with abnormalities involving fetal placental vascular pathology. Studies using standardized assessment are needed to define the role of the placenta in CDH and correlate its status with disease severity and neonatal outcomes.

articles.title: TRIM22 promotes cervical cancer lymph node metastasis through Wnt/β-catenin-associated invasion and lymphangiogenesis.
articles.authors: Shao C, Wen W, Zhan Y et al.
articles.abstract: Lymph node metastasis is a major determinant of recurrence and survival in cervical cancer, but the molecular mechanisms linking tumor-cell invasion to lymphangiogenic remodeling remain incompletely understood. We investigated the role of tripartite motif-containing 22 (TRIM22) in cervical cancer lymph node metastasis. TRIM22 expression was examined in cervical cancer cell models with high lymph node metastatic potential and clinical specimens from 280 patients with early-stage cervical cancer. TRIM22 was upregulated in highly metastatic cells and lymph node-positive tumors. High TRIM22 expression was associated with aggressive clinicopathological features, lymph node metastasis, and poor survival. Gain- and loss-of-function experiments showed that TRIM22 promoted epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT)-like marker changes, migration, invasion, VEGF-C expression, and lymphangiogenic activity. In a footpad-popliteal lymph node metastasis model, TRIM22 increased lymphatic vessel density and metastatic tumor burden in draining lymph nodes. RNA sequencing identified Wnt signaling as a major pathway affected by TRIM22 silencing. TRIM22 overexpression increased nuclear β-catenin levels and TCF/LEF reporter activity, whereas TRIM22 knockdown decreased both measures and the expression of several metastasis-related genes. Pharmacological inhibition of Wnt/β-catenin signaling with IWR-1-endo attenuated TRIM22-induced invasion, lymphangiogenesis, and lymph node metastasis. These findings support a functional role for TRIM22 in cervical cancer lymphatic dissemination and implicate Wnt/β-catenin signaling in these phenotypes. However, the direct molecular link and β-catenin-specific dependency remain to be established.

articles.title: Secondary findings in hereditary breast and ovarian cancer predisposition genes in 5070 Polish non-oncological exomes.
articles.journal: European journal of human genetics : EJHG
articles.authors: Czukiewska E, Szczęśniak D, Nowak-Kępczyk M et al.
articles.abstract: Whole-exome sequencing (WES) enables identification of medically actionable hereditary cancer predisposition findings beyond the primary diagnostic indication. We performed a retrospective analysis of 5100 clinical WES tests. After exclusion of 30 oncology-related cases, a non-oncological cohort of 5070 WES tests was used to evaluate pathogenic and likely pathogenic findings in hereditary breast and/or ovarian cancer predisposition genes. A variant-level dataset comprised 151 unique pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants. The overall detection frequency of pathogenic or likely pathogenic findings in hereditary breast and/or ovarian cancer predisposition genes was 7.1%. The highest gene-level frequencies were observed for CHEK2 (1.54%), ATM (1.34%), BRCA2 (0.75%), BRCA1 (0.61%) and PALB2 (0.59%). Moderate-penetrance hereditary cancer genes accounted for 3.81% of the cohort, slightly exceeding the frequency observed for high-penetrance hereditary cancer and Lynch syndrome-associated genes (3.33%). Among genes included in the ACMG secondary findings framework, BRCA2, BRCA1, and mismatch repair genes accounted for most secondary findings, whereas PTEN and NF1 findings were predominantly phenotype-driven. Of the pathogenic and likely pathogenic findings, 46.7% occurred in genes included in the ACMG Secondary Findings framework, whereas 53.3% occurred in other hereditary cancer predisposition genes analysed in this study. This distribution reflects the deliberately selective scope of the ACMG SF framework and the broader spectrum of hereditary cancer susceptibility findings that may be encountered in clinical WES.

articles.title: MRI-based radiomics and deep learning for the prenatal diagnosis of Placenta Accreta Spectrum: a systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Sirico A, Pisani D, Sandullo L et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: accuracy of Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS) diagnosis using conventional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is still limited by subjective interpretation. Increasing evidence showed that radiomics and Deep Learning (DL) may improve diagnostic objectivity by extracting quantitative features from MRI data. This study aimed to synthesize the evidence on the diagnostic performance and clinical utility of these models.
METHODS: a systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted following PRISMA-DTA guidelines and PRISMA 2020 recommendations: PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases from inception to December 2025. We searched for primary studies evaluating MRI-based radiomics or DL models for the binary diagnosis of PAS. Data were extracted to create 2 × 2 contingency tables and used a bivariate random-effects model to calculate pooled sensitivity, specificity, and to generate a summary ROC (SROC) curve. We assessed robustness via leave-one-out sensitivity analysis, and clinical utility using Fagan's nomogram and likelihood ratios. A secondary meta-analysis was performed for the prediction of postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) ≥1000 mL.
RESULTS: twelve studies met the inclusion criteria (N = 1135 patients). The pooled sensitivity for PAS diagnosis was 0.83 (95% CI: 0.75-0.89) and pooled specificity was 0.82 (95% CI: 0.74-0.88). The summary AUC was 0.896, confirming high diagnostic accuracy. The positive likelihood ratio (LR+) was 4.61 and the negative likelihood ratio (LR-) was 0.21. Subgroup analyses based on AI model type (p > 0.05) and study design (p > 0.05) did not find significant differences between groups but revealed that single-center studies tended to report higher accuracy compared to multicenter studies. The secondary meta-analysis on massive PPH prediction (n = 4 studies, N = 353 patients: 165 PPH+ and 188 PPH-) yielded a pooled sensitivity of 0.88 (95% CI: 0.63-0.97), a pooled specificity of 0.78 (95% CI: 0.50-0.93), and an AUC of 0.901.
CONCLUSIONS: MRI-based AI models demonstrate high exploratory pooled accuracy for the prenatal diagnosis of PAS in high-risk cohorts. These results suggest that these tools show promising exploratory accuracy and may provide decision support as an adjunct ("human-in-the-loop") in equivocal cases. However, their real-world clinical generalizability remains constrained by retrospective designs and index test threshold optimization.

articles.title: Fertility, pregnancy, and parenthood: Risks and impacts among urologists.
articles.authors: Schoentgen NS, Methorst C, Cholley I et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: The feminization of urology highlights challenges regarding pregnancy and parenthood. We surveyed French urologists to evaluate the impact of parental leave on service organization, surgical activity, and gestational risks.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted from April to August 2023 among members of AFU and AFUF. A total of 325 urologists responded (31% women, 69% men; mean age: 46 years). Data were analyzed using Sphinxdeclic.
RESULTS: Male urologists had more children than females (3 vs. 2, P<0.01). Overall, 37% delayed childbearing due to career (68% of women). Infertility rate was 16%. Parental leave was perceived as having a negative impact for 32% of colleagues. Only 13% of women had coverage replacement, 31% ceased night shifts, and 15% worked t until the end of their pregnancy. Ionizing radiation exposure continued in 64% of cases. High complication rates occurred during pregnancy (48%), including miscarriages (21%) and preterm births (24%). Only 30% continued breastfeeding upon returning. 41% of private practitioners experienced a negative financial impact. Only 31% of men took paternity leave.
CONCLUSION: Pregnancy among female urologists carries high complication rates. Despite growing gender parity in French urology, structural adaptations during pregnancy, lactation support, and paternity leave adoption remain inadequate. Institutional reforms are required to safeguard reproductive health and ensure equity.

articles.title: Prevalence and determinants of antiseizure medication dispensing among pregnant persons in the United States: A retrospective claims-based cohort study, 2004-2021.
articles.authors: Leal LF, Djidjou PK, Pana R et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To describe trends and identify factors associated with antiseizure medications (ASMs) dispensing among pregnant persons in the United States.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective claims-based cohort study within AMerican PREGNANcy Mother-Child CohorT (AM-PREGNANT). We identified pregnant persons aged 15-45 years continuously enrolled from 12 months before the last menstrual period (LMP) through pregnancy end, with ≥1 ASM dispensing from 2004 to 2021. Annual prevalence of ASM dispensing was estimated by pregnancy start year. Within a first-ever ASM dispensing cohort, we examined dispensing patterns across pregnancy time windows, ASM-related indications and changes in dispensing during pregnancy. We also assessed factors associated with ASM dispensing at LMP among those initiating ASM therapy before pregnancy.
RESULTS: The cohort included 337 449 pregnant persons. Annual ASM dispensing prevalence remained stable (10%-13%). Among those with first-ever ASM dispensing (n = 115 896), 56% had dispensing before pregnancy, of whom 65% had no dispensing during pregnancy. The most common starting ASMs were clonazepam (28%), topiramate (25%) and gabapentin (20%). Dispensing patterns varied by indication: epilepsy was characterized by lamotrigine, levetiracetam and topiramate, generally dispensed for >60 days, whereas psychiatric and pain indications showed more variable patterns, typically with <30 days of dispensing. Factors associated with ASM dispensing at LMP included pre-specified indications, comorbidities and pre-conception medication dispensing; among these, epilepsy/seizure had the strongest association (aOR 2.14; 95% CI 1.78-2.59).
CONCLUSIONS: ASM dispensing varied by indication, with most pre-pregnancy dispensing not continuing during pregnancy. Epilepsy/seizure was most strongly associated with dispensing at LMP, with additional associations observed for comorbidities and pre-conception medication dispensing.

articles.title: Computed Tomography-Derived Body Composition as a Predictor of Chemotherapy Dose Reduction in Patients With Endometrial Cancer.
articles.authors: Wu PY, Hsu KL, Cheng YM et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Associations between computed tomography (CT)-derived body composition, endometrial cancer, and chemotherapy tolerance remain unclear. We compared CT-derived body composition between patients with endometrial cancer and healthy women and assessed whether pretreatment body composition was associated with chemotherapy-related dose reduction.
METHODS: This retrospective, single-center cohort study used automated CT-based body-composition analysis to quantify skeletal muscle and adipose tissue area and density. Dose reduction was a relative delivered dose of <85% of the full chemotherapy regimen. Patients with endometrial cancer were compared with propensity score-matched healthy controls and stratified by whether standard-dose chemotherapy was maintained or dose reduction was required. Logistic regression identified dose reduction predictors. Survival outcomes were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method and compared using the log-rank test.
RESULTS: Overall, 116 patients with endometrial cancer, with a mean age of 56.37 ± 9.07 years, were compared with 371 matched healthy women. In unadjusted comparisons, patients with endometrial cancer had a less favorable CT-derived body composition profile, characterized by poorer skeletal muscle quality and greater adipose tissue accumulation; however, these differences did not remain significant after false discovery rate (FDR) correction. Among the cancer cohort, 85 received standard-dose chemotherapy, and 31 required dose reduction. Patients requiring dose reduction had significantly lower total skeletal muscle area than those without dose reduction (90.89 ± 12.78 vs. 99.40 ± 18.39 cm2, P = 0.007) and a lower skeletal muscle index (36.65 ± 4.78 vs. 40.96 ± 6.69 cm2/m2, P < 0.001). Only total skeletal muscle index (SMI) remained significant after FDR correction (adjusted P = 0.008). Age-adjusted multivariable analysis showed that advanced FIGO stage (OR 0.327, 95% CI 0.116-0.897, P = 0.030) and higher total SMI (OR 0.853, 95% CI 0.763-0.939, P = 0.002) were associated with lower odds of dose reduction. No significant survival differences were observed.
CONCLUSION: Patients with endometrial cancer showed less favorable CT-derived body composition in unadjusted comparisons, although these differences were not significant after FDR correction. Lower pretreatment SMI was associated with chemotherapy dose reduction in this selected retrospective cohort.

articles.title: Prevalence of von Willebrand disease among adolescents and young women with heavy menstrual bleeding in hospital-based settings: A systematic review.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric and adolescent gynecology
articles.authors: Nayak S, Badagabettu S, D'souza A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heavy menstrual bleeding (HMB) affects up to 40% of adolescent and reproductive-age females and is a leading cause of complications such as severe anemia, iron deficiency and hospitalization. In adolescents and young women, it is commonly linked to anovulatory cycles and underlying inherited bleeding disorders, with von Willebrand disease (VWD) being the most prevalent but frequently underdiagnosed. This systematic review explores the prevalence of VWD among adolescents and young women aged ≤25 years assessed for HMB within hospital-based settings and evaluates diagnostic setting gradients.
METHODS: This review included six databases - PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, CINAHL, and ProQuest that were searched electronically using relevant keywords and MeSH terms. After the search, the articles were transferred to Rayyan software for further screening. The quality of the included studies was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute Prevalence Critical Appraisal Tool. Data extraction was performed, and the findings were presented narratively.
RESULTS: Among 1,709 young women with heavy menstrual bleeding across 16 studies, 199 were found to have von Willebrand disease, yielding an overall occurrence rate of 11.64%. Subgroup analysis by clinical referral setting revealed a distinct diagnostic gradient: Specialized Hematology and Hemophilia Treatment Centres (HTCs) demonstrated the highest prevalence at 16.78% (77/459), followed by Inpatient / Acute Emergency Admissions at 10.20% (25/245), General Tertiary Referral Hospital Settings at 10.20% (65/637), and Pediatric & Adolescent Gynaecology (PAG) / Multidisciplinary Outpatient HMB Clinics at 8.70% (32/368).
CONCLUSION: von Willebrand disease is a highly significant underlying cause of heavy menstrual bleeding in young women, affecting 11.64% of patients presenting to hospital-based settings, including nearly 1 in 11 patients (8.70%) evaluated in specialized Pediatric & Adolescent Gynaecology (PAG) clinics. These findings support targeted diagnostic testing rather than universal screening, specifically for patients who present to hospital-based settings and PAG clinics.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD42024563010.

articles.title: Metformin mitigates trophoblast GLUT1 inhibition through HIF-1α/Fibronectin/AMPK pathway in preeclampsia.
articles.authors: Lee CI, Tsai PY, Tam HL et al.
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia (PE) is a complex gestational hypertensive disorder associated with dysregulated placental energy metabolism, and fibronectin (FN) plays a critical role in its development. Although metformin has shown potential in reducing the risk of PE, its effects on FN and trophoblast glucose transport regulation remain unclear. In this study, experiments were conducted using FN-pretreated and FN-knockdown HTR-8/SVneo cells, clinical placental specimens, and a preeclampsia mouse model. Aberrant FN and GLUT1 expression was observed in human preeclamptic placentas. Under hypoxic conditions, FN and GLUT1 were upregulated in two trophoblastic cell lines (HTR-8/SVneo and JAR) and in primary placental cells. However, exogenous FN suppressed hypoxia-associated GLUT1 upregulation, reduced extracellular L-lactate levels, and impaired trophoblast invasion and ciliogenesis. These effects were associated with activation of AMPK signaling. Metformin reduced HIF-1α, FN, and phosphorylated AMPK levels in FN-treated trophoblasts under hypoxia, while increasing GLUT1 expression and extracellular L-lactate levels and restoring trophoblast invasion and ciliogenesis. Notably, metformin increased AMPK phosphorylation in FN-silenced cells, suggesting that its effects on AMPK signaling depend, at least partly, on FN status. In the mouse model, increased placental FN was accompanied by altered GLUT1 expression, impaired primary cilia formation, and changes in AMPK-related signaling. Metformin treatment improved maternal blood pressure and fetal growth, reduced placental FN levels, and increased GLUT1 expression and ciliogenesis. In conclusion, FN disrupts trophoblast function under hypoxia and is associated with changes in GLUT1 expression and lactate output, involving AMPK signaling. Metformin alleviates these dysfunctions by suppressing FN and reversing FN-mediated GLUT1 inhibition and AMPK activation. These findings identify the HIF-1α/FN/AMPK axis as a critical mechanism in PE pathophysiology and support the potential repurposing of metformin for PE prevention.

articles.title: The evaluation of the potential application of friedelin as an alternative to estrogen in an ovariectomized rat model.
articles.authors: Saini R, Sharma SK, Sonkar VK et al.
articles.abstract: Menopause is a condition where ovaries stop functioning due to a decrease in hormonal levels (estrogen). It leads to loss of fertility, hot flashes, anxiety, and vaginal dryness. It is recommended to take hormonal therapy to escape from these problems. Although hormonal therapy has some benefits, there are severe health-related risks like cardiovascular disease and ovarian cancer. These problems forced to search for safer alternatives like phytoestrogen. The objective of this study was to test the efficacy of friedelin as an estrogen. Friedelin is a plant-derived triterpenoid compound. Ovariectomized rats were given friedelin for 28 days, and after that behavioral parameters were recorded along with other analyses like serum estradiol level estimation, uterine histology, and deciduoma formation. Estradiol-driven gene expression (mRNA and protein level) was also checked, along with immunofluorescence localization; these genes were estrogen receptor alpha (ER-α), estrogen receptor beta (ER-β), complement component 3 (C3), early growth response 1(EgR1), and proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA). Progesterone-like activity of friedelin was also checked. Improved behavioural responses were recorded, with significant increases in serum estradiol levels and epithelium thickness along with increased endometrial gland numbers. The significant upregulation of estrogen-responsive genes was found at the mRNA and protein levels in friedelin-treated groups. The localization of these genes was found primarily in endometrial stroma, luminal, and glandular epithelium. Deciduoma formation occurred only in the progesterone-administered group which denies friedelin's progesterone-like activity. The friedelin showed estrogen-like activity. Further, preclinical and clinical investigations are needed to establish friedelin's safety and efficacy for medical applications.

articles.title: Carboplatin tissue pharmacokinetics following intraperitoneal and systemic treatment: a microdialysis porcine study.
articles.authors: Petersen EK, Bue M, Schmedes AV et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Understanding carboplatin's tissue pharmacokinetics is critical for assessing its locoregional potential in Hyperthermic and Normothermic Intraperitoneal Chemotherapy (HIPEC, NIPEC) in ovarian cancer. This study assessed carboplatin exposure in tissues associated with ovarian cancer carcinomatosis across clinically relevant treatment regimens, using microdialysis in a healthy porcine model.
METHODS: Animals were divided into three groups receiving HIPEC, NIPEC, or intravenous (IV) carboplatin. A minor cytoreductive surgery was performed in the HIPEC and NIPEC groups, followed by carboplatin perfusion (800 mg/m2). The IV group received a 30 min carboplatin infusion (625 mg). Unbound carboplatin concentrations were measured by microdialysis at intra-abdominal target sites during and after chemotherapy. The primary endpoint was parietal peritoneum AUC0-∞ between groups.
KEY RESULTS: Parietal peritoneal AUC0-∞ was higher after HIPEC than after IV treatment (geometric mean ratio 2.37; 95% CI 1.08-5.17), whereas the NIPEC-IV (1.61; 0.73-3.53) and the exploratory HIPEC-NIPEC (1.47; 0.58-3.73) comparisons were inconclusive. Omental exposure showed a similar numerical pattern. IV treatment showed numerically higher exposure in plasma, rectum, liver, and superficial stomach. Perfusate carboplatin concentration decreased by approximately 32%. Greater inter-individual variability was evident following intraperitoneal chemotherapy.
CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS: The intraperitoneal regimens achieved numerically higher carboplatin exposure in the peritoneal lining than the IV regimen, with lower systemic exposure but greater variability. The study was not powered to determine whether hyperthermia affects carboplatin pharmacokinetics. These findings may inform further development and clinical evaluation of intraperitoneal carboplatin chemotherapy in ovarian cancer.

articles.title: Biomechanical Insights for Reducing Pelvic Floor Injuries during Vaginal Birth.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics and gynecology
articles.authors: Pipitone F, Chaffin JA, LaCross J et al.
articles.abstract: Vaginal birth is one of the most demanding biomechanical processes the human body experiences, yet it proceeds uneventfully in most women. Nevertheless, about one in five primiparous women sustain levator avulsions, and perineal tears of varying severity are considerably more common; for some the functional consequences are lifelong, underscoring the need for improved preventive strategies. In addition, the full burden of birth-related soft tissue injury, much of which is still poorly characterized, is possibly greater. Insights from sports biomechanics, where injury risk is understood in terms of tissue stress and strain, loading rate and magnitude, and number of loading cycles, offer a valuable scientific framework for understanding how, when, where and why maternal tissues fail during vaginal birth. After reviewing the core biomechanical concepts relevant to childbirth, we show how they apply to labor and delivery. We illustrate how tissue hysteresis, creep, and stress relaxation facilitate progressive birth canal dilation while reducing peak tissue stress, and how unusual demand, rapid loading, unfavorable force direction and stress concentration increase injury risk. For example, forceps-assisted delivery can markedly alter the magnitude, rate, and direction of tissue loading, thereby substantially increasing the risk for pelvic floor and anal sphincter injury. Birth canal tissue compliance varies up to seven-fold between individuals, highlighting that injury risk is not uniform; so investigating pregnancy-related soft tissue adaptations may help identify at-risk women. Furthermore, capacity-demand analyses may help guide clinical decision-making, because a mismatch is the ultimate determinant of outcome. We also examine the mechanisms of striated muscle injury relevant to the levator ani. Apart from passive sarcomere hyperelongation, we highlight how fetal head descent that stretches a contracted levator muscle subjects it to what is termed eccentric loading, carrying a substantially greater injury risk than stretching relaxed muscle. This underscores the value of prenatal pelvic floor relaxation training for use during active labor. Finally, we discuss factors that increase the risk of severe perineal laceration, including stress concentration and tear propagation in midline episiotomy. By examining childbirth through a biomechanical lens, this article demonstrates how established principles of tissue mechanics can be applied to everyday obstetric…

articles.title: The fundamental problem of risk prediction for individuals: health AI, uncertainty, and personalized medicine.
articles.authors: Barreñada L, Steyerberg E, Timmerman D et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Clinical prediction models are commonly evaluated regarding performance for a population, although decisions are made for individuals. The classic view relates uncertainty in risk estimates for individuals to sample size (estimation uncertainty) while other sources are model uncertainty (variability in modeling choices) and applicability uncertainty (variability in measurement procedures and between populations). We aim to illustrate the uncertainty of prediction models in estimating individual risks with an ovarian cancer example.
STUDY DESIGN AND SETTING: We used real and synthetic data for ovarian cancer diagnosis to train 59400 models with variations in estimation, model, and applicability uncertainty. We then used these models to estimate the probability of ovarian cancer in a fixed test set of 100 patients and evaluate the variability in individual estimates.
RESULTS: We show empirically that estimation uncertainty can be strongly dominated by model uncertainty and applicability uncertainty, even for models that perform well at the population level. Estimation uncertainty decreased considerably with increasing training sample size, whereas model and applicability uncertainty remained large.
CONCLUSION: Individual risk estimates are far more uncertain than often assumed. Model uncertainty and applicability uncertainty usually remain invisible when prediction models or algorithms are based on a single study. Predictive algorithms should inform, not dictate, care and support personalization through clinician-patient interaction.

articles.title: A statewide mystery caller study of real-world availability of contraception in Connecticut pharmacies.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA
articles.authors: Contreras AK, Qasba N, Buck S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: There is limited knowledge regarding availability of over-the-counter emergency contraceptive pill (OTC EC), ulipristal acetate emergency contraceptive pill (UPA EC), and over-the-counter progestin-only oral contraceptive pills (OTC POP) in Connecticut's supportive legislative environment.
OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated real-world availability of these products in Connecticut pharmacies.
METHODS: We conducted a statewide mystery-caller study of 532 pharmacies between June and August 2025. Each pharmacy was contacted twice, posing once as an adult and once as a minor, using a standardized script to assess product availability and location. Pharmacies were randomized to caller sequence (i.e., whether the first call was conducted as an adult or minor). Chi-square tests assessed differences by caller identity, call sequence effects (i.e., whether the initial call prompted stocking), pharmacy type, and geographic location.
RESULTS: Overall, 7.7% of pharmacies consistently stocked all three contraceptive methods across both calls. Consistent availability was highest for OTC EC (74.4%), followed by OTC POP (48.3%) and UPA EC (13.2%). Availability was similar by caller type, except for OTC EC, which was more frequently reported as available to adult callers than minor callers (83.3% vs 78.4%, p=0.043). Consistent availability varied by county (p=0.016) and pharmacy type (p<0.001), with retail pharmacies more likely to consistently stock all methods than supermarket, hospital, and independent pharmacies. Consistent unlocked aisle placement was reported by 7.6% of pharmacies for OTC EC and 13.2% for OTC POP.
CONCLUSION: Despite supportive state policies, pharmacy-based access to ECs and OTC POP remains limited and geographically variable. Strengthening pharmacy-level support is critical to ensuring reliable and equitable contraceptive access.

articles.title: A multi-level intervention to improve cervical cancer prevention in safety-net settings: The DOSE-CC study protocol for a hybrid type-1 effectiveness-implementation stepped wedge randomized controlled trial.
articles.authors: Perkins RB, Arevalo M, Fontenot HB et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer is highly preventable, but screening is under-utilized. Approximately 75% of individuals diagnosed with cervical cancer were unscreened, under-screened, or did not receive adequate follow-up after abnormal results. Thus, effective interventions to improve cervical cancer screening and follow-up care are needed. This paper describes the protocol for a multi-level intervention called Development of Systems and Education for Cervical Cancer prevention (DOSE-CC).
METHODS: We will use a hybrid type 1 effectiveness-implementation, stepped-wedge randomized controlled trial design to assess intervention impact on screening and follow-up. The trial will be conducted in four safety net sites in Florida, Hawaii, and Massachusetts, with guidance from a national advisory board and clinical champions at each site. We will systematically adapt our prior successful intervention, which focused on HPV vaccination of adolescents, to address screening and follow-up. The adapted intervention will involve longitudinal contact with practices and support system changes to improve screening and follow-up processes.
RESULTS: Findings will evaluate the impact of DOSE-CC on (a) screening receipt during medical visits; (b) follow-up care after abnormal results; and (c) population-level up-to-date screening rates at participating sites using data from electronic medical records. We will use the Reach, Effectiveness, Adoption, Implementation, and Maintenance Qualitative Evaluation for Systematic Translation (RE-AIM QuEST), a mixed-methods framework to assess implementation outcomes from health care worker, clinical champion, and patient perspectives.
CONCLUSIONS: Results from the randomized controlled trial will assess the impact of the DOSE-CC intervention on cervical cancer screening and follow-up rates, and guide evidence-based future scale-up to other settings.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: clinicaltrials.gov, NCT07226037, registered on 2025-11-10.

articles.title: AKT as a central node integrating multidrug resistance mechanisms in ovarian Cancer.
articles.authors: Ibrahim SO, Lee B, Choi J et al.
articles.abstract: Ovarian cancer, particularly high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC), remains a leading cause of gynecologic cancer mortality. Although HGSOC responds to platinum-taxane therapy, 70-85% relapse, with acquired resistance playing a major role. The phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)/protein kinase B (AKT)/mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) pathway, centered on AKT, contributes to this resistance. Current literature examines AKT's downstream consequences in isolation, overlooking their collective contribution to tumor evolution; this review addresses that gap by separating upstream AKT activation from downstream resistance outputs. Intrinsic genomic alterations (PIK3CA mutation, phosphatase and tensin homolog [PTEN] loss) and extrinsic tumor microenvironment (TME) cues converge on AKT, which drives four emerging resistance mechanisms (metabolic reprogramming and ferroptosis evasion, epigenetic modulation of homologous recombination inhibitor sensitivity, cancer stem cell plasticity, and immune evasion, discussed with therapeutic targeting), integrated with classical mechanisms into a unified chemoresistance framework. AKT promotes chemoresistance by coordinating ATP-binding cassette transporter-mediated drug efflux, RAD51/BRCA-dependent DNA repair, and an elevated apoptotic threshold via Bcl-2-associated agonist of cell death and survivin modulation. Spatial organization and interconnections are highlighted, including amplified AKT activation at the tumor-stromal interface through cancer-associated fibroblast-derived exosomal PTEN silencing. We evaluate therapeutic strategies (AKT and poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors, folate receptor alpha-targeted antibody-drug conjugates such as mirvetuximab soravtansine, and metabolic modulation through the AKT/mTORC1 axis) by targeting multiple nodes simultaneously. Patient-derived organoids, CRISPR/Cas9 screening, and circulating tumor DNA monitoring enable clinical translation, supporting rationally designed combinations over sequential monotherapy and reframing AKT from a poor-prognosis marker to a therapeutic target in recurrent, chemoresistant ovarian cancer.

articles.title: Estrogen loss and Alzheimer's disease: five exposures ordered by age, and why timing is the variable to test.
articles.authors: Kim BS, Kim HS, Choe YM et al.
articles.abstract: Alzheimer's disease occurs about twice as often in women as in men. A widely held hypothesis attributes part of the excess to loss of ovarian estradiol at menopause and, at its simplest, predicts that risk tracks the level of estrogen available to the brain. That prediction can be read against aromatase inhibitors, which engage brain aromatase and which millions of postmenopausal women take for years. We place this exposure alongside three other forms of estrogen loss - natural menopause, premenopausal oophorectomy and ovarian function suppression - and one receptor-level comparator, tamoxifen; order the five by age at exposure; and read them against the level-based model and its timing-modified form. Three randomized trials found no cognitive decrement with aromatase inhibition, and cohorts from four countries show no excess dementia during available follow-up (adjusted hazard ratio 1.04, 0.90-1.20, against no endocrine therapy). The ordering is difficult to reconcile with residual estrogen level as the operative variable (the lowest level carries no observed excess), weighs against abruptness (surgical and natural menopause did not differ in 233,802 women once age at menopause was adjusted), and is consistent with age: menopause before 40 carried a hazard ratio of 1.47, and in one breast-cancer cohort hormone-modulating therapy was associated with dementia at 0.48 at ages 65-69 and 2.39 at ≥90. The comparison is hypothesis-generating: current evidence does not support a simple monotonic model in which less estrogen means more disease; age at estrogen loss, and tissue state at that age, are the variables to test next.

articles.title: Examining the intersection of extreme heat exposures, social determinants of health, and adverse pregnancy outcomes: a scoping review.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
articles.authors: Rattan JE, Lindley SM, Preer Ii B et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Extreme heat exposure during pregnancy is associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes (APOs), complications themselves linked to long-term maternal cardiovascular risk, and these effects appear to vary by social and environmental context (e.g., neighborhood deprivation, greenness, and rural-urban residence). We describe the U.S. evidence and characterize how social determinants of health (SDoH), particularly area-level measures, are defined in this literature.
DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science Core Collection were searched through July 14, 2025, plus secondary searches in September 2025.
STUDY ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included U.S.-focused empirical epidemiologic studies and evidence syntheses that (1) assessed extreme heat exposure in pregnancy; (2) incorporated at least one individual- or area-level SDoH as exposure, covariate, or effect modifier; and (3) reported at least one APO, from preterm birth, low birth weight, stillbirth, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, and gestational diabetes to composite APOs, severe maternal morbidity, and acute cardiovascular events.
STUDY APPRAISAL AND SYNTHESIS METHODS: Two reviewers independently screened records; a senior reviewer resolved conflicts. Data were extracted into standardized forms and synthesized narratively. Per scoping review guidance, formal risk-of-bias assessment was not performed.
RESULTS: We included 37 studies (28 empirical and 9 reviews). Heat exposure was typically defined using percentile-based thresholds (most commonly the 90th or 95th local percentile), heat-wave definitions, apparent-temperature metrics, or absolute cutoffs, with the week before delivery the most frequent window. Preterm birth was the most evaluated outcome, followed by birthweight-related outcomes and stillbirth. Individual-level socioeconomic measures (e.g., education, insurance) appeared in nearly all empirical studies, whereas area-level measures-neighborhood income or poverty, deprivation indices, greenness or tree canopy, heat-trapping land cover, region, and rural-urban residence-appeared in fewer than half. Five of 12 studies incorporating area-level SDoH reported stronger heat-APO associations in disadvantaged or…
TWEETABLE STATEMENT: Heat exposure in pregnancy is linked to adverse outcomes, and risk may be higher in neighborhoods experiencing socioeconomic deprivation, highlighting the need to measure area-level social determinants in climate-maternal health research.

articles.title: Quantitative glycoproteomics reveals distinct alterations in spermatozoa and seminal plasma from men with asthenozoospermia.
articles.authors: Cheng Q, Cai F, Su T et al.
articles.abstract: Protein glycosylation is a highly prevalent post-translational modification in male reproduction. Alterations in protein glycosylation have been observed in the semen of men with infertility; however, the role of altered protein glycosylation remains unclear. Using advanced glycoproteomic approaches, we investigated the alteration of site-specific N-glycosylation in spermatozoa and seminal plasma from normozoospermic controls (n = 35) and men with asthenozoospermia (n = 38), a common cause of male infertility. Our results revealed that both spermatozoa and seminal plasma exhibited distinct N-glycosylation patterns. A total of 127 glycoproteins in spermatozoa and 118 glycoproteins in seminal plasma exhibited differential N-glycosylation in patients with asthenozoospermia. Gene ontology analysis indicated that these glycoproteins were significantly enriched in the extracellular vesicles, with several serving as prominent extracellular vesicles markers, including CD59, CD63, and tetraspanin-8. Additionally, significant alterations were observed in the N-glycosylation of galectin-3, a crucial glycoprotein for fertilization that is primarily found on spermatozoa and transferred via extracellular vesicles in seminal plasma. This study provides characterization of site-specific N-glycosylation alterations in both spermatozoa and seminal plasma from men with asthenozoospermia. These findings suggest a potential association between altered site-specific N-glycosylation and asthenozoospermia, possibly involving extracellular vesicles-sperm interactions, although the underlying mechanisms remain to be experimentally validated. Moreover, these alterations were significant for specific N-glycans or N-glycosites, suggesting their potential as novel biomarkers and therapeutic targets for male infertility. Several intact N-glycopeptides identified in spermatozoa and seminal plasma showed strong correlations with progressive motility, highlighting the potential contribution of altered N-glycosylation to sperm movement.

articles.title: Advancement of Gender Equity in Academic Urology Leadership-A 10-Year Update.
articles.authors: Rajan T, Duraes FR, Puig E et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To characterize current gender representation across academic urology leadership, examine associations with experience and subspecialty, and quantify changes over the past decade.
METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study of the 148 U.S. academic urology residency programs as of January 2026. Data on Chair, Vice Chair, Program Director, and Associate Program Director positions were extracted from official websites, including gender, experience, and subspecialty. Statistical analyses included Chi-square tests, ANOVA, linear regression, and Fisher's Exact Test for comparison to 2017 data.
RESULTS: Female representation showed a hierarchical gradient: Chairs 6.8%, Vice Chairs 22.4%, Program Directors 25.9%, and Associate Program Directors 40.3%. Compared to 2017, Program Directors increased from 8.1% (OR 3.97, p<0.001) and Vice Chairs from 4.2% (OR 6.64, p=0.01), while Chairs increased from 3.2% to 6.8% (p=0.27, not significant). Female leaders had 7.3 fewer years of experience than males (13.8 vs 21.0 years, p<0.01). Gender and subspecialty were significantly associated (p<0.01), with females concentrated in Urogynecology and Reconstructive Pelvic Surgery (URPS) and Trauma/Reconstruction, while males dominated Oncology and Endourology.
CONCLUSIONS: Female representation improved significantly across mid-level leadership, with a robust pipeline at junior levels. Although chair positions remain largely unchanged, the experience gap demonstrates women enter leadership at comparable career stages as men, suggesting temporal trends toward equity. Subspecialty disparities do exist, necessitating targeted efforts to diversify training and broaden pathways to senior leadership.

articles.title: A comparison of UK and French guidelines on the identification of pregnant women at low-risk of complications: a nationwide population-based study.
articles.journal: Journal of gynecology obstetrics and human reproduction
articles.authors: Chantry AA, Hocquette A, Viaud M et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare UK and French guidelines on the identification of pregnant women at low-risk of complications DESIGN: National population-based study SETTING: All births in France over 1 week in 2021 POPULATION: 11,845 women with a live-born singleton, with data abstracted from medical records and maternal interviews MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Prevalence of low-risk women and discrepancies in low-risk exclusion criteria between UK and French guidelines RESULTS: The prevalence of women at low-risk was 64.2% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 63.3-65.0) and 71.2% (70.4-72.0) according to UK and French guidelines, respectively. Overall, 58.9% (58.0-59.8) of women were at low-risk according to both guidelines, 5.2% (4.8-5.6) according to UK guidelines only and 12.3% (11.7-12.9) for French guidelines only. Risk level is assessed at the beginning of pregnancy in French guidelines but at the end of pregnancy in UK guidelines. Uterine scar and insulin-treated gestational diabetes were the main low-risk exclusion criteria in UK but not French guidelines.
