This study used a qualitative methodology comprising 1:1 semi-structured interviews with patients, pharmacists, physicians/nurse practitioners, and leaders from stakeholder organizations to identify measures of a high-quality prescribing service delivered by pharmacists. Data analysis was completed using reflexive thematic analysis. A constructive workshop with a sample of participants was conducted to validate and prioritize the quality measures and determine implementation feasibility.
RESULTS: Sixty-four interviews were analyzed (16 patients, 12 pharmacists, 23 physicians/nurse practitioners, and 13 stakeholder organization leaders). Thirty-three measures were proposed, aligning with 5 major themes: patient experience, efficacy, safety, access, and cost-effectiveness. Patients emphasized the importance of privacy and the use of appropriate pronouns within the theme of patient experience, while physicians/nurse practitioners focused on clinical efficacy, suggesting that adhering to documentation standards and interdisciplinary communication are the top measures of quality. All interviewee groups agreed that access-based quality indicators, such as wait times and geographical distribution, are important to develop. Cost-effectiveness, a unique theme not typically linked to quality, emerged as a key measure.
DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION: This study identified 33 possible measures that can be used to develop quality indicators for pharmacists prescribing in community-based practice settings to evaluate such programs.

articles.title: Epidemiologic profile of self-reported drug allergy in a sample of adolescent females suffering from dysmenorrhea.
articles.authors: Vázquez-Nava F, Vázquez-Rodríguez CF, Vázquez-Rodríguez EM et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Self-reported drug allergy (SRDA) continues to be a major global public health problem, particularly among adult females.
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study is to determine the epidemiologic profile of SRDA in adolescent females aged 13-19 years with dysmenorrhea.
MATERIAL AND METHOD: In this cross-sectional study, data of 821 participants were analyzed. The data were collected using a self-administered questionnaire. The diagnosis of allergic disease was established with self-reported information provided by participants, without performing laboratory tests or physical examination.
RESULTS: The mean age of adolescent females was 17.8 ± 0.7 years. The mean age at the onset of menarche was approximately 11.8 ± 1.4 years; moreover, 59.3% of the participants experienced regular menstruations, but 72.0% suffered from dysmenorrhea. A total of 83 (10.1%) adolescent females reported having SRDA; of these, 23 participants (27.7%) reported being allergic to more than two medications; moreover, the age at the onset of SRDA was 10.7 ± 6.6 years. Multivariate logistic regression analysis revealed that allergic rhinitis, consumption of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), and recommended use of NSAIDs by mothers were associated with SRDA. Allergic rhinitis and consumption of NSAIDs without prescription were associated with SRDA in adolescent females suffering from dysmenorrhea.
CONCLUSION: It is important that parents understand the adverse effects that these medications generate if used without professional supervision. Healthcare professionals should be better trained to identify adolescent females with greater susceptibility to reporting SRDA.

articles.title: Why don't they tell women about these issues? A qualitative investigation into barriers for women seeking help for pelvic floor symptoms.
articles.authors: Campbell KG, Moffatt F, Shaw R et al.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo investigate barriers to help-seeking for women with pelvic floor dysfunction.DesignQualitative semi-structured interview and focus group study, reflexive thematic analysis to develop overarching themes.SettingInterviews and focus groups were conducted online, via TEAMs.ParticipantsThirty adult women were recruited by email from an existing database of women who previously self-reported pelvic floor symptoms. Poster adverts and word of mouth were also used to purposefully increase representation. Twelve interviewees took part in three focus groups (n = 3, n = 4, n = 5). Most, 24 (80%), were white, and six (20%) were Pakistani Muslims. The majority (23, 76.7%) were educated to degree level or above. Other demographics such as age, reported symptoms, and employment status varied.ResultsThree main themes were developed: (1) 'An inevitable part of womanhood: the daily and ongoing challenges of pelvic floor symptoms', the embarrassment of coping with symptoms in public and the inevitability of this as part of women's lives; (2) 'The challenges: stumbling blocks to healthcare', with the key barrier identified as being lack of knowledge regarding symptoms, how and where to seek help; (3) 'The solution: navigating the route to pelvic health', including the need for clear public health messaging and education throughout the lifespan.ConclusionWomen believed that public health messaging regarding women's health issues should include clear, reliable information about pelvic health, delivered at all stages of women's lives. Simple education could empower women to make informed, appropriate choices regarding their pelvic health, thereby improving their quality of life.

articles.title: A Multimodal Hyaluronic Acid Approach to Compensate Menopause-Related Skin Changes: Hyaluronic Acid Serum Subanalysis With HA Filler Injection.
articles.journal: Dermatologic surgery : official publication for American Society for Dermatologic Surgery [et al.]
articles.authors: Bravo BSF, Braz AV, Coimbra D et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Estrogen depletion during menopause reduces collagen, elastin, and glycosaminoglycans (GAG) synthesis, particularly hyaluronic acid (HA), and is associated with skin thinness, wrinkles, reduced elasticity, and decreased hydration.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy of an integrated facial antiaging approach using a multiglycan HA serum with HA filler injection in menopausal women.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A serum formulation (containing HA, dipotassium glycyrrhizate, purple rice extract, Lactobacillus/soybean ferment extract, pro-Xylane) was applied twice daily on the face from Day -14 to Day 56 and integrated with nasolabial fold HA dermal filler injection on Day 0. In a post hoc subanalysis of 12 menopausal women, facial aging signs were assessed using instrumental measurements of skin elasticity and firmness, and standardized photography.
RESULTS: At baseline, net skin elasticity in the temple area and in the nasolabial fold area were lower in the menopausal subgroup compared with the overall cohort. In menopausal women, nasolabial and temple skin elasticity showed improvement between baseline and Day 56.
CONCLUSION: A multimodal HA serum integrated with HA dermal injection may offer a promising facial rejuvenation strategy in menopausal women with skin aging signs.

articles.title: Serum Protein Changes and Acute-Phase Response in Patients Receiving Doxorubicin-Cyclophosphamide Chemotherapy in Ethiopia: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Nida T, Bedada AT
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with breast cancer in low and middle income countries (LMICs) receiving doxorubicin-cyclophosphamide (AC) chemotherapy face heightened toxicity risks due to limited supportive care infrastructure.
AIMS: This prospective study characterized changes in serum total protein, albumin, and high sensitivity-C-reactive protein (Hs-CRP) during AC chemotherapy in Ethiopian women with breast cancer and described these changes by age, menopausal status, body mass index (BMI), and disease stage.
METHODS: In this single-center cohort study at Tikur Anbessa Specialized Hospital (TASH), Addis Ababa, 45 adult women with histologically confirmed invasive breast carcinoma scheduled for neoadjuvant or adjuvant AC chemotherapy were enrolled. Serum total protein, albumin, and Hs-CRP were measured at baseline and 21-28 days after Day 1 of the fourth AC cycle. Analyses were complete-case. Pre-to-post changes were evaluated by paired t-tests and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Time × subgroup interactions were assessed by repeated measures ANOVA, with Hs-CRP natural-log transformed for the interaction tests. Bonferroni correction was applied across six interaction tests. Subgroup analyses were unadjusted and exploratory; multivariable regression and sensitivity analyses were not performed.
RESULTS: Forty-two patients (93.3%) completed both assessments (mean age 44.8 ± 11.9 years; 52.4% premenopausal; 64.3% Stage III; no Stage IV). After four AC cycles, mean serum total protein declined from 7.3 ± 0.6 to 7.0 ± 0.7 g/dL (-4.1%; p = 0.020) and albumin from 4.1 ± 0.4 to 3.8 ± 0.5 g/dL (-7.3%; p < 0.001), while median Hs-CRP rose from 3.2 (IQR: 1.8-4.5) to 6.1 (IQR: 3.9-8.4) mg/L (+90.6% in medians; median paired difference + 2.6 mg/L, bootstrapped 95% CI 1.8-3.4; p < 0.001). Hypoalbuminemia prevalence increased from 7.1%…
CONCLUSIONS: In Ethiopian women receiving four cycles of AC chemotherapy, serum total protein and albumin fell and Hs-CRP rose, with a larger albumin decline in women aged ≥ 56 years; numerical differences by menopausal status and stage were not statistically significant after correction. The pattern is consistent with an acute-phase response; hepatic synthetic function was not assessed, and other contributors such as infection, hemodilution and reduced intake could not be excluded. These descriptive findings are hypothesis generating, and larger studies with clinical outcomes are needed before albumin and Hs-CRP are used to guide supportive care.

articles.title: Data quality assessment of maternal and newborn indicators from District Health Information Software 2 in five African countries for the period 2014-2023.
articles.authors: Akuze J, Otieno GP, Shabani J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tracking progress of sustainable development goal (SDG) targets requires robust monitoring systems, yet data quality remains challenging across sub-Saharan Africa. Most countries rely on aggregated data from District Health Information Software 2 (DHIS2) or surveys to track maternal, newborn and child health (MNCH) indicators. We evaluated MNCH data quality in DHIS2 across Ghana, Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, and Zimbabwe (2014-2023).
METHODS: We analysed 16 ENAP-aligned indicators and their 29 corresponding data elements captured in DHIS2 across health facility levels. We applied the WHO Data Quality Review framework to assess availability, reporting completeness, internal consistency (ratio-based validation metrics and temporal trends), and external consistency (comparison with UN Inter-agency Group for Child Mortality Estimation (UN IGME), Maternal Mortality Estimation Inter-Agency Group (MMEIG), and World Health Organization Global Health Observatory data).
RESULTS: Of 29 data elements, Uganda had highest availability (72-76% during 2020-2023), followed by Kenya (62-66%), Tanzania (52%), and Ghana and Zimbabwe (41% each). Reporting completeness varied substantially: Tanzania achieved >95% facility reporting across all levels, while other countries showed disparities between hospitals and lower-level facilities. Internal consistency revealed problematic patterns for mortality-related ratios in Ghana (stillbirth-to-neonatal mortality ratios reaching 5.0-12.5) and Kenya (KMC-to-low birthweight ratios >2.0). After adjusting DHIS2 estimates for facility birth coverage, stillbirth rates generally exceeded or matched UN IGME estimates, whereas maternal mortality ratios showed substantial underreporting relative to MMEIG estimates. Ghana showed the closest MMR alignment and Kenya the largest discrepancy. Neonatal mortality was underreported in Ghana and Uganda but appeared higher than UN IGME estimates in Tanzania, a finding sensitive to aggregation method.
CONCLUSIONS: DHIS2 data quality varies substantially across countries, with country-specific challenges in availability, completeness and consistency. Strengthening facility-level data capture and developing an MNCH data quality module are crucial for improving data reliability.

articles.title: EPIGEN-Prostate: Identifying multi-omic markers of prostate cancer in Aotearoa New Zealand men.
articles.authors: Smith J, Yee A, Dutta A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: DNA methylation biomarkers have demonstrated promise as potential clinical biomarkers for improved detection and risk stratification of prostate cancer (PCa). Despite this, only sparse genome-scale, sequencing-based DNA methylation data are available in the early PCa setting. The EPIGEN-Prostate study aims to identify novel cell-free DNA methylation biomarkers from blood and multi-omic biomarkers from prostate tissue for detecting clinically significant PCa (csPCa).
STUDY DESIGN: EPIGEN-Prostate is a multi-centre, prospective, longitudinal cohort study of patients undergoing investigation for potential PCa, with a biomarker discovery-focused design. The primary objective of this study is to characterise novel cell-free DNA-based molecular biomarkers for non-invasive PCa detection and risk stratification. Secondary objectives include the development of multi-omic risk classifiers to predict disease progression and treatment response.
ENDPOINTS: The primary endpoint is the presence or absence of csPCa, defined here as International Society of Urological Pathology grade group ≥2. Secondary endpoints will include disease stage at presentation, disease recurrence following curative treatment, metastasis-free survival, and overall survival.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: Individuals aged ≥18 years, scheduled to undergo prostate biopsy, and able to provide informed consent are eligible to participate. Blood samples will be prospectively collected before prostate biopsy, and prostate biopsy tissue will be retrieved for analysis after regular processing. Participants proceeding to radical prostatectomy may contribute surgical tissue and serial postoperative blood samples. Pre-biopsy plasma and matched prostate tissue samples will undergo genome-wide DNA methylation profiling using reduced representation bisulfite sequencing approaches. Tissue samples will also undergo RNA sequencing and genetic profiling. Clinical outcomes will be collected for up to 15 years. Biomarker discovery and validation will integrate molecular and clinical data using nested case-control analyses for each objective.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable. Human ethical approval was obtained via the New Zealand Health and Disability Ethics Committee - Southern (HDEC 21/STH/184).

articles.title: Antimuscarinic medication use and risk of glaucoma in patients with overactive bladder: a literature review and disproportionality analysis using individual case safety reports from FAERS.
articles.journal: Canadian journal of physiology and pharmacology
articles.authors: Sadeghi H, Lau R, Omrani M et al.
articles.abstract: This study investigated the potential association between antimuscarinic medications and glaucoma by integrating evidence from a literature review with pharmacovigilance analysis of the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS). A systematic search of MEDLINE and EMBASE through 15 July 2025 identified eight studies, one pooled analysis of two randomized controlled trials, five observational studies, and two case reports that collectively suggested an association between anticholinergic use and increased risk of glaucoma or elevated intraocular pressure. Concurrently, an active-comparator restricted disproportionality analysis of FAERS data (2004Q1-2023Q4) was conducted to compare glaucoma reports among users of oxybutynin, tolterodine, solifenacin, darifenacin, fesoterodine, and trospium versus mirabegron. Adjusted reporting odds ratios (RORs) and information components (IC025) were calculated following READUS-PV guidelines. Compared with mirabegron, antimuscarinics demonstrated a higher reporting rate of glaucoma (adjusted ROR: 3.02; 95% CI: 2.03-4.50; IC025: 0.15), with tolterodine showing the strongest signal (adjusted ROR: 7.67; 95% CI: 4.90-12.02; IC025: 1.24), followed by darifenacin, fesoterodine, and solifenacin. No signals were observed for oxybutynin or trospium. These findings suggest that certain antimuscarinics, particularly tolterodine, darifenacin, and fesoterodine, may be associated with an increased risk of glaucoma and warrant further pharmacoepidemiologic investigation to confirm safety and inform prescribing decisions.

articles.title: Pembrolizumab plus lenvatinib in advanced endometrial cancer: pharmacology, efficacy, safety and future perspectives.
articles.journal: Expert opinion on drug metabolism & toxicology
articles.authors: Ferrero S, Alessandri F, Centurioni MG et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pembrolizumab plus lenvatinib is an established post-platinum option for advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer, particularly mismatch repair-proficient (pMMR) disease, in which single-agent programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) blockade has limited activity.
AREAS COVERED: This narrative review critically evaluates the pharmacology, pharmacokinetics, metabolism, drug-interaction potential, efficacy and safety of pembrolizumab plus lenvatinib. Evidence from KEYNOTE-146, KEYNOTE-775, its 5-year analysis, ENGOT-en9/LEAP-001 and contemporary real-world cohorts was identified through searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science and the Cochrane Library from database inception to 14 August 2026, supplemented by ClinicalTrials.gov, regulatory documents and major congress proceedings.
EXPERT OPINION: Pembrolizumab plus lenvatinib improves survival after platinum therapy in immune checkpoint inhibitor-naive advanced endometrial cancer, but substantial toxicity requires proactive monitoring and frequent lenvatinib dose modification. Its therapeutic position is being redefined by first-line chemoimmunotherapy and the negative ENGOT-en9/LEAP-001 trial, while post-immunotherapy efficacy, predictive biomarkers and prospectively validated dosing strategies remain key research priorities.

articles.title: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy and surgery versus chemoradiotherapy for locally advanced cervical cancer.
articles.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
articles.authors: Athanasiou A, Bowden SJ, Ellis LB et al.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Chemoradiotherapy (CRT) is the primary treatment for locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC). However, CRT is associated with high toxicity, and access to radiotherapy infrastructure remains limited or unavailable in some settings globally. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) followed by radical surgery has therefore been proposed as an alternative to CRT, but the evidence regarding its efficacy and toxicity compared to CRT remains unclear.
OBJECTIVES: To compare NACT followed by radical surgery versus CRT for LACC.
SEARCH METHODS: We searched CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase, and ClinicalTrials.gov up to 20 May 2026, with no date or language restrictions. We also searched the reference lists of included studies and contacted experts in the field.
ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included randomised controlled trials (RCTs) in women with LACC (FIGO 2018 stage IB3/IIA2/IIB/IIIA-C/IVA) comparing NACT followed by radical surgery to CRT. We excluded non-randomised studies.
OUTCOMES: Our critical outcomes were overall survival, disease-free survival, and progression-free survival. Important outcomes included recurrence, acute and late toxicity, and quality of life.
RISK OF BIAS: We assessed risk of bias in the included studies using Cochrane's RoB 1 tool.
SYNTHESIS METHODS: We performed a random-effects meta-analysis using the inverse-variance method. We assessed the certainty of evidence using the GRADE approach.
INCLUDED STUDIES: Three RCTs (from four reports), with a total of 1326 women, reported on the outcomes of interest and were included in the meta-analysis.
SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS: NACT + radical surgery may result in little to no difference in five-year overall survival compared to CRT (hazard ratio (HR) 1.11, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.90 to 1.36; I² = 0%; 2 studies, 1259 participants; low-certainty evidence). The evidence is very uncertain for five-year disease-free survival (HR 1.28, 95% CI 0.97 to 1.69; 1 study, 635 participants; very low-certainty evidence) and five-year progression-free survival (HR 1.37, 95% CI 1.07 to 1.75; 1 study, 626 participants; very low-certainty evidence). NACT + radical surgery probably increases grade ≥ 3 acute toxicity (risk ratio (RR) 1.82, 95% CI 1.45 to 2.29; I² = 0%; 2 studies, 1224 participants; moderate-certainty evidence). The evidence is very uncertain for grade ≥ 3 late toxicity (RR 0.71, 95% CI 0.50 to 1.01; 1 study, 591 participants; very low-certainty evidence). NACT…
REGISTRATION: doi: 10.1002/14651858.CD014684.

articles.title: Association of postpartum glycemic control with serum MMP-9, ET-1, hypertension, and dyslipidemia in women with gestational diabetes mellitus.
articles.authors: Lu H, Song R, Dong J et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine the association between 12-month postpartum glycemic control and serum matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9)/endothelin-1 (ET-1) levels, hypertension, and dyslipidemia in women with prior gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), and to explore statistical indirect effects involving these biomarkers.
METHODS: A total of 300 women with prior GDM followed up at 12 months postpartum were included. HbA1c, MMP-9, ET-1, blood pressure, and lipid profiles were assessed at the same follow-up visit. Participants were stratified into good (n = 141) and poor (n = 159) glycemic control groups based on a glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) cutoff of 5.7%. General characteristics, vascular biomarker levels, and the prevalence of hypertension and dyslipidemia were compared between the groups. Correlation and logistic regression analyzes were performed, followed by exploratory regression-based indirect-effect analyzes involving MMP-9 and ET-1.
RESULTS: The poor control group had significantly higher levels of MMP-9 and ET-1. HbA1c was positively correlated with both biomarkers. The prevalences of hypertension and dyslipidemia in the poor control group were 28.9% and 37.1%, respectively, and were significantly higher than those in the good control group. Exploratory analyzes showed significant indirect-effect estimates involving MMP-9 and ET-1, with model-derived proportions of approximately 22% to 26%; however, these contemporaneous associations do not establish causal mediation.
CONCLUSION: Poor glycemic control at 12 months postpartum was associated with higher MMP-9 and ET-1 levels and a greater prevalence of hypertension and dyslipidemia. The observed indirect effects should be interpreted as exploratory statistical associations rather than evidence of temporal or causal mediation.

articles.title: Underrecognised legacies of preeclampsia: a biosocial DOHaD perspective for research in sub-Saharan Africa.
articles.authors: Penkler M, Conrad ML, Fahlbusch FB et al.
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia is often approached as an acute obstetric complication, yet its longer-term implications for maternal and offspring health remain insufficiently understood, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). Preeclampsia is a significant contributor to maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality worldwide, with a disproportionate burden in SSA. Although its clinical management has improved, particularly in high-income countries, important questions remain regarding its causes, long-term consequences, and the extent to which existing evidence applies to SSA populations. In this viewpoint, we propose that conceptualising preeclampsia in SSA through a biosocial Developmental Origins of Health and Disease (DOHaD) lens provides a useful framework for investigating how biological, social, and environmental processes jointly shape maternal and offspring health across the life course. We review evidence and identify four priority domains for investigation: understanding context-specific causes and mechanisms; improving detection, care-seeking, and health system pathways; examining long-term maternal and offspring outcomes; and strengthening research infrastructures. We argue that advancing research on preeclampsia in SSA requires interdisciplinary approaches that integrate biological, clinical, epidemiological, and qualitative research. Such a research agenda has the potential to improve understanding of preeclampsia beyond its acute manifestations and to inform more equitable strategies for maternal and child health across the life course.

articles.title: Sexual Violence/Abuse and Cervical Cancer: A Systematic Review of the Relationship.
articles.authors: Hooper L, Crentsil C, Meyrick J
articles.abstract: Sexual violence/abuse may influence cervical carcinogenesis through increased human papillomavirus exposure, trauma-related immune dysregulation and reduced engagement with prevention and care. However, the evidence on the co-occurrence of cervical cancer and sexual violence/abuse has not been systematically synthesised. MEDLINE, PsycINFO, CINAHL Plus, PsycArticles, EMBASE and Scopus were searched for English-language studies published between January 2000 and January 2025. Studies were eligible if they reported the prevalence of cervical cancer among survivors of sexual violence/abuse or vice versa. Risk of bias was assessed using Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tools. Seven studies from community, primary care and gynaecological oncology settings met inclusion criteria, covering a population of 8,840 participants. Among survivors of sexual violence/abuse, cervical cancer prevalence ranged from 5.4% to 32.3% and was consistently 1.5 to 2.7 times higher than among non-exposed comparators within the same settings. Among cervical cancer populations, sexual violence/abuse prevalence ranged from 18.4% to 57.5%, with stronger associations observed for severe or penetrative exposures. Adjusted odds ratios and relative risks ranged from approximately 3.3 to 11.15 at the highest exposure levels, consistent with a dose-response pattern. Findings point to a need for prevention strategies that consider how gender intersects with exposure to sexual violence/abuse. The review also suggests elevated co-occurrence between cervical cancer and sexual violence/abuse relative to global population estimates (~10% intimate-partner violence and ~6% non-partner violence). Limitations include small samples and measurement heterogeneity. Findings support co-produced, survivor-centred and trauma-informed approaches to cervical cancer prevention and oncology care that address barriers to healthcare engagement. Larger studies using validated measures and confounder-aware designs are needed.

articles.title: Ferric derisomaltose for the treatment of iron deficiency with or without anemia in women's health: an expert review.
articles.authors: Murji A, Abdul-Kadir R, Benson A et al.
articles.abstract: Iron deficiency (ID) with or without anemia is highly prevalent in women, and is commonly caused by abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB; including heavy menstrual bleeding), increased iron requirements during pregnancy, or postpartum hemorrhage (PPH). ID or iron deficiency anemia (IDA) in women of reproductive age has been associated with a substantial burden on quality of life, impaired physical and cognitive functioning, decreased productivity, and increased healthcare costs. The presence of ID/IDA during pregnancy has also been linked to poorer maternal outcomes and fetal developmental impairments, including an increased risk of neurodevelopmental disorders in neonates. Despite the high prevalence of ID/IDA and negative impact on women's health, these conditions are frequently overlooked and undertreated, in part due to the nonspecific nature of symptoms, such as fatigue. There is an increasing body of evidence for the use of intravenous (IV) iron to treat ID/IDA in women. Although efficacy is largely comparable among IV iron formulations when equivalent doses are used, there are factors that distinguish certain IV iron formulations from others. This review aims to discuss available evidence for the treatment of ID/IDA in women with ferric derisomaltose (FDI; a high-dose IV iron formulation), focusing on AUB, pregnancy, and PPH. Based on existing data, FDI represents a clinically-effective option for iron repletion in these contexts, and a low risk of hypersensitivity reactions and hypophosphatemia. There is scope for further research within the field of ID/IDA in women's health to address unmet needs and evidence gaps across the patient care pathway.

articles.title: Quality benchmarks in CRS-HIPEC surgery: An 11-year single-center analysis of outcomes, safety, and perioperative performance (2014-2024).
articles.journal: Advances in clinical and experimental medicine : official organ Wroclaw Medical University
articles.authors: Kazanowski M, Lesiak P, Wierzbicki J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Quality indicators (QIs) are central to safe delivery of cytoreductive surgery with hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (CRS-HIPEC), yet program-level benchmarking across tumor types is scarce.
OBJECTIVES: To describe the structure, process, and outcome QIs of a single-center CRS-HIPEC program (2014-2024) and to assess temporal trends in cytoreduction completeness, early mortality, length of stay (LOS), renal safety, and multidisciplinary team (MDT) integration against contemporary international benchmarks.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: A retrospective cohort study of consecutive CRS-HIPEC procedures (2014-2024) was conducted at a Polish tertiary center. Prespecified QIs included complete or near-complete cytoreduction (CC-0/1), 30- and 90-day mortality, LOS, LOS > 10 days, unplanned reoperation, 30-day readmission, MDT uptake, and acute kidney injury (AKI; defined using Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) serum creatinine criteria). Time trends were displayed with Shewhart charts and funnel plots; Wilson's 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs) were used for proportions.
RESULTS: Among 319 procedures (colorectal cancer (CRC) 111; ovarian cancer 87; mesothelioma/other 57; low-grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasm/pseudomyxoma peritonei (LAMN/PMP) 52; gastric cancer 12), the CC-0/1 rate was 93.4% overall (CRC 96.4%; LAMN/PMP 100%; ovarian cancer 90.8%; gastric cancer 91.7%; mesothelioma/other 86.0%). Thirtyand 90-day mortality were 0.6% and 1.6%, respectively; tumor-specific 30-day mortality ranged from 0% to 1.9%. Median LOS fell from 8.6 to 7.4 days (2014-2018 vs 2019-2024), and LOS > 10 days declined from 25.0% to 13.2%. Peritoneal cancer index (PCI) correlated weakly with LOS (Spearman's ρ = 0.13, p = 0.019), while AKI occurred in 70/308 (22.7%, 95% CI: 18.4-27.7), predominantly stage 1; AKI did not differ by cisplatin exposure (26.0% vs 21.2%, p = 0.389). The proportion of procedures with documented MDT discussion increased to approx. 20-33% after 2018.
CONCLUSIONS: Over 11 years, a single-center CRS-HIPEC program achieved high-quality cytoreduction with low early mortality and a reduction in LOS, meeting or exceeding contemporary QI standards. Incorporating AKI and MDT uptake into routine audit supports comprehensive, program-level benchmarking.

articles.title: Perioperative Outcomes of Laparoscopic Rectopexy for the Treatment of Full-Thickness Rectal Prolapse: A singlecenter experience from Dhulikhel Hospital, Nepal.
articles.authors: Malla BR, Laudari U, Khadka D et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Complete rectal prolapse (CRP) is a full-thickness circumferential protrusion of the rectum through the anal canal that significantly impairs quality of life. Laparoscopic rectopexy has emerged as the preferred abdominal approach because of its favorable perioperative outcomes. However, evidence from Nepal remains limited.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the perioperative outcomes of laparoscopic rectopexy in patients with complete rectal prolapse treated at a tertiary care center in Nepal.
METHOD: A retrospective observational study was conducted using a prospectively maintained database of patients who underwent laparoscopic rectopexy for complete rectal prolapse at Dhulikhel Hospital between January 2015 and July 2023. Patient demographics, operative details, perioperative outcomes, postoperative complications, length of hospital stay, and recurrence were reviewed and analyzed using descriptive statistics.
RESULT: Thirty-four patients (27 females and 7 males) underwent laparoscopic rectopexy during the study period. All patients presented with a protruding rectal mass per anus, with constipation and diarrhoea being the most common associated symptoms. Four patients who underwent laparoscopic ventral rectopexy had concomitant cystocele. The median operative time was 200 minutes, and the median postoperative hospital stay was 3 days. There was no perioperative mortality. During follow-up of up to 96 months, one patient developed recurrent rectal prolapse. Postoperative complications included urinary incontinence (11.8%), constipation (8.8%), discitis (2.9%), and postoperative pain (2.9%).
CONCLUSION: Laparoscopic rectopexy is a safe and effective treatment for complete rectal prolapse, with low perioperative morbidity, a short hospital stay, and a low recurrence rate. These findings support its feasibility as a minimally invasive treatment option in resource-limited settings.

articles.title: Study of First Trimester Uterine Artery Doppler Screening for Predicting Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes.
articles.authors: Lama S, Shrestha A, Shakya S
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy are the second leading cause of maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality, complicating 5-10% of pregnancies. Early detection and prophylactic interventions can reduce adverse outcomes. Firsttrimester uterine artery Doppler is a noninvasive tool for predicting and detecting abnormal placental perfusion.
OBJECTIVE: To determine the role of first-trimester uterine artery pulsatility index (PI) in predicting hypertensive disorders and adverse pregnancy outcomes and to evaluate pregnancy outcomes in patients with abnormal uterine artery Doppler who are treated with aspirin.
METHOD: A prospective cohort study was conducted at Dhulikhel Hospital for one year period. Uterine artery Doppler was performed at 11 to 13 weeks 6 days, and mean PI ≥ 1.5 was abnormal and normal if pulsatility index < 1.5. Women with PI ≥ 1.5 received low-dose aspirin 150 mg until 34 weeks. Participants were followed until delivery; maternal and fetal outcomes were recorded. Statistical analyses were done with p < 0.05 considered significant.
RESULT: Of 202 women, 177 (87.6%) had PI ≥ 1.5. Hypertension developed in 25 cases (12.4%), predominantly in the high-PI group. First-trimester PI had a sensitivity of 96% and specificity of 13.6% for predicting hypertension. Complications included hemolysis, elevated liver enzyme and low platelet (HELLP) and abruptio in 1%, oligohydramnios 7.43%, fetal growth restriction (FGR) 18.8% and stillbirth 0.5%.
CONCLUSION: First trimester uterine artery Doppler ultrasound is a valuable screening tool for early prediction of adverse pregnancy outcomes and should be implemented in prenatal care protocol. Starting low dose aspirin in early pregnancy improves placental perfusion reducing maternal and fetal complications.

articles.title: PM54 induces transcriptional collapse across cell-derived and patient-derived cancer models.
articles.authors: Diez MM, Fernández-Miranda I, Nuñez GS et al.
articles.abstract: Oncogenic transcriptional programs sustain malignant cell states and create therapeutic vulnerabilities in cancer. Here, we evaluated the antitumor activity and mechanism of PM54, a next-generation synthetic ecteinascidin analog, across diverse preclinical models. PM54 was tested in a 59-cell-line panel, mechanistic flow cytometry assays, short-term RNA sequencing in 32 cancer cell lines, six cell-derived xenografts (CDX), and three patient-derived orthotopic xenografts (PDOX). PM54 formed stable DNA adducts and showed broad low-nanomolar antiproliferative activity, with a mean half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) of 4.19 nM. Mechanistically, PM54 reduced nascent RNA synthesis, decreased RNA polymerase II levels, activated DNA-damage signaling, promoted S-phase accumulation, and triggered apoptosis. Short-term RNA sequencing revealed conserved repression of cell cycle, DNA repair, MYC-, mTOR-, and RNA polymerase II-associated programs. Pathway-level analyses identified two transcriptional response patterns, termed primed and adaptive patterns, differing in the extent of PM54-induced suppression of proliferative and oncogenic pathways. In vivo, PM54 reduced tumor growth and extended survival across six CDX models, with complete regressions in selected small-cell lung cancer (SCLC), melanoma, and prostate cancer models. In three PDOX models, PM54 reduced tumor burden by 81% in an experimentally generated cisplatin-resistant high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma, 69% in ovarian clear cell carcinoma, and 84% in gastric adenocarcinoma. These findings support evaluation of PM54 as a transcription-targeting therapeutic.

articles.title: CARM1-expressing ovarian cancers are selectively sensitive to HSP70 inhibition.
articles.authors: Kumari S, Gupta S, Jamil A et al.
articles.abstract: High-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) remains the most lethal gynecologic malignancy, emphasizing the need for new targeted therapies. We recently identified CARM1-expressing HGSOCs as a distinct molecular subset associated with poor prognosis. To uncover therapeutic vulnerabilities in this subgroup, we performed a small-molecule inhibitor screen and identified the molecular chaperone heat shock protein 70 (HSP70) as a selective target in CARM1-high epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) cells. Pharmacological inhibition of HSP70 suppressed the growth of CARM1-expressing cells but not CARM1-knockout or normal epithelial cells, confirming on-target selectivity. Mechanistically, coactivator-associated arginine methyltransferase 1 (CARM1) regulates expression of multiple HSP70 co-chaperone genes from the DNAJ family without affecting total HSP70 expression. A newly developed HSP70 inhibitor, AP-4-139B, significantly reduced tumor growth in CARM1-high xenografts. Importantly, AP-4-139B was well tolerated with no detectable toxicity. Together, these results identify CARM1 as a key regulator of the HSP70 co-chaperone network and reveal HSP70 inhibition as a selective and well-tolerated therapeutic strategy for CARM1-expressing ovarian cancers.

articles.title: Racial Disparities in Postpartum Morbidity and Mortality: A Systematic Review of Structural and Healthcare Systems Factors With AI/ML Applications.
articles.journal: International journal of MCH and AIDS
articles.authors: Baba D, Mmamelu P
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Racial disparities in maternal and postpartum health remain substantial in the United States. In 2024, the maternal mortality rate among non-Hispanic Black women was 44.8 deaths per 100,000 live births, compared with 14.2 among non-Hispanic White women. This systematic review synthesized contemporary evidence on racial disparities in postpartum morbidity and mortality, contributing structural and healthcare factors, emerging artificial intelligence and machine-learning applications, and interventions intended to improve postpartum outcomes and equity.
METHODS: This systematic review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. The evidence synthesis focused on U.S.-based primary empirical studies and authoritative government surveillance and analytic sources addressing maternal and postpartum outcomes, racial and ethnic disparities, structural and social determinants of health, healthcare access, artificial intelligence and machine-learning applications, and interventions relevant to postpartum health. We used systematic and scoping reviews for citation identification and contextual interpretation but did not count them as independent primary evidence. Because of substantial heterogeneity in study designs, populations, exposures, and outcomes, findings were synthesized narratively.
RESULTS: The evidence demonstrated persistent racial and ethnic disparities across maternal mortality, severe maternal morbidity and postpartum hemorrhage, peripartum cardiomyopathy and hypertensive disorders, postpartum mental health, and access to postpartum care. In 2024, non-Hispanic Black women experienced a maternal mortality rate approximately 3.2 times that of non-Hispanic White women. Pregnancy-related mortality surveillance further showed that a substantial proportion of deaths occurred beyond 42 days after pregnancy, underscoring the importance of care throughout the…
CONCLUSIONS AND GLOBAL HEALTH IMPLICATIONS: Persistent racial disparities in U.S. maternal and postpartum health likely reflect intersecting clinical, healthcare-system, socioeconomic, and structural factors. Reducing these inequities requires sustained postpartum surveillance and care, rigorous evaluation of interventions, attention to structural determinants, culturally responsive mental-health services, and transparent validation of emerging predictive technologies across diverse populations.

articles.title: Impact of Congenital Uterovaginal Anomalies on Maternal and Fetal Outcomes at a Tertiary Hospital in Punjab: A Prospective Observational Study.
articles.authors: Kaur J, Grover S, Deepika
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Congenital uterovaginal anomalies result from abnormal formation, fusion, or resorption of the Müllerian ducts during embryogenesis. They may remain asymptomatic or present with abnormal uterine bleeding, dyspareunia, subfertility, recurrent pregnancy loss, preterm birth, or fetal malpresentation. This study evaluated maternal and fetal outcomes among pregnant women with congenital uterovaginal anomalies at a tertiary referral hospital.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This single-center prospective observational comparative study was conducted in the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, Government Medical College and its associated tertiary-care hospital, Amritsar, Punjab, India, from April 1, 2022 to March 31, 2025. Consecutive total-enumeration sampling included all eligible singleton pregnancies with a previously diagnosed anomaly or an anomaly identified during the index pregnancy, delivery, or cesarean section. Multiple pregnancies were excluded. All 32 eligible women were included; therefore, no a priori sample-size calculation was performed. Maternal and fetal outcomes were summarized descriptively and compared with contemporaneous aggregate hospital data for pregnant women without a documented uterovaginal anomaly. Odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated, and categorical outcomes were assessed using Pearson's chi-square test or Fisher's exact test, as appropriate. A two-sided p-value <0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Among 5,407 pregnancies/deliveries recorded during the study period, 32 women had a congenital uterovaginal anomaly (hospital-detected prevalence, 0.59%). Most participants (78.13%) were aged 21-35 years. Arcuate uterus was the most frequent anomaly (28.13%), followed by bicornuate and septate uteri (21.88% each). A history of subfertility was present in 40.63% of women, and 43.75% had experienced a previous preterm birth. During the index pregnancy, three spontaneous abortions (9.38%) and two…
CONCLUSION: Congenital uterovaginal anomalies should be considered in women with unexplained subfertility, recurrent pregnancy loss, recurrent preterm birth, or fetal malpresentation. Early recognition permits individualized counselling, targeted antenatal surveillance, and delivery planning. Because many anomalies in this cohort were detected only during cesarean delivery, careful documentation and postpartum counselling are essential to guide the management of future pregnancies.

articles.title: Emerging antimicrobial resistance among uropathogens causing urinary tract infections in pregnant women: a retrospective study from Saudi Arabia.
articles.authors: Akhtar MS, Muyidi AA, Alqhtani R et al.
articles.abstract: It is evident that urinary tract infections (UTIs) can lead to poor maternal and perinatal outcomes. We designed this study to assess the susceptibility patterns of urinary pathogens to antimicrobials, along with their applicability for the mother and fetus, to ensure effective UTI treatment during pregnancy. This retrospective study was conducted to assess bacterial UTIs in the inpatient department of a tertiary care teaching hospital in Saudi Arabia. A total of 154 pregnant women with a confirmed case of UTI were included. Urine samples were collected by the midstream urine sampling method as per the standard procedure. We observed that around 52% of participants were in the 26-35 age group. The most common isolate was Escherichia coli (58.44%), followed by Klebsiella pneumoniae (22.73%) and Streptococcus group B (3.90%). Considering the best choices in pregnancy for Escherichia coli isolates, nitrofurantoin (100%) showed the highest efficacy among participants, followed by fosfomycin (88.8%), amoxicillin-clavulanic acid (84.28%), and cefotaxime intravenously (90%). In prenatal care, it is of the utmost importance to regularly evaluate the susceptibility and resistance pattern of antimicrobials to UTI-related pathogens during the course of pregnancy in order to provide optimal therapy for both mothers and infants.

articles.title: Validation of Interstitial Lung Disease Coding in US Claims Data in Patients with Solid Tumors.
articles.authors: Shen M, Wang S, Schneeweiss S et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The validity of ILD coding in US claims data among patients with cancer remains unclear.
METHODS: We conducted a study to test the validity of ILD coding in claims data in patients with lung, breast, ovarian, endometrial, cervical, or colorectal cancer. We used electronic health record (EHR) data from the Mass General Brigham Health Care System linked with Medicare, Medicaid, and commercial claims data from 01/01/2017 to 12/31/2024. The base algorithm required two ICD-10-CM codes for ILD, each 7 to 180 days apart. Several nested algorithms additionally requiring ILD coding by a pulmonologist, ILD-relevant procedure, excluding autoimmune diseases, and requiring chemo/immunotherapy treatment were defined. The positive predictive values (PPVs) of each claims-based algorithm were calculated against the reference standard established through chart review by pulmonologists.
RESULTS: The cohort consisted of 360 patients. PPV of the base algorithm was 59% (95% confidence interval: 53%-64%). The algorithm additionally requiring ILD-relevant procedure with chemo- or immunotherapy administration and excluding those with autoimmune conditions was 64% (57%-71%). The PPV of base algorithm among patients with colorectal cancer was the lowest - 38% (24%-52%). The PPVs improved meaningfully when the index diagnosis of ILD was coded by a pulmonologist, ranging from 78-88% across different algorithms.
CONCLUSION: We found that, in patients diagnosed with lung, breast, gynecologic, or colorectal cancer, claims-based ILD diagnoses demonstrated moderate to low alignment with a reference standard by expert chart review. It can be improved when ILD is coded by a pulmonologist, though at the cost of substantially fewer cases of ILD identified.

articles.title: Limited predictive value of second-to-third trimester complete blood count-derived inflammatory indices for preeclampsia: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics & gynecology and reproductive biology: X
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol X
articles.authors: Suntipap M, Kassayanan P, Nontaprom K et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the discriminatory performance of seven complete blood count (CBC)-derived inflammatory indices for preeclampsia (PE) and their incremental value beyond a primary maternal clinical comparator.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included singleton pregnancies with routine CBC testing between 26.0 and 36.9 weeks of gestation at a tertiary hospital in Thailand. Pregnancies with PE or eclampsia were compared with normotensive pregnancies. Discrimination was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis and logistic regression. Incremental value beyond a model comprising maternal age, body mass index, gestational age at CBC measurement, primigravidity, and pregestational diabetes was evaluated, with false discovery rate correction for multiple testing.
RESULTS: Among 8982 pregnancies, 276 (3.1%) were complicated by PE or eclampsia. CBC testing occurred at a median gestational age of 32.1 weeks. Individual indices showed limited discrimination, with AUCs ranging from 0.438 to 0.513 in the primary direction. NLR, MLR, and SIRI were lower among pregnancies with PE. After adjustment, SIRI reached nominal statistical significance, while NLR and MLR showed similar inverse estimates; none remained significant after false discovery rate correction. The primary maternal clinical comparator had an AUC of 0.723. Adding any individual index increased the AUC by no more than 0.0037 and provided minimal incremental net benefit.
CONCLUSIONS: CBC-derived inflammatory indices showed limited standalone discrimination for PE and negligible incremental value beyond the primary maternal clinical comparator. These findings do not support their use as standalone or incremental markers of PE risk at this gestational window.

articles.title: Metabolic and hormonal biomarkers in pregnancies with polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (formerly polycystic ovary syndrome): a nested prospective cohort study with longitudinal sub-analysis.
articles.authors: Tantanavipas S, Neven ACH, Alesi S et al.
articles.abstract:
STUDY QUESTION: Do metabolic and hormonal biomarker profiles in early pregnancy and their longitudinal variations across gestation differ among women at high risk of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) with and without polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS, formerly polycystic ovary syndrome [PCOS]), and are they associated with maternal and neonatal complications?
SUMMARY ANSWER: Among pregnant women at high risk of GDM, PMOS was associated with persistently elevated free androgen index (FAI) throughout pregnancy, whereas no interaction between elevated FAI and PMOS status on maternal and neonatal complications was identified.
WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY: Insulin resistance and hyperandrogenism are important pathophysiologic features of PMOS and are also part of the physiological changes during normal pregnancy. Pregnancies with PMOS have been associated with a higher risk of maternal and neonatal complications than those without PMOS.
STUDY DESIGN SIZE DURATION: Nested prospective cohort study with longitudinal sub-analysis using pooled data from two international multicentre clinical trials (TOBOGM study and B2B&Me trial). A total of 151 pregnancies at high risk for GDM were included from January 2018 to December 2021.
PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS SETTING METHODS: At baseline (before 24 weeks' gestation), 151 pregnancies at high risk for GDM were included (65 PMOS and 86 non-PMOS). Longitudinal sub-analysis included 75 pregnancies (15 PMOS and 60 non-PMOS). Metabolic biomarkers (fasting plasma glucose [FPG], insulin, C-peptide) and hormonal biomarkers (testosterone, dihydrotestosterone [DHT], androstenedione [A4], sex hormone-binding globulin [SHBG], and anti-Mullerian hormone [AMH]) were measured to derive indices of insulin resistance (homeostatic model assessment for insulin resistance [HOMA-IR], quantitative insulin sensitivity check index [QUICKI], fasting glucose to insulin ratio [FGIR]) and FAI. These were assessed cross-sectionally and in exploratory longitudinal sub-analyses of a subset of participants across gestation using linear mixed-effects models. Interaction analyses explored whether biomarkers modified associations between PMOS and adverse maternal or neonatal outcomes.
MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE: PMOS was associated with higher pre-pregnancy and baseline BMI and greater insulin resistance (elevated fasting insulin, HOMA-IR, and FGIR, and lower QUICKI).…
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBERS: ACTRN12616000924459 and ACTRN12620001240932.

articles.title: 4P-model: A machine learning-driven approach to expand non-invasive prenatal testing for early risk stratification of placenta accreta spectrum via genome-wide cfDNA promoter profiling.
articles.authors: Hao R, Wang B, Zhang B et al.
articles.abstract: Placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) is a leading cause of life-threatening obstetric hemorrhage, yet early diagnosis remains challenging. Traditional non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT) is limited to fetal aneuploidy screening, while its potential for maternal placental disorders is underexplored. We conducted a multicenter nested case-control study to investigate whether machine learning-driven genome-wide cell-free DNA (cfDNA) promoter profiling, derived from routine NIPT data, could extend the utility of NIPT to enable early prediction and subtype risk stratification of PAS. NIPT data were analyzed from 1060 individuals with a history of uterine surgery (126 increta/percreta, 139 accreta, and 795 controls after propensity score matching). A training set of 280 participants was used for feature selection with recursive feature elimination across five machine learning algorithms, and the best-performing model was validated in an internal cohort, a PLUS cohort with deeper sequencing, and two external cohorts generated on independent platforms. Pairwise differential analyses identified 211 candidate genes with altered promoter coverage. After feature selection, we developed the 4P-model, a 15-gene multiclass risk stratification model, to differentiate increta/percreta, accreta, and controls with a macro-average AUC of 0.973. Robust performance was reproduced across three NIPT platforms and the PLUS cohort, with AUCs of 0.882-0.946. These findings support that machine learning facilitates the translation of genome-wide cfDNA promoter signals embedded in NIPT data into early prediction and risk stratification of PAS. This noninvasive and scalable approach extends the diagnostic window, offering a clinically feasible tool for timely referral, improving perinatal outcomes.

articles.title: Aging-related immune remodeling in ovarian cancer: endocrine cues, cellular senescence, and tumor-immune crosstalk.
articles.authors: Wang J, Yang X, Huang W et al.
articles.abstract: Ovarian cancer is diagnosed predominantly after menopause, but chronological age, reproductive aging, cellular senescence, immunosenescence, and treatment-related immune dysfunction are frequently conflated. This overlap obscures whether immune phenotypes arise from aging, tumor histotype, therapy, or tumor-derived signals and limits the interpretation of age-associated biomarkers and treatment studies. This narrative review critically evaluates how menopause-associated endocrine remodeling, stromal and cellular senescence, senescence-associated secretory phenotype factors, and IL-6, CXCL8, TNF-α, and IL-1β signaling may interact with the ovarian-cancer immune microenvironment. Histotype-defining genomic pathways, including TP53 alteration, homologous-recombination deficiency, and KRAS-MAPK signaling, are separated from mechanisms plausibly modified by aging. Evidence is interpreted according to four contexts: human ovarian cancer, non-malignant human ovary or pelvic tissue, ovarian cell and animal models, and indirect studies from other cancers or organs; age-resolved findings are considered separately. Human evidence supports marked heterogeneity in immune infiltration, T-cell dysfunction, suppressive myeloid programs, and cytokine signaling, but direct age-resolved clinical evidence remains limited. Tumor-driven immune escape, therapy-induced senescence, and systemic immunosenescence can generate overlapping phenotypes and require explicit separation in study design and interpretation. This review highlights an evidence framework based on histotype, tissue compartment, treatment exposure, functional age, and longitudinal sampling. Progress requires prospective cohorts that include older and frail adults and jointly assess tumor biology, immune state, treatment toxicity, and clinical outcome.

articles.title: Periconceptional Uptake of Folic Acid and Associated Factors Among Pregnant Women at Soroti Regional Referral Hospital, Uganda.
articles.authors: Atwijukire A, Namujju J
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Periconceptional folic acid supplementation reduces the risk of neural tube defects, but timely uptake remains low in many low- and middle-income settings.
PURPOSE: To determine the prevalence of preconceptional and first-trimester folic acid uptake and to identify factors associated with uptake among pregnant women attending antenatal care at Soroti Regional Referral Hospital, Uganda.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: An analytical cross-sectional study was conducted among 179 pregnant women attending antenatal care between 14 March and 23 April 2024. Folic acid uptake was self-reported. Data were collected using a researcher-administered structured questionnaire and analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 27. Multivariable binary logistic regression was used as an association model, and adjusted odds ratios (aORs), 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and p values are reported.
RESULTS: Preconceptional folic acid uptake was 10.1% (18/179; 95% CI 6.5%-15.3%), while 54.7% (98/179; 95% CI 47.4%-61.9%) reported first-trimester uptake. Knowledge of folic acid benefits was associated with higher odds of preconceptional uptake, but the estimate was imprecise because only 18 women reported this outcome (aOR 19.51, 95% CI 2.40-158.51; p=0.005). For first-trimester uptake, first antenatal care attendance at 4-6 months rather than 1-3 months was associated with lower odds (aOR 0.075, 95% CI 0.033-0.170; p<0.001), while knowledge of folic acid benefits was associated with higher odds (aOR 3.50, 95% CI 1.40-8.75; p=0.007).
CONCLUSION: In this single-center, cross-sectional study based on self-reported information, preconceptional folic acid uptake was very low, and almost half of the participants did not report first-trimester uptake. Knowledge of folic acid benefits and earlier first antenatal care attendance were associated with timely uptake; these associations are not causal, and estimates for preconceptional uptake are imprecise and should be interpreted with caution.

articles.title: Public financing, external assistance and household health payments: a causal machine learning analysis of 173 countries, 2000-2023.
articles.authors: Alraeesi R, Alsawalqa RO, Khan Y
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Out-of-pocket (OOP) payments remain the dominant health financing mechanism in many countries while development assistance for health is contracting. Existing cross-country evidence on financing composition and household payments is weakened by an accounting identity linking regressors to the outcome and by the allocation of financing to high-burden settings.
METHODS: We analyzed 4,141 country-year observations from 173 countries (2000-2023) using the WHO Global Health Expenditure Database and Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) indicators. Government and external shares of current health expenditure (CHE) were entered jointly, so each effect represents a reallocation from domestic private financing. The primary outcome was per capita real out-of-pocket spending. Double machine learning was applied across three specifications, culminating in a within-country design with three-year lags, pre-treatment covariates, and a baseline adjustment. Inference was country-cluster-robust.
RESULTS: Within countries, reallocating 10 percentage points from private to government financing was associated with 11.4% lower out-of-pocket spending per capita (95% confidence interval [CI: 7.9-14.8]), and reallocating to external financing was associated with 14.7% lower spending (11.2-18.0); the difference was not significant (p = 0.075). Conventional specifications overstated these effects by 2.6-2.9-fold. Share-based estimates matched the value implied by the accounting identity. Results were robust across all sensitivity analyses. No effects on tuberculosis, Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV), or maternal mortality were detected, and regional estimates did not support a policy typology.
CONCLUSION: Shifting financing toward pooled government or external sources is associated with lower household payments, but by far less than cross-country estimates suggest. Financing targets and assessments of aid withdrawal should rely on evidence from within the country.

articles.title: Explainable machine learning and multivariable logistic regression for identifying prevalent self-reported physician-diagnosed chronic lung disease in postmenopausal women: development and multi-cohort external validation.
articles.authors: Du C, Xue N, Dang L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic lung disease (CLD) is an important cause of morbidity among postmenopausal women, yet simple non-invasive community screening tools are lacking. We aimed to develop and externally validate an interpretable multivariable prediction model for identifying prevalent self-reported physician-diagnosed CLD in this population.
METHODS: We analyzed postmenopausal women from the US Health and Retirement Study (HRS; development n = 4,578, internal validation n = 1,962), with external validation in the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA; n = 4,574) and a Chinese clinical cohort (n = 650). The primary outcome was prevalent self-reported or clinically recorded physician-diagnosed CLD, including chronic bronchitis, emphysema, or COPD where available. Predictors were selected via nested LASSO penalization. Twelve candidate statistical and machine-learning algorithms were benchmarked; the primary multivariable logistic regression model was evaluated on native uncalibrated probabilities at a locked screening threshold (9.81%) across discrimination, calibration, and clinical net benefit.
RESULTS: The current 9-predictor model retained smoking status, self-rated health, arthritis, heart disease, osteoporosis, basic activities of daily living difficulty, depressive symptoms, physical activity, and employment. The multivariable logistic regression model achieved AUROCs of 0.771 (95% CI, 0.748-0.793) in HRS development, 0.769 (0.734-0.803) in internal validation, 0.762 (0.735-0.790) in ELSA external validation, and 0.693 (0.634-0.750) in the Chinese cohort. Current smoking and poor self-rated health showed the strongest associations with prevalent CLD. In the Chinese clinical cohort, the model exhibited severe calibration underestimation (observed-to-expected ratio 2.763), demonstrating negative external validation driven by spectrum bias between community and hospital-based settings.
CONCLUSION: A parsimonious 9-predictor logistic regression model achieves acceptable discrimination and calibration across community cohorts for identifying prevalent self-reported physician-diagnosed CLD among community-dwelling postmenopausal women. However, direct transport to hospital-based settings is not supported without local recalibration because of pronounced spectrum bias.

articles.title: Fetal structural and chromosomal anomalies and cesarean delivery for non-reassuring fetal status: A population-based study in Central New York.
articles.authors: Rojas-Mendez P, Sampson R, Wojtowycz M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prior studies suggest higher cesarean delivery (CD) rates among pregnancies complicated by congenital anomalies; however, the contribution of specific indications, particularly CD coded as non-reassuring fetal status (NRFS), remains understudied.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between fetal anomalies and the likelihood of CD coded as NRFS, and to characterize this association across joint categories of small-for-gestational-age (SGA) and preterm birth.
STUDY DESIGN: This retrospective cohort study used data from the New York Statewide Perinatal Data System, including 220,368 deliveries ≥20 weeks' gestation from 2011 to 2023. The primary outcome was CD coded as NRFS as the sole indication. The primary exposure was the presence of ≥1 structural or chromosomal fetal anomaly, analyzed as a composite and by anomaly subgroup. Logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and absolute risk differences were calculated to aid clinical interpretation. Joint-category analyses were performed to evaluate the association across combinations of SGA and preterm birth. Bivariate analyses compared baseline characteristics by anomaly status.
RESULTS: Among 220,368 deliveries, 904 (0.4%) were classified as having a composite anomaly. The rate of CD coded as NRFS was higher among pregnancies with a composite anomaly (9.8% vs. 3.7%; relative risk, 2.69), corresponding to an absolute risk difference of 6.2 percentage points. After adjustment, composite anomaly status was associated with higher odds of CD coded as NRFS (aOR, 2.72). The magnitude of association varied by anomaly type, with higher odds observed in omphalocele (aOR, 4.66), chromosomal disorders other than trisomy 21 (T21) (aOR, 4.09), and congenital heart disease (aOR, 2.97). In joint-category analyses, the magnitude of association varied across combinations of composite anomaly status, SGA, and preterm birth.
CONCLUSION: Selected fetal structural and chromosomal anomalies were associated with higher odds of CD coded as NRFS, after adjustment for intrapartum factors. This association varied by anomaly subtype and across joint categories defined by SGA and preterm birth. These associations may reflect both underlying fetal vulnerability and variation in clinical decision-making rather than physiologic intolerance to labor alone.

articles.title: Preoperative prognostic nutritional index, opioid-sparing anesthesia, and outcomes after gynecologic cancer surgery: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Yin D, He K, Wen G
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preoperative prognostic nutritional index (PNI) may identify patients at increased perioperative risk, but whether PNI is associated with differences in outcomes across anesthetic strategies remains uncertain.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 342 women undergoing surgery for ovarian, endometrial, or cervical cancer from 2019 to 2024. PNI was calculated as serum albumin (g/L) + 5 × absolute lymphocyte count (109/L); PNI < 45 was used as a prespecified pragmatic cutoff. A propofol-based total intravenous, opioid-sparing multimodal strategy, with regional or neuraxial analgesia when feasible, was compared with volatile-based anesthesia and opioid-centered analgesia. Outcomes included postoperative biomarkers, 30-day complications, return to intended oncologic therapy (RIOT) within 42 days, recurrence-free survival (RFS), and overall survival (OS). Regression models examined PNI-by-strategy interactions.
RESULTS: PNI < 45 was present in 156/342 patients (45.6%). Within this stratum, median postoperative day 3 CRP was 79.1 vs. 92.6 mg/L, major complications occurred in 18.8% vs. 43.3%, and timely RIOT occurred in 79.1% vs. 55.4% with opioid-sparing vs. conventional anesthesia, respectively. Reported 36-month RFS estimates were 72.8% vs. 36.5%. In the cancer-type-stratified adjusted Cox model, the low-PNI term in the conventional-anesthesia reference stratum was associated with RFS (adjusted HR 2.14, 95% CI 1.31-3.48), with a nominal PNI-by-strategy interaction for RFS (interaction HR 0.46, 95% CI 0.22-0.94; p = 0.033). The interaction was not significant for OS (p = 0.837) or after changing the PNI cutoff to 44 or 46.
CONCLUSIONS: Lower PNI was associated with greater perioperative and oncologic risk. The observed RFS interaction is exploratory and sensitive to PNI dichotomization; residual oncologic, procedural, and calendar-era confounding precludes causal interpretation. Prospective confirmation with continuous PNI modeling and detailed cancer-specific adjustment is required.

articles.title: Testosterone Therapy and Sexual Health in Men and Women: Is There a Role for Long-Acting Subcutaneous Pellets?
articles.authors: Rojas-Zambrano JG, Molina-Varas EA, Rojas-Zambrano A
articles.abstract: Testosterone influences sexual desire and sexual response in men and women, but the clinical reasons for prescribing it differ between the sexes. In men, treatment is reserved for symptomatic hypogonadism confirmed by repeated morning measurements, and placebo-controlled trials show improvements in libido and sexual activity, with smaller and less consistent effects on erectile function. In women, the indication with the strongest support is hypoactive sexual desire disorder after menopause, where randomized trials of transdermal testosterone show moderate gains in desire, arousal, orgasm, and satisfaction, along with less sexual distress. Subcutaneous testosterone pellets release the hormone for several months after a single office procedure and appeal to patients who prefer infrequent dosing. Most of the evidence for testosterone therapy, however, comes from transdermal and injectable preparations. Pellet studies in men describe steady release, a predictable duration of action, extrusion as the most frequent complication, and erythrocytosis that cannot be corrected by lowering the dose once the pellets are in place. The few randomized comparisons of pellets with other formulations were small, did not include transdermal testosterone, and were not designed around validated sexual-function outcomes. In women, pellets are used off-label, are often compounded, and can produce serum concentrations well above the female physiological range; current professional guidance advises against their use for hypoactive sexual desire disorder. This narrative review describes the physiology of testosterone in both sexes, the diagnostic criteria and validated instruments used to assess sexual function, the trial evidence for testosterone therapy, and the pharmacology, effectiveness, and safety of pellets. Pellets are a reasonable option for selected hypogonadal men who do not seek fertility, accept a formulation that cannot be quickly reversed, and agree to hematocrit monitoring. In women, current guidance does not support their use, and any exception requires informed consent, close monitoring, and acknowledgment that it departs from that guidance.

articles.title: Peripartum infective endocarditis in complex congenital heart disease: Melody valve infection after caesarean delivery.
articles.authors: Hopkins TM, Wander G, Tari S et al.
articles.abstract: We describe the pregnancy and postpartum course of a 26-year-old nulliparous woman with repaired double outlet right ventricle, ventricular septal defect, and severe pulmonary stenosis who was managed by a multidisciplinary pregnancy heart team. She underwent emergency caesarean delivery at 38 weeks. Her postpartum course was complicated by suspected pulmonary embolism and infective endocarditis of a Melody valve, requiring right ventricle-pulmonary artery conduit replacement. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges of postpartum cardiopulmonary symptoms in women with complex congenital heart disease and raises important questions regarding infective endocarditis prophylaxis in women with prosthetic cardiac material.

articles.title: Luteal phase support strategies in ovarian stimulation-intrauterine insemination cycles: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.authors: Yan X, Xu M, Su C et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Luteal phase support (LPS) is widely used in ovarian stimulation-intrauterine insemination (OS-IUI) cycles, but the comparative effectiveness of different LPS strategies remains uncertain. This study aimed to compare the effects of available LPS strategies on reproductive outcomes following OS-IUI.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, Scopus, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception to August 7, 2026 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating pharmacological LPS after OS-IUI. The primary outcome was clinical pregnancy, and secondary outcomes included ongoing pregnancy, live birth, biochemical pregnancy, multiple pregnancy, and miscarriage. Frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis was performed for outcomes forming connected evidence networks, while conventional pairwise meta-analysis was used when network analysis was not feasible. Treatment effects were expressed as risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Risk of bias was assessed using the revised Cochrane Risk of Bias tool for randomized trials (RoB 2), and certainty of evidence was evaluated using the Confidence in Network Meta-Analysis (CINeMA) framework or the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach, as appropriate.
RESULTS: 22 RCTs involving 4,994 women were included. For clinical pregnancy, 21 RCTs involving 4,547 women contributed to a network of 8 LPS strategies. The results showed that vaginal progesterone (VP) was associated with a significantly higher clinical pregnancy rate than no luteal phase support/placebo (NP) (RR = 1.27, 95% CI 1.09-1.50; Moderate certainty). For live birth, 4 RCTs involving 956 women showed that VP was associated with a higher live birth rate than NP (RR = 1.61, 95% CI 1.19-2.18; moderate certainty). Besides, VP combined with a GnRH agonist was associated with a lower multiple pregnancy rate than VP alone (RR = 0.29, 95% CI 0.10-0.85; very low certainty). No clear differences among LPS strategies were observed for ongoing pregnancy,…
CONCLUSION: In OS-IUI cycles, VP was associated with higher clinical pregnancy and live birth rates than NP. Compared with VP combined with a GnRH agonist, VP was associated with a higher multiple pregnancy rate, although the certainty of evidence was very low and this finding should be interpreted cautiously. Further well-designed RCTs are needed to confirm these findings and determine the optimal LPS strategy.

articles.title: Effect of radiofrequency therapy in the treatment of de novo dyspareunia at 4 to 12 months postpartum: a randomized clinical trial.
articles.authors: Box C, Carralero-Martínez A, Manresa M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obstetric pelvic floor trauma, including vaginal, perineal, and anal sphincter injuries, commonly causes postpartum perineal pain, which may persist for up to 12 months. As a result, sexual dysfunction is frequent, with dyspareunia being one of the most common symptoms.
OBJECTIVE: The main goal of this study is to assess radiofrequency (RF) therapy efficacy in women with de novo dyspareunia persisting 4 to 12 months postpartum, in terms of pain, sexual health, quality of life (QoL), and the effects that persist 6 months after treatment.
STUDY DESIGN: A total of 88 women presenting de novo dyspareunia due to obstetric lesions that persisted at 4 to 12 months postpartum were included in this double-blinded randomized clinical trial. The goal was to assess the effect of intravaginal and abdominal capacitive-resistive monopolar RF therapy in combination with self-performed daily perineal massage. The participants were divided into two groups, on-RF and off-RF, and received 5 sessions. In both groups, pain, QoL, sexual function, and pelvic floor dysfunction symptoms were assessed at baseline, after completing the study, and at 6 months. To assess the efficacy of RF therapy, the difference between baseline and postintervention numeric rating scale scores (the primary variable) and the secondary variables, sexual function and QoL, was compared between the intervention and control groups.
RESULTS: A total of 76 participants finished the intervention, 39 in the on-RF group and 37 in the off-RF group, and a total of 37 completed the 6-month follow-up. Patients in the on-RF group showed a greater reduction and ended with lower mean pain scores (standard deviation) [2.1 (1.9) vs 5.6 (2.1); P<.001] and greater improvement in sexual function and QoL.
CONCLUSION: Active RF therapy combined with patient-performed daily perineal massage significantly reduces pain levels in women with de novo postpartum dyspareunia to a greater extent than sham-RF therapy and daily perineal massage, and this effect seems to persist for at least 6 months after treatment as seen in the participants with available follow-up data.

articles.title: Real-world implementation of AI-assisted starting gonadotropin dosing in routine ovarian stimulation: an exposure-defined, propensity score-matched observational cohort study.
articles.authors: Xu H, Ma C, Feng G et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Starting gonadotropin dose selection in controlled ovarian stimulation is conventionally guided by clinician experience. This pilot, single-centre, exposure-defined, matched observational cohort study assessed the feasibility of deploying an artificial intelligence-assisted gonadotropin dosing tool (POvaStim) in routine practice, comparing clinicians using the tool versus conventional experience-based judgement. Because AI use was completely confounded with clinician group and clinician experience was not prospectively quantified, the independent contribution of the decision-support tool cannot be isolated.
METHODS: Consecutive women undergoing IVF/ICSI with a GnRH-antagonist protocol were treated between August 3 and December 31, 2022; only the starting dose was AI-assisted. One-to-one propensity score matching on body weight, ovarian reserve score and gonadotropin preparation yielded 119 matched pairs. Primary outcomes were cumulative clinical pregnancy and live birth per oocyte retrieval (data-lock 31 December 2024).
RESULTS: Cumulative clinical pregnancy occurred in 67 of 119 (56.3%) in the AI-assisted arm versus 76 of 119 (63.9%) in the control arm (risk difference -7.6%, 95% CI -20.0 to +4.8; P = 0.234), and cumulative live birth in 59 of 119 (49.6%) versus 60 of 119 (50.4%) (risk difference -0.8%, 95% CI -13.5 to +11.9; P = 0.897), counting the 16 women without an ascertainable outcome by the data-lock date as non-events. A complete-case analysis excluding these 16 women gave materially unchanged results. These wide confidence intervals do not exclude clinically important differences; the study was not an equivalence or non-inferiority trial. Starting-dose selection was substantially less variable in the AI-assisted arm (interquartile range 43% narrower; variance 2.43-fold lower, 95% CI 1.69-3.50). Gonadotropin exposure was nonetheless higher in the AI-assisted arm (+27.4 IU/day). POvaStim recommended similar doses in both arms: the AI-assisted dose was rounded upward from it in 94.1% of cycles, while control-arm clinicians, unaware of the recommendation, more often prescribed below it. Elective freeze-all, chiefly for hyperstimulation prevention, was more frequent in the AI-assisted arm (46.2% versus 34.5%; risk…
