articles.abstract: Intrauterine insemination (IUI) is a widely used fertility treatment with numerous add-ons and protocol variations, many of which are offered empirically. This guideline systematically reviews the available evidence to provide evidence-based recommendations for their clinical use, aiming to optimise treatment outcomes, standardise practice and facilitate future research. A total of 25 interventions were evaluated, including follicular monitoring, LH surge detection, catheter type, bladder filling, insemination technique, operator experience, cervical mucus aspiration, endometrial scratching, hydrotubation, ovarian stimulation, ovulation triggering and timing, intrauterine infusions, medications affecting endometrial receptivity or uterine contractility, double insemination, ultrasound guidance, bed rest and luteal phase support. A systematic literature search identified 154 randomised controlled trials involving 34,825 participants. Meta-analyses were conducted where feasible. However, the limited availability of adequately powered trials and the predominantly low-quality evidence restrict the certainty of most recommendations. These limitations should be clearly communicated during patient counselling. Future research should prioritise high-quality trials evaluating the effectiveness of IUI add-ons in specific patient populations, considering underlying infertility diagnoses.

articles.title: Food Environments, Structural Disadvantage, and Risk of Gestational Diabetes and Preeclampsia.
articles.journal: Women's health issues : official publication of the Jacobs Institute of Women's Health
articles.authors: Amoah AA, Wychgram C, Curriero FC et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity is a modifiable risk factor for gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and preeclampsia, conditions that elevate maternal morbidity, mortality, and long-term cardiovascular risk. Lifestyle interventions are standard preconception recommendations for risk reduction, yet their feasibility is shaped by neighborhood and structural contexts. To explore these relationships, we evaluated associations of GDM and preeclampsia with neighborhood food environments, access to vendors authorized to accept benefits from the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC), and racialized economic segregation.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using electronic medical records from individuals with live births (N = 12,635) at three Maryland hospitals (2016-2021). Neighborhood exposures included the following: 1) food swamps-areas with a high density of unhealthy food retailers relative to healthy ones-measured using the modified Retail Food Environment Index (mRFEI); 2) racialized economic segregation, measured using the Index of Concentration at the Extremes (ICE); and 3) WIC vendor density per 1,000 residents. All exposures were modeled in tertiles, with the lowest tertile (Q1) indicating the most disadvantaged or lowest access and the highest (Q3) as reference. We used multivariable logistic regression with generalized estimating equations to assess associations with GDM and preeclampsia.
RESULTS: Lower WIC access (lowest vs. highest tertile: adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.20; 95% confidence interval [CI] [1.02, 1.41]) and greater neighborhood disadvantage (ICE Q1 vs. Q3: aOR, 1.21; 95% CI [1.01, 1.44]) were associated with higher odds of GDM. No neighborhood measures were consistently associated with preeclampsia.
CONCLUSION: Structural disadvantage and lower WIC vendor density were associated with higher odds of GDM but not preeclampsia. Expanding nutrition assistance infrastructure and addressing neighborhood disadvantage may improve maternal cardiometabolic health.

articles.title: First trimester cervical length and cervical change in the prediction of prematurity related outcomes.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
articles.authors: Souka AP, Rouvali A, Antsaklis P et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transvaginal cervical length (CL) measurement in the second trimester is an established screening tool for identifying pregnant individuals at risk of spontaneous preterm birth, but the clinical value of the first trimester cervical length (CL) remains controversial. As the majority of the studies focus on a single time-point measurement, less is known about the prognostic value of the change in CL between the first and the second trimester in predicting prematurity.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate first trimester CL as well as the change in CL between the first and the second trimester as predictors of late miscarriage, cervical shortening at anytime before 32 weeks, cerclage insertion and spontaneous preterm delivery (SPD).
STUDY DESIGN: This retrospective study included 6,116 singleton pregnancies with transvaginal cervical evaluation at 11-14 weeks and/or at 18-24 weeks and documented pregnancy outcomes. Outcomes assessed were late miscarriage at 16-24 weeks, cervical shortening (≤15 mm and ≤25 mm) before 32 weeks, placement of cervical cerclage, spontaneous preterm delivery before 28 weeks (SPD 28), before 32 weeks (SPD 32) and before 37 weeks (SPD 37), and a combined adverse outcome (CAO) including all the above. Prognostic accuracy was assessed using multivariate logistic regression and ROC curve analysis, adjusting for maternal characteristics and obstetric history.
RESULTS: First-trimester CL was significantly associated with late miscarriage (p=0.049), SPD 37 (p<0.014), cervical shortening (p<0.01), cerclage placement (p<0.01), and CAO (p<0.01). The risk increased nonlinearly, with a marked rise below 30 mm. For each 1 mm of decrease in first-trimester CL, the risk of CAO increased by 26%. Overall, mean CL change between first and second trimesters was minimal (-1.7%); however, pregnant individuals with CAO exhibited a significantly steeper decline compared to the ones without CAO (-9.4% vs -0.03%, p<0.001). The combination of second-trimester CL and CL change outperformed single-timepoint measurements in predicting late miscarriage (p=0.015) and cervical shortening (p<0,001).
CONCLUSIONS: Shorter first-trimester CL and pronounced cervical shortening between the first and second trimester are significantly associated with a spectrum of the adverse pregnancy outcomes related to prematurity.

articles.title: Endometrial fertility. Management of adenomyosis in gynecology and infertility.
articles.authors: Somigliana E, Fornelli G, Benaglia L et al.
articles.abstract: Adenomyosis has long been underrecognized, with limited evidence guiding its clinical management. In the last decade, the introduction of the Morphological Uterus Sonographic Assessment (MUSA) criteria and the growing recognition of its strong association with endometriosis have substantially changed the understanding of the disease. In women seeking pregnancy, treatment options remain challenging. Surgery is invasive, technically demanding, and associated with recurrence and potential obstetric risks, while hormonal therapies are incompatible with conception and have not demonstrated a benefit for infertility. IVF may overcome some adverse effects of adenomyosis on fertility, but its impact on embryo implantation remains problematic. Accordingly, available evidence suggests a possible reduction in live birth rates following IVF. However, current studies are limited by potential confounders. Studies investigating the use of medical pretreatment before IVF, including GnRH agonists, dienogest, or levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine systems, remain insufficient and inconsistent. Further prospective studies and randomized controlled trials using standardized inclusion criteria are needed.

articles.title: Cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 inhibitors in non-breast malignancies.
articles.authors: Ghidini A, Garassino I, Bukovec R et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Selective CDK4/6 inhibitors established a major role in breast cancer, but activity across other malignancies varies substantially. This structured narrative review asks whether apparently similar cell-cycle alterations confer clinically meaningful dependence and contrasts controlled with signal-finding evidence.
METHODS: In this structured narrative review we synthesized prospective non-breast CDK4/6-inhibitor studies represented in the authors' existing literature collection and expanded extraction table, prioritizing randomized comparisons, histology, biomarker strategy, clinical benefit, survival maturity, and toxicity. Published 2026 trial reports and meeting results were selectively verified.
RESULTS: The most compelling randomized signal is in dedifferentiated liposarcoma: SARC041 (108 randomized patients) improved median progression-free survival (PFS; 9.67 vs 1.52 months; HR 0.39, 95% CI 0.25-0.59), whereas overall survival (OS) remains inconclusive (HR 0.55, 95% CI 0.28-1.07), with crossover complicating interpretation. Endocrine combinations show encouraging phase II results in low-grade serous ovarian and estrogen receptor-positive endometrial cancers. Negative randomized and alteration-selected basket studies caution against extrapolating from isolated pathway lesions. Emerging clinical activity with other inhibitors, including dalpiciclib, requires controlled confirmation.
CONCLUSIONS: Clinical development beyond breast cancer should be organized by lineage-specific dependence, demonstrable RB-axis function, rational combination partners, and endpoints suited to cytostatic treatment. Evidence strength, competing options, and toxicity must determine whether a promising signal warrants practice change.

articles.title: Pain assessment and analgesic use following the implementation of a pain management protocol during IVF: a prospective study.
articles.journal: Journal of gynecology obstetrics and human reproduction
articles.authors: Hill E, Cathelain A, Beaucamp F et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The ENDALGOFIV 1 study evaluated pain during IVF in patients with and without endometriosis, showing stable pain levels in patients with endometriosis but increased pain in those without endometriosis. Following the implementation of a standardized analgesic protocol, this study aimed to assess pain management in real-life clinical practice by evaluating pain levels and actual analgesic use during IVF, and comparing pain levels with those observed in the ENDALGOFIV 1 study.
DESIGN: A prospective, monocentric, observational cohort study with a historical control group (ENDALGOFIV 1) was conducted in the Lille University Hospital ART department from January 2023 to March 2024.
EXPOSURE: Pain assessment questionnaires using validated scales were completed at key points in the IVF course: before starting treatments, at the end of stimulation and on the day of oocyte retrieval.
MAIN RESULTS: Data from 278 patients in ENDALGOFIV 1 (73 with endometriosis) and 186 patients in ENDALGOFIV 2 (47 with endometriosis) were analyzed. Baseline pain scores were similar between groups, except for higher catastrophizing scores in ENDALGOFIV 2. After oocyte retrieval, pain scores were higher in ENDALGOFIV 2 than in ENDALGOFIV 1 (numeric pain rating score: 3.77 vs. 3.12, p = 0.01). This difference remained significant in patients without endometriosis (3.82 vs. 3.13, p < 0.01), but not in those with endometriosis. During stimulation, analgesic use was numerically higher among patients with endometriosis than among those without endometriosis (34.6% vs. 17.3%, p = 0.097). After retrieval, only half of patients reported taking the prescribed treatment.
CONCLUSION: Pain management during IVF remains challenging. Higher pain levels after oocyte retrieval were observed in ENDALGOFIV 2, particularly among patients without endometriosis. However, the low uptake of prescribed analgesics, together with the historical control design, limits the interpretation of these findings and prevents attributing the observed differences solely to the new protocol. These results highlight the importance of assessing actual analgesic use in clinical practice and support the need for more individualized pain management strategies.

articles.title: Metabolic Profiles and Insulin Therapy Requirements among Pregnant Women with Gestational Diabetes Mellitus and Type 2 Diabetes across Self-Identified Race/Ethnic Groups in Brooklyn, New York, United States.
articles.authors: Singh S, Martingano D, Mastrogiannis DS et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and type 2 diabetes (T2 DM) present varying metabolic patterns across populations, yet the extent to which these differences appear at diagnosis remains unclear. This study examines whether baseline metabolic profiles differ among pregnant women from diverse racial and ethnic backgrounds. Our objective was to determine whether these metabolic differences may influence diabetes management during pregnancy.
STUDY DESIGN: We conducted a 2-year retrospective study of 200 insulin-naïve women at NYU Langone Hospital at Brooklyn, NY, diagnosed with GDM and/or T2 DM in the third trimester. The diagnostic criteria were standard two-step testing, 50-g glucose challenge (1-h GCT, cut-off 135 mg/dL) followed by a 100-g oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT). Baseline fasting laboratories included glucose, C-peptide, and lipid profiles, with insulin sensitivity estimated using IS-HOMA (C-peptide). Management followed standardized diet, exercise, metformin when appropriate, and weight-based basal-bolus insulin titrated to fasting glucose levels 85 to 90 mg/dL and 2-hour postprandial 115 to 120 mg/dL.
RESULTS: Significant race/ethnicity-specific metabolic phenotype differences emerged. Hispanic-Latina women and American-born Black women had higher BMI, higher fasting C-peptide, and lower insulin sensitivity, whereas Asian (Southeast and East Indian) and Caribbean/Haitian Black women showed lower C-peptide but higher insulin sensitivity. Lipid patterns also varied. There was no statistically significant difference in birthweight across groups.
CONCLUSION: In this cohort, we observed distinct metabolic profiles across racial and ethnic groups at the time of GDM or T2 DM diagnosis in pregnancy. These differences, particularly in insulin sensitivity, C-peptide levels, and BMI, suggest that metabolic phenotype varies meaningfully by race and ethnicity. Incorporating these patterns into clinical decision-making may help refine diabetes management strategies and support more equitable perinatal outcomes.
KEY POINTS: · Baseline metabolic profiles differed across racial/ethnic groups.. · Insulin sensitivity and C-peptide showed distinct phenotype patterns.. · Birthweight did not vary significantly by race/ethnicity.. · Metabolic phenotypes may inform individualized diabetes management.. · Race/ethnicity shapes insulin needs and metabolic risk at diagnosis..

articles.title: Departure From Planned 39-Week Delivery for Fetal Congenital Heart Disease: Indications for Earlier Birth.
articles.authors: Packer CH, Ronai C, Carreon CK et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Delivery >39 weeks' gestation is recommended for fetuses with congenital heart disease (FCHD). However, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP), maternal diabetes and fetal growth restriction (FGR) are more common in these pregnancies and often necessitate early delivery. We evaluated indications for delivery at <39 weeks and examined maternal covariates, cardiac diagnoses and placental pathology.
STUDY DESIGN: This retrospective observational study included maternal-fetal dyads with prenatally diagnosed, structurally isolated, genetically unremarkable FCHD delivered at a single center. Gestational age and delivery indication were obtained from medical record. Placental pathology was assessed using Amsterdam criteria. Regression models evaluated associations with gestational age and neonatal mortality.
RESULTS: 46.3% (99/214) delivered <39 weeks; 65.6% (65/99) were due to maternal or fetal compromise, and 34.3% (33/99) to obstetric indications. HDP (20.1%) was strongly associated with <39-week delivery (32.3% vs 9.6%, p<0.001) and the greatest reduction in gestational age (-2.31 weeks, p<0.001). Multivariable analysis identified preeclampsia, type 2 diabetes, lower birthweight Z-score, and race as independent predictors of earlier delivery (p<0.05). Neonatal mortality was higher with maternal/fetal indications (15.7%) versus obstetric (5.4%) or elective FCHD delivery (5.6%) (p=0.02).
CONCLUSION: Nearly half of FCHD infants delivered before 39 weeks, largely due to maternal and placental disease, underscoring the importance of placental health in this population.

articles.title: Reproductive health in women in Britain from 2010 to 2024: findings from repeated, cross-sectional National Surveys of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal).
articles.authors: Pathak N, Gascoyne C, Hough A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Major policy and funding shifts threaten access to essential reproductive services and reproductive autonomy in Britain (England, Scotland, and Wales) amid growing attention towards hormone hesitancy and declining birth rates. We report on prevalence, changes, and sociodemographic differences in reproductive health indicators among women of reproductive age in Britain from 2010 to 2024.
METHODS: Britain's National Surveys of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal) are cross-sectional, nationally representative surveys (Natsal-3 Sept 6, 2010, to Aug 31, 2012; Natsal-4 Sept 20, 2022, to April 5, 2024). Using 3198 Natsal-4 probability sample participants (assigned female at birth, aged 16-54 years, and reported vaginal sex ever), we estimated weighted prevalences of key health indicators of reproductive autonomy: reporting no effective contraception use, hormonal contraception use, abortion, unplanned or ambivalent pregnancy, infertility, help-seeking for infertility, and fertility intentions, and compared these with Natsal-3. Age-adjusted regression assessed changes between Natsal-3 and Natsal-4 by sociodemographic subgroups. Using Natsal-4 combined probability and non-probability samples (N=7053), we examined associations with age, education, area-level deprivation, ethnicity, and country of birth.
FINDINGS: In Natsal-4, 18·5% (95% CI 16·6-20·7) of women at risk of unintended pregnancy reported not using any effective contraception, and 41·9% (33·8-50·6) of past-year pregnancies were scored as unplanned or ambivalent. The prevalence of ever having had an abortion increased from Natsal-3 to Natsal-4 (from 16·0% to 20·7%, age-adjusted odds ratio [OR] 1·35, 95% CI 1·18-1·55), whereas overall prevalences of other indicators were stable. Subgroup analyses showed declining overall hormonal contraception use in those younger than 35 years (eg, from 64·6% to 50·3% for those aged 16-24 years, OR 0·55, 95% CI 0·39-0·79). The proportion of those aged 16-44 years reporting definitely not wanting children more than doubled from Natsal-3 to Natsal-4 (from 7·7% to 16·6%; adjusted OR 1·66, 95% CI 1·28-2·16), driven by women younger than 35 years. In Natsal-4, women with below degree-level education, living in more deprived areas, or of Black, African, Caribbean, or Black British ethnicity were more likely to report no effective…
FUNDING: The Wellcome Trust, the Economic and Social Research Council, and the National Institute for Health and Care Research.

articles.title: Association of Excess Gestational Weight Gain with Neonatal Hypoglycemia.
articles.authors: Bailey EJ, Sibbald CA, Rhoades JS et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Neonatal hypoglycemia is a significant contributor to neonatal morbidity. Diabetes, preterm delivery, cesarean delivery, growth restriction, and maternal obesity have been shown to increase the risk. We hypothesized that excess gestational weight gain is associated with increased rates of neonatal hypoglycemia.
STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study of singleton, term deliveries in a single center between January 1, 2016 and December 31, 2021, excluding patients with preexisting or gestational diabetes. The primary outcome was incidence of neonatal hypoglycemia. Institute of Medicine guidelines were used to determine category of gestational weight gain based on pre-pregnancy body mass index. Secondary outcomes included rates of macrosomia and neonatal intensive care unit admission by gestational weight gain category. Multivariable logistic regression was used to adjust for potential confounders (macrosomia and pre-pregnancy obesity).
RESULTS: There were 23,902 term, singleton deliveries. Patients with excess gestational weight gain were more likely to be non-white, have undergone a cesarean delivery (CD) (29 vs. 22%, p < 0.001), have higher birthweight (3,522 vs. 3,333 g, p < 0.001), and have a higher pre-pregnancy body mass index (27 vs. 26, p < 0.001) compared with patients with appropriate gestational weight gain. The odds of neonatal hypoglycemia were significantly higher for women with excess gestational weight gain (adjusted odds ratio 1.28, 95% CI: 1.12-1.47). Odds of macrosomia and neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admissions were also increased. Conversely, appropriate weight gain was protective against neonatal hypoglycemia (adjusted odds ratio 0.73, 95 %: 0.63-0.85).
CONCLUSION: These data suggest that independent of maternal body mass index, macrosomia, or diabetes status, excess gestational weight gain is associated with an increased risk of neonatal hypoglycemia. Although more research is needed to elucidate the pathophysiology and confirm these findings, these data suggest that counseling on gestational weight gain should address a potential increased risk of neonatal hypoglycemia at birth with excess gestational weight gain.

articles.title: Association between seminal HPV DNA detection and bacterial profiles in infertile men.
articles.journal: Revista de investigacion clinica; organo del Hospital de Enfermedades de la Nutricion
articles.authors: Soto EP, González-Díaz CA, Romero BIR et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus (HPV) detection and seminal microbial dysbiosis are associated with impaired semen quality, through mechanisms involving oxidative stress and inflammation.
METHODS: Semen samples from infertile men were analyzed for HPV DNA using polymerase chain reaction (PCR). Predominant bacterial genus was identified through 16S rRNA gene PCR amplification and sequencing. Pro-inflammatory cytokine and oxidative stress markers were quantified. The dielectric properties of DNA were evaluated by electrical bioimpedance spectroscopy (EBiS).
RESULTS: Seminal HPV DNA was detected in 73% of semen samples. The Shannon-Wiener diversity index revealed significantly greater bacterial diversity in HPV DNA positive samples compared with HPV DNA negative samples (2.54 vs. 1.13, p<0.001). The most frequently identified bacterial genera were Enterococcus (34.5%), Pseudomonas (12.1%), and Escherichia (10.3%). The HPV DNA negative group exhibited a significantly higher relative abundance of Enterococcus than the HPV DNA positive group (62.5% vs. 23.8%, p<0.008). These microbial shifts were accompanied by increased pro-inflammatory cytokine levels, evidence of oxidative DNA damage, and poorer semen quality parameters.
CONCLUSIONS: Seminal HPV DNA associated changes in relative abundance of seminal bacteria may contribute to male infertility.

articles.title: Snapshot of pregnancy Hypertension and Preeclampsia content on TikTok - a look at themes and quality.
articles.authors: Sarker M, Jacobs E, Wiley R et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We analyzed the most viewed hypertensive disorders of pregnancy content on TikTok, specifically characterizing the themes, assessing the quality, and determining how metrics differs for healthcare provider created content.
STUDY DESIGN: We conducted a cross-sectional study of the top 100 English videos by play count using the hashtags #preeclampsia, #preeclampsiaawareness, #gestationalhypertension, #pregnancyhypertension, #eclampsia, and #postpartumhypertension. Videos were generated using the TikTok Data Extractor by Apify.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcome was content quality via the Global Quality Score (GQS) - a validated tool ranging from 1 (low, use discouraged) to 5 (high, medically useful). Secondary outcomes included the number of videos relevant to the hashtag, and assessments of medical claims content using mDISCERN. Secondary analysis included sub-stratifying by healthcare provider status.
RESULTS: Of the top 600 videos across all hashtags, 527 (87.8%) were relevant and 109 (20.7%) videos were created by healthcare providers. The median [interquartile range (IQR)] GQS for all videos was 1 (Anonymous. Gestational Hypertension and Preeclampsia: ACOG Practice Bulletin, Number 222. Obstet Gynecol [Internet]., 2020; Williamson et al., 2023 [1,3]) suggesting videos were low quality and not useful. The GQS for healthcare provider content was higher (3 [1.5,3] versus 1 (Anonymous. Gestational Hypertension and Preeclampsia: ACOG Practice Bulletin, Number 222. Obstet Gynecol [Internet]., 2020; Khosla et al., 2021 [1,2]), p < 0.01). Only 47 (8.9%) videos made medical claims and the overall median [IQR] mDISCERN score was 2 (Anonymous. Gestational Hypertension and Preeclampsia: ACOG Practice Bulletin, Number 222. Obstet Gynecol [Internet]., 2020; Williamson et al., 2023 [1,3]) and was higher for healthcare provider content (2 [1.5,3] versus 1 [0,1], p < 0.01). Moreover, content by healthcare providers was more accurate (84.4% versus 13.3%, p < 0.01).
CONCLUSION: The TikTok hypertensive disorders of pregnancy content, while relevant, is of low quality and usefulness. Of the content making medical claims, the accuracy was higher for healthcare provider created content. This identifies an opportunity for healthcare professionals to create reliable, accessible content as an alternative for patient education.

articles.title: Current perspectives of CAR-T cells therapy in peritoneal carcinomatosis.
articles.journal: European journal of surgical oncology : the journal of the European Society of Surgical Oncology and the British Association of Surgical Oncology
articles.authors: Qian-Zhang S, Domínguez-Prieto V, Romero-Triana D et al.
articles.abstract: Peritoneal carcinomatosis (PC) is a frequent pattern of tumor dissemination across multiple malignancies, including colorectal, gastric, ovarian, and pancreatic cancers, and is associated with poor prognosis and limited survival. Although cytoreductive surgery (CRS) with or without hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC) has improved outcomes in selected patients, its indication remains restricted, leaving a substantial proportion of patients without curative options, and recurrence rates remain high even after treatment. Therefore, the development of novel therapeutic strategies is urgently needed. Chimeric antigen receptor T (CAR-T) cell therapy has emerged as a promising approach, achieving remarkable success in hematological malignancies and gaining increasing attention in solid tumors. Several tumor-associated antigens, including CEA, CLDN18.2, GUCY2C, EpCAM, and mesothelin, have been investigated across different tumor types, showing encouraging preclinical and early clinical results. In particular, similar to HIPEC, regional delivery strategies such as intraperitoneal administration may enhance tumor targeting, improve cell trafficking, and increase therapeutic efficacy in peritoneal disease. However, CAR-T cell therapy in PC faces important challenges inherent to solid tumors, including antigen heterogeneity, limited tumor trafficking and infiltration, and a hostile tumor microenvironment characterized by dense stromal barriers and immunosuppressive conditions, which ultimately limit its efficacy. Overcoming these barriers is essential to optimize therapeutic outcomes. This review summarizes the current evidence on CAR-T cell therapy in major solid tumors associated with PC, highlighting key targets, administration strategies, and clinical outcomes, while addressing the main limitations and emerging strategies to improve its clinical application, as well as future perspectives for its integration into multimodal treatment approaches.

articles.title: Autistic traits and behavioral problems at age 8 after assisted reproductive technology: A Japanese multicenter cohort study of singleton term children born to infertile couples.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Hara M, Ueno K, Ono M et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study compared autism-related traits and behavioral/emotional problems at age 8 among singleton term children born to infertile couples who conceived without IVF or embryo transfer (no-IVF/ET), or by fresh (FreET) or frozen-thawed embryo transfer (FET).
METHODS: In a multicenter JISART cohort, 854 children were analyzed (no-IVF/ET, n = 100; FreET, n = 340; FET, n = 414). The main model (Model 2) included 617 children, of whom only 74 were no-IVF/ET comparators. Autism-related traits were assessed using the Autism Spectrum Quotient Children's Version (AQ), and behavioral/emotional problems were assessed using the Child Behavior Checklist (CBCL). Group differences were examined using sex-stratified adjusted analyses, and exploratory threshold analyses used Firth's logistic regression pooling boys and girls.
RESULTS: Among girls, AQ and CBCL scores did not differ significantly between the groups. Among boys, the FreET-no-IVF/ET AQ difference was 3.30 points in Model 1 (Dunnett-adjusted 95 % CI, 0.31-6.29; P = 0.028) and 3.22 points in Model 2 (-0.16 to 6.60; P = 0.063). The AQ scores after FET and CBCL scores in both ART groups did not differ significantly from those in the no-IVF/ET group. The unadjusted threshold proportions did not differ significantly among the groups. In exploratory Firth regression pooling boys and girls, FreET was associated with higher odds of AQ ≥ 25 (OR, 4.18; 95 % CI, 1.22 to 21.79; Holm-adjusted P = 0.041).
CONCLUSIONS: Among term singleton children with available age-8 outcomes, Model 2 showed no significant differences in continuous AQ or CBCL scores between the ART and no-IVF/ET groups. The association between FreET and AQ ≥ 25 is exploratory and requires confirmation.

articles.title: Relugolix combination therapy for symptomatic uterine fibroids in routine practice: a multicentre, retrospective observational study of one-year outcomes.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Estadella J, Verguts J, Gracia M et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the real-world use, efficacy and safety of relugolix combination therapy (relugolix 40 mg, estradiol 1 mg, norethisterone acetate 0.5 mg; Ryeqo) in women with symptomatic uterine fibroids across three European centres.
METHODS: Multicentre, retrospective observational study (June 2023-June 2024) at one Belgian centre (Jessa Hospital, Hasselt) and two Spanish centres (Hospital Clínic and Hospital de la Santa Creu i Sant Pau, Barcelona). Women aged 18-50 years with symptomatic uterine fibroids eligible for relugolix combination therapy were followed in routine practice. Outcomes included bleeding control, amenorrhoea, haemoglobin, fibroid and uterine volume, discontinuation, surgery and adverse events.
RESULTS: A total of 189 women were enrolled (mean age 44.4 years). Heavy menstrual bleeding was the main symptom (58.8 %). Amenorrhoea was achieved by 49.4 % of women (mean 64 days), and 70 % of the remainder reported improved bleeding. Haemoglobin rose from 10.5 g/dL at baseline to 11.8 and 11.9 g/dL (p < 0.002 and p < 0.0023). No significant change in uterine or fibroid volume was observed. Most women (72.8 %) reported no side effects; headache (12.1 %) and vasomotor symptoms (7.5 %) were most frequent. Treatment was discontinued by 37.0 %, mainly for persistent bleeding. During follow-up 47.1 % underwent surgery, only 31.5 % after failure of medical treatment.
CONCLUSIONS: In routine European practice, relugolix combination therapy produced rapid control of heavy menstrual bleeding and a sustained rise in haemoglobin, though without significant change in fibroid or uterine volume. Counselling about expected early bleeding may improve adherence. These real-world data complement the LIBERTY trials and support use in daily practice, including as a bridge to surgery.

articles.title: Dicrotophos exposure is associated with spermatogenic impairment and BCAT1-associated Sertoli-cell dysfunction: A disease-oriented toxicogenomic study of non-obstructive azoospermia.
articles.authors: Zhou R, Zhang K, Wu S et al.
articles.abstract: Non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA) is a severe form of male infertility. Pesticide exposure has been suspected to impair spermatogenesis, yet the molecular route by which it might do so remains poorly understood. Here we combined a disease-oriented toxicogenomic screen with transcriptomic, biochemical and in vivo experiments. We derived a 20-gene signature from public human testicular transcriptomes and reproduced it in a busulfan mouse model of spermatogenic injury. The signature classified NOA and control samples in discovery and external cohorts. Intersecting the Comparative Toxicogenomics Database with pesticide annotation and predicted reproductive toxicity yielded seven candidates; we carried dicrotophos forward because it was the least characterized of the seven. Docking and microscale thermophoresis identified BCAT1 as the strongest binder among three proteins tested (Kd = 48.61 μM; 95% CI 42.19-56.08 μM), and molecular dynamics supported a stable complex. Single-cell data placed BCAT1 mainly in Sertoli cells. In TM4 cells, dicrotophos slowed BCAT1 degradation without changing its specific transaminase activity and reduced blood-testis barrier and Sertoli-cell support genes, effects partly reversed by Bcat1 knockdown. Subchronic exposure of mice produced dose-related spermatogenic damage, lower testosterone and higher testicular BCAT1. Two-sample Mendelian randomization linked genetically predicted plasma BCAT1 to NOA (odds ratio = 2.05, 95% CI = 1.22-3.47). Our findings provide evidence that dicrotophos exposure is associated with spermatogenic impairment in mice, and identify BCAT1-associated Sertoli-cell dysfunction as one plausible mechanism; whether this pathway operates in human NOA remains untested.

articles.title: High-risk human papillomavirus predominance and genotypic diversity among women with cervical complaints in Bangladesh.
articles.journal: Journal of infection and public health
articles.authors: Tusar MTT, Ara R, Das A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is the main cause of cervical cancer (CC) in Bangladesh. This study investigated HPV occurrence, circulating genotypes, and their phylogenetic relationships among Bangladeshi women with cervical complaints. It also characterized the complete genome, lineage, and mutations of an HPV45 strain from Bangladesh.
METHODS: Cervical swabs from 102 women with cervical complaints were obtained at a tertiary-care hospital in Bangladesh. HPV was detected by PCR amplification using gene-specific primers. Among the HPV-positive samples, those showing strong PCR band intensity were selected for Sanger sequencing of the partial L1 gene. Complete genome sequencing of a representative HPV45 strain was performed on an Illumina NovaSeq X Plus platform. Phylogenetic analyses were conducted using MAFFT, IQ-TREE2, and RAxML-NG. Mutational, structural, and protein stability analyses were performed using bioinformatic and structural modeling tools.
RESULTS: HPV DNA was detected in 47.1% (48/102) of participants. Of the 36 samples selected for Sanger sequencing based on strong PCR band intensity, 21 were successfully sequenced. Genotyping of sequenced strains revealed a predominance of high-risk HPV genotypes (95.45%); HPV16 (68.18%) and HPV18 (13.63%). Phylogenetic analyses demonstrated genotype-specific clustering and close genetic relatedness to globally circulating strains. Complete genomic characterization of an HPV45 strain (HPV_MGH-TT01) revealed a 7,849-bp genome belonging to the A2 sublineage, with 98.0-99.9% nucleotide identity to global reference strains. Multiple amino acid substitutions were identified, particularly within the E2 protein, although structural analyses predicted only minor conformational alterations.
CONCLUSIONS: The predominance of high-risk HPV genotypes and the genomic characterization of HPV45 highlight the importance of large-scale genomic surveillance and expanded molecular screening for preventing CC in Bangladesh.

articles.title: Hidden PI3K-Akt gene programs define stromal, immune, and spatial contexts associated with ovarian cancer prognosis and chemotherapy response.
articles.authors: Li Y, Liu Z
articles.abstract: Dysregulated PI3K-Akt signaling contributes to ovarian cancer progression and treatment resistance, but its effects occur within a heterogeneous tumor microenvironment. We investigated whether clinically relevant PI3K-Akt programs include hidden network-dependent signals associated with prognosis and chemotherapy response. We analyzed 327 PI3K-Akt pathway genes in TCGA ovarian cancer using netLDA to identify outcome-associated programs containing marginal and network-supported hidden signals. Prognostic performance was evaluated in independent cohorts. Predictive regulatory modules (PRMs) were characterized using protein-protein interactions, pathway and tumor-microenvironment analyses, single-cell RNA sequencing, cell-cell communication, spatial transcriptomics, and model-based virtual perturbation. We identified a 50-gene signature comprising 18 marginal-effect genes and 32 hidden network-supported genes, with 38 genes organized into five PRMs centered on HSP90AB1, EFNA2, LAMC1, GNG12, and EPHA2 and the remaining 12 retained as singleton features. The modules represented distinct stress/survival, receptor, ECM/stromal, inflammatory/immune, and cell-matrix adhesion programs and showed prognostic value across independent cohorts. LAMC1-PRM was associated with stromal and EMT features and localized to fibroblast/CAF-rich contexts, whereas GNG12-PRM was associated with immune signaling and myeloid compartments. Spatial transcriptomics revealed nonrandom organization and response-associated differences, including stronger LAMC1-fibroblast/CAF organization in poor-response tissues and increasing GNG12-myeloid organization with response. Virtual perturbation supported network-dependent predictive contributions not evident from marginal effects alone. Clinically relevant PI3K-Akt dysregulation comprises biologically distinct network-dependent programs spanning tumor, stromal, immune, and spatial compartments. Contrasting LAMC1-centered stromal/ECM and GNG12-centered immune/myeloid organizations were associated with chemotherapy-response heterogeneity, linking hidden PI3K-Akt signals to ovarian tumor microenvironment architecture.

articles.title: Association of intrinsic capacity with prevalent and incident cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic multimorbidity among Chinese adults aged 45 years or more: Evidence from a longitudinal cohort study.
articles.authors: Li M, Sun Y, Liu Y et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To examine the cross-sectional and longitudinal associations of intrinsic capacity with multimorbidity across cardiovascular, kidney, and metabolic domains.
STUDY DESIGN: We conducted cross-sectional and longitudinal analyses using data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study, with, respectively, totals of 9117 and 5829 participants aged ≥45 years.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Multimorbidity was defined as conditions in at least two of the three domains: cardiovascular, kidney, and metabolic. Multivariable logistic and Cox regression models were used to evaluate prevalent and incident multimorbidity, respectively. Restricted cubic spline, subgroup, and sensitivity analyses were performed.
RESULTS: Each 1-point higher score for intrinsic capacity was associated with lower odds of prevalent multimorbidity (odds ratio 0.759, 95% confidence interval 0.713-0.807) and a lower risk of incident multimorbidity (hazard ratio 0.849, 95% confidence interval 0.805-0.896). Decreased intrinsic capacity was associated with higher odds of prevalent multimorbidity (odds ratio 1.649, 95% confidence interval 1.399-1.943) and a higher risk of incident multimorbidity (hazard ratio 1.220, 95% confidence interval 1.072-1.388). Restricted cubic spline analyses did not detect significant nonlinearity, and the associations were broadly consistent across subgroup and sensitivity analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: Lower intrinsic capacity was associated with both prevalent and incident cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic multimorbidity. Intrinsic capacity assessment may complement disease-based health evaluation in middle-aged and older adults.

articles.title: NIR-II thermoelectric nanoplatform for metabolic reprogramming-enhanced cuproptosis in uterine tumors.
articles.authors: Lu X, Zhang L, Yi R et al.
articles.abstract: Uterine tumors, including endometrial cancer (EC) and cervical cancer (CC), remain formidable threats to women's health. Unmet clinical needs include fertility preservation in younger patients, treatment of advanced or recurrent disease, limited options for patients unable to undergo surgery, and resistance to chemotherapy or radiotherapy. These challenges motivate the exploration of localized, minimally invasive, and potentially fertility-preserving energy-driven therapeutic strategies. However, the development of such nanotherapies remains constrained by material-level bottlenecks, particularly insufficient second near-infrared (NIR-II) energy utilization and suboptimal catalytic efficiency, which may limit their therapeutic efficacy. Herein, we report a second near-infrared (NIR-II)-responsive thermoelectric nanoplatform based on a conductive copper-hexahydroxyphenanthrene metal-organic framework (CuHPT) for uterine tumor therapy. Upon 1064 nm laser irradiation, CuHPT achieves exceptional photothermal conversion efficiency, establishing steep localized temperature gradients that activate an internal thermoelectric field via the Seebeck effect. This built-in field effectively suppresses charge carrier recombination, thereby enhancing catalytic reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. Following cellular uptake, CuHPT releases intracellular copper ions and induces metabolic reprogramming characterized by elevated oxidative phosphorylation and mitochondrial hyper-respiration. This hyper-metabolic state hypersensitizes tumor cells to copper-induced proteotoxicity and is accompanied by cuproptosis, as evidenced by changes in the expression of cuproptosis-related proteins. Furthermore, CuHPT-mediated photothermoelectric therapy remodels the tumor immune microenvironment by promoting dendritic cell maturation and M1 macrophage polarization. Collectively, this study establishes an NIR-II-responsive nanoplatform that couples photothermoelectric energy conversion with metabolic reprogramming to enhance cuproptosis, providing a promising strategy for uterine tumor therapy.

articles.title: Impact of a prompted voiding programme on urinary incontinence among hospitalised older adults in a functional recovery unit.
articles.authors: Martín-Losada L, Solís-Muñoz M, González-Blázquez C et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the effectiveness of a prompted voiding programme in restoring urinary continence at discharge among older adults hospitalised in a functional recovery unit.
DESIGN: Quasi-experimental, pre-post intervention study without a control group.
METHODS: Non-probability sampling was used to recruit individuals aged 65 and over; with urinary incontinence with less than one year's clinical course; with a reversible cause; admitted to the Functional Recovery Unit in a medium stay hospital; and receiving an individualised prompted voiding programme.
PRIMARY OUTCOME VARIABLE: urinary continence at discharge. Secondary variables: sociodemographic, clinical characteristics, related to urinary incontinence, related to the programme. Data were collected: October 2019 to December 2023. Descriptive and multivariate analyses were performed using STATA 18, 95% confidence level. The study was approved by the research ethics committee.
RESULTS: 158 patients completed the study. The sample was predominantly female, median age of 83 years. Most patients had medical conditions and medications that could adversely affect urinary continence. Incontinence associated with dependency was the high prevalence, it was generally of recent onset, with moderate-to-heavy urinary leakage occurring several times per day. More than half of the patients regained continence, and those who did not achieve full recovery experienced a reduction in the frequency of urine leakage.
CONCLUSION: The prompted voiding programme was effective in restoring urinary continence and improving the severity of urinary incontinence. Registration The study was registered with the United States Clinical Trial Registry (NCT04117126). Registered on 17/08/2019, the first recruitment 15/10/2019.
REPORTING METHOD: The study adheres to the Transparent Reporting of Evaluations with Nonrandomised Designs (TREND) statement.

articles.title: Heparin combined with D-penicillamine, hypotaurine, and epinephrine supports collared peccary sperm function and interspecific embryo development.
articles.authors: Santos MVO, Oliveira LRM, Pereira ABM et al.
articles.abstract: The collared peccary is an ecologically important species that is increasingly threatened by anthropogenic pressures, emphasizing the need for assisted reproductive technologies such as in vitro fertilization (IVF). In wild mammals, IVF remains limited by the lack of species-specific protocols. We previously demonstrated that heparin induces sperm capacitation more effectively than caffeine. We evaluated whether D-penicillamine, hypotaurine, and epinephrine (PHE) improve heparin-based capacitation, sperm function, and interspecific IVF (iIVF) using porcine oocytes. Four media were tested: Tyrode's albumin lactate pyruvate (TALP), TALP with heparin (T-H), TALP with PHE (T-PHE), and TALP with heparin plus PHE (T-H-PHE). Sperm parameters were assessed after 1, 3, and 6 h of incubation, and sperm-oocyte interactions and embryo development were evaluated after iIVF. Total and rapid motility were higher in T-H and T-H-PHE after 3 h. Capacitation increased between 1 and 3 h in TALP and T-H, whereas T-PHE and T-H-PHE reached maximum values at 1 h. After 6 h of incubation, reactive oxygen species levels were highest in the TALP and T-H, whereas the T-H-PHE exhibited the lowest levels. More than 80% of non-cleaved oocytes had bound sperm and their fertilization rate was similar between groups. Cleavage and morula rates were similar among groups, whereas a single blastocyst development occurred only in T-H-PHE. This is a proof-of-concept observation that needs to be further explored. In conclusion, combining heparin with PHE improved sperm motility, capacitation, reduced oxidative stress, and supported embryonic development. These findings provide a practical basis for developing species-specific IVF protocols for peccaries.

articles.title: Beliefs About Pregnancy and Perceptions of Clinical Care Influencing the Uptake of Antenatal Care and Facility-Based Delivery: Findings Across the CHAMPS Network.
articles.journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
articles.authors: Blevins J, Maixenchs M, Hardison-Moody A et al.
articles.abstract: Although quality antenatal care (ANC) and facility-based delivery reduce maternal and under age 5 years mortality, various factors impede uptake of these services. We conducted a qualitative study to assess the influence of common perceptions and practices about pregnancy and birth outcomes on: 1) understanding causes of complicated pregnancies and birth outcomes, and 2) attitudes toward pregnancy care. The study consisted of semistructured interviews or focus group discussions with women currently pregnant for the first time; women who had delivered a healthy child to term; women who had experienced a miscarriage or stillbirth; clinical health providers; traditional health practitioners; religious leaders; husbands of pregnant women; and parents and in-laws of pregnant women. A total of 107 events (97 interviews and 10 focus group discussions) were conducted within the catchment communities of sites of the Child Health and Mortality Prevention Surveillance Network in Bangladesh, Ethiopia, Kenya, Mozambique, and Sierra Leone. Analyzing narrative data, three relevant topics were identified to describe beliefs and attitudes toward pregnancy care: 1) influences of clinical frameworks for understanding pregnancy, 2) influences of cultural frameworks for understanding pregnancy, and 3) specific alignment/tension between community members' beliefs and pregnancy care. We concluded by highlighting two barriers: 1) suspicion between clinical and traditional providers, and 2) the impact of cultural belief on the uptake of ANC, especially in the first trimester; and two recommendations: 1) identify trusted partners to facilitate collaboration, and 2) encourage the expansion of low-cost pregnancy support services to improve uptake of ANC and facility-based delivery.

articles.title: GESS-AEEM consensus on testosterone therapy in women: a clinical implementation framework.
articles.journal: Climacteric : the journal of the International Menopause Society
articles.authors: Sánchez-Prieto M, Iglesias Bravo E, Gutiérrez LE et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to provide a Spanish clinical implementation consensus on systemic testosterone therapy in women, translating international evidence and guidance into an operational framework for Spain and comparable European settings.
METHODS: A multidisciplinary panel of 13 experts reviewed evidence identified through PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase and the Cochrane Library from January 2000 to April 2026. Sources were characterized by study design, directness, applicability and key limitations. Draft statements were refined through a two-round modified Delphi process, with agreement predefined as ≥80%. A revised special-populations statement underwent focused post-review confirmatory voting. No formal Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) assessment was performed.
RESULTS: Physiological-dose transdermal testosterone may be considered for postmenopausal women with hypoactive sexual desire disorder after comprehensive biopsychosocial assessment. Serum testosterone should not be used diagnostically but supports safe prescribing and detection of supraphysiological exposure. The consensus addresses off-label prescribing, assay continuity, monitoring, discontinuation, safety communication and special populations. Non-transdermal formulations, supraphysiological dosing and use for non-sexual indications are not supported.
CONCLUSIONS: This article does not propose a new therapeutic indication or supersede existing guidance. The article provides a contextualized implementation framework to support consistent and safe clinical practice.

articles.title: The Obstetrician-Gynecologist's Role in Adoption.
articles.authors: American College of Obstetricians & Gynecologists' Committee on Ethics
articles.abstract: Obstetrician-gynecologists may find themselves at the center of adoption discussions when caring for pregnant patients who are considering relinquishing their parental rights and placing their child for adoption. In this Committee Statement, the Committee on Ethics of the American College of Obstetricians & Gynecologists discusses related ethical issues and aims to provide professional recommendations and physician safeguards while centering the patient with a trauma-informed approach.

articles.title: Wharton's jelly insufficiency and its implications for perinatal outcomes and regenerative medicine: A review.
articles.authors: Habiba UE, Shamim S, Sarwar I et al.
articles.abstract: Wharton's jelly (WJ) is the hydrated extracellular matrix (ECM) of the umbilical cord, providing mechanical protection for the umbilical vessels and a niche for WJ-derived mesenchymal stromal cells (WJ-MSCs). This narrative review examines WJ insufficiency in relation to perinatal vascular risk and the functional quality of cells harvested for regenerative medicine. PubMed and Google Scholar were searched through October 2026 for studies of WJ structure, cord pathology, prenatal assessment, and WJ-MSC function. A lean cord, defined by a cross-sectional area below the 10th percentile for gestational age, was reported in 73.8% of fetuses with fetal growth restriction (FGR) in one cited cohort. The reported clinical spectrum includes reduced umbilical vein blood flow, thrombosis, and intrauterine fetal death (IUFD). Nine case reports and case series published between 1978 and 2021 describe structural cord abnormalities associated with WJ deficiency. Broader clinical findings are organized into a proposed five-tier severity continuum that has not been prospectively validated. WJ-MSCs from pregnancies complicated by gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) or maternal obesity show functional alterations that are not captured by cell yield alone. Whether reduced WJ content or a lean cord independently lowers MSC potency remains untested. For preeclampsia and intrauterine infection, the proposed effects on WJ-MSC quality are inferred from adjacent evidence rather than demonstrated directly. Sonographic WJ-area assessment, Doppler monitoring, molecular biomarkers, and potency-based donor stratification are proposed research approaches. Prospective studies linking antenatal WJ measurements to perinatal outcomes and post-isolation MSC function are needed before the severity framework or proposed surveillance and cord-banking strategies can be adopted clinically.

articles.title: Combined Prenatal Environmental Stressors Induce Suprachiasmatic Degeneration with Unexpected Behavioural Resilience in Long-Evans Rats.
articles.authors: Soja S, Edem E, Obajuluwa A et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Environmental heat stress and displacement adversity during pregnancy pose significant risks to neurodevelopment, particularly in regions with high maternal mortality and population displacement. The suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN), the brain's master circadian pacemaker, is vulnerable to prenatal environmental insults, yet the combined impact of thermal and psychosocial stressors on SCN development remains unexplored. We examined the effects of prenatal heat stress and displacement-like conditions on SCN morphology and behaviour across two critical developmental stages.
METHODS: Twenty-five timed-pregnant Long-Evans rats were exposed to heat stress (38-40°C, 2 h daily), displacement conditions (overnight food/water restriction plus overcrowding), combined stressors, or control conditions from gestational days 15-20. Male offspring were assessed at postnatal days 10 (neonatal) and 30 (juvenile).
RESULTS: Heat exposure induced significant maternal hyperthermia (2.5-2.9°C elevation). Histological analysis revealed marked SCN cellular degeneration across stress groups at both developmental stages, characterised by reduced cell counts, pyknotic nuclei, and disrupted tissue architecture. Despite structural damage, juvenile behavioural testing revealed paradoxical outcomes: combined stress exposure reduced anxiety-like behaviour in the elevated plus maze, enhanced sociability in three-chamber testing, while preserving recognition memory. Growth analysis demonstrated preferential brain sparing despite reduced somatic growth, with significantly elevated brain-to-body weight ratios in stress-exposed animals.
CONCLUSION: These findings demonstrate that prenatal environmental stressors cause lasting damage to the SCN but trigger adaptive behavioural responses. The dissociation between structural vulnerability and functional adaptation suggests complex neurodevelopmental programming with implications for populations experiencing heat exposure and displacement adversity.

articles.title: Ovarian cancer screening using serum CA125 and transvaginal ultrasound: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Chen Y, Wu Y, Shi X et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The clinical utility of ovarian cancer screening remains unclear. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of serum cancer antigen 125 combined with transvaginal ultrasound in the early detection of ovarian cancer and the improvement of prognosis.
METHODS: Systematically searched five electronic databases to identify eligible randomised controlled trials. The primary outcomes were ovarian cancer incidence and ovarian cancer-specific mortality. Results were evaluated using relative risks and 95% confidence intervals.
RESULTS: Four randomised controlled trials were included in this meta-analysis, comprising 188147 participants in the screening group and 187394 in the control group. Pooled results showed no statistically significant difference in overall ovarian cancer incidence and ovarian cancer-specific mortality between the two groups (all p>0.05). Subgroup analysis further showed that the screening group had a significantly higher detection rate of Stage I ovarian cancer than the control group (relative risks=1.35, 95% confidence interval:1.14-1.60; p<0.001). For histological subtypes, the screening group had a significantly higher detection rate of serous carcinoma (relative risk=1.09, 95% confidence interval:1.01-1.19; p=0.030), but a significantly lower detection rate of mucinous carcinoma (relative risk=0.69, 95% confidence interval:0.51-0.94; p=0.020). No statistically significant difference was observed between the two groups in other subgroups (all p>0.05).
CONCLUSION: For asymptomatic women in the general population, combined serum cancer antigen 125 and transvaginal ultrasound screening should be approached with caution. Current evidence indicates that this screening strategy neither reduced​ the overall incidence of ovarian cancer nor improved​ overall survival, despite potentially increasing the detection rate of Stage I and early-stage serous carcinoma.

articles.title: Regional variation in adolescent births and associations with adverse perinatal outcomes in Georgia: A birth registry-based cohort study.
articles.authors: Khachidze N, Anda EE, Manjavidze T et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In Georgia, approximately 2,700 (5.8%) adolescents give birth every year. Adolescent births are a public health concern due to an increased risk of various adverse maternal and newborn outcomes. We aimed to evaluate the regional variation of adolescent births and also the associations between maternal age and preterm birth (PB), neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission, and perinatal death (PD) in Georgia.
METHODS: The study population included all childbirths in women aged <30 years between 2017 and 2022, comprising 173,238 women and their 175,213 newborns. We used three age groups: adolescents aged <18, and 18-19 years, and adults aged 20-29 years (reference group). Logistic regression analysis was performed to evaluate the associations between maternal age and PB, NICU admission, and PD. Population attributable fractions and absolute numbers of the selected adverse outcomes attributable to adolescent births were estimated.
RESULTS: The adolescent birth rate (ABR) was 22.2 per 1000 adolescents in Georgia in 2022. Most of the adolescents aged <20 years lived in the regions of Kvemo Kartli, Kakheti, and Imereti with an ABR of 70.3 per 1000, 35.3 per 1000, and 26.4 per 1000, respectively. Newborns born to adolescents aged <18 (PB adjusted odds ratio [aOR]= 1.25, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.11-1.41; NICU aOR= 1.19, 95% CI: 1.06-1.33; PD aOR= 1.33, 95% CI: 0.99-1.80) and 18-19 years (PB aOR= 1.04, 95% CI: 0.98-1.11; NICU aOR= 1.08, 95% CI: 1.01-1.16; PD aOR= 1.17, 95% CI: 0.98-1.40) had higher odds for almost all the selected perinatal outcomes than newborns born to the reference group of 20-29-year-old women. If adolescents <20 years had postponed childbirth until they were between 20 and 29 years old, approximately 14 cases of singleton preterm birth (1%), 16 NICU admissions (1%), and 4 perinatal deaths (2%) occurring between 2017 and 2022 could have been prevented.
CONCLUSION: Our findings revealed large geographical differences in adolescent births across Georgia, with the highest rates in Kvemo Kartli, Kakheti, and Imereti. Adolescent childbirth, particularly among those <18 years, was linked to higher risks of PB, NICU admission, and PD compared to adults aged 20-29 years. Targeted interventions, such as improved access to reproductive health education and family planning, are needed, especially in high-burden regions.

articles.title: Association between active helicobacter pylori infection and Iron Deficiency Anemia among pregnant women attending antenatal care in Uganda: An analytical cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Yaweh J, Okello M, Kasujja M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Helicobacter pylori infection has been associated with iron deficiency anaemia (IDA) during pregnancy, but evidence from Uganda remains limited. This study compared IDA prevalence by H. pylori status, assessed the adjusted association between H. pylori positivity and IDA, and explored factors associated with IDA among infected pregnant women.
METHODS: A facility-based analytical cross-sectional study was conducted among 392 pregnant women attending antenatal care at Mubende Regional Referral Hospital, Uganda, from August to December 2025. Participants were systematically recruited into H. pylori-positive and -negative analytical groups (196 each). Active H. pylori infection was determined using stool antigen testing, and IDA was defined by concurrent anaemia and serum ferritin <15 µg/L. Prevalence ratios (PRs) were estimated for the H. pylori-IDA association, while logistic regression explored factors associated with IDA among H. pylori-positive women.
RESULTS: IDA was more prevalent among H. pylori-positive than -negative women (14.8% [29/196] vs 6.6% [13/196]). H. pylori positivity was associated with a higher prevalence of IDA (cPR = 2.23, 95% CI: 1.20-4.16; p = 0.012), including after adjustment for residence, iron-rich food consumption and household income (aPR = 2.22, 95% CI: 1.16-4.24; p = 0.016). Median haemoglobin was lower among H. pylori-positive women (11 vs 12 g/dL; p < 0.001). Among H. pylori-positive women, lack of deworming (aOR=4.88, 95% CI: 1.73-13.79), tea or coffee consumption with meals (aOR=4.31, 95% CI: 1.22-15.20), and inadequate handwashing (aOR=3.18, 95% CI: 1.15-8.76) were associated with higher odds of IDA.
CONCLUSIONS: H. pylori positivity was associated with a higher prevalence of IDA among pregnant women attending ANC at Mubende Regional Referral Hospital. Lack of deworming, tea or coffee consumption with meals, and inadequate handwashing were associated with IDA among H. pylori-positive women. The cross-sectional design precludes causal inference, and the subgroup findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited number of IDA cases.

articles.title: Untargeted plasma metabolomics reveals metabolite alterations and pathway perturbations in gestational diabetes mellitus.
articles.authors: Chaiyachate K, Pongsamakthai M, Jamnongkan W et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is defined as glucose intolerance first detected during pregnancy and is associated with adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes. Metabolomics provides a system-level approach to characterize metabolic alterations associated with gestational insulin resistance. This study aimed to identify plasma metabolite differences between women with GDM and normal glucose tolerance (NGT) and to evaluate the discriminatory performance of a metabolite-based panel.
METHODS: Plasma samples from 270 pregnant women (169 GDM and 101 NGT) were analyzed using an untargeted 1H nuclear magnetic resonance (1H NMR)-based metabolomics approach. Differential metabolites were identified using univariate, followed by multivariate modeling and regression adjustment for maternal age and pre-pregnancy body mass index. Discriminatory performance was evaluated using Random Forest (RF), Partial Least Squares-Discriminant Analysis (PLS-DA), and Linear Support Vector Machine (Linear-SVM) models with Receiver Operating Characteristic curve analysis. Pathway enrichment analyses were performed using KEGG and SMPDB, and disease-based enrichment was assessed using HMDB.
RESULTS: Among 31 identified metabolites, 14 differed significantly between GDM and NGT. Integration of univariate and multivariate analyses prioritized nine metabolites-acetone, citrate, glucose, succinate, glycine, 3-hydroxybutyrate, leucine, phenylalanine, and the CH = CH bond of unsaturated lipids-that remained independently associated with GDM after covariate adjustment. All nine metabolites were elevated in the GDM group. A nine-metabolite panel achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.76 (95% CI: 0.70-0.81) using the RF model. Pathway enrichment identified valine, leucine, and isoleucine biosynthesis and ketone body metabolism as significantly enriched pathways. HMDB-based disease enrichment showed overlap with preeclampsia-related metabolic signatures.
CONCLUSION: Untargeted 1H NMR metabolomics, combined enrichment analyses, identified coordinated metabolic disturbances in GDM involving amino acid and ketone body metabolism. A nine-metabolite panel demonstrated moderate discriminative performance and provides mechanistic insight into GDM-associated metabolic adaptations, supporting their potential utility for future biomarker validation and translational studies.

articles.title: Popularity Without Proof: A Narrative Review of Peptide Adjuncts to Testosterone Therapy in Body Composition and Functional-Driven Use.
articles.authors: Liberto R, Davila J
articles.abstract: Testosterone replacement therapy (TRT) has expanded beyond traditional indications, particularly among younger men. In this population, testosterone can form the base of a wider protocol that, combined with several peptides, including growth hormone (GH) secretagogues and restorative peptides, aims to improve body composition, strength, and recovery. Despite widespread use, no published study has evaluated these combinations for body composition, strength, or function. GH secretagogues have been shown to increase GH and/or insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) levels, and some may increase lean or fat-free mass. However, these changes generally do not reliably improve strength or physical function. Evidence for restorative peptides, such as BPC-157 and TB-500, remains largely preclinical, with minimal to no data supporting their efficacy in humans. Variable product quality from unregulated sources is a cause for concern. Testosterone and peptide regimens are increasingly utilized despite significant gaps in the evidence. This necessitates distinguishing between established indications and experimental uses, and informed, nonjudgmental counseling as a harm-reduction strategy. The aim of this review is to examine the available human evidence regarding GH secretagogues and restorative peptides used as adjuncts to testosterone therapy, focusing on body composition, strength, and safety.

articles.title: Handheld Raman spectroscopy for ex vivo molecular assessment of cervical lesions: A methodological feasibility study.
articles.authors: Zhang Y, Wang H, He Y et al.
articles.abstract: Current diagnostic workflows for cervical lesions remain constrained by processing time, sampling representativeness, and limited molecular-level tissue assessment. Handheld Raman spectroscopy may provide label-free molecular profiling of ex vivo tissue specimens. In this methodological feasibility study, we evaluated a defined ex vivo acquisition workflow using a handheld 785-nm Raman spectrometer. We systematically evaluated laser power, integration time, and tissue thickness, and 128 mW laser power, 4000 ms integration time, and approximately 1-mm-thick tissue sections were selected as the working acquisition conditions for subsequent cervical measurements. The cervical cohort comprised 74 patients contributing 212 Raman spectra and was evaluated for two predefined primary binary classification tasks: invasive cervical cancer versus noncancer lesions (B1) and high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL) versus benign lesions plus low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (LSIL) (B2). Exploratory spectrum-level analyses yielded AUCs of 0.774 for B1 and 0.782 for B2. However, under repeated nested patient-grouped cross-validation of the previously selected model families, with all spectra from each patient retained within the same validation fold and hyperparameters optimized using training patients only, the mean patient-level AUC was 0.519 ± 0.051 for B1 and 0.639 ± 0.074 for B2. The corresponding median AUCs were 0.522 (IQR, 0.497-0.545) and 0.642 (IQR, 0.620-0.688), respectively. In patient-aware differential peak analysis, repeated measurements from the same patient were aggregated before statistical testing. Six prespecified Raman bands (1003, 1306, 1341, 1516, 1586, and 1638 cm-¹) remained significant after false discovery rate (FDR) correction for B1, whereas no prespecified band remained significant after FDR correction for B2. These findings support the methodological feasibility of handheld Raman acquisition under the present defined ex vivo workflow and indicate the presence of lesion-associated spectral variation in cervical tissue, while also demonstrating substantial attenuation of classification performance under patient-independent validation. Handheld Raman spectroscopy should therefore currently be regarded as an exploratory adjunctive approach for ex vivo molecular tissue assessment rather than a standalone diagnostic method. Larger patient cohorts, spatially registered Raman-histology validation, fresh-tissue studies, and…

articles.title: Perceived community acceptance on maternal and newborns care continuum and its correlates in Ethiopia.
articles.authors: Damtew SA, Yohannes M, Armdie AZ et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal and newborns care continuum completion decision making process is influenced by seeking validation and the sole approval from significant others. Evidences have shown that community acceptance is one of the bottlenecks hindering the completion of the maternal and newborns care continuum and their retention in the care. It is also among the critical determinants for the success of the paradigm shift on the maternal, newborns and child health (MNCH) care continuum completion. However, this area is understudied, leading a dearth of evidence in Ethiopia. Hence, this study aimed at documenting the level of perceived community acceptance on maternal and newborns care continuum and identifying associated factors among pregnant women. The findings could provide actionable evidence for the Ethiopian Health Ministry and relevant developmental partners to improve maternal and newborns health outcomes.
METHODS: This study has used the baseline cross sectional data form the Ethiopian Performance Monitoring for Action (EPMA) cohort one survey. The study screened, enrolled and collected data from pregnant and six week postpartum women. However, the analytic sample were 2,219 pregnant women. Frequencies were computed to describe the pregnant women. Multinomial logistics regression statistical modeling was fitted to identify correlates of…
CONCLUSIONS: This suboptimal level of perceived community acceptance on maternal and newborns care continuum by most people in the community signals that interventions and programs are required to nurture a positive influence of the community on women to complete the care continuum. Context specific and age sensitive programs and interventions which aimed in choice based contraceptive provision, empowering women to choose their childbirth attendant and place; and postpartum contraceptive use counseling are imperative to improve perceived community acceptance on maternal and newborns care continuum. These interventions need to target younger, less educated, economically disadvantage, rural women and those with polygamous marriage. Improving birth preparedness and complication readiness and installing the inter-pregnancy preconception care packages are imperative in this regard. Enhancing mechanisms for incorporating community input is the core implication. These include strengthening the implementation of community score cards; and testing and scaling up the community maternal and newborns health family meetings.

articles.title: 3D and 4D Hysterosalpingo-Contrast Sonography: Advanced Tubal Patency Assessment.
articles.journal: Radiographics : a review publication of the Radiological Society of North America, Inc
articles.authors: Cossi PS, Fernandes FF, Silva LLC et al.
articles.abstract: Female infertility affects approximately 15% of couples of reproductive age, with tubal disease responsible for up to one-third of cases. Therefore, accurate, minimally invasive evaluation of tubal patency is a cornerstone of fertility assessment. Among the available modalities, including hysterosalpingography (HSG), MR HSG, and laparoscopic chromopertubation, hysterosalpingo-contrast sonography (HyCoSy) has gained prominence as a valuable alternative to conventional methods due to its safety, accessibility, and diagnostic reliability. Recent advances in contrast-enhanced US involving the use of second-generation microbubble agents combined with three-dimensional (3D) and four-dimensional (4D) acquisition technologies have significantly improved the performance of HyCoSy. These developments enable real-time volumetric visualization of the uterine cavity and fallopian tubes, enhancing both anatomic delineation and functional assessment of tubal patency. In addition, combined 3D and 4D (3D-4D) HyCoSy enables complementary evaluation of uterine morphology, adnexal structures, and associated infertility-related disorders such as endometriosis and adhesions, facilitating a comprehensive "one-stop" reproductive imaging approach. This article is intended to serve as a practical guide to performing 3D-4D HyCoSy with microbubble contrast agents, including preparation, technical parameters, and findings interpretation. In addition, the authors compare HyCoSy with conventional techniques, review characteristic imaging patterns of tubal patency and occlusion, and discuss potential pitfalls and preventive strategies. As an advanced US technology combined with a dynamic functional perspective, 3D-4D HyCoSy represents a powerful, cost-effective, and patient-friendly tool for integrated fertility evaluation in modern radiology practices.

articles.title: The genetic path for cardiomyopathies after the European Society of Cardiology Guidelines 2023: a consensus statement of the Italian CardioGenetics Group.
articles.authors: Grasso M, Iascone MR, Alioto L et al.
articles.abstract: This consensus document results from a three-phase process conducted among Italian geneticists, experts in cardiovascular genetics. The proposal was first presented and discussed at the annual meeting of the Italian CardioGenetics Group (ICGG) (2025), then drafted, circulated, and finally revised and approved by consensus of all contributing members. The 2023 guidelines of the European Society of Cardiology introduced, for the first time, a Class I Level of Evidence B recommendation for genetic testing in cardiomyopathies, formally integrating a structured genetic pathway into the diagnostic process and assigning it a central clinical role for patients and their families. This document provides expert statements on: the 2023 ESC recommendations on genetic testing in cardiomyopathies; the guidance of the European Society of Human Genetics and the Italian Society of Human Genetics (SIGU) regarding clinical genetic testing within the National Health System; the ESC phenotype-first diagnostic approach; tailored genetic testing strategies and tools; positions on direct-to-consumer genetic testing (DTC-GT); quality standards in accordance with national and international regulations; cautious interpretation of variants of uncertain significance; gene curation, variant classification and reclassification according to the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics criteria; definition of completeness of genetic testing in clinical practice; and the role of genetic testing in reproductive counselling and preimplantation genetic testing.

articles.title: Failure of Fentanyl Sublingual Tablet Dissolution in Severe Xerostomia and Emergency Rescue Management: A Case Report.
articles.journal: Journal of pain & palliative care pharmacotherapy
articles.authors: Suzuki H, Hagiwara E, Yamauchi K
articles.abstract: Severe xerostomia may impair dissolution and transmucosal absorption of fentanyl sublingual tablets, complicating rescue analgesia in patients with cancer. We report a 77-year-old woman with advanced ovarian cancer, leptomeningeal metastases, severe xerostomia, and a nasogastric tube. During hospitalization, fentanyl sublingual tablets relieved headache. After transfer to a hospice-oriented residential care facility, pain-related vocalization persisted. Despite use of oral moisturizers, a fentanyl sublingual tablet remained intact under the tongue approximately 30 min after administration and was removed. The transdermal fentanyl dose was increased, but additional analgesia was considered necessary. Because no alternative rescue medication was immediately available, a 100-μg fentanyl sublingual tablet was dissolved in warm water and administered through the nasogastric tube as a one-time off-label emergency measure. Vocalization ceased 30 min later, with no apparent respiratory depression, excessive sedation, nausea, vomiting, or tube obstruction. Nasogastric administration of fentanyl sublingual tablets is nonstandard and should not be adopted routinely. The response cannot be attributed definitively to nasogastric fentanyl administration because the developing effect of the increased transdermal dose and symptom fluctuations could not be excluded. Nevertheless, this case may inform rescue-medication and route-of-administration decisions when severe xerostomia compromises sublingual administration and no suitable alternative is immediately available.

articles.title: Exploring RSV prevention among pregnant people and healthcare professionals in Aotearoa, New Zealand.
articles.authors: Young A, Richards N, Abbas R et al.
articles.abstract: In Aotearoa New Zealand (NZ), RSV causes severe disease in infants, particularly Māori and Pacific infants, and is a high burden on the health system. Although an antenatal RSV vaccine and long-acting monoclonal antibodies are available internationally to prevent disease, they are not yet available in NZ. This study aims to explore the knowledge and perceptions of pregnant people and health care providers regarding RSV preventative options, and strategies for supporting a potential future immunization rollout in NZ.
