In this mixed-methods study, a cross-sectional survey of health care professionals (HCPs) across NZ and qualitative interviews with recently/pregnant Māori, Pacific, or ethnic minority migrants were conducted. A directed content analytic approach was used for analysis. Most HCPs (79.5%; 159/200) thought there was a high need for universal antenatal RSV vaccination, and 73.5% (147/200) ranked antenatal vaccination as their preferred prevention strategy over either targeted or universal infant monoclonal antibody. However, pharmacists comprised 63% of respondents. Interviewed caregivers (n = 13) would prefer to be offered whichever option had the longest duration of protection. If effectiveness and length of protection were similar, most preferred the antenatal vaccine so their infant was not injected to avoid discomfort or potential side effects their infant may experience. Recommendation from trusted HCPs, access to clear information from credible sources, and accessible and trusted administration settings are critical to supporting immunization acceptance. These insights can inform future implementation of a comprehensive rollout of an equitable preventative immunization program, reducing the risk of severe infant RSV disease.

articles.title: Placental transcriptomes differ in human pregnancies complicated by severe fetal left heart obstruction.
articles.authors: Leon RL, Lu H, Ossa Galvis MM et al.
articles.abstract: The etiology of severe left-sided obstructive lesions (LSOL) of the heart, a common form of congenital heart disease (CHD), often remains unknown even after comprehensive genetic testing. Preclinical models implicate placental perturbations in abnormal cardiogenesis; however, little is known about connections between human placenta and fetal cardiac diseases. We profiled term placentas from severe LSOL pregnancies (n = 20) with and without placental pathologies and healthy controls (n = 10) to test whether severe fetal LSOL is associated with distinct transcriptomic and cellular states. Bulk RNA-sequencing of archival formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissues identified 1,030 differentially expressed protein-coding genes (580 [up], 450 [down]). Upregulated programs involved heart-valve development, endothelial signaling, and extracellular-matrix processes; while endocrine, trophoblast and gamma-aminobutyric acid signaling processes were downregulated. Severe LSOL pregnancies with histologically normal placentas showed enrichment of lymphatic-vascular development and cyclic-nucleotide signaling. Digital deconvolution analysis inferred reduced trophoblast fractions with reciprocal increase in endothelial and immune cell types. These findings support a unique placental gene expression in abnormal cardiac development, even in the absence of overt placental histopathology. These RNA expression signatures may serve as candidate biomarkers and lay the groundwork for mechanistic studies of the heart-placenta axis and future risk stratification in pregnancies with fetuses diagnosed with severe LSOL.

articles.title: Trends in Menopause Hormone Therapy.
articles.authors: Sarnak DO, Shen W, Alexander GC

articles.title: Maternal KIR-Fetal HLA-C Interactions in IVF and Pregnancy: Evidence, Clinical Implications, and Ethics; A Narrative Review.
articles.authors: Margiana R, El-Sehrawy AAMA, Basunduwah TS et al.
articles.abstract: A successful pregnancy depends on tightly regulated communication between maternal uterine natural killer (uNK) cells and fetal extravillous trophoblasts (EVTs), in which maternal killer-cell immunoglobulin-like receptors (KIRs) and fetal human leukocyte antigen-C (HLA-C) help shape uNK-cell activation, trophoblast migration, and uterine vascular remodeling. Some genetic combinations of maternal KIR and fetal HLA-C have been found to be linked to problems in pregnancy and fertility; however, the evidence is evaluated in an inconsistent way when it comes to the definitions of ancestry, gestation, outcomes, study designs, and genetic testing methods. A clinically useful level of risk has not yet been established, and the fact that a specific genotype pairing is associated with an individual's reproductive outcome does not mean that it was the cause of that outcome. The review looks at the molecular evidence, compares the results from studies on assisted reproduction with those from population-based reproductive studies, and evaluates whether testing the parents or the embryos could lead to improvements in therapeutic methods. It also reviews established indications of preimplantation genetic testing (PGT), embryo HLA-C selection trials, donor selection, the use of intralipid, intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG), granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF), and single-embryo transfer. Current guidelines do not recommend routine HLA-C matching or KIR-directed immune modulation for recurrent implantation failure (RIF). The results of KIR/HLA-C testing also do not currently alter evidence-based prenatal care, which still depends on the patient's medical history and the presence of clear clinical findings. Although preliminary studies provide substantial evidence, the findings still require validation through larger studies and randomized trials, and adverse effects and equity concerns need to be addressed before embryo selection or specific treatments can be formally introduced into standard clinical practice.

articles.title: IVG and the future of embryo selection: from reproductive autonomy to reproductive optimization.
articles.journal: Journal of assisted reproduction and genetics
articles.authors: Choong E, Radway-Fatuga D, Takahashi S et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: In vitro gametogenesis (IVG) has the potential to transform assisted reproduction by generating functional gametes from pluripotent stem cells and expanding access to genetic parenthood. However, a less explored consequence is its potential to enable the production of hundreds of embryos, fundamentally changing the scale and nature of embryo selection. This paper examines how such "embryo abundance" could intensify existing ethical concerns surrounding preimplantation genetic testing, polygenic embryo screening, and artificial intelligence-driven embryo ranking.
METHODS: This paper presents a conceptual and ethical analysis of the implications of large-scale embryo production and selection enabled by IVG, focusing on reproductive autonomy, disability, procreative beneficence, inequality, and the commercialisation of reproductive medicine.
RESULTS: Increasing the number of embryos available for selection may shift reproductive decision-making from therapeutic medicine towards reproductive optimization, creating new pressures to select the perceived "best" embryo. As selection becomes increasingly technologically feasible and socially normalized, reproductive choice may paradoxically evolve into expectations of reproductive responsibility.
CONCLUSIONS: IVG requires anticipatory ethical and regulatory consideration extending beyond questions of safety and access. Governance must address not only whether IVG can be introduced safely, but also how large-scale embryo selection may reshape understandings of reproductive autonomy, human variation, and responsible parenthood.

articles.title: Bone Marrow Dendritic Cells-derived Exosomes Alleviate Ovariectomy-induced Depression in Rats by Suppressing NF-κB-mediated Neuroinflammation and Restoring T-cell Homeostasis.
articles.authors: Bashir SM, William MM, Abdou K et al.
articles.abstract: Depression is a prevalent neuropsychiatric disorder, particularly among post-menopausal women, and is strongly linked to neuroinflammation and immune dysregulation. Emerging evidence suggests that exosomes derived from bone marrow dendritic cells (BMDCs) possess potent immunomodulatory properties. The present study investigated their therapeutic efficacy in an ovariectomy-induced rat model of post-menopausal depression. BMDCs were prepared and identified, and then the exosomes were isolated by differential ultracentrifugation. Forty-five female rats were randomly allocated into three groups (n = 15): sham-operated rats (SO), ovariectomized rats (OVX), and ovariectomized rats treated with BMDCs-derived exosomes (EXO), administered intravenously via the tail vein at a dose of 200 µg/kg/dose in 0.2 mL PBS on days 7 and 14 post-ovariectomy. Behavioral, neurochemical, and immunological assessments were subsequently performed. Ovariectomy-induced depression was associated with increased hippocampal neuronal apoptosis, enhanced microglial activation, and elevated levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines. In addition, ovariectomy disrupted T-cell homeostasis, as evidenced by alterations in CD4, CD8, and regulatory T-cell populations, and activated NF-κB signaling, thereby promoting a shift toward the pro-inflammatory M1 microglial phenotype. Administration of BMDCs-derived exosomes significantly attenuated these alterations by suppressing M1 polarization, enhancing the M2 phenotype, restoring T-cell balance, and inhibiting NF-κB activation. BMDCs-derived exosomes can be considered as a promising candidate for the management of post-menopausal depression and similar neuropsychiatric disorders through modulation of neuroinflammation and immune responses.

articles.title: Vulvar Paget Disease: From Empirical Management to Emerging Precision Oncology Strategies.
articles.authors: Corrado G, Pomati G, Palluzzi E et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Extramammary Paget disease (EMPD) is a rare cutaneous adenocarcinoma arising in apocrine gland-bearing skin, most commonly affecting the vulva. While non-invasive disease generally follows an indolent course with favorable prognosis, invasive locoregionally advanced or metastatic EMPD remains a major therapeutic challenge because of poor outcomes, lack of disease-specific guidelines, and limited efficacy of conventional systemic therapies. This unmet need supports a shift from empirical treatment toward biologically informed strategies. We performed a narrative review of PubMed and clinical trial registries to evaluate current therapies and emerging molecularly driven approaches, with particular focus on vulvar Paget disease (VPD).
RECENT FINDINGS: Available evidence suggests that conventional cytotoxic chemotherapy offers only temporary disease control with limited durable benefit. In contrast, recent molecular and immunological discoveries are reshaping the therapeutic landscape. HER2 currently represents the most clinically actionable target, supported by a strong biological rationale, multiple clinical reports, and the best prospective evidence available to date. Other potential targets include immune-related biomarkers, steroid hormone receptor signaling, GLUT1, NECTIN4, tumor mutational burden, and selected histology-agnostic genomic alterations, highlighting the marked biological heterogeneity of EMPD. However, most evidence remains preclinical or derives from small case series. Immune checkpoint inhibitors have shown sporadic but clinically meaningful activity in selected patients, particularly in tumors with high tumor mutational burden, supporting biomarker-driven immunotherapeutic strategies. Advanced EMPD should be regarded not simply as a rare chemoresistant malignancy, but as a biologically heterogeneous disease requiring comprehensive pathological, immunohistochemical, and molecular characterization to guide future precision-based therapies.

articles.title: Farm typologies and reproductive management organisation associated with pregnancy per artificial insemination in peri-urban cattle farms around Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso.
articles.authors: Yamboué AT, Ouédraogo A, Hanzen C
articles.abstract: Pregnancy outcomes following bovine artificial insemination (AI) remain highly variable in peri-urban cattle systems of sub-Saharan Africa. This study aimed to identify farm typologies based on reproductive management characteristics and to determine organisational characteristics associated with pregnancy per AI (P/AI) in peri-urban cattle farms of Burkina Faso. A cross-sectional multi-stakeholder survey was conducted in 52 farms around Ouagadougou, involving 52 farmers, 52 resident herders and 12 inseminators. Data were analysed using multiple correspondence analysis, hierarchical cluster analysis and non-parametric tests. Overall P/AI was 42.7 ± 23.7% (95% confidence interval: 36.1-49.3%), ranging from 0 to 90% among farms. Three farm groups were identified: Group A (n = 17; widespread record-keeping and strong integration of AI into breeding strategies), mean P/AI 52.9%; Group B (n = 6; limited record-keeping and frequent discontinuation of AI), 5.0%; and Group C (n = 29; sustained AI use and high perceived economic benefit of AI), 44.5%. P/AI was lower in Group B than in Groups A and C (both P = 0.001), whereas Groups A and C did not differ (P = 0.154). Farms maintaining reproductive records had higher P/AI than those without records (48.8% vs. 13.4%; P < 0.001). Inseminator unavailability was the constraint most frequently reported by farmers (78.8%), whereas all inseminators (n = 12) reported inadequate oestrus detection. Given the cross-sectional design, these findings indicate associations rather than causal effects; reproductive record-keeping, oestrus detection and access to AI services nonetheless warrant further attention.

articles.title: Exploring the molecular biology of apoptosis in cervical cancer through proteomic signatures and computational analysis of Bacillus subtilis Lipopeptides.
articles.authors: Nafisah W, Lisdiana L, Sajidah ES et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bacillus subtilis produces diverse bioactive lipopeptides associated with various biological activities, including potential anticancer effects. However, their molecular targets and mechanisms against cervical cancer remain insufficiently characterized.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to characterize lipopeptide-associated biosynthetic pathways in a local Indonesian Bacillus subtilis strain and investigate the potential molecular targets and anticancer mechanisms of representative lipopeptides against cervical cancer using an integrated in silico approach.
METHODS: Lipopeptide-associated proteins were characterized using LC-HRMS-based proteomic analysis. Representative lipopeptides were selected based on detected protein entries and supporting literature. Target prediction was performed using SwissTargetPrediction and SEA Search, while cervical cancer-associated genes were obtained from OMIM and GeneCards. Overlapping targets were analyzed using protein-protein interaction and functional enrichment analyses. Molecular docking was performed against prioritized caspase targets, followed by 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations.
RESULTS: LC-HRMS-based proteomic analysis identified protein entries associated with surfactin-, iturin-, and fengycin-related biosynthetic pathways. Surfactin, iturin A, and fengycin were selected as representative lipopeptides. Network pharmacology identified 25 overlapping targets, with apoptosis-related processes and pathways among the enriched functions. Caspase-3, caspase-8, and caspase-9 were prioritized as key targets. Molecular docking showed that iturin A had the most favorable docking profile, particularly toward caspase-8. Molecular dynamics revealed target-dependent conformational responses across the caspase complexes.
CONCLUSION: The integrated computational findings suggest that iturin A may interact with apoptosis-associated caspases, supporting its potential involvement in the anticancer activity of B. subtilis-derived lipopeptides. Experimental studies are required to validate these predicted interactions and their functional relevance in cervical cancer.

articles.title: Gynecologic problems in adolescents and young adults: a 30-year referral cohort from a tertiary pediatric and adolescent gynecology clinic in Korea.
articles.authors: Min J, Kim SE, Lee DY et al.
articles.abstract: Adolescent gynecologic practice relies largely on adult-derived evidence, as age-specific data remain limited. We compared the spectrum of gynecologic problems in Korean adolescents and young adults and, as a secondary analysis, examined whether the age at diagnosis of congenital causes of primary amenorrhea has changed over three decades. We retrospectively reviewed 6,350 patients (adolescents aged 10-19 years, n = 2,841; young adults aged 20-29 years, n = 3,509) who attended a pediatric and adolescent gynecology clinic between January 1995 and December 2024. Chief complaints, final diagnoses, and trends in age at diagnosis across three 10-year periods were analyzed. Menstrual disorders were the most frequent complaint in both groups but were more prevalent in adolescents (74.4% vs. 64.7%, p < 0.001). Endocrine disorders were the leading diagnosis, again more frequent in adolescents (36.4% vs. 28.2%, p < 0.001). Turner syndrome was the predominant cause of primary amenorrhea in adolescents (39.8%), and Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser (MRKH) syndrome in adults (62.0%). Polycystic ovary syndrome appeared more prevalent among adolescents with secondary amenorrhea (51.1% vs. 37.8%, p = 0.019), but this difference did not persist after applying adolescent-specific criteria (33.3% vs. 37.3%, p = 0.516). The median age at diagnosis of Turner syndrome decreased from 18 to 13 years (ρ =- 0.580, p < 0.001), whereas that of MRKH syndrome was unchanged (median 20 years; ρ =- 0.033, p = 0.731).Conclusion: Within the limits of a single-center referral cohort, the gynecologic disease spectrum is age-specific. Despite improved imaging access, diagnostic delay in MRKH syndrome showed no detectable improvement, supporting proactive pelvic imaging in adolescents with primary amenorrhea. What is Known • Adolescent gynecologic care is largely extrapolated from adult evidence, and long-term trends in the age at diagnosis of congenital causes of primary amenorrhea have not been characterized. What is New • Over 30 years, median age at Turner syndrome diagnosis fell from 18 to 13 years, whereas MRKH syndrome showed no detectable change from 20 years, indicating persistent diagnostic delay.

articles.title: Tailored lateral internal sphincterotomy: a retrospective analysis on functional and recurrence outcomes in a highly selected cohort.
articles.authors: Bonomo LD, Gallo G, Gravante G et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lateral internal sphincterotomy (LIS) is the gold standard treatment for chronic anal fissure (CAF), but concerns regarding postoperative fecal incontinence limit its acceptance. Tailored LIS, restricted to the fissure apex, has been proposed to preserve continence while maintaining efficacy. This study aimed to evaluate functional outcomes and recurrence rates after tailored LIS in a highly selected cohort.
METHODS: A retrospective single-center study was conducted including patients with idiopathic CAF and increased anal sphincter tone undergoing tailored LIS between January 2019 and December 2024 after failure of conservative therapy. Patients with preoperative continence impairment or additional confounding factors were excluded. Continence was assessed pre- and postoperatively using the Vaizey score. Postoperative continence disorder was defined as Vaizey ≥ 1. Recurrence was defined as fissure persistence or relapse requiring re-intervention.
RESULTS: Sixty-two patients completed at least 1-year follow-up (median 3 years). All had a preoperative Vaizey score of 0. Clinical success was achieved in 60 patients (96.8%; 95% CI 88.8-99.6%), while recurrence occurred in 2 patients (3.2%; 95% CI 0.4-11.2%). Nine patients (14.5%; 95% CI 6.9-25.8%) developed some degree of continence alteration within the first postoperative year. No cases of solid stool incontinence were observed (0%; 95% CI 0-5.8%). Gas incontinence occurred in 14.5% (95% CI 6.9-25.8%) and liquid stool incontinence in 4.8% (95% CI 1.0-13.5%). Mild continence alteration (Vaizey 1-4) was observed in 9.7% (95% CI 3.6-19.9%) and moderate incontinence (Vaizey 5-9) in 4.8% (95% CI 1.0-13.5%).
CONCLUSIONS: In appropriately selected patients, tailored LIS achieves high healing rates with a low incidence of clinically relevant continence impairment at mid-term follow-up. Limiting sphincter division to the fissure apex appears to balance efficacy and continence preservation.

articles.title: PECRoP-003: Determinants and operative outcomes of three- versus four-arm configuration in robotic surgery for benign gynecologic disease: a multicenter cohort study.
articles.authors: Borghese B, Gaudet Chardonnet A, Blanc T et al.
articles.abstract: Robotic gynecologic surgery can be performed with three or four robotic arms, but no data guide this choice in benign disease. We aimed to identify the determinants of four-arm configuration and its association with operative outcomes. We performed a secondary analysis of data collected prospectively in the PECRoP multicenter registry (nine Paris university hospitals), including 753 women operated on with the da Vinci Xi system for benign or pre-invasive gynecologic disease between 2023 and 2025 with three (n = 304) or four (n = 449) arms. Determinants were assessed by surgeon-clustered logistic regression (generalized estimating equations) and operative outcomes by surgeon-clustered linear regression. Endometriosis (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.41, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.45-3.99), sacrocolpopexy (aOR 3.21, 1.48-6.97) and body mass index (aOR 1.05 per kg/m², 1.03-1.08) were associated with four arms, and adenomyosis with three arms (aOR 0.60, 0.40-0.89). Four-arm use ranged from 32% to 93% across centers and from 26% to 100% across surgeons, and this variation persisted after adjustment for measured case-mix. Four-arm configuration was associated with longer console time (+ 23.9 min, 95% CI 11.6-36.3) and operating room occupation (+ 31.0 min, 15.8-46.2), including within the 13 surgeons who regularly used both configurations (console time + 20.9 min, 6.2-35.7), without a detectable difference in conversions (2.0% vs. 2.9%) or major complications (2.0% vs. 2.4%), although the study was underpowered for rare events. The fourth arm is chosen for complex cases but also reflects local practice. These associations may partly reflect unmeasured case complexity and warrant prospective evaluation.Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03274050 (first submitted 24 July 2017).

articles.title: Trio-based whole-exome sequencing and minigene assay identify a novel MYH11 splice site variant (c.2997 + 5G > C) in recurrent fetal megacystis.
articles.authors: Li W, Qian Y, Gao P et al.
articles.abstract: Megacystis-microcolon-intestinal hypoperistalsis syndrome (MMIHS) is a severe visceral myopathy with high perinatal mortality. Although autosomal dominant inheritance due to heterozygous ACTG2 variants is most common, autosomal recessive transmission involving biallelic loss-of-function variants in MYH11 is increasingly recognized, making prenatal diagnosis challenging, particularly for novel variants of uncertain significance (VUS). In this study, we report a nonconsanguineous Chinese family exhibiting recurrent fetal megacystis. Trio-based whole-exome sequencing (Trio-WES) identified compound heterozygous variants in the MYH11 gene: a maternally inherited 1.9 Mb deletion encompassing MYH11 at 16p13.11, and a novel paternally inherited splice-site variant (c.2997 + 5G > C). The pathogenicity of the c.2997 + 5G > C variant was confirmed through a minigene splicing assay, which demonstrated aberrant splicing characterized by intron retention, and through in silico simulation, which predicted that the insertion disrupts the native α-helical structure of the myosin chain, inducing disordered coil conformations characterized by turns and hairpins. This confirmation facilitated a definitive prenatal diagnosis. This study identifies a novel pathogenic splice site variant in MYH11 associated with MMIHS and provides functional evidence supporting its role in the disease's etiology. Our findings highlight the critical importance of integrating genomic analyses with functional assays to refine interpretation of VUS, expand the mutational spectrum of MMIHS, and improve genetic counseling for affected families.

articles.title: Adjuvant chemotherapy and overall survival in premenopausal women with HR+/HER2 - early breast cancer: a national cancer database analysis in the era of genomic testing and CDK4/6 inhibitors.
articles.authors: Lopetegui-Lia N, Gokun Y, Davenport AP et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Genomic assays guide adjuvant treatment decisions in early-stage hormone receptor-positive/HER2-negative (HR+/HER2-) breast cancer, yet contemporary treatment patterns and outcomes among premenopausal women remain incompletely characterized, particularly as adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibitors enter routine use. We characterized adjuvant chemotherapy use and its association with overall survival (OS) in premenopausal women with early-stage HR+/HER2- breast cancer, stratified by Oncotype DX recurrence score (RS) and by eligibility for adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibitor therapy.
METHODS: In this retrospective National Cancer Database (NCDB) analysis, we identified 19,419 premenopausal women (age < 50 years as a surrogate for menopausal status), diagnosed with stage I-III HR+/HER2-, clinically node-negative (including those pathologically node-positive) invasive breast cancer between 2018 and 2022. Primary and secondary exposures were adjuvant chemotherapy and CDK4/6 inhibitor eligibility. The primary outcome was OS. Cox proportional hazards models with robust variance were adjusted a priori for age, RS, and positive lymph nodes, with additional RS-stratified analyses.
RESULTS: Overall, 13,490 women (69.5%) received no adjuvant chemotherapy. Chemotherapy receipt rose with genomic risk and CDK4/6 inhibitor eligibility, while OncotypeDX testing was least frequent in the highest-risk groups. Adjuvant chemotherapy was independently associated with improved OS overall (adjusted HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.47-0.86). In RS-stratified analyses, the association was limited to RS 21-25 (aHR 0.24, 95% CI 0.08-0.68) and unknown RS (aHR 0.61, 95% CI 0.42-0.89).
CONCLUSION: Adjuvant chemotherapy was associated with improved OS, mostly among RS 21-25 and a higher-risk unknown-RS group. Frequent absence of genomic testing among CDK4/6 inhibitor-eligible women highlights an opportunity to better integrate genomic and clinical-anatomic risk in treatment selection.

articles.title: Mechanism-based targeted drug delivery strategies for uterine fibroids (leiomyomas): from pathogenesis to therapy.
articles.authors: Firdous Z, Shirasath KR, Goyal SN et al.
articles.abstract: Uterine fibroids (leiomyomas) are benign, monoclonal smooth-muscle tumors with a characteristically fibrotic extracellular matrix (ECM). They are highly prevalent, affecting approximately ​70-80% ofwomen by the age of 50 and represents a significant global health burden due to their adverse effects on reproductive health, quality of life and overall well-being. The pathophysiology of this illness is multifaceted, including hormonal dysregulation, aberrant transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β) signaling, excessive ECM remodeling, angiogenesis, unique genetic/epigenetic modifications and some emerging pathways in fibroid biology. The usual diagnosis includes pelvic examination, ultrasound, MRI, hysteroscopy and hysterosonography. Traditional treatments are mostly surgical with high recurrence rates and possible loss of fertility. Recent advances have focused on the use of novel drug delivery systems (NDDS) for mechanism-based targeted therapeutics, including nanoparticles, liposomes, hydrogels, vaginal delivery and stimuli-responsive delivery vectors designed to exploit specific biochemical pathways and morphological features of uterine fibroids. NDDS are being investigated for the targeted administration of hormone modulators, TGF-β inhibitors, ECM-targeting agents, anti-angiogenic agents and genetic therapy (siRNA/miRNA) to fibroid tissue, with the aim of reducing systemic toxicity and improving treatment success. However, the evidence is largely preclinical (cell and animal models), and this review critically appraises the strengths, limitations and stage of development of each strategy. The translation of these advanced medicines into clinical practice is challenged by fibroid heterogeneity, possible immunogenicity and toxicity of nanomaterials, manufacturing difficulty, and regulatory constraints. However, future strategies are based on individualized nanomedicine, AI-driven drug discovery and multi-target combo therapy to increase effectiveness, limit recurrence, and maintain fertility. In summary, mechanism-based targeted drug delivery is a promising but still largely preclinical strategy for uterine fibroids. By linking molecular pathology with delivery technology, it may enable more precise and patient-centred therapies, but this potential must be confirmed in clinically relevant models and clinical trials.

articles.title: Bruceine D induces ferroptosis in ectocervical Ect1/E6E7 cells by modulating GSTP1 and MAPK14 signaling and downregulating GPX4.
articles.authors: Han M, Lian S, Zhu J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) is the principal cause of cervical precancerous lesions and cervical cancer. Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death, is a potential therapeutic target in HPV-associated malignancies. Bruceine D (BD), a bioactive quassinoid isolated from Brucea javanica, exhibits antitumor and antiviral activities. However, its effects on HPV-associated cervical epithelial cells remain unclear.
METHODS: The effects of BD on HPV16 E6/E7-immortalized ectocervical epithelial cells (Ect1/E6E7) were evaluated using cell viability, colony formation, EdU incorporation, and cell-cycle assays. Ferroptosis-associated changes were assessed by measuring lipid peroxidation, glutathione (GSH) and malondialdehyde (MDA) levels, mitochondrial membrane potential, and the expression of ferroptosis-related proteins. Pharmacological rescue experiments using ferroptosis inhibitors and pathway inhibitors were performed to investigate the underlying mechanisms. Network pharmacology analysis and experimental validation were used to identify candidate regulatory targets.
RESULTS: BD significantly inhibited Ect1/E6E7 cell proliferation and induced G0/G1 cell-cycle arrest in a concentration-dependent manner. BD treatment increased lipid peroxidation and MDA levels, depleted intracellular GSH, disrupted mitochondrial function, and downregulated GPX4. Ferroptosis inhibitors partially reversed BD-induced cell death, supporting the involvement of ferroptosis. Network pharmacology analysis and experimental validation implicated GSTP1 and MAPK14 in the cellular response to BD. Pharmacological inhibition of MAPK14 attenuated BD-induced ferroptotic responses, suggesting a role for GSTP1/MAPK14-associated signaling. BD also exhibited synergistic antiproliferative effects when combined with the ferroptosis inducer erastin.
CONCLUSION: BD reduces the survival of HPV16 E6/E7-immortalized cervical epithelial cells by inducing ferroptosis associated with GPX4 downregulation and GSTP1/MAPK14 signaling. These findings support further preclinical investigation of BD and ferroptosis-based approaches in HPV-associated cervical disease.

articles.title: Maternal thyroid function in the first half of pregnancy and child internalising and externalising problems over time.
articles.authors: Keestra SM, Molenaar ACM, de Rooij SR et al.
articles.abstract: Adequate gestational thyroid function is important for offspring neurodevelopment, yet behavioural implications of variation within the normal range are unclear. We examined associations with externalising and internalising problems across repeated assessments in childhood and adolescence. 2,606 mother-child dyads from the Amsterdam Born Children and their Development (ABCD) cohort with maternal free thyroxine (FT4) and thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) measurements in the first half of pregnancy and at least one child SDQ assessment. Primary analysis excluded women with overt thyroid disease or thyroid medication use and children born < 32 weeks or < 1500 g. Linear mixed-effects models were applied to Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ) scores at 5-6, 11-12 and 15-16 years, via mother-, teacher-, and self-report. Secondary analyses included logistic regression for borderline SDQ cut-offs, sex interactions, and effect modification by TSH. FT4 showed a U-shaped association with teacher-reported externalising problems (quadratic β = 9.49, FDR-adjusted p = 0.03), with higher scores at both low and high FT4. Higher FT4 was associated with lower child-reported internalising problems (β = -0.17, FDR-adjusted p = 0.04). For both primary associations, there was no evidence of FT4-by-age interaction, suggesting differences in problem levels rather than thyroid-related differences in symptom change over time. At age 5-6, FT4 showed a non-linear association with teacher-reported hyperactivity/inattention above the threshold, with a negative linear term (OR = 0.83, 95% CI: 0.72 to 0.97) and a positive quadratic term (OR = 1.11, 95% CI: 1.02 to 1.20). At age 11-12, higher FT4 was associated with fewer self-reported peer problems (OR = 0.84, 95% CI:0.71-0.99). In exploratory analyses, curvature of the FT4-externalising association varied by maternal TSH; no sex modification was detected. Within a cohort free of overt thyroid disease, maternal thyroid function in the first half of pregnancy was associated with domain- and rater-specific differences in child internalising and externalising problems. We found no evidence that these associations changed across the available repeated assessments, suggesting differences in average problem scores rather than differences in how symptoms changed with age.

articles.title: Persistent bowel dysfunction and health-related quality of life after surgery for Hirschsprung disease: generic versus disease-specific outcomes and measurement heterogeneity in children and adolescents.
articles.authors: Fatima R
articles.abstract: Hirschsprung disease (HD) is a condition that can implant intestinal continuity surgically although technical success does not necessarily correlate with its age-specific bowel functionality. This critical narrative review addresses the association of persistent postoperative bowel dysfunction and health-related quality-of-life (HRQoL) with specific emphasis on discordance between generic and disease-specific measures, and on heterogeneity in the outcome measures. The literature review was updated: June 20 to July 15, 2026(PubMed), Web of science, Google Scholar, and NCBI Bookshelf. Twenty-five records were filtered and 19 sources published since 1998 constituted the main evidence base of outcomes; all sources were categorized according to evidence level and population and mixed HD/anorectal-malformation (ARM) evidence was classified as indirect. Reported constipation and fecal incontinence/soiling do not represent consistent reliable prevalence studies and vary greatly among the studies because of age, follow-up, operative method, definitions, questionnaire, type of respondent and bowel-management practice. The chronic obstructive symptoms need an assessment of mechanical or histopathologic errors that can be corrected prior to the intensification of bowel management. No statistically significant difference in generic HRQoL at the group level was shown between healthy comparison and available evidence, though results indicated a great degree of heterogeneity, precluding a general interpretation; disease-specific instruments and symptom-stratified analyses showed evidence of statistically important impairment in a sub-group with chronic dysfunction. Parent- proxy and child self-reports are not interchangeable but rather give complementary views. A standardized follow-up ought to thus combine effective bowel-function evaluation, generic and disease-specific HRQoL questionnaires, in addition to child plus parent reports.

articles.title: Association Between Menopause Duration and Oral Health Manifestations: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.authors: Santhiya K, Pavithra D, Kavitha M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Menopause is associated with hormonal changes that influence multiple body systems and may affect oral health, thereby impacting overall well-being and quality of life in midlife women. Oral health manifestations during the postmenopausal period often remain under-recognized in routine healthcare.
OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study is to assess the association between duration since menopause and oral health manifestations in postmenopausal women.
METHODOLOGY: This cross-sectional study included 75 postmenopausal women attending a dental outpatient clinic. Participants were categorized based on duration since menopause into three groups: 1-5 years, 6-10 years, and >10 years (25 participants in each group). Oral health manifestations including xerostomia, burning mouth symptoms, taste disturbances, tongue coating, and periodontal status were assessed using the standard clinical indices. Statistical analysis included Spearman correlation, Kruskal-Wallis test for continuous variables, Chi-square test for categorical variables, and age-adjusted regression analyses (ordinal logistic, binary logistic, and linear regression as appropriate).
RESULTS: An increasing trend in oral health manifestations was observed with longer duration since menopause in midlife women. Significant associations were observed in unadjusted analyses; however, none remained statistically significant after adjustment for age.
CONCLUSION: Although oral health manifestations appear to increase with longer duration since menopause, these associations were attenuated after age adjustment and were not independent of age. In this cross-sectional study, the findings should therefore be interpreted as descriptive trends rather than causal relationships. Increased awareness of these manifestations may support improved oral healthcare in postmenopausal women.

articles.title: Role of Transvaginal Three-dimensional Power Doppler Ultrasound and Hysteroscopy in Postmenopausal Bleeding.
articles.authors: Sharma V, Meena J, Singhal S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postmenopausal bleeding (PMB) is a warning symptom and is associated with endometrial malignancy in 10%-15% of cases. Endometrial thickness (ET) measurement using transvaginal ultrasound (TVS) guides the course of action, with ET >4 mm being ominous. Three-dimensional power Doppler (3DPD) ultrasound raises diagnostic utility with endometrial volume (EV) and vascularity indices-vascularization index (VI), flow Index (FI) and vascularization FI (VFI), while hysteroscopy provides a direct view of uterine lesions. Previous studies have worked on role of 3DPD or hysteroscopy in PMB patients, but none have compared these two. Hence, this study was conducted.
METHODS: This prospective observational study was conducted at a tertiary center, including 75 women with PMB. They underwent 3DPD ultrasound followed by hysteroscopy and endometrial biopsy. The diagnostic accuracy of Doppler parameters was analyzed using receiver operating characteristic curves. Hysteroscopic results were compared with histopathology, followed by comparison of 3DPD and hysteroscopy.
RESULTS: Out of 75 patients, 65 (86.6%) had benign pathologies and 10 (13.4%) had malignancies. 3DPD parameters VI, VFI, and EV were significantly higher in the malignant group. EV had the highest diagnostic performance, with an area under curve (AUC) of 0.88 (cutoff ≥7.34 cm3), yielding 80% sensitivity and 80% specificity. VI, FI, and VFI achieved sensitivity/specificity of 80%/78.5%, 70%/70.8%, and 80%/73.8%, with AUCs of 0.83, 0.69, and 0.82, respectively. Hysteroscopy demonstrated 100% sensitivity and specificity for detecting endometrial malignancy and endometrial polyps. Cohen's kappa analysis of hysteroscopy and 3DPD showed agreement of 78.67%, 70.67%, 78.67%, and 80% between hysteroscopy and VI, FI, VFI and EV, respectively.
CONCLUSION: 3DPD, particularly EV, is a valuable noninvasive tool in PMB. Hysteroscopy remains a highly sensitive and specific modality for detecting malignancy, showing good correlation with 3DPD.

articles.title: Cancer Risk in Premature Ovarian Insufficiency: Current Evidence and Clinical Implications.
articles.authors: Devanbu VGC, John JB, Karpagam KV
articles.abstract: Premature ovarian insufficiency (POI), defined as loss of ovarian function before 40 years with elevated gonadotropins and oligo/amenorrhea, is increasingly recognized as a systemic condition with long-term health consequences. While cardiovascular, skeletal, and neurocognitive risks are well established, the relationship between POI and cancer risk remains less clearly understood. This mini-review summarizes current evidence on site-specific malignancy risks in women with POI and evaluates the influence of hormone replacement therapy (HRT) on cancer outcomes. Available epidemiological studies, cohort analyses, and guideline recommendations addressing cancer incidence in POI were reviewed, with emphasis on breast, ovarian, endometrial, colorectal, and autoimmune-associated malignancies. Women with spontaneous POI generally demonstrate a reduced risk of breast, ovarian, and endometrial cancers, largely attributed to lower lifetime estrogen exposure and fewer ovulatory cycles. However, cancer risk may vary by etiology: autoimmune POI is associated with increased thyroid cancer incidence, while genetic subgroups such as fragile X mental retardation 1 premutation carriers may exhibit altered ovarian cancer susceptibility. Importantly, physiological HRT in POI differs fundamentally from postmenopausal hormone therapy and does not appear to increase overall cancer risk when continued until the average age of natural menopause. POI is typically associated with lower risks of hormone-dependent malignancies, though subgroup-specific variations exist. Individualized counseling, appropriate progestin opposition, and further POI-specific cohort studies are essential to refine cancer surveillance strategies.

articles.title: Vitamin D Deficiency and Knee Osteoarthritis in Midlife Women: A Prospective Cohort Study with Annual Monitoring, Supplementation, and Menopausal Stratification.
articles.authors: Gupta M, Goyal A, Dinkar KS et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Midlife women face increased risk of knee osteoarthritis (OA), osteoporosis, and metabolic comorbidities. Vitamin D deficiency, highly prevalent in this population, may contribute to OA pathogenesis through effects on cartilage metabolism, bone remodeling, and inflammatory pathways. Addressing Vitamin D status during the menopausal transition is central to preventive care and healthy aging.
METHODS: In a 5-year prospective cohort study, 420 women aged 40-60 years without radiographic OA were enrolled. Serum 25(OH)D was measured annually. Deficiency was defined as <20 ng/mL, insufficiency as 20-29 ng/mL, and sufficiency as ≥30 ng/mL. Deficient participants received oral cholecalciferol (1000-2000 IU/day, adjusted annually). Primary outcome measures included radiographic OA (Kellgren-Lawrence grade ≥2) and clinical OA (ACR criteria). Cox proportional hazards models assessed risk adjusting for body mass index, menopausal status, physical activity, comorbidities, diet, and sunlight exposure.
RESULTS: At baseline, 38% were deficient. Over 5 years, 112 women developed OA. Incidence was highest in persistently deficient postmenopausal women (40%, hazard ratio [HR]: 2.30, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.50-3.52), intermediate in perimenopausal deficient women (28%, HR: 1.60, 95% CI: 1.02-2.52), and lowest in sufficient women (14%, reference). Correction of deficiency reduced incidence to 20% (absolute risk reduction [ARR]: 16.3%, number needed to treat [NNT]: 6.1). Annual monitoring revealed that sustained sufficiency reduced OA risk (adjusted HR: 0.6, 95% CI: 0.4-0.9, P = 0.01). Sustained sufficiency yielded ARR 22.2% and NNT 4.5. These findings highlight Vitamin D optimization as a clinically meaningful preventive strategy.
CONCLUSION: Persistent Vitamin D deficiency is a modifiable risk factor for knee OA in midlife women, particularly postmenopausal women. Annual monitoring and supplementation reduce incidence, with ARR and NNT values demonstrating tangible clinical impact. Preventive care pathways should integrate Vitamin D screening into midlife women's health programs to reduce musculoskeletal disease burden and enhance quality of life during the menopausal transition.

articles.title: Prediction of lncRNA-cervical cancer associations using a multi-view collaborative variational autoencoder with knowledge distillation transfer learning.
articles.authors: Yuan M, Xiong T, Abasi X et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) play critical regulatory roles in the pathogenesis of cervical cancer, and accurate identification of lncRNA-cervical cancer associations is important for understanding the molecular mechanisms of the disease and discovering potential therapeutic targets. However, the extreme scarcity of cervical cancer-specific lncRNA association data constitutes a major bottleneck limiting the performance of existing computational prediction methods.
METHODS: To address this challenge, we propose a Multi-View Collaborative Variational Autoencoder based on Knowledge Distillation Transfer Learning (MVCVAE), which integrates multi-source heterogeneous data fusion and cross-disease knowledge transfer in a task-oriented manner. The multi-view collaborative variational autoencoder constructs dual-view feature representations of lncRNA and disease similarities and employs a symmetric encoder-decoder architecture to learn complex lncRNA-disease association patterns in the latent space. The knowledge distillation transfer learning framework adopts a teacher-student network design: a teacher model is pre-trained on a large-scale dataset containing 12,865 lncRNA-disease associations to learn general association patterns, and the resulting prior knowledge is effectively transferred to a student model targeting 92 cervical cancer associations through feature distillation and prediction distillation strategies.
RESULTS: In five-fold cross-validation, MVCVAE achieves an AUC of 0.9228 ± 0.0058.
DISCUSSION: Through the synergistic effects of multi-view heterogeneous information fusion and cross-domain knowledge transfer, MVCVAE demonstrates strong performance in predicting lncRNA-cervical cancer associations, effectively addressing the limitations imposed by the scarcity of cervical cancer-specific lncRNA association data.

articles.title: Precision Menopause Care in the Era of Artificial Intelligence: Bridging Global Evidence and Indian Realities.
articles.authors: Sharma S, Mehra R
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Menopause is a universal biological milestone with profound implications for women's long term health. Increasing life expectancy has shifted the focus of care from symptom relief to healthy aging, chronic disease prevention, and quality of life.
OBJECTIVES: This review explores the evolution of menopause management toward precision medicine, the emerging role of artificial intelligence (AI) and digital health, global evidence, and the opportunities and challenges within the Indian healthcare landscape.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A narrative synthesis of international guidelines, consensus statements, and emerging literature was undertaken to contextualize precision menopause care. The Integrative Precision Menopause Care Framework (IPMCF) is proposed, integrating Clinical, Biological, Digital, Contextual, and Compassionate Precision upon the foundations of evidence based medicine, ethical governance, and woman centred care.
RESULTS: Precision menopause care extends beyond genomics to encompass multi omics, behavioural, and contextual determinants. AI offers potential for risk prediction, digital phenotyping, and decision support, while digital health ecosystems enable longitudinal monitoring and telemedicine. Global consensus emphasizes individualized assessment, shared decision making, and prevention. In India, opportunities include telemedicine, mobile health, and the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission, but challenges remain in cultural silence, fragmented services, and limited longitudinal datasets.
CONCLUSION: Precision menopause care must balance innovation with equity, ethics, and compassion. Vision 2035 anticipates proactive, preventive, and participatory care shaped by validated AI, digital health, and population specific evidence. Current applications remain largely investigational; robust validation, inclusive datasets, and context sensitive implementation are essential to ensure meaningful improvements in autonomy, equity, and health outcomes for midlife and older women.

articles.title: Association between Menopause-related Knowledge, Attitude, Coping Practices, and Perceived Stress among Postmenopausal Women: A Cross-sectional Study.
articles.authors: Mukherjee S, Roy S, Sharma S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Menopause is a natural transition, but poor understanding of symptoms, negative perceptions, and limited coping practices may increase perceived stress among postmenopausal women. This study aimed to assess menopause-related knowledge, attitude and coping practices, and determine their association with perceived stress among postmenopausal women.
METHODS: A community-based, analytical, cross-sectional study was conducted among 240 postmenopausal women aged 45-65 years. Data were collected using a structured Knowledge, Attitude and Practice questionnaire, and the Perceived Stress Scale-10. Sociodemographic and reproductive variables were also recorded. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Chi-square test, Pearson correlation, and multiple linear regression.
RESULTS: The mean age of the participants was 56.2 ± 5.8 years. Good menopause-related knowledge was observed in 38.3% of women, favorable attitude in 46.7%, and good coping practices in 34.2%. Moderate-to-high perceived stress was present in 61.7% of participants. Knowledge, attitude, and coping practice scores showed significant negative correlations with perceived stress. Poor coping practices, unfavorable attitude, low knowledge, low education, and severe menopausal symptoms were independently associated with higher perceived stress.
CONCLUSION: Better menopause-related knowledge, favorable attitude, and healthier coping practices were associated with lower perceived stress among postmenopausal women. Integrating menopause education, counseling, and stress screening into primary healthcare may improve psychological well-being in this population.

articles.title: Clinical Profile of patients attending Well Women Clinic in an Underprivileged Area in Bengaluru City.
articles.authors: Varghese S, Johnson AR, Gnanaselvam NA et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Breast and cervical cancer are common cancers among women in India. In Primary health care, gynecological morbidities such as bleeding, vaginal discharge, mental health issues, and the presence of comorbidities need provision of comprehensive care.
METHODS: We conducted a secondary data analysis of data from the monthly Well Women's Clinic conducted in an underprivileged area in Bangalore City from 2022 to 2025. Women's symptoms, clinical presentations, vital signs, anthropometric measurements, depression, anemia, diabetes and hypertension screening, and diabetes and PAP smear reports were analyzed.
RESULTS: A total of 313 women have sought the services of the Well Women's Clinic during the study period. The mean age of the study participants was 44 years (±13) with an average parity of 2 (±1). The mean age at menopause was 46 years (±5). Most of them were married (83.7%). Of the participants, 176 (61.5%) had comorbidities. Overweight was present among 118 (38.7%) and obesity among 102 (33.5%) of the women. Waist circumference indicated a substantial risk among 187 (78.6%) of the women. Of the presenting symptoms, 6 (1.9%) had a breast lump, 40 (12.8%) had irregular cycles, 36 (11.5%) had vaginal discharge, and 38 (12.1%) had genitourinary symptoms. Pap smear report was abnormal in 34 (21.5%) of the women. Of the Pap smear report, one was reported as a precancerous lesion.
CONCLUSION: In primary health care, provision of comprehensive women's health care includes screening of common noncommunicable diseases, depression, anemia, and cancer. Gender norms in the community prevent women to seek early access to care.

articles.title: Menopausal Symptoms in Natural and Surgical Menopause: Correlation with Serum Estradiol and Testosterone Levels.
articles.authors: Gupta S, Yadav P, Gupta N et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Menopause is a physiological transition often associated with bothersome somatic, psychological, and urogenital symptoms. While natural menopause occurs gradually, surgical menopause results in abrupt hormone withdrawal, often leading to more severe symptoms. The extent to which serum estradiol and testosterone influence these symptoms remains inadequately defined in the Indian population.
OBJECTIVES: The objectives of this study were to compare the severity and pattern of menopausal symptoms in women with natural and surgical menopause and to evaluate their correlation with serum estradiol and free testosterone levels.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A comparative observational study was conducted over 2 years at Sarojini Naidu Medical College, Agra, involving 198 postmenopausal women (102 - natural and 96 - surgical) within 5 years of menopause. Menopausal symptoms were assessed using the Menopause Rating Scale (MRS). Serum estradiol and free testosterone were measured using chemiluminescence immunoassay. Data were analyzed using t-tests, analysis of variance, and correlation statistics, with significance set at P < 0.05.
RESULTS: Women with surgical menopause showed significantly higher total MRS scores across somatic, psychological, and urogenital domains (P < 0.001). The mean serum estradiol was lower in the surgical group (72.3 ± 45.2 pmol/L) compared to the natural group (89.7 ± 38.4 pmol/L; P = 0.003). No significant difference was observed in free testosterone levels (P = 0.967). Symptom severity correlated inversely with estradiol levels, particularly in natural menopause. Free testosterone showed no meaningful correlation in either group.
CONCLUSION: Surgical menopause is associated with a significantly greater burden of menopausal symptoms, closely linked to reduced estradiol levels. Hormonal profiling may guide personalized treatment strategies for improved symptom control.

articles.title: ORIHIME® Mesh Size Adjustment Can Improve Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms and Prevent Complications Such as Prolapse Recurrence in Patients Undergoing Transvaginal Mesh Surgery.
articles.authors: Kuroda K, Hamamoto K, Kawamura K et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Pelvic organ prolapse (POP), a multifactorial condition defined as the descent of the pelvic organs through the vaginal wall, often correlates with lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS). Transvaginal mesh (TVM) surgery has a significant impact on LUTS; however, its therapeutic effects may vary depending on the type and shape of the mesh used. This study investigated the effects of mesh type used on LUTS and other surgical outcomes.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated 169 patients with POP who underwent TVM at our hospital. Preoperative and postoperative parameters were evaluated for the following patient groups: the Polyform™ group; those in the ORIHIME® group treated without adjustment of mesh size (AMS) beneath the bladder, with or without wide arms, designated as AMS (-), and those in the ORIHIME® group treated with AMS beneath the bladder with wide arms, designated as AMS (+).
RESULTS: Post-void residual urine volume, International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS), Quality of Life (QOL) scores, the Overactive Bladder Symptom Score (OABSS), and International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire Short-Form score significantly decreased after surgery compared with the preoperative condition in all groups. However, the 60-min pad weight test showed a significant change after surgery only in the AMS (+) group. Upon comparing the preoperative and 1-year postoperative outcomes, the AMS (+) group showed significantly better outcomes in the IPSS plus QOL scores, OABSS, and the rate of prolapse recurrence than the AMS (-) and/or Polyform™ groups.
CONCLUSION: AMS beneath the bladder can improve LUTS and prevent complications such as recurrence.

articles.title: Transvaginal Mesh Surgery using the Adjusted Size of ORIHIME® Mesh with Wide-arm Widths: Favorable Postoperative Outcomes Compared to Conventional Polypropylene Mesh.
articles.authors: Kuroda K, Hamamoto K, Kawamura K et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Pelvic organ prolapse (POP) is defined as the downward displacement of pelvic structures. Transvaginal mesh surgery (TVM) is a surgical approach that serves as a viable intervention for POP repair; nonetheless, its effectiveness may differ depending on the mesh type and design employed. This study aimed to examine the influence of mesh type on postoperative quality of life (QOL) related to POP and other postoperative outcomes.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Preoperative and postoperative parameters, including the prolapse QOL (P-QOL) questionnaire score, were evaluated between two patient groups: patients treated with a wide-arm ORIHIME® mesh of adjusted mesh size (AMS) were assigned to the ORIHIME® AMS (+) group, and patients treated with a Prolift-type TVM using Gynemesh® PS or an Elevate-type TVM using a Polyform™ mesh comprised the nonORIHIME® group.
RESULTS: Almost all postoperative P-QOL component scores significantly decreased from preoperative scores in both groups. However, no significant decreases were found in the personal relationship subscale scores at 3 and 12 months postsurgery in the ORIHIME® AMS (+) group and at 3 months postsurgery in the non-ORIHIME® group compared with their preoperative values. The role limitations' subscale was significantly lower in the ORIHIME® AMS (+) group than in the non-ORIHIME® group. The ORIHIME® AMS (+) group demonstrated significantly better outcomes in urinary incontinence (UI) and mesh exposure rates compared with the non-ORIHIME® group.
CONCLUSION: Adjustment of the wide-arm ORIHIME® mesh size improved postoperative QOL and reduced complications such as UI compared with TVM using conventional mesh products.

articles.title: Development, Comparison With Genetic Counselors' Assessments, and Usability Evaluation of Japanese Version of Cancer Risk Assessment System in Primary Care (JCRAS-PC) for Hereditary Breast and Ovarian Cancer and Lynch Syndrome.
articles.journal: Journal of general and family medicine
articles.authors: Narumoto K, Kojima R, Shibata A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer risk associated with hereditary breast and ovarian cancer (HBOC) and Lynch syndrome (LS) can be mitigated by risk assessment based on personal and family health information, followed by evidence-based preventive strategies. However, no validated risk assessment digital tool exists for primary care in Japan. We aimed to develop a guideline-based digital tool, called the Japanese version of the cancer risk assessment system in primary care (JCRAS-PC), compare its assessments with those of genetic counselors, and evaluate its usability.
METHODS: A multidisciplinary team developed JCRAS-PC, where primary care physicians (PCPs) enter personal and family cancer history within a pedigree and receive an assessment of whether referral for genetic counseling or testing for HBOC/LS is warranted. Referral criteria were consolidated from Japanese and international guidelines. We compared JCRAS-PC assessments with those of two genetic counselors across 35 de-identified real-world cases and calculated kappa statistics. Usability was evaluated through semi-structured individual interviews with seven PCPs using inductive thematic analysis.
RESULTS: In the evaluation, JCRAS-PC was revised for implementation errors. The revised JCRAS-PC assessments showed complete agreement with those of genetic counselors in all 35 cases (prevalence-adjusted bias-adjusted kappa = 1.00). Thematic analysis confirmed enhanced usability, and PCP participants' feedback led to revisions to improve functionality. In interviews, JCRAS-PC appeared to positively influence PCPs' knowledge and attitudes toward clinical cancer genetics.
CONCLUSIONS: We developed JCRAS-PC, evaluated its agreement with genetic counselors' assessments, and confirmed its usability for Japanese PCPs. Its clinical validity and utility in primary care populations warrant further investigation.

articles.title: Racial and ethnic disparities in cervical length screening for spontaneous preterm birth prediction.
articles.authors: Wang-Koehler E, Cenac LA, Wheeler SM et al.
articles.abstract: Preterm birth (PTB) remains the leading cause of perinatal morbidity and mortality in the United States, with persistent racial and ethnic disparities, particularly at earlier gestational ages. Cervical length (CL) screening is one of the few clinically actionable strategies for identifying individuals at elevated risk for spontaneous PTB (sPTB), providing a focused lens to examine these disparities. This review examines (1) CL screening disparities among patients with and without a history of sPTB, (2) differences in CL across racial and social groups, (3) how race and social context relate to CL-based prediction of sPTB, (4) sPTB disparities after accounting for CL, and (5) whether CL screening reduces disparities in sPTB outcomes. Overall, evidence on disparities in screening uptake is mixed. Opt-out programs with high overall uptake (>90%) showed minimal racial differences, whereas programs with lower uptake found Black, Hispanic, and/or Asian patients less likely to receive CL screening; most studies cannot distinguish screening never offered from screening declined. Black individuals are consistently more likely to have a short cervix before 24 weeks-with rates of CL ≤25 mm approximately two to four times higher than White individuals across studies-as well as higher rates of funneling, intra-amniotic debris, and cervical dilation, though the factors underlying these differences are not well characterized. Findings for Hispanic and Asian patients were less consistent. Prediction models that combine CL with race and social factors perform better than CL alone, but differences in the test performance of CL itself across groups have not been established. Evidence on the remaining questions are limited, and whether CL screening reduces disparities in sPTB remains uncertain. Further research is needed to answer the questions that remain and to identify the structural factors that may contribute to these disparities.

articles.title: Oral microbiota, serum metabolites, and gestational diabetes mellitus: a multistage Mendelian randomization study.
articles.authors: Pan C, Li X, Xiong X et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Oral microbial dysbiosis may connect oral health with systemic metabolic disease, including gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM). We assessed associations of oral microbial features with GDM, and explored potential mediation by serum metabolites.
METHODS: We integrated Chinese oral microbiota, serum metabolites, and GDM genome-wide association study (GWAS) datasets using multistage Mendelian randomization (MR), with external replication in European-ancestry and multi-ancestry datasets. Generalized Summary-data-based MR was the primary approach, supported by complementary MR approaches, bidirectional analyses, heterogeneity and pleiotropy assessments, and multiple-testing correction.
RESULTS: Ten of the 3,117 oral microbial features were significantly associated with GDM after false discovery rate (FDR) correction within the same genus. The strongest positive and inverse associations involved s_Treponema B USGB 1373 (OR: 1.83, 95% CI: 1.29-2.61, P adj  = 0.003) and s_Bacteroidaceae USGB 979 (OR: 0.76, 95% CI: 0.64-0.90, P adj  = 0.001). Screening 2,759 serum metabolites yielded three candidate chains with nominal indirect effects involving s_Streptobacillus USGB 672 with 4-(3-hydroxybutyl) phenol, and s_Saccharimonadaceae USGB 1287 with Azelaoyl PAF or 5-chloro-2-hydroxy-p-benzoquinone (estimated indirect-effect proportions 15.2%, 20.8%, and 31.8%, respectively). Neither the microbiota-metabolite nor metabolite-GDM associations survived FDR correction.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest potential associations between oral microbiota and GDM risk. Larger GWAS datasets on oral microbiota, serum metabolites, and GDM are needed to validate these associations and assess mediation.

articles.title: Impact of co-occurring maternal nicotine use, depression, and anxiety on perinatal outcomes.
articles.authors: Mize EJ, Garg B, Crosland BA et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Nicotine is the most commonly used substance in pregnancy, and the prevalence of mental health disorders in pregnancy is rising. In this study, we analyzed the association of nicotine use and depression and/or anxiety disorders, separately and together, on perinatal outcomes, an understudied area.
METHODS: Retrospective cohort study using California linked vital statistics and hospital discharge data (2008-2020). Patients were categorized into eight categories: (1) no nicotine use or depression or anxiety (reference), (2) nicotine use only, (3) depression only, (4) anxiety only, (5) depression and anxiety, (6) nicotine use and depression, (7) nicotine use and anxiety, and (8) nicotine use with depression and anxiety. The maternal outcomes measured were hypertensive disease of pregnancy, preterm delivery <37 and <32 weeks, severe maternal morbidity (SMM), and non-transfusion SMM; while the neonatal outcomes were neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission, small for gestational age (SGA), respiratory distress syndrome (RDS), infant deaths, and hypoglycemia. We included 4,897,855 singleton, non-anomalous gestations delivered between 23 and 42 weeks and excluded individuals using other substances or diagnosed with bipolar disorder. Results were analyzed by chi-square tests and multivariable Poisson regression models.
RESULTS: Of the pregnant individuals included in this study, nicotine use was present in 1.4%, depression alone in 1.1%, anxiety alone in 1.2%, and combined depression and anxiety in 1.2%. Among maternal outcomes, SMM demonstrated a statistically significant association with combined nicotine use, depression, and anxiety (adjusted risk ratio [aRR], 2.20 [1.29-3.75]). Hypertensive disease was higher in groups with anxiety: only anxiety (15.3%), depression and anxiety (15.4%), and nicotine and anxiety (15.4%) compared to the reference group (7.7%). Among neonatal outcomes, infant death (aRR, 3.96 [1.66-9.46]), RDS (aRR, 2.03 [1.20-3.43]), and hypoglycemia (aRR, 1.67 [1.82-3.92]) were each significantly associated with combined nicotine use, depression, and anxiety. No other statistically significant increase in groups with nicotine use, depression, and anxiety were…
CONCLUSION: Nicotine and depression/anxiety combined was associated with a higher risk of SMM, RDS, hypoglycemia, and infant death than each alone. These data can inform mechanistic research into the interaction between nicotine and mental health on perinatal outcomes.

articles.title: A Pilot Study of Virtual Yoga on Quality of Life in Women Undergoing In Vitro Fertilization: Differential Benefits for Those with a History of Dysmenorrhea.
articles.authors: Wilson JM, Dusanka R, Kurian A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Infertility affects millions of women, with in vitro fertilization (IVF) as a common treatment. Women undergoing IVF often experience distress and reduced quality of life (QoL), and many also have a history of dysmenorrhea (i.e., chronic menstrual pain), which may influence their treatment experience. This single-arm pilot study examined the impact of a virtual yoga program on distress and fertility-related QoL, and explored whether effects differed between women with and without dysmenorrhea.
METHODS: Participants undergoing IVF completed the Fertility Quality of Life tool, assessing Emotional, Mind-Body, Relational, Social, Environment, and Treatment Tolerability domains, along with measures of distress (stress, anxiety, depression), before and after a 6-week virtual yoga program. The Satyananda-based program featured beginner-level sessions led by a fertility-focused instructor, combining asanas, pranayama, and meditation.
RESULTS: The sample (N = 26) reported an average of 2.8 years of infertility (standard deviation = 2.3), with 35% reporting a history of dysmenorrhea; baseline QoL and distress did not differ between those with and without dysmenorrhea. QoL significantly improved across Emotional, Mind-Body, Relational, and Environment domains, with women with dysmenorrhea showing significantly larger gains in the Emotional and Relational domains. Distress did not significantly change.
CONCLUSION: This pilot study suggests that a virtual yoga program may offer psychosocial benefits during IVF, with exploratory analyses indicating that improvements may be more pronounced among women with a history of dysmenorrhea. Larger, adequately powered studies are needed to confirm these findings and identify the individuals most likely to benefit.

articles.title: Anti-HBc seropositivity among women of childbearing age in Indonesia: a nationally representative cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Pracoyo NE, Musadad DA, Besral et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to estimate the national prevalence of hepatitis B core antigen (anti-HBc) seropositivity, indicating prior hepatitis B virus (HBV) exposure, among Indonesian women aged 15-49 years. Additionally, the study sought to identify associated sociodemographic factors.
METHODS: We analyzed data from the 2018 Indonesian Basic Health Survey (Riskesdas), a nationally representative survey with a complex sampling design and appropriate sampling weights. Anti-HBc seropositivity was measured at the Sulianti Saroso Laboratory. Of the 19,418 participants, 12,617 women were included in the final analysis. Survey-weighted logistic regression was applied to estimate adjusted odds ratios (ORₐⱼ) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: Anti-HBc seropositivity was significantly more common among women aged >35 years (ORₐⱼ = 1.72; 95% CI: 1.58-1.87), those with lower educational attainment (ORₐⱼ = 1.16; 95% CI: 1.05-1.28), employed women (ORₐⱼ = 1.19; 95% CI: 1.09-1.29), rural residents (ORₐⱼ = 1.28; 95% CI: 1.18-1.40), and women reporting contraceptive use (ORₐⱼ = 1.22; 95% CI: 1.11-1.35).
CONCLUSION: Anti-HBc seropositivity remains a significant public health concern among Indonesian women of childbearing age, particularly those who are older, less educated, employed, living in rural areas, and reporting contraceptive use. Policy recommendations should prioritize maternal screening, timely and universal birth dose vaccination, administration of hepatitis B immunoglobulin (HBIG) when indicated, and improved vaccination coverage among unvaccinated adults.

articles.title: Surgical Resection of Extra-Abdominal Metastases of Low-Grade Serous Ovarian Cancer: A Case Series.
articles.authors: Gaillard T, Mariolo A, Hotton J et al.
articles.abstract: Surgical removal of extra-abdominal spread of low-grade serous ovarian cancer has not been largely described in the literature. We report three cases of the association of abdominal and thoracic surgery in patients with metastatic low-grade serous ovarian cancer. It seems to have no deleterious impact on global management. Real impact on survival remains unclear.

articles.title: MIF and CXCL8 shape inflammatory myeloid-epithelial crosstalk in cervical squamous cell carcinoma: a machine learning and integrative transcriptomic investigation.
articles.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
articles.authors: Wang W, Li X, Li J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Progression from high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL) to cervical squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) is accompanied by extensive epithelial remodeling and changes in the inflammatory immune microenvironment. However, how stage-specific epithelial states interact with inflammatory myeloid responses, spatial immune organization, and patient prognosis remains unclear. This study investigated these changes and identified inflammation-related molecular features associated with clinical outcome.
METHODS: Single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, bulk transcriptomic and survival cohorts, and drug-response data were integrated. Stage-associated cell states, epithelial trajectories, gene co-expression programs, and predicted cell-cell communication were analyzed across normal cervical tissue, HSIL, and squamous cell carcinoma. Machine-learning survival models were developed in TCGA-CESC and evaluated in GSE39001, GSE52903, and CGCI-HTMCP-CC. Pathway enrichment and immune deconvolution were used to assess biological and immune features associated with the prognostic model. Drug-response prediction, molecular docking, 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations, and immunohistochemistry provided additional computational and tissue-level evaluation.
RESULTS: HSIL was characterized by a proliferative epithelial state, whereas SCC was enriched for an epithelial state associated with keratinization stress, interferon responses, and inferred copy-number abnormalities, accompanied by increased inflammatory myeloid populations. Spatial transcriptomic analysis showed stronger immune and myeloid programs at the invasive front than in the tumor core. Predicted epithelial-myeloid communication in SCC prominently involved MIF-CD74 receptor complexes and CXCL8-CXCR2 signaling. A five-gene prognostic model consisting of MIF, SPP1, CXCL8, CALML5, and CD74 achieved C-indices of 0.748, 0.696, and 0.691 in TCGA-CESC, GSE39001, and GSE52903,…
CONCLUSION: Progression from HSIL to SCC was associated with coordinated epithelial remodeling, inflammatory myeloid activation, and spatial reorganization of the immune microenvironment. MIF-CD74 and CXCL8-CXCR2 signaling were implicated in epithelial-myeloid communication, while the five-gene inflammatory model showed reproducible prognostic performance across independent cohorts. These results support further investigation of MIF- and CXCL8-related inflammatory signaling in cervical cancer progression and prognosis.

articles.title: A novel postpartum hemorrhage prediction model for women with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy in secondary hospitals of middle-income settings.
articles.authors: Yang M, Wang M, Li N
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to develop and validate a risk-stratification tool to aid clinical referral decision-making for postpartum hemorrhage among women with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy. The tool targets secondary hospitals with basic laboratory capacity in middle-income settings.
METHODS: This was a retrospective study. 2,761 women diagnosed with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy formed the development set (training and internal validation sets), and 592 women from the same hospital constituted a temporal validation set to evaluate model performance. LASSO regression was applied for optimal feature selection, and the prediction model was constructed using multivariable logistic regression. Model performance was evaluated via the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, calibration curves, decision curve analysis, and clinical impact curves.
RESULTS: Key predictors, including placental abruption, placenta previa, placenta accreta, macrosomia, hemoglobin level, international normalized ratio, D-dimer concentration, and parity, were incorporated into a nomogram. The model achieved areas under the curve of 0.733 (training set), 0.756 (internal validation set), and 0.877 (temporal validation set). The apparent and bias-corrected calibration curves deviated from the ideal line at low predicted probabilities and gradually approached it as predicted PPH risk increased. Decision curve analysis indicated that the model yielded a higher net benefit compared with treat-all and treat-none strategies, whereas the clinical impact curve characterized the counts of predicted high-risk women and observed PPH events across risk thresholds.
CONCLUSION: The model demonstrated moderate discrimination and may be suitable for stratifying postpartum hemorrhage risk among women with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy.

articles.title: Androgen-Secreting Thecoma Fibroma Mimicking PCOS-A Diagnostic Challenge.
articles.authors: Aljenaee K, Alsubaiei M, Hajji S
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ovarian fibrothecomas are uncommon benign sex cord-stromal tumors, accounting for ~3.3% of ovarian tumors. They are usually hormonally inactive or estrogen-producing; androgen secretion is uncommon. Because hyperandrogenism is frequently attributed to polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), an androgen-secreting ovarian tumor may be overlooked when symptoms are progressive but virilization is absent.
CASE REPORT: A 42-year-old woman developed new-onset hirsutism, acne, menstrual irregularity, and later scalp hair loss. She was initially diagnosed with PCOS after being reported with biochemical hyperandrogenism and polycystic ovarian morphology on ultrasound (US); the original testosterone value was unavailable. Following transient symptomatic improvement with a combined oral contraceptive pill (COCP), her symptoms recurred and progressed. Repeat evaluation showed a total testosterone level of 5.83 nmol/L and dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate (DHEAS) of 14 µmol/L. CT demonstrated a 5.1 × 4.2 × 4.0 cm mass adjacent to the right ovary with normal adrenal glands. Right oophorectomy was performed, and histopathology confirmed a fibrothecoma with focal luteinization. Three months after surgery, acne and hirsutism improved, and total testosterone decreased to 0.50 nmol/L.
CONCLUSIONS: Progressive or newly developed hyperandrogenism should not be attributed to PCOS solely on the basis of polycystic ovarian morphology. The tempo of symptoms, biochemical findings, and clinical context should guide evaluation for alternative ovarian or adrenal causes. This case illustrates an uncommon PCOS mimic and the importance of reassessing the diagnosis when the clinical course is atypical.

articles.title: Rewiring immune cell death in ovarian cancer: pyroptosis, apoptosis, and the immunosuppressive microenvironment.
articles.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
articles.authors: Zhu H, Kang L, Shen L
articles.abstract: Ovarian cancer remains the most lethal gynecological malignancy, in large part because of its highly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) and limited responsiveness to current immunotherapies. Emerging evidence indicates that programmed cell death of immune cells is an important determinant of immune dysfunction, tumor immune escape, and therapeutic resistance.
