Among these processes, apoptosis and pyroptosis exert distinct but interconnected effects on antitumor immunity. Excessive apoptosis contributes to the depletion of cytotoxic T cells and natural killer (NK) cells, whereas apoptosis-resistant tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) and other immunosuppressive populations can persist and sustain immune suppression. In contrast, pyroptosis is highly context dependent: controlled activation may enhance antitumor immunity through gasdermin-mediated membrane permeabilization, inflammatory cytokine release, dendritic cell (DC) activation, and improved antigen presentation, whereas excessive or persistent pyroptotic signaling may promote chronic inflammation and recruitment of immunosuppressive myeloid cells. Importantly, apoptosis and pyroptosis are interconnected through shared regulatory nodes, including caspase-8, gasdermin proteins, mitochondrial stress, and inflammatory signaling pathways. This review summarizes the characteristics, key signaling pathways, and functional consequences of pyroptosis and apoptosis in major immune-cell populations within the ovarian cancer microenvironment, with particular emphasis on their context-dependent roles in tumor immune evasion and on opportunities to overcome immunosuppression and improve immunotherapy.

articles.title: Perioperative factors associated with delayed passage of flatus after laparoscopic uterine myomectomy: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Liu Q, Gu J, Luo R et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Delayed passage of flatus (DPF) after laparoscopic uterine myomectomy may indicate slower gastrointestinal recovery, but procedure-specific evidence is limited.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of 342 consecutive adult patients who underwent laparoscopic uterine myomectomy between March 2021 and March 2025. The endpoint was no documented passage of flatus within the first 3 postoperative days. Because oral-intake intolerance, nausea or vomiting, abdominal distension, and nasogastric-tube use were not systematically captured, the endpoint was treated as DPF rather than consensus-defined postoperative ileus. A three-variable logistic regression model was restricted to preoperative and intraoperative variables and interpreted as an exploratory association model.
RESULTS: DPF occurred in 35 patients (10.2%). Plain radiographs in all 35 patients meeting this threshold showed multiple air-fluid levels and diffuse small- and large-bowel gas. No focal mechanical obstruction was documented after record review that included bedside abdominal findings and radiography. In the primary complete-case model (341 patients; 35 events), pre-existing constipation (odds ratio [OR] 12.84, 95% confidence interval [CI] 3.65-45.21), intraoperative intestinal adhesion (OR 39.91, 95% CI 13.89-114.71), and operative time (OR 1.014 per minute, 95% CI 1.006-1.023) remained associated with DPF after adjustment. The wide CIs, particularly for intestinal adhesion, indicated substantial uncertainty in the magnitude of association. The model had an apparent area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve of 0.939 (bootstrap 95% CI 0.894-0.978) and a Brier score of 0.040. At the data-derived Youden-index threshold, apparent sensitivity was 0.857 and apparent specificity was 0.908. A single 5-fold cross-validation yielded an area under the curve of 0.923.
DISCUSSION: These center-specific findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective external validation using a multidimensional gastrointestinal-recovery endpoint.

articles.title: Comparative analysis of vascular endothelial growth factor levels in placental, fetal-membrane, and umbilical-cord tissues: associations with maternal obstetric complications.
articles.authors: Altal O, Hulliel AF, Al Sharie AH et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) is a central regulator of placental angiogenesis, but the extent to which tissue-level VEGF expression differs across obstetric complications and among gestational compartments remains unclear. This study evaluated VEGF protein concentrations in placental villous tissue, fetal membranes, and umbilical cord across diverse pregnancy phenotypes.
METHODS: A prospective observational cohort study with subsequent group classification was conducted at King Abdullah University Hospital, Irbid, Jordan. Eighty-six pregnancies were classified into five groups: uncomplicated controls, small-for-gestational-age (SGA), pre-eclampsia/eclampsia, gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), and thrombophilia. VEGF concentrations were quantified by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) in placental, membrane, and umbilical cord tissues obtained at delivery. Between-group differences were assessed using non-parametric analyses, while multinomial logistic regression, Spearman correlation, principal component analysis, clustering, and cross-validated receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis were performed.
RESULTS: VEGF concentrations showed substantial overlap among clinical groups. No significant differences were observed in placental VEGF (P = 0.802), membrane VEGF (P = 0.139), or umbilical cord VEGF (P = 0.525), with negligible effect sizes (ε 2 ≤ 0.04). Multivariable modelling demonstrated no significant association between any VEGF compartment and pathological pregnancy groups. Correlations between compartments were weak, with modest associations between membrane and umbilical cord VEGF (ρ = 0.29, P = 0.006) and placental and membrane VEGF (ρ = 0.22, P = 0.046). Multivariate analyses failed to identify distinct VEGF expression patterns, and a three-marker classifier showed poor discrimination after cross-validation…
CONCLUSION: In this cohort, total tissue VEGF measured at delivery did not clearly distinguish pregnancies complicated by SGA, pre-eclampsia/eclampsia, GDM, or thrombophilia from uncomplicated pregnancies. The limited sample size, however, means that smaller effects cannot be excluded. The weak inter-compartment correlations may be more consistent with locally regulated angiogenic processes than with a unified tissue signature, although sampling and methodological factors may also contribute. These findings highlight the limitations of total VEGF tissue measurement as a biomarker of placental disease.

articles.title: Reveals apoptosis enrichment and proliferative-program suppression in intrauterine adhesion, with exploratory stromal mapping.
articles.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
articles.authors: Liu Y, Yang X
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intrauterine adhesion (IUA/Asherman syndrome) is a leading cause of acquired infertility in women, characterized by dysregulated apoptosis and fibrosis of endometrial stromal cells (ESCs). Bioelectrical stimulation (ES) holds potential for tissue repair, but its cytological mechanism for regulating ESC apoptosis remains unclear.
METHODS: Transcriptomic data from GEO dataset GSE224093 were used for differential gene expression (DEG) analysis, GO/KEGG enrichment, WGCNA co-expression networks, PPI network construction, and GSEA. Public single-cell data were used for ESC subpopulation annotation and apoptosis scoring. An H2O2-induced ESC injury model was established; low-frequency ES (1 Hz, 2 mA, 12 h/day) was applied, and cell viability, apoptosis rate, mitochondrial membrane potential and Bcl-2/Bax/Cleaved-Caspase-3 proteins were measured. RT-PCR verified mRNA expression.
RESULTS: GSE224093 analysis identified 892 DEGs. Hallmark GSEA revealed strong inflammatory enrichment in IUA (Interferon Gamma Response: NES = +1.89, FDR = 0.001; Myogenesis: NES = +1.90, FDR = 0.001) and broad suppression of proliferative programs (Myc Targets V1: NES = -3.80; E2F.
TARGETS: NES = -3.73; G2-M Checkpoint: NES = -3.46; all FDR = 0.001). Single-cell data revealed stromal-state differences between AS-Pre and WOI control libraries that are interpretable as exploratory given preparation imbalance. In vitro experiments confirmed ES reduced the ESC apoptosis rate from 38.2% to 14.7% (P < 0.001), upregulated Bcl-2 (2.8-fold), and downregulated Bax (0.48-fold) and Cleaved Caspase-3 (0.37-fold). RT-PCR results were highly consistent with protein-level findings (Spearman r = 0.92, P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Bioelectrical stimulation significantly inhibits pathological apoptosis of ESCs in IUA by activating the Bcl-2/Bax/Caspase-3 anti-apoptotic axis and stabilizing MMP, thereby promoting endometrial repair. The integrated transcriptomic and in vitro evidence presented here provides a cytological basis for ES as an adjuvant treatment for IUA, pending prospective clinical validation.

articles.title: Releasing Immunosuppression in the Tumor: A Phase 1/2 Study of Arginase Inhibitor INCB001158 in Combination with Chemotherapy in Advanced Malignancies.
articles.journal: Journal of immunotherapy and precision oncology
articles.authors: Naing A, Javle M, Cho M et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Arginase is overexpressed in many advanced cancers, which can deplete arginine in tumors to promote immunosuppression. Arginase inhibition may enhance the efficacy of standard chemotherapy regimens by increasing arginine levels and modulating arginine-mediated immune function. INCB001158 is a potent and selective arginase inhibitor that was assessed in combination with chemotherapy.
METHODS: This was an open-label, nonrandomized, phase 1/2 dose-escalation/expansion study in adults with advanced or metastatic solid tumors. INCB001158 was administered orally twice daily (bid) in combination with chemotherapy (mFOLFOX6, gemcitabine/cisplatin, or paclitaxel). Phase 2 tumor-type cohorts were colorectal cancer, biliary tract cancer (BTC), ovarian cancer (OC), gastroesophageal cancer, and endometrial cancer. Primary end points included safety, tolerability, and overall response rate (ORR).
RESULTS: Fifty-four patients were enrolled in phase 1 and 95 in phase 2. No dose-dependent adverse event trends were observed. Recommended phase 2 dose of INCB001158 was 100 mg bid. Two phase 2 expansion cohorts met criteria for Simon 2-stage expansion: patients with BTC treated with INCB001158 100 mg bid plus gemcitabine/cisplatin, and patients with platinum-resistant OC treated with INCB001158 100 mg bid plus paclitaxel. The overall response rate was 24.2% (8/33 patients, all partial responses) in the BTC cohort and 16.7% (1/24 complete response and 3/24 partial responses) in the OC cohort. Pharmacodynamic increase in arginine levels was observed systemically in blood plasma and locally detected by mass-spectrometry images of tumor tissue.
CONCLUSIONS: INCB001158 was generally well tolerated and associated with increases in arginine levels and responses in the BTC cohort, suggesting that combination regimens with chemotherapy may provide clinical benefit for some patients. ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT03314935; EudraCT 2017-002904-29.

articles.title: Nutrition-related lipid metabolism and ferroptosis in endometrial cancer: transcriptomic profiling and hypoxia-associated gene expression.
articles.authors: Lou X, Cai W, Wang J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endometrial cancer is closely linked to obesity, insulin resistance and nutrition-related metabolic dysfunction. We examined lipid-synthesis and ferroptosis-related programs across tumor cell states and assessed lipogenic and ferroptosis-regulatory gene expression under hypoxia.
METHODS: Six single-cell RNA-sequencing libraries from three primary endometrial tumors and one Visium section were analyzed alongside 545 TCGA-UCEC tumors. Lipid-metabolism, ferroptosis, hypoxia and immune scores were evaluated at cellular, spatial and bulk-tissue levels. HEC-1-A and KLE cells were cultured under normoxia or hypoxia for 24 h, with three independent cultures per condition, and gene expression was assessed by qRT-PCR.
RESULTS: After quality control and doublet removal, 4,167 cells were retained and assigned to 14 annotated populations. Epithelial cells had the highest median lipid-synthesis score. Among 1,273 epithelial-lineage cells, hypoxia was weakly correlated with the ferroptosis-driver score (r = 0.091, FDR = 0.0096), but not with defense. Across 1,347 spatial spots, epithelial and lipid-synthesis scores were positively correlated (r = 0.191, FDR = 1.5 × 10-11). TCGA resistance scores were lower in serous than endometrioid tumors and higher in MSI-H than MSS tumors. Resistance was not independently associated with overall survival (HR = 0.83, 95% CI 0.47-1.47) and was unrelated to BMI. Under hypoxia, SREBF1, FASN and SCD expression was higher in both cell lines, together with CA9, GPX4, SLC7A11, AIFM2 and ACSL4.
CONCLUSION: Lipid-synthesis and ferroptosis-related programs varied across endometrial-cancer cell states and tissue regions. Hypoxic cell models showed concurrent changes in lipogenic and ferroptosis-regulatory transcripts. These findings identify metabolic transcriptional responses for functional investigation, without establishing a dietary effect or independent prognostic value for the resistance score.

articles.title: Revisiting common female infertility factors traditionally associated with impaired oocyte quality: insights from IVF outcomes and AI-derived oocyte score performance.
articles.authors: Del Collado M, Braga DPAF, Setti AS et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While advanced maternal age is consistently associated with impaired oocyte competence and poorer reproductive outcomes, the effects of other female infertility factors, including polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), endometriosis, and body mass index (BMI), remain debated. Moreover, whether AI-derived oocyte quality metrics retain their predictive value across different female infertility conditions remains unclear.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study evaluated whether common female infertility factors are associated with oocyte and embryo competence and cumulative reproductive outcomes in intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) cycles, and assessed the performance of an AI-derived composite oocyte score across these populations. The study included 14,420 injected oocytes from 1,856 autologous ICSI cycles performed between 2020 and 2025. Outcomes were compared between controls and women with polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), endometriosis, overweight, or obesity; controls were additionally stratified by maternal age (<38 versus ≥38 years). Age-based propensity-score weighting was applied for pairwise female-factor comparisons, followed by adjusted mixed-effects regression models accounting for patient- and retrieval-cycle-level clustering.
RESULTS: Endometriosis and obesity were not associated with consistent reductions in laboratory or clinical outcomes, whereas overweight was associated with lower top-quality blastocyst and cumulative reproductive outcomes. Advanced maternal age showed the most consistent detrimental pattern, including lower MAGENTA and KIDScore values, reduced blastocyst development and euploidy rates, and lower cumulative pregnancy rates. PMOS cycles showed largely preserved laboratory outcomes, higher MII yield, and higher observed cumulative pregnancy rates. The composite MAGENTA score was associated with higher odds of fertilization (OR 1.53), blastocyst formation (OR 1.67), and top-quality blastocyst formation (OR 1.26), and with higher KIDScore (β = 0.21). These associations were generally observed across the evaluated female-factor groups, and…
DISCUSSION: Overall, female infertility factors appear to affect reproductive competence through distinct patterns rather than a uniform impairment in oocyte quality, with maternal age showing the most consistent adverse association and AI-derived oocyte assessment providing complementary predictive information across heterogeneous populations.

articles.title: Racial disparities in ovarian cancer incidence and mortality in Brazil: a population based analysis.
articles.authors: Lima Siqueira Dos Santos A, Mendes SV, Fidelis Junior JT et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to assess racial disparities in the incidence and mortality of ovarian cancer in Brazil.
METHODS: Data were obtained from three national sources: the Population-Based Cancer Registries (2010-2017), the Hospital-Based Cancer Registries, and the Mortality Information System (2000-2023). Crude and age-adjusted rates per 100,000 women were calculated by race (White vs. Black/Brown). Temporal trends were analyzed using Joinpoint regression, estimating the Annual Percent Change (APC).
RESULTS: From 2010-2017, a total of 19,186 incident ovarian cancer cases were recorded, of which 61.9% occurred in White and 30.1% in Black/Brown women. Incidence rates declined among White women (APC -2.36%, p = 0.007) but remained stable among Black/Brown women (APC + 1.77%, p = 0.47). From 2000-2023, mortality increased among Black/Brown women (+1.85%/year, p < 0.001) and remained stable among White women (+0.11%/year, p = 0.39). Hospital-based data (n = 40,762) showed that Black/Brown women were younger (64.4% <60 years), less educated (55.6% <8 years), and more often lived in the Northeast region (53.2%). Compared with White women, they were less frequently staged at diagnosis (49.4% vs. 43.0%, p < 0.001), had longer delays to treatment initiation (≥60 days: 8.3% vs. 6.5%, p < 0.001), and higher early mortality rates (21.4% vs. 19.0%, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: While ovarian cancer incidence is declining among White Brazilian women, Black/Brown women experience stable incidence and rising mortality. Socioeconomic vulnerability, regional disparities, and delays in treatment-rather than biological differences-appear to drive this gap. Implementing targeted policies to ensure equitable access to timely diagnosis and optimal care is essential to reduce these avoidable inequalities.

articles.title: Association between preoperative MRI-measured membranous urethral length and early urinary continence recovery after robot-assisted radical prostatectomy: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Mao P, Ye F, Zhu X et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP) is a key surgical approach for localized prostate cancer, yet early postoperative urinary incontinence remains a major functional concern. Membranous urethral length (MUL), measurable by preoperative MRI, may predict continence recovery, but its relationship with early outcomes warrants further clarification.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between preoperative MRI-measured MUL and early complete urinary continence recovery after RARP, and to evaluate its dose-response relationship and discriminative ability.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 152 patients who underwent RARP (October 2024-March 2026). MUL was measured on preoperative T2-weighted MRI by two independent observers. Urinary continence (0 pads/day) was assessed at 1 and 3 months after catheter removal. Multivariable Logistic regression (1 month) and Firth penalized Logistic regression (3 months) were used. Restricted cubic spline, ROC curves, and propensity score matching were performed.
RESULTS: Median MUL was 13.49 mm. Interobserver agreement was excellent (ICC = 0.946). Complete continence recovery rates at 1 and 3 months were 51.32% and 79.61%, respectively. Each 1-mm MUL increase was independently associated with higher odds of continence recovery at 1 month (OR = 1.758, 95% CI: 1.450-2.132, P<0.001) and 3 months (OR = 1.502, 95% CI: 1.247-1.809, P<0.001). Older age and higher BMI were associated with lower odds of 3-month recovery (both P<0.05). RCS analysis showed a linear dose-response relationship (P overall<0.001; P nonlinearity=0.540). MUL demonstrated moderate discriminative ability for 1-month (AUC = 0.822) and 3-month (AUC = 0.773) continence recovery.
CONCLUSION: Longer preoperative MUL was independently associated with higher likelihood of complete urinary continence recovery at 1 and 3 months after catheter removal, with an approximately linear dose-response relationship. MUL has good measurement reproducibility and moderate predictive value, supporting its potential as an imaging biomarker for preoperative continence risk stratification in RARP patients.

articles.title: Association between hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and infantile vascular anomalies in the Collaborative Perinatal Project.
articles.authors: Wong JJ, Chakraborti Y, Caniglia EC et al.
articles.abstract: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) affect 10%-22% of pregnancies globally and are characterized by vascular dysfunction. Yet, their influence on fetal vascular development remains incompletely understood. Port-wine stains (PWS) and infantile hemangiomas (IH) provide a compelling model for investigating this gap. As the most common vascular anomalies of infancy, affecting 0.3%-0.5% and an estimated 1.5%-4.4% of infants, respectively, their clinical manifestations appear at or within weeks of birth, minimizing the latency between intrauterine exposure and outcome. PWS are congenital vascular malformations appearing at birth as red-to-purple birthmarks most commonly on the face and neck, while IH are raised, bright-red postnatal vascular tumors emerging in the first weeks of life on the face, scalp, and trunk. Both cause significant cosmetic and functional morbidity when located on the face or airways, and PWS may additionally signal underlying neurological involvement. Using data from the Collaborative Perinatal Project (1959-1966), a prospective cohort of 59 391 pregnancies across 12 US centers, we examined whether HDP are associated with PWS and IH. HDP were classified into five categories (normotensive [reference], chronic hypertension, gestational hypertension, preeclampsia/eclampsia, and superimposed preeclampsia/eclampsia). PWS and IH were ascertained through standardized physician examinations through the first year of life. We estimated adjusted relative risks (aRR) using log-binomial generalized estimating equations with inverse probability weighting for selection bias and propensity score weighting for confounding. Among 59 391 pregnancies, 312 (0.5%) developed PWS and 797 (1.3%) developed IH. Superimposed preeclampsia/eclampsia was associated with PWS (aRR, 2.75; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.12-6.75). No HDP type was associated with IH.

articles.title: Measuring maternal mortality and mortality disparities: a health-adjusted approach.
articles.authors: Yuan AY, Atanasov V, Weston BW et al.
articles.abstract: Racial and ethnic disparities in maternal mortality are well known, especially the higher rates for Black and Native American women. However, the underlying causes remain unclear. These disparities may stem from disparities in background health across groups or from factors specific to childbirth and maternal care. We examine maternal mortality disparities using a novel method that controls for population differences in overall health. Unadjusted maternal mortality rate (MMR) ratios for Black, Asian, Hispanic, and Native American women relative to White women, measured over 2010-2022, excluding COVID-19 deaths, are 2.7, 0.91, 0.88, and 2.58. In contrast, adjusted ratios are 1.83, 1.31, 1.27, and 1.24, respectively. Poor background health contributes to the high maternal mortality risk among Black and Native American women, while better underlying health among Asian and Hispanic women masks their elevated adjusted maternal mortality risk. We also document substantial cross-state heterogeneity in adjusted MMRs and racial/ethnic disparities in these rates. In some states, minority women face substantially higher maternal mortality risks relative to White women, while in others-notably California-health-adjusted disparities are small.

articles.title: Prevalence and impact of urinary incontinence in Canada: a systematic review of the quantitative and qualitative literature and a meta-analysis of quantitative data.
articles.authors: Kolahdooz F, Jang SL, Lawrence S et al.
articles.abstract: Urinary incontinence (UI) is defined as involuntary urine leakage. It is a rarely reported common condition that adversely affects quality of life because many consider it a normal part of aging. UI continues to be stigmatizing. This study's aim was to conduct a systematic review of existing literature on the prevalence and impact of UI in Canadians (≥16 years) and perform a meta-analysis on the prevalence of UI in Canada. A systematic electronic literature search of PubMed/Medline, EMBASE, CINAHAL, Cochrane, ISI Web of Knowledge, and Scopus databases from January 1980 to April 2024 was completed. Papers published on the prevalence and impact of UI were selected. We conducted meta-analysis using random-effects models and pooled prevalence of UI based on study setting, sex, and age. Quantitative studies were examined for internal validity, generalizability, reliability, and objectivity, and qualitative studies for credibility, transferability, confirmability, and dependability. Out of 1089 titles, 34 were included: 16 prevalence, 10 impact, and 8 addressing both the prevalence and impact. UI was more prevalent in women than men (meta-analysis: 34% [95% CI, 25%-44%] vs 19% [95% CI, 7%-31%]; P < .001). Women were reluctant to seek medical help and suffered symptoms longer than men. Overall, the prevalence increased with age, reaching as high as 52% among women 85+ years. UI affected individuals socially, emotionally, physically, and financially. Included papers did not consider differences in prevalence or impact across ethnic, cultural, or socioeconomic groups. Increased awareness of management and treatment will improve quality of life.

articles.title: Reevaluating the link between maternal age and stillbirth risk in the context of socioeconomic confounding.
articles.authors: Sarnak D, Stolte A, Bustos B et al.
articles.abstract: Previous research finds a J-shaped relationship between maternal age and stillbirth risk but often overlooks socioeconomic confounding, which may obscure underlying risk patterns, particularly among individuals with advanced maternal age (≥35 years) who tend to have greater socioeconomic advantage. Moreover, it is unclear whether the maternal age-stillbirth association differs by race/ethnicity, despite racial/ethnic differences in socioeconomic status. Using a fetuses-at-risk approach and restricted US vital statistics data from 2015 to 2019 (18,182,261 live births and 85,658 stillbirths), we examined the relationship between maternal age and stillbirth risk, assessed how adjustment for socioeconomic confounding influences this relationship, and evaluated whether race/ethnicity modifies the association. In the full sample, minimally adjusted models showed a J-shaped association between maternal age and stillbirth risk. However, after adjusting for socioeconomic confounding, the relationship shifted to a positive linear association. Before adjustment for socioeconomic confounding, the maternal age-stillbirth gradient appeared steeper among non-Hispanic Black, Hispanic, and non-Hispanic American Indian/Alaska Native individuals compared to non-Hispanic White and non-Hispanic Asian/Pacific Islander individuals. These patterns attenuated after full adjustment, except among non-Hispanic American Indian/Alaska Native individuals. Findings suggest that not adequately accounting for confounding by socioeconomic status may result in a misrepresentation of the relationship between maternal age and stillbirth risk.

articles.title: Association of uterine-entry technique with chorioamniotic membrane separation after fetoscopic laser surgery for twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome: two-center retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
articles.authors: Burnett BA, Parobek CM, Imamoglu M et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Chorioamniotic membrane separation (CAS) is a recognized iatrogenic complication of fetoscopic laser photocoagulation (FLP), the standard treatment for twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome (TTTS). We compared the incidence of CAS between two different means of uterine entry for FLP: the sharp-trocar and Seldinger techniques.
METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study of monochorionic diamniotic twin pregnancies complicated by TTTS undergoing FLP between 16 + 0 and 26 + 0 weeks' gestation at two tertiary fetal centers in the USA from January 2012 to August 2025. The uterine-entry technique was center-specific: one center used the Seldinger technique exclusively, while the other used sharp-trocar entry exclusively. All patients at both centers underwent routine short-interval postoperative fetal ultrasound examination, with particular attention paid to membrane integrity at the entry sites. The primary outcome was CAS diagnosed intraoperatively or during postoperative ultrasound performed within 48 h after surgery. Secondary outcomes included gestational age at delivery, latency from FLP to delivery, preterm birth < 32 and < 34 weeks, and survival 48 h after FLP, at birth and at 30 days postnatally. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analysis evaluated associations between clinically relevant anatomical and procedural variables and the occurrence of CAS.
RESULTS: In total, 889 pregnancies that underwent a FLP procedure for TTTS were included (591 using Seldinger entry, 298 using sharp-trocar entry). Sharp-trocar entry was associated with a lower rate of CAS (8.1% vs 14.4%; P = 0.01) and lower rates of delivery before 32 weeks (42% vs 59%; P < 0.001) and delivery before 34 weeks (61% vs 77%; P < 0.001). Among cases with complete data, after adjusting for clinically relevant anatomical and procedural variables, sharp-trocar entry was independently associated with lower odds…
CONCLUSIONS: Sharp-trocar entry during FLP for TTTS was associated with a lower incidence of CAS, longer latency from procedure to delivery and later gestational age at delivery compared with the Seldinger technique. Because the entry technique was center-specific, these differences cannot be attributed exclusively to the technique. Survival was similar between the two groups. Prospective studies in which both entry techniques are used in the same center are needed to confirm these findings. © 2026 International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology.

articles.title: Impact of the pink October campaign on breast cancer screening in the Alpes-Maritimes region (France): A regional perspective.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Barranger E, Najib B
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Our objective was to describe monthly variations in breast cancer screening activity during the Pink October campaign and assess whether the observed increase extended beyond the campaign period in the Alpes-Maritimes region of France.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational study of aggregated monthly mammogram counts from January 2022 to December 2024. Data on organized screening (DO) were available for all 3 years, whereas data for individual screening (DP) were available only for 2024. Monthly screening activity during October and November was compared with activity during the remaining months using the statistical methods described below.
RESULTS: Organized screening activity peaked in October in each study year, with reported increases of 31% in 2022, 27% in 2023, and 48% in 2024 relative to the respective annual monthly means. The October-November comparison yielded P-values of 0.001 in 2022, 0.049 in 2023, and 0.054 in 2024. The 2024 result did not reach the conventional threshold for statistical significance. Individual screening showed a smaller October increase in 2024 (+10% relative to its annual monthly mean), and the October-November comparison was not statistically significant (P = 0.178). These findings describe temporal variations in screening activity and do not establish a causal effect of the campaign.
CONCLUSION: Mammography activity, particularly organized screening, increased during the Pink October period in the Alpes-Maritimes region. However, the aggregated data cannot establish whether this increase represented additional screening or a redistribution of examinations across the calendar year. Further multicenter studies using longer time series and individual-level data are needed to assess the campaign's effect on screening participation.

articles.title: Early Continuous Glucose Monitoring to Lower the Risk of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus in Women With Pre-Pregnancy Obesity: Protocol for the Multicentre Randomised Controlled Trial (GLOW).
articles.authors: Lu Y, Tian Z, Niu J et al.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Pre-pregnancy obesity substantially increases the risk of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), yet preventive strategies before routine GDM screening remain limited. The Glucose monitoring to Lower risk of GDM in Obese pregnant Women (GLOW) trial aims to determine whether continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) initiated in early pregnancy reduces the incidence of GDM in women with pre-pregnancy obesity.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: GLOW is a national, multicentre, open-label, parallel-group randomised controlled trial enrolling 1034 women with pre-pregnancy body mass index ≥ 28 kg/m2, a singleton pregnancy and gestational age ≤ 14+6 weeks at eight hospitals in China. Participants will be randomised 1:1 to routine antenatal care alone or routine antenatal care plus CGM. In the CGM group, five consecutive 14-day sensors will be used from 14+0-14+6 to 24+0-24+6 weeks of gestation (70 days in total), with access to glucose values and standardised CGM education. The primary endpoint is the incidence of GDM diagnosed by a 75-g oral glucose tolerance test at 24+0-24+6 weeks. Secondary outcomes include gestational weight gain, maternal metabolic and anthropometric measures, lifestyle behaviours and maternal and neonatal outcomes.
RESULTS AND CONCLUSIONS: GLOW will determine whether early CGM introduced before routine GDM screening can reduce GDM incidence and favourably influence maternal metabolic and pregnancy outcomes in women with pre-pregnancy obesity. The findings may inform the role of early CGM as a preventive strategy in this high-risk population.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry: ChiCTR2600130043.

articles.title: A body shape index and body roundness index in women with and without the polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Gynecological endocrinology : the official journal of the International Society of Gynecological Endocrinology
articles.authors: Pérez-López FR, Fernández-Alonso AM, Hernández-Bustamante EA et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the association of a body shape index (ABSI) and body roundness index (BRI) in women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), also known as polyendocrine metabolic ovary syndrome (PMOS).
METHODS: This study was registered at PROSPERO [CRD420251177545] and followed the PRISMA Guidelines. We searched evidence in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and SciELO databases. Two case-control and seven cross-sectional studies reported ABSI and BRI results in PMOS patients and women without the syndrome.
RESULTS: Systematic review and meta-analysis of ABSI (eight studies, 3193 participants) association with PMOS (SMD = 0.45, 95%CI = 0.07, 0.83; I 2 = 90.5%, τ2 = 0.18) and body mass index (BMI) (MD = 3.76, 95%CI = 1.61, 5.91 kg/m2; I 2 = 93.8%, τ2 = 5.84). In five studies (840 participants), BRI levels were higher in PMOS patients than in the control group (SMD = 1.09, 95%CI = 0.53-1.66) 95%CI = 0.53-1.66; I 2 = 85.9%; τ2 = 0.17), and BMI MD = 4.31 kg/m2, 95%CI = 1.98, 6.65; I 2 = 83.9%, τ2 = 2.87). Subgroup analyzes by geographic region showed no significant differences in ABSI and BRI estimates between European and Asian. The BRI finding remained statistically significant in all leave-one-out analyzes, whereas the statistical significance of the ABSI finding was sensitive to individual study exclusion.
CONCLUSION: PMOS patients have enhanced ABSI and BRI levels compared to women without the syndrome. Further high-quality studies from other world regions are needed to evaluate heterogeneity at different PMOS clinical stages.

articles.title: Patient barriers to colposcopy attendance following an abnormal Cervical Screening Test: A qualitative study of patient and healthcare professional perspectives.
articles.authors: Temminghoff L, Bastable A, Steele A et al.
articles.abstract: Approximately 53 percent of people referred for colposcopy after an abnormal Cervical Screening Test in Australia face barriers to accessing appointments within the recommended 90 days, increasing the risk of delayed diagnosis and poorer health outcomes. This study aimed to explore barriers to colposcopy attendance from the perspectives of Australian patients and health‑care professionals. A qualitative thematic analysis design was used. Semi‑structured interviews were conducted with four patients referred for colposcopy and 11 health‑care professionals who refer to or perform the procedure. Interviews were transcribed and thematically analyzed. Three main themes describing barriers to colposcopy attendance were identified. 1. Stress and anxiety were common, driven by limited understanding of the procedure and misconceptions about cancer risk. 2. Information barriers affected both groups, including difficulty interpreting screening results and a lack of resources to support patient education. 3. Structural and health system barriers, including logistical barriers, inflexible appointments and poor clinic communication, further hindered attendance. In addition to screening and vaccination, patients need to be supported through the clinical pathway to equitably eliminate cervical cancer. Focusing on patient education and communication poses a cost-effective solution for improving colposcopy attendance and patient experience.

articles.title: Exercise self-efficacy, physical activity, and menopausal symptoms in Malaysian midlife women: A cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Nga CZJ, Che Muhamed AM, Farah NM
articles.abstract: Physical activity (PA) is associated with fewer menopausal symptoms, yet many midlife women remain insufficiently active. Exercise self-efficacy is a key correlate of exercise behavior, but evidence among linking all these factors in Malaysian women is limited. We examined the associations between menopausal symptoms, PA and exercise self-efficacy in 159 women aged 40-60 years (93 perimenopausal, 66 postmenopausal). Participants completed a symptom questionnaire, the International Physical Activity Questionnaire-Short Form and the Exercise Self-Efficacy Scale (ESES). The most reported symptoms were dry skin (44.7 percent), brain fog (42.1 percent) and hair thinning or loss (39.0 percent). Mean moderate-to-vigorous PA was 139 minutes/week; 39.6 percent of women had low PA and 32.7 percent met the WHO recommendation. Each one-point higher ESES score was associated with 13 percent higher PA after adjustment for age, BMI and menopausal phase (p < .001), and the proportion meeting the WHO recommendation rose from 17 percent in the lowest to 56 percent in the highest ESES quartile. Higher PA was associated with modestly fewer symptoms (IRR = 0.96 per 600 MET-min/week, p = .027), although this was not robust in sensitivity analyses. Strengthening exercise self-efficacy is a promising target for increasing PA in midlife women, and longitudinal studies are needed to establish whether PA reduces menopausal symptoms.

articles.title: Women's Understanding of Risk of Postpartum Hemorrhage: A Qualitative Study.
articles.authors: Carr BL, Pollock W
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) has significant short- and long-term effects for women. Research typically focuses on women who experience severe bleeding. Little is known about women's understanding of their risk or decision-making regarding PPH.
METHODS: The aim of this study was to explore women's understanding of risk for PPH, preferences for discussing this risk, and views on a prediction tool for postpartum hemorrhage. Women who had recently birthed were invited to participate. Eight women were interviewed to discuss their experiences and also comment on a graphical model representing variables associated with risk and conditions related to change of risk for PPH. This Bayesian Network model was developed using perinatal data and expert knowledge from maternity clinicians. The Framework Method was used to identify, manage, and analyze themes across six phases.
RESULTS: Three main themes were identified: Personal Risk, Controlling the Risk, and Knowing. Personal Risk had two subthemes: Transparency and Continuity of Care. Both women who experienced PPH and those who did not wanted to be informed about the possibility of PPH and what the impact of this would be. The prediction tool was considered a useful, visual tool to help aide this discussion.
CONCLUSION: Women want to understand their individual risk and be informed about how their risk of PPH relates to their personal circumstances. Being informed about their risk afforded some degree of control, assisted decision-making, and enabled women to choose what to do with that information. Participants reported the prediction tool was easy to understand and potentially useful.

articles.title: Quality of life with first-line ribociclib plus endocrine therapy vs combination chemotherapy in clinically aggressive HR+/HER2- ABC: RIGHT Choice.
articles.authors: El Saghir NS, Abdel-Razeq H, Im SA et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The RIGHT Choice phase 2 randomized clinical trial of pre/perimenopausal women with clinically aggressive hormone receptor-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (HR+/HER2-) advanced breast cancer (ABC) reported a statistically significant progression-free survival benefit with ribociclib plus endocrine therapy (ET) over combination chemotherapy (21.8 vs 12.8 months; HR, 0.61; 95% CI: 0.43-0.87; P = .003), with lower rates of symptomatic adverse events. This prespecified analysis compared QOL outcomes between treatment arms in RIGHT Choice to support treatment decision-making in these patients.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: Pre/perimenopausal women with clinically aggressive HR+/HER2- ABC were randomized 1:1 to first-line ribociclib plus letrozole/anastrozole/goserelin or investigator's choice of combination chemotherapy. Median time to definitive deterioration (mTTDD) from randomization in Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy-Breast (FACT-B) scores (≥10%) or a composite mTTDD endpoint (including treatment discontinuation) was determined by Kaplan-Meier methods.
RESULTS: mTTDD in FACT-B overall health status, trial outcome index (TOI), and nausea scores was prolonged in patients receiving ribociclib plus ET versus combination chemotherapy (HR, 0.72, 0.63, and 0.59, respectively), while the pain score was similar between treatment arms (HR, 1.05). The composite mTTDD in overall health status, TOI, pain, and nausea scores was longer in patients in the ribociclib arm (HR, 0.68, 0.65, 0.76, and 0.62, respectively).
CONCLUSIONS: Treatment with first-line ribociclib plus ET translates into improved QOL versus combination chemotherapy in patients with clinically aggressive HR+/HER2- ABC. These data reinforce efficacy and safety findings supporting cyclin-dependent kinase 4 and 6 inhibitors plus ET as the preferred option in this population.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03839823.

articles.title: Feasibility and factors associated with successful back transfer after maternal transfer for postpartum hemorrhage: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Imatake H, Haraoka Y, Ueda Y et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) requires multidisciplinary management at tertiary care centers. Back transfer after clinical stabilization is an important component of regional perinatal care, but the clinical characteristics associated with back transfer decisions remain poorly understood. This study examined the rate of back transfer and the factors associated with actual back transfer decisions among women transferred for PPH.
METHODS: A retrospective single-center cohort study was conducted among postpartum women transferred to the Kyoto University Hospital for established or impending PPH between April 2013 and September 2025. The primary outcome was the rate of back transfer, and associated clinical factors were assessed using multivariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: Among 163 eligible women, 92 (56.4%) underwent successful back transfer. A higher shock index at admission was negatively associated with successful back transfer (odds ratio, OR = 0.12; 95% confidence interval, 95% CI = 0.02-0.46; P = 0.005). Compared with tone, trauma (OR = 0.10, 95% CI = 0.03-0.28, P < 0.001) and tissue (OR = 0.26, 95% CI = 0.09-0.74, P = 0.013) were negatively associated with successful back transfer. A higher post-treatment hemoglobin concentration was positively associated with successful back transfer (OR = 1.32, 95% CI = 1.02-1.74, P = 0.041).
CONCLUSION: More than half of the women in this selected cohort underwent back transfer after maternal transfer for PPH. Lower shock index at admission, hemorrhage caused by uterine atony, and higher post-treatment hemoglobin concentration were associated with back transfer. These exploratory findings may inform future efforts to develop standardized back transfer criteria.

articles.title: Circulating biomarkers in early-stage hepatocellular carcinoma for risk stratification, diagnosis and prognosis.
articles.authors: Monti E, Bella M, Vianello C et al.
articles.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, largely due to tumor heterogeneity, late diagnosis, and high recurrence rates even after curative treatment. Although HCC is potentially curable when detected at an early stage, suboptimal surveillance, particularly in patients with underlying cirrhosis or metabolic risk factors, limits the proportion of patients eligible for curative therapies. Current surveillance strategies for at-risk populations have intrinsic limitations, and the performance of imaging and serum biomarkers remains suboptimal. Moreover, the lack of reliable prognostic biomarkers for detecting early recurrence hampers post-treatment surveillance and impacts clinical outcomes. In this context, circulating biomarkers have emerged as promising tools for improving both early detection and prognostic stratification. Liquid biopsy has the potential to enable early, non-invasive diagnosis of HCC and allows longitudinal assessment of tumor progression through serial sampling. In early-stage HCC, blood candidates may complement or outperform conventional approaches by enabling earlier diagnosis and more accurate risk stratification. In this review, we summarize recent advances and current challenges in the clinical translation of circulating biomarkers. We focus on key liquid biopsy components, including circulating cell-free DNA, particularly circulating tumor DNA, circulating tumor cells, non-coding RNAs, extracellular vesicles, proteins and metabolites, such as bile acids and lipids, highlighting their diagnostic and prognostic potential and their possible integration into personalized management strategies for patients with early-stage HCC.

articles.title: Fertility care for transgender and gender diverse individuals in Germany: an interview study with healthcare providers on the importance of care, care provision, barriers, and improvement strategies.
articles.authors: Werner M, Barton C, Becker-Hebly I et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: As gender-affirming care can impact fertility in transgender and gender diverse individuals (TGDI), fertility preservation (FP) may help TGDI to have biological children in the future. The reported discrepancy between the proportion of TGDI who express a desire to have biological children (up to 50%) and low FP utilization rates (3-10%) highlights the need for high-quality fertility care, including fertility related counseling and the provision of FP. However, there is limited knowledge of the extent to which fertility care is being offered in Germany. Therefore, this study aims to examine the current state of fertility care for TGDI in Germany from the perspective of healthcare providers.
METHODS: We conducted 30 semi-structured interviews with healthcare providers from various somatic and mental healthcare disciplines caring for TGDI in Germany. The interview guide addressed four topics of interest: the importance of care, care provision, barriers to care, and improvement strategies. The interviews were transcribed and analyzed using structuring qualitative content analysis by Kuckartz. Deductive and inductive coding were applied to identify main and subcategories from the interviews.
RESULTS: Almost all interviewees considered fertility care for TGDI to be highly important and believed that fertility counseling should be an integral part of care, while they highlighted that the importance of FP depended on the individual family planning desires and life circumstances of TGDI. Most interviewees routinely provided fertility counseling prior to gender-affirming care. We identified several barriers to fertility care for TGDI in Germany: TGDI-related (knowledge gaps, low priority of FP, dysphoria), healthcare provider-related (lack of knowledge, experience, gender sensitivity), procedural (invasiveness of FP, dysphoria triggers), structural (inadequate healthcare infrastructure, research, costs), legal (historic requirement of infertility, prohibition of surrogacy and egg donation), and societal (discrimination, cis- and heteronormative image of family life). To address these barriers, the interviewees suggested promoting healthcare providers' competence, further research and guidelines, standardizing fertility counseling, enhancing interdisciplinary cooperation, ensuring…
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Our study was approved by the Hamburg Medical Council ("Ärztekammer Hamburg") for conduct as a "scientific case" (2023-300381-WF, September 11th, 2023).

articles.title: Mapping the sex-dimorphic hormonal ecosystem in osteoarthritis: non-linear interactions between androgen activity and estrogen.
articles.authors: Deng B, Chen T, Chen Q et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The pronounced sex disparity in osteoarthritis (OA) risk implicates sex hormones, yet single-hormone studies have yielded inconsistent results. We hypothesized that androgen activity influences OA not in isolation but within a dynamic network defined by sex, menopausal status, and estradiol.
METHODS: We analyzed 13,848 adults from NHANES (2013-2016, 2021-2023) using an integrated framework combining complex-survey regression, two-way restricted cubic splines, generalized additive models (GAMs), and SHAP-based machine learning to model non-linear interactions across the estradiol-FAI plane.
RESULTS: Higher free androgen index (FAI) was significantly associated with lower OA risk only in post-menopausal females (OR = 0.85, 95% CI: 0.74-0.97, P = 0.021); associations in pre-menopausal females (OR = 0.75, P = 0.145) and males (OR = 0.94, P = 0.714) were not statistically significant. Non-linear models revealed distinct regional patterns: a "buffering" pattern in post-menopausal females, where the low-estradiol/low-FAI quadrant exhibited the highest risk (GAM P = 0.002; regional synergy mean = 0.077); a "cross-over" pattern in males (GAM P = 0.042); and a flat surface in pre-menopausal females, serving as a negative control. Candidate boundaries (e.g., estradiol ≈ 2.63, FAI ≈ - 0.54 in post-menopausal females) emerged from SHAP dependence plots as hypothesis-generating indicators requiring formal validation. Machine learning confirmed that standalone predictive contributions of sex hormones were minimal (mean |SHAP| ≤ 0.0135), supporting their role as contextual modulators rather than primary drivers.
CONCLUSIONS: Sex hormone effects on OA are context-dependent and non-linear, only discernible when examined in combination. The regional risk patterns-particularly the low-low quadrant in post-menopausal females-represent the robust core of our findings and provide a conceptual framework for understanding sex disparities through steroid interaction. Candidate boundaries are hypothesis-generating and await validation.

articles.title: The impact of video-based educational tools on pregnancy outcomes in pre-existing diabetes mellitus (the ETOS-DM study): study protocol for a national randomised controlled trial.
articles.authors: Pilegaard SP, Søholm JC, Ladefoged V et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite advancements in diabetes management with diabetes technologies, a large proportion of pregnant individuals with type 1 and type 2 (pre-existing) diabetes do not achieve the recommended glycaemic targets, resulting in a high risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes including fetal overgrowth. Novel approaches for diabetes management are urgently needed, and animated videos are increasingly recognised as effective tools for delivering health information across health literacy levels. This study aims to evaluate the impact of adding animated educational videos, available via a smartphone application (app), to usual care, compared to usual care alone, on fetal growth in pregnant individuals with pre-existing diabetes.
METHODS: This national, multicentre, parallel group, open-label randomised controlled trial (RCT) is nested within the Danish Diabetes Birth Registry 2 (DDBR2) study, which includes pregnant individuals with pre-existing diabetes and their offspring. Individuals who consent to participate in the DDBR2 study and fulfil in- and exclusion criteria are enrolled before 14 weeks of gestation, randomised 1:1 and followed until 1 month after delivery. For this study, 15 animated educational videos (1-5 min) were developed using a three-stage framework involving iterative stakeholder input from experts, the target group, and an animation/film director. The videos contain evidence-based information on diabetes self-management in pregnancy. In addition to usual care, the intervention group receives unlimited access to these videos through the "Pregnant with Diabetes" smartphone app, whereas the control group receives usual care alone. Randomisation stratifies for diabetes centre, diabetes type, and the use of multiple daily injections or insulin pumps in individuals with type 1 diabetes. The primary outcome is offspring birth weight standard deviation score. Data analysis will follow the intention-to-treat principle.
DISCUSSION: This study is expected to provide valuable evidence for improving diabetes management during pregnancy for individuals with pre-existing diabetes. The strengths of this large RCT are the involvement of experts and the target group in the development of the intervention and the comprehensive evaluation of fetal outcomes. However, a lack of a systematic mechanism to encourage the use of the intervention may impact its effectiveness.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06250192. Registered on February 1, 2024.

articles.title: Breastfeeding outcomes after postpartum haemorrhage: a socio-ecological secondary analysis of the WOMAN trial.
articles.authors: Gilroy J, O'Connell J, Cooney F
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Breastfeeding has been recognised as a significant driver of neonatal and infant outcomes, particularly in Low- and Middle-income Country (LMIC) settings. Postpartum haemorrhage (PPH) is an increasingly common complication of childbirth, with multiple effects on mothers and their babies. This study aimed to explore the association between aspects of PPH care and outcomes, as they relate to the Socio-Ecological Model of Health for breastfeeding, and the rates of breastfeeding among this cohort of women.
METHODS: This was a secondary analysis of data from the WOMAN trial. The WOMAN trial was a randomised, controlled, pharmaceutical trial in 193 hospitals across 21 countries between 2010 and 2016. A binary logistic regression model was developed to examine the associations between the status of clinical and psycho-social factors from the individual and organisational levels of the Socio-Ecological Model of Health for breastfeeding and the rates of any breastfeeding during the study period.
RESULTS: 16,285 mothers of healthy singleton babies were included in the current study. Factors that may result in maternal-infant separation in the immediate postpartum period were associated with lower rates of any breastfeeding in the study period. These included: the mother requiring transfer between hospitals following PPH (Odds Ratio 0.47 [95%CI 0.41-0.54]) and the mother being admitted to ICU postpartum (OR 0.65 [95%CI 0.54-0.78]). Maternal pain (OR 0.65 [95%CI 0.58-0.75]) and maternal anxiety or depression (OR 0.63 [95% CI 0.53-0.75]) were also associated with lower rates of breastfeeding.
CONCLUSIONS: Some women who experience PPH are at increased risk of not initiating breastfeeding, particularly if there is maternal-infant separation. Organisational factors such as hospital transfer and ICU admission were strongly associated with reduced breastfeeding rates. Individual psycho-social and physical challenges, including pain and psychological distress, further compound these difficulties. Identifying women at higher risk of breastfeeding disruption following PPH could allow targeted support and interventions. Within emergency obstetric care there is a need for universal implementation of breastfeeding-friendly practices, informed by multi-disciplinary, evidence-informed guidelines.

articles.title: "I sneak from home": how health system constraints undermine covert contraceptive use among women facing partner opposition in public health facilities in Uganda.
articles.authors: Misinde C, Okechi SO, Kukundakwe A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Covert contraceptive use - the use of family planning without a male partner's knowledge - is well documented in sub-Saharan Africa and is typically studied as an individual response to partner opposition. Population estimates suggest it describes a substantial minority of contraceptive users in Uganda. Much less is known about how the routine performance of public-sector family planning (FP) and post-abortion care (PAC) services affects whether concealment can be sustained. We examined the experiences of women navigating partner opposition, and of the providers serving them, at public health facilities supported by the ACTUATE project in Uganda.
METHODS: This paper reports the qualitative component of the ACTUATE end-line evaluation; the structured client exit interview survey conducted as part of the same evaluation is reported separately. Between 25 March and 7 April 2025 we conducted seven focus group discussions with 70 women clients (ten per group) and 18 key informant interviews with facility in-charges, medical officers, doctors and midwives, at ten facilities from Health Centre III to General Hospital level across nine districts and four regions of Uganda. Three structured field observation reports provided a third data source. Focus group participants were women aged 18 years and above who had received PAC or FP services at the facility. Data were analysed thematically using a hybrid inductive-deductive approach. Reporting follows the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research (COREQ).
RESULTS: Partner opposition arose spontaneously in six of the seven focus groups and was described by providers in 10 of the 18 interviews. Women reported selecting methods for concealability rather than for duration…
CONCLUSIONS: Stockouts, waiting time, outreach scheduling and procedure privacy are long-standing priorities of family planning programmes, and sustained work on them has produced measurable gains. What these data add is an account of what these constraints cost women whose access depends on concealment, for whom a visit that overruns or a method that is unavailable can compromise autonomy rather than merely cause inconvenience. Attending to concealment within existing quality-of-care measurement - recording the distribution of visit durations rather than the mean, the proportion of procedures conducted in enclosed space, and the temporal distribution of service days - would make this group of clients visible in routine data.

articles.title: HTLV infection among pregnant women attending a viral hepatitis referral center in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
articles.authors: Mello VM, Guimaraes GSN, Ferreira KCP et al.
articles.abstract: Human T-cell lymphotropic virus (HTLV) remains a neglected infection worldwide, despite its potential for severe disease and vertical transmission. In Brazil, the burden of HTLV infection among pregnant remains poorly understood, underscoring the need for updated epidemiological data to guide elimination strategies. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence and socio-epidemiological profile of HTLV infection in pregnant receiving care at a referral center in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. We conducted a mixed (retrospective and prospective) cohort study of 403 pregnant (409 gestational events) referred between 2016 and 2024. All participants were screened for HTLV-1/2 using chemiluminescent immunoassay and confirmed by Western blot. Sociodemographic and clinical data were collected from medical records. HTLV testing was performed in 305 pregnant, with four confirmed infections (prevalence of 1.31% [CI 0,36% - 3,32%]). Three cases (75%) were HTLV-1 and one (25%) HTLV-2. Most women self-identified as mixed race (75%) and had low educational attainment (75%). Coinfections with HBV, HCV, and HIV were detected in 50%, 50%, and 25% of cases, respectively. HTLV prevalence among pregnant was higher than some previous regional estimates, underscoring the need for timely diagnosis to mitigate the risk of new infections. These findings underscore the need for universal antenatal screening, health education, and targeted public health interventions to prevent vertical transmission in Brazil.

articles.title: Correlation between maternal serum pgRNA levels during pregnancy and neonatal virological characteristics at birth in HBV-infected pregnant women.
articles.authors: Zhang Y, Wu Y, Zhang Z et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the relationship between serum pregenomic RNA (pgRNA) in pregnant women with chronic HBV (CHB) infection during pregnancy and maternal clinical characteristics, virological characteristics of newborns at birth, and mother-to-child transmission (MTCT) outcomes.
METHODS: 312 pregnant women with CHB and their newborns were followed up for 12 months, and their clinical data were collected. Spearman correlation analysis was used to evaluate associations between maternal indicators and neonatal outcomes, and logistic regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with neonatal HBeAg positivity.
RESULTS: Maternal HBV DNA, HBsAg, and HBeAg levels were significantly higher in the pgRNA-positive group. All infants followed up to 12 months were negative for both HBsAg and HBV DNA, yielding a 100% success rate of MTCT prevention. Neonatal HBeAg levels at birth were associated with maternal pgRNA levels. Maternal pgRNA levels were significantly higher in mothers of HBeAg-positive newborns than in those of HBeAg-negative newborns, whereas no significant association was found between maternal pgRNA levels and neonatal HBsAg or HBV DNA status. Neonatal HBeAg level was weakly positively correlated with maternal pgRNA levels (r = 0.17, P < 0.01) and maternal HBeAg levels (r = 0.12, P < 0.05). Maternal pgRNA, HBeAg, HBsAg, HBV DNA, age, and treatment were identified as factors associated with neonatal HBeAg status, whereas multivariate analysis showed that only maternal HBeAg remained an independent associated factor.
CONCLUSION: Maternal serum pgRNA is associated with neonatal HBeAg status at birth. However, under standardized combined immunoprophylaxis, maternal pgRNA was not associated with MTCT failure.

articles.title: Adverse pregnancy outcomes by maternal anxiety disorder during pregnancy occurring with and without other mental health conditions: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Baer RJ, Oltman SP, Adeyemi D et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anxiety disorders during pregnancy are common. Understanding whether the presence of anxiety with comorbid mental health conditions confers an increased risk to pregnant people and their infants is understudied.
METHODS: The sample included singleton liveborn infants in California from 2007-2020. Mental health conditions during pregnancy were obtained from discharge records. Adverse pregnancy outcomes examined included placental abruption, severe maternal morbidity (SMM), small or large for gestational age infant, preterm birth, or early term birth. Relative risks and 95% confidence intervals for each adverse outcome were estimated using modified Poisson regression with a log link and robust sandwich standard errors for people with an anxiety disorder diagnosis versus people without a mental health diagnosis. Calculations were made for people with any anxiety disorder, anxiety disorder only, anxiety disorder with comorbid depression, anxiety disorder with a comorbid non-depression mental health diagnosis, and anxiety disorder with comorbid depression and another mental health diagnosis. Four different models were considered: 1) unadjusted, 2) adjusting for racial/ethnic group, education, insurance, participation in Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC), adequacy of prenatal care, age, and parity, 3) adjusting for model two plus infection, smoking, and drug/alcohol use, and 4) adjusting for model three plus diabetes and hypertension.
RESULTS: Of 5,836,541 maternal-infant pairs, 2.2% pregnant people had an anxiety disorder diagnosis during their pregnancy or at the birth admission. Of those with anxiety, 29.4% had a comorbid mental health diagnosis. People with an anxiety disorder during pregnancy were at increased risk of nearly all the adverse pregnancy outcomes examined. In fully adjusted models, individuals with anxiety and depression were 1.7-times more likely to have a provider-initiated birth…
CONCLUSION: Maternal anxiety disorder diagnosis during pregnancy was associated with an elevated risk of an adverse pregnancy outcome even after adjustment for maternal factors. Rates of adverse outcomes were higher among individuals with a comorbid mental health diagnosis than those with an anxiety disorder alone. These findings indicate that individuals with anxiety disorders are at increased risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes, highlighting the importance of prioritizing mental health support during pregnancy.

articles.title: The effect of the centering pregnancy model on diabetes self- management, self-efficacy, pregnancy experience, and perinatal outcomes in women with diabetes: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.authors: Maghalian M, Abbasalizadeh F, Mohammad-Alizadeh-Charandabi S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and type 2 diabetes in pregnancy pose significant maternal and perinatal risks. The Centering Pregnancy group care model may improve diabetes self-management and pregnancy experience, but its effectiveness in Iran-particularly on perinatal outcomes-remains unproven. This trial evaluated whether Centering Pregnancy improves diabetes self-management, self-efficacy, and pregnancy experience (primary outcomes), and secondary outcomes including maternal satisfaction, breastfeeding at 6 weeks postpartum, preterm delivery, NICU admission, and cesarean section, compared with standard care in Iranian women with GDM or type 2 diabetes.
METHODS: This randomized controlled trial enrolled 100 women (50 per group) from Tabriz clinics. The intervention group received four bi-weekly group sessions plus standard care; controls received routine care. Primary outcomes (diabetes self-care activities [SDSCA], self-efficacy [DMSES], and pregnancy experience [PES]) were measured at baseline and 36-39 weeks. Secondary outcomes included satisfaction (Visual Analogue Scale), breastfeeding performance (Agunbiade instrument) at 6 weeks postpartum, and perinatal outcomes including preterm delivery, NICU admission, and cesarean section. from medical records. Analysis followed intention-to-treat principles using ANCOVA, with 6-week postpartum follow-up.
RESULTS: The intervention group showed significantly greater improvements in SDSCA (MD = 0.9, 95% CI: 0.3-1.4, p = 0.002), DMSES (MD = 0.8, 95% CI: 0.3-1.2, p = 0.001), and PES Uplifts (MD = 2.2, 95% CI: 0.3-4.1, p = 0.026) compared to the control group. Breastfeeding performance was significantly better in the intervention group compared to the control group (MD = 0.8, 95% CI: 0.4-1.3, p < 0.001). Perinatal outcomes showed lower rates in the intervention group but these differences were not statistically significant (p > 0.05). No significant between-group differences were observed for PES Hassles, or satisfaction (p > 0.05).
CONCLUSION: The Centering Pregnancy model is an effective patient-centered strategy for enhancing diabetes self-management, self-efficacy, and positive pregnancy experiences in Iranian women with diabetic pregnancies. Favorable but non-significant trends in perinatal outcomes warrant investigation in larger trials. This approach may be considered for integration into standard care protocols.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: IRCT20220718010324N70.

articles.title: Treated and untreated maternal asthma and early pregnancy outcomes: a retrospective cohort study of 324,238 infants.
articles.authors: Shakhshir LA, Pell JP, Hastie CE et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Continued use of asthma medication during pregnancy is recommended, because asthma exacerbations often increase during pregnancy, and poor control may adversely affect maternal and foetal health. However, evidence on whether adverse outcomes arise from the treatment itself or just the underlying disease remains inconsistent. This study examined the relationship between maternal asthma, and its medication, and early pregnancy outcomes.
METHODS: A retrospective birth cohort was constructed using population-wide linked Welsh health records of 324,238 infants born between 2009 and 2022. Logistic regression was used to investigate associations between maternal asthma (treated, untreated, and medication exposure) and pregnancy outcomes: stillbirth, iatrogenic and spontaneous preterm delivery, small/very small for gestational age (SGA/VSGA), and low Apgar score.
RESULTS: Of the 324,238 infants, 39,040 (12.0%) had mothers with asthma: 20,840 (6.4%) had treated asthma, 8,230 (2.5%) had untreated asthma, and 9,970 (3.1%) were prescribed asthma medications without recorded asthma diagnoses. Compared to offspring of mothers with no maternal asthma (reference group), those whose mothers had treated asthma had higher odds of SGA (aOR 1.13, 95% CI 1.07-1.19), VSGA (aOR 1.14, 95% CI 1.03-1.26), Apgar score < 7 (aOR 1.14, 95% CI 1.01-1.29), and iatrogenic preterm delivery (aOR 1.13, 95% CI 1.01-1.26). Associations were observed across multiple classes of asthma medication with stronger associations among the offspring of mothers prescribed more than one medication class and those with add-on therapies including long-acting muscarinic antagonists, short-acting muscarinic antagonists, leukotrienes antagonist and theophylline, consistent with more severe, or poorly controlled, asthma rather than medication effects. Untreated asthma was associated with higher risk of iatrogenic preterm delivery, and treated asthma was associated with lower risk of spontaneous preterm delivery…
CONCLUSIONS: The non-specific associations observed across different classes of asthma medication and dose-relationships with polytherapy suggested confounding by indication and severity. The findings for iatrogenic preterm delivery further supported an effect of the underlying disease rather than its treatment. These findings, together with the lower risk of spontaneous preterm delivery among treated mothers, support guideline recommendations to continue asthma treatment during pregnancy.

articles.title: Biopsychosocial factors associated with menstrual pain, menstrual attitudes, health literacy, and physical activity across age-based cohorts: a cross-sectional comparative study.
articles.authors: Yiğit Kocamer M, Sert B
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Menstrual pain is influenced by biological, psychological, and sociocultural factors. This study compared menstrual pain, menstrual attitudes, health literacy, and physical activity across age-based cohorts of women and examined the associations between menstrual attitudes and menstrual pain.
METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 1,220 women with primary dysmenorrhea were classified into three age-based cohorts corresponding to Generations Z (n = 380), Y (n = 440), and X (n = 400). Menstrual pain, menstrual attitudes, health literacy, and daily step counts were assessed using validated instruments. Group differences were examined using χ² and Kruskal-Wallis tests followed by Dwass-Steel-Critchlow-Fligner post-hoc comparisons where appropriate. Spearman correlation and adjusted multiple linear regression analyses were performed.
RESULTS: Significant differences were observed across the age-based cohorts in menstrual pain, menstrual attitudes, and health literacy (all p < 0.05), whereas physical activity did not differ significantly. Women in the youngest age-based cohort reported the highest pain levels and more positive menstrual attitudes, whereas women in the oldest age-based cohort had the lowest health literacy scores. Significant differences were identified across all MAQ subscales, with the largest effect observed for the Anticipation and Prediction of Menstruation subscale (ε²=0.084). Correlation analyses showed that the associations between menstrual attitude dimensions and pain varied across cohorts, although a weak negative association between pain and the Denial of the Effects of Menstruation subscale was consistently observed. In the adjusted regression model, perceiving menstruation as a bothersome event (β = 0.159, p < 0.001) and as a natural event (β = 0.062, p = 0.026) were positively associated with pain, whereas denial of the effects of menstruation was negatively associated with pain (β=-0.243, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Menstrual pain and menstrual attitudes differed across age-based cohorts, and specific dimensions of menstrual attitudes were independently associated with pain severity. These findings support a biopsychosocial perspective on menstrual pain and highlight the importance of age- and life-stage-sensitive approaches to menstrual health. Because of the cross-sectional design, causal inferences cannot be made.

articles.title: Performance of a DNA methylation marker panel in cervical samples from women with abnormal cytology findings.
articles.authors: Zeiser I, Schubert K, Hippe J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reliable triage methods are essential in cervical cancer screening to avoid overtreatment. DNA methylation markers offer an objective molecular readout with potential to keep false-positive rates low. We evaluated the GynTect® DNA methylation assay as a triage marker in cervical samples from women with abnormal cytology, in comparison with the p16/Ki-67 Dual Stain test CINtec Plus®.
METHODS: Surplus liquid-based cytology samples from 1,000 women with cytology ≥ PAP III (Low-Grade Squamous Intraepithelial Lesion = LSIL, or worse) were tested with GynTect® (markers: ASTN1, DLX1, ITGA4, RXFP3, SOX17, ZNF671). cobas® HPV and p16/Ki-67 Dual Stain (CINtec Plus®) results were available for all samples; histopathology was available for a subset of 601 samples. Positivity rates with 95% confidence intervals were calculated using the Wilson score method.
RESULTS: Overall GynTect positivity was 27.7% versus 88.3% for p16/Ki-67 Dual Stain. Methylation positivity correlated with cytological severity: 17.0% in LSIL, 30.2% in moderate High-​Grade Squamous Intraepithelial Lesion HSIL, and 65.0% in the PAP IV group (high-grade SIL/AIS and HSIL suspicious for invasion). Among HPV16/18-positive samples, 38.4% were GynTect-positive versus 94.8% p16/Ki-67 Dual Stain-positive. By histopathology, GynTect positivity was 15.0% (CIN I), 27.0% (CIN II), and 56.5% (CIN III); all four cancer cases were GynTect- and p16/Ki-67 Dual Stain​-positive. Of 191 GynTect-positive cases with histopathology, 73% had CIN II or CIN III.
CONCLUSIONS: GynTect positivity (27.7%) was significantly lower than p16/Ki-67 Dual Stain positivity (88.3%), with a statistically significant monotonic trend across increasing cytological severity (Cochran-Armitage trend test, p < 0.001) and histopathological categories (p < 0.001). All four histologically confirmed carcinomas were GynTect-positive. These findings are consistent with a potential role for GynTect in selective triage after abnormal cytology, with lower positivity rates suggesting higher selectivity for high-grade disease compared with p16/Ki-67 Dual Stain. Prospective validation in primary HPV-screening triage populations is required to determine whether this translates into clinical benefit.

articles.title: Diagnostic performance of RMI I-IV for pelvic/adnexal masses after hysterectomy: a retrospective single-center study.
articles.authors: Zhou M, Wang M, Xin L
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate and compare the diagnostic performance of four Risk of Malignancy Index (RMI) models (I-IV) in differentiating benign from malignant pelvic masses newly developed in post-hysterectomy patients.
METHODS: This 10-year retrospective single-center study enrolled 171 patients with newly developed pelvic/adnexal masses after hysterectomy who received surgical resection and pathological diagnosis. Baseline clinical and imaging parameters-including age, CA125 level, tumor size, ultrasound features, and menopausal status-were collected. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and DeLong's test were used to compare the area under the curve (AUC) of RMI I-IV, while the Youden index was used to determine the optimal cutoff for each model. Diagnostic sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy were calculated using both traditional published thresholds and cohort-specific optimal cutoffs.
RESULTS: Numerically, RMI I exhibited the highest specificity (98.6%) and the largest AUC value (0.973, 95% CI: 0.942-1.000) among the four evaluated indices. Overall, all RMI models demonstrated good diagnostic performance. At a cutoff of ≥ 60, RMI I achieved a sensitivity of 96.7% and a specificity of 91.5%. In pairwise DeLong's tests, the AUC of RMI I was significantly higher than that of RMI II and RMI IV (p = 0.009 and 0.013, respectively), while its advantage over RMI III did not reach statistical significance (p = 0.057).
