articles.title: Efficacy of sacubitril/valsartan and bosentan in amelioration of estradiol induced endometrial changes via regulation of Wnt/β-catenin and IL6/JAK/STAT3 pathways.
articles.authors: Refaie MMM, Ibrahim MFG, Sherkawy HS et al.
articles.abstract: Endometrial hyperplasia (EHP) commonly affects elderly females in the pre-menopausal period and can progress to carcinoma. Immune dysregulation has a crucial role in mediating such disorders. Thus, studying its pathogenesis and finding ameliorative medical treatment becomes mandatory. This motivated us to perform the current experiment of induced EHP in female rats using estradiol (EST) (2 mg/kg/day) intramuscular injection with or without using bosentan (BOS) (50 mg/kg/day) and/or Sacubitril/valsartan (SV) (60 mg/kg/day) for 3 weeks. We found typical histopathological features of EHP, elevation of total oxidant status (TOS), oxidative stress index (OSI), interleukin 6/Janus kinase/Signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (IL6/JAK/STAT3), and Wnt/β-catenin pathways with increased uterine weights. However, there is a significant diminution in total antioxidant capacity (TAC) and caspase-3 immune expression. Interestingly, BOS and/or SV administration significantly ameliorated the histopathological and biochemical disturbances. This improvement may be attributed to the pharmacological ability of SV to block angiotensin receptors and neprilysin besides blocking endothelin receptors by BOS. Furthermore, SV/BOS could regulate apoptosis with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties.

articles.title: Histological subtype-specific gasdermin expression suggests distinct pyroptotic and inflammatory profiles in ovarian cancer.
articles.authors: Keskin A, Berkel C, Yeldir N et al.
articles.abstract: Gasdermin (GSDM) family members are key effector proteins that mediate pyroptosis, a pro-inflammatory form of programmed cell death characterized by plasma membrane pore formation and the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines. Despite their established role in inflammation, the relationship between GSDM expression and systemic inflammatory responses across various histological subtypes of ovarian cancer remains poorly understood. In the present study, mRNA and protein expression levels of six GSDM family members were examined in ovarian cancer tissues representing various histological subtypes (serous, endometrioid, clear cell, and mucinous), and in benign/non-malignant (histologically normal) ovarian tissues obtained from healthy women without ovarian cancer. Besides, GSDM expression profiles were analyzed in peripheral blood samples obtained from ovarian cancer patients and control women. In addition, serum levels of certain inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β and IL-18) were measured in patients with ovarian tumors of different histological subtypes, and in control women. Our findings showed histological subtype-dependent differences in the expression of several gasdermin family members at both mRNA and protein levels, in ovarian tissue and serum samples. Notably, GSDMB and GSDMF protein levels were found to be significantly reduced in high grade serous tumors compared with benign (normal) ovarian tissues; and GSDMB protein levels were decreased in endometroid tumors compared to normal ovaries. Furthermore, we found that histological subtype-specific alterations in GSDM mRNA expression are more prominent in ovarian tissues than in peripheral blood mRNA samples. Analysis of serum cytokines demonstrated that patients with serous and mucinous ovarian cancer have higher levels of IL-1β and IL-18 in their serum, compared with those with other histological subtypes of ovarian cancer. These results likely indicate that inflammatory responses may vary among different ovarian cancer histological subtypes and point to the presence of histological subtype-specific inflammatory profiles in this highly heterogeneous malignant disease. Overall, our findings suggest that GSDM-mediated pyroptosis and associated inflammatory pathways differ across different histological subtypes of ovarian cancer and may possibly contribute to disease heterogeneity.

articles.title: The Menopausal Transition as a Critical Window for Cardiovascular Risk Modification and Intervention Opportunities.
articles.authors: Mehta JM, Manson JE
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review examines the cardiometabolic changes that occur during the menopausal transition (MT), emphasizing how hormonal fluctuations may contribute to the development of adverse cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk factors. It identifies gaps in evidence regarding safe and effective treatments for cardiometabolic risk reduction during the MT.
RECENT FINDINGS: The MT is characterized by hormonal shifts driving adverse changes in body composition, lipid profiles, vascular function, and metabolic regulation. These alterations are associated with accelerated progression of cardiovascular risk factors and may contribute to the increase in CVD risk observed after menopause. Growing evidence suggests that the MT represents a distinct period of cardiometabolic vulnerability and provides an opportunity for early risk identification and prevention. Lifestyle and behavioral modifications, as well as control of blood pressure, lipids, and other established risk factors, are the foundations of risk-reducing management and treatment. Early cardiometabolic risk assessment and individualized, lifestyle -centered management are essential to optimize cardiovascular outcomes during the MT. Further research is needed to clarify therapeutic strategies for this critical window in women's cardiometabolic health.

articles.title: CGRP-CALCRL-VEGFR signaling promotes angiogenesis and cervical cancer progression.
articles.authors: Lu J, Li S, Han Q et al.
articles.abstract: Neuro-tumor crosstalk is increasingly recognized as a fundamental driver of cancer progression. Calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP), a neuropeptide classically associated with sensory neurons, has emerged as a key mediator of tumor growth, immune suppression, and cancer-associated symptoms across multiple malignancies. However, the role of CGRP signaling in cervical cancer remains poorly defined. We comprehensively analyzed CGRP expression and its clinical relevance in cervical cancer using TCGA transcriptomic datasets, gene correlation analyses, and survival models. Single-cell RNA sequencing data were leveraged to define the cellular distribution of the CGRP receptor calcitonin receptor-like receptor (CALCRL). In HUVECs, CALCRL was silenced by siRNA and evaluated using proliferation, tube-formation, gene-expression, rescue, and signaling assays, including exogenous α-CGRP stimulation and VEGFR1/VEGFR2 overexpression. In vivo, CGRP-receptor inhibition was evaluated in SiHa, CaSki, and HeLa xenograft models using Fremanezumab or olcegepant. Elevated CGRP expression was associated with adverse prognosis in TCGA-CESC, and independent clinical validation showed that high CALCB expression was associated with poorer survival (log-rank P = 0.0036). Single-cell transcriptomic analyses consistently revealed that CALCRL expression was highly enriched in endothelial cells. CALCRL silencing impaired endothelial proliferation and angiogenic capacity, whereas exogenous α-CGRP enhanced these phenotypes in control cells but not in CALCRL-silenced cells. VEGFR1 or VEGFR2 overexpression partially rescued the proliferation defect caused by CALCRL depletion. Pharmacological inhibition of CGRP-receptor signaling consistently suppressed tumor growth across SiHa, CaSki, and HeLa xenograft models. These findings provide preclinical evidence that CGRP-CALCRL signaling promotes cervical cancer progression through endothelial angiogenic activity and VEGFR-associated signaling, supporting further investigation of this pathway as a potential therapeutic target.

articles.title: Predominance of Ureaplasma Parvum in Intrauterine Infection-Related Stillbirths in a series of 10 cases.
articles.authors: Huo L, Lei W, Liao Y et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to investigate whether stillbirths with funisitis are associated with intrauterine infection and specific microorganisms (especially Ureaplasma parvum).
METHODS: A retrospective analysis of 10 stillbirths with funisitis was conducted on fetal organ tissues; multiplex suspension microarray was applied to screen 12 common microorganisms in the female genital tract, with pathogen confirmation via quantitative PCR and pathogen serotype confi rmation via sequencing.
RESULTS: Our study revealed that UP represented the most commonly identified microorganism in organ specimens from stillbirths complicated by funisitis. Serovars 3 and 6 were most common. A positive UP finding in the stillbirth corresponded to a positive detection of UP in the maternal cervical swab.
CONCLUSION: There was a plausible association between UP infection and stillbirth with funisitis. The application of molecular pathology offers significant benefits for providing clues for elucidating the potential etiology and preventing adverse pregnancy outcomes. Due to the small sample size and lack of a control group, this study cannot establish a causal relationship between UP infection and stillbirth.

articles.title: Sex hormone-binding globulin during menopausal transition- associations with hormone therapy use, android fat, physical activity and eating behaviour.
articles.authors: Lankila H, Hyvärinen M, Kekäläinen T et al.
articles.abstract: BackgroundSex hormone-binding globulin SHBG is related to metabolic adversities, and menopausal women are at higher risk for increased abdominal adiposity associated with these detrimental changes. Health behaviours and the use of exogenous estrogen-containing therapy may contribute to metabolic health.ObjectivesTo investigate longitudinal changes in SHBG concentrations during the menopausal transition and their associations with hormone therapy use, android fat and health behaviours.DesignA longitudinal study included 298 Finnish women aged 47-55 years.MethodsData from a 4-year follow-up study ERMA and EsmiRs were used. SHBG was quantified using immunoassays, and android fat mass was measured with DXA. Health behaviours were assessed using accelerometer-measured physical activity and questionnaire-derived eating behaviour. Participants were categorized into PRE-POST group (pre- or perimenopausal at the baseline and postmenopausal at the follow-up, n = 148), PRE-PRE group (pre- or perimenopausal at both timepoints, n = 57) or POST-POST group (postmenopausal at both timepoints, n = 93). Linear mixed models were used to study the role of health behaviours and android fat mass as predictors of SHBG.ResultsThere were no differences at baseline SHBG levels between the groups. During the follow-up, SHBG increased in PRE-POST group (p = 0.036) among hormone therapy (HT) users, while there was a decrease in same group in HT non-users (p = 0.001). While higher android fat mass was associated with lower levels of SHBG in the sample with all participants, an increase of SHBG levels during the follow-up was detected independent of android fat mass and health behaviours in HT users.ConclusionsMenopausal estrogen-containing therapy may be a main driver for changes in SHBG concentrations during the menopausal transition. However, women not using hormone therapy, might benefit from regular eating styles to promote metabolic health during menopausal transition.

articles.title: Pregnancy outcomes following fetal shunt placement in twin gestations.
articles.authors: Chmait D, Monson MA, Korst LM et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Fetal shunt placement in twins remains controversial due to technical difficulties and potential procedure-related risks to the healthy co-twin. We report outcomes following referral for possible shunt placement in twin gestations.
METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study of twin gestations referred for shunt placement at a single center (2007-2023). Conditions eligible for shunt placement included: cystic fetal lung lesions or pleural effusions with secondary fetal hydrops and genitourinary (GU) tract obstruction with oligohydramnios. Results are reported as n (%) or median (range).
RESULTS: Among the 20 patients referred for possible shunt placement, 3 were not eligible (ie, chest lesion without hydrops [n=2], GU obstruction without oligohydramnios [n=1]). Of the 17 eligible patients, 14 underwent shunt placement (9 GU, 5 thoracic) and 3 GU patients underwent expectant management. There were 9 dichorionic diamniotic and 5 monochorionic diamniotic twins. The gestational age (GA) at initial surgery was 21.9 (17.7-30.6) weeks. Four (28.6%) patients underwent a second procedure for a displaced shunt. No intraoperative complications (eg, incidental septostomy) occurred. The interval from initial surgery to delivery was 12.3 (2.4-20.0) weeks with a delivery GA of 33.1 (28.6-37.9) weeks. Twelve (85.7%) shunted twins were 30-day survivors, and unaffected co-twin survivorship was 100%.
CONCLUSION: Shunt placement in twins meeting surgical criteria can be accomplished with relatively minimal risk to the co-twin. Therefore, patients with twin gestations may be considered candidates for fetal shunt placement at experienced centers.

articles.title: Severe Fetal Anemia and Pancytopenia in Maternal Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Treated with Serial Intrauterine Transfusions and Intravenous Immunoglobulin: A Case Report.
articles.authors: Pn LN, Padmalatha VV, Gopalaswamy V et al.
articles.abstract: Severe fetal anemia with hydrops and multilineage cytopenia is rarely reported in pregnancies complicated by maternal systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). We report a 33-year-old woman with SLE and maternal thrombocytopenia whose fetus developed hydrops and an MCA-PSV of 1.823 MoM at 24+6 weeks. Fetal sampling before the first intrauterine transfusion (IUT) showed hemoglobin 3.3 g/dL, hematocrit 10.5%, WBC 0.28 × 10³/µL and platelets 17 × 10³/µL. The first IUT at 25+6 weeks corrected the anemia, although profound leukopenia and thrombocytopenia were documented immediately afterward. Repeat sampling immediately before a second IUT at 28+1 weeks showed hemoglobin 10.5 g/dL, WBC 0.14 × 10³/µL and platelets 26 × 10³/µL. Serial IUTs corrected fetal anemia; maternal IVIG was given empirically because of concern for an additional immune contribution, without proof of immune-mediated cell destruction or an independent IVIG effect. Fetal growth restriction and abnormal Dopplers contributed to delivery at 33+6 weeks. The neonate had normal blood counts without postnatal transfusion. This case highlights the importance of targeted evaluation for fetal anemia when concerning sonographic findings arise in SLE pregnancies.

articles.title: Two Persons, One Womb: Testing the Social Construction of Reproduction in Conjoined Twins.
articles.authors: Villalba A
articles.abstract: Standard models of reproductive autonomy presuppose a singular and bounded subject. This paper challenges that assumption by analysing the limit case of dicephalus parapagus conjoined twins where two distinct persons share a single reproductive system. I argue that this physiological configuration creates an ontological indeterminacy that biological essentialism cannot resolve. Drawing on a previous constructivist framework of reproduction, I demonstrate that when gestation is a shared biological event but personhood is distinct, the designation of "mother" cannot be discovered in the tissue but must be acknowledged through intention. The analysis proceeds to examine the severe ethical conflict arising when one twin wishes to reproduce while the other does not. I contend that prioritizing the reproductive desire of one sister over the refusal of the other constitutes a violation of bodily integrity analogous to involuntary gestational surrogacy. Consequently, I argue that in shared bodies, the non-reproducing person must hold an absolute power of veto. This aligns with established bioethical precedents, such as those discussed by Robertson, where the right to avoid involuntary biological parenthood is often held to supersede a former partner's desire to gestate shared embryos. Finally, this paper posits that the principles derived from this extreme case offer a necessary heuristic for broader bioethical issues. The example of conjoined twins validates the distributed maternity of Reciprocal IVF in lesbian couples while simultaneously reinforcing the protections against coercive surrogacy. By deconstructing the most extreme form of shared biology, this paper offers an exploration of a case of fragmented maternity and its implications.

articles.title: Interleukin-6 and the maternal-placental immune axis in preeclampsia: from implantation to postpartum cardiovascular disease.
articles.authors: Baroutis D, Papapanagiotou A, Giannakaki AG et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Preeclampsia is a leading cause of maternal and perinatal morbidity and is increasingly understood as a disorder of maternal-fetal immune maladaptation, in which interleukin-6 (IL-6) occupies a central position. IL-6 is usually examined at a single disease stage, which obscures its role as a continuous mediator.
CONTENT: This narrative review traces IL-6 across the preeclampsia continuum: signalling biology; the decidual immune niche; the regulatory T-cell/T-helper-17 and signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 axes; defective placentation; antiangiogenic endothelial injury; the clinical phenotype; postpartum inflammation; and remote cardiovascular disease. Evidence is labelled by provenance, the roles of IL-6 as biomarker, mediator and therapeutic target are distinguished, and aspirin, heparin and IL-6-directed therapies are appraised.
SUMMARY: IL-6 links immune-tolerance failure to angiogenic imbalance and endothelial dysfunction, and altered inflammatory profiles persist years after delivery. Causal evidence, however, rests largely on animal and in vitro work; human data are associative and confounded by shared cardiometabolic risk; and the first large trial of IL-6 ligand inhibition lowered inflammation without reducing cardiovascular events.
OUTLOOK: Longitudinal, signalling-specific measurement, explicit separation of marker from mediator and target, and safety-led evaluation in pregnancy are required before this axis can inform prevention or postpartum cardiovascular risk stratification.

articles.title: Genomic Correlates of Chemoradiation Response in Locally Advanced Cervical Cancer: Implications for Precision Oncology.
articles.authors: Jayalie VF, Rusda M, Gondhowiardjo SA et al.
articles.abstract: Locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC) accounts for a major healthcare burden in low- and middle-income countries, where five-year overall survival remains below 75% despite concurrent chemoradiation therapy (CCRT) as the curative standard. Treatment response is highly variable, yet clinical management is largely uniform. This review synthesizes current evidence on the genomic correlates of CCRT in LACC, spanning alterations in PIK3CA, PTEN, TP53, KRAS, ARID1A, and APOBEC-driven mutational signatures. These pathways offer biologically coherent explanations for radioresistance, but the strength and maturity of supporting evidence vary considerably, and evidence for most markers remains prognostic rather than treatment-predictive. No single genomic marker yet supports routine clinical use, and genome-only models omit complementary contributions from the tumor microenvironment, hypoxia, cancer stem cell biology, and clinicopathological or imaging-derived parameters. We further discuss the translational gap between genomic discovery and clinical implementation, with particular attention to population representation and resource constraints in high-burden settings. Prospective, population-inclusive genomic trials are urgently needed to translate these findings into equitable precision radiotherapy for patients with LACC worldwide.

articles.title: Small area estimation of hysterectomy prevalence and cervical cancer screening in the U.S. states and counties.
articles.journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology
articles.authors: Liu B, Stout NK, Lee R et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer screening (CCS) is essential for early detection, yet reliable granular estimates at state and county levels remain limited, especially considering that hysterectomy, the second most common surgery among U.S. women, affects screening eligibility.
METHODS: Data from the National Health Interview Survey (NHIS) and Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS) for 2012-2016 and 2021-2023 were used to develop state- and county-level small area models estimating hysterectomy and CCS prevalence (with and without correcting hysterectomy). Model diagnostics and internal and external validation were conducted, including analyses of associations between CCS prevalence and cervical cancer incidence and mortality.
RESULTS: Model-based estimates of hysterectomy and CCS prevalence (both hysterectomy-corrected and uncorrected) were produced for all U.S. states and 3,142 counties for 2012-2016 and 2021-2023. Substantial geographic variation across counties was observed. Moderate negative correlations between CCS prevalence and cervical cancer incidence and mortality were identified, e.g., state-level weighted Pearson correlation coefficients were -0.3565 (p<0.0001) for 2012-2016 and -0.2638 (p<0.0001) for 2021-2023.
CONCLUSIONS: These modeled estimates improved precision and adjusted for differences between BRFSS and NHIS. Hysterectomy-corrected CCS estimates partially addressed misclassification of the screening-eligible population. By leveraging the large BRFSS sample and the higher response rates and household coverage of NHIS, this approach provides small area estimates to support cancer surveillance, targeted interventions, and public health decision-making.
IMPACT: These estimates serve as a resource for health departments and policymakers to identify underserved communities, prioritize resources, and monitor progress toward reducing disparities in cervical cancer prevention.

articles.title: Non-hormonal management of menopause symptoms-the statement of the European Society of Gynecology.
articles.journal: Gynecological endocrinology : the official journal of the International Society of Gynecological Endocrinology
articles.authors: Castelo-Branco C, Kiesel L, Yoldemir T et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Menopausal symptoms, particularly vasomotor symptoms (VMS), sleep disturbances, mood disorders, and genitourinary syndrome of menopause (GSM), affect a substantial proportion of women and may significantly impair the quality of life. Although menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) remains the most effective treatment, many women have contraindications to hormonal treatment or prefer non-hormonal options.
OBJECTIVE: To review and provide evidence-based recommendations on current non-hormonal interventions for the management of menopausal symptoms.
METHODS: The European Society of Gynecology convened an expert panel that performed a comprehensive literature review using MEDLINE and EMBASE. Clinical guidelines, systematic reviews, meta-analyzes, randomized controlled trials, and relevant primary studies evaluating non-hormonal interventions for menopausal symptoms were identified, critically appraised, and synthesized through a structured consensus process.
RESULTS: Lifestyle modification, including healthy diet, regular physical activity, weight control, sleep hygiene, and behavioral interventions, forms the foundation of menopausal care. Among pharmacological therapies, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors, gabapentin, clonidine, oxybutynin, and pregabalin demonstrate varying degrees of efficacy for VMS. Neurokinin receptor antagonists, particularly fezolinetant and elinzanetant, represent the most effective evidence-based non-hormonal pharmacologic therapies currently available. Cognitive behavioral therapy and clinical hypnosis effectively reduce VMS-related distress and improve sleep and quality of life. Evidence for complementary approaches such as mindfulness, yoga, acupuncture, acupressure, reflexology, phytoestrogens, S-equol, DT56a, purified pollen extracts, and black cohosh ranges from moderate to limited. For GSM, lubricants, moisturizers, hyaluronic acid preparations, and pelvic floor muscle…
CONCLUSIONS: Non-hormonal therapies provide effective and individualized treatment options for menopausal symptoms, particularly for women who are unable or unwilling to use MHT. Neurokinin receptor antagonists, selected pharmacologic agents, psychological interventions, and targeted GSM therapies represent the strongest evidence-based approaches currently available. The choice of treatment should consider symptom profile, contraindications, adverse effects, regulatory approval, and patient preferences.

articles.title: Topical Minoxidil for Female Pattern Hair Loss: Clinical Outcomes in Postmenopausal Women.
articles.journal: Dermatologic surgery : official publication for American Society for Dermatologic Surgery [et al.]
articles.authors: Waide RJ, Liu HP, Patel Shah A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Female pattern hair loss (FPHL) affects up to 50% of women and becomes increasingly prevalent after menopause. Declining estrogen levels, altered hormonal balance, and follicular miniaturization contribute to disease progression, which can substantially impair quality of life (QoL).
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to review the pathophysiology and psychosocial impact of FPHL, discuss patient counseling and treatment expectations, and evaluate the benefits of topical minoxidil in postmenopausal women.
METHODS: Published evidence on FPHL pathophysiology, psychosocial outcomes, treatment barriers, and minoxidil efficacy and tolerability was searched for online using Google and via PubMed. Publications were reviewed for relevance based on the objectives as listed above before being selected for inclusion in our narrative. Findings from a post hoc subgroup analysis of postmenopausal women in a phase III clinical trial of once-daily 5% minoxidil topical foam (MTF) were also assessed.
RESULTS: FPHL is influenced by genetic susceptibility, aging, and menopausal hormonal changes. Hair loss is associated with reduced self-esteem, social withdrawal, anxiety, and impaired QoL. Delayed treatment initiation is common. In a phase III study, 5% MTF significantly increased hair count versus vehicle at 24 weeks. Post hoc analyses demonstrated significant hair regrowth in postmenopausal women with both early and advanced hair loss.
CONCLUSION: Once-daily 5% MTF is effective in postmenopausal women regardless of disease severity. Early recognition, patient education, individualized treatment selection, and psychosocial support are essential for optimal outcomes.

articles.title: Prospective randomised study comparing laparoscopic and open varicocelectomy: A single-centre experience.
articles.authors: Faridi SH, Aadil M, Ahmad M et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Varicocele is a common cause of male infertility and scrotal pain. Surgical options include open, laparoscopic and microsurgical varicocelectomy; however, comparative prospective randomised data are limited. The aim of the study was to compare laparoscopic and open varicocelectomy in terms of operative parameters, post-operative recovery, complications and semen analysis changes.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: A prospective randomised study was conducted over 24 months (February 2024-February 2026) and included 100 patients with Grade 2 and 3 varicocele. Patients were allocated into laparoscopic ( n = 50) and open ( n = 50) groups. Outcomes assessed included operative time, post-operative pain using VAS score, hospital stay, time to return to normal activity, complications, recurrence and semen analysis changes. Statistical analysis was performed using appropriate tests, with P < 0.05 considered significant.
RESULTS: Operative time was significantly different between groups (23.40 ± 7.52 vs. 24.70 ± 4.78 min; P = 0.033). The laparoscopic group had significantly shorter hospital stay (1.43 ± 0.36 vs. 1.96 ± 0.28 days; P < 0.001) and earlier return to normal activity (5.04 ± 0.48 vs. 6.36 ± 0.51 h; P < 0.001). Post-operative pain was significantly lower in the laparoscopic group, both at 6 h and at discharge ( P < 0.001). Improvement in semen analysis was seen in 35 (70%) and 28 (56%) of laparoscopic and open group patients, respectively ( P = 0.21). Complications and recurrence were comparable.
CONCLUSIONS: Both techniques are safe and effective for varicocele treatment. Laparoscopic varicocelectomy offers advantages of reduced pain, shorter hospital stay and faster recovery, while improvement in semen analysis is comparable.

articles.title: Controversies in NEN: An ENETS position statement on fertility, sexual function and pregnancy in patients with neuroendocrine neoplasms.
articles.authors: Tsoli M, Del Olmo-García M, Dierickx L et al.
articles.abstract: Neuroendocrine neoplasms (NENs) are a heterogeneous group of tumours with increasing incidence and improved survival, leading to a growing population of patients of reproductive age. Despite this, the impact of NENs and their treatment on fertility, sexual function and pregnancy outcomes remains insufficiently addressed in clinical practice. This position statement aims to synthesise available evidence and provide expert guidance on the management of reproductive health in both male and female patients with NENs. Current data suggest that both the disease and treatment, including somatostatin analogues, targeted therapies, chemotherapy and peptide receptor radionuclide therapy, may affect gonadal function and sexual health. Fertility preservation strategies should be discussed early, particularly in younger patients undergoing potentially gonadotoxic treatments. Sexual dysfunction, often under-reported, may result from secretory syndromes, treatment side-effects or psychosocial factors, and warrants proactive assessment and multidisciplinary management. Pregnancy in patients with NENs is feasible in selected cases but requires careful planning and close monitoring due to potential risks related to tumour behaviour and treatment exposure. The available evidence is limited and largely based on small series, highlighting the need for individualised decision-making. This statement emphasises the importance of integrating reproductive counselling into routine care, and promoting collaboration among NEN physicians, reproductive specialists, and other healthcare professionals to improve patient-centred outcomes.

articles.title: Dry eye disease in women with polycystic ovary syndrome: the role of meibomian gland dysfunction and underlying mechanisms.
articles.authors: Bomze Z, Babik K, Nowinska A et al.
articles.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a common endocrine disorder that may be associated not only with reproductive and metabolic disturbances but also with ocular surface abnormalities, particularly dry eye disease (DED). Current evidence indicates that women with PCOS may exhibit structural and functional alterations of the meibomian glands, including gland loss, ductal abnormalities, and impaired lipid secretion, potentially contributing to tear film instability. Reduced tear break-up time (TBUT) is consistently reported, whereas Schirmer test results are often preserved, suggesting a predominantly evaporative dry eye phenotype. Hormonal imbalance, particularly hyperandrogenism, may play a complex and incompletely understood role in ocular surface homeostasis and could contribute to gland dysfunction. Furthermore, insulin resistance may impair meibomian gland metabolism, promote oxidative stress, and accelerate glandular atrophy. Chronic low-grade systemic inflammation has also been implicated and may further exacerbate ocular surface damage. The interaction of hormonal, metabolic, and inflammatory factors may increase the risk of DED in women with PCOS; however, the available evidence remains limited and heterogeneous. Further well-designed studies are required to clarify underlying mechanisms and support the development of targeted multidisciplinary management strategies.

articles.title: Sexual, Pharmaceutical, and Lifestyle Variables in a Cohort of Pregnant Western Australian Women, and Their Association With Detection of Vaginal Microorganisms and Preterm Birth.
articles.journal: The Australian & New Zealand journal of obstetrics & gynaecology
articles.ta: Aust N Z J Obstet Gynaecol
articles.authors: Payne MS, Doherty DA, Furfaro LL et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The vaginal microbiome is shaped by factors such as sexual behaviour, smoking, and feminine hygiene practices. Although these associations are well documented in non-pregnant women, less is known in pregnancy, particularly in Australia, despite links between the vaginal microbiome and complications like preterm birth (PTB).
AIM: To document sexual, pharmaceutical, and lifestyle variables in pregnant Australian women and examine their associations with vaginal microorganisms and, secondarily, PTB risk.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: Mid-pregnancy (12-23 weeks' gestation) vaginal swabs from 936 women in the Predict1000 study were analysed for key microorganisms using qPCR. Participants completed a recruitment survey on medication use, urinary/vaginal infections, smoking, alcohol use, sexual practices, and vaginal douching. Associations between these factors, PTB (spontaneous and indicated), and specific microorganisms were assessed using Chi-square, Fisher's exact, and Mann-Whitney tests.
RESULTS: Thirteen percent of women reported smoking during pregnancy. Over half reported vaginal intercourse 1-2 times per week, although one quarter reported none. Thirty-two percent engaged in other sexual activities, most commonly oral sex (25%), followed by use of sex toys (11%). Vaginal douching was uncommon (3%). Sexual behaviour and douching were not associated with PTB risk. Smoking was associated with increased rates of non-optimal microbes, an association that persisted after correction for multiple comparisons. Associations between reduced frequency of vaginal intercourse (< 2 times/week) and lower prevalence of non-optimal vaginal microbes, and between douching and higher detection of Gardnerella vaginalis and Ureaplasma parvum, were also observed but did not remain significant after correction.
CONCLUSION: Sexual, pharmaceutical, and lifestyle factors influenced the vaginal microbiota in pregnancy, but none were associated with PTB risk.

articles.title: Inositol for infertile women with polycystic ovary syndrome.
articles.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
articles.authors: Vercoe MA, Rodenburg C, Mackenzie-Proctor R et al.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: This is an update of a previously published review. Women with infertility may use adjunctive therapies to improve reproductive outcomes. Myo-inositol and D-chiro-inositol are dietary supplements widely available and commonly used by women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS; renamed polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) in May 2026). The use of inositol for women with PCOS and infertility is based on proposed effects on insulin sensitivity and ovarian function. In clinical practice, myo-inositol is frequently prescribed for women with PCOS undergoing ovulation induction/intrauterine insemination or before in vitro fertilisation (IVF). However, the quality and certainty of the evidence supporting this practice remains unclear. This review aimed to assess the benefits and harms of inositol (including myo-inositol and D-chiro-inositol) in women with PCOS experiencing infertility.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the benefits and harms of inositol oral supplementation for reproductive outcomes among women with polycystic ovary syndrome experiencing infertility.
SEARCH METHODS: We searched CENTRAL (which includes trial registries), the Cochrane Gynaecology and Fertility Group Specialised Register, MEDLINE, Embase, PsycINFO, AMED, and Epistemonikos to 10 November 2025. We also checked reference lists and contacted experts in the field for any additional trials.
ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included randomised controlled trials (RCTs) that compared any type, dose, or combination of oral inositol versus placebo, no treatment, or another active intervention in women with PCOS and infertility. Trials that compared different types of inositol were also eligible.
OUTCOMES: Our critical outcomes were live birth and any adverse event (including miscarriage, multiple pregnancy, and ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS)), as reported by trial investigators. Our important outcomes were clinical pregnancy and gestational diabetes.
RISK OF BIAS: We assessed risk of bias using the Cochrane RoB 1 tool.
SYNTHESIS METHODS: Two review authors independently selected eligible studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias. We pooled studies using a fixed-effect model, and calculated odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). We assessed the overall certainty of evidence by applying…
REGISTRATION: Protocol (2016) available at https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD012378. Previous review (2018) available at https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD012378.pub2.

articles.title: Patterns of Care in Patients With Cervical Cancer in Western Australia: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: The Australian & New Zealand journal of obstetrics & gynaecology
articles.ta: Aust N Z J Obstet Gynaecol
articles.authors: Mannolini K, Nathan E, Leung Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer is an important public health concern with underserved populations having higher incidence and mortality.
AIMS: To examine associations between patient and tumour characteristics, receipt of appropriate treatment and survival.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of cervical cancer patients managed by the Western Australian Gynaecological Cancer Service from 1 January 2009 to 31 December 2018. Appropriate treatment was defined by international guidelines. Univariable and multivariable analyses assessed associations between demographic and tumour factors and receipt of appropriate treatment. Survival outcomes were evaluated using multivariable Cox regression.
RESULTS: Of 526 patients included, 95.4% received treatment, of which 94.4% received appropriate treatment. Non-English-speaking patients had reduced odds of completing treatment (OR 0.28, 95% CI 0.10-0.80, p = 0.018), and patients of lower socioeconomic status had reduced odds of timely treatment (OR 0.57, 95% CI 0.35-0.93, p = 0.025). Patients aged over 60 years had lower odds of receiving any, complete and timely treatment. Those diagnosed between 2014 and 2018, versus 2009-2013 had increased odds of completing treatment (OR 3.08, 95% CI 1.45-6.45, p = 0.003). Higher disease stage was associated with lower odds of receiving and completing treatment. Overall- and disease-free survival were poorer among patients aged over 60, those with advanced-stage disease, those diagnosed in 2009-2013, and those who received incomplete treatment or no treatment.
CONCLUSIONS: Most patients received appropriate treatment. Non-English-speaking patients, older patients, and those of low socioeconomic status were less likely to receive appropriate care. Older age, advanced disease stage, diagnosis in 2009-2013, and incomplete treatment were associated with poorer survival.

articles.title: Misdiagnosed as a Urinary Tract Infection: A Rare Presentation of Advanced Vulval Carcinoma with Urinary Symptoms and Introital Obliteration in an Octogenarian.
articles.authors: Sarwade A, Sharma SV, Kolate D
articles.abstract: Vulval carcinoma is an uncommon but clinically significant gynecological malignancy that disproportionately affects elderly postmenopausal women. Diagnosis is frequently delayed because of atypical presenting complaints, social stigma surrounding genital examination, and the tendency to attribute symptoms to more benign urological conditions. We describe an 82-year-old multiparous woman (para 8, living 8) with a 30-year history of menopause who was initially managed elsewhere for a presumed urinary tract infection before being referred to our department. She presented with a 3-month history of progressive burning micturition and perineal pain. Examination revealed a fungating right labial mass with seropurulent discharge, complete obliteration of the introitus, and bilateral inguinal lymphadenopathy. Per-rectal examination confirmed posterior vaginal wall fixity. Punch biopsy of the lesion demonstrated well-differentiated squamous cell carcinoma. Staging workup classified the disease as FIGO Stage IIIC. The patient was referred for multimodal oncological management. This case illustrates that urinary symptoms in elderly women warrant thorough genital examination to exclude vulval malignancy. A high index of clinical suspicion, early biopsy, and prompt oncological referral are essential to improving outcomes in this vulnerable population.

articles.title: Patient Perceptions of Clinician Attire in the Outpatient Urogynecology Clinic.
articles.authors: Chong W, Gencerliler N, DiDominica M
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Clinician attire is a visible, nonverbal component of the clinical encounter that influences patient perception. Understanding its effect in sensitive subspecialties like urogynecology provides actionable insights for clinical communication.
OBJECTIVE: This study evaluated how clinician attire influences patient perceptions of professionalism, friendliness, aptitude, and empathy within an outpatient urogynecology setting.
STUDY DESIGN: In this single-center, cross-sectional survey, adult female patients rated 4 standardized, artificial intelligence-generated photographs of a gender-neutral model wearing (1) formal attire, (2) formal attire with a white coat, (3) scrubs, and (4) scrubs with a white coat. Participants used a 5-point Likert scale to assess each image across the 4 domains. Data were analyzed using 1-way repeated-measures analysis of variance and mixed-effects linear regression models to assess the independent and interactive effects of scrubs and white-coat use.
RESULTS: A total of 222 participants completed the survey. Clinician attire significantly influenced all 4 perception domains (P<0.001). Formal attire without a white coat was consistently rated the lowest. Formal attire with a white coat received the highest ratings for professionalism and aptitude, whereas scrubs scored highest for friendliness and empathy. Mixed-effects models demonstrated that white coats independently correlated with higher ratings across all domains. Conversely, although scrubs were associated with higher perceived friendliness, empathy, and aptitude, they resulted in slightly lower professionalism ratings compared with formal attire. A negative interaction term indicated that the white coat's positive effect was attenuated when paired with scrubs.
CONCLUSIONS: Clinician attire significantly shapes patient perceptions in urogynecology. Although white coats bolster perceived professionalism and aptitude, scrubs enhance friendliness and empathy. Attire is a modifiable factor that clinicians can strategically align with the goals of specific encounters.

articles.title: Pedagogical assessment of an online nursing course on advanced practice in promoting childhood continence.
articles.authors: Rodrigues NDS, Coelho MMF, Martins G
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: to assess the pedagogical structure and content validity evidence of an online course on Advanced Practice Nursing in promoting infant continence.
METHODS: a methodological study for content assessment with the participation of 14 experts using the Educational Content Validity Instrument in Health. Data were analyzed using R 4.2.2 software, applying the Friedman and Kruskal-Wallis tests and calculating the Content Validity Coefficient and the Content Validity Index.
RESULTS: the course demonstrated high pedagogical validity and overall consistency across the instrument's domains, with an average score of 96.2% and expert assessments above the 80% cut-off point, demonstrating the robustness and practical applicability of the educational material.
CONCLUSIONS: the course demonstrated validity and relevance, establishing itself as an effective educational strategy for training nursing students in promoting infant continence.

articles.title: Male infertility disclosure on Reddit: a study of emotional expression, information exchange, and peer support.
articles.authors: Khatun M, Patel N, Loid M et al.
articles.abstract: Infertility imposes significant psychological and social burdens on both women and men. However, research on infertility communication has predominantly focused on women, leaving discussions of male infertility (MI) relatively underexplored. This study investigates MI-related communication within the r/maleinfertility subreddit on Reddit. Using natural language processing, we analysed 10,769 posts and 80,381 comments published between 2013 and 2025, examining sentiment, emotion, topic structure, hyperlink networks, and discussions surrounding diagnostic testing, treatment decisions, and donor sperm. Topic modelling revealed distinct communication functions. Posts primarily focused on clinical sense-making, including interpretation of semen analysis results, hormonal testing, and assisted reproduction decisions, whereas comments emphasised emotional support, experiential guidance, and alternative reproductive pathways. Emotional expression varied across topics, with heightened fear and sadness in discussions involving genetic testing, surgical sperm retrieval, and donor sperm. Hyperlink analysis revealed frequent references to peer-reviewed medical literature, suggesting active evidence-seeking behaviour. These findings highlight the role of online peer communities in providing emotional support and facilitating information exchange about MI. Such communities may complement clinical care by helping individuals interpret diagnoses, manage emotional distress, and navigate treatment and donor-related decisions.

articles.title: Environmentally Relevant F-53B Exposure Triggers Ovarian Cancer Progression via C5aR1-Mediated Noncanonical Signaling: An Adverse Outcome Pathway (AOP) Underlying Hybrid EMT and Stemness.
articles.authors: Dong S, Wang Y, Fang S et al.
articles.abstract: Significant gaps remain in the health risk assessment methodologies for the PFOS (perfluorooctanesulfonic acid) alternative 6:2 Cl-PFESA (6:2 chlorinated polyfluoroalkyl ether sulfonate, F-53B), which has been widely recognized as the alternative to PFOS in China. To address this research gap, our study integrated multidimensional techniques to mechanistically construct an Adverse Outcome Pathway (AOP) for F-53B-induced ovarian cancer progression. Our findings demonstrated that exposure to environmentally relevant concentrations of F-53B significantly enhanced the migratory and invasive capabilities of ovarian cancer cells. Within the AOP framework of F-53B-induced hybrid epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and enhanced tumor stemness, the upregulation of C5aR1─triggered by ERα acting as a noncanonical receptor of F-53B─constitutes the molecular initiating event (MIE). Following this MIE, the recruitment of β-arrestin1 and Src was induced, leading to the assembly of a C5aR1/β-arrestin1/Src signaling complex. This complex facilitated the binding of β-arrestin1 to β-catenin and drove the nuclear translocation of β-catenin, ultimately activating hybrid EMT and stemness of tumor cells. Administration of the C5aR1 inhibitor PMX205 effectively abrogated subsequent key events (KEs) caused by F-53B exposure. Through in vitro and in vivo validation, our study established an AOP framework that provides a novel perspective for evaluating the potential risk of PFAS substitutes in promoting cancer progression.

articles.title: Evaluating Evidence for Causal Relationships and Transcriptomic Overlap Between Polycystic Ovary Syndrome and Diabetic Nephropathy: A Bidirectional Mendelian Randomization and Cross-Dataset Transcriptomic Study.
articles.authors: Zhang Y, Li P, Chen X et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and diabetic nephropathy (DN) share metabolic and inflammatory features, but direct causality and reproducible molecular overlap remain uncertain.
METHODS: We reassessed bidirectional summary-data Mendelian randomization (MR) for two FinnGen phenotypes and analyzed 11 disease-control transcriptomic contrasts from nine public GEO accessions. Inverse-variance-weighted (IVW) MR was primary, with correction for two directional hypotheses and sensitivity analyses. Dataset-specific limma models accounted for donor dependence, available covariates, PCOS weight strata, and shared controls. All 50 Hallmark gene sets were tested with correlation-adjusted mean rank (CAMERA), and two programs were examined with mroast as a method-sensitivity analysis. Three genes from an archived public GEO candidate list (C3, HLA-DPA1, IGFBP3) were reevaluated as a fixed exploratory candidate set without further feature selection.
RESULTS: DN liability showed a nominal IVW association with PCOS (11 variants; odds ratio 1.190, 95% confidence interval 1.007-1.406; p = 0.041) that did not survive correction for two directions (adjusted p = 0.082), and the reverse estimate was null. CAMERA identified interferon-gamma and inflammatory-response programs at false discovery rate (FDR) < 0.05 in 6 of 11 contrasts for each program, but only four of eight source-study units supported each program under a stricter within-source rule; mroast supported 2 and 4 of 11 contrasts, respectively.No gene reached FDR < 0.05 in GSE80432, and none of the three exploratory candidates showed FDR-significant support in the three additional PCOS accessions.
CONCLUSIONS: The analyzed data do not establish a multiplicity-adjusted causal PCOS-DN relationship or a reproducible shared single-gene marker. The MR analysis was limited by small instrument counts and unquantified FinnGen sample overlap, precluding causal confirmation. Immune-inflammatory activity recurred in several datasets, but its support depended on cohort and gene-set method and should be considered hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: Fertility Treatment with Ovulation Induction or Intrauterine Insemination and the Risk of Cerebral Palsy in Offspring.
articles.authors: Kettner LO, Henriksen TB, Kesmodel US et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate the association between ovulation induction or intrauterine insemination and cerebral palsy in offspring, and to examine the potential mechanisms underlying an association, including specific treatment regimens, mediation by preterm birth, confounding by indication, and the association with specific subtypes of cerebral palsy.
METHODS: This nationwide cohort study included all liveborn, singleton children in Denmark conceived from July 1995 and born before January 2017. The children were followed until March 2022. Children conceived after ovulation induction or intrauterine insemination were identified from redeemed prescriptions for the specific hormones used for these treatments, recorded in the Danish National Prescription Registry. Children with cerebral palsy were identified from the Danish Cerebral Palsy Registry and the Danish Cerebral Palsy Follow-up Program.
RESULTS: The study included 1,231,058 singleton children; 47,017 children were conceived after ovulation induction or intrauterine insemination, and 2,104 children were diagnosed with cerebral palsy. Children conceived after ovulation induction or intrauterine insemination had an increased risk of cerebral palsy compared to spontaneously conceived children (adjusted odds ratio (aOR): 1.36; 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.11-1.66). The point estimate remained similar in a sibling analysis. The risk was primarily related to the use of clomiphene citrate (aOR: 1.44; 95% CI: 1.16-1.80). A mediation analysis showed that most of the increased risk was statistically mediated by prematurity and antecedent factors (proportion eliminated: 87%; 95% CI: 36-137%). In line with this, the risk was highest for spastic bilateral cerebral palsy (aOR: 1.76; 95% CI: 1.33-2.34), severe motor impairment (aOR: 1.66; 95% CI: 1.17-2.35), and for cerebral white matter lesions (aOR: 1.70; 95% CI: 1.24-2.33).
CONCLUSION: Ovulation induction or intrauterine insemination was associated with an increased risk of cerebral palsy in offspring. The risk was related to treatment with clomiphene citrate, and most of the increased risk was statistically mediated by prematurity and antecedent factors.

articles.title: Maternal thyroid status and immune adaptation at the maternal-fetal interface: distinguishing direct from indirect pathways.
articles.authors: Ma H, Qin J
articles.abstract: Pregnancy depends on coordinated endocrine and immune adaptation to support fetal tolerance, antimicrobial defense, trophoblast invasion, and vascular remodeling. Maternal thyroid dysfunction is associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, but serum thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) and free thyroxine (FT4) do not define T4/T3 exposure in placental or decidual cells. This Mini Review examines direct and indirect immune pathways, distinguishing maternal thyroid status from local thyroid hormone (TH) transport and metabolism, receptor-dependent signaling, and thyroid autoimmunity. Placental hormone handling has the strongest experimental support: MCT8/MCT10 and DIO2/DIO3 regulate local availability, although much of the transport evidence comes from term placentas. Human trophoblast and endometrial or decidual stromal studies suggest context-dependent effects on decidualization and trophoblast behavior. These responses could affect immune adaptation indirectly through changes in the immune, metabolic, and vascular niche. Evidence for direct TH effects on uterine natural killer (uNK) cells and decidual macrophages remains limited and gestational-age dependent. Direct evidence for decidual regulatory or effector T cells and dendritic cells is lacking, and many proposed mechanisms come from animal or nonpregnant settings. The available data do not support a single TH-driven immune phenotype or establish whether maternal thyroid status acts mainly through immune cells or surrounding tissues. Studies combining paired blood and interface tissue, longitudinal sampling, local T3/T4 measurements, pathway-specific perturbation, and human multicellular models are needed to test both routes and connect hormone supply and metabolism with immune and vascular function. Thyroid autoimmunity should be analyzed separately from local TH receptor signaling.

articles.title: Prevalence and Predictors of Intrauterine Device Failure Among Women in Sub-Saharan Africa: A Scoping Review.
articles.authors: Nanyiri J
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although highly effective in unintended pregnancy prevention, intrauterine device uptake remains perennially low in sub-Saharan Africa, partly due to the perceived risk of device failure, whose prevalence and predictors remain poorly understood in the sub-regional context.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the prevalence and predictors of intrauterine device failure (IUDF) in women in sub-Saharan Africa.
METHODS: A scoping review approach was used, with comprehensive searches conducted in ten databases: ProQuest, EBSCO, PubMed, ScienceDirect, MEDLINE, Ovid EMBASE, CINAHL, PsycINFO, Web of Science, and Google Scholar. The search was guided by article saturation to minimize duplication. The Population (P), concept (C), and context (C) approaches were used to set the eligibility criteria, and data were analyzed using descriptive frequency counting and content analysis.
RESULTS: Of the 51 studies identified through the search strategy, only six full-text articles met the eligibility criteria. Only five of these studies quantified the prevalence of Intrauterine Device (IUD) failure, which ranged from 0.2% to 7.4%, with the highest reported in Ethiopia. Only three studies reported predictors of IUD failure, including nationality, increasing parity, mispositioning during insertion, small uterine cavity, and IUD fitting by less experienced healthcare workers.
CONCLUSION: Over the past 10 years, very few studies in sub-Saharan Africa have credibly estimated the prevalence of IUD failure or identified predictors of IUD failure. Only six studies made such an attempt; however, none were designed with methodological rigor to allow credible quantification of the prevalence of IUD failure. Although all six studies included IUD failure as an outcome, none explicitly examined the predictors of IUD failure. Nonetheless, the few available studies indicate that IUD failure is a reality, with significant variation across regions ranging from 0.2% to 7.4%. Both intrapersonal and service provision characteristics predict IUD failure, with the service provision factors taking precedence.

articles.title: Effects of a preconception lifestyle intervention on cardiorespiratory fitness and glycaemic outcomes in people with increased risk of gestational diabetes: secondary findings from the BEFORE THE BEGINNING randomised controlled trial.
articles.authors: Sujan MAJ, Skarstad HMS, Rosvold G et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Obesity rates are rising globally, and many females of reproductive age are physically inactive, which may adversely affect future maternal and neonatal health. In this secondary analysis, we investigated the effect of a combined preconception lifestyle intervention on cardiorespiratory fitness and glycaemic outcomes after 7 weeks.
METHODS: This article reports analyses of secondary outcomes from the BEFORE THE BEGINNING randomised controlled trial, in which we randomised females who were planning pregnancy, at risk of gestational diabetes mellitus and did not have diagnosed diabetes 1:1 to intervention or control. The intervention consisted of time-restricted eating (TRE) and exercise training and spanned from preconception throughout pregnancy. TRE involved restricting energy intake to ≤10 hour/day on ≥5 days per week. Exercise volume was based on a heart-rate-based metric (Personal Activity Intelligence, PAI), with the goal of ≥100 weekly PAI-points. The main outcomes of interest in this secondary analysis were cardiorespiratory fitness and glycaemic outcomes after 7 weeks of intervention in the preconception period.
RESULTS: Among 167 randomised participants, we included 166 in the intention-to-treat analysis. After 7 weeks of preconception intervention, there was no significant between-group difference in relative peak oxygen uptake (0.8 mL·kg-1·min-1; 95% CI -0.2 to 1.9, p=0.10) or glucose area under the curve (0.0 mmol·hour/L; 95% CI -0.1 to 0.2, p=0.76).
CONCLUSION: 7 weeks of preconception TRE combined with exercise training did not result in statistically significant improvements in cardiorespiratory fitness or glycaemic outcomes in people with increased risk of gestational diabetes.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT04585581.

articles.title: Literature-Derived Network and Semantic Mapping of Pain Catastrophizing and Traditional East Asian Medicine Pattern Constructs.
articles.authors: Kim TY, Kim JH, Kim JH
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Pain catastrophizing comprises rumination, magnification, and helplessness. Different medical traditions may describe neighboring cognitive, affective, somatic, and functional domains using different vocabularies. We characterized literature-derived conceptual proximity between pain-catastrophizing subdomains and traditional East Asian medicine pattern constructs without treating proximity as diagnostic or clinical correspondence.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: PubMed, PubMed Central, and OASIS were accessed on June 5, 2026. The final analysis was restricted to 2259 PubMed Central-retrieved full-text records; 2214 met corpus criteria. Three pain-catastrophizing subdomains and 14 traditional East Asian medicine pattern constructs formed 42 candidate pairs, of which 24 were graph connected and 18 unconnected. The primary mapping score combined semantic similarity, a graph-derived weighted common-neighbor component, and binary graph proximity. Peer-review-requested validation quantified pattern- versus subdomain-level score variation, used 10,000 constrained permutations, and evaluated a node-strength-normalized common-neighbor sensitivity.
RESULTS: Pattern construct accounted for 99.91% of total primary-score variation, compared with 0.04% for pain-catastrophizing subdomain. Across the 24 connected pairs, 129 shortest two-edge paths involved six intermediate nodes rather than a single bridge. In the constrained null analysis, the maximum observed score was not unusually extreme (empirical p=0.0831), whereas the mean of the five highest scores (p=0.0024) and the concentration of variance by pattern construct (p<0.001) exceeded null expectations. Node-strength normalization changed the highest-ranked pattern construct from phlegm-related to dampness; adjusted and primary ranks remained correlated (Spearman rho=0.9509), but top-five overlap was 2 of 5.
CONCLUSION: The analysis identified a pattern-dominant, literature-conditioned structure rather than strongly pair-specific mappings. Results were sensitive to graph-strength normalization. They characterize conceptual proximity in published texts and graph structure; they do not establish diagnostic equivalence, clinical validity, causality, treatment efficacy, or treatment guidance.

articles.title: Research priorities for sexual and reproductive health, equity, and access in a post-Roe context.
articles.authors: DeCosta D, Desai S, Malcolm N et al.
articles.abstract: Since the 2022 U.S. Supreme Court ruling in Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization, state-level laws governing health care provision and access have increased. While the current legal landscape has devastating consequences for abortion, evidence suggests ripple effects on sexual and reproductive health (SRH) care and equity broadly. A coordinated, robust body of research is needed to understand, anticipate, and respond to the far-reaching consequences of this ruling. This commentary brings together perspectives from the SRH and health services fields to present six research priorities that researchers, funders, policymakers, and advocates can leverage to advance SRH care access and equity.

articles.title: Sleep duration and anti-müllerian hormone levels in female firefighters.
articles.authors: Baker JA, Valenti M, Farland LV et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the relationship between anti-müllerian hormone (AMH) levels and sleep duration in female firefighters.
STUDY DESIGN: We used baseline data collected at time of enrollment into the Women Firefighter Study, part of the Fire Fighter Cancer Cohort Study (FFCCS), including demographic information, reproductive history, and self-reported average off-duty sleep, along with serum AMH concentration.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE: We used linear regression models to estimate the association between off-duty sleep duration (categorized by <7 hours and ≥ 7 hours on average) and log transformed AMH. We adjusted for age (continuous and squared), body mass index (BMI), and oral contraception use. The formula (exp (  β ^   )-1)*100 was used to calculate the percent difference in AMH values.
RESULTS: Among 566 participants, those that reported <7 hours of sleep while off-duty had statistically significantly lower AMH levels compared to those who reported ≥ 7 hours of off-duty sleep (-18.0 %, 95% confidence interval [CI]: -32.7, -0.2).
CONCLUSION: Less than 7 hours of off-duty sleep was associated with lower AMH levels. Increasing off-duty sleep is a potential modifiable risk factor to benefit reproductive health in female firefighters.

articles.title: Normative Distal Radius Radiological Measurements: The Influence of Age, Gender, and Menopause.
articles.journal: Clinical medicine insights. Arthritis and musculoskeletal disorders
articles.ta: Clin Med Insights Arthritis Musculoskelet Disord
articles.authors: Oulianski M, Yehuda OB, Jammal M et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Distal radius fractures are prevalent, with management dependent on accurate radiological assessment. Most morphologic reference values derive from Western cohorts, raising questions about their generalizability. This study established reference distal radius radiological parameters in the Israeli population derived from emergency department patients with non-fractured wrist injuries and explored the effects of age, gender, and menopause.
METHODS: A retrospective review included adults with wrist contusions at an Israeli emergency department. Exclusions were prior fractures, surgery, or poor radiographs. Standardized anteroposterior and lateral wrist radiographs were reviewed for 6 parameters: radial height, inclination, radiocarpal angle, volar angulation, volar tilt, and ulnar variance, measured twice by a blinded observer (intraclass correlation coefficient, 0.92-0.98). Stratification by age and gender used 50 years as a menopause proxy. Statistical analysis included t tests (Bonferroni correction, α = 0.010) and effect sizes.
RESULTS: Of 585 patients, 466 met criteria (mean age, 45 years; 40.6% female). Mean values were 13.4 mm for radial height, 25.4° for inclination, 11.6° for radiocarpal angle, 145.1° for volar angulation, and 17.1° for volar tilt. Radial height was significantly greater in males than in females (P < .001). Ulnar variance was neutral in 69.5%, negative in 17.8%, and positive in 12.7%. Volar angulation declined significantly with age in women, especially post-menopause (P < .01), but not in men.
CONCLUSIONS: Distal radius morphology in Israelis aligns with international norms. Age-stratified differences in volar angulation among women over 50, which may reflect menopausal bone remodeling, indicate that both age and sex should be incorporated into individualized assessments. In the management of distal radius fractures in postmenopausal women, baseline volar angulation is approximately 3° lower than in younger women, a factor that may influence reduction targets.

articles.title: Research progress of artificial intelligence applications in obstetrics.
articles.authors: Zhang L, Liu Y, Zhao Y et al.
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being applied across obstetrics, with applications spanning electronic medical record analysis, prenatal ultrasound, fetal monitoring, prediction of pregnancy complications, labor management, postpartum care, and telemedicine. The evidence reviewed in this article indicates that AI can improve automated information extraction, image and signal interpretation, and risk discrimination across multiple obstetric tasks, with particularly consistent advances in fetal ultrasound analysis, cardiotocography (CTG) interpretation, and early prediction of gestational diabetes, preeclampsia, and preterm birth. However, model performance is heterogeneous and is often reported using discrimination or classification metrics rather than patient-centered clinical outcomes. In CTG research, models differ substantially in whether they classify interpretation categories, detect fetal hypoxia or acidemia, or predict neonatal outcomes, making direct comparison difficult. Similarly, high predictive accuracy for pregnancy complications does not establish that AI implementation itself improves maternal or neonatal outcomes, and the clinical benefit of treatment should not be attributed to the predictive model without intervention studies. Across obstetric applications, limited external validation, dataset shift, class imbalance, calibration, interpretability, workflow integration, and data governance remain major barriers to clinical translation. This review therefore emphasizes the distinction between technical model performance and demonstrated clinical utility, and highlights the evidence required to move AI applications from retrospective development toward prospective, clinically integrated obstetric care.

articles.title: Endometrial Testing and Immune Therapy Evaluation in Recurrent Implantation Failure After Euploid Embryo Transfer.
articles.authors: Ikhsan M, Jahan U, SenGupta S et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Recurrent implantation failure (RIF) can occur despite transfer of chromosomally euploid embryos, suggesting non-embryonic factors. This retrospective study evaluated the impact of endometrial testing and immunomodulatory therapy on live birth outcomes in women with RIF.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: A single-centre retrospective cohort study was conducted at the Centre for Reproductive and Genetic Health (CRGH), London (2017-2024). Women <45 years with ≥2 failed euploid blastocyst transfers were included. Participants were grouped into those receiving endometrial investigation and/or immunomodulatory therapy vs no investigation/intervention. The primary outcome was live birth per patient. Logistic regression analyses identified predictors of live birth.
RESULTS: From 3445 euploid embryos transferred, seventy-eight women enrolled (59 investigation/immunomodulatory group, 19 no investigation/intervention). Live birth rates were not statistically different between the investigation/immunomodulatory group and the control group (42.3% vs 26.3%, p=0.211). Multivariable analysis showed intralipid therapy was independently associated with higher live birth odds (aOR 4.528, 95% CI 1.337-15.332, p = 0.015). Although the bootstrap resampling find a wider bias-corrected and accelerated (BCa) 95% CI for this association (0.931-76.861). Endometrial tests (ERA, EMMA, ALICE) were not independently associated. The model showed good discrimination (AUC = 0.804).
CONCLUSION: Intralipid therapy was associated with improved live birth in RIF after failed 2 consecutive euploid embryo transfers, while endometrial testing showed no significant independent effect. The small retrospective cohort and the intralipid association are exploratory, hence susceptible to confounding and model instability.

articles.title: Interplay of Insulin Resistance, Hyperandrogenism, and Obesity in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: Pathogenesis and Therapeutic Insights.
articles.journal: Diabetes, metabolic syndrome and obesity : targets and therapy
articles.authors: Bao F, Sun L, Guo W
articles.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a complex disorder of ovarian dysfunction primarily driven by a self-perpetuating pathophysiological cycle. This network centrally involves the interplay of insulin resistance (IR), hyperandrogenism, and obesity. IR stimulates ovarian and adrenal androgen production and can promote increased food intake. The resulting hyperandrogenemia, in turn, exacerbates insulin resistance and contributes to obesity. Furthermore, obesity worsens both IR and hormonal dysregulation through the release of inflammatory cytokines and adipokines, thereby reinforcing the entire cycle. This narrative review aims to critically examine the core pathological interplay between IR, hyperandrogenism, and obesity in PCOS. Building on this foundation, the review systematically explores the rationale and emerging evidence for novel therapeutic strategies that target these key components, moving beyond the established framework of current treatments. Lifestyle interventions, including dietary modification and physical activity, remain the cornerstone of PCOS management, particularly for overweight and obese patients. Current PCOS management primarily relies on oral contraceptives for symptomatic control of hyperandrogenism. Insulin-sensitizing agents form the other pillar of therapy. While metformin is widely used, newer classes of antidiabetic drug-including Dipeptidyl peptidase 4 inhibitors, sodium-glucose co-transporter protein 2 inhibitors, and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists-have demonstrated potential benefits that extend beyond glycemic control, offering improvements in weight, insulin sensitivity, and androgen levels. The discussion also extends to future perspectives, evaluating investigational approaches such as stem cell therapy and aldo-keto reductase 3 inhibitors, which, though not yet part of clinical practice, may represent future targeted treatment avenues. The management of PCOS is evolving from a symptomatic approach towards a more pathophysiologically-targeted and personalized strategy. A deep understanding of the IR-hyperandrogenism-obesity cycle is crucial for developing and implementing these novel therapies, which hold promise for improving long-term reproductive, metabolic, and cardiovascular outcomes for patients with PCOS. Future research should focus on validating these emerging treatments through robust clinical trials and defining their place within individualized treatment algorithms.

articles.title: Semicurative Radiation Therapy for Cervical Cancer in a Nonagenarian: A Case Report and Literature Review.
articles.journal: Case reports in obstetrics and gynecology
articles.authors: Kusada T, Kinjo M, Oshiro D et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The number of nonagenarians has been increasing globally. However, they are less likely to get specialist consultations. This may be due to the lack of an appropriate treatment method for them and uncertainty about the intensity and range of treatments they need and can tolerate. Radiation therapy (RT) is often administered to older patients, including nonagenarians, and its efficacy and safety have been reported in many studies.
CASE PRESENTATION: We present a literature review and the case of a nonagenarian with cervical cancer who was treated with "semicurative" RT and achieved good treatment outcomes, although the observation period was only 12 months. We defined semicurative RT as RT that is less aggressive than curative RT but more aggressive than palliative RT or no treatment, aiming to control cancer. A 92-year-old woman was diagnosed with International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics Stage IIB cervical squamous cell carcinoma. The patient and her family agreed that she would undergo semicurative RT. After completion of 45 Gy small-pelvis irradiation by external beam RT, tumor shrinkage was observed on magnetic resonance imaging, and her general condition was preserved. Therefore, irradiation at 18 Gy in three fractions was planned for the high-risk clinical target volume comprising the uterine cervix and tumor by brachytherapy. However, the patient experienced fatigue after the second fraction and requested to finish treatment without the last fraction. After treatment, the cervical tumor disappeared without severe late complications related to RT, despite vaginal adhesion, and the patient was able to perform activities of daily living.
CONCLUSION: Semicurative RT may be considered for nonagenarian patients with cervical cancer when their general condition is good and they want high treatment efficacy without severe complications. However, further studies on semicurative RT for this patient population are warranted.

articles.title: The status of preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A) - A critical appraisal.
articles.authors: Orvieto R, Patrizio P, Gleicher N
articles.abstract: Preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A) relies on extended embryo culture and trophectoderm biopsy at the blastocyst stage. Its utility is thus dependent on obtaining an adequate embryo yield and blastulation rates. i.e. before embryos can be evaluated at the blastocyst stage, they must first survive extended culture and reach that stage for biopsy. Maternal age notably influences these parameters, with increased age associated with declining euploidy rates and higher oocyte requirements to obtain euploid blastocysts. This limits PGT-A's applicability in poor-prognosis patients. Moreover, the biological and technical limitations inherent to PGT-A including intra-embryonic mosaicism and chromosomal heterogeneity pose significant challenges to its accuracy and clinical application. Multiple studies have demonstrated discordance between trophectoderm (TE) biopsies and inner cell mass (ICM) chromosomal constitution, raising questions about the reliability of TE biopsies as a surrogate for whole embryo chromosomal status. Several studies also suggest that PGT-A does not universally improve live birth rates and may inadvertently exclude embryos with reproductive potential, especially in patients with few blastocysts. Professional societies, including PGDIS, highlight favorable outcomes but may underemphasize conflicting evidence. Currently, the broad application of PGT-A is not supported, especially in low embryo yield scenarios. Individualized counseling, transparent laboratory reporting, and further prospective trials are essential to define PGT-A's role in modern IVF.

articles.title: The effectiveness of health information systems in supporting early detection and referral pathways for high-risk pregnancies: A systematic review.
articles.authors: Deharja A, Hargono A
articles.abstract: Maternal mortality remains a major public health challenge, particularly in low and middle-income countries, where delayed detection and referral of high-risk pregnancies contribute to preventable complications. This systematic review evaluated the effectiveness of Health Information Systems (HIS) in supporting the early detection and management of high-risk pregnancies through improved referral processes, monitoring, and clinical decision-making. The review followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420250641958). PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect were searched for peer-reviewed English-language empirical studies published between January 2015 and March 2025. Eligible studies evaluated HIS interventions for maternal health or detection and reported outcomes related to early detection, referral effectiveness, clinical decision support or maternal health improvement. Methodological quality was assessed using Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tools. Findings from 19 eligible studies were synthesized narratively according to HIS type. HIS interventions improved early detection accuracy, antenatal follow-up, screening compliance, and clinical decision support. mHealth improved antenatal care adherence, while telemedicine and telemonitoring supported remote monitoring and reduced unnecessary hospitalization. EHR and e-Registries enhanced risk classification, and artificial intelligence models demonstrated promising predictive performance for preeclampsia and other maternal complications. However, the evidence base was limited by heterogeneous study designs, limited direct mortality outcomes, infrastructure constraints, digital literacy gaps, and interoperability challenges. Direct evidence demonstrating reductions in maternal mortality remains limited. HIS can strengthen maternal surveillance, referral pathways, and clinical decision support for high-risk pregnancies. Sustainable impact requires integrated infrastructure, workforce training, effective data governance, and standardized outcome evaluation.
