articles.title: Timeliness of gynecologic oncology care in Kingston, Ontario in 2023: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Merhi RC, Moshi S, Pudwell J et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To quantify intervals from referral-to-treatment for patients with gynecologic cancers at Kingston Health Sciences Centre (KHSC) in Ontario, Canada, compared to published Cancer Care Ontario (CCO) benchmarks, and identify patient-, disease-, and system-level factors associated with treatment delay.
METHODS: Single-centre retrospective cohort study of 144 individuals diagnosed with gynecologic cancer in 2023 at Kington Health Sciences Centre.
RESULTS: Of 144 eligible patients, the median referral-to-treatment interval was 45.5 [35.0-68.0] days. The consult-to-treatment phase accounted for the majority of the delay at 27.0 [20.0-43.8] days, compared with the referral-to-consult interval at 16.0 [12.0-22.0] days. Overall, 70.8% of patients received initial consultation and disposition planning within 21 days of referral, while only 50.0% received or began treatment within 28 days of consultation. Among high-risk cases, 75.0% met referral-to-consult benchmarks, and 50% met consult-to-treatment benchmarks. Treatment delays differed significantly by cancer site (p < 0.025), with the shortest intervals observed in ovarian cancer at 22.0 [14.0-38.0] days, and the longest delays seen in vulvar cancers at 65.0 [37.0-99.0] days. Documented reasons for delay included patient illness, and additional review of pathology or further expert consultation. Referring provider, rurality, symptoms at presentation and cancer grade did not significantly affect wait time segments.
CONCLUSION: KHSC met provincial benchmarks for referral to consultation more frequently than treatment initiation benchmarks. These findings suggest that system level inefficiencies arise primarily after consultation and underscore the need for targeted interventions to improve post-consult care pathways and ensure equitable, timely access to treatment.

articles.title: Glycoursodeoxycholic Acid and Insulin Resistance in Women With Normoandrogenic Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome Undergoing In Vitro Fertilization.
articles.authors: Lv L, Yin X, Zhu T et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To characterize paired serum and follicular fluid (FF) bile acids in normoandrogenic polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (NA-PMOS) and investigate associations of glycoursodeoxycholic acid (GUDCA) with endocrine-metabolic indices and in vitro fertilization (IVF) outcomes.
METHODS: This retrospective case-control study included 20 women with NA-PMOS and 20 age-comparable controls without PMOS undergoing IVF. Fifteen bile acids were measured in serum and FF. Analyses assessed group differences, metabolic and IVF associations, and discrimination between diagnostic groups.
RESULTS: Compared with controls without PMOS, women with NA-PMOS had higher fasting insulin, triglycerides, and triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and a lower high-quality embryo rate. GUDCA was lower in NA-PMOS in FF (137.01 vs. 332.60 nmol/L; p = 0.0004768; q = 0.007152) and serum (31.59 vs. 71.85 nmol/L; p = 0.03022; q = 0.2704). Apparent areas under the curve (AUCs) were 0.849 for FF, 0.713 for serum, and 0.871 for their combination. Serum GUDCA correlated inversely with TyG (ρ = -0.582, p = 0.0028); the association persisted after adjustment for age, BMI, and diagnostic group (β = -0.348, p = 0.0415). Within NA-PMOS, serum GUDCA correlated inversely with fasting insulin and homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR). In the pooled cohort, FF GUDCA correlated inversely with baseline anti-Müllerian hormone, total testosterone, and oocyte counts. GUDCA in neither matrix was significantly associated with high-quality embryo rate.
CONCLUSIONS: Lower GUDCA in serum and FF characterizes this exploratory IVF-based NA-PMOS sample, with stronger between-group evidence in FF. Serum GUDCA was associated with metabolic indices, while FF GUDCA was associated with ovarian characteristics and response. No significant association with high-quality embryo rate was observed. These findings warrant prospective validation.

articles.title: Prevalence of anaemia, associated factors and utilisation of anaemia control interventions among women of reproductive age in rural Kerala: a cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Johny V F, Mangalath SC, Maliakel SF et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anaemia remains a major public health concern among women of reproductive age, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Despite national initiatives in India, including Anaemia Mukt Bharat, the burden of anaemia and utilisation of control interventions vary across settings. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of anaemia and examine its associated factors in a rural area of Kerala.
METHODS: A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 160 women aged 18-49 years in a rural area of Thrissur district, Kerala, between September 2023 and March 2024. A multistage sampling technique was used. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire and haemoglobin was measured using a portable haemoglobinometer. Anaemia was defined according to WHO criteria. Associations were assessed using χ2 tests and multivariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: The prevalence of anaemia was 71.9%, with most cases being moderate (60.0%) and no severe anaemia observed. Younger women (18-24 years) had a higher prevalence. Women aged 25-34 years had lower odds of anaemia compared with those aged 18-24 years (adjusted OR (AOR) 0.08; 95% CI 0.01 to 0.67). Recent anthelminthic intake (AOR 0.30; 95% CI 0.13 to 0.72) and receipt of government iron supplementation (AOR 0.31; 95% CI 0.10 to 0.96) were associated with lower odds. Among recipients, obtaining iron supplementation from primary health centres was associated with lower odds than field-level distribution (AOR 0.14; 95% CI 0.04 to 0.57). Only 40.6% reported using any contraceptive method.
CONCLUSIONS: A high prevalence of anaemia was observed among women of reproductive age in this rural Kerala setting, with younger age, recent anthelminthic intake and government iron supplementation being significantly associated with anaemia status. These findings highlight the need for further research to better understand the utilisation of anaemia control interventions and their relationship with anaemia in similar settings.

articles.title: The modified cardiometabolic index and all-cause mortality in women: Divergent associations by menopausal status (NHANES 1999-2023).
articles.authors: Liu Y, Zhou Y, Niu Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death in women. The menopausal transition confers elevated metabolic risk, but the prognostic value of the Modified Cardiometabolic Index (MCMI) across menopausal stages remains undefined. We hypothesized that elevated MCMI levels would be associated with all-cause mortality risk and that menopausal status might modify this association.
METHODS: We analyzed data from 9,626 women in the 1999-2023 NHANES. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios for all-cause mortality stratified by menopausal status. Sensitivity analyses excluding early deaths and Schoenfeld tests were performed for model validation.
RESULTS: The relationship between MCMI and mortality varied substantially by menopausal status. Among premenopausal women, a 1-unit increase in MCMI was associated with a 49% higher mortality risk. A clear dose-response relationship was noted: the highest MCMI tertile conferred a more than 3-fold higher risk compared with the lowest tertile. In contrast, among postmenopausal women, higher MCMI was associated with relatively lower all-cause mortality hazards after full adjustment. All models satisfied the proportional hazards assumptions and showed no evidence of multicollinearity.
CONCLUSION: MCMI's prognostic role for all-cause mortality Age, race, smoking history, educational level, alcohol intake, physical activity, marital status, PIR, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and cancer were adjusted for in the analysis. These findings support menopausal-stage-specific cardiovascular risk assessment in women.

articles.title: Limosilactobacillus reuteri ameliorates diet-associated metabolic dysfunction in PCOS-like rats: associations with intestinal lipid remodeling and GPR120-related regulation.
articles.authors: Wang C, Li S, Zhai J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a common endocrine-metabolic disorder frequently accompanied by dyslipidemia. However, the relationships among Limosilactobacillus reuteri (L. reuteri) supplementation, gut microbiota-associated lipid remodeling, and PCOS-related metabolic dysfunction remain unclear.
METHODS: A high-fat diet combined with dehydroepiandrosterone-induced PCOS-like rat model (HFHA) was established to evaluate the effects of L. reuteri supplementation. Gut microbiota composition, lipidomic profiles, jejunal GPR120/PPARγ-related molecular markers, and fatty-acid transporter expression were assessed. Potential GPR120-associated involvement was pharmacologically evaluated using AH-7614, with complementary experiments performed in Caco-2 cells.
RESULTS: L. reuteri alleviated high-fat diet-associated metabolic dysfunction, reducing body-weight gain, dyslipidemia, and hepatic steatosis. Formal interaction analyses further supported metabolic-context-dependent effects for several metabolic and endocrine endpoints. L. reuteri supplementation altered gut microbial composition and was associated with increased abundances of colonic fatty-acid features putatively annotated as FA(22:5), FA(24:5), and FA(24:6). These colonic lipid-profile changes occurred alongside increased jejunal GPR120 expression, reduced PPARγ abundance, and lower CD36/FABP2 expression. AH-7614 co-treatment attenuated several metabolic, reproductive, and intestinal effects associated with L. reuteri supplementation. In Caco-2 cells, pharmacological modulation or overexpression of GPR120 reduced FFA-induced CD36 and FABP2 expression and intracellular lipid accumulation, whereas AH-7614 or Barbadin treatment attenuated these responses.
CONCLUSION: L. reuteri improves diet-associated metabolic dysfunction in PCOS-like rats, accompanied by gut microbiota remodeling, altered intestinal lipid profiles, reduced intestinal lipid accumulation, and GPR120-associated regulation of CD36 and FABP2. These findings support a potential role for altered intestinal lipid handling in the metabolic effects of L. reuteri, although the identities, origins, and direct receptor activities of the relevant lipid mediators require further investigation.

articles.title: Feasibility and acceptability of a digital tool for monitoring family planning service quality in Women's routine visits: A mixed method formative pilot study.
articles.authors: Ubuane OI, Baruwa S, Akomolafe TO et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The evolving landscape of family planning (FP) services in Nigeria includes digital tools for monitoring and assessing the quality of care (QoC), along with the broader healthcare system's focus on primary health care (PHC). This transformation is not unique to Nigeria; many countries recognize the crucial and interconnected roles that PHC and QoC play in ensuring access to essential health services, promoting community well-being, and improving health outcomes. This study aims to provide insights into the perceptions and experiences of women utilizing a digital tool to assess the QoC they receive in Nigeria, discuss the challenges faced by users, and their suggestions for improvement.
METHODS: The Digital FP QoC monitoring survey was self-administered by FP clients of Patent and Proprietary Medicine Vendors (PPMVs). Clients were encouraged to take a monitoring survey using QR code scanning. Two focus group discussions with five to ten women from each state were conducted after four weeks of data collection. The transcripts were uploaded and analyzed using the NVivo version R software.
RESULTS: The women's perceptions of the digital tool were overwhelmingly positive. Most women expressed that the survey questions were clear and easy to understand. Almost all women reported challenges with device compatibility and a lack of Internet data/network, highlighting the potential barriers faced by women in different regions, especially those in rural areas.
CONCLUSION: This study underscores the significance of healthcare provider support, user-friendly design, and the need for a balanced approach that considers the preferences and challenges faced by women from different demographic groups and regions.

articles.title: Standardized botanical blend for vasomotor and nonvasomotor menopause symptoms: A decentralized open label trial.
articles.authors: Lederman S, Minkin MJ, Nachtigall L et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterize changes in vasomotor, sleep, musculoskeletal, and psychological symptoms of menopause during treatment with a standardized botanical blend (SBB).
METHODS: This decentralized open label trial of SBB was performed in the United States between May and December 2024. The SBB contains curcumin, green tea extract, and phycocyanin, and reduces hypothalamic neurokinin B signaling in animal models. Perimenopausal or postmenopausal women experiencing ≥5 moderate-to-severe hot flashes (HF) daily received SBB for 12 weeks. Vasomotor symptoms were assessed using daily HF diaries and the Hot Flash Related Daily Interference Scale (HFRDIS). Sleep was evaluated using the PROMIS Sleep Disturbance (PROMIS-SD) short form (SF-8b). Psychological symptoms and quality of life were assessed with the Menopause Rating Scale (MRS), Greene Climacteric Scale (GCS), and MENQOL. Musculoskeletal symptoms were captured with an exploratory joint and muscle pain questionnaire. Continuous outcomes were analyzed using mixed-model repeated measures and dichotomized responder rates were evaluated using categorical tests.
RESULTS: 134 participants completed the study. With SBB supplementation, mean within-subject moderate to severe HF frequency decreased by -2.7 per day (58.5% reduction) at week 4 and -3.3 per day (71.6% reduction) at week 12 (p <0.001). Sleep disturbance improved significantly, with a reduction in PROMIS-SD T-score of -7.2 (95% CI: [-8.7, -5.8]) at week 4 and -9.0 [-10.7, -7.2] at week 12 (p <0.001). Musculoskeletal pain ratings declined by 38.6% and 43.4% at weeks 4 and 12, respectively (p <0.001). Psychological symptoms scales also showed commensurate improvement. Responder rates significantly improved from baseline in all domains. Improvements met or exceeded the accepted threshold for minimal clinical important difference.
CONCLUSIONS: SBB supplementation was associated with clinically significant improvements across vasomotor and nonvasomotor symptom domains.

articles.title: ASTRO study: acupuncture sets of trial reported core outcomes for women's health across the lifespan.
articles.authors: Levett KM, Buay VC, Citkovitz C et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Clinical trials of acupuncture are difficult to meaningfully aggregate due to small sample sizes and reductionist, heterogeneous outcome measures. To improve the quality of evidence, standardised reporting of minimum data that reflects whole-person health, essential to East Asian Medicine (EAM), is needed. The Core Outcome Measures in Effectiveness Trials (COMET) initiative offers a methodology for developing core outcome sets (COS) through collaborative group consensus, including consumers. This study presents the 'Acupuncture Sets of Trial Reported Outcomes' (ASTRO) for women's health. Using domains of pain, sleep, mood/cognition and safety, the ASTRO framework captures EAM complexity as well as standardising reporting outcomes.
PURPOSE: To develop a COS for acupuncture trials in women's health, reflecting whole-person health outcomes across the lifespan.
METHODS: We used a COMET-informed three-stage consensus process involving practitioners, researchers, patients and policymakers to develop a COS for reporting minimum data for acupuncture trials in women's health. This process involved a systematic review, roundtable discussion, two-round Delphi survey and a consensus meeting. We examined the conditions of menstrual health, polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome, fertility, pregnancy and menopause to develop an outcome set for safety, feasibility and EAM specific outcomes.
RESULTS: From 320 studies, 579 outcomes were identified for the survey items and 319 respondents participated in two Delphi survey rounds. The attrition rate was 52% between surveys and respondents were mainly from English-speaking countries. A final COS of 12 outcomes was agreed on:Safety (n=2): serious adverse events and minor adverse events.EAM (n=8): primary and secondary patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs), patient experience/satisfaction, EAM diagnostic indices (eg, tongue and pulse), demographics and changes in pain, sleep and mood/cognition.Feasibility (n=2): acceptability and cost.
CONCLUSIONS: The ASTRO Women's Health COS enables consistent, whole-person outcome reporting to improve the quality and comparability of acupuncture research.

articles.title: The Association of Hormone Replacement Therapy With Rotator Cuff Tendinopathy and Rotator Cuff Repair Among Menopausal Women.
articles.authors: Chaljub CR, Haver KC, Pescatore SM et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rotator cuff (RC) tendinopathy is a common condition that causes shoulder pain and weakness. The decline of estrogen during menopause may increase RC tendinopathy risk. While hormone replacement therapy (HRT) may counteract these effects, its role in tendon health remains unclear.
PURPOSE: To examine the prevalence of RC tendinopathy and subsequent rotator cuff repair (RCR) surgery among menopausal women taking HRT compared with those not taking HRT.
STUDY DESIGN: Cohort study; Level of study, 3.
METHODS: The authors utilized the TriNetX database to evaluate RC tendinopathy and subsequent RCR in menopausal women aged 45 to 60 years. Two cohorts were created: (1) menopausal women taking estradiol and (2) menopausal women not taking estradiol. Cohorts were 1 to 1 propensity score matched for hyperlipidemia, osteoarthritis, nicotine dependence, type 2 diabetes, thyrotoxicosis, alcohol-related disorders, rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, injections, body mass index, and demographic factors. Outcomes evaluated were RC tendinopathy diagnosis (International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision [ICD-10] codes: M67.81, M75.10, M75.11, M75.12, S43.42, M75.4, M75.5) and RCR (Current Procedural Terminology [CPT]: 29827, 23410, 23412, 23420) at 1, 5, and 10 years after HRT.
RESULTS: Each cohort included 177,198 menopausal women. Women on HRT had significantly higher rates of RC tendinopathy at 1 year compared with women not taking HRT (odds ratio [OR], 1.095 [95% CI, 1.016-1.179]; P = .018). Significantly more women taking HRT also underwent RCR after 1 year (OR = 1.309 [95% CI, 1.045-1.641]; P = .019). After 5 years on HRT, menopausal women were significantly more likely to be both diagnosed with RC tendinopathy (OR = 1.139 [95% CI, 1.088-1.192]; P < .0001) and undergo RCR (OR = 1.278 [95% CI, 1.122-1.456]; P < .0001). After 10 years on HRT, menopausal women demonstrated a similar trend with increased instances of RC tendinopathy (OR = 1.152 [95% CI, 1.105-1.202]; P < .0001) and RCR (OR = 1.279 [95% CI, 1.137-1.439]; P < .0001).
CONCLUSION: Menopausal women taking HRT had significantly higher instances of RC tendinopathy and RCR at all time points. These findings suggest a potential association between HRT and tendon pathology, warranting further research into the interplay between menopause, HRT, and musculoskeletal health to better inform clinical practice.

articles.title: Large language model-assisted machine learning for postpartum urinary incontinence prediction: Model development and validation study.
articles.authors: Xie F, Wang X, Liu Q et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Accurate prediction of postpartum urinary incontinence (UI) remains challenging, as existing models often fail to fully utilize information in unstructured electronic medical records (EMRs). This study aimed to develop and validate a prediction model integrating structured and unstructured clinical data to improve postpartum UI risk assessment.
METHODS: Two prospective cohorts were recruited for model development and validation. A large language model (LLM) was used to extract clinical information from unstructured EMRs and integrate it with structured data. Seven machine learning algorithms were trained and internally validated using stratified five-fold cross-validation, with the optimal model selected based on the area under the curve (AUC). The final model was externally validated and compared with a baseline logistic regression model developed using structured data only. Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) was used to interpret feature importance.
RESULTS: A total of 1605 pregnant women were included, and 20.7% experienced postpartum UI. LLM achieved up to 98.9% overall accuracy in extracting information from unstructured EMRs. Among the seven models, the multilayer perceptron (MLP) achieved the best performance, with internal validation and external validation AUC of 0.813 and 0.782, respectively, outperforming the baseline model. SHAP identified severity of UI during pregnancy, duration of second stage of labor, and number of vaginal deliveries as the most influential predictive factors in the model. A web-based calculator was developed to support future clinical implementation.
CONCLUSIONS: By incorporating a LLM into the development process, we established a robust prediction model for postpartum UI. This innovative approach may facilitate early risk identification.

articles.title: Age modifies the association between endometrial thickness and live birth after frozen embryo transfer: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Rostami M, Khadem Ghaebi N, Ziaee A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The impact of endometrial thickness (EMT) on reproductive outcomes remains a critical consideration in assisted reproductive technology, yet its age-specific influence requires further clarification.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the association between EMT and live birth rate (LBR) in frozen embryo transfer (FET) cycles.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 557 FET cycles performed at Milad Infertility Center, Mashhad, Iran, from March 2020 to February 2025. Live birth was analyzed by multivariable logistic regression and clinical pregnancy by modified Poisson regression. EMT was modeled continuously and categorically. Spline models assessed non-linearity, inverse probability weighting assessed sensitivity to missing covariate data, and an EMT-by-age-group interaction was tested.
RESULTS: In complete-case adjusted analyses (n = 366), each 1-mm increase in EMT was associated with higher odds of LBR (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]: 1.37, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.14-1.65; p < 0.001); inverse probability weighted sensitivity analysis was similar (aOR: 1.38, 95% CI: 1.15-1.67; p < 0.001). A statistically significant interaction between EMT and maternal age was identified (P-interaction < 0.001). In age-stratified analyses, this positive association was most pronounced in women aged 35-39 yr (aOR: 3.38, 95% CI: 1.84-6.23), but was attenuated and non-significant in women < 35 yr and those ≥ 40 yr. Compared with EMT 8.0-8.9 mm, EMT < 7.0 mm was associated with lower odds of LBR (aOR: 0.27, 95% CI: 0.10-0.77; p = 0.014).
CONCLUSION: EMT is a crucial predictor of live birth in FET cycles, but its clinical significance is strongly dependent on maternal age. These findings support an age-stratified approach to counseling and decision-making when EMT is low in FET cycles.

articles.title: Effectiveness of mobile applications in pregnancy care: An umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
articles.authors: Mehrabi R, Bagherzadeh Z, Akbari S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mobile health applications are increasingly integrated into antenatal care as supportive tools to enhance maternal knowledge, promote healthy behaviors, and improve clinical and psychosocial outcomes.
OBJECTIVE: This umbrella review aimed to synthesize and critically appraise evidence on the effectiveness of mobile applications in pregnancy care.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A systematic search was performed using PubMed, Scopus, EMBASE, and Web of Science, without language restrictions. Search terms included "mobile applications" and "pregnancy". This umbrella review synthesized evidence from 21 systematic reviews and meta-analyses published up to May 17, 2025, covering 180 randomized controlled trials with sample sizes ranging from 456-10,348 participants. The methodological quality of eligible articles was assessed using AMSTAR 2.
RESULTS: Findings consistently showed that mobile applications can improve maternal knowledge, self-management, physical activity, diet, weight control, and adherence to prenatal care recommendations. Positive effects were also reported for mental health, including reductions in stress and depressive symptoms, while evidence suggested decreased cesarean section rates, neonatal intensive care admissions, and adverse maternal-fetal outcomes. Despite encouraging results, the overall evidence is constrained by methodological limitations, heterogeneous app designs, small sample sizes, short follow-up periods, and incomplete reporting, reducing the strength and generalizability of conclusions.
CONCLUSION: Mobile health interventions demonstrate considerable potential as complementary strategies in prenatal care. Future research should focus on high-quality, large-scale, long-term trials with culturally sensitive, personalized approaches. Strong collaboration among researchers, healthcare providers, and technology developers is essential to fully harness the impact of mobile applications on maternal and neonatal health.

articles.title: Expression of selected sperm microRNAs in teratozoospermia and globozoospermia and their association with sperm motility and intracytoplasmic sperm injection outcomes: A cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Hosseinabadi F, Rashki Ghaleno L, Alizadeh Moghadam Masouleh A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are small non-coding RNAs that regulate gene expression after transcription. Therefore, changes in miRNA levels can interfere with post-transcriptional gene regulation and are linked to various disease conditions, including male infertility.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to assess the expression levels of sperm miRNAs in globozoospermia and teratozoospermia, compare them with those in normozoospermic men, and explore the relationship between miRNA levels, sperm parameters, and intracytoplasmic sperm injection outcomes.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, a total of 59 semen samples (14 globozoospermic, 20 teratozoospermic, and 25 normozoospermic) were collected. Sperm were separated from seminal plasma for the assessment of DNA fragmentation, DNA oxidation, protamine deficiency, and the expression of 9 miRNAs (namely miR-15a-5p, miR-10a-5p, miR-26b-5p, miR-34c-5p, miR-149-5p, let-7a-5p, miR-320b-3p, miR-296-3p, and miR-191-5p) using reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction. The relationships between fertilization rate, embryo quality score, and the evaluated sperm parameters were analyzed following intracytoplasmic sperm injection.
RESULTS: Among the miRNAs examined, miR-191 demonstrated significantly elevated expression levels in globozoospermic samples relative to normozoospermic controls (p = 0.03). Within the normozoospermic cohort, miR-15a-5p, miR-10a-5p, and miR-320b exhibited positive correlations with sperm motility (p = 0.03, p = 0.02, p = 0.04, respectively). Similarly, in the globozoospermic cohort, all miRNAs except miR-34c showed positive correlations with motility. The findings also revealed increased DNA oxidation in both teratozoospermia and globozoospermia samples compared to the normozoospermia group (p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Although the examined sperm miRNAs did not exhibit significant correlations with morphology or fertilization rate, significant associations between several miRNAs and sperm motility were observed in specific study groups, particularly among globozoospermic men.

articles.title: Delayed Secondary Postpartum Hemorrhage 15 Days After Repeat Cesarean Delivery Complicated by Endometritis, Hysterotomy Dehiscence, and Definitive Hysterectomy.
articles.authors: Jaimes AVP, Sparagana S, Carrillo L et al.
articles.abstract: Delayed postpartum hemorrhage after cesarean delivery should prompt consideration of uterine incision dehiscence, particularly when accompanied by fever, persistent bleeding despite conservative therapy, or imaging suggestive of hematometra. Early multidisciplinary evaluation and timely definitive surgical management may be lifesaving and prevent progression to hemorrhagic shock, sepsis, and maternal morbidity.

articles.title: Dosimetry-guided morphomic modeling using daily FBCT for automated all-in-one radiotherapy eligibility assessment in postoperative cervical cancer.
articles.authors: Xu Y, Chen H, Xu X et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop an automated decision-making model based on daily fan-beam CT (FBCT) morphomic features to determine whether a treatment fraction is suitable for AIO-RT initiation.
METHODS: A total of 48 postoperative cervical cancer patients with 313 FBCT fractions were retrospectively analyzed. Morphomic features were extracted from bladder, rectum, intrarectal gas, bilateral femoral head, and inter-organ spatial relationships. Feature selection was performed using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), and predictive models were built using Random Forest (RF) and Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM) under leave-one-patient-out cross-validation.
RESULTS: Both models achieved consistent discriminative performance (AUC = 0.958 for RF and 0.952 for GBM). Bladder-related morphological features were the dominant predictors, particularly bladder volume and shape-derived descriptors. Spatial features also contributed to classification performance, while rectal gas showed limited but complementary predictive value.
CONCLUSION: The proposed FBCT-based morphomic framework can accurately identify unsuitable fractions for AIO-RT before workflow initiation, providing a practical and interpretable decision-support tool for adaptive radiotherapy workflow optimization.

articles.title: MTHFR C677T and one-carbon metabolism in adverse maternal-fetal outcomes: links to hypertension and renal/endothelial burden.
articles.authors: Cheng J, Li X, Mei Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adverse pregnancy outcomes (APOs) encompass heterogeneous maternal, fetal/placental, and pregnancy-loss phenotypes. The clinical relevance of methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) C677T may therefore depend less on genotype alone than on the surrounding one-carbon metabolic environment. We investigated genotype-metabolism relationships across rigorously adjudicated maternal-fetal phenotypes.
METHODS: In this hospital-based retrospective cohort, 474 of 484 pregnancy records met prespecified criteria for primary analysis. Pregnancies were classified as reference, maternal-predominant, fetal/placental-predominant, maternal-fetal dual-hit, or pregnancy loss. MTHFR C677T was modeled primarily as CT/TT versus CC. An a priori one-carbon metabolism index (OCMI) integrated standardized homocysteine, folate, and vitamin B12. Associations were evaluated using age-adjusted regression, interaction modeling, natural cubic splines, and sensitivity analyses including inverse-probability weighting.
RESULTS: MTHFR C677T showed little evidence of association with overall or phenotype-specific APO after age adjustment. Higher homocysteine was strongly associated with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP; OR 2.32 per SD, 95% CI 1.61-3.34) and mapped preferentially to a renal/endothelial-related biochemical burden, which was itself strongly associated with HDP (OR 3.99 per SD, 95% CI 2.79-5.70). The MTHFR-homocysteine interaction was null. By contrast, among 177 OCM-complete pregnancies, the MTHFR-OCMI interaction with HDP was suggestive (OR 2.46, 95% CI 1.10-5.52; BH-FDR q = 0.085) and showed evidence of genotype-dependent non-linearity. Renal/endothelial-related burden showed a nonlinear association with maternal-fetal dual-hit involvement, with the strongest association observed in the highest quartile.
CONCLUSION: MTHFR C677T appears more consistent with a context-dependent susceptibility factor than with an isolated correlate of APO. Integrating one-carbon metabolism with maternal-fetal phenotyping identified a coherent pattern of associations between metabolic disturbance, hypertensive morbidity, and renal/endothelial-related biochemical burden, while the genotype-OCMI signal warrants prospective validation.

articles.title: Mechanotransduction in the placental endothelium: molecular mechanisms and implications for pregnancy complications.
articles.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
articles.authors: Wan B, Li Y, He G
articles.abstract: The placental endothelium is exposed to a distinctive and continuously changing mechanical microenvironment shaped by fluid shear stress, cyclic stretch, and hydrostatic pressure. Mechanotransduction maintains endothelial homeostasis through coordinated signaling involving the endothelial glycocalyx, integrin-based adhesions, mechanosensitive ion channels, including Piezo1 and TRPV4, Rho-family GTPases, and the Hippo-YAP/TAZ pathway, which serves as key regulators to convert mechanical stimuli into biochemical signals. Conversely, defective spiral-artery remodeling generates pathological placental perfusion, hypoxia-reoxygenation injury and altered paracrine signaling; these secondary disturbances may impair fetoplacental endothelial mitochondrial quality control by promoting DRP1 dependent mitochondrial fission and impairing mitochondrial fusion (MFN2/OPA1), resulting in mitochondrial fragmentation, reactive oxygen species accumulation, and endothelial dysfunction. In severe preeclampsia (PE), reduced YAP/TAZ activity has been linked to both Hippo-dependent signaling through MST1/2 and LATS1/2 and Hippo-independent regulation involving the S1PR2-RhoA/ROCK-actin axis, with consequences for extravillous trophoblast invasion. Emerging approaches targeting placental mechanotransduction, including gestational stage-specific mitochondria-targeted antioxidants, pharmacological modulation of mechanosensitive ion channels, and placenta-on-a-chip platforms for mechanistic investigation and compound screening, offer new translational opportunities. This review integrates current understanding of placental endothelial mechanotransduction, examines its dysregulation in pregnancy-related complications including PE, fetal growth restriction (FGR), and gestational hypertension (GH). While partial mechanistic overlap exists between these conditions, GH represents a distinct and generally milder clinical phenotype; fetoplacental endothelial-specific molecular features of GH remain largely uncharacterized and constitute an important knowledge gap. We further identify priorities for the development of mechanism-based precision interventions for PE, FGR and GH.

articles.title: Endogenous Lifetime Hormone Exposure Shows Stronger Associations with Cerebrovascular Rather Than Neuroanatomical Brain Measures in Postmenopausal Women in the UK Biobank.
articles.authors: Gandey Z, Côté S, Bertrand A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Following menopause, women face increased risk of cognitive decline and cerebrovascular disease, including stroke, often attributed to declining hormone levels. However, substantial interindividual variability exists, with some women remaining relatively protected, while others are more vulnerable. Cumulative endogenous lifetime hormone exposure (LHE-Endo) may represent an important factor contributing to these differences, yet the specific brain substrates underlying its associations with late-life brain health remain unclear.
METHODS: Using UK Biobank data, we investigated associations between LHE-Endo and neuroimaging markers of cerebrovascular and neuroanatomical brain health in postmenopausal women. Outcomes included regional white matter hyperintensity volumes (WMHV), cortical and subcortical gray matter volumes (GMV), total white matter volume (WMV), and white matter microstructure (fractional anisotropy [FA]). We further compared WMH subtypes and examined sex hormone receptor expression using single-nucleus RNA sequencing data.
RESULTS: Longer LHE-Endo was associated with lower total WMH burden (t = -3.87, p = 0.0001), with stronger effects in periventricular (t = -4.31, p = 0.00002) than deep WMH (t = -1.27, p = 0.2). No significant associations were observed with cortical GMV (t = 1.13, p = 0.2), total WMV (t = -0.10, p = 0.9), or total FA (t = 0.64, p = 0.5). Transcriptomic data confirmed this result, showing higher expression of sex hormone receptors in vascular cells than in neuronal and axonal populations.
CONCLUSION: LHE-Endo is more strongly associated with cerebrovascular than neuroanatomical measures in postmenopausal women, suggesting vascular pathways, particularly periventricular white matter, as key biological substrates linking hormone exposure to brain aging.

articles.title: Ovarian rejuvenation: Ways to restart the ovaries: A narrative review.
articles.authors: Oo WJ, Lam AQ, Tee ST et al.
articles.abstract: Following the escalation of global infertility rate, female infertility has raised significant health concerns. Despite a myriad of treatment options being available to overcome female infertility, the majority remain nonspecific. Thus, ovarian dysfunction is recognized as a prominent pathophysiological condition, prompting the emergence of novel therapeutic strategies for ovarian rejuvenation. Several potential approaches include in vitro activation, artificial ovaries, telomerase reactivation, stem cell-based therapy, platelet activation therapy, mitigation of fibrosis and inflammation, and hormone replacement therapy, with the latter being rather conventional. Mounting evidence has suggested promising outcomes, such as restored hormone levels, increased follicle counts and maturation, and higher-quality oocytes. Besides, their working principles are based on countering fibrosis and inflammation, which often support the decline in ovarian function. While these methods aim to revive ovarian function under different circumstances, inconsistent findings are still being reported, emphasizing their uncertainty in practical terms. This review discusses novel therapies showing potential for ovarian rejuvenation and provides new insights into their specific roles in ameliorating ovarian conditions of various natures and at different stages.

articles.title: SVIP knockdown alters UPS protein expression in human testicular embryonal carcinoma cells.
articles.authors: Kipel Ş, Çayli S, Aktaş Gİ et al.
articles.abstract: Testicular tumours are the most common malignant tumors in men between the ages of 15-34. Approximately 95% of testicular tumors arise from germ cells. Small VCP-interacting protein (SVIP) is a protein that regulates its function and autophagy by binding to p97/VCP, which is involved in protein degradation associated with the endoplasmic reticulum. Recent studies on SVIP have shown that SVIP is an androgen-sensitive protein. The development of secondary sex characteristics is influenced by androgens, which are significant steroid hormone. Androgens also initiate and maintain spermatogenesis in the male reproductive system. Mutations of androgen receptors are often seen in patients with disorders of male reproductive development and can cause male infertility. Studies are showing that the ubiquitin proteasome system (UPS) in the male reproductive system affects fertility. Therefore, investigating the expressions of USP26 and UXT, which are components of the UPS, is important for testicular biology. The expressions of SVIP, AR, Ubiquitin, USP26 and UXT were analysed by immunofluorescence, western blot and q RT-PCR method to determine the expressions of SVIP and the UPS proteins that it interacts in human testicular embryonal carcinoma cells (CRL-2073) and to see the effects of suppressed SVIP expression on other proteins after SVIP siRNA transfection. At SVIP siRNA applied CRL-2073 cells, SVIP, AR, USP26 and Ubiquitin expressions decreased, while UXT expression increased, according to immunofluorescence and western blot results. According to the qRT-PCR results, SVIP gene expression decreased and AR, Ubiquitin, USP26 and UXT gene expressions increased in the group given SVIP siRNA. As a result, this study demonstrated the expression of SVIP and its interacting UPS proteins in CRL-2073 cells for the first time, making an unique and significant contribution to the literature.

articles.title: Determinants of maternal near-misses in Al-Najaf governorate, Iraq: A matched case-control study.
articles.authors: Madlool H, Karami M, Delpisheh A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Improving maternal health is one of the most significant global challenges. Consequently, studying the causes and factors contributing to maternal near-misses (MNMs) is crucial for enhancing the obstetric care quality. The aim of this study was to identify the factors related to MNMs among the study participants in Al-Najaf, Iraq.
METHODS: Investigators carried out a matched case-control study in Al-Najaf Governorate from September 2023 to June 2024. The study included 429 participants (143 cases and 286 controls), each case was matched by age and residency with two controls in the same hospital. The data were collected using a modified WHO structured checklist through face-to-face interviews and medical records review in three selected hospitals. Multivariate conditional logistic regression was used to estimate adjusted odds ratios (aORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). STATA version 17 was used to analyze the data.
RESULTS: Postpartum hemorrhage was the top cause, accounting for 56% of MNM cases. The odds of developing MNM among women with inadequate antenatal care (ANC) visits (<4 visits) were greater than those among women who had 8 or more ANC visits aOR = 4.1 (95% CI:1.31-12.7). Women with cesarean section history were almost seven-fold increased odds of experiencing a MNM event aOR = 6.69 (95% CI: 3.04-14.7). Women with any pregnancy complications history were almost eight-fold more likely to develop MNM aOR = 8.06 (95% CI: 2.17-29.8).
CONCLUSIONS: Inadequate antenatal care visits, pregnancy complication history, and a history of cesarean sections were statistically significant factors associated with experiencing MNMs.

articles.title: Human leukocyte antigen-G isoforms HLA-G2/6, rather than HLA-G1/4/5, are associated with poorer survival in patients with epithelial ovarian cancer.
articles.authors: Zhang X, Han QY, Dai BK et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The novel immune checkpoint human leukocyte antigen-G (HLA-G) is a promising candidate target for solid cancer immunotherapy. However, knowledge gaps on the clinical relevance of diverse HLA-G isoforms remain.
METHODS: In this study, with the successful generation of monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) against the HLA-G2/6 and HLA-G1/4/5 isoforms, the immunoreactivity scores (IRS) of both HLA-G2/6 and HLA-G1/4/5 expression (n = 304) were retrospectively analyzed using immunohistochemistry (IHC) in patients with epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC). The significance of the IRS status of HLA-G2/6 and HLA-G1/4/5 related to the clinical variables (n = 304) and prognosis (n = 251) of patients with EOC was evaluated.
RESULTS: The IRS of HLA-G2/6neg (n = 7), HLA-G2/6low (n = 105), and HLA-G2/6high (n = 192) and those of HLA-G1/4/5neg (n = 12), HLA-G1/4/5low (n = 48), and HLA-G1/4/5high (n = 244), respectively. Both HLA-G2/6high (p = 0.029) and HLA-G1/4/5high (p = 0.016) were the most frequently expressed in other EOC types, followed by the serous and mucinous subtypes. HLA-G2/6high was remarkably found in patients with advanced pN1 (p < 0.001), while HLA-G1/4/5high in patients with advanced pT3 (p = 0.024). The log-rank Mantel-Cox analysis showed that HLA-G2/6high was significantly associated with poorer overall survival (OS) (HLA-G2/6neg/low = 10.0 years vs. HLA-G2/6high = 6.25years; p = 0.036). Furthermore, patients with HLA-G2/6high had worse prognosis for those who are elder (>53 years, p = 0.049) and with the serous subtype (p = 0.028). However, HLA-G2/6 expression was not an independent prognostic risk factor for this EOC cohort.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings revealed, for the first time, that HLA-G2/6 rather than HLA-G1/4/5 isoform expression is associated with poorer survival in patients with EOC.

articles.title: Clinical and cervical factors associated with obstetric outcomes following cervical cerclage: a ten-year retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Sengi A, Gündüz R, Özmaskan F et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate obstetric and neonatal outcomes following cervical cerclage and to identify maternal and cervical characteristics associated with gestational age at delivery in a ten-year retrospective cohort.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed the records of 66 women who underwent cervical cerclage for cervical insufficiency between 1 January 2013 and 1 January 2023 (cerclage at 12 to 25 weeks; four multiple pregnancies, 6.1%). Cerclage was classified as emergency (examination-indicated; n = 23, 34.8%) or elective (history- or ultrasound-indicated; n = 43, 65.2%). Associations with gestational age at delivery were evaluated using correlation analysis, stratification by indication, multivariable regression, and a sensitivity analysis excluding multiple pregnancies.
RESULTS: Sixty-six women were included. In unadjusted analyses, later gestational age at cerclage (r = -0.349, p = 0.004), shorter cervical length (r = 0.562, p < 0.01), and greater cervical dilation (r = -0.540, p < 0.01) were associated with earlier delivery, whereas maternal age, parity, and previous cerclage were not. Emergency cerclage was associated with earlier delivery than elective cerclage (median 31 vs. 37 weeks, p = 0.007), and the association of cervical length with delivery timing differed between strata (interaction p = 0.016). In the primary adjusted model no variable was significant; cervical length (β = 0.21 weeks per mm, p = 0.055) and cervical dilation (β = -1.36 weeks per cm, p = 0.088) were borderline, and cervical length became significant when an emergency indicator replaced dilation (β = 0.31, p = 0.005). For delivery before 34 weeks, neither cervical dilation (OR 1.83 per cm, p = 0.062) nor cervical length (OR 0.90 per mm, p = 0.064) was significant. Excluding multiple pregnancies gave similar results. Apgar scores were delivery-related outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cohort, earlier cerclage, longer cervical length, and less advanced cervical changes were associated with later delivery in unadjusted analyses; in the primary adjusted model no variable was independently significant, although cervical length and dilation were borderline and findings were sensitive to model specification. These findings do not establish causal effectiveness, as no untreated control group was available. Prospective controlled studies are needed.

articles.title: Stillbirth and Its Associated Factors Among Women in Haramaya District, Eastern Ethiopia: A Community-Based Study.
articles.authors: Amin A, Dheresa M, Mezmur H
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to determine the prevalence and identify the factors associated with stillbirth in Haramaya District, Eastern Ethiopia.
METHODS: We extracted 10,557 registered births that occurred between January 1, 2020 and December 30, 2022 from 12 kebeles. A multivariable logistic regression model was used to identify factors associated with stillbirth. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05.
RESULTS: The prevalence of stillbirth was 2.3% (95% CI: 2.1%, 2.6%). Home delivery (AOR = 1.49; 95% CI: 1.07 - 2.10), Previous history of stillbirth (AOR = 12.59; 95% CI: 9.51 - 16.66), and preterm birth (AOR = 18.30; 95% CI: 12.08 - 27.75) were significantly associated with stillbirth.
CONCLUSIONS: The prevalence of stillbirth in this study was high relative to global targets for 2030. Strengthening systems to promote safe facility-based deliveries and implementing targeted community-based interventions that enhance early pregnancy monitoring are crucial for reducing stillbirth rates in rural settings.

articles.title: Follitropin alfa versus follitropin alfa/lutropin alfa (rFSH/rLH) in progestin-primed ovarian stimulation: a prospective two-center observational cohort study.
articles.authors: Pabuccu E, Tohma YA, Ozkavukcu S
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The contribution of recombinant LH during progestin-primed ovarian stimulation (PPOS) remains uncertain. We compared recombinant FSH alone (GON) with recombinant FSH plus recombinant LH (PER) in a prospective two-center observational cohort.
METHODS: The full enrolled cohort included 213 women (121 GON; 92 PER), including 11 with day-3 transfer. MII oocyte count was the primary outcome. The primary negative binomial model adjusted for female age, AMH, baseline AFC, previous failed cycles and center. Propensity scores used the same covariates; matching was 1:1, exact within center, using Mahalanobis distance within a logit propensity-score caliper. The per-protocol (PP) population comprised the 202 women whose embryos were cultured to day 5; in the full-cohort (ITT) analysis, the 11 women with day-3 transfer contributed zero day-5 blastocysts.
RESULTS: The primary adjusted MII incidence rate ratio (IRR) for PER versus GON was 1.01 (95% CI 0.91-1.11; p = 0.910); the PP IRR was 1.00 (95% CI 0.91-1.11; p = 0.939). The number of MII oocytes was similar in both groups (median 11 in both), and this finding did not change after adjustment for baseline characteristics or after propensity-score matching. PER was associated with more day-5 blastocysts (median 4 vs. 3) and more top-quality blastocysts (median 2 vs. 1), and these differences persisted after adjustment and matching. Positive β-hCG rates after the first frozen embryo transfer were similar (47.6% vs. 43.2%). OHSS was rare (1 PER and 2 GON cases, all mild), and no cycle was canceled.
CONCLUSIONS: No statistically significant difference in MII count was detected, and equivalence was not established. The higher day-5 blastocyst counts associated with PER may reflect an effect of LH on embryo developmental competence rather than on oocyte yield; this exploratory finding does not establish a causal or clinical benefit and requires confirmation in randomized trials. https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07348757, NCT07348757.

articles.title: Orchestrating implantation: endometrial receptivity as a convergence point of endocrine, metabolic, and immune signals.
articles.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
articles.authors: Zhu Z, Li Y, Zhang X et al.
articles.abstract: Endometrial receptivity is a transient and highly coordinated functional state that enables embryo apposition, adhesion, invasion, and subsequent pregnancy establishment during the window of implantation, and its disruption represents an important contributor to infertility, recurrent implantation failure, and early pregnancy loss. In this review, we integrate current evidence on the molecular and cellular mechanisms governing endometrial receptivity, with particular emphasis on the dynamic interplay among hormonal signaling, intracellular regulatory pathways, metabolic reprogramming, and the immune microenvironment. Estrogen and progesterone orchestrate the transition of the endometrium from proliferation to differentiation and decidualization, while signaling networks including Wnt/β-catenin, PI3K/AKT/mTOR, LIF/JAK/STAT, and TGF-β/BMP coordinate epithelial function, stromal remodeling, angiogenesis, and embryo-endometrial communication. Metabolic pathways involving glucose, lipids, and amino acids provide not only energetic and biosynthetic support but also signaling and epigenetic inputs required for decidualization and implantation, whereas uterine natural killer cells, T cells, macrophages, and dendritic cells establish the finely balanced immune environment necessary for maternal-fetal tolerance. These regulatory layers converge at shared signaling and functional nodes, including PI3K/AKT/mTOR, STAT3, TGF-β/SMAD, amino-acid-dependent epigenetic regulation, and angiogenic pathways, thereby coupling decidualization, immune tolerance, vascular remodeling, and trophoblast invasion. Importantly, emerging evidence supports a conceptual shift from viewing impaired receptivity as the consequence of isolated molecular defects toward understanding it as a systems-level disruption of interconnected endocrine, metabolic, immune, and cellular networks, a common pathological feature across infertility-associated disorders such as endometriosis, polycystic ovary syndrome, chronic endometritis, and adenomyosis. Defining the temporal and spatial coordination of these networks may facilitate the development of more reliable biomarkers and mechanism-based, personalized strategies for assessing and restoring endometrial receptivity, ultimately improving implantation and reproductive outcomes.

articles.title: Disputes over frozen embryos in China: an empirical legal-ethical analysis of judicial practice.
articles.journal: Journal of law and the biosciences
articles.authors: Zhao Y, Lin Y
articles.abstract: This Article analyses 94 frozen-embryo dispute case records from China, identified through China Judgments Online and spanning docket years 2013-25. It distinguishes claims for continued performance of assisted reproductive technology (ART) medical service contracts from claims for embryo return or disposition. Four factual scenarios concern continued ART after a spouse's death or disappearance, posthumous family or kinship claims, post-divorce disputes, and return disputes during marriage; three records lack sufficient information for scenario assignment. Plaintiffs obtained full or partial embryo-related civil relief in 87 cases (92.55 per cent), including rights recognition that does not necessarily permit clinical embryo transfer. Courts used public-order and related ethical reasoning in divergent ways, while some decisions expanded protection for widowed women continuing an existing reproductive project. Persistent difficulties include embryos' uncertain legal status, gaps in rules for exceptional circumstances, conflicting normative frameworks, and safeguards against unlawful surrogacy. The Article proposes treating frozen embryos as a special category of 'ethical objects' and refining scenario-specific disposition rules, institutional obligations, and ethical oversight to protect reproductive interests while addressing downstream risks.

articles.title: Sleep symptoms, reproductive hormones, and treatment trajectories across the menopausal transition: analyses of two observational cohorts.
articles.authors: Kong X, Liu W, Mao H
articles.abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVES: Sleep disturbance is common during the menopausal transition, but whether menopausal context is associated with the pace of improvement during insomnia treatment is unclear. We first examined associations of menopausal stage and reproductive-hormone variation with sleep symptoms in a community cohort, and then sleep-quality trajectories during routine insomnia treatment across estimated menopausal proxy groups in a clinical cohort.
METHODS: Two observational cohorts were analysed separately. The Study of Women's Health Across the Nation (SWAN) included 3,280 women and 22,925 person-visits; mixed-effects and generalized-estimating-equation models examined stage-related symptom burden, annual persistence, and within- versus between-woman hormone associations. The clinical cohort comprised 431 women receiving insomnia treatment (a hospital-affiliated digital sleep programme delivering cognitive-behavioural and relaxation content, pharmacotherapy, or both) in three estimated hormone-plus-age proxy groups (99 regular-cycling, 89 perimenopausal, 243 postmenopausal), with 2,522 Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) assessments over 12 months. Linear mixed-effects models estimated average monthly PSQI change (points/month) by group; logistic and Cox models estimated response, remission, and time to first observed response.
RESULTS: In SWAN, sleep-symptom burden increased across the menopausal transition (ordinal trend +0.23 points per stage on the 3-15 score, p < 0.001); late perimenopause had the largest adjusted burden difference relative to premenopause (β = 0.788, p < 0.001). Persistence odds were higher in early perimenopause (OR = 1.281, p = 0.002) and natural postmenopause (OR = 1.389, p = 0.003). Higher log-transformed follicle-stimulating hormone (β = 0.221) and lower log-estradiol (β = -0.144), relative to each woman's own mean, were associated with greater burden (both p < 0.001); between-woman hormone terms were not significant. In the clinical cohort, PSQI scores improved in all proxy groups (estimated slopes -0.65, -0.45, and -0.67…
CONCLUSIONS: Menopausal stage and within-woman reproductive-hormone variation were associated with sleep-symptom burden in SWAN. During routine insomnia treatment, sleep quality improved in all estimated menopausal proxy groups, and average improvement trajectories did not differ significantly between groups. Prospective studies with menstrual-history-based staging and standardised treatment are needed.

articles.title: Gestational weight gain trajectories and outcome-informed reference ranges among women with gestational diabetes: a BMI-stratified cohort study.
articles.authors: Yuan P, Kong L, Zhang S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gestational weight gain (GWG) is an important modifiable component of nutritional management in gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), but stage-specific patterns and appropriate total GWG ranges across pre-pregnancy body mass index (BMI) categories remain uncertain. This study aimed to characterize gestational-age-specific GWG trajectories and stage-specific patterns in relation to GDM diagnosis based on oral glucose tolerance testing (OGTT), derive BMI-stratified local reference ranges for total GWG, and internally compare their risk-stratification performance with national recommendations.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 9,008 women with singleton pregnancies complicated by GDM who delivered between February 2021 and December 2025. Population-level centile curves characterized GWG patterns, and the interquartile range of total GWG among women without adverse pregnancy outcomes (APOs) defined the locally derived, outcome-informed empirical reference range (LOC). Generalized additive models and multivariable logistic regression assessed associations between GWG and APOs. LOC and National Health Commission (NHC) discrimination was internally evaluated using 2,000 bootstrap resamples with optimism correction.
RESULTS: GWG showed stage- and BMI-specific patterns, increasing more rapidly before OGTT-based diagnosis and generally slowing thereafter. Post-diagnosis rates approached NHC recommendations among underweight or normal-weight women but remained relatively high among overweight or obese women. The LOC ranges were 11.0-15.0, 9.2-14.0, 7.5-13.0, and 6.0-11.5 kg for underweight, normal weight, overweight, and obesity, respectively. After false discovery rate correction, inadequate GWG was associated mainly with low birth weight (LBW) and small for gestational age (SGA), whereas LOC-based associations with preterm birth in underweight and normal-weight women were less robust in the 28-week landmark analysis. Excessive GWG was primarily associated with preeclampsia, macrosomia, large for gestational…
CONCLUSION: GWG trajectories and locally derived total GWG ranges differed across pre-pregnancy BMI categories. The locally derived ranges were broadly consistent with national recommendations and may provide supplementary information for selected BMI-outcome combinations. These findings may inform prospective evaluation of stratified, dynamic weight-management approaches within the framework of national recommendations.

articles.title: Proteomics-based immune activation signatures are associated with kidney allograft rejection.
articles.authors: Schröter I, Loi L, Rudek M et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Biopsy-based diagnostics for the detection of kidney allograft rejection are invasive and imperfect, highlighting the need for non-invasive biomarkers. However, the potential of plasma proteomics for assessing alloimmune injury remains unclear.
METHODS: Therefore, proteomic profiling was performed in 88 kidney transplant recipients undergoing indication biopsy using the Olink Target 96 Inflammation panel. Differential protein expression analyses compared biopsy-proven rejection with no rejection. A composite proteomic score derived from the three most discriminatory proteins was evaluated in relation to histopathology, donor-derived cell-free DNA (dd-cfDNA), and graft outcomes.
RESULTS: Among 92 analyzed proteins, TNFRSF9 showed the strongest association with rejection, followed by CXCL9 and IL-12B. The composite proteomic score discriminated rejection from no rejection (AUC 0.85, 95% CI 0.72-0.95), while integration with dd-cfDNA improved discrimination (AUC 0.88, 95% CI 0.78-0.99). Signals from the predefined inflammation-related protein panel increased progressively from no rejection to borderline changes and overt rejection (P < 0.001). The score correlated with histopathological indices of activity, antibody-mediated rejection/microvascular inflammation, T-cell-mediated rejection/tubulointerstitial inflammation, and chronicity. Patients with borderline changes displayed heterogeneous proteomic signatures, with most overlapping the no-rejection group and a smaller subset exhibiting rejection-like signatures. The score correlated moderately with dd-cfDNA (ρ=0.32, P = 0.009) and remained independently associated with death-censored graft failure (HR 2.67, 95% CI 1.31-5.42).
CONCLUSION: Together, these exploratory findings suggest that plasma proteomic signatures may reflect aspects of alloimmune injury across the rejection spectrum and are associated with chronic histological damage and graft failure. These findings support further investigation of plasma proteomics as a complementary approach for non-invasive assessment of kidney allograft injury while potentially also offering insights into mechanisms driving progressive allograft dysfunction.

articles.title: Overtreatment risk of postoperative radiotherapy in FIGO I-III cervical small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma: a population-based study.
articles.authors: Mo DC, Huang JF, Luo PH et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cervical small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (SCNEC) is a rare, highly aggressive cervical malignancy. Radical hysterectomy is standard for localized disease, yet the survival benefit of postoperative radiotherapy (RT) remains controversial. This study assessed postoperative RT's prognostic impact in SCNEC patients, screened potential RT beneficiaries, and generated evidence to mitigate overtreatment risk.
METHODS: Patients with pathologically confirmed FIGO I-III cervical SCNEC diagnosed between 2000 and 2023 were extracted from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database. All eligible patients underwent radical hysterectomy. Inverse probability treatment weighting (IPTW) balanced baseline features to reduce selection bias. Primary endpoints were overall survival (OS) and cancer-specific survival (CSS). Analyses included weighted Kaplan-Meier curves, multivariate Cox regression, and Fine-Gray competing risk models to evaluate RT's prognostic effect.
RESULTS: A total of 175 eligible patients were identified, among whom 96 (54.9%) received surgery combined with postoperative RT and 79 (45.1%) underwent surgery alone. Before IPTW adjustment, no significant differences in OS or CSS were observed between the two groups. After IPTW, weighted survival analyses showed that postoperative RT did not improve OS (hazard ratio [HR]=1.02, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.67-1.54, P = 0.101) and CSS (HR = 1.04, 95%CI: 0.70-1.56, P = 0.198) in the overall cohort. Fine-Gray competing risk analysis further showed that postoperative RT was not associated with reduced cancer-specific mortality (HR = 1.11, 95%CI: 0.73-1.69, P = 0.630). Multivariate Cox regression analysis indicated that year of diagnosis and omission of lymph node resection were independent adverse prognostic factors for both endpoints, and stratified analyses showed no measurable heterogeneity of RT…
CONCLUSION: Postoperative RT was not associated with improved OS or CSS for patients with FIGO stage I-III cervical SCNEC following radical hysterectomy, suggesting a potential overtreatment risk that warrants close clinical attention for this surgically treated population. Given the high malignancy and propensity for systemic metastasis of SCNEC, future studies should focus on integrating immunotherapy strategies targeting the programmed cell death-1 (PD-1)/programmed cell death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) axis or delta-like ligand 3 (DLL3) to overcome the limitations of local radiation.

articles.title: IVF medical tourism in Malaysia-an overview of current market dynamics and ethical challenges for intended parents/patients.
articles.journal: Journal of law and the biosciences
articles.authors: Chin AHB, Roslan R, Mohamad CABC et al.
articles.abstract: In vitro fertilization (IVF) medical tourism is expanding as more patients travel to jurisdictions offering treatments restricted or unavailable at home. Malaysia is a favored Asian destination because of its permissive clinical assisted reproduction environment, particularly in the case of preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A), elective egg freezing (EEF), and egg donation. Using credence goods theory, this article argues that the risk is information asymmetry. Fertility clinics possess information that intended parents/patients cannot readily assess, even after treatment, and may therefore misrepresent services. This asymmetry is intensified where decisions are emotionally-pressured, age-sensitive, costly, and irreversible. The article examines PGT-A, EEF, and egg donation as illustrations of this risk. It treats underhand practices not as established facts, but as possible vulnerabilities created by regulatory gaps. The analysis also examines the failures of the 2009 and 2016 ART (Assisted Reproductive Technique) services bills, arguing that durable legislation requires consensus among medical, religious, commercial, governmental, and patient stakeholders. Malaysia should replace non-enforceable guidelines with a coherent ART regulatory framework incorporating mandatory disclosure, advertising restrictions, independent counseling, cooling-off periods, licensing, audit, and enforceable sanctions. Such reforms would reduce misrepresentation, safeguard foreign patients, and strengthen Malaysia's standing as an IVF medical-tourism destination.

articles.title: Skin Acceptability of a Topical Cream Containing Zinc Oxide, Zinc Gluconate, Taurine and Panthenol in Females With Urinary Incontinence.
articles.authors: Celleno L, Landini L, Kamal DM et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Incontinence-associated dermatitis (IAD) can be exacerbated by friction and occlusion from a diaper/incontinence pad. Skin barrier function in IAD can be preserved through humectant and emollient-containing protective agents.
AIMS: To investigate the efficacy, skin acceptability, and cosmetic qualities of a cream containing zinc oxide, zinc gluconate, taurine, and panthenol.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: Participants without IAD who used diapers included otherwise healthy females ≤ 65 years old with urinary incontinence due to surgery/a traumatic event (n = 11) or > 65 years old with urinary incontinence from any cause (n = 11). The cream was used for 28 days, applied to clean, dry skin within the diaper area at each diaper change/as needed. Participants noted daily any reactions and sensations of discomfort. The investigator conducted a visual clinical examination of the skin around the application area at study start (D0) and after 28 days (D28), noting at D28 any reactivity (location, intensity, percentage) and product intolerance. Participants reported any discomfort and rated product efficacy and tolerability.
RESULTS: At D28, no participant had clinical signs or sensations of discomfort or experienced a treatment-related adverse event. The product was rated by the dermatologist as 'very good' in terms of skin acceptability and tolerance. Most participants agreed the product had good moisturizing efficacy, helped alleviate redness and irritation, and made their skin feel protected and comfortable.
CONCLUSION: The investigational cream containing zinc oxide, zinc gluconate, panthenol, and taurine was generally well-tolerated. Further investigations, including a control group, are needed to determine if the cream prevents IAD.

articles.title: Public Discourse on Menopausal Skin Management: A YouTube Infodemiology Study of Treatment Perceptions, Sentiment, and Unmet Needs Across 43 954 Viewer Comments.
articles.authors: Diremsizoglu E, Arslan EA, Demirbas A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Menopausal skin changes carry significant psychosocial burden yet remain clinically under-addressed. As women increasingly turn to digital platforms for information and peer experience, YouTube viewer comments represent an underexplored source of real-world treatment perceptions at scale.
METHODS: Cross-sectional infodemiology study using the YouTube Data API v3 (14 March 2026). 342 videos yielded 43 954 analyzable comments after automated cleaning (350-comment/video cap). Videos were classified into four content-type categories (Cohen's κ = 0.934). A 13-category management subcorpus (n = 10 861; 24.7% of full corpus) was constructed by pre-specified keyword matching.
RESULTS: The study corpus showed predominantly positive sentiment (59.6% positive, 19.1% negative; median 0.36, IQR 0.00-0.73). Hormone replacement therapy (HRT) dominated the management subcorpus (54.8%) yet generated the lowest sentiment of any category (median 0.10; 30.2% negative), differing significantly from all others (p < 0.001). Alternative approaches (median 0.72; 77.7% positive) and supplements (median 0.50; 74.6% positive) attracted the highest positivity. Personal/lifestyle content generated higher positivity (median 0.59; 70.6%) than clinician content (median 0.32; 57.7%; p < 0.001). Following the FDA's November 2025 HRT boxed warning removal, a higher proportion of positive HRT comments was observed in the post-announcement period (53.1% vs. 50.5%; p = 0.126) over the 4.5-month available window. A negative temporal trend was observed over 116 months (Spearman ρ = -0.424, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: HRT generates the most negative public commentary of any management category, while supplements and alternative approaches attract positivity disproportionate to their evidence base. Clinician content elicits lower viewer positivity than lifestyle creators. Dermatologists should address HRT safety misconceptions and increase online representation of evidence-based procedural options.

articles.title: 2025 Harriet Dustan Lecture: Sex Differences in Immune-Mediated Hypertension: Why Menopause Matters.
articles.authors: Brooks HL, Sylvester MA, Michea L
articles.abstract: Hypertension is an inflammatory disease with the immune system playing a key role in mediating hypertensive outcomes and end-organ damage. The risk of hypertension is greater in men than in women before women enter menopause. After menopause, a woman's risk for developing hypertension increases and accelerates beyond that of age-matched men. Moreover, after menopause, the rate of hypertension control in women is lower than in men. Indeed, cardiovascular drug efficacy in women is different from that in men, with recent studies highlighting serious side effects of angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors and β-blockers in postmenopausal women. Despite these sex differences, sex-specific clinical practice guidelines are still sparse, as is the consideration of a woman's hormonal status. In addition, preclinical models of immune-mediated hypertension are still mainly performed in male animals. The goal of this review is to highlight recent advancements in the field of sex differences in immune-mediated hypertension and to identify the major gaps in understanding immune mechanisms that lead to hypertension development in males and females, and as menopause progresses.

articles.title: Biological Aging Associates With Preeclampsia and Gestational Hypertension.
articles.authors: Li X, Mo Y, Lin Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Biological aging is a fundamental driver of chronic disease, yet its role in the cause of preeclampsia and gestational hypertension remains poorly defined.
METHODS: We used a multimodal framework that triangulated genetic, epidemiological, and experimental approaches to assess the associations of biological aging with preeclampsia and gestational hypertension. Publicly available human and mouse transcriptomic data were analyzed to identify shared aging- and preeclampsia-associated signatures, while the potential of nicotinic acid to alleviate aging- and preeclampsia-related features was further evaluated in experimental models.
RESULTS: Two-sample Mendelian randomization demonstrated that biological age acceleration was associated with higher odds of preeclampsia (odds ratio, 1.55 [95% CI, 1.22-1.96]; P=2.67×10-4) and gestational hypertension (odds ratio, 1.56 [95% CI, 1.12-2.19]; P=0.009), while positive genetic correlations were also observed for both outcomes. In the nested case-control study, higher early pregnancy biological age acceleration was consistently associated with preeclampsia risk in both primary (odds ratio, 1.16 [95% CI, 1.01-1.35]; P=0.047) and sensitivity (odds ratio, 1.14 [95% CI, 1.03-1.29]; P=0.042) analyses, with the associations persisting after covariate adjustment and exclusion of systolic blood pressure from biological age acceleration calculation. Mouse models exhibited preeclampsia-like features accompanied by concordant alterations in biological age-related biomarkers and telomere dysfunction. These changes were partially attenuated by nicotinic acid treatment, whereas placental organoids showed limited growth responses to nicotinic acid. Complementing these phenotypic observations, transcriptomic analyses identified shared aging- and preeclampsia-associated signatures across human and mouse data sets.
CONCLUSIONS: Convergent evidence links biological aging with preeclampsia and gestational hypertension, particularly biological age acceleration with preeclampsia. Experimental findings provide complementary context but do not establish a specific mechanism or therapeutic role for nicotinic acid.

articles.title: Beyond Inoperability: Living With Advanced Ovarian Cancer. A Qualitative Study.
articles.authors: Paulsen A, Fegran L, Rabben J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Women with advanced ovarian cancer often face prognostic uncertainty, and many are deemed inoperable due to strict criteria for primary surgery, yet little is known about their experiences when cytoreductive surgery is not feasible.
OBJECTIVE: To explore how women with inoperable ovarian cancer experience and make sense of the decision that cytoreductive surgical treatment is not feasible.
METHODS: Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 12 women (October 2023-April 2024) diagnosed with inoperable ovarian cancer, and data were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis following Braun and Clarke.
RESULTS: The analysis generated three themes: (1) being Informed that surgery was not feasible: emotional responses shaped by expectations and preparedness, (2) making sense of the information: understanding and accepting the decision, and (3) adjusting to the decision: living between hope and awareness of limited time.
CONCLUSION: When cytoreductive surgery was not an option, women generally adapted by focusing on treatment and everyday life. Clear communication and follow-up may support understanding and confidence in the treatment plan.

articles.title: Weight-loss effects of GLP-1 receptor agonists in reproductive-age women with overweight or obesity and polycystic ovary syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.authors: Wu HY, Zhang M, Yao F
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In reproductive-aged women with polycystic ovary syndrome, overweight or obesity exacerbates metabolic and reproductive risks; lifestyle interventions and metformin have limited weight-loss effects, and more effective pharmacological weight-loss strategies are urgently needed. The aim of this article is to evaluate the weight-loss and body-shape outcomes of GLP-1 receptor agonists in reproductive-aged women with overweight or obesity and PCOS, and to assess risk of bias and certainty of evidence.
METHODS: Multiple databases and trial registry platforms were searched (2015.1-2025.12), and parallel RCTs in reproductive-aged women with overweight or obesity and PCOS comparing GLP-1 receptor agonists with non-GLP-1 regimens were included. The primary outcome was body weight change, secondary outcomes were BMI and waist circumference, and the exploratory outcome was visceral adiposity. A random-effects meta-analysis was performed, with effect sizes as mean difference or Hedges-corrected standardized mean difference, and RoB 2 and GRADE were used to assess risk of bias and certainty of evidence.
RESULTS: Five RCTs (N.=319) were included. Compared with controls, GLP-1 receptor agonists significantly reduced body weight (MD -2.80 kg, 95% CI: -3.94~-1.66), BMI (MD -1.02 kg/m2, 95% CI: -1.41~-0.62), and waist circumference (MD -3.53 cm, 95% CI: -4.63~-2.42), and sensitivity analyses showed consistent directions. An exploratory subgroup analysis suggested a potentially larger effect with monotherapy (-3.43 vs. -2.04 kg, P=0.021); this finding is based on a limited number of comparisons and should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating. However, because the pooled estimate combines monotherapy and combination-regimen trials with different comparators (placebo, metformin, or calorie-restricted diet), this result should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory. Pooled analysis of visceral adiposity (k=3) showed a reduction (SMD -0.73, 95% CI: -1.35~-0.11), but precision…
