CONCLUSIONS: In reproductive-aged women with overweight or obesity and PCOS, GLP-1 receptor agonists may offer weight-loss benefits and improvements in central obesity compared with conventional regimens; however, these findings are derived from a small, clinically heterogeneous pool of trials with short follow-up and low-certainty evidence. The pooled estimates should therefore be interpreted with caution and considered hypothesis-generating rather than definitive.

articles.title: Premenopausal Depression and Risk of Cardiovascular Disease After Menopause: A Large Real-World Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Raju P, Jiang LF, Kutty A et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: While depression has been linked to adverse cardiometabolic profiles in postmenopausal women, its temporal relationship with cardiovascular disease (CVD) when occurring before menopause remains unclear. This study examined whether depression diagnosed prior to menopause was associated with incident CVD after menopause.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network. Postmenopausal women were assigned to 2 cohorts: cohort 1 included women with depression diagnosed before menopause and without preexisting CVD, premature menopause, or conventional CVD risk factors (smoking, diabetes mellitus, hypertension, dyslipidemia, overweight/obesity, or family history of ischemic heart disease); cohort 2 included comparable women without premenopausal depression. Propensity score matching balanced baseline characteristics, including age at menopause, current age, and ethnicity. Risk differences and risk ratios (RRs) with 95% CI were calculated to compare incident CVD (myocardial infarction, coronary heart disease, stroke, heart failure, or cardiovascular death). Time-to-event outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier curves and log-rank testing, and hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated using Cox proportional-hazards regression.
RESULTS: Initial queries identified 90,638 women in cohort 1 and 1,237,202 in cohort 2. After matching, 88,884 women remained in each cohort, with a mean (SD) age of 57.6 (11.4) years. Follow-up varies according to database entry time, with maximum follow-up of 20 years. Women with premenopausal depression had a higher incidence of postmenopausal CVD than those without depression (4.0% vs. 3.3%; RR, 1.23; 95% CI, 1.17-1.29; p < 0.001), corresponding to an absolute risk difference of 0.7% (95% CI, 0.6%-0.9%). Because the proportional hazards assumption was not satisfied, the Cox HR was interpreted as a secondary average time-to-event summary rather than as the primary effect estimate. The estimated HR for incident CVD was 1.21 (95% CI, 1.15-1.27; log-rank p < 0.001), representing an average association across the follow-up period rather than a constant hazard over time.
CONCLUSION: Women with premenopausal depression had a higher cumulative incidence of postmenopausal CVD than matched women without depression, suggesting that premenopausal depression may represent a marker of increased cardiovascular vulnerability in midlife women.

articles.title: Functional impact of LRRC17-K108 lactylation on proliferation, apoptosis, and metabolic regulation in endometrial cancer cells.
articles.journal: The Journal of international medical research
articles.authors: Gao T, Wu F, Wang Z
articles.abstract: ObjectiveEndometrial cancer, particularly endometrioid endometrial carcinoma, is a prevalent gynecologic malignancy; however, the molecular mechanisms linking metabolic reprogramming and post-translational modifications remain poorly understood.MethodsHerein, we conducted a bioinformatics reanalysis combined with in vitro functional experiments, analyzed publicly available proteomics and lysine lactylation datasets (ProteomeXchange, PXD065831) and performed functional assays in Ishikawa and HEC-1-B cell lines transfected with LRRC17 variants. The assays included colony formation, 5-ethynyl-2'-deoxyuridine, transwell, terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase-mediated dUTP nick-end labeling, metabolic enzyme activity measurements, and western blotting.ResultsLactylation omics revealed widespread lysine lactylation changes correlating with tumor grade. LRRC17-K108 lactylation (LRRC17-K108la) promoted proliferation and invasion while inhibiting apoptosis in both cell lines. LRRC17-K108la also enhanced G6PDH and L-LDH activities and altered NADP+/NADPH ratios, indicating metabolic reprogramming. RNA-seq followed by Gene Ontology and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes analyses demonstrated enrichment of pathways related to the p53 signaling pathway; these findings were supported by changes in PCNA, RB1, and p-P53 expression.ConclusionsLRRC17-K108la serves as a critical mediator linking metabolic remodeling and cell function in endometrioid endometrial carcinoma. These findings provide mechanistic insights into the role of lactylation in gynecologic cancers and suggest potential therapeutic targets for metabolic and epigenetic intervention in endometrioid endometrial carcinoma.

articles.title: Peripheral and Uterine NK Cell Immunometabolic Concordance: A Minimally Invasive Approach to Endometrial Receptivity Assessment.
articles.journal: American journal of reproductive immunology (New York, N.Y. : 1989)
articles.authors: Celik O, Celik S
articles.abstract:
PROBLEM: Recurrent implantation failure (RIF) occurs even after euploid embryo transfer, indicating a maternal determinant beyond embryo quality. A landmark meta-analysis showed that peripheral NK (pNK) cell numbers do not correlate with endometrial NK (uNK) cell numbers and called for functional rather than numerical assessment.
METHOD OF STUDY: Narrative synthesis of immunometabolism, reproductive immunology, endometrial tissue metabolism, and uterine luminal sampling evidence to develop a testable model.
RESULTS: We propose that pNK cells may exhibit immunometabolic states correlated with, but not identical to, those of endometrial uNK cells (immunometabolic concordance). Concordance does not imply functional equivalence: pNK cells are predominantly cytotoxic, whereas uNK cells are angiogenic and immunomodulatory. We propose three axes, ΔΨm, mtROS, and intracellular lipid load, as measurable determinants of uNK function. Among minimally invasive routes, uterine luminal fluid currently has the most direct feasibility evidence, whereas cervical mucus remains hypothesis-generating and unproven. Assay-specific confounders, including P-glycoprotein-mediated dye efflux, are explicitly addressed. Six testable predictions and a prospective validation protocol are presented.
CONCLUSION: If validated, the model could reduce reliance on endometrial biopsy; if not, it will show that functional NK assessment requires compartment-specific analysis.

articles.title: What's Hot and What's New in Xenotransplantation From the Young Investigator Committee of the IXA-Clinical Science.
articles.authors: Eisenson D, de Mazancourt ES, Ladowski J et al.
articles.abstract: The 2025 International Xenotransplantation Association (IXA) Congress in Geneva, convened in parallel with World Health Organization meetings on xenotransplantation guidance, marked a transition in clinical xenotransplantation from demonstrating that pig organs can function in humans to defining how graft injury is detected, interpreted, and managed in real time. We synthesize the major clinical themes that emerged from the meeting across kidney, heart, liver, and lung xenotransplantation. In kidney xenotransplantation, the NYU and Massachusetts General Hospital living-recipient experiences now delineate two complementary injury patterns-antibody- and complement-driven with a membranoproliferative, IgA-positive, innate-rich phenotype, and T cell-mediated with persistent innate immune activation-both converging on macrophage and NK-cell biology that conventional immunosuppression does not address. The first registration-supporting Phase 1/2/3 trial of a 10-gene-edited xenokidney (EXPAND) has begun, framed by IXA position-paper recommendations and supported by recent FDA approvals. In cardiac xenotransplantation, real-time complement-function monitoring, global longitudinal strain, and donor-derived cell-free DNA emerge as an actionable surveillance toolkit, while other allotransplant biomarkers translate poorly. In liver xenotransplantation, extracorporeal cross-circulation and the first preliminary data describing auxiliary pig-to-human liver transplant (171-day survival) position porcine livers as bridge-support platforms rather than definitive replacements. Lung xenotransplantation remains confined to ex vivo perfusion and short-term preclinical models. Cross-cutting priorities include donor-pig design and individual graft phenotyping that accounts for transgene expression heterogeneity, prospectively validated multimodal monitoring, management of nephrotic-range proteinuria and associated urinary loss of biologic immunosuppressants, and dedicated registry, ethical, and patient-engagement infrastructure to support trustworthy clinical expansion.

articles.title: "I Need a Doctor Online": Online Health Consultation and Perceived Patient-Centered Communication in the Association Between Health-Related Social Media Use and Cancer Screening Intention Among Brazilian Women.
articles.authors: Qiu SS, Zhang L, Xie Q et al.
articles.abstract: Breast and cervical cancer are leading causes of cancer-related deaths among Brazilian women, and regular screenings are vital for reducing mortality and are cost-effective for cancer prevention. In digital health communication environments, understanding how health-related social media use, online health consultation, and perceived patient-centered communication are associated with women's cancer screening intention has important implications for health communication theory and practice. Using cross-sectional national survey data from Brazil (N = 530 women), this study examined whether health-related social media use is associated with women's cancer screening intention and tested a moderated serial mediation model in which online health consultation and perceived patient-centered communication were examined as intervening variables, with online health information overload as a moderator. Results showed that health-related social media use was not directly associated with women's cancer screening intention (β = .021, b = .014, p > .05). However, the hypothesized serial indirect association through online health consultation and perceived patient-centered communication was statistically significant (β = .013, b = .008, bootstrap 95% CI = [.002, .017]). Online health information overload moderated the association between health-related social media use and online health consultation (b = .186, p < .001). Guided by Channel Complementarity Theory and the health communication pathway model, the findings suggest that health-related social media use may be associated with women's cancer screening intention through complementary online consultation and perceived patient-centered communication.

articles.title: Inhaled Glucocorticoids During Pregnancy: A Population-Level Drug Utilization Study in Denmark From 2001 to 2023.
articles.authors: Al-Sagit NNJ, Damkier P, Gram EB
articles.abstract: We investigated trends of inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) use among pregnant women in Denmark from 2001 to 2023 using aggregated data from the Danish Health Data Authority, where recorded prescription redemptions in the National Prescription Register are linked to pregnancies recorded in the Danish Medical Birth Registry. Use of combination preparations (ICS and beta2-agonists) increased substantially (from 1.3 to 21 per 1000 pregnant women), corresponding to a 16-fold increase, while use of single-agent preparations (ICS) decreased gradually (from 17 to 11 per 1000 pregnant women). Combination preparations became more prevalent than single-agent preparations in 2020 among pregnant women, reflecting changes in treatment guidelines and recommendations in 2019. ICS use was higher before than during pregnancy in 2001 (22 vs. 18 per 1000 women) but lower before than during pregnancy in 2023 (30 vs. 32 per 1000 women), with the pattern reversing in 2015. Use during pregnancy was highest among the oldest women (≥ 40 years), with some variation over time, while it fluctuated substantially among the youngest women (≤ 19 years) and increased more steadily among women aged 20-39 years. Overall, our results highlight changes in ICS use among pregnant women that are well aligned with national and international asthma guidelines.

articles.title: Donor-derived cell-free DNA levels predict 3-year outcomes in kidney transplant recipients with stable function.
articles.authors: Cheng D, Cuello Garcia H, Li X et al.
articles.abstract: Donor-derived cell-free DNA (dd-cfDNA) is a promising noninvasive biomarker for detecting acute rejection in kidney transplant recipients, but its prognostic value in patients with stable graft function remains unclear. This study evaluated the association between dd-cfDNA levels and long-term clinical outcomes. We retrospectively analyzed 267 kidney transplant recipients with stable renal function between January 2020 and July 2023, stratified by plasma dd-cfDNA levels into three groups: A (<1%, n = 205), B (1-<2%, n = 34), and C (≥2%, n = 28). Each patient contributed a single index dd-cfDNA measurement obtained during routine outpatient follow-up, which defined baseline; the interval from transplantation to the index measurement did not differ among groups (p = 0.124). Clinical outcomes included changes in serum creatinine, incidence of adverse events, graft loss, patient mortality, and biopsy findings over three years. Creatinine levels remained stable in Group A but increased significantly in Groups B and C from baseline to year 3 (1.38 to 1.96 mg/dL, p < 0.0001; and 1.36 to 1.84 mg/dL, p = 0.0019, respectively). Adverse events were significantly more frequent in Groups B (41.2%) and C (42.9%) compared with Group A (9.8%, p < 0.001). Graft loss rates were 0.98%, 11.76%, and 7.14% in Groups A, B, and C, respectively (p = 0.002), and mortality showed a significant increasing trend across groups (p = 0.023). Elevated dd-cfDNA levels are associated with adverse long-term outcomes in kidney transplant recipients with stable graft function, suggesting that dd-cfDNA may serve as a valuable tool for early risk stratification and long-term monitoring in transplant care.

articles.title: Immune protection against anogenital HPV in Rwandan women with and without HIV following the introduction of quadrivalent HPV vaccination.
articles.journal: Journal of the National Cancer Institute
articles.authors: Castle PE, Rutwaza MG, Tuyishime O et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Prophylactic human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccines have demonstrated population effectiveness in preventing cervical cancer. Evidence for protection of women with HIV (WWH) is lacking. In 2011, Rwanda introduced quadrivalent HPV vaccination nationally, primarily targeting girls in grade 6, providing an opportunity to evaluate its long-term effectiveness in WWH compared to women without HIV (WWoH).
METHODS: Data from 3,058 of 3,148 (97.1%) Rwandan women with complete results from four sub-cohorts recruited and enrolled were analyzed: 769 WWoH born before 1996, 755 WWoH born 1996 or more recently, 773 WWH born before 1996, and 761 WWH born 1996 or more recently. We tested vaginal and anal specimens for high-risk HPV genotypes. We used self-report of HPV vaccination and measured anti-HPV16 antibodies levels by HPV16 VLP ELISA as HPV vaccination proxies to examine the protective effects, using logistic regression, of HPV vaccination on vaginal and/or anal (combined, "anogenital") HPV16 and/or HPV18 (HPV16/18).
RESULTS: Self-reported HPV vaccination (vs. not) (adjusted odds ratio (aOR)=2.71, 95%CI=2.29-3.21) was most strongly positively, and WWH (vs. WWoH) (aOR=0.68, 95%CI=0.60-0.78) was most strongly negatively, associated with higher anti-HPV16 antibody levels. Anogenital HPV16/18 prevalence decreased from 11.0% to 2.5% in those with the lowest to highest quartile of anti-HPV16 antibody levels, respectively (ptrend<0.001). The highest quartile of anti-HPV16 antibody levels was associated with lower anogenital HPV16/18 (aOR=0.23, 95%CI=0.13-0.38); similar associations were observed for the highest quartile in WWH (aOR=0.23; 95%CI=0.12-0.46) as in WWoH (aOR=0.24, 95%CI=0.10-0.58).
CONCLUSION: WWH who were likely vaccinated against HPV vaccination had lower prevalence of anogenital HPV16/18.

articles.title: Integrative Multiomics Analysis and Machine Learning Identify Core Host Targets of Gut Microbial Metabolites in Gestational Diabetes Mellitus.
articles.authors: Zhai P, Song X, Wang H et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study is to systematically investigate molecular mechanisms associated with gut microbial metabolite effects in gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), and to screen and validate key host targets to provide foundations for early diagnosis and targeted intervention.
METHODS: Gut microbial metabolite targets from the gutMGene database were integrated with GDM patient differentially expressed genes from the GEO database (GSE103552, 11 GDM vs. 8 controls). Core targets were screened via protein-protein interaction network and machine learning, then validated by Western blot (n = 5 per group). Functional enrichment analysis was used to elucidate biological pathways; single-cell transcriptomic data (GSE173193: 2 GDM vs. 2 controls; GSE212309: 4 GDM vs. 3 controls) validated cell-specific target expression; immune signature analysis explored microenvironment correlations. Drug-likeness and toxicity were assessed for candidate metabolites.
RESULTS: Seventeen intersection targets between gut microbiota metabolites and GDM were identified, primarily enriched in AGE-RAGE, PI3K-Akt, and cell cycle signaling pathways. Machine learning consistently screened GSK3B and CDK4 as core targets. Western blot analysis confirmed significant upregulation of GSK3B in GDM placental tissues. Single-cell analysis revealed high GSK3B expression in extravillous trophoblasts and CDK4 downregulation in villous cytotrophoblasts. Both genes showed associations with immune cell signature scores. The constructed metabolite-target network revealed complex interaction relationships involving 26 metabolites and 51 gut microbes.
CONCLUSION: GSK3B and CDK4 were identified as candidate host targets associated with gut microbiota metabolites in GDM, potentially contributing to pathogenesis through placental cell function and immune microenvironment changes, providing targets for mechanistic investigation and therapeutic exploration.

articles.title: Is It Safe to Treat Patients with Botulinum Toxin A During the Peri-Conception Period of Pregnancy? A Systematic Review of the Literature.
articles.authors: Azar SS, Darvish N, Patel NN et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Risks of peri-conception exposure to botulinum toxin remain poorly characterized.
OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate the frequency of reported adverse maternal and fetal outcomes, including miscarriage, preterm labor, and congenital anomalies, in patients undergoing botulinum toxin injection in the peri-conception period compared to the general United States obstetric population.
METHODS: A PRISMA-guided systematic review identified studies (inception through November 7, 2025) reporting patient outcomes after botulinum toxin injection during the peri-conception period (3 months before and after conception). Reviews, editorials, and animal studies were excluded.
RESULTS: Of 586 articles, 10 met inclusion criteria. 80% of studies were case reports or series. Included studies comprised 136 women and 143 pregnancies (median age 33.5 years). Botulinum toxin was most commonly given for migraine (88%), dosed from 2.5 to 500 units. Five pregnancies (3%; n = 5; 95% CI: 1.5 - 8.0%) resulted in miscarriage. One case of preterm labor with fetal renal anomaly and one case of fetal growth restriction were reported.
CONCLUSION: Peri-conception botulinum toxin exposure was not associated with increased adverse outcomes compared with population rates, though evidence is limited by small, heterogenous studies.

articles.title: A Machine Learning Model for Predicting 28-Day Mortality in Critically Ill Ischemic Stroke Patients With Systemic Inflammatory Response Syndrome: A Retrospective Cohort Study Based on MIMIC-IV and eICU Databases.
articles.authors: Liu H, Fan C, Zou J
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS) commonly complicates ischemic stroke (IS) in critically ill patients and is associated with increased mortality. We aimed to develop and externally validate an interpretable model for predicting 28-day mortality in this population.
METHODS: We used the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) database for model development and internal validation and the eICU database for external validation. Critically ill IS patients with SIRS during the first ICU day were included. The model predicted mortality occurring between the 24-hour landmark and day 28 after ICU admission. MIMIC-IV patients were randomly divided into training and testing sets at a 7:3 ratio. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression selected predictors for six algorithms. The model with the highest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) in the testing set was externally validated and compared with the Oxford Acute Severity of Illness Score (OASIS) alone. Performance was assessed using discrimination, calibration, and decision curve analysis.
RESULTS: The study included 2,438 patients: 1,620 from MIMIC-IV and 818 from eICU. Nine predictors were selected: age, white blood cell count, red blood cell distribution width, blood urea nitrogen, anion gap, Charlson Comorbidity Index, SIRS score, OASIS, and mechanical ventilation. Among the six models evaluated in the testing set, logistic regression (LR) achieved the highest AUC (0.846) and was therefore selected for external validation. In the external validation cohort, the LR model achieved a higher AUC than OASIS alone (0.794 vs. 0.758), and showed reasonable calibration and potential clinical utility.
CONCLUSION: We developed and externally validated an interpretable ML-based model for predicting 28-day mortality in critically ill IS patients with SIRS. The LR model showed good discrimination and reasonable calibration in external validation. Prospective multicenter validation and clinical-impact assessment are required before implementation.

articles.title: The Barriers and Facilitators for People With Bipolar Disorder Deciding to Attend and/or Complete Cancer Screening of the Cervix, Breast and Bowel: A Qualitative Study Using Normalisation Process Theory.
articles.authors: Sykes K, Barker J, Giles EL et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bipolar disorder affects 1.3 million people in the United Kingdom. People with bipolar disorder are less likely, than the general population to attend and/or complete cancer screening.
AIMS: To explore the barriers and facilitators towards thinking about, and/or completing cervical, breast and colorectal screening by people with bipolar disorder.
METHODS: Semi-structured interviews with 27 people living with bipolar disorder in the North-East and Cumbria (January 2023 to June 2023). Deductive thematic analysis was completed using the constructs of Normalisation Process Theory (NPT). NPT was used to ensure recommendations from the study were developed through an implementation lens.
RESULTS: Participants with bipolar disorder highlighted how their mental health influenced their decision to complete cancer screening, or not. Most participants understand what screening was and why it was important to complete screening. However, they described barriers such as anxiety, forgetfulness and fear in completing screening. As well as systemic barriers such as appointments not being at a good time, unfamiliar screening locations and discomfort in waiting rooms were also specifically highlighted for cervical and breast screening. Whilst for colorectal screening, home testing kits were seen as useful, participants felt unsupported in completing the kit, and feared completing the kit wrongly.
CONCLUSIONS: The identification of barriers and facilitators to cancer screening has highlighted a clear need to increase awareness and providing tailored support for people with bipolar disorder. Offering multiple screening options could further improve screening participation among the group.

articles.title: Predictive ability of hyperspectral signatures from single immobilized spermatozoa as a novel approach to non-invasive sperm selection during ICSI.
articles.authors: Gil Juliá M, Pacheco-Rendón RM, de Los Santos JM et al.
articles.abstract:
STUDY QUESTION: Can hyperspectral imaging of single immobilized spermatozoa prior to ICSI be used to characterize individual spermatozoa quality and develop predictive models for fertilization, blastulation, and blastocyst usability?
SUMMARY ANSWER: Hyperspectral imaging characterization of individual immobilized spermatozoa was successfully implemented prior to ICSI and enabled the development of predictive models for key reproductive outcomes.
WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY: Sperm selection during ICSI is mainly based on morphology and motility, which provide limited information about functional competence. Most techniques capable of assessing molecular sperm quality are destructive and cannot be applied to the injected spermatozoon. Hyperspectral imaging (HS) is a non-invasive technique capable of generating molecular spectral fingerprints of individual cells.
STUDY DESIGN, SIZE, DURATION: This prospective two-phase study was conducted between March 2020 and August 2024 and included 93 couples undergoing ICSI cycles at a single IVF centre.
PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS, SETTING, METHODS: Single immobilized spermatozoa were imaged prior to ICSI using a hyperspectral camera coupled to a micromanipulation microscope. Phase I evaluated the feasibility and short-term technical repeatability of hyperspectral acquisition, as well as preliminary classification consistency across repeated acquisitions. Phase II included a safety evaluation using a sibling donor-oocyte design and the development of predictive models using hyperspectral spectra and clinical data. Machine learning models based on XGBoost decision trees were trained to predict fertilization, blastulation, and usable blastocyst formation.
MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE: Hyperspectral imaging was successfully implemented prior to ICSI. Phase I supported high short-term technical repeatability under stable acquisition conditions, with a global intraclass correlation coefficient of 0.999. Exploratory spectral classification across repeated technical acquisitions achieved a sensitivity of 93.84% and a specificity of 96.76%. In the safety evaluation, fertilization, blastulation, and usable blastocyst rates were comparable between HS-ICSI and standard ICSI groups. Predictive models based on hyperspectral spectra and clinical data were developed, with chained models integrating both data types showing the most favourable balance between predictive precision and uncertainty among the…
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: N/A.

articles.title: Cardiac Structure and Function After Preeclampsia, Including Global Longitudinal Strain: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Sethi Y, Kumar S, Arora M et al.
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia is associated with an increased long-term risk of cardiovascular disease and heart failure, particularly heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. Whether abnormalities of cardiac structure and function persist after delivery, and whether global longitudinal strain (GLS) detects subclinical myocardial dysfunction when left ventricular ejection fraction is preserved, remains incompletely defined. We updated the evidence on postpartum cardiac structure and function after preeclampsia and synthesized postpartum GLS. Of the 27 studies in the index review, 25 provided re-extractable arm-level data; with 5 new studies, the data set comprised 30 reports and 32 comparisons. Prior preeclampsia was associated with a higher left ventricular mass index (MD, 5.24 g/m2; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.77-7.70; k = 25), greater relative wall thickness (MD, 0.03; 95% CI, 0.01-0.05; k = 16), higher E/e' (MD, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.42-1.51; k = 15), and lower E/A (MD, -0.10; 95% CI, -0.19 to -0.02; k = 23). Left ventricular ejection fraction did not differ (MD, -0.62 percentage points; 95% CI, -1.51 to 0.27; k = 25), nor did isovolumic relaxation or deceleration time. GLS was less negative after preeclampsia (MD, 2.05 percentage points; 95% CI, 0.34-3.76; k = 4).

articles.title: Comparative Effects of Technology-Based Educational Interventions for Improving Cancer Screening Among Migrant Women: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.authors: Krzyż EZ, Lin CJ, Hulu SRK et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Migrant women have lower participation in breast and cervical cancer screening than non-migrant populations, contributing to delayed diagnoses and health inequities. Technology-based educational interventions may improve screening uptake; however, their comparative effectiveness remains unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate and compare the effectiveness of technology-based educational interventions for improving cancer screening uptake among migrant women using a network meta-analysis.
METHODS: A systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials was conducted across 6 electronic databases and clinical trial registries from inception to December 24, 2025. Eligible studies included migrant women receiving technology-based educational interventions to improve cancer screening uptake. A frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis was performed in R using the netmeta package. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using Cochrane RoB 2.0 and Confidence in Network Meta-Analysis.
RESULTS: Fifteen studies (16 datasets) were included. Multicomponent interventions significantly increased screening uptake compared with usual care (odds ratio 5.50, 95% confidence interval 2.56-11.82) and ranked as the most effective strategy (P score = 0.92). Text messaging, voice messaging, and video-based interventions demonstrated positive but nonsignificant effects.
CONCLUSIONS: Multicomponent technology-based educational interventions were more effective than single-modality approaches in improving cancer screening uptake among migrant women.
IMPLICATIONS FOR ONCOLOGY NURSING PRACTICE: Oncology nurses may play a central role in delivering multicomponent, culturally tailored interventions that combine digital education with personalized support, patient navigation, and community engagement. By integrating human connection with technology-assisted care, nurses may help address the complex cultural, informational, and access-related barriers that contribute to inequities in preventive cancer services.

articles.title: Hypogonadism in men with prolactinoma.
articles.authors: Broul M, Hujová A, Radovnická L et al.
articles.abstract: Hypogonadism is one of the most consequential manifestations of prolactinoma in men, yet its course is often reduced to a single testosterone result. Prolactin excess can reversibly suppress hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal signalling, whereas large tumours may damage gonadotroph function and other pituitary axes. These mechanisms create a dynamic phenotype that includes androgen-deficiency symptoms, impaired spermatogenesis, anaemia, adverse body composition, skeletal fragility and sexual dysfunction. Dopamine agonists are the usual first causal treatment, and transsphenoidal surgery is appropriate in selected patients; neither biochemical control nor tumour shrinkage proves gonadal or sexual recovery. Contemporary cohorts indicate that testosterone recovery occurs mainly during the first year but may continue through 24 months, and is more likely with smaller tumours, higher baseline or six-month testosterone, earlier prolactin normalisation and preserved pituitary function. Men with persistent symptomatic hypogonadism require a fertility-sensitive decision: continued observation when recovery remains plausible, consideration of testosterone replacement when fertility is not sought, or specialist gonadotrophin treatment when fertility is desired; clomiphene is an off-label option supported only by small uncontrolled studies. Sexual desire and erectile function should be measured separately because both may remain impaired despite eugonadism and require additional cardiometabolic, medication and psychosexual assessment. This Review integrates endocrine, reproductive and sexual outcomes into a time-resolved framework. The central principle is that prolactin control, endogenous gonadal recovery, fertility and sexual recovery are related but non-equivalent treatment goals.

articles.title: Polygenic scores improve persistent smoking prediction over single variants and phenotypic factors.
articles.authors: Jones SK, Benton ML, Tindle HA et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Smoking is a leading cause of preventable death and illness. Genetically-informed precision interventions are feasible, but whether genetic risk for persistent smoking can be captured by high-risk single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) or requires comprehensive assessment using whole-genome polygenic risk scores (PRS) is unknown. This study compared discriminatory performance of a baseline model for long-term persistent smoking based on phenotypic predictors with models that (1) integrate phenotypic predictors with three well-characterized SNPs and (2) incorporate phenotypic predictors and PRS for smoking cessation.
DESIGN: Data were from the Nurse's Health Study (NHS) and NHS II, two all-female, prospective cohorts that collected data every 2 years. Two independent data sources were used from baseline (1976 for NHS and 1989 for NHS II) and up to 2014 for NHS and 2015 for NHS II.
SETTING: Population-based, longitudinal cohort studies of nurses from 17 states in the United States.
PARTICIPANTS: Female, baseline ever-smokers of European ancestry with whole-genome genetic data (NHS: n = 10 017; NHS II: n = 2793).
MEASUREMENTS: Baseline models included phenotypic and other predictors influencing smoking behavior: age, year of follow-up, smoking intensity, menopausal status, hormone replacement therapy use, early initiation of smoking and body mass index (kg/m2). Additional genetic predictors for persistent smoking were estimated by (1) three well-characterized risk SNPs for smoking (CHRNA5 rs16969968, CYP2A6 rs56113850, DRD2/ANKK1 rs1800497) and (2) PRS. The primary outcome of the study was improvement in predictive performance as measured by the area under the receiver operating characteristics curve (AUC) between baseline models for long-term persistent smoking and models adding genetic risk with (1) risk SNPs and (2) PRS.
RESULTS: Within NHS, the baseline model showed moderate predictive performance for persistent smoking with an AUC of 0.674. Adding SNPs showed similar performance (AUC = 0.675), whereas adding PRS statistically significantly improved…
SUMMARY: Among females of European ancestry, polygenic risk scores appear to enhance identification of individuals at high risk for long-term, persistent smoking compared with single well-known risk variants and phenotypic predictors. Combining genetic and phenotypic factors can improve risk stratification and precision intervention guidance for long-term smoking abstinence management.

articles.title: Development of a specialised reproductive rheumatology consultation service: analysis of referral patterns across preconception, pregnancy, and lactation.
articles.authors: Vossen D, Kernder A, Odehnal D et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Women with inflammatory rheumatic and musculoskeletal disease (iRMD) face unique challenges during preconception, pregnancy, and lactation. In 2024, a specialised consultation service was developed and implemented at the tertiary rheumatology centre of the Rheumazentrum Ruhrgebiet, Ruhr University Bochum, Herne, Germany, to address these specific needs.
METHODS: Demographic characteristics, disease- and treatment-related data, reproductive status, referring physician, reasons for consultation, and recommendations for disease management were collected between 1 January 2024 and 3 April 2025.
RESULTS: Overall, 57 patients were included; the mean age was 33.3 ± 4.4 years and the mean disease duration was 6.3 ± 4.8 years. Almost all patients (94.7%) had a confirmed diagnosis of an iRMD. 57.9% were planning a pregnancy, 40.4% were pregnant, and 1.8% were breastfeeding. At baseline, 21.8% were receiving csDMARDs and 50.9% were receiving bDMARDs. Glucocorticoid use was documented in 16.1%. Patients were referred by rheumatologists (35.7%), the in-house outpatient clinic (37.5%), general practitioners (14.3%), gynaecologists (10.7%), and the in-house inpatient clinic (1.8%). The most frequent reasons for consultation were patient concerns regarding pregnancy and medication safety. Consultation reasons differed descriptively between patients in the preconception period and pregnant patients; however, these exploratory differences should be interpreted with caution. Recommendations made during consultation included modification of DMARD therapy (35.1%), initiation of fetal bradycardia screening (19.3%), and preeclampsia prophylaxis (8.8%).
CONCLUSION: A dedicated reproductive rheumatology consultation service provides structured support for women with iRMDs throughout preconception, pregnancy, and lactation. Medication adjustments and targeted preventive measures were recommended for more than one-third of patients, highlighting the potential value of preconception referral and specialized reproductive rheumatology consultation.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Changes in nurses' knowledge and observed clinical practice following a competency-based educational intervention in pelvic organ prolapse and urinary incontinence care: a quasi-experimental single-group pretest-posttest study.
articles.authors: Elrefay BW, El-Nemer AMR, Fadel EA et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In the assessment of pelvic organ prolapse (POP), approximately half of women may present with varying degrees of pelvic organ descent, although many do not exhibit clinical symptoms. Therefore, nurses have an important role in timely assessment, prevention of complications, and provision of appropriate supportive care. This study aimed to evaluate changes in nurses' knowledge and observed clinical practice following a competency-based educational intervention for the care of women with POP and urinary incontinence (UI).
METHODS: The study followed a quasi-experimental, single-group pretest-posttest design and included 60 nurses working in the outpatient department of the Urology and Nephrology Center, Mansoura University, Egypt. Data were collected using three researcher-developed instruments: the Demographic Structured Interview Schedule, the Nurses' Knowledge Structured Interview, and the Nurses' Observational Practice Checklist. Nurses' knowledge and observed clinical practice were assessed before the intervention and reassessed immediately after completion of the educational intervention.
RESULTS: Statistically significant immediate post-intervention improvements were observed in nurses' knowledge and clinical practice. The mean overall knowledge score increased from 17.05 ± 1.92 at baseline to 19.18 ± 1.97 immediately after the intervention (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, p < .001). Perineal care practice scores increased from 26.80 ± 6.93 to 49.33 ± 3.93, pessary insertion practice scores increased from 25.33 ± 6.81 to 50.73 ± 3.85, and pelvic floor muscle exercise instruction scores increased from 9.80 ± 3.25 to 20.42 ± 1.94 (all p < .001).
CONCLUSION: Participation in the competency-based educational intervention was associated with significant immediate improvements in nurses' knowledge and observed clinical practice related to POP and UI care. These findings represent short-term post-training changes, and further controlled studies with longer follow-up are needed to determine whether these improvements are sustained over time.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06639217, registered on 10 October 2024. Retrospectively registered.

articles.title: Pregnancy and neonatal outcomes of sequential embryo transfer versus double cleavage-stage embryo transfer and double blastocyst transfer in frozen-thawed embryo transfer cycles: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Chen X, Yi R, Zhou S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sequential embryo transfer (Seq-ET), involving the transfer of a cleavage-stage embryo followed by a blastocyst within the same frozen-thawed embryo transfer (FET) cycle, has been proposed as an alternative strategy to improve reproductive outcomes. However, evidence regarding its effectiveness and neonatal safety compared to the traditional double embryo transfer (DET) in the general infertile population remains limited.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study incorporated 2,959 FET cycles, using Seq-ET (n = 165), and DET strategies at Day 3 cleavage (D3-DET, n = 1,043) or Day 5/6 blastocyst (D5/6-DET, n = 1,751) stage in our reproductive center (2023.07-2025.01). The Seq-ET group was separately matched with the D3-DET or D5/6-DET group by propensity score matching (PSM). Propensity score-adjusted logistic regression analyses were used to control for confounding factors. The live birth rate (LBR), biochemical pregnancy rate, clinical pregnancy rate (CPR), implantation rate, miscarriage rate, multiple pregnancy rate, multiple live birth rate and neonatal outcomes were analyzed between groups.
RESULTS: Seq-ET had significantly higher biochemical pregnancy rate (81.99% vs. 63.52%, P < 0.001), CPR (67.08% vs. 43.57%, P < 0.001), and LBR (51.55% vs. 33.86%, P < 0.001) than D3-DET. Compared with D5/6-DET, Seq-ET showed comparable biochemical pregnancy rate, CPR, and LBR, but was associated with a significantly lower multiple pregnancy rate (20.91% vs. 33.94%, P = 0.014) and higher miscarriage rate (22.73% vs. 13.94%, P = 0.048). Neonatal outcomes were analyzed separately for singleton and twin live births. No significant differences were observed among singleton live births. Among twin live births, D5/6-DET had shorter gestational age at delivery, while other neonatal outcomes did not differ between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Seq-ET yielded superior pregnancy outcomes compared with D3-DET and achieved pregnancy outcomes comparable to D5/6-DET while reducing the risk of multiple pregnancy, although a higher miscarriage rate was observed in the Seq-ET group. Neonatal outcomes were generally comparable between groups, with the except of shorter gestational age at delivery for twin live births in D5/6-DET group. These findings indicate that Seq-ET may serve as a viable alternative double embryo transfer strategy in FET cycles.

articles.title: The German ELSA Study: experiences of counselling and care in situations of unwanted pregnancy: a qualitative typology of women who terminate an unwanted pregnancy.
articles.authors: Wyrobisch-Krüger A, Hahn D, Herzig L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The contribution reports the findings from a set of interviews investigating the social and health resources and concerns of women who had terminated an unwanted pregnancy. The goal was to investigate their actions and experiences in connection with decision-making and termination. The research was conducted at Fulda University, Germany, and was part of the research project investigating the situations and experiences of women who had experienced an unwanted pregnancy, and the associated counselling and other services.
METHODS: Twenty-five semi-structured interviews conducted between February and August 2022 and analysed using the Documentary Method to generate a typology. The interviewed women were aged between 17 and 41.
RESULTS: Decisions about abortion are made in light of problems and resources, and are influenced by current and future (anticipated) life plans. Abortion is understood as an opportunity to realise or safeguard life planning (in relation to career, family, health and socioeconomic status). Four types were identified: "preserve" (protecting the achieved), "stabilise" (guarding agency), "orientate" (keeping options open), and "realise" (pursuing specific life goals). Notably, the identified types correspond broadly to specific age groups and phases (for example starting a family, birth of children, career development, or need for stability in challenging circumstances). The phase of life the woman was in at the time of the unwanted pregnancy was highly influential.
CONCLUSION: It is too rarely acknowledged that the decision to terminate a pregnancy may also represent a positive choice. For the interviewed women, a termination offered the possibility to retain agency in difficult situations, to strengthen their autonomy, to preserve development opportunities, and to protect existing achievements. The decision to terminate a pregnancy should therefore be understood as a resource-orientated aspect of biographical development.

articles.title: Age-platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio phenotypes and prevalent osteoporotic fracture in postmenopausal women: cross-cohort analysis with interpretable machine learning.
articles.authors: Li Z, Niu S, Liu Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fragility fractures in postmenopausal women often occur before the bone mineral density (BMD) T-score reaches - 2.5. Chronic low-grade inflammation contributes to postmenopausal bone loss, but inflammatory markers have not entered fracture-risk assessment.
METHODS: We applied Gaussian mixture modeling to age and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR) in 1,000 women aged ≥ 50 years from NHANES 2005-2018, using age as a proxy for postmenopausal status and osteoporosis as the outcome. Three age-PLR subgroups were identified and mapped by standardized Euclidean distance to 572 inpatients assessed for bone health at Deyang People's Hospital (2023-2025), where prevalent osteoporotic fracture was the outcome. An NHANES XGBoost model generated a source-derived osteoporosis probability feature for the hospital fracture model; it was not interpreted as a direct fracture probability. We performed exploratory age-stratified PLR analyses.
RESULTS: In NHANES, the High-Risk and Elderly-Low subgroups had higher covariate-adjusted odds of osteoporosis than Low-Risk (odds ratio [OR] 3.64, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.94-6.84, P < 0.001; and OR 3.97, 95% CI 2.37-6.65, P < 0.001, respectively). Robust regression down-weighting outliers attenuated the High-Risk estimate to 1.21 (95% CI 0.69-2.14, P = 0.565). In the hospital cohort, High-Risk was associated with prevalent osteoporotic fracture after covariate adjustment (OR 2.20, 95% CI 1.15-4.22, P = 0.017) and BMD adjustment (OR 2.09, P = 0.027). Adding the source-derived feature improved discrimination compared with the hospital-only model (area under the curve 0.716 vs. 0.675; DeLong P = 0.025), but provided limited incremental net benefit. PLR was associated with osteoporosis among women aged 50-64 years (OR 1.09 per 10-unit increase, P = 0.013), but not in older groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Source-derived age-PLR phenotypes were associated with osteoporosis in NHANES and prevalent fracture in a selected hospital cohort. The feature modestly improved discrimination but showed limited incremental clinical utility. These cross-sectional findings do not establish temporality, prediction, or independence from BMD and require prospective external validation.

articles.title: Knowledge, attitudes, and practices of general practitioners regarding menopause management and hormone replacement therapy in primary care: a cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Jiang Y, Gu X, Zhou Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A large population of middle-aged and elderly women has emerged, making menopause management (MM) and hormone replacement therapy (HRT) a major public health challenge in China. General practitioners (GPs) serve as the gatekeepers of the healthcare system; however, there is a noticeable deficiency in their knowledge and practices regarding MM and HRT.
METHOD: This cross-sectional study was conducted from March 1 to August 31, 2025, at 56 randomly selected community health service centers in Shanghai, China. We employed convenience and snowball sampling methods to recruit licensed GPs, and data were collected using a 21-item questionnaire covering demographic and occupational information, knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding MM and HRT, as well as perceived barriers. Statistical analyses were performed using Stata/SE 15.0, with descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and multivariable logistic regression. A two-tailed P < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: A total of 828 GPs participated. Most identified lifestyle adjustment (97.8%) and psychological counseling (97.6%) as health priorities, while 83.7% recognized HRT as relevant. For HRT benefits, 97.3% recognized symptom relief, 90.5% recognized osteoporosis prevention, and 85.7% recognized cardiovascular risk reduction. For HRT risks, 89.4% identified endometrial cancer, 86.8% identified breast cancer, and 73.6% identified thrombosis. Only 15.9% of GPs were familiar with the indications and contraindications of HRT, and 13.7% with its different administration routes. Regarding attitudes, 40.4% held a positive attitude toward recommending HRT. In practice, 15.1% actively recommended HRT, and 5.4% had ever prescribed it. Multivariable logistic regression identified HRT availability at the community health center (adjusted OR = 56.58, 95% CI: 16.21-197.54, P < 0.001) and experience as a gynecologist (adjusted OR = 34.52, 95% CI: 11.70-101.88, P < 0.001) as the strongest independent predictors of prescribing behavior; overall attitude toward HRT (adjusted OR = 19.60, 95% CI: 8.25-46.56,…
CONCLUSION: Substantial gaps exist between GPs' knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding MM and HRT. Prescribing is driven by drug availability and gynecological experience, while recommendation is driven by attitude, knowledge, and training. Improving menopause care in primary care requires tiered interventions addressing both individual-level and system-level barriers.

articles.title: PROTECT: PRegnancy Outcomes using continuous glucose monitoring TEChnology in pregnant women with early-onset Type 2 diabetes: a multicentre randomised controlled trial - study protocol.
articles.authors: Lee TTM, Collett C, Hayes M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early-onset type 2 diabetes (EOT2D), meaning type 2 diabetes diagnosed before the age of 40 disproportionately affects women from socially deprived and minority ethnic groups. EOT2D is now the most common form of pre-existing diabetes complicating pregnancy. These pregnancies carry high risks of congenital anomalies, stillbirth, neonatal death, and of both maternal and neonatal morbidity. Maternal glycaemia is the key modifiable risk factor yet remains suboptimal and is often accompanied by limited self-monitoring of blood glucose (SMBG). Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM) offers continuous real-time glucose profiles, potentially enabling better dietary, lifestyle and therapy adjustments.
METHODS / DESIGN: The PROTECT trial is a multicentre, randomised controlled trial designed to evaluate whether CGM improves maternal glucose and neonatal outcomes in women with EOT2D. The trial will recruit 422 pregnant participants (≤ 16 weeks 0 days' gestation, HbA1c ≥ 43 mmol/mol) from around 20 UK NHS antenatal diabetes clinics. After a run-in phase with masked CGM, participants will be randomised to either real-time CGM (FreeStyle Libre 3) or standard SMBG. The primary maternal outcome is percentage of time in pregnancy-specific glucose target range (3.5-7.8 mmol/L). The primary neonatal outcome is a composite of neonatal care unit admission or death. Secondary outcomes include maternal HbA1c, glycaemic variability, insulin use, obstetric complications, neonatal morbidity, psychosocial measures, and cost-effectiveness. An internal pilot will assess recruitment feasibility, before proceeding to the full trial. Qualitative interviews with women and healthcare professionals will explore barriers and facilitators to CGM use. Statistical analyses will follow intention-to-treat principles.
DISCUSSION: This is the largest trial to date investigating CGM in EOT2D pregnancy, aiming to generate robust evidence on clinical efficacy, lived experiences, and economic impact, informing future NHS policy and practice.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ISRCTN12804317 Registration Date: 23/10/2023.

articles.title: The association between intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy and risk of small for gestational age in China: a meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Tan X, Hu Y, Chen H
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To identify the relationship of intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) with the occurrence risk of small for gestational age (SGA) in China.
METHODS: The Chinese National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), Medline and Web of Science databases were searched for available studies. Relative risks (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were combined and subgroup analysis based on the specific comorbidity was conducted.
RESULTS: Thirteen studies with 24712 cases were included. The incidence rates of SGA among the ICP and non-ICP patients were 14.04% (294/2094) and 4.66% (1053/22618), respectively. Pooled results demonstrated that ICP was significantly related to the occurrence of SGA (RR=3.12, 95% CI: 1.99-4.88, P＜0.001) in Chinese pregnant women. Subgroup analysis based on specific comorbidity also showed the relationship between ICP and SGA among patients with gestational diabetes mellitus (RR=6.09, 95% CI: 2.96-12.55, P＜0.001) and hepatitis B virus infection (RR=3.22, 95% CI: 1.69-6.12, P＜0.001).
CONCLUSION: In China, ICP was associated with the occurrence of SGA in China and pregnant patients with ICP experienced a significantly higher risk of SGA.

articles.title: Maternal obesity, overweight, and pregnancy outcomes: a cross-sectional study at Korle Bu Teaching Hospital, Ghana.
articles.authors: Sefogah PE, Tagoe S, Tagoe E et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Obesity and overweight remain rising public health challenges globally, with worse outlook in low-resource settings. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of obesity and overweight, the associated sociodemographic characteristics, and the maternal and neonatal pregnancy outcomes at Korle Bu Teaching Hospital, Ghana.
METHOD: This hospital-based analytical cross-sectional study was conducted at the maternity block of Korle Bu Teaching Hospital between March and June 2024. Participants were postpartum women aged 18 years and above who had singleton pregnancies, delivered after 28 weeks of gestation, had booking weight and height recorded in their antenatal records, and were enrolled within 24-72 h after delivery. Data collection utilized pretested questionnaires, and Body Mass Index was calculated using antenatal booking weight and height. Descriptive statistics, including mean (with standard deviation), frequency tables, charts, and graphs, were used to summarize the results. A chi-square test was used to determine the possible association between independent variables and BMI categories. Fisher's exact test was utilized when any of the categories had fewer than five participants. All associations were evaluated at a 95% confidence interval and a 5% significance level.
RESULTS: The average age of the respondents was 31.1 ± 5.9years, with modal age-group of 30-34; and average gestational age at booking was 10weeks 3 days(± 1week4days). Overall, 30.3% of participants were obese and 27.8% overweight. Although obesity and overweight appeared more frequent among participants with hypertensive disorders, gestational diabetes, and caesarean deliveries, none of these associations reached statistical significance (all p > 0.05). Majority (81.3%) had term delivery; 94% of infants had normal Apgar scores at both 1 and 5 min, while at 5 min 3.5%, 1.0%, and 1.5% had mild, moderate, and severe asphyxia, respectively. An…
CONCLUSION: We found a high prevalence of obesity and overweight among pregnant women. Higher BMI was more common among women who were married, multiparous, unemployed, or had no formal education. It was also more common among those with hypertensive disorders, gestational diabetes, postpartum haemorrhage, caesarean delivery, and macrosomia. However, none of these associations reached statistical significance in this sample. Interventions focusing on promoting healthy weight management and physical activity during pregnancy are essential.

articles.title: Beyond age and ovarian reserve: a prospective study exploring inflammatory and cycle-specific biomarkers to enhance IVF outcome prediction.
articles.journal: Journal of assisted reproduction and genetics
articles.authors: Omes C, Montobbio G, De Amici M et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Conventional predictors such as age and AFC fail to fully explain the substantial inter-individual variability in in vitro fertilization outcomes. This prospective exploratory study investigated whether integrating systemic and local inflammatory biomarkers-specifically calprotectin measured in plasma and follicular fluid-with conventional clinical parameters improves the prediction of cumulative clinical pregnancy.
METHODS: We prospectively enrolled consecutive patients undergoing in vitro fertilization and analyzed 75 completed cycles in which all retrieved oocytes and resulting embryos were used. Calprotectin concentrations were quantified in plasma and follicular fluid collected at oocyte retrieval. We evaluated associations with cumulative clinical pregnancy using univariable and multivariable logistic regression. Predictive models obtained were internally validated using a bootstrapping procedure to estimate optimism-corrected discrimination.
RESULTS: Age and antral follicle count confirmed their established predictive roles, whereas calprotectin concentrations alone showed no significant association with cumulative pregnancy. In multivariable models, follicular fluid calprotectin showed a negative trend with pregnancy probability, whereas plasma calprotectin showed the opposite trend. Combining age, antral follicle count, and inflammatory parameters yielded strong discriminative performance; after bootstrap correction, the optimism-corrected area under the curve reached 0.862 for the peri-retrieval model and 0.841 for the post-fertilization model. Heatmap visualizations highlighted distinct risk patterns across age strata and inflammatory profiles.
CONCLUSIONS: Integrating local and systemic inflammatory biomarkers with conventional clinical predictors provides complementary insights into in vitro fertilization success, suggesting that local microenvironmental stress and systemic immune activation exert divergent effects on reproductive potential. These exploratory, hypothesis-generating findings require confirmation in larger, prospective cohorts.  TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06872294. Registered 20 March 2025.

articles.title: High AUC and selection stability do not establish single-gene biomarker value in tumor-versus-normal transcriptomics: a null-controlled multi-cohort analysis in endometrial carcinoma.
articles.authors: Luo L, Zhu Z, Xiao Y et al.
articles.abstract: Transcriptomic biomarker studies of endometrial carcinoma (EC) often report near-perfect discrimination, yet few candidates reproduce. Because tumor-versus-normal contrasts shift much of the transcriptome, a high area under the curve (AUC) can arise from many genes. We benchmarked discrimination and machine-learning selection stability against random gene sets. Vote counting across three Gene Expression Omnibus cohorts (162 EC, 50 controls) identified 182 recurrent genes. In The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) endometrial cohort, where 67.2% of genes were differentially expressed, the most stably selected gene, NUMA1, did not outperform random single genes (AUC 0.829; P = 0.235), nor did the recurrent signature (P = 0.193). Stability-selected multivariable gene sets reached AUCs of 0.995-0.999 in TCGA. After these TCGA results, we examined HAND2-AS1, OSR2, PEG3 and RUNX1T1 post hoc as an illustrative panel; TCGA therefore informed its selection, and GSE146889 was external but not blinded. These genes formed a three-cohort intersection only under a non-prespecified GSE106191 analysis; the prespecified analysis detected no differential expression. The panel exceeded random four-gene scores in TCGA (AUC 0.988; P = 0.006), but not recurrent-consensus subsets (P = 0.61), and showed no detectable advantage in GSE146889 (AUC 0.945; P = 0.064). Post hoc sensitivity analyses across six recorded analytic paths yielded the same qualitative pattern. The score correlated with stromal (rho = - 0.426) but not immune content (rho = - 0.014), and the genes were detected mainly in fibroblasts. In tumor-versus-normal data with marked compositional differences, neither high AUC nor stable selection establishes a gene's uniqueness or tumor-cell relevance; confirmation requires new, prespecified cohorts.

articles.title: Cross-species single-cell transcriptomic comparison of human granulomatous lobular mastitis with two mouse models.
articles.authors: Li Y, Hu F, Lou Y et al.
articles.abstract: Granulomatous lobular mastitis (GLM) is a chronic inflammatory breast disease characterized by etiological heterogeneity, recurrence, and lobulocentric noncaseating granulomatous inflammation. Two experimental models-the human GLM lesion homogenate plus complete Freund's adjuvant (HTH) model and the metoclopramide plus complete Freund's adjuvant (MET) model-have not been directly evaluated against the cellular landscape of human GLM. We assessed the two induction protocols using a common evaluation schedule and compared them with human GLM using longitudinal clinical scoring, histopathology, single-cell RNA sequencing, human-mouse ortholog mapping, and cross-species integration. Both protocols produced GLM-like mammary inflammation. In the sections examined, HTH showed more prominent lobulocentric granulomatous changes, whereas MET showed neutrophilic infiltration and ductal injury. The pooled scRNA-seq libraries differed in the fibroblast, B cell, and T cell states recovered, and several states identified in human GLM were sparsely represented in the mouse datasets. Because each mouse model contributed only one pooled scRNA-seq library, these observations are descriptive and require confirmation in independent samples. The findings provide a preliminary pathological and transcriptomic reference for further evaluation of GLM models.

articles.title: Hyperandrogenism drives pathogenic adipocyte differentiation to promote insulin resistance in PMOS.
articles.authors: Feng G, Dong Y, Huang X et al.
articles.abstract: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) is characterized by hyperandrogenism and insulin resistance, but the mechanisms linking androgen excess to metabolic dysfunction remain unclear. Here we show, using single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) of visceral adipose tissue from women with PMOS and body mass index-matched controls across normal-weight, overweight and obese groups, that PMOS is associated with the expansion of a distinct preadipocyte population, PreA2, enriched for genetic risk related to both reproductive and metabolic traits. Computational analyses and primary cell experiments identify NR4A1 as a driver of the androgen-associated acquisition of the PreA2 state. Trajectory analyses reveal a C/EBPβ-associated differentiation pathway from PreA2 to an adipocyte state termed Ad3, characterized by increased THBS1 secretion. In human adipocytes exposed to high androgen concentrations, THBS1 knockdown partially restores insulin responsiveness. Related transcriptional features are also observed in the reanalysis of an snRNA-seq dataset generated from visceral adipose tissue of dihydrotestosterone-treated female mice. Our study provides a comprehensive single-nucleus atlas of adipose tissue in PMOS and identifies a preadipocyte differentiation trajectory linking hyperandrogenism-associated adipocyte remodelling to insulin resistance.

articles.title: Maternal polystyrene nanoplastics exposure compromises ovarian reserve by disrupting oocyte adhesion and granulosa cell homeostasis.
articles.authors: Li W, Zhou X, Zhang F et al.
articles.abstract: Polystyrene nanoplastics (PS-NPs), as an emerging environmental contaminant, have attracted growing concern owing to their widespread distribution and bioaccumulation capacity. This study investigated the effects of maternal PS-NPs exposure on primordial follicle (PF) assembly in offspring, a process critical for lifelong ovarian reserve establishment. Using a mouse model combined with single-cell RNA sequencing, we characterized the impact of PS-NPs on oocytes and granulosa cells during early folliculogenesis. We demonstrate that PS-NPs undergo intergenerational transfer, crossing the placental barrier to accumulate preferentially in the ovarian cortex of offspring. PS-NPs exposure significantly impaired cyst breakdown and PF assembly, resulting in a marked reduction in ovarian reserve. Mechanistically, PS-NPs enhanced intercellular adhesion within germline cysts by activating the JNK/WNT-β-catenin signaling, causing cyst dissociation defects. Also, PS-NPs suppressed the FAK/PI3K signaling, inhibiting granulosa cell proliferation and inducing apoptosis, ultimately impeding PF formation. This work provides a scientific basis for understanding nanoplastic-associated ovarian disorders, including premature ovarian insufficiency.

articles.title: Anatomy of periprostatic nerves and nerve-sparing strategy for radical prostatectomy.
articles.authors: Ma Q, Liu Y, Han Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Radical prostatectomy is an important curative treatment for localized prostate cancer, but postoperative urinary incontinence and erectile dysfunction substantially impair quality of life. Understanding individual variation in periprostatic nerves, fascia, and supporting structures is essential for balancing oncological control with functional preservation. This narrative review examines periprostatic nerve and fascial anatomy, nerve-sparing grading systems, established surgical techniques, and emerging adjuncts for individualized surgical planning.
METHODS: PubMed was searched through July 2026 using 'prostate', 'pelvic autonomic nerve', 'neurovascular bundle', 'nerve sparing', 'radical prostatectomy', 'continence', 'erectile function', and 'NeuroSAFE'. Relevant guidelines and standard anatomical texts were also reviewed, alongside anatomical and clinical studies directly addressing periprostatic nerve anatomy, nerve-sparing techniques, or functional and oncological outcomes.
RESULTS: Anatomical and histological studies show substantial variation in periprostatic nerve distribution. Nerve fibres are not confined to conventional posterolateral neurovascular bundles. Some extend into the anterolateral prostate and course through multilayered, heterogeneous fascial structures. Anatomy-based grading systems provide practical intraoperative frameworks but cannot accurately quantify nerve preservation in individual patients. Bilateral or more extensive nerve sparing is associated with better recovery of urinary continence and erectile function. However, these associations are influenced by baseline function, tumour risk, surgeon experience, and inconsistent outcome definitions. Contemporary approaches increasingly preserve a broader complex of nerves, fascia, and supporting structures. Refined techniques may improve early functional recovery, although comparative long-term evidence remains limited. Multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging, NeuroSAFE, and intraoperative nerve-identification technologies may further support individualized planning and real-time adjustment of dissection planes.
CONCLUSIONS: A detailed understanding of individualized periprostatic nerve and fascial anatomy underpins effective nerve-sparing surgery. Integrating anatomy-based grading, patient-specific planning, and advanced adjunctive technologies may improve the balance between oncological control and functional preservation.

articles.title: Risk factors for congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract.
articles.authors: Chen CC, Lai PC, Shieh CC
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract (CAKUT) are a leading cause of pediatric renal failure. This study evaluated risk factors and assessed their robustness.
METHODS: PubMed, EMBASE, and Scopus searches yielded 33 studies (24 case-control, 9 cohort). Frequentist and Bayesian random-effects meta-analyses estimated associations between CAKUT and maternal/neonatal risks.
RESULTS: Frequentist analysis identified increased risk for pre-pregnancy BMI 25.0-29.9 (OR, 1.24; 95% CI, 1.06-1.45), ≥30 (OR, 1.27; 95% CI, 1.07-1.51), and ≥25 kg/m² (OR, 1.24; 95% CI, 1.11-1.37). Maternal age <20 years was protective (OR, 0.61; 95% CI, 0.51-0.73). Other predictors included family history of CAKUT/kidney disease, maternal diabetes subtypes (type 1, type 2, pre-gestational, and gestational diabetes), preterm birth (OR, 1.59; 95% CI, 1.25-2.03), small-for-gestational-age (SGA), and large-for-gestational-age (LGA). Bayesian analysis validated most factors. Although 95% CrIs crossed unity for BMI 25.0-29.9 kg/m², BMI ≥ 30 kg/m², T2DM, SGA, LGA, alcohol consumption, RASi use, and hypertension, their posterior distributions were predominantly above 1. High BMI, family history, and diabetes remained robust in high-quality subsets.
CONCLUSIONS: Confirming established risks and identifying novel associations, these findings identify maternal metabolic factors as consistent correlates of CAKUT and support their evaluation as potentially modifiable targets.
IMPACT: Current meta-analyses lack synthesis on novel CAKUT determinants (maternal exposures, comorbidities, gestational weight gain, extreme fetal weight) and Bayesian approaches, which are essential to robustly address heterogeneity in sparse data. Our frequentist analysis confirmed established risks and identified novel associations: family history, SGA, LGA, and type 1 and 2 diabetes. Bayesian meta-analysis supported the main findings and showed posterior probabilities that OR > 1 of ≥90% for BMI subgroups, T2DM, RASi use, and hypertension. Maternal metabolic factors are consistently associated with CAKUT and represent potentially modifiable targets that warrant evaluation in future prospective and interventional studies.

articles.title: Routine laboratory trajectories predict organ-level complications in cancer.
articles.authors: Lübberstedt J, Braitsch K, Lammert J et al.
articles.abstract: Routine laboratory panels drawn during cancer treatment constitute longitudinal physiological recordings of organ function, yet their temporal structure is discarded by single-timepoint prognostic tools. A transformer trained on 2,777,595 laboratory measurements from 3905 patients with multiple myeloma or ovarian cancer predicted which of 162 treatment-associated complications would be newly recorded within two years, spanning eight clinical categories, achieving 1.5- to 6.1-fold enrichment above prevalence. Across individual endpoints it exceeded non-sequential baselines, including engineered-trajectory models, by +0.024 to +0.070 in mean AUROC. Predictions generalised across both cancers, divergence concentrating in disease-specific complications, and biomarker masking recovered signatures consistent with established pathophysiology. External validation on MIMIC-IV and MMRF CoMMpass showed transferability, strongest for renal and metabolic endpoints, attenuated for infection endpoints. On CoMMpass it added prognostic value to ISS staging. Routine oncological laboratory data carry complication-specific physiological signal months before a complication is recorded, and require no testing beyond standard oncological care.

articles.title: The Complex Relationship Between Volume and Outcome of AMS 800 Implants in the SATURN Database.
articles.authors: Van der Aa F, Thiruchelvam N, Heesakkers J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: SATURN is a prospective, multicenter registry that collects data from 28 European centers. Contrary to expectations, previous analyses of the SATURN registry showed higher revision rates in higher-volume centers.
OBJECTIVE: We further evaluated the relationship between center volume and 1-yr safety outcomes after AMS 800 implantation using real-world SATURN data.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: We reviewed 1046 SATURN implantations and included 684 patients who received an AMS 800 artificial urinary sphincter from 25 European centers. Centers were categorized by annual AMS 800 implant numbers as low (<10), intermediate (10-25), or high (>25).
OUTCOME MEASUREMENTS AND STATISTICAL ANALYSIS: The 1-yr complication, revision, and explant rates were assessed using Kaplan-Meier and log-rank tests and Pearson chi-square tests, with multivariable Cox regression adjusted for relevant patient- and procedure-related covariates and accounting for center-level clustering.
RESULTS AND LIMITATIONS: Crude analyses differed by center volume for complications, revisions other than explantation, and all revisions, including explantation, but not for explants. Complication rates were 16.7%, 25.8%, and 17.8% in low-, intermediate-, and high-volume centers, respectively, demonstrating a nonmonotonic pattern with the intermediate-volume group as the main outlier. Rates of revision other than explantation were 5.1%, 12.3%, and 11.2%, respectively, whereas rates of all revisions including explantation were 9.6%, 18.9%, and 16.9%, respectively, and were thus higher in both intermediate- and high-volume centers than in low-volume centers. After adjustment, there was no statistically significant global association between center volume and any of the four 1-yr outcomes; the observed crude differences were not retained after adjustment. This observational registry analysis is subject to confounding and cannot establish causality.
CONCLUSIONS: Although crude analyses showed differences in complication and revision rates across volume groups, the complication pattern was nonmonotonic, with the intermediate-volume group representing the main outlier, whereas revision-related outcomes were higher in both intermediate- and high-volume centers than in low-volume centers. After multivariable adjustment and accounting for center-level clustering, no evidence of an independent center-volume effect was observed for any of the four 1-yr outcomes.

articles.title: Utility of Examining 100 Metaphase Cells in the Evaluation of Low-Level Aneuploidy Mosaicism.
articles.journal: American journal of medical genetics. Part A
articles.authors: Iwata-Otsubo A, Cai P, Knudson-Horneber L et al.
articles.abstract: Karyotype analysis is the gold standard of care for evaluating patients suspected of having mosaicism involving sex chromosomes or autosomes. Accurately determining the level of mosaicism is important, as it can vary widely and may be linked to disease severity. However, current guidelines do not clearly specify how many cells should be examined in order to exclude low-level mosaicism. In our retrospective study of cytogenetic results from 113 specimens, each with a minimum of 100 cells examined, we assessed whether the extensive analysis provided additional clinical value. Common indications for cytogenetic testing in these cases include Turner syndrome, premature ovarian failure, Klinefelter syndrome, infertility, and multiple miscarriages. In 83% (94/113) of cases, additional cells were examined because initial analysis suggested low-level mosaicism; however, further analysis did not confirm the initial findings in 66 of these 94 cases, indicating they were likely artifacts. Notably, none of the seven repeated analyses of 100 or 200 cells corroborated previous reports of low-level or clinically suspected mosaicism. Examination of additional cells confirmed the presence of a second cell line at low level in 25% (28/113) of cases, most often associated with X chromosome aneuploidies in adult females, likely age-related and without clear clinical significance. These results suggest that case-by-case consideration is still important, but no clinically significant findings resulted from analyzing more than 40 cells, indicating that extensive additional cell analysis is generally unnecessary for ruling out low-level mosaicism in clinical cytogenetic practice.

articles.title: Uterine Sarcomas: Updates and Challenges.
articles.journal: Surgical oncology clinics of North America
articles.authors: Avila M, Hoffman MS
articles.abstract: Uterine sarcomas represent a rare subset of sarcomas, making up 1% of all solid organ sarcomas and 3% of all uterine cancers. They arise as mesenchymal tumors from muscle and connective tissues. The most common subtypes include uterine leiomyosarcoma at 63%, low-grade and high-grade endometrial stromal sarcoma at 21%, and the remainder include the less common subtypes like undifferentiated uterine sarcoma, adenosarcoma, perivascular epithelioid cell tumor, SMARCA4-deficient uterine sarcoma, uterine tumor resembling ovarian sex cord tumor, NTRK-rearranged sarcoma, rhabdomyosarcoma, and inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor. Through a surgical lens, this review will explore the most current diagnostic criteria and management strategies available.

articles.title: Seroepidemiological survey of Neospora caninum infection in dairy goats from Rio de Janeiro state, Brazil.
articles.journal: Veterinary parasitology, regional studies and reports
articles.authors: Arruda IF, Millar PR, Balaro MFA et al.
articles.abstract: Neosporosis is a significant veterinary parasitosis caused by coccidian species Neospora caninum. Parasitism by N. caninum can lead to important reproductive changes, such as abortion, stillbirth, and neonatal death in domestic ruminants like goats. Considering the foregoing, the aims of the current study are to determine the seroprevalence of N. caninum infection in dairy goats bred in farms in Rio de Janeiro State, and to identify possible risk factors for these animals. Blood samples were collected from 460 dairy goats bred in dairy farms in Niterói, Nova Friburgo, Sapucaia, Tanguá, Valença and Vassouras cities, Rio de Janeiro State, between October 2020 and December 2022. Serum samples were subjected to enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) to investigate anti-N. caninum IgG antibodies based on using this protozoan's total soluble antigen.
