CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04951206.

articles.title: Inflammatory Bowel Disease in Pregnancy.
articles.authors: Boyd T, Kane S
articles.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) presents unique clinical considerations related to fertility, medical therapy, and delivery planning. The strongest predictor of adverse pregnancy outcomes is active disease, making maintenance of remission a central management priority. Prepregnancy counseling for patients with IBD should address reproductive goals, nutritional status, and the potential effect of prior pelvic surgery on fertility. Most established IBD therapies, including aminosalicylates, thiopurines, and biologic agents, can be continued to maintain remission, whereas methotrexate is contraindicated, and Janus kinase inhibitors and sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor modulators are generally avoided. Delivery planning should be individualized, with cesarean delivery generally favored for active perianal Crohn disease or rectovaginal fistula and shared decision making emphasized for patients with an ileal pouch-anal anastomosis. Optimal outcomes depend on coordinated multidisciplinary care that prioritizes disease control, treatment continuation, and individualized reproductive and delivery planning.

articles.title: Circulating TOX+ TIGIT+ CD57+ TEMRA CD8+ T cells are associated with efficacy of combined aPD-L1, aCTLA-4 and metronomic chemotherapy in advanced cervical cancer.
articles.authors: Bertucci A, Maby P, Chrétien AS et al.
articles.abstract: To improve ICI efficacy in advanced CC, a promising strategy is to combine anti-PDL-1, anti-CTLA-4 and chemotherapy. The phase I/II MOVIE trial reported a clinical benefit rate of 53.1% of durvalumab, tremelimumab and metronomic oral vinorelbine in patients with pretreated metastatic CC. The objective of this study is to discover immune efficacy biomarkers of this combination. We analyzed 29 advanced CC patients from MOVIE multicentric prospective clinical trial (NCT03518606). We used high-dimensional mass cytometry (CyTOF) to explore the immune landscape in baseline peripheral blood mononuclear cells. We developed 3 immune panels of 40 antibodies (T cells, NK cells and myeloid cells) for the deep-phenotyping of PBMCs. Our bioinformatics workflow of CyTOF data included dimensionality reduction (opt-SNE, UMAP), automated clustering (PhenoGraph) and regression (CITRUS). The biomarker candidates were submitted to a model prediction composed of 11 machine-learning algorithms. In baseline blood samples, high-dimensional analyses consistently identified a population of TOX+TIGIT+CD57+ TEMRA (CD45RA+CCR7-) CD8+ T cells associated with improved clinical outcomes: clinical benefit (CB), progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS). This population was confirmed by manual gating and 11 machine-learning algorithms. After determining a cut-off at 0.73% of CD45+ cells, patients with an increased blood baseline frequency of TOX+TIGIT+CD57+ TEMRA (CD45RA+CCR7-) CD8+ T cells had an improved CBR (76% vs 25%, p=0.005), an improved PFS (HR=0.35, CI95, 0.13-0.95, p=0.013) and an improved OS (HR=0.19, CI95, 0.07-0.53, p=0.001). Multivariate analysis with classical CC prognostic factors confirmed the OS benefit of our biomarker (HR=0.15, CI95: 0.05-0.47, <0.001).

articles.title: Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy and Black-White Racial Disparities in Severe Maternal Morbidity.
articles.authors: Smith-Webb RS, Parker SE, Werler MM et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To estimate the proportion of the Black-White racial disparity in severe maternal morbidity (SMM) that could be eliminated by preventing hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP).
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 1,242,574 Black and White birthing people 12-55 years of age with deliveries in Massachusetts from 1998 to 2021 using PELL (Pregnancy to Early Life Longitudinal data system). Maternal race was used as a proxy for exposure to racism. The primary outcome was SMM excluding blood transfusion-only events (SMM-20); we also considered SMM including blood transfusion-only events (SMM-21) and cardiac complications. We conducted causal mediation analyses with HDP as the mediator and used G-estimation to estimate the Black-White racial disparity in SMM that would remain if HDP were prevented. We calculated the proportion of the disparity that could be eliminated by preventing HDP and severe HDP separately.
RESULTS: Compared with White birthing people, Black birthing people experienced 63.8 excess SMM-20 events per 10,000 in-hospital deliveries (95% CI, 58.1-69.6). If HDP were prevented, the disparity would be reduced to 38.6 excess SMM-20 events (95% CI, 32.9-44.2), suggesting that 39.6% of the absolute Black-White racial disparity in SMM-20 could be eliminated. The estimated proportions eliminated were 33.1% for SMM-21 and 57.6% for cardiac complications. The proportion of the Black-White racial disparity eliminated by preventing severe HDP alone was 27.9% for SMM-20, 20.7% for SMM-21, and 31.3% for cardiac complications.
CONCLUSION: Preventing HDP could substantially reduce Black-White racial disparities in SMM.

articles.title: Structure-based computational screening of cyclotides as putative CYP19A1-binding scaffolds for modulation of estrogen biosynthesis in adenomyosis.
articles.authors: Üstünel S, Ali N
articles.abstract: Adenomyosis is a chronic estrogen-dependent gynecological disorder associated with dysmenorrhea, abnormal uterine bleeding, chronic pelvic pain, infertility, and recurrent implantation failure. Because human placental aromatase cytochrome P450 (CYP19A1) plays a central role in local estrogen biosynthesis, this study employed an integrated in silico workflow to identify cyclotide scaffolds capable of interacting with CYP19A1. The receptor structure was prepared and validated, while protein-protein interaction analysis confirmed its involvement in steroidogenesis and estrogen biosynthesis. Twenty cyclotides were modeled and screened against the predicted active site of CYP19A1. Based on an integrated evaluation of HADDOCK and ClusPro docking, binding orientation, and interaction characteristics, cycloviolacin O4 was prioritized as the lead candidate. The predicted CYP19A1-cycloviolacin O4 complex exhibited a HADDOCK score of -82.8 ± 9.8, a cluster RMSD of 0.2 ± 0.1 Å, and a ClusPro energy score of -872.1. Docking against the reference inhibitor exemestane and the reference peptide SNA-60-367-10 provided additional computational benchmarking. Subsequent 500 ns molecular dynamics simulations, normal mode analysis, and MM-GBSA/MM-PBSA calculations supported the predicted structural stability and dynamic compatibility of the complex, yielding binding free energies of -66.58 ± 3.46 kcal/mol (MM-GBSA) and -4.56 ± 4.29 kcal/mol (MM-PBSA). Computational safety assessment predicted cycloviolacin O4 to be non-antigenic, non-allergenic, and non-toxic, while immune simulation suggested a balanced immune response. Collectively, these findings identify cycloviolacin O4 as a computationally predicted CYP19A1-binding cyclotide scaffold. However, these observations are derived exclusively from computational analyses and require biochemical, cellular, and in vivo validation before any conclusions regarding biological activity or therapeutic potential can be drawn.

articles.title: A circuit mechanism for psychosis vulnerability during perimenopause.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.ta: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
articles.authors: Perez SM, Boley AM, Reiley HB et al.
articles.abstract: The transition to menopause is a period of profound physiological change that encompasses nearly one-third of a woman's lifespan and is associated with a distinct rise in the incidence of psychosis. Despite the clinical burden of menopause-associated psychosis, the circuit-level mechanisms linking reproductive aging to psychiatric vulnerability remain poorly defined. Current understanding is limited by rodent models that utilize abrupt surgical hormone loss, which fail to capture the progressive endocrine fluctuations and follicular depletion characteristic of the natural menopausal transition. Here, we investigate how the gradual transition from perimenopause to postmenopause regulates the ventral hippocampus-mesolimbic dopamine circuit, a pathway centrally implicated in the development of psychotic symptoms. Specifically, we show that the perimenopausal transition induces a transient state of ventral hippocampal hyperactivity that selectively drives dopamine system dysfunction, whereas this modulatory control is absent in the postmenopausal state. These findings reveal that psychosis-related circuit instability is precipitated specifically by the hormonal transition itself, rather than the persistent state of estrogen deficiency that follows. This contrasts with the long-standing "estrogen protection hypothesis," which posits that low hormone levels are the primary driver of symptoms and explains why standard hormone replacement and antipsychotic therapies often yield inconsistent results. Our results establish that perimenopause is a mechanistically distinct neurobiological window characterized by a unique failure of hippocampal-dopamine circuit regulation. By identifying this specific period of circuit instability, this work provides a framework for stage-specific psychiatric interventions and reframes reproductive aging as a series of distinct transitions in brain function.

articles.title: Timing of Antenatal Care, Stillbirth, and Infant Mortality in Migrant Mothers in Australia.
articles.authors: Hossain S, Oei JL, Munasinghe S et al.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Timely antenatal care (ANC) reduces pregnancy risks, yet the association between delayed ANC and stillbirth or infant mortality among migrant mothers in Australia has not previously been investigated.
OBJECTIVE: To examine whether delayed ANC is associated with higher stillbirth and infant mortality among Australia-born compared with migrant mothers.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This retrospective cohort study assessed births to non-Indigenous mothers in New South Wales from January 1, 2002, to December 31, 2020, followed up to infant age of 1 year. Mothers were categorized as Australia-born, migrant from English-speaking country (ESM), or migrant from non-English-speaking country (non-ESM). Data were analyzed between August 2025 and June 2026.
EXPOSURES: Timing of first ANC, defined as 12 weeks or earlier, 13 to 19 weeks, 20 weeks or later, or no ANC.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The main outcome was stillbirth (at ≥20 weeks) and infant mortality (at prehospital discharge, posthospital discharge, or 1 year). Adjusted relative risks (ARRs) were estimated using Poisson regression models, stratified by migration group.
RESULTS: This study included 1 720 033 births (median [IQR] maternal age, 31.2 [27.4-34.8] years; 884 235 male infants [51.4%]), including 1 132 193 (65.8%) to Australia-born, 116 026 (6.7%) to ESM, and 471 814 (27.4%) to non-ESM mothers. Late ANC (>12 weeks) was more common in non-ESM mothers (190 338 [40.3%]) than Australia-born (334 790 [29.6%]) or ESM (41 029 [35.4%]) mothers. In cross-group comparisons, non-ESM mother status was associated with higher risk of adverse outcomes regardless of ANC timing. Compared with Australia-born mothers with early ANC (≤12 weeks), a higher risk of stillbirth (ARR, 1.25; 95% CI, 1.18-1.33) and 1-year (ARR, 1.32; 95% CI, 1.22-1.44), predischarge (ARR, 1.39; 95% CI, 1.25-1.54), and postdischarge (ARR, 1.19; 95% CI, 1.03-1.37) infant mortality was observed in non-ESM mothers accessing ANC by 12 weeks. Similar risk patterns were observed in non-ESM mothers with late ANC. In within-group comparisons, among Australia-born mothers, each category of delayed ANC was associated with higher risk. No ANC was associated with the highest risks across all maternal groups for stillbirth and…
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study of 1.72 million births, higher risks of stillbirths and infant mortalities were observed in non-ESM mothers regardless of ANC timing, warranting further investigation.

articles.title: Robot-assisted hysterectomy for large uteri: perioperative outcomes with the da Vinci Xi and SP systems.
articles.authors: Masuda S, Kanno K, Kitamura R et al.
articles.abstract: We compared perioperative outcomes of robot-assisted hysterectomy (RAH) for large uteri using the da Vinci Xi and SP systems. This retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients who underwent RAH for benign indications with a uterine weight of ≥ 500 g between January 2023 and April 2026 at a single Japanese center. Among 200 patients, 162 underwent Xi and 38 underwent SP procedures. Operative time (OT) did not differ significantly between the groups (104 [85-126] vs. 113 [98-133] min, p = 0.083), whereas docking time was shorter with SP (3 [2-4] vs. 2 [1-3] min, p < 0.001). Estimated blood loss (EBL) was lower with SP (25 [5-100] vs. 5 [5-34] mL, p = 0.043). After adjustment for uterine weight, body mass index, previous abdominal surgery, and severe endometriosis, SP use was independently associated with longer OT (unstandardized regression coefficient, 15.1 min; 95% confidence interval, 5.2-25.0, p = 0.003), whereas the robotic platform was not independently associated with EBL. Uterine weight and severe endometriosis were independently associated with longer OT, whereas uterine weight was associated with greater EBL. Postoperative complications and conversion to laparotomy did not differ considerably between groups. The SP system may offer an alternative to Xi for RAH in patients with large uteri.

articles.title: Functional recovery after robot-assisted radical prostatectomy: a patient-centred perspective.
articles.authors: Mastroianni R, Ragusa A, Iannuzzi A et al.
articles.abstract: Erectile dysfunction (ED) and urinary incontinence (UI) are among the most distressing sequelae after robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP), substantially affecting quality of life. Exploring patients' perceptions of functional recovery and willingness to undergo corrective surgery may improve rehabilitation and shared decision-making. This cross-sectional survey included patients previously treated with RARP, identified from a single-center IRB-approved prostate cancer database. Baseline demographic, clinical, and pathological data were collected. Erectile function was assessed using the IIEF-5. Patients completed the Sexual Recovery and Urinary Continence Recovery questionnaires after receiving standardized information on penile prosthesis (PP) and artificial urinary sphincter (AUS) implantation. Descriptive statistics, Chi-square, and ANOVA analyses were performed. Between April and September 2025, 214 patients completed the questionnaires. Mean age was 65 years, and 67% underwent nerve-sparing surgery. At a mean follow-up of 21 months (range 2-77 months), 89% reported postoperative ED, with a mean IIEF-5 score of 7; 93% had mild-to-severe ED. The mean importance of erectile function recovery was 8/10. Overall, 15% of patients with ED expressed interest in PP implantation. Younger men were more likely to consider PP surgery (p < 0.001). Although older men expressing willingness reported higher interest scores (9/10), differences across age groups were not statistically significant (p = 0.33). Overall urinary continence was rated 7/10, 39% reported UI, and 19% of patients with UI expressed willingness to undergo AUS implantation, with no significant age-related differences. Recovery of erectile and urinary function remains a major priority after RARP. Patients' willingness to consider definitive surgical rehabilitation highlights the importance of individualized counselling and shared decision-making.

articles.title: Comparing 7 mm versus 8 mm as the Optimal Threshold for Fresh Embryo Transfer Cancellation in Thin Endometrium: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Han Q, Teng Y, Chen Y et al.
articles.abstract: This study looked at women with a thin uterine lining during in vitro fertilization to find out when it is better to freeze all embryos and transfer later instead of doing a fresh embryo transfer. We evaluated nearly 80,000 treatment cycles and analyzed 4,401 cycles in which women had a thin uterine lining. We found that for women with a lining thinner than 7 mm, freezing the embryos for a later transfer significantly increased the chances of a live birth. For women with a lining between 7 mm and 8 mm, a fresh transfer resulted in a higher chance of pregnancy. By favoring a 7 mm cutoff over an 8 mm cutoff, doctors can avoid unnecessary treatment delays and emotional stress for many patients while ensuring the best possible chance of a successful and healthy pregnancy.

articles.title: Early ICG Fluorescence During Layer-by-Layer Presacral Dissection in Robot-Assisted Sacrocolpopexy.
articles.authors: Tanaka Y, Takahashi A, Yoneoka Y et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: Safe presacral access to the anterior longitudinal ligament during robot-assisted sacrocolpopexy requires an understanding of the layered anatomy around the hypogastric nerve and presacral vessels. Intravenous indocyanine green (ICG) fluorescence has been reported to visualize pelvic vessels and provide anatomical cues along the hypogastric nerve pathway. This video demonstrates its early use during layer-by-layer presacral dissection.
METHODS: A 79-year-old woman with Pelvic Organ Prolapse Quantification stage III uterine prolapse underwent robot-assisted sacrocolpopexy. ICG (0.25 mg/kg) was administered intravenously immediately before commencing presacral dissection at the sacral promontory. White-light and near-infrared fluorescence views were alternated during layer-by-layer presacral dissection.
RESULTS: Major pelvic vessels became fluorescent within approximately 1 min after ICG administration. Layer-by-layer dissection delineated the prehypogastric nerve fascia and the anatomically presumed course of the hypogastric nerve. Intermittent fluorescence imaging provided additional anatomical cues along this course and revealed presacral vascular signals before the corresponding vascular structures became clearly apparent under white-light observation. Operative time was 210 min, blood loss was minimal, and no Clavien-Dindo grade ≥II perioperative complications occurred. No pelvic organ prolapse recurrence was observed at 10 months.
CONCLUSIONS: Combining layer-based anatomical understanding with early ICG fluorescence imaging may provide adjunctive orientation cues before deeper presacral dissection.

articles.title: Prevalence and Associated Factors of Pelvic Floor Dysfunction Symptoms in Peruvian Women, 2025.
articles.authors: Sologuren-García G, Tejedo JR, Linares CL
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: Pelvic floor dysfunctions (PFDs) affect women's quality of life and constitute a public health problem. In Peru, population-based evidence regarding their magnitude and associated factors is limited. We aimed to estimate the national prevalence of PFD symptoms and identify associated sociodemographic and obstetric factors among Peruvian women.
METHODS: This was an observational, cross-sectional, analytical study. A total of 1280 women were selected using a probabilistic, stratified, two-stage sampling design with national and macroregional representativeness. Symptoms were assessed through face-to-face interviews using the PFDI-20 and PFIQ-7 instruments. The analysis incorporated sampling weights, stratification, and clustering using the survey package in R. Associations were estimated using the Rao-Scott chi-square test and Poisson regression models with robust variance.
RESULTS: The prevalence of PFD symptoms was 40.1% (95% CI 35.8-44.6). In the adjusted analysis, prevalence was higher in the older age groups, particularly among women aged 55-64 years (aPR 3.47) and those aged 65 years or older (aPR 3.22), compared with women aged 18-24 years. Higher prevalence was also associated with multiparity (aPR 1.62), grand multiparity (aPR 1.72), and a history of delivering a macrosomic newborn (aPR 1.22).
CONCLUSIONS: Approximately four in ten Peruvian women reported PFD symptoms. Older age, multiparity, grand multiparity, and a history of fetal macrosomia were independently associated with higher prevalence. These findings support active symptom screening and preventive pelvic floor care across the life course.

articles.title: Lower Urinary Tract Outcomes Following Surgery for Urinary Tract Endometriosis: The Role of Functional Assessment.
articles.authors: Rajshekhar S, Morris JS, Stretch A et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: Lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) in endometriosis are common but under characterised. We evaluated LUTS burden and patient-reported outcomes following surgery for urinary tract endometriosis and explored multidisciplinary management.
METHODS: We conducted a cohort study using a prospectively maintained database of patients undergoing laparoscopic excision of bladder (n = 14) or ureteric (n = 37) endometriosis between January 2019 and May 2023 at a tertiary referral centre. Symptoms were assessed preoperatively and at 6 months using the British Society for Gynaecological Endoscopy Pelvic Pain Questionnaire, EuroQol 5-Dimension 3-Level (EQ-5D-3L) and Visual Analogue Scale Quality of Life (VAS) score. Urogynaecological outcomes and Clavien-Dindo complications were recorded.
RESULTS: Bladder pain improved significantly in both cohorts (p < 0.005), alongside improved quality of life. Voiding difficulty showed limited or variable improvement. Postoperative urogynaecology/urology input was required in 79% of patients with bladder and 38% with ureteric endometriosis. VAS quality-of-life scores increased from 50 (95% CI 14 to 60) to 68 (95% CI 28 to 84) and from 50 (95% CI 46 to 60) to 80 (95% CI 70 to 80) in bladder and ureteric endometriosis respectively (p < 0.005 for both). EQ-5D-3L pain/discomfort scores worsened in both bladder (p < 0.05) and ureteric (p < 0.0005) groups, whereas anxiety/depression scores remained unchanged.
CONCLUSIONS: Optimal management of urinary tract endometriosis requires holistic multidisciplinary care throughout assessment, surgery and postoperative follow-up. Treatment was associated with improved bladder pain and quality of life, although voiding dysfunction and mental health outcomes remained variable. Causality cannot be established; longer-term comparative studies using validated patient-centred outcomes are needed.

articles.title: Reported Approaches to Vaginal Pessary Use for Treating Pelvic Organ Prolapse in Women: A Secondary Analysis of Randomised Controlled Trials.
articles.authors: Johnson EE, Kenny RPW, Oliver A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pessaries are non-surgical devices used to help to treat pelvic organ prolapse (POP) in women. Currently, we know little about how the components of interventions that involve the use of a vaginal pessary for POP are reported within randomised controlled trials (RCTs). Our objective was to describe how interventions involving pessaries for POP are reported in current RCTs.
METHODS: We searched the Cochrane Incontinence Specialised Register, from inception until 31 March 2023, then MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, CENTRAL, ClinicalTrials.gov and ICTRP from 1 April 2023 to 24 April 2025. We included RCTs involving women aged 18 and over with POP that included a pessary in at least one study arm. Two reviewers independently screened titles and abstracts and full texts before extracting data according to a pre-piloted form, which included the Template for Intervention Description and Replication (TIDieR) checklist. Results are presented using tables and graphs with an accompanying narrative.
RESULTS: We included 14 studies that described pessary interventions. Across all the studies included, there was a large variation in how TIDieR domains were reported and in the level of detail provided regarding the approach to pessaries. Only one of the studies included provided details for all 12 of the TIDieR domains.
CONCLUSIONS: Current reporting of pessary interventions in RCTs lacks the detail required to be reproducible and transferable to clinical practice. Future RCTs including pessary interventions should ensure that all aspects of the TIDieR checklist are addressed.

articles.title: Development and validation of a self-reported cognitive measure (Meno-Cog) for perimenopause.
articles.authors: He L, Jaff NG, Stoner C et al.
articles.abstract: Cognitive issues, such as forgetfulness and difficulty concentrating, are often reported during the menopause transition. However, current understanding of women's cognitive experiences is often restricted to memory issues; other experiences, such as struggling with multitasking, are largely neglected. This may show a knowledge gap in women's cognitive health and highlight potential unmet needs during this transition. We developed and assessed the quality of a self-reported cognitive scale, the Menopause-Specific Cognitive Scale (Meno-Cog), which measures a diverse range of everyday cognitive challenges relevant to the menopause transition. The Meno-Cog was shown to be a reliable and useful tool for women going through the menopause transition. This scale will be helpful in understanding cognitive experiences during the menopause transition, monitoring treatment progress, identifying any unmet needs, and potentially improving the quality of menopause care. Future research should also explore the use of Meno-Cog with women from more diverse backgrounds.

articles.title: Urgency in women with pelvic organ prolapse: a comprehensive analysis of pathophysiology, diagnostics and therapeutic strategies.
articles.authors: Budny-Winska J, Kryza-Ottou A, Fuchs T et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Pelvic organ prolapse (POP) and the accompanying lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) - primarily urgency and overactive bladder (OAB) syndrome - pose a significant challenge in modern urogynecology. The aim of this paper is to summarize current knowledge regarding the pathophysiology, diagnosis, and management of OAB symptoms in women with POP.
STATE OF KNOWLEDGE: The etiology of detrusor overactivity in POP is multifactorial, involving mechanical bladder outlet obstruction (BOO) resulting from urethral kinking, as well as the traction of sensory receptors at the bladder base. No correlation has been demonstrated between the overall stage of pelvic organ prolapse and the severity of urinary urgency. However, there is the association between urgency and specific anatomical defects, particularly within the anterior and apical compartments. Comprehensive diagnostics, including a bladder diary, post-void residual (PVR) volume assessment, and a pessary test, are crucial for predicting surgical success. Treatment should follow a stepwise approach, starting with conservative measures (lifestyle modifications, pelvic floor muscle training) and pharmacotherapy (antimuscarinic drugs, β3-receptor agonists, local estrogen therapy). In the event of conservative treatment failure, surgical correction of the defect (e.g., anterior colporrhaphy, apical suspension) resolves urgency in 60-80% of patients, although individual risk factors must be taken into account.
CONCLUSIONS: The coexistence of POP and OAB requires a holistic, individualized therapeutic approach. In women with symptomatic pelvic organ prolapse, precise identification of the anatomical defect and thorough preoperative evaluation are key to achieving successful outcomes.

articles.title: Structure-Dependent Maternal-Fetal Transfer and Fetal Hepatic Accumulation of PFOA and Hexafluoropropylene Oxide (HFPO)-Based Alternatives: Implications for Fetal Liver Metabolic Disruption.
articles.authors: Zhang M, Tian Y, Pan Y et al.
articles.abstract: Hexafluoropropylene oxide (HFPO)-based compounds have been increasingly adopted as replacements for legacy per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) such as perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), yet evidence on developmental toxicity remains limited. This study investigated structure-dependent maternal-fetal transfer, fetal tissue distribution, and hepatic effects of PFOA and four HFPO-based alternatives, including hexafluoropropylene oxide dimer acid (HFPO-DA) and hexafluoropropylene oxide trimer acid (HFPO-TA) homologues, in gestational mice. All compounds were detected in maternal serum, fetal tissues, and amniotic fluid in a dose-dependent manner, but transplacental transfer efficiencies varied markedly. C9 HFPO-TA showed the greatest fetal accumulation, indicating enhanced fetal retention. Desorption electrospray ionization mass spectrometry imaging revealed preferential hepatic localization of PFOA and HFPO trimers, with fetal hepatic burden increasing with van der Waals volume, suggesting structure-dependent enrichment. Metabolomics showed broad alterations of fetal hepatic metabolism, dominated by altered lipids and lipid-like molecules. 5-Aminolevulinic acid, a key heme precursor, was consistently reduced, whereas ALAS1 and ALAD protein levels increased, indicating perturbation of heme biosynthesis. The provisional, study-specific developmental reference doses derived from fetal or placental endpoints were comparable to or lower than those based on maternal hepatomegaly, suggesting greater developmental sensitivity. These findings reveal structure-dependent fetal liver accumulation and support incorporating fetal-specific endpoints into PFAS risk assessment.

articles.title: Mitochondrial-Endocrine Axis Dysfunction Mediates Diet-Dependent Susceptibility to Nanoplastic Ovarian Toxicity and PCOS Risk.
articles.authors: Ji Z, Li Q, Jiang X et al.
articles.abstract: Nanoplastics (NPs) pollution represents an emerging threat to reproductive health, yet how dietary habits modulate this toxicity remains largely unexplored. Here, mice were assigned to a control (CD), high-fat (HFD), or high-fiber (HFib) diet and received oral doses of deuterated polystyrene nanoparticles at 0, 5, or 25 mg/kg/day over an eight-week period. Ovarian NP accumulation was dose-dependent under CD, reaching 23.33 ± 5.39 μg/g tissue at the highest dose. HFD markedly elevated this burden to 96.87 ± 13.44 μg/g, whereas HFib significantly reduced it to 7.77 ± 1.32 μg/g. Functionally, HFD synergized with NPs to disrupt estrous cyclicity (only 13% regular cycles), suppress anti-Müllerian hormone by 74%, and increase follicular atresia rate, while HFib maintained near-normal ovarian physiology. Transcriptomics identified steroid hormone biosynthesis and oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) as core pathways convergently dysregulated by NPs across all diets. Mechanistically, HFD amplified NP-induced ovarian oxidative stress, inflammation, and mitochondrial OXPHOS impairment, culminating in hyperandrogenism and profound estradiol deficiency. Conversely, HFib preserved aromatase expression and mitochondrial respiratory capacity, thereby restoring steroidogenic homeostasis. Mendelian randomization further linked human orthologues of these dysregulated genes, including UQCR10 and COX4I1 encoding mitochondrial complex III and IV subunits, to elevated polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) risk, highlighting the central role of OXPHOS disruption. These findings establish a diet-NP interaction pattern with implications for reproductive health guidance in populations.

articles.title: Length of Ischemic Time Is Critical for Accurate Determination of Homologous Recombination Capacity by Immunofluorescence Staining in Ovarian Cancer Formalin-Fixed Paraffin-Embedded Samples.
articles.authors: Karagöz E, Pikkusaari S, Eriksson MR et al.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT.—: Tubo-ovarian high-grade serous carcinomas (HGSC) that are deficient in homologous recombination (HR) are more sensitive to poly ADP-ribose polymerase (PARP) inhibitors than their HR-proficient counterparts. To target PARP inhibitors to the right patients, HR status must be accurately determined. Functional HR (fHR) assays, which assess HR status by quantifying RAD51, are promising approaches for identifying HR-deficient cases. However, these tests have yet to be optimized for pre-analytical variables and tissue properties that may impact RAD51 quantification.
OBJECTIVE.—: To establish how typical pre-analytical variables (ischemic time, formalin fixation, and ethanol storage) and tissue-level necrosis and hypoxia affect read-outs of fHR capacity, with systematic evaluation of prolonged ischemic time. Additionally, biological (intra-tumor) variation in fHR measurements was assessed.
DESIGN.—: The immunofluorescence-based fHR assay was performed on a retrospective and a prospectively collected cohort of formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded HGSC specimens with varying pre-analytical and tissue-level conditions. Intra-tumor variation in fHR capacity was assessed in multiple tumor areas and independent tumor pieces.
RESULTS.—: Prolonged ischemic time led to a substantial reduction in nuclear RAD51 signal, resulting in lower fHR scores and false fHR deficiency calls. The other examined variables did not significantly impact fHR scores. Intra-tumor variation in fHR scores was low, and the fHR category, when determined from different regions of the same tumor, remained unchanged.
CONCLUSIONS.—: Prolonged ischemic time adversely affects fHR assay performance, highlighting the importance of monitoring and documenting sample handling processes, particularly in HGSC, and warrants caution when interpreting fHR results from archival tumor material for which such information is unavailable.

articles.title: Tumor Cell-Free DNA Assay Analytical Performance in 101 Clinical Laboratories Participating in a College of American Pathologists Proficiency Testing Program.
articles.authors: Lockwood CM, Yellapantula V, Tsai JM et al.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT.—: Tumor cell-free DNA (cfDNA) assays are increasingly used for mutation detection in therapy selection and disease monitoring. This study evaluates the laboratory performance in College of American Pathologists (CAP) Molecular Oncology Committee tumor cfDNA proficiency testing (PT) during a 2-year period.
OBJECTIVE.—: To assess the analytical performance of clinical laboratories offering tumor cfDNA assays using well-characterized PT specimens and compare performance across analytical methods.
DESIGN.—: This study examined laboratory performance in CAP cfDNA PT programs from 2018 and 2019, with laboratories receiving multiple mailings longitudinally. Testing encompassed 12 specimens targeting 16 clinically significant canonical single-nucleotide variants in 5 oncogenes: EGFR (epidermal growth factor receptor), KRAS (KRAS proto-oncogene, GTPase), BRAF (B-Raf proto-oncogene, serine/threonine kinase), NRAS, (NRAS proto-oncogene, GTPase), and IDH1 (isocitrate dehydrogenase 1). A total of 5088 PT responses from 101 laboratories were analyzed. Results were classified as true positive, false negative, true negative, or false positive, and stratified by next-generation sequencing (NGS) versus non-NGS methods and US Food and Drug Administration-approval status.
RESULTS.—: Gene-specific sensitivities ranged from 87.1% (176 of 202) to 100.0% (80 of 80), with specificities from 98.7% (1284 of 1301) to 100.0% (827 of 827). For EGFR mutations, which had samples at lower variant allele fractions (VAFs), NGS-based assays demonstrated higher sensitivity than non-NGS methods (95.7% [88 of 92] versus 81.7% [85 of 104]; P = .002). Within the 0.1% to 0.3% VAF range, NGS-based approaches achieved significantly higher sensitivity (96.1% [73 of 76]) than non-NGS methods (78.2% [61 of 78]) (P = .01).
CONCLUSIONS.—: Clinical laboratories achieved high analytical sensitivity and specificity for tumor cfDNA PT across 5 oncogenes. NGS-based assays demonstrated superior analytical performance for EGFR mutation detection at low VAFs, with performance differences most pronounced in the 0.1% to 0.3% VAF range.

articles.title: Laboratory Capacity and Consideration for Use of Cervical Cancer Screening and Triage Tests: Cross-Sectional Survey Results of Laboratories Participating in the College of American Pathologists 2023 Gynecologic Cytopathology (PAP Education) Program.
articles.authors: Goyal A, Tabbara SO, Nayar R et al.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT.—: Cervical cancer screening and management guidelines have been changing rapidly. Current screening options include cytology alone, cytology plus human papillomavirus (HPV) testing (cotesting), and primary HPV testing with reflex to cytology or p16/Ki-67 dual staining, or with extended genotyping.
OBJECTIVE.—: To understand laboratory practices around test(s) offered for cervical cancer screening and triage modalities for positive HPV test results.
DESIGN.—: The College of American Pathologists invited 1432 laboratories (participating in the PAP Education program) to complete a supplemental questionnaire in one of their 2023 educational mailings.
RESULTS.—: Overall, 532 questionnaires were completed (387 domestic, 145 international). Among the 387 domestic laboratories, 89.7% (347) offered cotesting, 88.9% (344) offered cytology (with reflex HPV testing for "atypical squamous cell of undetermined significance"), and 16.0% (62) offered primary HPV testing (with reflex cytology). US Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved primary HPV platforms were available in 45% (108 of 240) of laboratories (Roche cobas: 41.7% [100]; BD Onclarity: 3.3% [8]). Main reasons for not offering HPV screening included not having an FDA-approved platform, and limited clinician requests. Partial HPV genotyping (HPV 16/18 ± HPV 45) was offered by 54.6% (206 of 377) and p16/Ki-67 dual staining by 6.3% (23 of 361) of laboratories.
CONCLUSIONS.—: Utilization of primary HPV screening by laboratories may be limited by access to FDA-approved testing platforms and limited client demand. Since this survey completion, Enduring Guidelines recommendations have been published for use of self-collected HPV testing and different triage modalities. Future surveys to assess the laboratories' response to evolving screening and management guidelines are warranted.

articles.title: Production, Drug Loading, and Therapeutic Delivery of Macrophage-Engineered Vesicles Via Nitrogen Cavitation.
articles.authors: Nagle J, Daniel NI, Dorosh AV et al.
articles.abstract: Endogenously produced engineered vesicles (EVs) serve many important signaling and regulatory functions in vivo, resulting in investigations into their utility as targeted therapeutic delivery vehicles. Unfortunately, the practicality of using endogenous EVs therapeutically is limited by the small number of EVs that are produced naturally. Therefore, researchers have focused on engineering artificial EVs at significantly higher yields and from a variety of cell sources. These artificial EVs have potential therapeutic effects on their own as well as the ability to serve as a means of localized drug delivery. Vesicles originating from immune cells such as macrophages are particularly attractive as these cells function in tissue repair, development, and are a critical component of the tumor microenvironment in many cancers. Macrophages are classically polarized into M1 and M2 phenotypes, where M1 cells drive pro-inflammatory responses, and M2 cells promote tissue repair. In the tumor microenvironment, tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are in an M2-like immunosuppressive state that supports cancer growth. Reprogramming M2 TAMs to an M1 state has shown promise as a novel cancer treatment strategy. We have developed a process to manufacture EVs from M1 macrophages that can reprogram M2 macrophages to an M1 state. Additionally, we are also capable of loading these vesicles with chemotherapeutics to enhance their anti-tumor effects. The anti-cancer efficacy of these engineered vesicles was tested both in vitro and in vivo in a murine ovarian cancer xenograft model. © 2026 Wiley Periodicals LLC. Basic Protocol 1: Manufacturing vesicles via nitrogen cavitation Alternate Protocol: Manufacturing cisplatin-loaded vesicles Support Protocol 1: Macrophage cell reprogramming Support Protocol 2: Vesicle characterization Support Protocol 3: Measuring cisplatin concentration in vesicles by mass spectrometry Basic Protocol 2: Measuring macrophage reprogramming and anti-tumor activity in vitro Basic Protocol 3: Intraperitoneal delivery of vesicles for in vivo treatment.

articles.title: Interventions for women with endometrioma prior to assisted reproductive technology.
articles.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
articles.authors: Harlow K, Igbokwe N, Bortoletto P et al.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: The link between endometriosis and infertility has been firmly established; however, the mechanism remains controversial. Management of ovarian endometriosis (endometrioma) in the context of assisted reproductive technology (ART) varies greatly both in regard to the intervention chosen or, indeed, the decision to treat at all. Management remains a key clinical decision for patients requiring fertility treatment and guidance from scientific evidence is vital. This is an update of a Cochrane review first published in 2010.
OBJECTIVES: To assess the effects of surgery, medical treatment, combination therapy (both medical and surgical) or no treatment for improving reproductive outcomes among women with endometrioma, prior to undergoing ART cycles.
SEARCH METHODS: We searched the Cochrane Gynaecology and Fertility Group's specialised register, CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase and PsycINFO on 7 October 2025. We also searched trial registries, checked reference lists of relevant studies and contacted experts in the field for any additional trials.
ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We selected randomised controlled trials (RCTs) that compared any medical and/or surgical intervention with another medical and/or surgical intervention or placebo/no intervention for the treatment of endometrioma prior to ART. The included population was women with endometrioma diagnosed by laparoscopy or pelvic imaging such as ultrasound, computed tomography (CT), or magnetic-resonance imaging (MRI).
OUTCOMES: Our critical outcomes of interest, as presented in the summary of findings tables, were: live birth and adverse events.
RISK OF BIAS: We used the Cochrane RoB 1 tool to assess bias in the included studies.
SYNTHESIS METHODS: Due to significant heterogeneity between the included studies, we synthesised the results into a narrative review. We summarised key findings from individual studies descriptively and we structured them by outcome domain. We used GRADE to assess the certainty of evidence for the critical outcomes.
INCLUDED STUDIES: We included a total of seven parallel-arm RCTs with 646 participants randomised. Two studies (173 participants) evaluated medical interventions and five studies (473 participants) evaluated surgical interventions for endometrioma prior to ART. No studies evaluated combination therapy.
SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS: No…
REGISTRATION: Protocol (2010) https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD008571. Original review (2010) https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD008571.pub2.

articles.title: Coverage, equity and barriers of preconception care in the Chilean public health system: A national mixed-methods study (2019-2022).
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Muñoz Soto V, Viviani P, Valdivia Cabrera G et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To analyze the use of preconception care (PCC) in the Chilean public health system between 2019 and 2022, and to explore the perceptions of regional and ministerial program leads regarding the barriers and facilitators that constrain its prioritization and uptake.
METHODS: Sequential explanatory mixed-methods study. We analyzed all 145 024 PCC visits in the Monthly Statistical Record (REM A-01, DEIS) for 2019-2022, by year, region, age group, and cadre. Visit rates and a coverage proxy used the National Health Fund (FONASA) female beneficiaries aged 15-44 as denominator (assumption: one visit/woman/year). Five semi-structured interviews with regional Programa Salud de la Mujer leads and the Ministry of Health (MINSAL) national lead were analyzed by inductive content analysis. The study was approved by CEC-Salud UC (December 2023; protocol 230 725 004).
RESULTS: PCC visits were 51 466 (2019), 21 799 (2020; -58% during COVID-19), 32 996 (2021) and 38 763 (2022); pre-pandemic levels were not recovered in any region except Magallanes. Coverage proxy percentages were 1.53%, 0.64%, 0.96%, and 1.10%. Visits concentrated in women aged 25-34; <19 and >40 years had markedly lower rates. Midwives delivered 99.06%-99.39%. Ñuble had the highest regional rate and Arica y Parinacota the lowest. Qualitative analysis yielded five categories (professional perceptions, facilitators, needs, challenges, recommendations) mapped.
CONCLUSION: PCC remains a covered but invisible service in Chile, severely underutilized and inequitably distributed. Embedding PCC into a renewed national policy, with clear technical guidance, monitoring indicators, and protected resources, is required.

articles.title: Menopausal Hormone Therapy History is Associated with Improved Postoperative Ambulatory Recovery in Postmenopausal Women with Hip Fragility Fractures.
articles.authors: Fox BQ, Kocher SD, Brown C et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare changes in ambulatory status after hip fracture surgery in women with and without a history of systemic menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) use.
METHODS: Design: Retrospective cohort.
SETTING: Single center academic Level 1 trauma center.
PATIENT SELECTION CRITERIA: Patients were included if they were female, >=50, received surgery for OTA/AO 31-A (intertrochanteric/peritrochanteric), 31-B (femoral neck), and 32-A (subtrochanteric) fragility fractures from December 2022 to September 2025, and had minimum 3-month follow-up data.
OUTCOME MEASURES AND COMPARISONS: Patients were categorized into "Ever User" and "Never User" groups based on MHT exposure documented in electronic records. Primary outcomes were postoperative ambulatory status, categorized using a six-level functional scale, and return to baseline ambulation, measured as a binary variable at 30 and 90 days postoperatively. Secondary outcomes included 30- and 90-day hospital readmission and six-month all-cause mortality. Comparisons of outcomes were made between cohorts following adjustment for age, American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) grade, baseline ambulatory status, and dementia diagnosis.
RESULTS: Among 358 included female patients, Ever Users (n=80) and Never Users (n=278) demonstrated similar ages (mean:80.6, range:60-100 vs. mean:78.8, range:50-101; P=0.14) and baseline ambulatory independence (48.8% vs. 46.0%, P=0.76). At 30 days, cohorts demonstrated similar rates of return to baseline function (25.3% vs. 23.4%; P=0.85). At 90 days, Ever Users demonstrated higher rates of independent ambulation (17.5% vs. 9.1%; P=0.029) and return to baseline status (53.8% vs. 35.8%; P<0.01). Thirty-day readmissions were less common among Ever Users (3.8% vs. 16.5%; P=0.0026), while 90-day readmission (23.8% vs. 21.6%; P=0.80) and six-month mortality (13.8% vs. 14.7%; P=0.97) were similar between groups. After adjustment for age, ASA grade, baseline ambulatory status, and dementia, MHT history was independently associated with 90-day return to baseline status (aOR 2.7, 95% CI 1.6-4.6, P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: In women undergoing fragility hip fracture surgery, history of menopausal hormone therapy use was independently associated with improved return to baseline ambulation by 90 days postoperatively. These findings suggested prior menopausal hormone therapy exposure may confer functional benefits extending beyond fracture…
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: III (Retrospective Cohort Study).

articles.title: Neuroendocrine drivers of polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) and the modifying role of adiposity.
articles.authors: Kyriakidou A, Koysombat K, Comninos AN et al.
articles.abstract: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), previously known as polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), is the commonest cause of anovulatory subfertility and represents a substantial and growing healthcare burden. PMOS is a complex neuroendocrine-ovarian-metabolic disorder in which dysregulation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal (HPG) axis disrupts ovarian function, further exacerbated by associated metabolic dysfunction. This review synthesises the current clinical evidence on neuroendocrine dysfunction in PMOS, using luteinising hormone (LH) pulsatility as a surrogate marker of gonadotrophin-releasing hormone (GnRH) neuronal activity. By drawing on parallel evidence from women with and without PMOS, we examine how adiposity modulates these parameters. In women without PMOS, obesity is associated with hypothalamic suppression. By contrast, a key neuroendocrine feature of PMOS is accelerated hypothalamic pulsatile GnRH neuronal activity, which preferentially drives LH secretion, culminating in ovarian androgen excess, follicular arrest, and anovulation. Although obesity is associated with lower mean LH concentrations due to attenuation of LH pulse amplitude, pulse frequency remains heightened. Given the high prevalence of obesity in PMOS, dampening of raised LH concentrations with obesity challenges its use as part of diagnostic criteria for PMOS in populations where obesity is prevalent. Obesity-induced metabolic dysfunction also leads to hyperinsulinaemia, which further exacerbates ovarian hyperandrogenism. The interplay between metabolic dysfunction and reproductive health is illustrated by weight-management interventions, which consistently improve ovulatory function in women with obesity and PMOS. Understanding the neuroendocrine impact of obesity on the pathophysiology of PMOS can inform both diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic targets.

articles.title: Association of single intrauterine fetal demise with severe brain injury and death in liveborn cotwins delivered before 32 weeks: large single-center retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
articles.authors: Cui X, Li Y, Yin S et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the independent association in twin pregnancy between single intrauterine fetal demise (sIUFD) and major short-term adverse outcomes, particularly severe brain injury (SBI) or death, in extremely and very preterm liveborn cotwins (delivered < 32 weeks), to examine whether this association extends beyond chorionicity and to identify critical gestational windows of vulnerability and potential mediating pathways.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort study included twin pregnancies, with or without sIUFD, delivered < 32 weeks at Shengjing Hospital of China Medical University, Shenyang, China, between January 2014 and December 2024, with neonates admitted immediately after birth to the hospital's neonatal intensive care unit. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to assess associations between sIUFD and the primary outcome, a composite of SBI or death of the liveborn cotwin prior to hospital discharge. Subgroup analyses stratified by chorionicity and gestational age at sIUFD were performed to identify risk patterns and critical gestational windows of vulnerability. Mediation analyses were conducted to explore whether the association between sIUFD and SBI or death was mediated by early-onset sepsis, disseminated intravascular coagulation within 24 h after birth or the 5-min Apgar score, and sensitivity analyses incorporating propensity-score matching to balance baseline confounders were performed to assess the robustness of the results.
RESULTS: In total, 1069 twin pregnancies delivered < 32 weeks were included (113 with and 956 without sIUFD). sIUFD was independently associated with significantly increased odds of SBI or death (adjusted odds ratio (aOR), 2.85 (95% CI, 1.61-4.97)). This association was consistent across monochorionic and dichorionic subgroups. The highest point estimate was observed when sIUFD occurred at 28 + 0 to 29 + 6 weeks' gestation (aOR, 3.72 (95% CI, 1.64-8.06)). Mediation analysis identified a 5-min Apgar score < 7,…
CONCLUSIONS: sIUFD is independently associated with an increased risk of SBI or death in liveborn cotwins delivered < 32 weeks, regardless of chorionicity, particularly when demise occurs at 28 + 0 to 29 + 6 weeks. Perinatal asphyxia is the primary mediator of this association. These findings support intensified monitoring of all surviving cotwins, with surveillance guided by the gestational age at sIUFD. © 2026 International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology.

articles.title: Efficacy of dietary supplements in improving sperm parameters in men with infertility: a network meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Shen XY, Lu LJ, Che BW et al.
articles.abstract: This network meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the efficacy of various dietary supplements on sperm parameters in men with infertility, thereby providing evidence-based guidance for future clinical practice. PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) on dietary supplements for treating male infertility published from database inception up to January 16, 2026. The risk of bias in the included studies was assessed utilizing the Cochrane risk-of-bias tool. This network meta-analysis included 56 studies. For improving semen volume, the top five supplements were lycopene, Nigella sativa oil (NSO), zinc, ubiquinol, and myoinositol. For improving sperm concentration, the top five supplements were omega-3, zinc, myoinositol, lycopene, and curcumin nanomicelle. For improving sperm progressive motility, the top five supplements were zinc, alpha-lipoic acid (ALA), myoinositol, vitamin E, and L-acetyl-carnitine (LAC). For improving the normal sperm morphology rate, the top five supplements were N-acetylcysteine (NAC), zinc, omega-3, NSO, and curcumin nanomicelle. For improving total sperm motility, the top five supplements were omega-3, curcumin nanomicelle, LAC, zinc, and ALA. For improving total sperm count, the top five supplements were ALA, curcumin nanomicelle, zinc, L-carnitine (LC), and LAC. Appropriate dietary supplements demonstrate significant efficacy in improving semen parameters in male patients with infertility. However, their efficacy varies across semen parameters. Zinc and omega-3 ranked relatively high across all six semen parameters. In clinical practice, the individual characteristics of different patients should be considered when selecting therapeutic agents and formulating personalized dietary supplement regimens.

articles.title: Updated clinical recommendations for cardiovascular risk assessment to facilitate hormone therapy prescribing: incorporating PREVENT risk calculator and the 2026 multisociety lipid guidelines.
articles.authors: Shufelt CL, Stuenkel CA, Lau ES et al.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of death among women and is a key consideration when evaluating candidates for menopausal hormone therapy (HT). Over the past two decades, recommendations regarding HT use have evolved substantially and now include the understanding that cardiovascular risk varies according to age, time since menopause onset, and baseline cardiovascular health. Consequently, cardiovascular risk assessment has become an integral component of menopause management. The recent introduction of the Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events (PREVENT) calculator and incorporation of PREVENT into the 2026 American College of Cardioloty/Amercian Heart Association multisociety dyslipidemia guideline represent an important shift in CVD prevention. PREVENT includes contemporary cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic risk factors and estimates both 10-year and 30-year cardiovascular risk for adults ages 30-79 years without known CVD. Concurrently, updated lipid management recommendations emphasize individualized risk assessment and consideration of risk-enhancing factors, and in some cases, coronary artery calcium scoring, along with more explicit lipid-lowering targets. This perspective provides a practical framework for integrating PREVENT-derived risk categories into menopause care. We outline cardiovascular risk stratification strategies for women considering HT, discuss the role of coronary artery calcium scoring and female-specific risk enhancers, and align contemporary lipid management recommendations with decisions regarding initiation of HT, including route of administration. By integrating cardiovascular risk assessment and menopause management, clinicians can optimize cardiovascular risk reduction and individualize treatment decisions for symptomatic midlife women.

articles.title: Bilateral oophorectomy after natural menopause and prevalent cardiometabolic and skeletal outcomes in US women: a cross-sectional NHANES analysis.
articles.authors: Tang C, Zheng Y, Zhan L et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To estimate associations between bilateral oophorectomy performed after natural menopause and prevalent cardiometabolic and skeletal outcomes in US women.
METHODS: We pooled 10 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey cycles (1999-2018). The analytic cohort included 321 women with chronology-confirmed bilateral oophorectomy after natural menopause and 5,363 referent women with natural menopause, no hysterectomy, and no confirmed bilateral oophorectomy. Survey-weighted quasi-Poisson models estimated prevalence ratios (PRs), adjusted for age, body mass index, education, smoking, alcohol use, and physical activity measured at the NHANES assessment. Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate control was applied across seven prespecified outcomes.
RESULTS: Bilateral oophorectomy after natural menopause was associated with higher cardiovascular disease prevalence (PR: 1.58; 95% CI: 1.13-2.21; P=0.008; q=0.039). Associations did not meet the false discovery rate threshold for diabetes (PR: 1.26; 95% CI: 0.94-1.71), hypertension (PR: 1.07; 95% CI: 0.93-1.22), osteoporosis (PR: 1.20; 95% CI: 0.90-1.60), or wrist fracture (PR: 1.54; 95% CI: 0.94-2.54). Hip and spine fractures were not estimable because of sparse exposed events. Adjustment for age at natural menopause attenuated the cardiovascular estimate (PR: 1.43; 95% CI: 1.02-2.02).
CONCLUSIONS: Bilateral oophorectomy after natural menopause was associated with higher self-reported cardiovascular disease prevalence. Because outcome timing relative to surgery was unavailable and residual confounding remains, this cross-sectional association should not be interpreted as causal or as a basis for clinical recommendations.

articles.title: The effect of aerobic and core stabilization exercises on primary dysmenorrhea in high school girls: A randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal: Journal of back and musculoskeletal rehabilitation
articles.authors: Cakmak Reyhan A, Yildirim A
articles.abstract: BackgroundPrimary dysmenorrhea is common in adolescents and is associated with menstrual pain, functional limitations, and reduced quality of life. Evidence regarding structured combined exercise programs implemented in school settings remains limited. This study examined the effects of a 12-week combined aerobic and core stabilization exercise program on pain, symptom severity, functional impairment, and quality of life in high school students with primary dysmenorrhea.MethodsA randomized controlled, assessor-blinded trial was conducted in which thirty high school girls were allocated to either an exercise group (n = 15) or a control group (n = 15). The intervention group completed a 12-week aerobic and core stabilization program, whereas the control group maintained usual activities. The primary outcome was menstrual pain intensity measured using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS). Secondary outcomes included the Premenstrual Syndrome Scale (PMSS), Menstrual Symptom Questionnaire (MSQ), Functional and Emotional Measure of Dysmenorrhea (FEMD), Dysmenorrhea Impact Scale (DIS), and Short Form-36 Health Survey (SF-36).ResultsThe exercise group demonstrated reductions in pain intensity, menstrual symptom severity, and functional impairment (p < 0.001). Quality-of-life scores improved across all domains (p < 0.001). No meaningful changes were observed in the control group (p > 0.05). Between-group analyses favored the exercise intervention across all outcomes (p < 0.001).ConclusionA combined aerobic and core-stabilization exercise program may be a feasible and effective adjunctive strategy for managing primary dysmenorrhea in adolescents. However, the restrictive BMI eligibility range (19.0-24.9 kg/m2) limits the generalizability of these findings to adolescents outside this range.

articles.title: Phenotypic age acceleration mediates the association between plant-based diet and advanced cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome among postmenopausal women: a population-based cross-sectional analysis.
articles.authors: Li N, Zhou G
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome framework highlights the links among metabolic disorders, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular complications. Research examining how plant-based dietary indices influence the progression of CKM and the potential role of biological aging remains limited.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study used data from 2,988 postmenopausal women participating in NHANES 2005-2018. Weighted logistic regression models estimated the associations between plant-based dietary indices and advanced CKM. Mediation analyses were conducted to evaluate the mediating role of phenotypic age acceleration.
RESULTS: Among the study population, 658 participants (22.0%) were identified with advanced CKM. A one-unit increase in the plant-based diet index (PDI) and the healthful PDI was associated with a lower odds of advanced CKM (adjusted odds ratio [OR]: 0.98; 95% CI: 0.96-1.00 and OR: 0.97; 95% CI: 0.94-0.99, respectively). In contrast, each one-unit increase in the unhealthful PDI was associated with 4% higher odds of advanced CKM (adjusted OR: 1.04; 95% CI: 1.01-1.07). These associations were consistent across population subgroups. Furthermore, phenotypic age acceleration partially mediated the association between PDI and advanced CKM, accounting for 16.0% (95% CI: 8.2%-25.4%).
CONCLUSIONS: Higher adherence to healthy plant-based dietary patterns is associated with a lower likelihood of advanced CKM among postmenopausal women. The association between PDI with advanced CKM may be partly mediated through reduced phenotypic age acceleration.

articles.title: Breast cancer in premenopausal and postmenopausal women: clinicopathological findings and survival outcomes from a large registry-based cohort in Southern Iran.
articles.authors: Ghaedi A, Johari MG, Mallahi A et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare clinicopathological characteristics, treatment patterns, and survival outcomes between premenopausal and postmenopausal women with breast cancer in Iran.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 6,930 women aged ≥18 years diagnosed with breast cancer between 2014 and 2022 from the Shiraz Breast Cancer Registry. Patients were stratified by menopausal status. Clinicopathological features, tumor receptor status, and treatment modalities were compared. Five-year overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS) were estimated using Kaplan-Meier methods and evaluated with multivariable Cox proportional hazards models.
RESULTS: Premenopausal women more frequently presented with aggressive tumor features, including larger tumor size, multifocality, necrosis, and adverse pathologic characteristics (all P<0.01). Postmenopausal patients had a higher prevalence of estrogen receptor-positive tumors (P=0.003) and more commonly received hormone therapy (P<0.001). Five-year OS was comparable between groups (96.1% vs. 96.0%, P=0.981), whereas DFS was higher in postmenopausal women (90.1% vs. 87.2%, P=0.030). In multivariable analysis, postmenopausal status (HR 0.49, 95% CI: 0.27-0.90) and hormone therapy (HR 0.43, 95% CI: 0.29-0.64) were independently associated with improved OS, whereas high tumor grade, concurrent lymphovascular and perineural invasion, and neoadjuvant chemotherapy were associated with poorer OS and DFS.
CONCLUSIONS: Menopausal status was associated with distinct tumor biology, clinicopathological features, and treatment patterns in breast cancer, with premenopausal patients showing more aggressive disease. Although menopausal status showed some association with survival outcomes, its effect appeared largely driven by age and underlying tumor characteristics, suggesting limited independent prognostic value.

articles.title: The relationships among gender perceptions, internalized misogyny, and body shame in postmenopausal women: a structural equation modeling study.
articles.authors: Gök B, Pelit Aksu S, Yaman Sözbir Ş
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine the associations among gender perception, internalized misogyny, and body shame in postmenopausal women using structural equation modeling.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 210 postmenopausal women recruited between March and May 2026. Data were collected using the Gender Perception Scale, the Internalized Misogyny Scale, and the Body Shame subscale of the Objectified Body Consciousness Scale. Higher Gender Perception Scale scores indicate more egalitarian gender perceptions, whereas higher Internalized Misogyny Scale and Body Shame subscale scores indicate greater internalized misogyny and body shame, respectively. Structural equation modeling was used to simultaneously examine the hypothesized associations among these variables, with age, educational level, family type, and postmenopausal height reduction included as covariates.
RESULTS: Gender perception was negatively correlated with internalized misogyny (r=-0.478, P<0.001) and body shame (r=-0.286, P<0.001), whereas internalized misogyny was positively correlated with body shame (r=0.320, P<0.001). In the structural model, more egalitarian gender perception was associated with lower internalized misogyny (standardized β=-0.48, P<0.001) and lower body shame (standardized β=-0.17, P<0.05), whereas greater internalized misogyny was associated with greater body shame (standardized β=0.25, P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: More egalitarian gender perception was associated with lower internalized misogyny and body shame, whereas greater internalized misogyny was associated with greater body shame. Given the cross-sectional design, these findings should not be interpreted as evidence of temporal or causal relationships. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify these relationships.

articles.title: Body composition and mortality across the reproductive cycle: findings from the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis.
articles.authors: Liang I, Flynn S, Watson K et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: There are greater changes in body composition during the menopause transition than at other stages in a woman's reproductive cycle. We studied fat mass (FM) and fat-free mass (FFM) in participants at different reproductive stages at the beginning of the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA) and evaluated their association with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and total mortality.
METHODS: In 3,439 women from MESA, equations to determine FM and FFM were derived from bioelectrical impedance analysis performed at exam 5 and applied to exam 1. Women were divided into three groups: reproductive phase (before final menstrual period [FMP]), menopause phase (FMP to 2 years subsequently), and late menopause phase (>2 years after FMP). Adjusted Cox multivariate models evaluated the association between FM, FFM, anthropometric measures, and MACE/total mortality.
RESULTS: In the full cohort, higher FM was significantly associated with increased MACE (HR per kg, 95% CI: 1.03 [1.01-1.05]) and mortality (1.03 [1.01-1.05]), while higher FFM was associated with lower mortality (0.96 [0.93-1.00]). In the menopause phase, FM and FFM showed clinically significant associations with total mortality (FM 1.18 [1.02-1.38]; FFM 0.71 [0.50-1.00]). These associations were not observed in women aged 48-52 years old.
CONCLUSION: Higher FM is associated with a higher risk of MACE/total mortality, whereas higher FFM is associated with a lower risk of total mortality. Associations noted in women in the menopause phase but not among similarly aged women suggest ovarian aging may influence these relationships.

articles.title: Association of omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acid intake and their ratio with severe dysmenorrhea among female adolescents: A case-control study.
articles.authors: Gracela E, Farapti F, Mat Daud Z' et al.
articles.abstract: BackgroundDysmenorrhea is a reproductive health disorder related to menstruation that is prevalent among adolescents and may lead to reduced productivity and quality of life. Severe dysmenorrhea is thought to be influenced by inflammatory mechanisms mediated by an imbalance in the dietary intake ratio of omega-3 to omega-6 fatty acids.AimTo examine the association between omega-3 intake, omega-6 intake, and the omega-3:omega-6 fatty acid intake ratio and severe dysmenorrhea compared with no dysmenorrhea among female adolescence.MethodsThis study used an analytical observational case-control design. The research was conducted from January to February 2025 at SMA Negeri 9 Surabaya, Indonesia, involving 90 female adolescents. The severity of menstrual pain was assessed using the Verbal Multidimensional Scoring System (VMSS). Dietary intake of omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids was measured using a semi-quantitative food frequency questionnaire (SQ-FFQ). Statistical analysis was performed using the Chi-squared test with a 95% confidence interval (CI).SummaryThe results of the study indicated a significant association between omega-3 fatty acid intake [P = 0.036, OR (95% CI) = 3.083 (1.170-8.129)] and the omega-3 to omega-6 intake ratio [P = 0.005, OR (95% CI) = 3.864 (1.573-9.492)] with severe dysmenorrhea. However, no significant association was found between omega-6 fatty acid intake and severe dysmenorrhea [P = 0.168, OR (95% CI) = 2.588 (0.818-8.188)]. Female adolescents are encouraged to pay attention to their dietary intake, particularly the consumption of omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids, which may be associated with the presence of severe dysmenorrhea.

articles.title: Dry eye disease in the menopausal transition: toward recognition as a hormonal manifestation.
articles.journal: Climacteric : the journal of the International Menopause Society
articles.authors: Skurski ZP, Mikkilineni A, Simon JA
articles.abstract: Dry eye symptoms affect an estimated 64-80% of perimenopausal and postmenopausal women, placing dry eye disease (DED) among the most prevalent yet least recognized manifestations of the menopausal endocrine transition. The pathophysiology centers on androgen deficiency and altered estrogen signaling, with sex hormone receptors expressed throughout the ocular surface, and the 2025 Tear Film and Ocular Surface Society Dry Eye Workshop III recognizes sex, gender and hormones as one of seven major domains influencing DED. Objective ocular surface signs are significantly worse in postmenopausal compared with premenopausal women even when subjective symptoms are similar, mirroring the symptom-sign dissociation well recognized in genitourinary syndrome of menopause. This hormonally mediated dry eye is described in recent literature as menopausal dry eye. This opinion advocates for routine screening using the validated Ocular Surface Disease Index-6 questionnaire, counseling patients on the ocular implications of hormone therapy and timely referral to eye care providers for persistent or moderate-to-severe symptoms. Recognizing dry eye as a menopausal disease can improve how ocular symptoms are attributed, discussed and treated in midlife women.

articles.title: Laparoscopic Management of Acute Appendicitis During Pregnancy-Does Appendicitis Severity Affect Neonatal and Maternal Outcomes?
articles.authors: Avrahami D, Lando MB, Sela HY et al.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo evaluate whether the severity of acute appendicitis affects maternal and neonatal outcomes in pregnant patients undergoing laparoscopic appendectomy.MethodA single center retrospective study was conducted between 1/2004 and 8/2023. Pregnant patients who underwent laparoscopic appendectomy for presumed appendicitis were identified and included according to inclusion criteria. Patients were stratified by disease severity into uncomplicated acute appendicitis (UAA), complicated acute appendicitis (CAA), and normal appendix (NA). Clinicopathological, maternal, and neonatal outcomes were compared using univariate analysis, followed by multivariate analysis for variables found significant.ResultsOf the 284 patients identified, 182 (64.1%) were included in the analysis of whom 145 (79.7%) had UAA, 21 (11.5%) had CAA and 16 (8.8%) had NA. Compared to patients with UAA and NA, those with CAA had longer operative times (51 minutes vs 30 and 41.5, p = <0.001, respectively), longer lengths of stay (4 days vs 2 and 1.5, p = <0.001) and their neonates had higher birth weights (3.33 vs 3.30 and 2.92, P = 0.011). There were no differences in the delivery mode, gestational age at delivery, preterm birth rates, incidence of small-for-gestational-age neonates, or postoperative complications. One fetal death was recorded. An exploratory analysis found that CAA was independently associated with increased birth weight.ConclusionIn pregnant patients undergoing laparoscopic appendectomy, the severity of acute appendicitis was not associated with adverse maternal or neonatal outcomes. These results suggest that laparoscopic management may be safe across the spectrum of appendicitis during pregnancy, warranting confirmation in larger multicenter studies.

articles.title: Dynamic changes in peritoneal washing cytology during neoadjuvant chemotherapy are associated with survival in advanced ovarian cancer undergoing interval debulking surgery.
articles.authors: Okawa M, Komatsu H, Hiratsuka Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Positive peritoneal washing cytology (PWC) at interval debulking surgery (IDS) is reported to predict poor outcome in advanced ovarian cancer, but longitudinal change in cytology across neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) has rarely been examined. We investigated whether the change in PWC before and after NAC is associated with survival.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 60 patients with International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics 2014 stage IIIA-IVB ovarian cancer who underwent NAC followed by IDS between 2015 and 2024. PWC was obtained at diagnostic surgery before NAC and at IDS after NAC. Survival was compared according to cytological status and its change using the Kaplan-Meier method and Cox proportional hazards models.
RESULTS: PWC was positive before and after NAC in 53 (88.3%) and 33 patients (55.0%), respectively. Among the 53 patients positive before NAC, 32 (60.4%) remained positive (persistence) and 21 (39.6%) converted to negative. Cytological status before NAC was not associated with survival, whereas positive cytology after NAC was associated with significantly shorter progression-free and overall survival (OS), as was cytological persistence. In multivariable analysis, positive cytology after NAC was associated with OS (hazard ratio 2.86, 95% confidence interval 1.22-7.18, P = .02).
CONCLUSIONS: Positive PWC after NAC was associated with poor OS in advanced ovarian cancer treated with NAC and IDS, and persistent positive cytology identified a particularly poor-prognosis subgroup. Because cytological status was closely linked to chemotherapy response and residual disease, and because the type of specimen obtained differed between the two time points, these exploratory findings require confirmation before clinical application.

articles.title: A Systematic Review on the Impact of Mental Health on Reproductive Hormones and Fertility Outcomes.
articles.authors: Ali J, Gami N
articles.abstract: Psychological stress and mental health disorders may interact with reproductive function through neuroendocrine, metabolic, behavioural, and oxidative pathways. This systematic review aimed to synthesize the available evidence on the relationship between psychological stress, mental health, reproductive hormones, and fertility outcomes in women and men, including outcomes associated with assisted reproductive technology (ART). PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar were searched for English-language human literature published between 2015 and 2025. Of 3,265 records identified, 1,020 duplicates were removed, 2,245 records underwent title and abstract screening, and 595 full-text reports were assessed for eligibility. Fifteen publications were included in the final narrative synthesis. The included evidence was heterogeneous and consisted predominantly of narrative reviews, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and one review of systematic reviews. A post hoc methodological appraisal was performed using Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) critical appraisal tools appropriate to the type of review. Stress-related activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis was associated across the reviewed literature with alterations in hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal signalling, with cortisol, prolactin, ghrelin, gonadotropins, and gonadal steroids implicated in proposed mechanisms. In women, the literature described associations with menstrual and ovulatory dysfunction, while male reproductive literature reported possible effects on testosterone and semen parameters. Evidence regarding a direct adverse effect of psychological distress on ART pregnancy outcomes was inconsistent, and meta-analytic evidence did not consistently demonstrate an association between pretreatment or treatment-related emotional distress and pregnancy outcomes. Psychological interventions showed more consistent benefits for reducing distress and improving coping than for improving reproductive endpoints. Psychological stress and reproductive health appear to be interrelated; however, the available evidence does not establish a definitive causal relationship between stress and impaired fertility. Interpretation is limited by heterogeneity in study designs, populations, stress measures, and reproductive outcomes, as well as overlapping evidence bases and the predominance of secondary literature. Prospective primary studies using standardized measures and rigorously…

articles.title: The management of endometriosis in adolescents and young adults: a systematic review.
articles.authors: Blyth U, Maslej L, Bennett G et al.
articles.abstract:
STUDY QUESTION: What evidence-based strategies are used in the treatment of endometriosis-associated symptoms in adolescents and young adults?
