SUMMARY ANSWER: The use of hormonal therapies and surgery was associated with improvements in pain symptoms in most studies; however, the certainty of evidence was very low, meaning that the true impact of these treatments remains uncertain.
WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY: Endometriosis is a chronic condition estimated to affect 1 in 10 women, with symptoms commonly present during adolescence. Current management strategies for endometriosis include analgesia, hormonal suppression, and surgery, as well as non-pharmacological measures.
STUDY DESIGN SIZE DURATION: This is a systematic review of the literature. Six databases (CINAHL, Cochrane Central Database of Controlled Trials, EMBASE, MEDLINE, PsychInfo, and Web of Science Core Collection) were searched from inception to May 2026. Search terms were related to endometriosis combined with terms regarding management and the adolescent age group.
PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS SETTING METHODS: Eligible studies included participants aged under 24 years with endometriosis and reported on outcomes in the management of endometriosis-associated symptoms. Only studies with full texts or data available in English were included. Screening and data extraction were performed independently and in duplicate by two authors. Key outcomes included pain, quality of life, recurrence, and side effects. Data were reported narratively. Risk of bias was assessed according to study design (ROB2, NOS, and JBI tools) and quality of evidence with the GRADE system.
MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE: The search identified 14 376 records, of which 333 full texts were assessed for eligibility, and 23 studies, with a combined total of 1561 participants, were included. There were two randomised controlled trials, one single-arm open-label interventional study, eleven cohort studies, and nine case series. Five studies investigated hormonal treatments, one other study assessed other pharmacological treatments, sixteen studies assessed surgical management with or without hormonal treatment, and one study investigated non-pharmacological treatments. Most studies reported improvements in pain symptoms; however, there was heterogeneity in study design, length of follow-up, and outcome measures.
LIMITATIONS REASONS FOR CAUTION: There is limited evidence in this age group. Most studies…
REGISTRATION NUMBER: CRD420251018467.

articles.title: Cardiovascular Events After Preeclampsia by Gestational Age at Diagnosis and Severity: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Chung CH, Ho CH, Chen YC et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Our objective is to evaluate the association between preeclampsia and early major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), including heart failure, stroke, and myocardial infarction. Additionally, we assessed whether the onset of preeclampsia (EOPE vs LOPE) affects cardiovascular risk differently. By utilizing a large, comprehensive, and nationwide dataset with strong longitudinal follow-up, we aim to evaluate whether gestational age at diagnosis is associated with distinct patterns of cardiovascular health, thereby enhancing postpartum surveillance and preventive strategies in clinical practice.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this nationwide cohort study using Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database (2016-2022), women with preeclampsia were matched 1:10 with controls by age, year, and residential area. The primary outcome was a composite of first hospitalization for myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, or heart failure. Secondary outcome included all-cause mortality. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs).
RESULTS: Among 31,694 women with preeclampsia and 316,940 controls, 1.97% and 0.79% developed MACE, respectively. Preeclampsia was associated with increased risks of MACE (aHR 1.81; 95% CI, 1.64-1.99), myocardial infarction (aHR 2.19; 95% CI, 1.34-3.59), stroke (aHR 1.59; 95% CI, 1.41-1.80), heart failure (aHR 3.85; 95% CI, 3.00-4.95), and all-cause mortality (aHR 1.85; 95% CI, 1.50-2.29). Both early- and late-onset preeclampsia were associated with elevated risk, with the largest point estimate observed in those with severe early-onset disease, particularly for heart failure (aHR 10.10; 95% CI, 6.57-15.53).
CONCLUSION: Preeclampsia is associated with substantially increased early cardiovascular risk. Both early- and late-onset disease warrant subsequent cardiovascular surveillance, particularly in severe cases.

articles.title: Longitudinal Dynamics of Circulating NET-Associated Biomarkers and Their Association with Progressive Perihematomal Edema After Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage.
articles.authors: Wei N, Yang J, Yue J et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: In patients with spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (sICH), perihematomal edema (PHE) is a major driver of secondary brain injury, yet the temporal dynamics of circulating neutrophil extracellular trap (NET)-associated biomarkers and their clinical relevance to PHE progression remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to characterize their longitudinal dynamics and associations with PHE progression and clinical outcomes after sICH.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, 200 patients with sICH (70 surgical and 130 non-surgical) and 50 healthy controls were enrolled, with serial peripheral blood samples collected at four predefined time points. Plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA), citrullinated histone H3 (CitH3), myeloperoxidase-DNA (MPO-DNA), and neutrophil elastase-DNA (NE-DNA) complexes were quantified. NET-associated neutrophil phenotypes were characterized by flow cytometry, with scanning electron microscopy for complementary ultrastructural assessment. PHE volume was quantified using 3D Slicer, and 90-day functional outcomes were assessed. In the non-surgical cohort, five regression algorithms were compared for exploratory estimation of peak PHE volume from baseline features using all 36 baseline variables within nested cross-validation. SHAP was used to interpret the best-performing model.
RESULTS: Circulating NET-associated biomarkers were markedly elevated in patients with sICH (all P < 0.001), with descriptive plots suggesting different temporal patterns in the surgical and non-surgical subgroups. SEM revealed NET-like extracellular ultrastructures in peripheral neutrophils. In the non-surgical cohort, PHEV was highest at T3 (3-5 days after onset) among the four scheduled assessments; baseline MPO-DNA was strongly correlated with peak PHE volume (ρ = 0.76, P < 0.001) and remained independently associated after multivariable adjustment. Within the non-surgical cohort, exploratory machine-learning analysis identified CitH3, MPO-DNA, and hematoma volume as the top-ranked contributors to peak PHEV…
CONCLUSION: Circulating NET-associated biomarkers showed temporal changes after sICH. In the non-surgical cohort, higher baseline MPO-DNA was associated with greater peak PHEV and unfavorable 90-day functional outcome. These findings point to a biological link that larger multicenter studies now need to confirm; the machine-learning findings remain exploratory and require external validation before clinical application.

articles.title: Clinical efficacy of mirabegron in the treatment of female patients with Parkinson's disease and overactive bladder.
articles.authors: Li L, Yu H, Zhang C
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare short-term clinical outcomes and adverse events associated with mirabegron and tolterodine treatment in female patients with Parkinson's disease (PD) and overactive bladder (OAB).
METHODOLOGY: This retrospective cohort analysis included 90 female patients with PD and OAB treated in Huzhou Third Municipal Hospital from January 2021 to October 2024. The final study cohort comprised 45 patients receiving mirabegron and 45 patients receiving tolterodine, selected in a 1:1 ratio with consideration of available baseline clinical characteristics. The primary efficacy outcome was the change in Overactive Bladder Symptom Score (OABSS) from baseline to 12 weeks. Secondary outcomes included changes in urinary diary variables and the occurrence of adverse events, while changes in the Nonmotor Symptoms Scale (NMSS) and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) were considered exploratory outcomes.
RESULTS: A significant group × time interaction was observed for urgency episodes/24 hours (IRR=0.684, 95% CI 0.515-0.908, P=0.009), indicating a greater reduction over time in the mirabegron group. No significant interactions were observed for nocturia episodes/night (IRR=0.938, 95% CI 0.794-1.108, P=0.450) or micturitions /24 hours(IRR=0.962, 95% CI 0.906-1.021, P=0.202). Significant group × time interactions were also observed for OABSS (estimate=-0.422, 95% CI -0.813 to -0.031, P=0.034) and PSQI (estimate=-1.956, 95% CI -3.098 to -0.813, P=0.001), whereas the interaction for NMSS was not significant (estimate=0.244, 95% CI -0.754 to 1.243, P=0.631). There was no significant difference in the incidence of individual adverse events between the two groups after treatment (P>0.05). However, the proportion of patients experiencing at least one adverse event was significantly lower in the mirabegron group than in the tolterodine group (20.0% vs. 44.4%, P=0.013).
CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cohort of female patients with PD and OAB, mirabegron treatment was associated with greater short-term improvements in selected OAB-related outcomes and sleep quality, as well as a lower proportion of patients experiencing adverse events, compared with tolterodine over 12 weeks. These findings require confirmation in prospective randomized studies.

articles.title: Histopathological Subtype and Cancer Stem Cell Marker Expression in Advanced Epithelial Ovarian Cancer: A Two-Year Progression-Free Survival Study.
articles.authors: Budiana ING, Saspriyana KY
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Late detection and significant recurrence rates make epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) one of the deadliest gynecologic cancers. Cancer stem cells (CSCs) have been associated with chemoresistance and relapse. However, their prognostic significance remains uncertain. This study examined CSC marker expression in advanced EOC with 2-year progression-free survival (PFS) and the predictive significance of type I/type II classification in histological subtypes.
METHODS: We performed an ambispective cohort study of 114 women with advanced EOC who had undergone optimal cytoreductive surgery and standard platinum-based chemotherapy. Expression of CD24, CD44, CD117, CD133, and aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH) was studied by immunohistochemistry. PFS was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier methods and correlations were assessed using chi-square or Fisher's exact test. The predictive value was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Independent predictors of PFS were identified by multivariate Cox regression analysis.
RESULTS: Most patients had stage III disease (60.5%) and were 40-59 years old (65.8%) significantly associated with poor survival (P < 0.001). Type II cancers had significantly worse 2-year PFS compared to type I tumors (21.3% vs. 44.8%, P = 0.008). None of the single CSC markers were significantly associated with PFS in univariate analysis (all P > 0.05) and had poor discrimination in ROC analysis. The combined assessment of CSC markers and histological classification further improved the prognostic stratification and was significantly associated with PFS (P < 0.05). In multivariate analysis, age, tumor stage, and histology type were independent predictors of PFS.
CONCLUSION: Expression of CSC markers alone is not an independent predictor of 2-year PFS in advanced EOC. Its prognostic relevance is modulated by tumor histology as type I/type II provides a stronger and more consistent prognostic stratification.

articles.title: Prevalence of Pathogenic Variants and Variants of Uncertain Significance in Patients With Epithelial Ovarian Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Zhang W, Chen D, Zeng J et al.
articles.abstract: Variants of uncertain significance (VUS) are increasingly identified when using multigene panel next-generation sequencing (NGS) for epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) patients. This meta-analysis is aimed at estimating the prevalence of pathogenic variants (PV) and VUS in EOC patients receiving multigene panel testing. We retrieved pertinent literature from PubMed, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Library, following the PRISMA 2020. Our analysis included 19 studies involving 3323 patients. Meta-analysis of proportions via logit transformation was performed. At the gene level, the pooled proportion of tested genes in which at least one PV was detected was 82%, and the corresponding proportion for VUS was 87%. At the patient level, 24% of patients carried at least one PV, and 11% carried at least one VUS. BRCA1/2 mutations accounted for the majority (22%) of PV within the homologous recombination repair (HRR) pathway, whereas expanding testing to additional HRR panels tripled the VUS rate (from 5% to 14%). The difference between PV prevalence and VUS prevalence was significantly greater for classic DNA damage repair (DDR) genes than for other panel genes. BRCA1, BRCA2, RAD51D, and RAD51C exhibited the greatest disparities in the proportions of PV and VUS, indicating a positive risk-benefit balance regarding clinical decision-making. Our findings suggest that the probability of detecting a VUS in other panel genes is significantly higher than in classic DDR genes, highlighting the underreporting of VUS in clinical studies. Routine clinical reporting may prioritize well-established EOC-risk genes, with multigene panel testing reserved for selected subgroups. Improving the reporting and classification of VUS is essential, and future studies should prioritize gene-specific VUS evaluation.

articles.title: Relationship Between Estrogen-Induced BRCA2 and Development of Gastric Cancer.
articles.authors: Hayashi T, Konishi I
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gastric cancer (GC) is the fourth most common malignancy, affecting one in 11 men (9.1%) and one in 23 women (4.38%). Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection and smoking are the primary risk factors for GC. Individuals who have multiple other family members with GC are also at higher risk owing to lifestyle and genetic factors. H. pylori-eradicating medications can reduce the risk of disease. The incidence of GC increases after 50 years of age, particularly among men; however, the reason for the differing incidence rates between the sexes remains unclear.
METHODS: To clarify the reasons for sex differences in GC incidence rates from a molecular pathological perspective, we utilized cancer genome profiling (CGP) and information on BRCA2 expression levels obtained by immunohistochemistry and the number of GC cases in the family.
RESULTS: We investigated the incidence of GC in families with hereditary breast and ovarian cancer (HBOC) and found it to be 4.2-fold higher than that in non-HBOC families. In families with versus without HBOC, men accounted for 74.57% and 53.67% of all GC cases, respectively, indicating that men are more likely to develop GC in the former group. Furthermore, estrogen stimulation induced breast cancer type 2 (BRCA2) expression in genetically modified mice as well as in cultured cells, and low-grade atypical cells were observed in the gastric mucosal tissues of female mice that underwent ovarian resection. Additional research experiment revealed that stimulation by the female hormone estrogen induces the expression of BRCA2, which suppresses the development of GC. Clinical studies have also shown that patients with GC who have high BRCA2 expression exhibit longer survival rates than those in whom BRCA2 expression is low.
CONCLUSIONS: Overall, the data suggest that the higher mortality rate of GC in men than in women may be due to a protective effect of BRCA2.

articles.title: N6-methyladenosine reader IGF2BP3 promotes endometrial cancer progression via modification of circ-EPB41L2 expression.
articles.authors: Lai L, Feng X, Zheng Y et al.
articles.abstract: Endometrial cancer is one of the primary contributors to cancer-related mortality on a global scale. Insulin-like growth factor 2 mRNA binding protein 3 (IGF2BP3) is a reader protein of N6-methyladenosine (m6A) modifications and serves a key role in the carcinogenesis of numerous solid tumors. The present study explored the role and underlying mechanism of IGF2BP3 in endometrial cancer. Bioinformatics methods were applied to examine m6A reader protein expression levels and their effect on survival. Reverse transcription-quantitative PCR and western blotting were used to determine IGF2BP3 expression in cancer and paracancerous tissues. After knockdown of IGF2BP3 expression, cell proliferation and migration were examined. Significantly expressed genes were identified through Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes and Gene Ontology analysis. Additionally, the cross-linking immunoprecipitation followed by high-throughput sequencing (CLIP-seq) database and methylated RNA immunoprecipitation (MeRIP) techniques were employed to ascertain the targets of IGF2BP3. The present study revealed that the expression levels of IGF2BP1, IGF2BP3, RNA binding motif protein 15 and YTH N6-methyladenosine RNA binding protein C2 differed between normal and endometrial cancer tissue, based on The Cancer Genome Atlas analysis. Through examination of endometrial cancer tissues and Kaplan-Meier analysis, IGF2BP3 was determined to be a target for further research. Following knockdown of IGF2BP3 expression in HEC-1A cells using short hairpin RNA transfection, proliferation and migration were decreased compared with those in the control group. A transcriptome-wide RNA-sequencing assay indicated that circular RNA (circ) was abnormally expressed in endometrial carcinoma and was regulated by IGF2BP3. CLIP-seq database analysis and MeRIP suggested that circ-erythrocyte membrane protein band 4.1 like-2 (EPB41L2) was the target of IGF2BP3. IGF2BP3 was involved in the progression of endometrial cancer and served an oncogenic role by targeting circ-EPB41L2 in an m6A-dependent manner.

articles.title: Age-related differences in postoperative pain after single-port access adnexal laparoscopy: a three-arm analgesic strategy comparison.
articles.authors: Paik ES, Yu M, Kang J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study evaluated age-related differences in postoperative pain and analgesic requirements after single-port access (SPA) laparoscopy for adnexal disease under three analgesic regimens.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 470 patients stratified into: <40 years (n = 257), 40-55 years (n = 138), and >55 years (n = 75). Patients received continuous wound infiltration (CWI) alone, intravenous patient-controlled analgesia (IV PCA) alone, or combined CWI + IV PCA. NRS pain scores at 6, 12, 24, and 48 h were the primary outcomes. Multivariable regression adjusted for analgesic regimen, surgery type, and body mass index, with additional adjustment for endometriosis in sensitivity analysis.
RESULTS: Unadjusted NRS scores did not differ among age groups. Rescue nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug use was higher in patients aged <40 years at 0-6, 6-12, and 24-48 h. After adjustment, patients aged <40 years had significantly higher NRS scores at 24 h (β = 0.276, p = 0.046). Combined CWI and IV PCA was associated with the lowest postoperative pain scores across age groups; however, a formal age × treatment interaction was not statistically significant. Sensitivity analysis yielded consistent findings.
CONCLUSIONS: Younger age (<40 years) was independently associated with modestly higher postoperative pain at 24 h after SPA adnexal laparoscopy, although this difference was below the minimal clinically important difference. These findings may inform individualized analgesic planning, pending confirmation in prospective studies.

articles.title: Gestational PFOS Exposure Impairs Placental System A (SNAT2)-Mediated Amino Acid Transport and Labyrinth Vascularization in Rats and Differentiated BeWo Monolayers.
articles.authors: Yadav P, Hofmann A, Mishra JS et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: This study investigated mechanisms underlying perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS)-associated fetal growth restriction. Specifically, we asked whether PFOS directly impairs transcellular transfer of substrates representing three major nutrient classes-glucose, long-chain fatty acid, and system A-mediated neutral amino acid transport-across the placental epithelial barrier, and examined the transporters involved.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Syncytialized human BeWo b30 monolayers cultured on collagen-coated Transwell inserts were exposed to PFOS (10 and 50 μM) for 24 h. Transcellular transport of [3H]-2-deoxy-D-glucose, [1-14C]-linoleic acid, and the system A-specific substrate L-[14C]MeAIB was quantified. Transporter expression was assessed by digital PCR and Western blot. Timed-pregnant Sprague-Dawley rats received PFOS (10 or 50 mg/L, corresponding to 1.2 and 6.1 mg/kg/day) in drinking water from gestational day (GD) 4 to 20 (n = 5 dams/group). Maternal intake and body weight, fetal and placental weights, and labyrinth zone SNAT and CD31 expression were quantified.
RESULTS: In BeWo monolayers, PFOS did not alter transcellular transport of 2-deoxy-D-glucose or linoleic acid but reduced MeAIB transport by 24% (10 μM) and 28% (50 μM). SNAT2 mRNA and protein were dose-dependently downregulated; SNAT1 mRNA was reduced only at 50 μM, with no change in SNAT1 protein, and SNAT4 was expressed at very low levels in this model. In pregnant rats, PFOS reduced fetal weight at both exposures (9% and 15% at 10 and 50 mg/L) and reduced placental and labyrinth zone weights, without altering maternal water intake, feed intake, gestational weight gain, or litter size. Quantitative immunohistochemistry showed dose-dependent reductions in labyrinth zone SNAT2 (60% and 79% at 10 and 50 mg/L) and SNAT1 immunostaining, with no change in SNAT4, together with reduced…
CONCLUSIONS: Gestational PFOS exposure impairs placental system A-mediated neutral amino acid transport, as measured with the system A-specific substrate MeAIB, without detectable effects on 2-deoxy-D-glucose or linoleic acid transfer under identical conditions, and is accompanied by downregulation of the stress-responsive syncytiotrophoblast transporter SNAT2. In vivo, this epithelial transport defect coincides with reduced labyrinth zone vascularization. Together, these epithelial and vascular changes describe a plausible route by which a persistent environmental contaminant constrains maternal-fetal nutrient supply.

articles.title: Menstrual, Reproductive, and Menopausal Histories of Female Patients with Cardiovascular Disease: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.authors: Goulets D, Quansah DY, Mir H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Female-specific factors may influence cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk; however, their distribution across different CVD diagnoses is not well characterized. This study examined associations between female-specific health factors and CVD subtype among female patients with established CVD.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included female patients aged ≥ 18 years with a diagnosis of CVD who received care at the University of Ottawa Heart Institute between June 2022 and December 2023. Participants were categorized by primary diagnosis: arrhythmia, coronary artery disease (CAD), cardiomyopathy, congenital heart disease, heart failure, valvular heart disease, peripheral vascular disease, or cerebrovascular disease. We examined the associations between female-specific factors and each diagnosis, compared with all other CVD diagnoses and adjusted for age.
RESULTS: Among the 2228 respondents, the most common diagnoses were arrhythmia (30.8%) and CAD (27.7%). Early menarche was more common among participants with CAD (odds ratio [OR] 1.60, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.11-2.31). Irregular menstrual cycles were more common among female patients with congenital heart disease (OR 1.43, 95% CI 1.01-2.02). Female patients with CAD also had greater odds of having gestational diabetes (OR 1.94, 95% CI 1.29-2.90), hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (OR 1.52, 95% CI 1.08-2.12), and premature menopause (OR 1.36, 95% CI 1.01-1.83). Migraine was associated with peripheral vascular disease (OR 1.97, 95% CI 1.18-3.29), and vasomotor menopausal symptoms were frequently reported by female patients with cerebrovascular disease (OR 2.45, 95% CI 1.10-5.49).
CONCLUSIONS: Female-specific reproductive and hormonal factors differed across CVD diagnoses among female patients with established CVD. These findings highlight the importance of incorporating reproductive and hormonal history into cardiovascular risk assessment, and they support the need for further research on sex-specific pathways underlying various CVD subtypes.

articles.title: Oral microenvironmental dysregulation and female reproductive health: clinical evidence, immunological mechanisms, and bidirectional crosstalk.
articles.authors: Yu J, Lei B, Zhang M et al.
articles.abstract: Oral microenvironmental dysregulation, particularly at the periodontal interface, represents a potential source of microbial and host-derived signals that may influence female reproductive health through host-microbiome interactions and immune-mediated inflammatory pathways. Clinical and epidemiological studies have reported associations between oral or periodontal conditions and bacterial vaginosis, fecundability, time to conception, polycystic ovary syndrome, and other gynaecological conditions; however, the evidence remains heterogeneous and causal relationships are not established. Most available clinical evidence is observational, while many of the proposed molecular and tissue-level mechanisms are supported by experimental or indirect evidence, with the strength of support varying across reproductive outcomes and biological pathways. This review synthesises current clinical evidence and discusses the biological and immunological mechanisms potentially linking oral and periodontal dysregulation with female reproductive health. At the periodontal interface, community-level microbial dysbiosis, altered physicochemical conditions, non-resolving inflammation, and epithelial barrier impairment may disrupt mucosal homeostasis and permit microbial products and host-derived inflammatory signals to access systemic circulation. These signals may subsequently be amplified through innate immune activation, altered myeloid-cell responses, endothelial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and metabolic pathways, thereby modifying tissue-specific responses in the cervicovaginal mucosa, endometrium, ovary, and gestational tissues. Direct haematogenous dissemination of oral microorganisms appears biologically plausible in selected intrauterine infections, whereas systemic host-mediated mechanisms may better explain the broader spectrum of reported oral-reproductive associations. Conversely, hormonal fluctuations and endocrine-metabolic disturbances may alter periodontal susceptibility and inflammatory responses to dental biofilm. Current evidence supports biologically plausible and potentially bidirectional interactions between oral mucosal dysregulation and female reproductive health, although their direction, magnitude, disease specificity, and clinical significance remain incompletely defined. Future longitudinal and interventional studies integrating periodontal phenotyping, microbiome profiling, immune-metabolic assessment, and reproductive evaluation are required to…

articles.title: Therapeutic efficacy of mesenchymal stem cells for the restoration of dysfunctional rat testes.
articles.authors: Mishra R, Kumari A, Negi A et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chemotherapy, especially with alkylating agents, can impair spermatogonial stem cells in young males, leading to infertility. This study evaluates the therapeutic efficacy of bone-marrow-derived Mesenchymal Stem Cells (BM-MSCs) in restoring testicular function of the dysfunctional testes in a chemo-ablated infertile rat model.
METHOD: Wistar male rats were randomly divided into three groups: the first control group without any treatment; the second group was infertile chemo-ablated, generated through the intraperitoneal injections of 15 mg/kg of Busulfan, twice with a two-week interval; and the third group was chemo-ablated and subsequently treated with intra-testicular injections of enriched MSCs. The BM-MSCs were cultured and sorted using magnetic-activated cell sorting (MACS), and purity was confirmed by Fluorescence-Activated Cell Sorting (FACS) analysis of positive and negative cell-surface markers. Purified MSCs were injected into the testes of the infertile rats. Results were evaluated after 2-10 weeks of treatment. After 2 weeks of MSC treatment, mating trials for these males were conducted every 2 weeks, and their testes, as well as serum samples; were collected for therapeutic assessment of MSCs.
RESULTS: Histological assessments of the excised testes revealed a gradual, significant improvement within 10 weeks of treatment. Additionally, the expression levels of stem cell and sperm maturation markers were elevated in the testes of treated animals, indicating recovery of spermatogenesis. Hormonal analyses demonstrated normalisation of FSH and Testosterone levels after treatment. Mating studies also demonstrated that the MSC-treated group delivered 7-8 pups per litter, whereas chemo-ablated animals remained totally infertile.
CONCLUSIONS: Overall findings support MSC transplantation as a promising approach to restore testicular function and fertility, inspiring continued exploration in regenerative medicine.

articles.title: VISTA as an emerging immune checkpoint in cervical cancer: spatial immune regulation, myeloid-T Cell crosstalk, and therapeutic opportunities.
articles.authors: Li W, Wei W, Wen D et al.
articles.abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade has improved the treatment of cervical cancer, yet resistance remains a major clinical challenge. V-domain immunoglobulin suppressor of T-cell activation (VISTA; encoded by VSIR) is an emerging immune checkpoint expressed across myeloid cells, lymphocytes, and vascular endothelium. Its clinical significance appears context-dependent: some studies associate VISTA with unfavorable clinicopathological features, whereas others link abundant intratumoral VISTA-positive immune cells to improved survival. These findings highlight a critical distinction between checkpoint expression and functional immune suppression. This Mini Review synthesizes cervical cancer-specific pathology and mechanistic evidence from other tumor models, focusing on myeloid-T-cell crosstalk, T-cell quiescence, ligand-dependent regulation, and endothelial control of immune-cell trafficking. Interactions involving PSGL-1, VSIG-3, and LRIG1 suggest that VISTA activity varies across cellular and microenvironmental contexts, although their causal roles in cervical cancer remain to be established. Experimental studies support investigating VISTA blockade alongside established checkpoint inhibitors, but available clinical data have not demonstrated efficacy in cervical cancer. Future studies should integrate compartment-specific VISTA assessment, spatial immune profiling, and functional analyses of paired pretreatment and on-treatment specimens to identify VISTA-dependent immune states. Such an approach may provide a basis for biomarker-guided patient selection and rational development of VISTA-targeted immunotherapies.

articles.title: Potential synergy between GLP-1 receptor agonists and follicle-stimulating hormone in improving spermatogenesis: biological rationale and future directions.
articles.authors: La Vignera S, Calogero AE, Cannarella R et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Male infertility represents a significant global health burden, with obesity and metabolic dysfunction emerging as major contributors to impaired spermatogenesis and functional hypogonadism. Follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) has been employed to stimulate spermatogenesis in selected patients, while glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have demonstrated beneficial effects on male reproductive function beyond their metabolic actions. Understanding their potential synergistic mechanisms may open new therapeutic avenues.
METHODS: We conducted a narrative review examining FSH signaling in spermatogenesis, GLP-1 receptor expression in testicular cells, the impact of obesity on male reproduction, and the molecular mechanisms underlying GLP-1RA-FSH synergistic interactions. Relevant studies were identified through a structured non-systematic search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus (last searched September 2025), using search terms including 'GLP-1 receptor agonists', 'semaglutide', 'liraglutide', 'follicle-stimulating hormone', 'FSH', 'spermatogenesis', 'male infertility', 'obesity', and 'functional hypogonadism', supplemented by manual reference screening. No formal quality appraisal tool was applied, consistent with the narrative review format.
RESULTS: FSH acts primarily through Sertoli cells via cAMP-dependent pathways, with clinical efficacy demonstrated in men with idiopathic oligozoospermia and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism. GLP-1 receptors are expressed in Leydig, Sertoli, and germ cells; GLP-1RAs improve testosterone, gonadotropin secretion, and sperm parameters predominantly in obese men with functional hypogonadism. Obesity impairs spermatogenesis through HPG axis suppression, insulin resistance, aromatase activity, oxidative stress, and chronic…
CONCLUSIONS: The convergence of GLP-1 and FSH signaling in testicular cells, combined with GLP-1RA metabolic benefits in obese infertile men, provides a strong biological rationale for combination therapy. Preliminary clinical evidence supports GLP-1RA efficacy in improving reproductive outcomes in men with obesity-associated hypogonadism; this benefit appears conditional on pre-existing metabolic dysfunction, with negligible or mildly adverse effects in eugonadal metabolically healthy men. Prospective randomized controlled trials are urgently needed to evaluate combined GLP-1RA and FSH therapy, with particular attention to responder profiles and long-term reproductive outcomes.

articles.title: Extracellular miR-517a in Embryo Culture Medium Is Associated With Implantation Failure After Frozen-Thawed Embryo Transfer.
articles.authors: Nagata K, Kajimura I, Nagata A et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate whether placenta-associated microRNAs in embryo culture medium can serve as non-invasive biomarkers of embryo implantation potential.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 122 patients who underwent frozen-thawed embryo transfer in 2022. Embryos were evaluated using the Gardner classification, and those scoring ≥ 3BB were defined as morphologically good-quality. Placenta-associated microRNAs [chromosome 19 microRNA cluster (C19MC): miR-517a, miR-518b, miR-517c; chromosome 14 microRNA cluster (C14MC): miR-323-3p, miR-411, miR-433] in embryo culture medium were quantified by RT-qPCR and correlated with implantation outcomes.
RESULTS: Forty-nine patients (40.2%) achieved pregnancy and 73 (59.8%) did not. C19MC levels were significantly higher in the non-pregnant group, with miR-517a showing the strongest association with implantation failure (p < 0.0001, AUC = 0.7246). Among morphologically good-quality embryos, the pregnancy rate increased from 53.8% to 64.7% when embryo selection incorporated miR-517a assessment. Multivariable logistic regression analysis demonstrated that extracellular miR-517a remained independently associated with implantation outcome after adjustment for maternal age, trophectoderm grade, and fertilization method.
CONCLUSIONS: Extracellular miR-517a may provide clinically useful, non-invasive information regarding embryo implantation potential and may complement conventional morphology-based embryo assessment.

articles.title: Gynecological cancers on a chip: status, advances, and future.
articles.authors: He Y, Shastri VP
articles.abstract: Gynecological cancers, including cervical cancer, ovarian cancer, and endometrial cancer, negatively influence women's physical and mental wellbeing. Modeling disease progression could enable new therapeutic interventions. The development of microfluidic technology has led to the creation of gynecological cancer-on-a-chip (CoC) models. Since the tumor microenvironment (TME), along with other physiological variables such as microvasculature, shear stress due to blood flow, and biological barriers, can be simulated in a chip setup, these factors can be used to model how tumor cells cross blood vessels and migrate to invade other organs. Therefore, fluidic chips, integrating organoids and other biofabrication concepts, provide a fresh approach to elaborate tumor molecular mechanisms and treatment strategies since physiological variables (signaling and cellular processes) can be controlled. Although gynecological cancer chips have many advantages, the number of related studies is limited. Currently, the research landscape is primarily focused on TME reconstruction and drug screening, while the incorporation of tissue-derived samples and organoids has yet to gain traction. This review summarizes the current status of research, along with technical progress and future challenges, thus providing a comprehensive reference for further research in this field.

articles.title: Multiomic liquid biopsy: emerging applications in disease quantification, biomarker detection, molecular phenotyping, and cancer signal of origin prediction.
articles.authors: Gheeya JS, Welch L, Porter J et al.
articles.abstract: The field of cancer-related liquid biopsy, largely defined as plasma circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) analysis by next-generation sequencing (NGS), is rapidly evolving from genomics-only approaches to multiomic assays that add components such as DNA fragmentomics and epigenomics, with or without proteomics, to a genomic backbone. Here we describe how integration of epigenomic profiling, particularly tumor-specific methylation signatures, may extend ctDNA testing beyond detection of genomic alterations toward broader molecular phenotyping, with applications in alternative approaches to tumor fraction quantification, enhanced detection of actionable genomic biomarkers and mechanisms of resistance, histologic and lineage characterization, and cancer signal of origin prediction. This evolution has facilitated the clinical application of liquid biopsy across the cancer care continuum, from screening/early detection to determining minimal residual disease (MRD) in early-stage cancers to selecting treatment and determining mechanisms of acquired resistance in advanced-stage cancers. These new multiomic assays may also support prospective biomarker-driven clinical trials incorporating complementary measures of tumor burden, genomic alterations, and molecular phenotype. Collectively, these advances suggest that multiomic liquid biopsy platforms may represent a major advance in precision oncology, enabling dynamic and comprehensive characterization of tumor biology.

articles.title: A tale of a different tail: does the H3f3b 3'UTR explain the divergent knockout phenotypes?
articles.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
articles.authors: Zhang J, Chung H, Wen D
articles.abstract: The replication-independent histone variant H3.3 is encoded by two unlinked genes, H3f3a and H3f3b, that produce an identical protein. Nevertheless, published H3f3b mutant models report markedly divergent phenotypes, ranging from normal viability and fertility to growth restriction, infertility, and perinatal lethality. Here, we propose that these discrepancies arise partly from differences in allele architecture, particularly the position and transcript context of the native H3f3b 3'UTR. Across the available alleles, the 3'UTR is deleted, retained downstream of an engineered polyadenylation signal, preserved in its native context, recoupled to a reporter coding sequence, or displaced downstream of an intervening reporter cassette. Homozygous H3.3B-KO-mCherry mice lack H3.3B protein but retain and transcribe the native chromosomal 3'UTR directly downstream of mCherry and are viable and fertile. By contrast, H3.3B-HA-IRES-EYFP is a protein-producing knock-in in which the full-length native 3'UTR is retained downstream of both the H3.3B-HA and EYFP stop codons, with the IRES-EYFP sequence interposed between the H3.3B-HA and the 3'UTR; homozygous mice show reduced birth weight and early postnatal lethality. Compound offspring carrying both engineered alleles and lacking an unmodified wild-type H3f3b allele were recovered at Mendelian frequency. These observations support altered 3'UTR context and 3'-end processing as potential contributors to the divergent phenotypes, although genetic background and other features of allele construction remain relevant. We discuss possible regulation of the H3f3b transcript in cis, effects on other genes through shared microRNAs or RNA-binding proteins, and control of alternative cleavage and polyadenylation, and propose matched allelic tests of these mechanisms.

articles.title: Integrating paternal preconception health and sperm molecular biology into proportionate clinical counseling.
articles.authors: Liu J, Qin L, Liu B et al.
articles.abstract: Paternal preconception health increasingly appears to modulate reproductive success through alterations in classical semen parameters and spermatozoal molecular architecture. Beyond nuclear genomic transmission, ejaculated spermatozoa convey regulatory chromatin configurations, retained histones, and diverse small non-coding RNA populations to the oocyte. This narrative review synthesizes evidence across metabolic conditions, lifestyle choices, environmental and occupational toxicant exposures, advanced paternal age, thermal insults, and gonadotoxic therapeutic regimens. Furthermore, emerging considerations regarding psychological strain, circadian misalignment, microplastic accumulation, and male reproductive tract microbial dysbiosis are critically evaluated. We critically synthesize preclinical, epidemiological, and interventional data addressing sperm concentration, motility, morphology, spermatozoal DNA integrity, and coupled clinical endpoints. These clinical benchmarks encompass fertilization efficiency, spontaneous miscarriage, and live-birth rates, alongside documented neurodevelopmental and cardiometabolic trajectories in offspring. Although observational studies link various paternal exposures to impaired semen quality, substantial heterogeneity persists across diverse patient cohorts. Crucially, direct empirical evidence demonstrating that exposure-associated spermatozoal molecular alterations survive post-fertilization reprogramming to cause adverse human phenotypes remains lacking. Postulated mechanistic axes include oxidative stress, systemic inflammation, endocrine disruption, and altered epididymal vesicular signaling, despite incomplete clinical validation. Nevertheless, the 74-90-day window of spermatogenesis and epididymal transit provides an actionable timeline for preconception risk mitigation, rather than a proven "epigenetic reset." We therefore propose an evidence-informed clinical framework delineating guideline-endorsed baseline evaluations and low-risk lifestyle counseling from investigational assays and commercial claims. Importantly, this framework does not assume that paternal exposure-associated sperm epigenetic alterations persist after fertilization, are transmitted across generations, or determine offspring health.

articles.title: Early detection and interception in hepato-pancreatic-biliary cancers: endoscopic imaging, liquid biopsy, and emerging molecular biomarkers.
articles.authors: Aseafan M, Alqayidi A, Dayis S et al.
articles.abstract: Early detection of hepato-pancreatic-biliary cancers requires different strategies because the populations at risk, precursor lesions, and accessible specimens vary by organ. This review examines established endoscopic imaging and tissue-acquisition pathways together with circulating and lesion-derived biomarkers. Inherited or familial pancreatic risk defines the main pancreatic surveillance population; endoscopic ultrasonography and magnetic resonance imaging are complementary, and prospective cohorts show a stage shift but also interval cancers and low-yield surgery. In pancreatic cysts, imaging features and selective tissue or cyst-fluid analysis can refine management, but no fluid marker independently identifies high-grade dysplasia with sufficient certainty. For biliary cancer, surveillance in primary sclerosing cholangitis depends on noninvasive imaging, whereas endoscopic ductal sampling, cholangioscopy-guided biopsy, and selective endoscopic ultrasonography address suspicious strictures; bile methylation and sequencing may increase diagnostic yield when an invasive procedure is already indicated. Endoscopy has a selective role in gallbladder lesions and a direct interception role in histologically confirmed ampullary adenomas. Hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance remains based on ultrasonography with alpha-fetoprotein; cell-free DNA methylation and multi-analyte blood tests are promising but have not replaced guideline-based surveillance. Across organs, case-control accuracy does not establish surveillance utility. Liquid biopsy complements rather than generally replaces histopathological diagnosis. Established adjuncts must be distinguished from investigational assays, including those with prospective diagnostic validation but no demonstrated surveillance utility. Integration requires specimen-specific analytical validation, independent testing in the intended-use population, and evidence of incremental clinical value over standard imaging and endoscopy. Interventional studies must show that this approach reduces late-stage diagnosis without excessive false-positive procedures.

articles.title: Impact of cervical cancer education on knowledge, attitudes and preventive practices among adolescent girls in secondary schools: a scoping review.
articles.authors: Jolayemi KI, Esan DT, Akingbade O et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer remains one of the most preventable yet deadliest cancers affecting women in Africa. Despite global advances in prevention through human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination, screening, and early treatment, Sub-Saharan Africa continues to experience disproportionately high incidence and mortality rates because of limited health infrastructure, inadequate awareness, and delayed diagnosis. Given that adolescence represents a critical window for establishing lifelong health behaviors, school-based cervical cancer education may provide an effective platform for improving knowledge and promoting preventive practices in line with the World Health Organization's (WHO) cervical cancer elimination strategy.
METHODS: This review was conducted in accordance with the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology for scoping reviews and reported following the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. A comprehensive search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, CINAHL, African Journals Online (AJOL), the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar was undertaken for studies published up to 2026. A total of 1,700 records were identified and screened, resulting in the inclusion of 20 eligible studies. Data were extracted, charted, and synthesized using a narrative approach.
RESULTS: Evidence suggests that baseline knowledge of cervical cancer and HPV among adolescent girls in African secondary schools remains generally low to moderate. A consistent knowledge-attitude gap was identified, whereby positive attitudes toward prevention frequently coexisted with limited factual understanding of cervical cancer risk factors, screening, and HPV vaccination. Educational interventions, including peer-led programmes, classroom-based teaching, health campaigns, and multimodal educational strategies, consistently produced significant improvements in knowledge and awareness. However, improvements were less…
CONCLUSION: School-based cervical cancer education represents a feasible and scalable strategy for improving cervical cancer literacy among African adolescents. However, achieving the WHO's cervical cancer elimination targets will require a shift from isolated educational sessions toward sustainable, curriculum-integrated, multilevel interventions involving schools, families, healthcare providers, and policymakers. Future research should prioritize the evaluation of long-term behavioral outcomes, particularly HPV vaccine uptake and participation in cervical cancer screening programmes.

articles.title: Perceptions and Barriers to the Use of Modern Contraceptive Methods and HIV Prevention Among Youth Aged 16-20 in Rural Eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo: A Qualitative Study.
articles.authors: Kazindu TM, Mwene-Batu P
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study explored young people's perceptions of modern contraceptive methods and HIV prevention, alongside the socioeconomic and cultural barriers they encounter three years post-implementation of Comprehensive Sexuality Education (CSE) in rural Eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. Evaluating this curriculum exposes critical implementation gaps.
METHODS: A qualitative cross-sectional study using semi-structured, face-to-face in-depth individual interviews was conducted in January 2025 among 64 students aged 16-20 across four secondary schools (two public, two faith-based) in South Kivu. A purposive stratified sampling strategy enabled intra-sample comparative analysis across genders and institutional models. Transcribed data underwent inductive thematic open coding with double independent coding to ensure inter-rater reliability.
RESULTS: Our findings expose a significant public health paradox. On one hand, an absolute semantic disconnect exists where 100% of interviewed youth were unfamiliar with the term "contraception", coexisting with a low rate of consistent condom use (17.7%) among sexually active participants, despite comprehensive theoretical mastery of HIV transmission pathways. On the other hand, constrained by community taboos and the fear of parental or religious sanctions, these adolescents underutilize formal youth-friendly healthcare channels. Instead, they engage in alternative risk behaviors, specifically the post-coital utilization of high-dose quinine and aspirin (reported by 40.9% of sexually active girls) as makeshift emergency contraceptives, inducing clinical side effects. Conservative religious leaders and parents with low formal education levels constituted the primary socio-cultural barriers, whereas schoolteachers were supportive.
CONCLUSION: Rural youth remain vulnerable to unintended pregnancies and HIV due to community-enforced silence and institutional linguistic barriers. Effective interventions must transcend classroom education to engage religious and parental gatekeepers, de-stigmatize family planning services, and adapt formal medical terminologies to local daily vernacular languages to align theoretical knowledge with behavioral change.

articles.title: Challenges in menopause care: Gaps in healthcare provision and information among women.
articles.authors: Brenk-Franz K, Petersen M, Strauß B
articles.abstract: Menopause is increasingly recognised as a biopsychosocial transition rather than only a reproductive milestone. While physical symptoms such as vasomotor symptoms are well documented, psychological, cognitive, sexual, and social changes also substantially affect women's quality of life. Despite growing scientific evidence, less is known about how women perceive healthcare support during this transition. This short communication presents findings from a cross-sectional survey of 539 women aged 35 years and older. Participants were asked about healthcare experiences, menopausal symptoms (MRS), psychological well-being (WHO-5 Well-Being Index), and hormone replacement therapy (HRT). 47.1% of women reported that menopause had never been proactively addressed by a physician, although 88.4% wished healthcare professionals would initiate discussions. More than half felt inadequately informed about menopausal changes, treatment options, and the benefits and risks of HRT, while almost 45% reported that their symptoms were not taken seriously. Overall satisfaction with medical care was low (27.5%). Multivariable general linear model (GLM) analyses examined predictors of satisfaction with menopause-related healthcare and showed that greater menopausal symptom burden was associated with lower satisfaction. The findings suggest substantial gaps in menopause-related healthcare. A more proactive and patient-centred approach may improve healthcare experiences and outcomes for women undergoing the menopausal transition.

articles.title: Factors influencing parental hesitancy toward HPV vaccination in Sub-Saharan Africa: a scoping review.
articles.authors: Opaleye OO, Esan DT, Esan TO et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prevalence of cervical cancer is highest in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), yet the region's coverage of the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine is still low and varies greatly between and within nations. HPV vaccination targets adolescents, making parental and caregiver consent and decision-making essential to vaccination program success. Parental hesitancy is a major determinant of whether national vaccination programs result in population-level protection, and a range of factors have been identified as drivers of parental reluctance.
OBJECTIVES: This scoping review aims to map and synthesize the evidence on factors influencing parental hesitancy toward HPV vaccination in Sub-Saharan Africa, including individual, household, sociocultural, informational, and health-system determinants, while identifying gaps for future research.
METHODS: An initial multi-database search (PubMed/MEDLINE, SpringerLink, ProQuest and ScienceDirect; May to June 2026) identified 236 records, of which 79 unique records were screened and 36 studies met the eligibility criteria. An updated search with expanded terms was then run in PubMed, ScienceDirect and SpringerLink and a new database, AJOL; (200 records), which added 22 eligible studies, giving 58 studies in total. Hesitancy was defined as delay in acceptance or refusal of vaccination despite service availability; studies of acceptance, willingness, knowledge, attitudes or perceptions were eligible when they also reported determinants of hesitancy. Data were charted and synthesized narratively.
RESULTS: The 58 included studies spanned ten Sub-Saharan African countries namely Nigeria, Cameroon, South Africa, Kenya, Ghana, Ethiopia, Tanzania, Uganda, Malawi, and Zambia, published between 2016 and 2026, and comprised cross-sectional surveys, qualitative studies, mixed-methods studies, a randomized survey experiment, quasi-experimental studies, and programmatic/stakeholder…
CONCLUSION: Parental hesitancy toward HPV vaccination across Sub-Saharan Africa is shaped by overlapping informational, sociocultural, economic, and trust-related factors that vary substantially by country, delivery platform, and rollout maturity. Closing the region's HPV vaccination gap may require country and community-tailored, multicomponent strategies combining trusted-messenger communication, dedicated safety-concern counseling, and continued attention to cost and access barriers, particularly in under-studied countries and rural settings.

articles.title: The ovarian cellular ecosystem in polycystic ovary syndrome: from cellular heterogeneity to clinical relevance.
articles.authors: Ferk P, Leskošek B
articles.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is one of the most biologically heterogeneous disorders in reproductive endocrinology, extending far beyond the classical features of hyperandrogenism, ovulatory dysfunction, and polycystic ovarian morphology. Although substantial progress has been made in defining the endocrine, metabolic, genetic, epigenetic, and inflammatory mechanisms associated with PCOS, these processes have largely been investigated independently, and their contribution to the marked clinical and biological heterogeneity of the disorder remains incompletely understood. Recent advances in cellular-resolution biology, including single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomics, spatial omics, and multimodal molecular profiling, together with computational systems biology, enable increasingly detailed characterization of cellular states, spatial organization, and molecular relationships within the ovarian-follicular environment. In this Review, we use the ovarian cellular ecosystem as an operational systems framework to test whether PCOS-associated abnormalities observed in individual ovarian and follicular compartments form reproducible higher-order patterns of multicellular organization. The framework is organized across five measurable domains: cellular composition and states, intercellular signaling relationships, spatial niche organization, cross-compartment molecular coupling, and systemic-ovarian coupling. Current direct human cellular-resolution evidence remains sparse and compartment-specific. Available studies support altered molecular and cellular states within selected ovarian and follicular compartments more strongly than coordinated, spatially organized, or progressive ecosystem-wide remodeling. We critically evaluate how cellular-resolution, spatial, multi-omics, computational and artificial intelligence approaches can be used to test these ecosystem-level hypotheses, explicitly distinguishing direct measurement from computational inference and identifying the validation required for functional or causal interpretation. Finally, we discuss the translational implications of this framework for biologically informed patient stratification, ecosystem-derived biomarker discovery, mechanism-informed therapeutic development, and precision reproductive endocrinology. By integrating current evidence within a falsifiable framework, this Review defines measurable features and validation criteria for testing ovarian ecosystem organization in PCOS and…

articles.title: Metabolic regulation of oocyte developmental competence: cellular cooperation, developmental transitions, and human evidence.
articles.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
articles.authors: Yang Z, Zhao Y, Miao C et al.
articles.abstract: Oocyte metabolism supports meiotic maturation and prepares the cytoplasm for fertilization and early cleavage. These functions depend on the exchange of substrates with cumulus cells, mitochondrial activity and organization, redox balance, and the use of metabolites in biosynthesis and chromatin regulation. This narrative review examines how these processes contribute to developmental competence, drawing on mammalian perturbation studies and human oocyte, cumulus-cell, follicular-fluid and embryo studies. Animal experiments show that disturbed substrate use or organelle organization can impair development despite meiotic progression or little change in total adenosine triphosphate (ATP) content. They also reveal dose- and stage-dependent responses to metabolic supplementation. Human studies identify related molecular and optical changes, particularly during reproductive aging, but the biological meaning of a measurement depends on the sampled cell, developmental stage and experimental conditions. Direct oocyte profiling, associated follicular samples and embryo measurements therefore address different questions. The Goldilocks concept helps frame the possibility that both insufficient activity and excessive demand can accompany developmental failure; it does not establish a common metabolic threshold for clinical selection. We discuss metabolic interventions as tests of mechanism and distinguish developmental rescue in experimental systems from benefit in vitro fertilization. The central challenge is to determine which metabolic changes contribute to loss of competence and which arise as responses to aging, culture or developmental arrest.

articles.title: The role of oxidative balance in the early diagnosis of oxidative stress-related diseases in infants born to mothers with preeclampsia.
articles.authors: Kutlu Can İ, Tanrıverdi S, Taneli F
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preeclampsia is a major cause of preterm birth and is associated with increased oxidative stress. Alterations in oxidative-antioxidative balance may contribute to oxidative stress-related neonatal diseases in preterm infants born to mothers with preeclampsia.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the oxidative and antioxidative status of preterm infants born to mothers with preeclampsia and investigate associations between oxidative stress biomarkers, particularly advanced oxidation protein products (AOPPs), and neonatal diseases.
METHODS: Thirty preterm infants (<37 weeks' gestation) requiring neonatal intensive care who were born to mothers with preeclampsia were enrolled in the preeclampsia group, and 30 gestational age-matched preterm infants born to normotensive mothers served as controls. Total oxidant status (TOS), total antioxidant status (TAS), 8-hydroxy-2'-deoxyguanosine (8-OHdG), and AOPPs were measured in cord blood and serum samples collected on postnatal days 1, 3, and 7. Biomarker levels were compared between groups, and their associations with respiratory distress syndrome (RDS), bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD), necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC), retinopathy of prematurity (ROP), intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH), and patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) were evaluated.
RESULTS: RDS, NEC, and PDA were significantly more frequent in the preeclampsia group (all p < 0.05). AOPP levels were significantly higher in the preeclampsia group in cord blood and on postnatal days 1, 3, and 7 (all p < 0.001). TAS and 8-OHdG levels did not differ significantly between groups at any time point (p > 0.05). Cord blood TOS levels were significantly higher in the preeclampsia group (p = 0.005), whereas TOS levels on postnatal days 1, 3, and 7 did not differ significantly (p > 0.05). No significant associations were found between serial biomarker levels and RDS, BPD, NEC, ROP, IVH, or PDA (p > 0.05).
CONCLUSION: AOPPs may represent a potential biomarker of oxidative stress in preterm infants born to mothers with preeclampsia. Further prospective studies are needed to determine their role in the early diagnosis of oxidative stress-related neonatal diseases.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence-based models for predicting bronchopulmonary dysplasia in preterm infants: a systematic review.
articles.authors: Avila-Alvarez A, Martínez-González RV, Fernández-González SM
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) is one of the most common chronic respiratory complications in preterm infants. Early identification of high-risk patients is essential for individualizing preventive strategies and optimizing therapeutic decisions. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) models have emerged as promising tools to improve predictive performance in this population.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate and synthesize the predictive performance of AI-based models for BPD development in preterm infants and to assess their methodological quality.
METHODS: A systematic review was conducted following PRISMA recommendations. We searched PubMed, Scopus and Cochrane Library up to February 2026. Studies developing or validating AI-based models for predicting BPD in preterm infants born at <32 weeks of gestation and/or with a birth weight < 1,500 g were included. Methodological quality and risk of bias were assessed using the PROBAST tool.
RESULTS: Eighteen studies were included. Random Forest and XGBoost were the most frequently used algorithms. AUC values for the best-performing models ranged from 0.80 to 1.00, showing improved performance as postnatal variables were incorporated. However, the PROBAST assessment revealed a high overall risk of bias in 72.2% of the studies, primarily due to deficiencies in the analysis domain. Clinical applicability raised high concern in 38.9% of the studies due to a lack of external validation and heterogeneity in outcome definitions.
CONCLUSIONS: AI-based models show high discriminative capacity for BPD prediction; however, they have not yet demonstrated clear superiority over conventional statistical models in robust comparisons. Their routine clinical implementation is currently limited by poor methodological quality and scarce external validation.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261466494, PROSPERO: CRD420261466494, registered retrospectively on August 4, 2026.

articles.title: NOTCH3/JAG1 signaling is associated with immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment features in ovarian cancer: links to nutritional risk, CD163+ macrophages, and CD8+ T cell exclusion.
articles.authors: Zhu H, He Y, Hao R et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: NOTCH3 signaling is frequently dysregulated in ovarian cancer and has been linked to tumor progression and treatment resistance. We investigated the prognostic significance of NOTCH3 expression and its associations with immune-cell infiltration, nutritional risk, tumor-associated biomarkers, and transcriptional programs in public single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 186 patients with epithelial ovarian cancer stratified by immunohistochemistry-assessed NOTCH3 expression (n = 93 per group). Clinicopathological variables, nutritional measures (BMI, serum albumin, and NRS-2002), tumor-associated biomarkers (CA-125 and HE4), immune markers (CD8+, CD4+, CD163+, FOXP3+, and PD-L1), treatment response, and survival were evaluated. Public scRNA-seq datasets were used for complementary exploratory analysis of NOTCH3-associated transcriptional patterns.
RESULTS: NOTCH3-high expression was associated with shorter overall survival, lower CD8+ TIL density, higher CD163+ tumor-associated macrophage density, lower chemotherapy response, and higher platinum resistance. High nutritional risk and hypoalbuminaemia were also associated with an immune-excluded phenotype after adjustment for clinicopathological covariates. The combined NOTCH3-high/NRS-2002 ≥ 3 subgroup had the poorest observed clinical outcomes. In the scRNA-seq analysis, epithelial cells showed the highest NOTCH3-related signature scores, and JAG1 showed the strongest co-expression with NOTCH3 among the evaluated ligands. These findings are associative and do not establish functional ligand-receptor signaling or a causal nutrition-mediated mechanism.
CONCLUSION: High NOTCH3 expression is associated with an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, adverse treatment response, and poorer survival in ovarian cancer. Nutritional risk identifies an additional clinically relevant correlate of immune and survival outcomes. The observational clinical design and exploratory public scRNA-seq analysis do not establish causality; functional validation and prospective studies are required before specific nutritional or NOTCH3-targeted interventions can be recommended.

articles.title: A single-cell atlas of uterosacral ligaments reveals progressive cellular remodeling in pelvic organ prolapse.
articles.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
articles.authors: Liu L, Hao Y, Deng X et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pelvic organ prolapse (POP) is a common disorder of pelvic support tissues, but its cellular basis in the uterosacral ligament (USL) remains poorly defined. Most existing single-cell studies, have failed to characterize stage-specific cellular changes across different POP severities, lacking a stage-resolved perspective across disease severity stages.
METHODS: We profiled USL samples from 10 women with POP (4 moderate, 6 severe) and 4 controls by single-cell RNA sequencing, and analyzed 167,609 high-quality cells using clustering, trajectory inference, differential expression, cell-cell communication, and transcription factor analyses to systematically decode progressive USL cellular alterations.
RESULTS: Ten major cell populations were identified. Fibroblasts, smooth muscle cells (SMCs), and endothelial cells formed the structural core of the USL, while macrophages, neutrophils, mast cells, and T cells showed progressive inflammatory activation with increasing disease severity. Fibroblasts were highly heterogeneous and shifted from progenitor-like and perivascular states toward inflammatory, matrix-remodeling, and myofibroblast-like phenotypes. SMCs moved from a contractile program to stress-responsive and ECM-remodeling states, and endothelial cells underwent functional reprogramming rather than major compositional change. Cell-cell communication between stromal cells declined, whereas fibroblast-immune interactions increased. Collagen-related signaling decreased, while immune-associated ligand-receptor programs became more prominent as disease advanced.
CONCLUSION: Distinct from previous cross-sectional single-cell studies on POP, this work provides a unique stage-resolved transcriptomic landscape covering moderate-to-severe POP stages. POP is marked by coordinated stromal remodeling, immune activation, and disrupted intercellular signaling in the USL. This single-cell transcriptomic atlas provides a refined framework for interpreting stage-specific molecular alterations across graded POP severities and may facilitate the development of targeted therapeutic strategies for pelvic floor dysfunction.

articles.title: Protective effects and mechanisms of polyphenols in animal models of testicular dysfunction: a preclinical systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Ni B, Tang J, Zhou M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Testicular dysfunction is a significant contributor to male infertility, characterized by impaired spermatogenesis, reduced testosterone production, and structural damage to testicular tissue. Polyphenols, a class of naturally occurring plant metabolites abundant in fruits, vegetables, and plant-derived beverages, show considerable promise in ameliorating testicular dysfunction in animal models. Their protective effects are primarily mediated through antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-apoptotic mechanisms, along with the modulation of steroidogenic pathways. This study examines the effects of polyphenols on testicular dysfunction in experimental animal models.
METHODS: A systematic search of six electronic databases (PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, the Web of Science Core Collection, China National Knowledge Infrastructure and Wanfang Data) was performed using keywords related to polyphenols and testicular dysfunction. The analysis incorporated preclinical animal studies evaluating polyphenol interventions for testicular injury. The methodological quality of the included studies was assessed using the CAMARADES checklist. This review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251171737).
RESULTS: A total of 46 studies involving 1,252 animals were included. The meta-analysis demonstrated that polyphenols: 1) Improved sperm parameters, significantly increasing sperm count [SMD = 3.36, 95% CI (1.62, 5.09), P < 0.0001] and progressive sperm motility [SMD = 6.95, 95% CI (4.54, 8.96), P < 0.0001], while reducing sperm abnormality rate [SMD = -5.70, 95% CI (-8.42, -2.97), P < 0.0001]; 2) Enhanced testicular structure, significantly increasing seminiferous tubule diameter [SMD = 3.91, 95% CI (1.46, 6.36), P < 0.01], germinal epithelium height [SMD = 4.70, 95% CI (2.34, 7.06), P < 0.0001], and epididymal weight [SMD = 1.98, 95% CI (0.08, 3.89), P < 0.05]; 3) Elevated serum testosterone concentration [SMD = 2.72, 95% CI (1.93, 3.50), P < 0.0001]; 4) Attenuated oxidative stress, decreasing ROS [SMD = -4.91, 95% CI (-7.10, -2.72), P < 0.0001] and MDA levels [SMD = -4.63, 95% CI (-6.18, -3.09), P < 0.0001], while increasing SOD [SMD = 4.41, 95% CI (2.46, 6.35), P < 0.0001] and GSH [SMD = 4.72, 95% CI (3.02, 6.43), P < 0.0001] activities; 5) Suppressed inflammatory responses, reducing TNF-α [SMD = -4.06, 95% CI (-5.70, -2.42), P < 0.0001],…
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251171737, identifier CRD420251171737.

articles.title: Association and epistasis analyses of obesity-related genes in osteoporosis.
articles.authors: Miranda-Duarte A, Velázquez-Quitl E, Martínez-Ramírez C et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Osteoporosis is a skeletal disease characterized by reduced bone mineral density, increased susceptibility to fracture. Obesity-related genes such as LEP, LEPR, ADIPOQ, and FTO play important roles in osteoporosis and both diseases are linked through metabolic processes. Nevertheless, the risk associated with obesity-related genes in osteoporosis and their gene-gene and gene-environment interactions have not been extensively studied. The objective of this study was to investigate the associations and interactions between single nucleotide variants in the LEP, LEPR, ADIPOQ, and FTO genes, along with body mass index and other participant factors, and their involvement in osteoporosis risk.
METHODS: This case-control study included 365 patients (195 controls and 170 with osteoporosis) who were classified according to WHO criteria based on densitometric measurements of the lumbar spine and femoral neck. Eight single nucleotide variants of LEP, LEPR, ADIPOQ, and FTO genes were genotyped using real-time PCR with TaqMan probes. Association analyses were performed under the codominant, dominant, and recessive inheritance models using unconditional logistic regression. Gene-gene and gene-environment interactions were explored using multifactor dimensionality reduction.
RESULTS: Women with OP were older and had lower body mass index than controls (p = 0.00001 for both) and obesity (BMI ≥ 30 kg/m²) was associated with reduced OP risk (p = 0.0001). Age, age at menarche, hypertension, diabetes, and arthritis increased the risk of osteoporosis, whereas higher BMI and coffee intake were protective factors. No significant associations were found for individual variants in any genetic model. However, two gene-gene interaction models suggest the synergistic contribution of some analyzed SNVs within a multilocus model with OP risk: (1) ADIPOQ rs1501299 and FTO rs9939609; and (2) LEPR rs1805134, ADIPOQ rs1501299, ADIPOQ rs17300539, and FTO rs9939609; nevertheless, there were not significant (p>0.05). A significant gene-environment interaction involving LEP rs2167270, BMI, age at…
CONCLUSION: Our exploratory findings suggest that LEP, LEPR, ADIPOQ, and FTO obesity-related genes may contribute to increased OP risk through complex gene-gene and gene-environment interactions rather than individual effects. These preliminary results provide further hypothesis-generating evidence that OP and obesity share underlying biological connections and metabolic pathways.

articles.title: Cost-effectiveness analysis of HRD testing for patients with advanced ovarian cancer in Italy: an update.
articles.authors: Rognoni C, Lorusso D, Costa F et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Ovarian cancer (OC) is the eighth most common cancer among women, with homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) present in about 50% of cases. In this subgroup, poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibitors show greater therapeutic benefit. This study aimed to update a cost-effectiveness analysis comparing upfront HRD testing with BRCA-only testing (BReast CAncer gene), which identifies mutations in roughly 25% of patients, to inform and optimize treatment strategies in Italy.
METHODS: A previously developed cost-effectiveness model was updated to incorporate new clinical evidence and cost data for PARP inhibitors (niraparib, rucaparib). The model projected costs and outcomes - life-years (LYs) and quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs) - over a lifetime horizon, comparing immediate HRD testing with BRCA testing alone or with sequential HRD testing after a negative BRCA result. Analyses were conducted from the Italian National Healthcare Service (NHS) perspective. Deterministic and probabilistic sensitivity analyses, together with scenario and threshold analyses, assessed the robustness of model results.
RESULTS: Upfront HRD testing remained cost-effective versus BRCA-only testing, with an incremental cost-utility ratio of 22,476€/QALY, and was cost-saving compared with sequential testing. Probabilistic sensitivity analysis showed that HRD testing was cost-effective in 99.3% of simulations considering a 50,000€/QALY willingness-to-pay threshold. Findings were robust across most scenarios, however cost-effectiveness was reversed with a 10-year time horizon, an HRD-positive/BRCA-negative prevalence in the range 3.95%-4.99%, or substantial acquisition cost increases for olaparib or rucaparib.
DISCUSSION: Although identifying genetic alterations in advanced OC incurs significant costs, upfront HRD testing is a cost-effective strategy compared with BRCA-only testing when considering all currently available treatment options. It enables more efficient allocation of healthcare resources while improving life expectancy and quality of life for women with advanced ovarian cancer.

articles.title: Association of integrated nutritional guidance and mindfulness-based stress reduction with fertility outcomes in women with polycystic ovary syndrome.
articles.authors: Qi J, Zhu M, Zou X
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association of an integrated nutritional guidance and mindfulness-based stress reduction (MBSR) program with fertility outcomes, metabolic parameters, and psychological well-being in women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS).
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study analyzed medical records of 326 women with PCOS who received fertility care between January 2023 and December 2024. Women were classified as integrated care (n=163) or conventional care (n=163) according to the clinical pathway received. The primary outcomes were clinical pregnancy and the proportion of women achieving at least one confirmed ovulation. Propensity-score matching (PSM) was performed to address measured treatment-selection differences, and missing psychological outcomes were handled using multiple imputation.
RESULTS: Clinical pregnancy was observed in 35.0% (57/163) of the integrated-care group and 19.6% (32/163) of the conventional-care group (OR = 2.20, 95% CI 1.33-3.64, p=0.002), while 72.4% versus 58.3% achieved at least one confirmed ovulation (OR = 1.88, 95% CI 1.18-2.98, p=0.007). After 1:1 PSM (145 matched pairs), the associations remained for clinical pregnancy (33.8% vs. 21.4%; matched OR = 1.90, 95% CI 1.11-3.27, exact McNemar p=0.025) and confirmed ovulation (71.7% vs. 60.0%; matched OR = 1.77, 95% CI 1.05-2.99, exact McNemar p=0.040). Model-estimated changes also favored integrated care for body weight (-2.7 kg, 95% CI -3.5 to -1.9), HOMA-IR (ratio of relative changes 0.70, 95% CI 0.62-0.79), total testosterone (-0.2 nmol/L, 95% CI -0.3 to -0.1), GAD-7 (-1.51, 95% CI -2.30 to -0.72), and PHQ-9 (-1.03, 95% CI -1.74 to -0.32).
