CONCLUSIONS: Receipt of integrated nutritional guidance and MBSR was associated with higher clinical pregnancy and confirmed-ovulation proportions and with more favorable metabolic and psychological changes than conventional care. Because treatment allocation was non-randomized, these findings should be interpreted as associations and require prospective confirmation.

articles.title: Serous Ovarian Carcinoma Presenting With Synchronous Breast Metastasis: A Case Report and Literature Review.
articles.authors: Omranipour R, Nozheh A, Esmaeilian S et al.
articles.abstract: Synchronous breast metastasis from ovarian cancer is exceptionally rare. A 53-year-old woman with FIGO IIIC high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma underwent cytoreductive surgery, chemotherapy, and breast radiotherapy. Immunohistochemistry confirmed metastatic disease. Complete response persisted for over 7 years before platinum-resistant recurrence, emphasizing accurate diagnosis and multimodal treatment in selected patients.

articles.title: First-trimester maternal exposures and offspring congenital heart defects: a Hungarian population-based case-control study, 1980-2009.
articles.authors: Suo Z, Váradi A, Hegyi P et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Congenital heart defects (CHDs) are a major cause of infant morbidity and mortality. Identifying modifiable maternal exposures during early pregnancy is important for CHD prevention and maternal and child health.
OBJECTIVES: To examine associations between first-trimester maternal active smoking and alcohol consumption and offspring CHDs, and to explore associations of selected maternal diseases and related treatments with CHD outcomes.
METHODS: This population-based case-control study used data from the Hungarian Case-Control Surveillance of Congenital Abnormalities (1980-2009), including 7,362 CHD cases and 56,894 controls. Overall CHDs were the primary outcome, with ventricular septal defect (VSD) and atrial septal defect (ASD) examined as secondary outcomes. Complete-case multivariable logistic regression estimated odds ratios (ORs) for smoking and alcohol consumption, with mutual adjustment and additional adjustment for maternal age, socioeconomic status, and offspring sex. Multiple imputation was performed as a sensitivity analysis. Maternal disease and treatment analyses were crude and exploratory.
RESULTS: First-trimester maternal smoking was associated with higher odds of overall CHDs (adjusted OR 1.50, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.30-1.71), VSD (1.36, 1.11-1.66) and ASD (1.62, 1.35-1.93). Multiple-imputation estimates were similar to the complete-case estimates. No statistically significant associations were observed between maternal alcohol consumption and CHD outcomes in either the adjusted complete-case analysis or the multiple-imputation analysis. Maternal epilepsy, migraine, anxiety disorder and anemia showed positive crude associations with one or more CHD outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Maternal smoking reported during the first trimester was associated with higher odds of overall CHDs, VSD, and ASD, supporting smoking cessation before conception and during pregnancy as a prevention priority. Exploratory associations involving maternal diseases and treatments require further investigation and should not be used to infer treatment effects or guide treatment decisions.

articles.title: Development and internal validation of prediction models for maternal adverse pregnancy outcomes in HELLP syndrome: a retrospective cohort study in China.
articles.authors: Lu Y, Huang X, Lin X et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: HELLP syndrome is uncommon but can cause serious maternal adverse pregnancy outcomes (APOs). We investigated whether routinely available clinical and laboratory variables could support outcome-specific risk prediction.
METHODS: We included all women with HELLP syndrome treated at Fujian Maternity and Child Health Hospital from January 2013 to June 2023. Five outcomes were modeled: placental abruption (PAB), posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES), postpartum hemorrhage (PPH), disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), and a severe maternal composite outcome. The primary analysis used repeated nested cross-validation in the full cohort. Missing-data filtering and imputation, predictor screening, model-family selection, hyperparameter tuning, and threshold estimation were performed within each outer training fold so that the held-out fold evaluated the entire modeling process. Candidate families were ridge logistic regression, elastic-net logistic regression, and random forest. A paired sensitivity analysis using multiple imputation by chained equations (MICE) was conducted to assess the effect of replacing mean/mode imputation.
RESULTS: Among 272 women, PAB occurred in 33 (12.13%), PRES in 23 (8.46%), PPH in 19 (6.99%), DIC in 9 (3.31%), and the severe composite outcome in 25 (9.19%). The corresponding AUCs were 0.715, 0.677, 0.833, 0.907, and 0.742. Ridge logistic regression was selected in 62%, 74%, 56%, and 62% of the outer folds for PAB, PRES, PPH, and the severe composite outcome, respectively. For DIC, the single-predictor logistic regression fallback was selected in 85% of the outer folds. In the paired analysis, MICE changed AUC by -0.002 to 0.009 and AUPRC by -0.005 to 0.002. PAB, PRES, and PPH did not meet the prespecified analysis criteria. DIC and the composite outcome met these criteria, although both estimates were limited by sparse events and the lack of external validation.
CONCLUSIONS: Although performance was not uniformly strong and external validation is still needed, routinely available data showed potential for early risk stratification. In particular, the severe composite outcome provided a clinically meaningful way to combine individually rare but serious complications and may help identify women who warrant closer surveillance.

articles.title: Comparative efficacy and safety of nonhormonal prescription drugs for vasomotor symptoms in women with breast cancer: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Liao YS, Deng YP, Song JL et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vasomotor symptoms (VMS) are common during and after breast cancer treatment, particularly among women receiving endocrine therapy. We compared the efficacy, acceptability, and safety of nonhormonal prescription pharmacological interventions for VMS in women with breast cancer or breast cancer survivors.
METHODS: We searched major databases and trial registries through July 2026 for randomized controlled trials comparing nonhormonal prescription drugs versus placebo or another eligible nonhormonal prescription drug in adult women with breast cancer-related VMS. The primary outcome was continuous VMS efficacy. Secondary outcomes included responder outcomes, all-cause discontinuation, discontinuation due to adverse events, any adverse events, and serious adverse events. We performed frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis, with Bayesian network meta-analysis as sensitivity analysis. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2, and certainty of evidence using a GRADE/NMA-GRADE approach.
RESULTS: Eighteen publications, corresponding to 19 study/substudy records and 2,224 randomized or allocated participants, were included. Five interventions were significantly more effective than placebo: escitalopram (SMD -1.08, 95% CI -1.80 to -0.37), desvenlafaxine 50 mg (SMD -0.87, 95% CI -1.60 to -0.15), desvenlafaxine 100 mg (SMD -0.80, 95% CI -1.44 to -0.15), elinzanetant (SMD -0.51, 95% CI -0.95 to -0.07), and venlafaxine 75 mg (SMD -0.42, 95% CI -0.76 to -0.07). Heterogeneity was moderate (I2 = 44.9%), with no significant global or local inconsistency. Frequentist P-scores ranked the five significant drugs top, confirmed by Bayesian sensitivity. Elinzanetant had high-certainty evidence, whereas venlafaxine 75 mg and gabapentin 900 mg had moderate-certainty evidence. Escitalopram and desvenlafaxine had large effects, but the supporting evidence was sparse. Discontinuation outcomes showed no statistically significant differences versus placebo, but sparse safety networks precluded a reliable comparative safety hierarchy; these null findings should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalent tolerability.
CONCLUSION: Nonhormonal prescription drugs are not interchangeable for breast cancer-related VMS. Elinzanetant provides the strongest high-certainty evidence among newer targeted options, and venlafaxine 75 mg is the best-supported…
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261460108, identifier CRD420261460108.

articles.title: The estrogen-ECM-integrin- cytoskeleton axis in pelvic organ prolapse: a mechanobiological framework linking matrix remodeling to repair failure.
articles.authors: Yang X, Chen L, Wang X et al.
articles.abstract: Pelvic organ prolapse (POP) is a common disorder of pelvic support, but its estimated prevalence depends strongly on ascertainment. A 2024 meta-analysis reported a pooled prevalence of 30.9%, increasing to 41.8% in examination-based studies. Altered collagen turnover and estrogen-responsive tissue remodeling are important features of POP, yet they do not fully explain how extracellular-matrix (ECM) abnormalities may become persistent defects in cellular force transmission and repair. This narrative Review develops an evidence-graded estrogen-ECM-integrin-cytoskeleton axis, organized around ECM mechanics and fibroblast mechanosensing. We distinguish ERα-, ERβ- and GPER-mediated signaling; indirect hormonal effects on the matrix presented to integrins; and the more limited evidence for direct hormonal control of integrin signaling in human POP. We examine LOX/LOXL-dependent matrix maturation while separating expression, catalytic activity and mature cross-link measurements. The integrin-talin-vinculin molecular clutch provides a candidate connection between abnormal matrix resistance, FAK/Src-RhoA/ROCK signaling, cytoskeletal function and YAP/TAZ-dependent transcription. However, POP-associated mechanics vary with tissue compartment, measurement scale and disease state. Reduced counter-resistance and clutch slippage therefore represent a testable scenario, not a universal disease sequence. We identify experiments that could distinguish matrix-mediated effects from intrinsic fibroblast dysfunction and connect these questions to biomaterial design, controlled loading and local pathway modulation. Clinical estrogen therapy and experimental mechanopharmacology must remain distinct: improved local tissue quality does not establish prevention of prolapse recurrence, and no YAP/TAZ-targeted drug is approved for POP.

articles.title: Acupuncture before and during letrozole ovulation induction in women with overweight or obesity and PCOS-related infertility: a randomized sham-controlled pilot trial.
articles.authors: Dou Z, Zhang Y, Hao J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity-related metabolic dysfunction may impair fertility outcomes in women with overweight or obesity and polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). We evaluated acupuncture initiated 3 months before letrozole ovulation induction and continued during treatment.
METHODS: In this single-center, randomized, participant-blinded, sham-controlled pilot trial, 60 women aged 20-35 years with a body mass index ≥25 kg/m² were assigned 1:1 to acupuncture or nonpenetrating sham acupuncture. Both groups received lifestyle guidance. Interventions were administered during the 3-month pretreatment phase and up to three letrozole cycles. The primary outcomes were continuing pregnancy and live birth. Secondary outcomes included other reproductive, anthropometric, metabolic, endometrial, and uterine artery Doppler outcomes.
RESULTS: A total of 60 women were randomized, 55 completed follow-up and were included in the per-protocol analysis, while all 60 were included in the intention-to-treat analyses of pregnancy outcomes. In the per-protocol analysis, the live-birth rate was significantly higher in the acupuncture group than in the sham acupuncture group (14/27 [51.9%] vs. 6/28 [21.4%]; P = 0.03). The continuing-pregnancy rates were 14/27 (51.9%) and 8/28 (28.6%), respectively (P = 0.10). The biochemical-pregnancy rate was also higher in the acupuncture group (17/27 [63.0%] vs. 9/28 [32.1%]; P = 0.03), whereas clinical pregnancy and pregnancy loss did not differ significantly between the groups. The intention-to-treat analyses showed similar effect directions, although the differences were not statistically significant for live birth (46.7% vs. 20.0%; P = 0.054) or continuing pregnancy (46.7% vs. 26.7%; P = 0.18). Cycle-level ovulation was summarized descriptively. Acupuncture was associated with greater improvements in body weight, glucose and lipid metabolism, insulin resistance, leptin, and adiponectin and with more favorable endometrial thickness and morphology and uterine artery Doppler indices (all P < 0.05). No serious adverse events occurred.
CONCLUSION: These preliminary findings suggest that continuous acupuncture spanning pretreatment and ovulation induction may be associated with a higher live-birth rate and improvements in metabolic and endometrial parameters. Given the exploratory nature and limited sample size of this pilot trial, confirmation in larger multicenter…
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://www.chictr.org.cn/, identifier ChiCTR2200062010.

articles.title: Hormonal contraceptive users exhibit increased approach responses to higher reward in an online approach-avoidance task.
articles.authors: Knihs de Camargo C, Vegelius J, Björkstrand J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hormonal contraceptives (HOC) are used worldwide; however, there are controversies regarding their effects on mental health with studies reporting HOC to be associated with mood symptoms, especially depression and anxiety. Costly avoidance, i.e., avoiding a potentially rewarding situation to minimize anticipated emotional distress, is thought to be a key component of affective disorders. This study aims to explore the relationship between the use of hormonal contraceptives, symptoms of depression and anxiety, and costly avoidance.
METHODS: Self-reported users of HOC (n = 139) and non-users (n = 209) completed the Inventory of Depression and Anxiety Symptoms (IDAS-II) and partook in an online approach-avoidance conflict task assessing costly avoidance. Statistical analyses included generalized mixed effects models, t-tests and Mann-Whitney U tests.
RESULTS: HOC users showed increased odds of approach behavior in the highest reward level. No direct associations were found between approach behavior and depression and anxiety symptoms. Upon further post-hoc analysis, HOC use did not moderate any association between approach behavior and affective symptoms.
CONCLUSIONS: In line with previous literature, HOC users showed less avoidant behavior than non-users. Results should be interpreted with caution, as the observational nature of the study opens up to self-selection bias. However, this represents an important first observation that warrants further longitudinal and/or placebo-controlled studies.

articles.title: Cell-free DNA in human ovarian follicular fluid as a potential biomarker of embryo quality in IVF cycles: a pilot study.
articles.authors: Jo EH, Kim TH, Eum JH et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: There is growing interest in evaluating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) in follicular fluid (FF) as a molecular feature of the follicular microenvironment and examining its association with subsequent embryo development. This exploratory pilot study aimed to investigate the association between FF cfDNA integrity, measured by the Arthrobacter luteus (ALU) 247/115 ratio, and morphology-based embryo quality in IVF cycles.
METHODS: This observational study analyzed 106 follicular fluid samples from patients undergoing IVF with intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) at a single fertility center. FF samples were collected during ovum pick-up, and cfDNA concentrations were quantified using ALU-quantitative PCR. To evaluate the ALU247/115 ratio in relation to age, participants were categorized into three age groups.
RESULTS: The ALU247/115 ratio showed a significant but weak positive correlation with embryo quality score across all patients (n = 106, r = 0.23, p = 0.016). Subgroup analysis revealed stronger correlations in women under 35 years (n = 31, r = 0.38, p = 0.035) and those aged 35-39 years (n =40, r = 0.32, p = 0.044). No significant correlation was observed in women aged 40 or older (n = 35, r = 0.21, p = 0.225).
CONCLUSIONS: In women under 40, increased cfDNA fragmentation in FF was associated with lower morphology-based embryo quality. However, the observed correlations were modest, and the absence of preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A), implantation, clinical pregnancy, and live birth outcomes limits clinical interpretation. These exploratory findings do not establish FF cfDNA as a clinically validated predictive biomarker or demonstrate that it improves embryo selection. Larger prospective studies incorporating embryo ploidy and clinically relevant reproductive outcomes are warranted.

articles.title: Adverse pregnancy outcomes and associated maternal and infection-related factors in a rural malaria-endemic setting in Western Kenya.
articles.authors: Kituyi SN, Odongo AO, Wachuka R et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Maternal health during pregnancy is critical for favorable birth outcomes and long-term wellbeing of both mothers and infants. Women in rural, malaria-endemic regions face unique biological and socioeconomic challenges that may increase the risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes (APOs). This study investigated the proportions and determinants of APOs among pregnant women attending antenatal care at Webuye sub-County Hospital in Western Kenya, a rural malaria-endemic setting.
METHODS: A secondary data analysis was conducted utilizing previously collected data of 302 women enrolled at different gestational ages and followed through delivery in a prospective cohort study. Maternal demographic, clinical, and infection-related factors were assessed, and associations with APOs were evaluated using chi-square tests and multivariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: Maternal age and gestational age at enrollment were significantly associated with malaria history (P-value <0.001). Maternal anemia (9.9%), abortion (6.3%), preterm birth (4.4%), miscarriage (1.7%), low birth weight (3.4%), stillbirth (7.6 per 1,000 births), neonatal death (3.8 per 1,000 live births) occurred at varying frequencies, indicating a range of adverse outcomes in the study cohort. Younger mothers (<20 years) and older mothers (>35 years) had a higher proportion of anemia (P-value = 0.026) than those aged 21-35 years, and reported malaria history was significantly associated with maternal anemia at enrolment (p-value = 0.02). An additional analysis using microscopy-confirmed malaria status showed a similar difference in hemoglobin levels between microscopy-positive and microscopy-negative participants (p-value < .001). Abnormal urinalysis findings suggestive of urinary tract infection were significantly associated with low birth weight (p-value = 0.031). No significant associations were found…
DISCUSSION: These findings describe the proportions of the occurrence of adverse outcomes in this rural population and identify maternal age, malaria exposure and abnormal urinalysis results as factors associated with selected outcomes. Strengthening malaria prevention, urinary infection screening, and encouraging early antenatal care attendance are critical to improving maternal and neonatal outcomes. Targeted interventions for adolescent and older mothers, along with enhanced point-of-care diagnostics, may reduce preventable complications in similar resource-limited, malaria-endemic settings.

articles.title: Preterm birth and its associated factors: a registry-based study in Eastern Iran.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology : the journal of the Institute of Obstetrics and Gynaecology
articles.authors: Khosravi Z, Sadeghi M, Sahebi M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preterm birth (PTB), defined as delivery before 37 completed weeks of gestation, continues to pose a significant public health challenge worldwide. This study was conducted to assess the prevalence and associated risk factors of PTB among women receiving prenatal care in eastern Iranian cities.
METHODS: This registry-based, population-level study analysed 273,060 births recorded between 2019 and 2023 in the SINA electronic health system affiliated with Mashhad University of Medical Sciences. The primary outcome was PTB. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was conducted to assess associations between PTB and maternal, foetal, and environmental determinants.
RESULTS: The overall prevalence of PTB was 6.45%. Factors significantly associated with increased odds of PTB included a history of PTB (OR = 3.11, CI:2.88-3.36, p < 0.001), exposure to domestic violence during pregnancy (OR = 2.37, CI:1.64-3.41, p < 0.001), preeclampsia (OR = 2.06, CI: 1.76-2.40, p < 0.001), placenta previa (OR = 1.61, CI: 1.06-2.43, p = 0.02), gestational diabetes (OR = 1.29, CI:1.21-1.38, p < 0.001), COVID-19 infection during pregnancy (OR = 1.10, CI:1.00-1.22, p = 0.04), urinary tract infection (OR = 1.14, CI:1.07-1.22, p < 0.001), inadequate gestational weight gain (OR = 1.17, CI: 1.13-1.22, p < 0.001), and suboptimal nutritional patterns (OR = 1.07, CI:1.00-1.15, p = 0.03). Conversely, consanguineous marriage (OR = 0.84, CI: 0.76-0.92, p < 0.001) and residence in urban or suburban areas (OR = 0.89, CI: 0.85-0.94, p < 0.001 and 0.94, CI: 0.90-0.99, p = 0.03, respectively) were associated with a decrease in PTB odds. Male sex of the neonate was also linked to increased risk of PTB (OR = 1.06, CI:1.02-1.11, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: PTB in eastern Iran is influenced by a complex interplay of medical, socio-economic, and environmental factors. Targeted interventions should prioritise screening for domestic violence, optimising maternal nutrition, and managing pre-existing maternal conditions. These findings highlight the necessity of comprehensive maternal health strategies to mitigate the burden of PTB.

articles.title: Anti-ZIKV IgG Subclass Profiles and Anti-DENV IgG Are Associated With Neonatal Outcomes Following ZIKV Infection During Pregnancy.
articles.authors: Antonelli ACB, Peres GBM, Ferreira GHC et al.
articles.abstract: Zika virus (ZIKV) is a flavivirus transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes. Most infected individuals present mild symptoms; however, vertical transmission of ZIKV can lead to Congenital Zika Syndrome (CZS), which includes microcephaly, neurological, hearing, ophthalmological, and morphological abnormalities. Given the high prevalence of dengue virus (DENV) exposure and antibody cross-reactivity among flaviviruses, understanding how maternal humoral antibody profiles relate to neonatal outcomes after ZIKV infection is important. In this exploratory study, we evaluated maternal and neonatal anti-ZIKV total IgG, anti-ZIKV IgG1 and anti-ZIKV IgG3, and anti-DENV IgG reactivity in relation to maternal-neonatal antibody patterns and neonatal outcomes. Samples from pregnant women and their newborns were collected in Brazil, including pregnancies with microcephaly and other clinical or imaging abnormalities. Anti-ZIKV and anti-DENV IgG reactivity was measured by ELISA. Lower neonatal anti-ZIKV IgG3 reactivity was observed in pregnancies with ophthalmological abnormalities in the individual comparison, although this association did not remain significant after false discovery rate adjustment. Lower neonatal anti-DENV IgG reactivity was observed in pregnancies with ophthalmological abnormalities and with any clinical or imaging abnormality, and both associations remained significant after false discovery rate adjustment. These exploratory associations are hypothesis-generating and do not establish functional protection or a causal role for the measured antibody profiles.

articles.title: Pregnancy Risk Information Systems for Psychotropic Medications: A Practical Review for Clinical Decision-Making.
articles.authors: Kim JH, Kim SH
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This review aimed to summarize pregnancy risk information systems for psychotropic medications and recent evidence on reproductive safety, with the goal of improving clinicians' awareness of drug-specific risk information relevant to individualized clinical decision- making in women with psychiatric disorders of reproductive age.
METHODS: We narratively reviewed official reproductive safety information resources from Australia, Europe, Korea, the United Kingdom, and the United States, together with recent umbrella-review evidence on psychotropic medication safety during pregnancy. Information on selected agents was organized by drug class.
RESULTS: National systems differed in structure and clinical utility. Australia and Korea retain category-based elements, whereas sources from Europe, the United Kingdom, and the United States provide more descriptive, context-based information. Antipsychotics were mainly associated with neonatal extrapyramidal or withdrawal symptoms and metabolic risk signals for selected agents. Mood stabilizers and anticonvulsants were more strongly associated with congenital malformations and neurodevelopmental disorders. Benzodiazepines and hypnotics were mainly associated with neonatal sedation, respiratory depression, hypotonia, feeding difficulties, and withdrawal symptoms after late-pregnancy or labor exposure. Antidepressants were associated with neonatal adaptation symptoms, persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn, and postpartum hemorrhage. Recent umbrella-review evidence showed that most reported associations remained at suggestive or weak levels of evidence.
CONCLUSION: Psychotropic medication use during pregnancy should be guided by individualized risk-benefit assessment, integrating drug-specific safety signals, evidence quality, exposure timing, lactation and fertility considerations, and the risks of untreated psychiatric illness.

articles.title: The strategic integration of emergency obstetric and neonatal care with contraceptive services.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Koch M, Kasliwal A, Ahsan A et al.
articles.abstract: Comprehensive Emergency Obstetric and Neonatal Care (CEmONC) indicators have strengthened health systems' capacity to manage acute obstetric emergencies and remain central to global maternal health monitoring. However, current EmONC frameworks omit contraception, despite its established role in preventing unintended pregnancy, supporting healthy interpregnancy intervals, and reducing recurrent exposure to obstetric risk. This gap reflects an artificial divide between emergency response and preventive care. This commentary argues that contraception should be recognized as an essential, integrated component of EmONC rather than a separate postpartum service. We outline the clinical rationale for embedding contraceptive counseling and provision within each EmONC signal function, noting that the nature of an obstetric emergency-hemorrhage, infection, hypertensive disease-often directly informs contraceptive eligibility and method selection. We further describe why the postpartum period after an obstetric emergency represents a critical, frequently missed opportunity for contraceptive counseling, particularly in low-resource and humanitarian settings where subsequent access to care is uncertain. We propose practical strategies for integration at the facility, health system, and global levels, including standardized counseling prompts, aligned supply chains, updated training curricula, and incorporation of contraceptive indicators into EmONC guidance and monitoring tools. Embedding contraception within EmONC would strengthen continuity across the maternal health continuum and better align global frameworks with the clinical realities of obstetric risk.

articles.title: Targeted next-generation sequencing-based mutational signature analysis in endometrial cancer: utility and limitations across molecular subtypes.
articles.journal: Journal of pathology and translational medicine
articles.authors: Kim U, Lee A, Lee KH et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Molecular subtype classification is essential for staging endometrial cancer, planning adjuvant treatments, and stratifying prognosis. However, the correlation between mutational signature analysis using tumor-only targeted next-generation sequencing (NGS) data and molecular subtypes, as well as the interpretive value at the individual case level, remains inadequately characterized.
METHODS: We performed mutational signature analysis on tumor-only targeted NGS data from 72 endometrial cancer cases using the SATS R package. Molecular classification into four subtypes (POLE-mutated, mismatch repair deficient [MMRd], TP53-mutant, and no specific molecular profile [NSMP]) was established through a standard stepwise algorithm that integrated NGS and immunohistochemistry.
RESULTS: Out of the 72 endometrial cancers, 12 were classified as POLE-mutated, 10 as MMRd, six as TP53-mutant, and 44 as NSMP. All POLE-mutated tumors exhibited POLE-associated signatures (SBS10a/SBS10b), including cases with non-hotspot POLE exonuclease variants and tumor mutation burdens below the conventional ultramutation threshold. MMRd-associated signatures showed a broader distribution across molecular subtypes; while the summed MMRd-associated signatures were typically higher in MMRd tumors, low-level contributions were also noted in subsets of NSMP and TP53-mutant tumors. Within the POLE-mutated group, MMRd-associated signatures were more pronounced in cases displaying subclonal MMR protein loss as determined by immunohistochemistry.
CONCLUSIONS: In this small, clinically selected cohort, targeted NGS-based mutational signatures provided exploratory, complementary information regarding POLE-associated mutagenesis and mixed MMR-related patterns. Overlapping signature distributions, dependence on the analytical pipeline, and the use of tumor-only targeted sequencing limit case-level interpretation. Mutational signature analysis should be interpreted in conjunction with established molecular tests and should not be used as a stand-alone classifier.

articles.title: Examining Implementation Barriers Among Community Champions Towards Improving Maternal and Child Health Outcomes Under the Uturo Model in Mbeya Region, Tanzania.
articles.journal: Health expectations : an international journal of public participation in health care and health policy
articles.authors: Mpambije CJ, Manyerere DJ, Myeya HE
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 3.1 targets reducing the maternal mortality ratio to 70 per 100,000 live births by 2030. Developing countries have intensified diverse strategies to realise the target. Community mobilisation to improve maternal and child health (MCH) is part of these strategies. In Tanzania, diverse community-based initiatives have been introduced, including the Uturo model, introduced in Mbeya region in 2000 and implemented by community champions. While the model has recorded impressive MCH outcomes, the barriers community champions face during implementation remain underexplored. This study therefore aims to highlight the barriers community champions encounter when implementing the Uturo model in Tanzania.
METHODS: This study used a qualitative case study design to explore the barriers community champions encountered while implementing the Uturo model. The study used purposive sampling to select 81 participants. Primary data were collected through individual interviews and focus group discussions with leaders, community health workers, local leaders, healthcare workers, and the council health management team. A document review complemented these tools, and the data were subjected to thematic analysis.
FINDINGS: The findings revealed that community champions played a significant role in improving MCH under the Uturo model since its inception in 2000. However, champions face several barriers that threaten the model's effective performance, including a lack of incentives, impassable roads, insufficient training, and limited professionalism. The potential of community champions to deliver quality MCH services is further limited by political interference and entrenched cultural practices, coupled with shortages of healthcare workers.
CONCLUSION: The success of the Uturo model hinges on motivated and dedicated community champions as frontline facilitators of MCH service delivery. However, structural, community, and health system hurdles undermine their potential to improve MCH services. Moreover, these barriers affect their performance and threaten the model's sustainability and scalability. To advance progress towards SDG 3.1 by 2030, Tanzania should formally recognise and support community champions through appropriate financial and non-financial incentives, such as stipends or allowances, transport facilitation, and regular…
PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: Individuals with lived experiences analysed and interpreted data.

articles.title: A Gap on Judgment of Fertility and the Need for Contraception Between Physicians and Patients With Rheumatic Diseases: A Multicenter Questionnaire Survey.
articles.authors: Moriyama M, Murakawa Y, Nagafuchi H et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Effective contraception is essential for women of reproductive age with rheumatic disease (RD), specifically those receiving teratogenic drugs, and physicians should recognize that these women may wish to conceive or control their fertility. This study aimed to evaluate the status of preconception care and contraception use, awareness, and counseling among women with RD in Japan.
METHODS: This cross-sectional questionnaire survey included Japanese women with RD (age: 18-45 years) and their attending physicians, conducted between September 2023 and May 2024 at 14 medical institutions. Patient and physician responses were linked and analyzed.
RESULTS: In total, 157 patients completed the survey. Of these, 35% of patients wished to conceive in the future and 38% were aware of their current need for contraception. The results revealed a gap between physicians' and patients' judgment of fertility and the need for contraception. Most patients used less effective contraceptive methods (condoms: 67.1%; withdrawal: 20.5%). Although patients were aware of the need for contraception, only 12% had received specific contraception instructions from their healthcare providers, whereas 39% had never received contraception counseling. Most of the patients decided on contraceptive methods themselves or together with their partners. One patient who tested positive for antiphospholipid antibodies used contraindicated estrogen-containing contraceptives.
CONCLUSION: Significant deficiencies exist in contraception counseling and awareness among women with RD. Proactive and system-building approaches are urgently required to improve preconception care and reproductive safety in this population.

articles.title: Socioeconomic and healthcare-related factors associated with cervical cytology uptake among women in Poland: a cross-sectional web-based study.
articles.journal: European journal of cancer prevention : the official journal of the European Cancer Prevention Organisation (ECP)
articles.authors: Pacholczak-Madej R, Zimny-Zając A, Kowalska-Bobko I et al.
articles.abstract: Cervical cancer screening participation is socially patterned. We assessed sociodemographic and healthcare-related factors associated with recent versus non-recent or absent self-reported cervical cytology among women in Poland. We pooled six annual editions of the National Health Test of Poles, an anonymous, voluntary web-based survey (2020-2025), including adult women reporting cytology history. Recent cytology was defined as testing within the preceding 24 months, whereas non-recent or absent cytology encompassed testing more than 24 months previously or no previous testing. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression models were used to identify associated factors. Among 744 621 women, 61.8% reported recent cytology and 38.2% reported non-recent or absent cytology. In multivariable analysis, no specialist visit and student or nonworking status showed the strongest associations with non-recent or absent cytology, with adjusted odds ratios (aOR) of 4.24 [95% confidence interval (CI) = 4.08-4.41] and 3.76 (95% CI = 3.63-3.90), respectively. Higher odds were also observed among retired or disabled women (aOR = 1.76, 95% CI = 1.72-1.80) and those without a recent general practitioner visit (aOR = 1.70, 95% CI = 1.56-1.85). Lower odds were associated with marriage (aOR = 0.44, 95% CI = 0.43-0.45), higher education (aOR = 0.59, 95% CI = 0.57-0.61), and a personal history of cancer (aOR = 0.77, 95% CI = 0.76-0.79). Non-recent or absent cytology was associated with socioeconomic disadvantage and limited healthcare contact. Improving access to cervical cancer prevention may require proactive recommendations, accessible referral pathways, and targeted support for women facing informational or practical barriers.

articles.title: Genetic Counseling When One Partner Carries a CF-Causing Variant and the Other Has the Intronic IVS8-5T Variant.
articles.authors: Massie J, Archibald AD, Smith M et al.
articles.abstract: Complex genetic counseling situations can arise when whole-gene sequencing is used as part of reproductive genetic carrier screening or newborn screening for cystic fibrosis (CF). One of the most common scenarios is when one reproductive partner carries a CF-causing variant such as c.1521-1523del (or p.F508del) and the other partner carries the c.1210-12T[5] (or IVS8-5T) variant. Questions arise as to what information to provide about the likely outcome if the fetus or newborn has both variants in trans, as well as implications for future pregnancies and other family members. In this paper, we consider an approach to genetic counseling based on knowledge of CFTR biology and available clinical data.

articles.title: GATA2: A Custodian of Endometrial Identity: Guarding the Uterine Lining in Health and Disease.
articles.journal: BioEssays : news and reviews in molecular, cellular and developmental biology
articles.authors: Polaki US, Mattix A, Matson DR
articles.abstract: GATA Binding Protein 2 (GATA2) is a conserved zinc-finger transcription factor that is required for the normal function of the thin functional lining of the uterus, known as the endometrium. Acting in a cross-regulatory feedback loop with the progesterone receptor (PGR), GATA2 both maintains endometrial PGR expression and cooperates with PGR on chromatin to enable PGR signaling ensembles. Now, numerous studies are beginning to provide additional mechanistic insights into the critical roles of GATA2 in both normal reproductive biology and in the pathogenesis of multiple uterine disorders. Recently, GATA2 dysregulation has also been implicated in the progression of multiple uterine cancer subtypes. This review aims to organize the seminal findings on uterine GATA2 functions to date and plot a path forward toward resolving major unanswered questions in this rapidly evolving area.

articles.title: Investigating the association between blood lipid profiles and insulin resistance and β-cell function indices in pregnant women.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Feng J, Xu X, Tian Z et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to examine the associations between first-trimester lipid markers and second-trimester insulin resistance (IR) and pancreatic β-cell function (BCF) indices in pregnant women. An exploratory aim was to explore the apparent discrimination of lipid markers for cohort-defined low insulin sensitivity.
METHODS: This retrospective secondary analysis used prospectively collected cohort data from 1202 pregnant women in Beijing, China. Lipids were measured at 4-8 weeks of gestation, and a 75 g oral glucose tolerance test was performed at 24-28 weeks. The Homeostatic Model Assessment of Insulin Resistance (HOMA-IR) and the Matsuda index were analyzed as continuous measures of IR and insulin sensitivity. BCF was assessed using surrogate indices: the Homeostatic Model Assessment of β-cell function (HOMA-β) and the 60-min insulinogenic index (IGI60). Linear-regression models adjusted for age and early-pregnancy body mass index examined the associations between each lipid marker and continuous HOMA-IR and the Matsuda index as the primary analyses and with HOMA-β and IGI60 as the secondary analyses. Binary logistic-regression and receiver operating characteristic analyses of cohort-defined low insulin sensitivity were exploratory.
RESULTS: After adjustment for age and early-pregnancy body mass index, all seven lipid markers were significantly associated with continuous HOMA-IR and the Matsuda index (all nominal P < 0.05). No statistically significant associations were observed with the surrogate β-cell-function indices HOMA-β or IGI60. In the exploratory analyses, the lipid markers were associated with the cohort-defined low-Matsuda category. Triglycerides/high-density lipoprotein cholesterol had the highest observed area under the curve in the total population (0.723; 95% confidence interval 0.689-0.756). The exploratory cutoff selected by maximizing Youden's index was 0.65, with a sensitivity of 74.1% and a specificity of 62.5%.
CONCLUSION: First-trimester lipid markers were associated with second-trimester IR and insulin-sensitivity indices, whereas no statistically significant associations were observed with the surrogate BCF indices used in this study. Triglycerides/high-density lipoprotein cholesterol showed moderate apparent discrimination for cohort-defined low insulin sensitivity and should be considered a hypothesis-generating candidate marker requiring external validation.

articles.title: Clustering of Maternal and Perinatal Complications Following Fresh and Frozen Embryo Transfer in First-Time Mothers: A Population-Based Cohort Study.
articles.journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.authors: Landsverk E, Opdahl S, Bergh C et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess how often women who give birth following frozen-thawed embryo transfer (frozen-ET), fresh embryo transfer (fresh-ET) and natural conception (NC) have pregnancies without maternal and perinatal complications, develop a single complication, or experience multiple complications.
DESIGN: A population-based cohort study.
SETTING: Denmark (2008-2014), Norway (2008-2015) and Sweden (2008-2015).
POPULATION: Restricted to singleton pregnancies among first-time mothers, this study included 6634 deliveries after frozen-ET, 25 660 after fresh-ET and 523 277 after NC.
METHODS: The following complications were studied: stillbirth, neonatal death (0-27 days after delivery), preterm birth (gestational age < 37 weeks), small for gestational age or large for gestational age (birthweight < -22% or > +22% from the expected birthweight according to sex and gestational age), low birthweight (< 2500 g), macrosomia (≥ 4500 g), Apgar score < 5 at 5 min, major birth defects, hypertensive disorders in pregnancy, placenta previa and placental abruption.
RESULTS: In first-time mothers, three of every four singleton pregnancies after frozen-ET and fresh-ET were without maternal and perinatal complications, compared to four of every five pregnancies after NC. In pregnancies with neonatal survival ≥ 28 days (99.3% after frozen-ET, 99.3% after fresh-ET, and 99.5% after NC), two or more complications affected one in 11 pregnancies after frozen-ET and fresh-ET, compared to one in 16 after NC.
CONCLUSION: In this study, we observed that most first-time mothers experienced pregnancies without maternal and perinatal complications following ART, and when complications occurred, they were typically without additional complications. Although single and multiple complications were more common following ART than after NC, the absolute differences were small. These findings may help set realistic expectations when counselling people who consider ART treatment, or those already in treatment.

articles.title: Pelvic Floor Muscle Reactivity Measured Using M-Mode Ultrasonography in Males With Post-Prostatectomy Incontinence.
articles.journal: International journal of urology : official journal of the Japanese Urological Association
articles.authors: Ide Y, Shimizu N, Hyohdoh Y et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To characterize changes in M-mode measures of bladder base movement during supervised pelvic floor rehabilitation and their associations with urinary incontinence severity.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 69 males with urinary incontinence after radical prostatectomy who received supervised pelvic floor muscle training with ultrasound biofeedback. Within-participant changes, correlations, and regression analyses were performed. Firth logistic regression for continence included age, baseline pad weight, time from surgery to training, and baseline elevation time.
RESULTS: Median pad weight decreased from 247 (interquartile range, 64-684) to 40 (0-195) g/day, and elevation time shortened from 0.31 (0.24-0.45) to 0.20 (0.18-0.23) s (both p < 0.001; r = 0.83). Elevation speed increased (p < 0.001; r = 0.68), whereas elevation length did not change (p = 0.972; r = 0.00). Continence was achieved by 26 participants (37.7%). Pad weight correlated with elevation time at baseline (Spearman's ρ = 0.348; p = 0.003) and final assessment (Spearman's ρ = 0.417; p < 0.001). No statistically significant association was detected between baseline elevation time and continence in the main Firth model (adjusted odds ratio per 0.1-s increase, 0.954; 95% confidence interval, 0.633-1.349; p = 0.797).
CONCLUSIONS: Lower pad weight, shorter elevation time, and greater elevation speed co-occurred during supervised rehabilitation. Elevation time was associated with incontinence severity cross-sectionally. No statistically significant association was detected between baseline elevation time and continence in the main Firth model. Prospective validation is required before clinical use.

articles.title: Pre-eclampsia screening and prevention: Implementing FIGO guidelines in a Thai population.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Sophark I, Suksai M, Geater A et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the real-world implementation, screening performance, aspirin uptake, and safety of a FIGO (the International Federation of Gynecology & Obstetrics)-based first-trimester pre-eclampsia screening and prevention program.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included women initiating antenatal care before 14 weeks of gestation at a tertiary referral center in southern Thailand from 2021 to 2024. Screening incorporated maternal factors, mean arterial pressure, and uterine artery pulsatility index. Women with a calculated risk of 1:100 or greater were classified as being at high risk and offered aspirin 162 mg nightly. Outcomes included screening coverage, detection rates, aspirin uptake, pregnancy outcomes, and bleeding complications.
RESULTS: Among 1713 pregnancies, 71 developed pre-eclampsia (4.1%), including 49 with severe features. Overall, 1106 women were screened (64.6%), but coverage reached 93.6% by the end of implementation. The screen-positive rate was 11.3%. Detection rates were 61.7% for overall pre-eclampsia, 69.6% for delivery before 37 weeks of gestation, 87.5% for delivery before 34 weeks of gestation, and 100% for delivery before 32 weeks of gestation, with false-positive rates of approximately 9%-11%. Aspirin uptake among screen-positive women was 99.2%. Pre-eclampsia was associated with higher rates of cesarean delivery, preterm birth, lower birth weight, and neonatal intensive care unit admission. No eclampsia, placental abruption, maternal intensive care unit admission, maternal death, stillbirth, or neonatal death occurred. After adjustment for potential confounders, aspirin was not associated with the risk of an estimated blood loss of 500 mL or more, and the risk of an estimated blood loss of 1000 mL or more did not differ significantly between groups.
CONCLUSION: FIGO-based first-trimester screening was feasible in routine care, with increasing coverage as implementation matured, near-universal aspirin uptake, and clinically useful detection of preterm pre-eclampsia. Aspirin use was not significantly associated with severe bleeding.

articles.title: HPV prevalence and risk factors in a population-based cervical cancer screening program in Tashkent, Uzbekistan.
articles.authors: Turabova NR, Akhmedova LM, Akhmedova SK et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Population-based evidence on high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) and cervical screening outcomes in Uzbekistan is limited. We assessed hrHPV prevalence, district variation, associated factors, and cytological findings in Tashkent.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 52,995 women aged 18-70 years attending routine cervical screening across Tashkent city during 2024-2025. HR-HPV testing was performed using real-time PCR; reflex liquid-based cytology was performed for all HPV-positive women. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent determinants of HPV positivity (n = 52,995) and cytological abnormality (n = 2,255 HPV-positive women with adequate cytology).
RESULTS: Overall HR-HPV positivity was 4.43% (95% CI: 4.26-4.61%), with significant heterogeneity across districts (p < 0.01); Bektemir district recorded the highest prevalence. Independent predictors of HPV positivity included older age (aOR 2.41, 95% CI 1.24-4.83, for 56-70 years), irregular menstruation (aOR 1.39, 95% CI 1.23-1.57), and early sexual debut, while barrier contraception (aOR 0.70, 95% CI 0.60-0.81) and grand multiparity (aOR 0.80, 95% CI 0.65-0.98) were protective. Among HPV-positive women, any cytological abnormality was detected in 24.6% and high-grade lesions in 17.3%. Keratosis was the strongest predictor of cytological abnormality (aOR 4.09-5.16, both p < 0.01).
CONCLUSIONS: This large population-based study establishes a comprehensive HPV epidemiological baseline for Tashkent and demonstrates the clinical yield of HPV-primary screening with reflexive cytology triage. District-level heterogeneity and identified risk profiles provide evidence for geographically targeted program optimization in support of Uzbekistan's progress toward WHO 90-70-90 cervical cancer elimination targets.

articles.title: Bibliometric Insights Into Research Trends on Insulin Resistance in Gestational Diabetes Mellitus Based on the Web of Science Core Collection (1997-2025).
articles.authors: Li L, Gao Q, Liu H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and insulin resistance (IR) constitute a major global health challenge. This study aims to systematically characterize the knowledge framework, collaborative networks, research fronts, and evolving hotspots in GDM and IR research.
METHODS: We identified 3658 records on GDM and IR from the Web of Science Core Collection (1997-2025) and included 3473 English-language articles and review articles after language and document-type screening. Using VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and the R package 'bibliometrix', we performed bibliometric and visualization analyses of publication trends, national and institutional contributions, journal impact, co-citation networks and keyword dynamics.
RESULTS: Annual publication output increased over time, particularly after 2014, with 322 publications in 2022. China contributed the largest number of publications, whereas citation indicators varied across countries after time-normalized assessment. International collaboration networks identified major contributing institutions, including Harvard University, the University of California System and the University of Toronto. Co-citation and keyword analyses revealed persistent research themes related to insulin resistance, obesity and glucose metabolism, whereas recent attention has focused on gut microbiota, biomarkers, epigenetic regulation, pregnancy outcomes and environmental exposures such as PFAS.
CONCLUSION: This bibliometric study provides an overview of the global research landscape of GDM and IR from 1997 to 2025. The findings demonstrate increasing research activity and evolving themes, including gut microbiota, biomarkers, epigenetic regulation and environmental exposures. These findings reflect patterns of scientific attention rather than established mechanisms or clinical efficacy, highlighting the need for further epidemiological and clinical validation.

articles.title: Age Redistribution and Demographic Contributors to Pelvic Organ Prolapse Disability Across Asia, 1990-2023: An Analysis of the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.authors: Zhang W, Yang X, Zhu W
articles.abstract:
AIM: To examine how the age distribution of pelvic organ prolapse-related disability changed across Asia and quantify the demographic contributors to changes in absolute disability burden.
METHODS: We analyzed Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 estimates for genital prolapse in five Asian regions and 34 countries and territories for 1990-2023. We assessed all-age years lived with disability and age-standardized rates. Age-specific rates and shares were examined among women aged 20 years or older using 5-year age groups and a final group aged 95 years or older. We decomposed adult burden changes into population growth, population aging, and age-specific rate change.
RESULTS: Counts increased in all five regions despite declining age-standardized rates. The age group with the largest disability share shifted from 65-69 to 70-74 years in High-income Asia Pacific and from 45-49 to 50-54 years in South Asia, but remained at 55-59 years in East Asia. Shares increased in all age groups aged 70 years or older in East Asia and High-income Asia Pacific. Population growth was the larger demographic contributor in South Asia, contributing 103.63% of the 1990 adult burden. Population aging contributed more than population growth in East Asia and High-income Asia Pacific, equivalent to 86.09% and 64.04% of their 1990 adult burdens.
CONCLUSIONS: Age redistribution differed across Asia. The age distribution of disability shifted toward older women in East Asia and High-income Asia Pacific, while middle adulthood remained prominent in South Asia. These patterns can inform pelvic floor care planning.

articles.title: Association Between Timing of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus Diagnosis and Perinatal Outcomes: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.authors: Hasegawa T, Nakamura E, Sato S et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To evaluate the association between the timing of gestational diabetes mellitus diagnosis and perinatal outcomes, including large-for-gestational-age birth, neonatal hypoglycemia, and postpartum dysglycemia.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study included women with gestational diabetes mellitus who delivered at Saitama Medical Center between April 2020 and March 2023. Women were classified according to the diagnosis of gestational diabetes mellitus before or at or after 24 gestational weeks. The primary outcome was large-for-gestational-age birth. Associations were evaluated in the overall cohort and after propensity score matching using infertility treatment, family history of diabetes, nulliparity, and pre-pregnancy body mass index.
RESULTS: Among 228 women, 97 were classified into the early diagnosis group and 131 into the late diagnosis group. The incidence of large-for-gestational-age birth was significantly lower in the early diagnosis group than in the late diagnosis group (13.4% [13/97] vs. 29.0% [38/131], p = 0.008). In the propensity score-matched cohort (92 pairs), this association remained significant (10.9% [10/92] vs. 28.3% [26/92], p = 0.005). Neonatal hypoglycemia and postpartum dysglycemia did not differ significantly between the groups after matching (p = 0.730 and p = 0.711, respectively).
CONCLUSIONS: Gestational diabetes mellitus diagnosed at or after 24 gestational weeks was associated with a higher incidence of large-for-gestational-age birth, whereas neonatal hypoglycemia and postpartum dysglycemia did not differ according to the timing of diagnosis.

articles.title: Contraceptive counseling among individuals with genetic conditions: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Nevins AW, Zemet R, Ojo E et al.
articles.abstract: Individuals with genetic conditions are at increased risk for adverse pregnancy outcomes; therefore, effective postpartum contraception is essential. Limited data exists regarding postpartum LARC counseling and uptake in this population. A retrospective chart review was used to evaluate documentation of LARC counseling in pregnancies of individuals with genetic diagnoses who delivered at two delivery sites from 2011 to 2024. LARC counseling was documented in 83.3% of patients, of which 27.1% initiated LARC. Nulliparity was associated with lower counseling rates, while antepartum disease progression and certain complications were associated with higher counseling. Variation by demographic and clinical factors suggests gaps in equitable counseling, highlighting the need to better understand barriers in this population.

articles.title: Impact of vibegron on quality of life in men with overactive bladder receiving treatment for benign prostatic hyperplasia: patient-reported outcomes from the randomized placebo-controlled COURAGE trial.
articles.journal: Health and quality of life outcomes
articles.authors: Peters KM, Staskin D, Thomas E et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Men receiving pharmacologic treatment for benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) may experience reduced quality of life (QoL) owing to persistent overactive bladder (OAB) symptoms. Vibegron, a β3-adrenergic receptor agonist, was approved for OAB symptoms based on the COURAGE trial. We present exploratory patient-reported outcomes from COURAGE.
METHODS: Eligible men were ≥ 45 years old with OAB symptoms receiving BPH treatment (α-blocker ± 5α-reductase inhibitor). Patients were randomly assigned 1:1 to receive vibegron 75 mg or placebo for 24 weeks. Patients completed the OAB questionnaire (OAB-q) and Patient Global Impression (PGI) scales at baseline and weeks 12 and 24. Changes from baseline in OAB-q subscores and PGI scales were assessed. An anchor-based approach was used to determine the distribution of change from baseline in COURAGE trial endpoints (micturitions, urgency, nocturia, and urge urinary incontinence [UUI] episodes) by category of change on the PGI change (PGI-C) scale.
RESULTS: Of 1105 patients (vibegron, n = 551; placebo, n = 554); 1080 (vibegron, n = 538; placebo, n = 542) had evaluable data and were included in the analysis. Baseline mean OAB-q and PGI scores were similar between treatment groups. Patients receiving vibegron had statistically significantly greater improvements vs. placebo from baseline to week 12 (P < 0.05) for all OAB-q subscale scores and improvements remained statistically significant at week 24 (P < 0.05), except for social interaction. Patients receiving vibegron had improvements from baseline on all PGI endpoints at weeks 12 and 24. A higher percentage of patients receiving vibegron (81.9%) reported improvement on the PGI-C vs. placebo (69.3%). Patients receiving vibegron who reported moderately or much better on the PGI-C scale demonstrated improvement in mean change from baseline to week 12 in micturitions, urgency, nocturia, and UUI.
CONCLUSIONS: Men with OAB symptoms receiving pharmacologic BPH treatment demonstrated statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in QoL with vibegron vs. placebo, consistent with improvements in OAB symptoms.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinicaltrials.gov NCT03902080 Registered 04-01-2019.

articles.title: Association of depressive symptoms using patient health questionnaire-9 with quality of life in postmenopausal women with DXA-confirmed osteoporosis.
articles.authors: Mehta NA, Savardekar LS, Shelke SB et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Depression is an under-recognized risk factor for osteoporosis (OP) and adversely affects quality of life (QOL). Data on depressive symptoms among postmenopausal women aged ≥50 years with osteoporosis in India are limited. This study aimed to assess depressive symptoms and their impact on QOL among postmenopausal women with osteoporosis from low- and middle-income urban communities.
METHODOLOGY: A total of 688 menopausal women aged ≥50 years were recruited through community-based camps (2016-2019), of whom 14.2%, 31.5%, and 54.2% were diagnosed as normal, osteopenia, and osteoporosis, respectively, by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) scans. A subset of 100 postmenopausal women aged 50-75 years with osteoporosis and ≥5 years since menopause was included using a consecutive convenience sampling technique. Depressive symptoms were assessed using the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9), and QOL was assessed using the WHOQOL-BREF through face- to- face (in-person) interviews. Participants were also assessed for non-communicable diseases (NCD) and musculoskeletal complaints.
RESULTS: Mild, moderate, and moderately severe depressive symptoms were observed in 17%, 4%, and 1% of the participants, respectively. The comparison of WHOQOL-BREF with depressive symptoms revealed that the physical domain of WHOQOL was significantly associated with depressive symptoms, indicating that women with depressive symptoms had substantially lower median scores [63.0 (IQR:50.0-69.0) vs. 88.0 (IQR: 81.0-94.0), Mann-Whitney U=128.0, z= -6.136, p<0.001, r=0.61].
CONCLUSION: Screening with the PHQ-9 and WHOQOL-BREF in community-based NCD camps may help in the early identification of depressive symptoms among menopausal women with osteoporosis. Integrating mental health screening with current geriatric and primary healthcare services through national initiatives, such as the National Mental Health Programme and Ayushman Bharat, may improve the overall quality of life.

articles.title: Epidemiological characteristics and genotype distribution of human papillomavirus infection in Lianyungang, Northern Jiangsu Province, China, 2021-2025.
articles.authors: Chen X, Cui D, Zhang Y et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To analyze the prevalence and genotype distribution of human papillomavirus (HPV) infection in Lianyungang, Northern Jiangsu Province of China, and to provide localized epidemiological data for the prevention and treatment of cervical cancer and related diseases.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on HPV genotyping data from 50,279 women at Lianyungang Maternal and Child Health Hospital from 2021 to 2025. Overall infection rate, genotype distribution, age-specific positivity, and longitudinal trends were evaluated.
RESULTS: The overall HPV prevalence was 18.57% (9,336/50,279), increasing from 15.30% in 2021 to a peak of 21.18% in 2023 but adjusting to 19.84% by 2025. Single infections were the predominant infection pattern (75.83%, 7,080/9,336). Age-specific prevalence exhibited a bimodal distribution, with the first peak in the ≤ 25 years group (23.56%, 810/3,438) and a second peak in the ≥ 56 years group (1,017/3,904, 26.05%). The five most prevalent genotypes were HPV52 (1,822/50,279, 3.62%), HPV16 (3.01%, 1514/50,279), HPV58 (2.46%, 1,239/50,279), HPV53 (1.97%, 989/50,279), and HPV39 (1.72%, 864/50,279), while HPV81 (1.70%, 856/50,279) were the most prevalent LR HPV genotypes. Annual analysis revealed HPV53 prevalence increasing significantly from 1.51% in 2021 to 2.72% in 2025 (P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: This study provides the largest-scale data on the recent epidemiological characteristics of HPV infection in Lianyungang, China, which will guide the development of local cervical cancer prevention and control strategies.

articles.title: Comparative evaluation of ChatGPT-4o and ChatGPT-5.1 for automated LUTS scoring from clinician-documented narratives.
articles.authors: Lee J, Lee J, Yoo S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) are commonly quantified using validated instruments such as the International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS) and the Overactive Bladder Symptom Score (OABSS). However, structured questionnaires are not consistently administered in routine outpatient practice, where clinicians frequently rely on narrative documentation. While generative large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated potential in clinical natural language processing, their performance stability across successive model generations for automated symptom scoring remains unclear. We conducted a head-to-head comparison of ChatGPT-4o and ChatGPT-5.1 to evaluate generational performance differences in automated LUTS scoring.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective secondary analysis of a previously reported outpatient cohort evaluated the performance of ChatGPT-4o and ChatGPT-5.1 in estimating LUTS-related scores from clinician-documented narratives. Free-text symptom narratives documented from electronic medical records were entered directly into each model using identical prompts. Ground-truth IPSS and OABSS total scores were obtained from completed questionnaires. Predictive performance was assessed using mean absolute error (MAE), root mean squared error (RMSE), intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), and Spearman's correlation coefficients. Classification of clinically significant LUTS (IPSS ≥ 8) and overactive bladder (OAB; OABSS ≥ 3 with urgency score ≥ 2) was evaluated using accuracy, Cohen's kappa (κ), and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). The analysis included 91 patients from the original cohort.
RESULTS: Among 91 patients (mean age 71.9 ± 10.3 years; 58.2% male), 49 completed IPSS and 78 completed OABSS. For IPSS prediction, MAE/RMSE were 4.88/6.34 for ChatGPT-4o and 4.92/7.01 for ChatGPT-5.1, with no significant differences between models. For OABSS prediction, MAE/RMSE were 1.88/2.76 and 2.03/2.93, respectively, again without significant differences. Agreement was moderate for IPSS (ICC 0.561-0.509) and higher for…
CONCLUSIONS: ChatGPT-4o and ChatGPT-5.1 demonstrated comparable and moderate performance in approximating LUTS-related symptom scores from unstructured clinical narratives. These findings suggest that generative AI models may serve as supportive tools for automated symptom quantification and indicate relative performance stability across model generations within real-world urological practice.

articles.title: Exploring women's empowerment in relation to contraceptive practices among married women in Bangladesh: a survey-weighted sequential logistic regression analysis.
articles.authors: Sarkar S, Pal B, Akib MMH et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Women's empowerment is multidimensional, yet contraceptive studies often combine distinct domains into one score. We examined whether household decision-making participation and rejection of wife-beating had different associations with current contraceptive use in Bangladesh.
METHODS: We analyzed cross-sectional data from currently married or partnered, nonpregnant women aged 15-49 years in the 2022 Bangladesh Demographic and Health Survey. Tetrachoric principal component analysis derived standardized scores for household decision-making and rejection of wife-beating. Survey-weighted logistic regression estimated associations with current use of any contraceptive method across sequential adjustment models. Modified Poisson regression, marginal standardization, modern-method analyses, and alternative empowerment specifications assessed robustness.
RESULTS: The complete-case sample included 17,345 women. Parallel analysis retained two empowerment components explaining 76.2% of total variance. In the fully adjusted model, each 1-standard-deviation higher household decision-making score was associated with higher odds of contraceptive use (OR = 1.068, 95% CI = 1.029-1.108; p < 0.001). The corresponding adjusted prevalence ratio was 1.023 (95% CI = 1.010-1.036), and the standardized prevalence difference comparing + 1 with - 1 standard deviation was 2.84% points (95% CI 1.25-4.42). Rejection of wife-beating was not independently associated with use (OR = 0.983, 95% CI = 0.946-1.021; p = 0.367). The domain-specific pattern persisted for modern contraceptive use and in reduced-adjustment analyses. Middle- and rich-wealth groups had lower adjusted odds than the poor group, showing that contraceptive use did not follow a simple positive wealth gradient.
CONCLUSIONS: Household decision-making participation, but not rejection of wife-beating, was associated with contraceptive use in this nationally representative sample. The findings show why empowerment domains should not be treated as interchangeable and support multidimensional measurement in family-planning research. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify temporality.

articles.title: Prevalance and factors associated with cervical cancer screening uptake among HIV positive women in the rural communities of Alebtong district in Uganda.
articles.authors: Atepo S, Iramiot JS, Wanume B et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer (CC) is the leading gynaecologic malignancy in Uganda and affects about 6959 women and 4607 die annually. Despite the launch of the global call to elimination of CC in 2020, only 10% of women in Uganda are screened and studies in Uganda among women of reproductive age group(WRAG) living with Human Immune virus (HIV) [(WRAG-LHIV)] have reported rates of 30.3% to 39.4%. Subsequently 85% patients with CC present with advanced disease leading to poor outcomes. Furthermore, women living with (HIV) have a six-fold higher risk of developing CC compared to their HIV negative counterparts. Alebtong district in Northern Uganda is reported to have a higher HIV prevalence than the national average and CCS uptake among women of reproductive age group living with HIV (WRAG-LHIV) is unknown. Therefore this study aimed to determine the prevalence of CCS uptake and its determinants among WRAG-LHIV in Alebtong district.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted at 7 purposively selected high volume antiretroviral therapy (ART) offering health facilities and their attached 34 community drug distribution points (CDDPs). 381 WRAG-LHIV were recruited by systematic sampling. Researcher administered pretested closed-ended questionnaires were used to collect quantitative data. The data was entered into Microsoft Excel and subsequently imported into Stata version 14 for statistical analysis. Statistical significance was set at a p-value < 0.05.
RESULTS: A total of 381 women with a mean age of 32.9 years (SD ± 7) participated in the study. The majority, 80.8% (308/381) had had at most primary education, 81.4% were either married/cohabiting and 53.3% (203/381) resided within 5 km of a health facility. Importantly, 53.5%( 204/381) had had early sexual debut and 81.6%( 311/381) were multiparous. The prevalence of cervical cancer screening (CCS) uptake was 49.6% (189/381). The statistically significant factors associated with CCS uptake were encouragement by friends and family members, spouse support, good knowledge about cervical cancer screening, and preference of male healthcare providers, literacy and…
CONCLUSION: CCS uptake among WRAG-LHIV was suboptimal and below the 70% target set for CC elimination. There is need for more emphasis on male involvement in terms of spouses and clinical team, peer advocacy integration of CCS into chronic care clinics and adopting modalities that would encourage community participation and males in CCS activities.

articles.title: Transperineal strain elastography for evaluating periurethral biomechanics in women with stress urinary incontinence: a diagnostic accuracy study.
articles.authors: Shahbazkhani AH, Shakki Katouli F, Torabi S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stress urinary incontinence (SUI) commonly reflects loss of urethral support and altered periurethral biomechanics. Strain elastography (SE) can quantify tissue deformation; however, its clinical diagnostic value for SUI is uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate periurethral strain elastography in women with and without SUI and to compare its diagnostic performance with established kinematic ultrasound parameters.
METHODS: In a prospective case-control study, 43 premenopausal women (23 SUI, 20 controls) underwent standardized transperineal B-mode ultrasound and strain elastography. Four periurethral ROIs-posterior-mid (A1), anterior-mid (A2; prespecified primary outcome), posterior-upper (A3), and anterior-upper (A4)-were sampled at rest and during Valsalva. Kinematic measures (bladder-neck descent [BND], retrovesical angle [RVA]) were recorded. Analyses used parametric or nonparametric tests as appropriate, Cohen's d effect sizes, bootstrap 95% CIs (2,000 replicates), ROC curves, and exploratory logistic regression models.
RESULTS: Groups were similar in age and BMI. At rest, strain ratios (SRs) did not differ. During Valsalva maneuver, however, controls demonstrated significantly higher strain ratios than SUI cases in all four regions, including posterior-mid (A1; p = 0.006), anterior-mid (A2; p = 0.003), posterior-upper (A3; p = 0.037), and anterior-upper (A4; p = 0.004), demonstrating consistently higher relative periurethral strain-ratio values in controls during Valsalva. Despite statistically significant mean differences, SR variables showed poor raw discriminatory performance on ROC analysis (AUC range 0.248-0.336), reflecting an unexpected direction of discrimination (controls having higher, "stiffer," SR values than cases). In contrast, kinematic parameters demonstrated excellent…
CONCLUSIONS: Transperineal SE detected group-level differences in relative periurethral deformation during Valsalva, but strain-ratio measures showed poor standalone diagnostic performance. In this sample, SE did not demonstrate improved discrimination beyond conventional kinematic parameters; however, the modest sample size and lack of internal validation limit the certainty and generalizability of this finding. BND and RVA remained substantially more accurate. Accordingly, SE should currently be regarded as an exploratory biomechanical research measure rather than a diagnostic test for SUI, and its potential complementary role requires further validation.

articles.title: Kidney disease progression during and after pregnancy in a Col4a3-/- mouse model of Alport syndrome: an experimental study.
articles.authors: Kong X, Wang F, Ma Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Alport syndrome (AS) is an inherited kidney disease. The effect of pregnancy on the kidney disease progression in AS females remains controversial.
METHODS: Col4a3-/- female mice were used to build the models of pregnancy at early Alport stage (12-week of age) and advanced Alport stage (18-week of age). Proteinuria, renal function and kidney pathology of the two groups of pregnancy mice were studied and compared with the same age groups of non-pregnancy Col4a3-/- female mice.
RESULTS: Col4a3-/- female mice at 18-week had significantly elevated BUN (p = 0.034), Scr (p = 0.034) and UACR (p = 0.05) compared to that at 8-week. The age of 12-week and 18-week were selected to build the models of pregnancy at early Alport stage (n = 7) and at advanced Alport stage (n = 9), respectively. Compared with non-pregnancy group, the UACR and BUN at 16-week (after delivery), 18-week, 21-week and 24-week of mice with pregnancy at early Alport stage were not significantly different. For the mice with pregnancy at advanced Alport stage, UACR (p = 0.036) was significantly increased at 21-week (after delivery); the BUN at 21-week and 24-week showed a rising trend. Two mice died at 23-24 weeks in the group of pregnancy at advanced Alport stage and most likely died from kidney failure. The serum CysC was significantly increased in both pregnancy groups at age of 24-week compared to non-pregnancy group. Glomerular sclerosis and interstitial fibrosis showed a worsening trend in the pregnancy groups, especially in the group of pregnancy at advanced Alport stage.
CONCLUSIONS: Pregnancy at advanced Alport stage predispose to accelerated progression of kidney disease, suggesting that early pregnancy may mitigate the impact of pregnancy on kidney disease progression in Alport syndrome.

articles.title: Assessing the need for reproductive genetic counseling among adults with cystic fibrosis.
articles.authors: Coulter E, Knapp S, Grassy M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reproductive health has become an increasingly important focus for people with cystic fibrosis (CF), and guidelines have recommended routine inclusion of genetic counselors on care teams to address questions regarding infertility, pregnancy planning, prenatal diagnosis, and other reproductive health considerations. Despite this, implementation of genetic counseling is still lacking, and there is limited literature documenting patient perspectives on reproductive genetic counseling, particularly in the era of highly effective cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) modulators that have transformed the landscape of clinical care.
METHODS: An electronic REDCap mixed-methods survey was distributed to adults with CF at our center to assess the need for reproductive genetic counseling and to understand current reproductive health concerns. Descriptive statistics were used to report quantitative and demographic data, and a thematic analysis was performed for free-response data.
RESULTS: A total of 237 patients were surveyed, and 116 (49%) responded. Of the 116 respondents, 31 (27%) had never heard of genetic counseling, and 82 (71%) had not previously received it. Forty-four of these 82 (54%) reported that they would find genetic counseling moderately or very helpful. The most important reproductive health topics included the effect of CFTR modulators on fertility and pregnancy, and carrier screening for partners and family members. Qualitative analysis revealed key content categories, including fertility status, concerns and uncertainty with personal health, and lack of informed discussions with providers. Multiple respondents also highlighted not wanting to pass CF onto a child.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings highlight a need and desire in the modern era among adults with CF for improved education regarding reproductive health.

articles.title: The hidden burden of insomnia in late pregnancy: prevalence and risk factors among Egyptian women.
articles.authors: Essa A, Ebeid I, Noureldeen IM et al.
articles.abstract:
