METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 82 patients with localized prostate cancer treated with MR-linac SBRT (n = 51) or IMRT (n = 31) between 2022 and 2025. Clinically meaningful declines in EPIC-50 domain scores were assessed at 1-3 and 9-12 months. Predictors of urinary quality-of-life deterioration were evaluated using logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic analysis.
RESULTS: The proportions of patients with clinically meaningful declines in urinary, bowel, sexual, and hormonal domains did not differ significantly between the treatment groups at either 1-3 or 9-12 months. Symptom-directed pharmacotherapy was initiated more frequently after IMRT, including medications for lower urinary tract symptoms (P = .028), gastrointestinal symptoms (P = .0044), and vasomotor symptoms (P = .0014). Among patients receiving MR-linac SBRT, a higher baseline International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS) was associated with urinary quality-of-life deterioration. An IPSS cutoff of ≥9 was significantly associated with urinary deterioration (odds ratio, 27.0, 95% CI 4.11-541.49; P = .0002).
CONCLUSIONS: MR-linac SBRT showed no significant differences in patient-reported quality-of-life outcomes compared with IMRT and was associated with less frequent use of symptom-directed pharmacotherapy. Baseline IPSS may help identify patients at increased risk of urinary quality-of-life deterioration after MR-linac SBRT.

articles.title: Inhibition of HDAC6 as a Therapeutic Strategy for Cervical Cancer Mediated by the p21 Signaling Pathway.
articles.authors: Yan W, Jia X
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to investigate the role of HDAC6 in cervical cancer by exploring its impact on cell proliferation, apoptosis, and interaction with the p21 signaling pathway.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis of cervical cancer tissue samples obtained from 40 patients (20 recurrent and 20 non-recurrent) was conducted. Immunohistochemistry was performed to assess HDAC6 and p21 expression levels in the clinical samples. HeLa cells were transfected with HDAC6-targeted lentivirus for knockdown experiments. The cell proliferation rate was evaluated using the Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8) assay, while apoptosis was measured by flow cytometry. Protein expression levels of HDAC6, p21, Bcl-2, and Bax were determined by western blotting. Cisplatin was applied to investigate its combined effect with HDAC6 knockdown on cell proliferation and apoptosis.
RESULTS: In clinical samples, elevated HDAC6 expression level was associated with advanced International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) stage and poor prognosis, while reduced p21 expression level was correlated with disease recurrence. In HeLa cells, HDAC6 knockdown led to a significant reduction (67.3%) in cell proliferation compared with controls (p < 0.05) and increased apoptosis rates (p < 0.05). The combination of HDAC6 knockdown and cisplatin further enhanced the inhibition of cell proliferation and promoted apoptosis more effectively than cisplatin or HDAC6 knockdown alone (p < 0.01). Western blot analysis revealed the reduced Bcl-2 expression level and the increased Bax and p21 expression levels in the HDAC6 knockdown group.
CONCLUSIONS: HDAC6 knockdown, as demonstrated by both clinical sample analysis and in vitro HeLa cell experiments, could inhibit cervical cancer progression by decreasing cell proliferation and promoting apoptosis. Its combination with cisplatin could be a promising therapeutic strategy.

articles.title: Predictive Value of Maternal Peripheral Blood PAF and sFlt-1 Levels for Preterm Birth Secondary to PPROM.
articles.authors: Li X, Li J
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preterm premature rupture of membranes (PPROM) is a leading cause of preterm birth, which seriously endangers maternal and neonatal health. Platelet-activating factor (PAF) and soluble FMS-like tyrosine kinase-1 (sFlt-1) play important roles in pregnancy, but their predictive value for preterm birth following PPROM remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the predictive value of maternal peripheral blood PAF and sFlt-1 levels for spontaneous preterm delivery (SPTD) secondary to PPROM.
METHODS: A total of 85 singleton pregnant women with a gestational age of 23 + 0 to 30 + 6 weeks who were diagnosed with PPROM were enrolled. Based on the occurrence of SPTD within 14 days after sampling, the participants were divided into an imminent SPTD group (iSPTD, n = 45) and a non-imminent SPTD group (non-iSPTD, n = 40). Serum levels of PAF and sFlt-1 were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Multivariate logistic regression was used to analyze their independent association with SPTD within 14 days post-sampling, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were employed to evaluate their predictive value.
RESULTS: Maternal peripheral blood levels of both PAF and sFlt-1 were significantly higher in the iSPTD group than in the non-iSPTD group (all p < 0.05). Multivariate logistic regression analysis revealed that PAF (odds ratio [OR] = 1.272, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.094 - 1.480) and sFlt-1 (OR = 1.179, 95% CI: 1.058 - 1.315) were independent risk factors for SPTD within 14 days after sampling. ROC curve analysis showed that the area under the curve (AUC) for predicting SPTD within 14 days was 0.762 for PAF and 0.738 for sFlt-1. The combined nomogram model achieved an AUC of 0.829, demonstrating good predictive performance.
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated maternal peripheral blood levels of PAF and sFlt-1 are independent risk factors for SPTD within 14 days after sampling in patients with PPROM. Both biomarkers exhibit predictive value for SPTD, and their combination in a nomogram model can further improve predictive performance, showing potential for clinical application.

articles.title: Cytomegalovirus Seroprevalence Among Pregnant Women in the Region of Rabat, Morocco: a Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.authors: Lamrani-Alaoui H, Zouaki A, Amin GE et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Congenital CMV infection can lead to outcomes such as hearing loss and neurodevelopmental disabilities.
METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated the CMV IgG seropositive rate in 200 pregnant women in the Rabat region to determine mothers' immune status and its distribution pattern. The sera were obtained from a serum bank between January and October, 2021. Questionnaires were administered to obtain information regarding the sociodemographic and clinical data of the enrollee. Maternal CMV serology was determined, using Alinity i chemilumi-nescence microparticle immunoassays for IgG quantitative detection.
RESULTS: The age range was from 17 to 46 years, with a median age of 30 years (IQR 24.8 - 35) and a mean gestation of 20.4 ± 4.1 week. The seroprevalence of CMV IgG antibodies was 198 (99%), while 1% of participants were seronegative.
CONCLUSIONS: We recorded a low risk profile for primary CMV infection during pregnancy due to the large number of seropositive women that were infected at a young age.

articles.title: Serum Vitamin D Combined with Obstetric Parameters to Construct a Nomogram Model for Predicting the Risk of PFD Disorders.
articles.authors: Li JC, Song JN, Liu CH et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postpartum pelvic floor dysfunction (PFD) significantly impacts women's quality of life and mental health. Although existing studies suggest various obstetric factors may contribute to PFD, there is a lack of early prediction tools based on readily available indicators. This study aimed to develop a nomogram model incorporating serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)VitD] levels and routine obstetric parameters to predict the risk of PFD.
METHODS: A total of 300 women who delivered and completed a 6-week postpartum follow-up were enrolled. Data on age, body mass index (BMI), duration of the second stage of labor, neonatal birth weight, and serum 25(OH) VitD levels within 24 hours postpartum were collected. Participants were divided into PFD and non-PFD groups based on follow-up outcomes. Logistic regression analysis was used to identify independent risk factors for PFD, and a nomogram prediction model was constructed. The model's performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA).
RESULTS: Multivariate logistic regression revealed that age, BMI, duration of the second stage of labor, birth weight, and 25(OH)VitD levels were independent predictors of PFD (p < 0.05). The nomogram model achieved an AUC of 0.830 with calibration curves demonstrating good agreement between predicted and observed probabilities. DCA indicated substantial clinical net benefit across a wide probability threshold range.
CONCLUSIONS: The developed nomogram model effectively predicts postpartum PFD risk using easily obtainable pre- and post-delivery indicators. This model may facilitate early identification of high-risk individuals, guiding personalized rehabilitation strategies and improving early intervention and prevention of PFD.

articles.title: Nationwide Assessment of Trends, Characteristics, and Outcomes of Pregnancy for Cancer Survivors.
articles.authors: Matsuo K, Komura N, Yamaguchi A et al.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Cancer survivors are individuals with a diagnosis of malignant neoplasm, either living with (ie, current cancer survivors) or free of (ie, past cancer survivors) cancer. As the prevalence of cancer survivors of reproductive age increases worldwide, assessment of pregnancy characteristics and outcomes among past cancer survivors is important.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the temporal trends, clinical and obstetric characteristics, and maternal morbidity at delivery among current and past cancer survivors.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This nationwide cross-sectional study used National Inpatient Sample data for hospital deliveries from 2016 to 2023. Analyses were conducted from April to May 2026.
EXPOSURE: A prior or current diagnosis of cancer at hospital delivery, with individuals classified as being a past cancer survivor, a current cancer survivor, or an individual without a cancer diagnosis.
MAIN OUTCOME AND MEASURE: The primary outcome was severe maternal morbidity at delivery, assessed with multivariable generalized linear models with a Poisson distribution.
RESULTS: Among 28 360 443 hospital deliveries, there were 106 740 (0.4%) hospital deliveries for past cancer survivors, 21 975 (<0.1%) for current cancer survivors, and 28 231 728 (99.5%) without a cancer diagnosis. The median (IQR) maternal age at delivery was 33 (29-36), 32 (27-36), and 29 (25-33) years among past cancer survivors, current cancer survivors, and individuals without a cancer diagnosis, respectively. During the 8-year study period, hospital deliveries for past cancer survivors increased from 30.1 to 45.6 per 10 000 hospital deliveries (average annual percentage change [AAPC] = 6.3% [95% CI, 5.1%-7.9%]), whereas hospital deliveries for current cancer survivors were unchanged (7.0 to 7.4 per 10 000 hospital deliveries; AAPC = 0.2% [95% CI, -2.8% to 3.7%]). Most hospital deliveries (57.6%) for past cancer survivors were full-term, whereas only 39.6% were full-term for current cancer survivors. Compared with the no cancer…
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this US cross-sectional study, the prevalence of hospital deliveries for past cancer survivors increased from 2016 to 2023, and severe maternal morbidity was increased at delivery for past and current cancer survivors. These findings support the importance of preconception evaluation for cancer survivors and early referral to tertiary care centers with multidisciplinary teams, as currently recommended by multiple organizations.

articles.title: Menstrual Disorders: Postmenopausal Uterine Bleeding.
articles.authors: Miller A, Paruchuri B
articles.abstract: Postmenopausal uterine bleeding, defined as any vaginal bleeding occurring at least 12 months after the final men-strual period, is a clinically significant symptom that warrants prompt evaluation. Although most cases are due to benign etiologies, such as genitourinary syndrome of menopause (vaginal or endometrial atrophy), endometrial pol-yps, or hormone-related changes, postmenopausal uterine bleeding is the presenting symptom in approximately 90% of patients with endometrial cancer. Early detection of endometrial cancer is essential, with the diagnostic approach focusing on ruling out other causes of bleeding, stratifying the patient's risk, and obtaining tests such as transvaginal ultrasonography or endometrial sampling (biopsy) to rule out malignancy. Management of postmenopausal uterine bleeding is based on the underlying cause and can range from hormone therapy to polypectomy for intracavitary polyps or surgical referral for atypical hyperplasia, endometrial intraepithelial neoplasia, or carcinoma. Postmeno-pausal bleeding can also lead to significant patient concern and distress, largely due to fear of underlying malignancy. A systematic, evidence-based approach to postmenopausal uterine bleeding evaluation allows clinicians to diagnose serious pathology early and address patient concerns with clear guidance and follow-up treatment plans.

articles.title: Menstrual Disorders: Premenopausal Abnormal Uterine Bleeding.
articles.authors: Paruchuri B, Miller A
articles.abstract: Abnormal uterine bleeding is a common and distressing concern for reproductive-aged females, potentially leading to long-term consequences such as iron deficiency anemia if not properly addressed. The International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics defines abnormal uterine bleeding as bleeding occurring outside the normal frequency of every 24 to 38 days, with additional criteria based on cycle length, regularity, and flow volume. Etiologies are classified using the PALM-COEIN system, which separates structural causes (polyp, adenomyosis, leiomyoma, and malignancy and hyperplasia) from nonstructural causes (coagulopathy, ovulatory dysfunction, endometrial disorders, iatrogenic factors, and conditions not otherwise classified). Transvaginal and transabdominal Doppler ultrasonography are the recommended initial diagnostic modalities for structural etiologies, and magnetic resonance imaging may be used if findings are inconclusive. Endometrial sampling is indicated in patients at increased risk for endometrial pathology, including those with obesity, chronic anovulation, a family history of malignancy, or age of 45 years or older. Management options include medical and surgical therapies. The levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system is a highly effective medical treatment, whereas hysterectomy remains the most definitive option, particularly for patients who have completed childbearing. Medical management adequately controls symptoms for many, although structural conditions often require procedural or surgical intervention.

articles.title: Menstrual Disorders: Amenorrhea.
articles.authors: Miller A, Paruchuri B
articles.abstract: Amenorrhea, defined as the absence or abnormal cessation of menses, warrants a timely, structured evaluation in primary care. It can signal possible dysfunction anywhere along the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian-uterine axis; thus, a systematic approach to workup is necessary to identify the underlying cause. Primary amenorrhea is the lack of menses by age 15 years in patients with normal secondary sexual development or by age 13 years in those with no breast development. Secondary amenorrhea is absence of menses for more than 3 months in those with previously regular cycles or for more than 6 months in those with previously irregular cycles. Common etiologies of amenorrhea include pregnancy, polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (formerly polycystic ovary syndrome), functional hypothalamic amenorrhea, thyroid disease, hyperprolactinemia (including macroprolactinemia), primary ovarian insufficiency, and anatomic outflow tract disorders. The recommended workup includes a history, physical examination, and selected laboratory tests (eg, levels of thyroid-stimulating hormone [thyrotropin], prolactin, follicle-stimulating hormone, and luteinizing hormone), with imaging guided by findings. Management addresses the underlying cause and reduces short- and long-term risks to other organ systems, such as the bone, endometrial, metabolic, and cardiovascular systems; it should involve shared decision-making and may entail referral.

articles.title: Beyond the Cervix: HPV Vaccine Attitude Profiles and Cancer Prevention Knowledge Gaps Among Vietnamese Medical Students.
articles.journal: Journal of cancer education : the official journal of the American Association for Cancer Education
articles.authors: Luong HT, Nguyen VN, Nguyen TK
articles.abstract: Medical students will be central to communicating human papillomavirus (HPV)-related cancer prevention as Viet Nam introduces HPV vaccination into its national immunization program. This study identified HPV vaccine attitude profiles among Vietnamese medical students, compared their knowledge of HPV-related cancers across profiles, and explored a brief tool to support tailored education. In a cross-sectional survey of 727 medical students conducted in May-June 2026, latent class analysis of 10 attitude items identified four profiles: Comprehensive Trust (25.7%), Selective Trust (29.0%), Passive Acceptance (42.4%), and Hesitant & Skeptical (2.9%). Hesitant & Skeptical students had the lowest HPV and HPV vaccine knowledge, whereas Selective Trust and Passive Acceptance did not differ in any knowledge domain. Across all profiles, knowledge was concentrated on cervical cancer: 79.1% of students recognized HPV as a cause of cervical cancer, compared with 44.0% for penile, 29.6% for anal, and 19.1% for oral cancer, and 25.0% did not recognize that males can be infected. A four-item classification tree reproduced profile membership with 88.9% accuracy (Cohen's κ = 0.83) in a held-out test set, although its sensitivity for the Hesitant & Skeptical profile was 50.0%. Medical students shared a cervix-centered understanding of HPV-related cancer but differed in their attitudes toward vaccination. Medical curricula should teach HPV-related cancers in both sexes to all students and add profile-informed counseling training; the four-item tool may help educators tailor this training but requires external validation.

articles.title: Comprehensive meta-analysis and meta-regression of peripartum cardiomyopathy: risk factors, cardiac function, and maternal-neonatal outcomes in 66,908 PPCM patients.
articles.journal: The Egyptian heart journal : (EHJ) : official bulletin of the Egyptian Society of Cardiology
articles.authors: Zenjaya KT, Christopher C, Timothy RA et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) is a potentially life-threatening condition and often diagnosed late, with many patients presenting in advanced heart failure. This study aimed to examine the demographics, risk factors, comorbidities, clinical characteristics, treatment patterns, and maternal and neonatal outcomes METHODS AND RESULTS: This meta-analysis followed PRISMA guidelines. A total of 4,341 records up to May 2025, were identified and 122 eligible studies reporting PPCM clinical characteristics, treatments, and outcomes were included. Heterogeneity was explored through meta-regression analyses assessing demographic, clinical, and study-level variables. An aggregate of 66,908 PPCM patients were reported across the included studies, with a pooled mean age of 30.1 years. Black or African women accounted for a disproportionately large proportion of the reported population compared with other racial groups. Approximately 62% of women presented with advanced heart failure (NYHA class III/IV). Pre-existing diabetes mellitus (OR 5.09) and hypertensive disorders, including pre-existing hypertension (OR 10.07), gestational hypertension (OR 7.75), and pre-eclampsia (OR 9.27), were associated with higher odds of PPCM. The pooled mean LVEF at diagnosis was 29.98%, which subsequently improved to 46.47% at 6 months and 49.12% at 12 months. Despite over half of PPCM patients achieving LVEF recovery (55%), maternal mortality remained high at 6% and neonatal mortality at 4%. Pharmacological treatments for PPCM varied widely, with high heterogeneity suggesting substantial differences in prescribing practices across studies.
CONCLUSION: The high prevalence of NYHA class III/IV symptoms at diagnosis underscores the importance of early detection and monitoring, while the variation in reported use of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) across studies highlights potential opportunities to optimize treatment in patients with PPCM. The observed improvement in LVEF during follow-up indicates that cardiac recovery is possible in patients with PPCM. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously given the observational nature and substantial heterogeneity of the included studies.

articles.title: Chromosome Y and X dosage in infertile men: associations with reproductive parameters and biological ageing.
articles.authors: Griseta V, Spaggiari G, Sperduti S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Male infertility remains unexplained in up to 50% of cases despite conventional clinical and seminal evaluation. Mosaic loss of chromosome Y (LOY), the most common acquired chromosomal alteration in men, has emerged as a biomarker of genomic instability and biological ageing, but its potential role in male reproductive dysfunction remains poorly understood. This study investigated chromosome Y and X dosage in infertile men using droplet digital polymerase chain reaction (ddPCR).
METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, chromosome Y and X dosage was quantified in peripheral-blood DNA using USP9Y/FSHR and AR/FSHR copy-number ratios. Estimated LOY and LOX percentages were derived from these ratios. Participants were compared within the cohort according to the WHO 6th edition semen reference values. Correlations with clinical, hormonal, testicular, and semen parameters were exploratory, univariate, and unadjusted for multiple testing.
RESULTS: A total of 169 infertile men were enrolled, including 50 (29.6%) without seminal alterations and 119 (70.4%) with at least one abnormal seminal parameter. Neither the USP9Y/FSHR and AR/FSHR copy-number ratios nor the estimated percentages of LOY and LOX differed significantly between the two groups. Mean estimated LOY values remained close to the expected physiological range, indicating no evidence of overt LOY. Weak nominal correlations were observed between estimated LOY and age (ρ = 0.174, p = 0.024), total sperm number (ρ = -0.163, p = 0.034), and prolactin (ρ = -0.167, p = 0.032). Estimated LOX showed no consistent association with the evaluated parameters.
CONCLUSIONS: Overt sex-chromosome loss was not evident in this cohort and chromosome dosage did not distinguish infertile men with abnormal semen parameters from those with reference-range semen parameters. Because no fertile control group was included, the study cannot determine whether sex-chromosome dosage is associated with infertility itself. The weak, unadjusted correlations are exploratory and their clinical relevance is uncertain.

articles.title: Metabolic-reproductive axis in normogonadotropic anovulation: a comparative study of polycystic ovary syndrome and hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian dysfunction.
articles.authors: Brodowicz J, Solnica B, Gawron I
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare hormonal and metabolic profiles in women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian dysfunction (HPOD), with particular emphasis on kisspeptin and ghrelin concentrations and on PCOS subsets characterized by hyperandrogenemia (HA), insulin resistance (IR), and obesity.
METHODS: The prospective study involved women aged 18-45 with menstrual irregularities. Participants underwent gynecological evaluations, including pelvic ultrasound, and biochemical serum analyses to assess hormonal and metabolic parameters.
RESULTS: Kisspeptin (p = 0.003) and ghrelin (p = 0.006) concentrations were significantly higher in PCOS than in HPOD. Distinct hormonal and metabolic profiles characterized PCOS, HPOD, and PCOS phenotypes. In PCOS, kisspeptin concentrations were higher in women with IR (p < 0.001) and HA (p = 0.003), whereas ghrelin concentrations did not differ by IR (p = 0.611) or HA (p = 0.153). Neither kisspeptin (p = 0.428) nor ghrelin (p = 0.240) differed by BMI category. Kisspeptin concentrations were positively correlated with ghrelin, thyroid-stimulating hormone, IR indices, C-reactive protein, and interleukin-6, and negatively with sex hormone-binding globulin and free thyroxine (all p < 0.05). Ghrelin concentrations positively correlated with dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate and negatively with free thyroxine (all p < 0.05). There were fewer significant correlations in HPOD. In multiple regression, ln(IL-6) was an independent positive predictor of ln(kisspeptin) (β = 0.296, p = 0.027) and fT4 a negative predictor (β=-0.059, p = 0.027), while for ln(ghrelin) only 17-OH-progesterone remained a positive independent predictor (β = 0.042, p = 0.019), with metabolic markers losing significance.
CONCLUSIONS: The lack of classical PCOS markers as independent predictors suggests that kisspeptin and ghrelin are regulated by primary inflammatory, thyroidal, and steroidogenic axes, with kisspeptin appearing inflammation-sensitive and ghrelin steroidogenesis-related, supporting a multi-axial model of PCOS.
STUDY REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov(NCT06793098), on January 20, 2025.

articles.title: Modeling the Effects of Hormonal Oral Contraceptive Dosing on Contraceptive Efficacy.
articles.authors: Kim R, Zhao L, Oremland LS et al.
articles.abstract: Examining the impact of oral contraceptive (OC) dosing is important to understand how hormonal contraceptives influence ovulation, the menstrual cycle, and critically, the contraceptive state. In this paper, we develop a mechanistic mathematical model that captures hormone dynamics observed in available data. The model enables us to assess the robustness and effectiveness of various contraceptive dosing regimens, and to evaluate how the dosing strength and the schedule of hormonal OCs affect contraception. Our model incorporates the pharmacokinetics of two exogenous hormones, progestin and ethinyl estradiol (EE). We characterize the impact of dosing schedules (using daily doses with no placebo pills, 24 days of active hormone pills followed by 4 placebo days, or 21 days of active hormone pills followed by 7 placebo days) and dosing strengths on hormonal cycling dynamics. Our results show that with an increasing dose of progestin, the cycle length increases, while increasing the dose of EE removes the periodic behavior completely. We found that the no-placebo dosing schedule shows the most consistent dynamics, while regimens with placebo days had more irregular dynamics. Our model also demonstrates that two theoretical scenarios of individuals with physiologically normal menstrual cycles and the same cycle length may experience different contraceptive efficacy for the same OC dose strength and schedule. Future studies using our model may inform evidence-based dosing protocols and guide clinical decision-making, particularly in the case of missed doses.

articles.title: Markers of Cardiovascular Risk Associated With Pregnancy.
articles.authors: Crooks T, Kondapalli L
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: We sought to provide a brief review of available scores and factors to consider when assessing cardiovascular risk of pregnancy. We also discuss maternal cardiovascular risk stratification of survivors of childhood and adolescent cancer and congenital heart disease and identify gaps in knowledge.
RECENT FINDINGS: The modified WHO 2.0 I-IV in conjunction with the CARPREG II provides the most robust risk score to date but still has shortcomings. No score specifically addresses cardiovascular risk of pregnancy in survivors of cancer. While several tools for assessing risk exist, consideration of patient-specific factors also play an important role. Moderate and high-risk patients may be best cared for by multidisciplinary teams.

articles.title: Whole-exome sequencing identifies known and potential candidate genes in primary amenorrhea with premature ovarian insufficiency.
articles.authors: Kazeminia M, Rahbarian N, Amiri-Yekta A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Premature ovarian insufficiency (POI), characterized by early depletion of the ovarian reserve, affects 3.5-3.7% of women and is a major cause of infertility. It presents as primary or secondary amenorrhea with hypergonadotropic hypogonadism. Genetic factors play a major role, particularly in primary amenorrhea.
METHODS AND RESULTS: Whole-exome sequencing (WES) was performed in seven women with idiopathic POI and primary amenorrhea. Variants were analyzed using two parallel approaches: targeted analysis of 1,163 established and candidate POI genes and an untargeted exome-wide search for additional candidate genes. Selected variants were interpreted according to American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG) guidelines and validated by Sanger sequencing. A likely molecular diagnosis was established in 28.6% (2/7) of cases: a homozygous pathogenic variant in LARS2, an established POI gene, and a homozygous truncating ZSWIM7 variant, in an emerging POI gene, in a patient who also carried a heterozygous likely pathogenic variant in POLG. The ZSWIM7 variant was considered the most plausible explanation for the phenotype. Additional variants of uncertain significance (VUS) were identified in previously reported POI-associated genes (ERCC6, HSF2BP, SOHLH2, and RYR3), while rare variants were identified in preliminary candidate genes (ZP4, ACADVL, CSH1, and RGS22).
CONCLUSIONS: These findings demonstrate the value of WES for the molecular diagnosis of POI, facilitating earlier diagnosis and improved genetic counseling. Further functional and segregation studies are required to establish the pathogenicity of the identified VUS and preliminary candidate genes.

articles.title: Association and limited predictive performance of first-trimester PAPP-A, free β-hCG, and nuchal translucency for adverse neonatal outcomes: Prospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Kumar N, Rathod PT, Bollam M et al.
articles.abstract: BackgroundEarly prediction of adverse neonatal outcomes remains challenging. This study evaluated the associations and predictive performance of first-trimester pregnancy-associated plasma protein-A (PAPP-A), free β-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG), nuchal translucency (NT), and maternal age.MethodsThis prospective cohort enrolled 1244 singleton pregnancies at 11-13 + 6 weeks, with 1229 analyzed after 15 were lost to follow-up. Primary outcome comprised preterm birth, low birth weight, or neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission. Associations were assessed using multivariable logistic regression. Predictive performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis, calibration, decision-curve analysis, and clinical impact curves. Models underwent held-out validation (30%), with additional bootstrap internal validation (1000 resamples) of the combined model.ResultsComposite adverse neonatal outcomes occurred in 469 pregnancies (38.2%). Lower PAPP-A MoM was independently associated with composite outcome (adjusted OR 0.274, 95% CI 0.188-0.399; p < 0.001), particularly low birth weight and NICU admission. In an exploratory model incorporating HDP and SGA, the PAPP-A point estimate reversed direction and became statistically nonsignificant (adjusted OR 1.510, 95% CI 0.942-2.420; p = 0.087), warranting cautious interpretation because of potential downstream adjustment bias. Discrimination for the composite adverse neonatal outcome was limited for PAPP-A alone (AUC 0.620, 95% CI 0.563-0.673) and the combined model (AUC 0.610, 95% CI 0.553-0.665), with no significant improvement following combination (paired DeLong p = 0.315). Bootstrap internal validation yielded an optimism-corrected development-sample AUC of 0.642, whereas the held-out validation AUC was 0.610. Decision-curve findings were exploratory and did not establish clinical benefit. Neither model demonstrated sufficient discrimination for individual-level risk stratification.ConclusionAlthough lower PAPP-A was independently associated with adverse neonatal outcomes, neither PAPP-A alone nor the combined model provided reliable individual-level prediction. Further development and external validation of integrated models are warranted.

articles.title: Factors associated with long-acting reversible contraceptive choice following voluntary termination of pregnancy.
articles.journal: The European journal of contraception & reproductive health care : the official journal of the European Society of Contraception
articles.ta: Eur J Contracept Reprod Health Care
articles.authors: Xu S, Damião SMP, Milhinhos CRF et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To identify sociodemographic, reproductive and healthcare-related factors independently associated with long-acting reversible contraception (LARC) choice following voluntary termination of pregnancy (VTP).
MATERIAL AND METHODS: A retrospective observational study was conducted at a VTP Unit in a Portuguese tertiary-care hospital between January 2025 and January 2026. Variables included age, ethnicity, educational level, occupational status, access to a family physician, attendance at a family planning consultation during the previous year, contraceptive method used before the index pregnancy, parity and previous VTP. The primary outcome was LARC choice following VTP.
RESULTS: Of 1,025 women assessed, 860 were included [median age 27 years (23-32)]; Among these, 482 (56.0%) selected a LARC: 233 (48.3%) chose a 52 mg LNG-IUD, 226 (46.9%) an ENG implant and 23 (4.8%) a Cu-IUD. In the multivariable analysis, younger age, higher parity, and occupational status were independently associated with LARC choice (p < 0.05). Each five-year increase in age was associated with a 24% reduction in the odds of LARC selection (aOR 0.76, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Younger age, higher parity and occupational status were independently associated with LARC choice. These findings may contribute to understanding post-VTP contraceptive patterns and identify areas for further research on contraceptive choice.

articles.title: Risk factors for gestational diabetes in pregnancies resulting from in vitro fertilisation: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Rakhmanova S, Saipova M, Fazliddinova F et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the clinical, metabolic, body-composition and circulating miR-29 correlates of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) in singleton pregnancies conceived after in vitro fertilisation (IVF).
METHODS: This observational cohort study included 210 singleton pregnancies (110 conceived after IVF and 100 conceived spontaneously) managed at a single tertiary centre between January 2022 and December 2024. GDM was defined as the diagnosis recorded in the clinical record and was based on the local 75-g oral glucose tolerance test protocol at 24-28 weeks. Body composition was measured by bioelectrical impedance analysis at 8-12 weeks and whole-blood miR-29a and miR-29b expression at 11-13 weeks by quantitative reverse-transcription PCR, normalised to miR-93-5p. Associations were examined using the chi-square test, Student t test, Pearson correlation, logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic analysis.
RESULTS: GDM occurred in 43 women (20.5%) and was more frequent after IVF than after spontaneous conception (27.3% versus 13.0%; p=0.010). In multivariable analysis, pre-pregnancy obesity (adjusted OR 10.74; 95% CI 3.99-28.94), triglycerides at or above 2.0 mmol/L (6.57; 2.57-16.77), low miR-29a (5.99; 2.41-14.92) and IVF conception (4.19; 1.55-11.36) were independently associated with GDM; the association with polycystic ovary syndrome was borderline (2.69; 0.99-7.30). Women with GDM had higher body fat percentage and visceral fat area (both p<0.001), but body fat percentage was not independent of the other covariates (3.00; 0.90-10.05; p=0.075). miR-29a discriminated GDM with an area under the curve of 0.81 (0.74-0.87).
CONCLUSION: In this cohort, GDM in IVF pregnancies was associated with pre-pregnancy obesity, dyslipidaemia and lower circulating miR-29a expression. Estimates were sensitive to the diagnostic threshold applied and require prospective validation.

articles.title: Intracrinology and tissue-selective effects of tibolone: mechanisms and implications.
articles.journal: Climacteric : the journal of the International Menopause Society
articles.authors: de Melo NR, Schmidt do Prado-Lima PA, Melo Pompei L et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Tibolone is a synthetic steroid widely used for the treatment of menopausal symptoms and prevention of osteoporosis. Unlike conventional menopausal hormone therapy (MHT), tibolone is converted into metabolites with estrogenic, progestogenic and androgenic activity, and their relative availability may differ among tissues. Intracrinology, whereby circulating steroid precursors are locally converted into active hormones or inactive metabolites within target tissues, provides a potential framework for understanding these differential effects. This study aimed to critically examine the intracrinological basis of tibolone pharmacology and assess the extent to which tissue-specific metabolism may contribute to its differential clinical effects across estrogen-sensitive tissues.
METHOD: A critical narrative review of experimental studies, randomized clinical trials and systematic reviews was conducted to evaluate tibolone metabolism and the distribution and activity of its metabolites in major target tissues, including breast, uterus, vagina, brain and bone.
RESULTS: Tibolone acts predominantly as a prodrug and is converted into three active metabolites: the estrogenic compounds 3α-hydroxytibolone and 3β-hydroxytibolone, and the Δ4-isomer, which has progestogenic and androgenic properties. Experimental evidence indicates that tissue-specific differences in enzyme expression, sulfation, desulfation and possibly membrane transport may influence the local balance and availability of these metabolites. In breast and uterine tissues, preclinical studies suggest a predominance of sulfated metabolites, a pattern compatible with comparatively limited availability of unconjugated estrogenic metabolites. In bone and vaginal tissue, clinical benefits are compatible with sufficient local or systemic estrogenic activity. Evidence relating intracrinology to effects in the central nervous system remains limited and largely indirect. Across tissues, clinical outcomes are influenced by population characteristics, underlying pathology, dose and concomitant treatment, and do not directly establish the proposed…
CONCLUSION: Intracrinology provides a biologically plausible framework for understanding the tissue-selective effects of tibolone. However, clinical findings are largely compatible with, rather than confirmatory of, this mechanism, and the balance of benefits and risks appears to vary according to tissue, clinical context and individual patient characteristics.

articles.title: Pravastatin improves uterine and carotid artery function through vascular bed-specific mechanisms in a rat model of excessive hypercholesterolemia in pregnancy.
articles.authors: de Oliveira AA, Graton ME, Spaans F et al.
articles.abstract: Excessive hypercholesterolemia (eHC) in pregnancy is a risk factor for adverse outcomes, including preeclampsia; however, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Uterine artery endothelial dysfunction in eHC is mediated by activation of the toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)/lectin-like oxidized LDL receptor-1 (LOX-1)/prostaglandin H synthase 1 (PGHS1) pathway. Pravastatin, a cholesterol-lowering drug, reduces the incidence of preeclampsia in high-risk pregnancies due to its pleiotropic effects. Outside of pregnancy, the pleiotropic effects include suppression of TLR4 and LOX-1 signaling. Whether pravastatin improves uterine artery endothelial function in eHC via inhibition of TLR4/LOX-1 is not known. We hypothesized that pravastatin suppresses TLR4/LOX-1 signaling, thereby improving uterine artery endothelial function in eHC pregnancies. Sprague Dawley rats were fed either a control diet or a high cholesterol diet from gestational day (GD) 6-20 and treated with vehicle or pravastatin (5 mg/kg/day) from GD10-20. On GD20, pregnancy outcomes were assessed, and endothelial function in uterine and carotid (a systemic vascular bed that is dysfunctional in postpartum eHC dams) arteries was evaluated using wire myography. In uterine arteries, pravastatin improved blood flow and endothelial function mainly via suppression of TLR4, while also increasing nitric oxide-mediated vasodilation. In carotid arteries, endothelial function was unchanged; however, functional responses to NOS inhibition suggested reduced NO contribution to vasodilation in eHC vehicle-treated dams, accompanied by increased reliance on PGHS2, both of which were normalized in pravastatin-treated dams. These findings demonstrate that pravastatin exerts vascular bed-specific effects and suggest that its use during pregnancy can improve maternal vascular function in eHC pregnancies.

articles.title: Fragment End Motif Analysis of Microbial Cell-Free DNA Improves Detection of Pathogens over Noise from Contaminants and Commensals.
articles.authors: Zhang H, Dominguez EG, Junak M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Circulating plasma microbial DNA (mDNA) is a promising biomarker for sepsis, but its accuracy is hindered by the low abundance of pathogen DNA and the presence of contaminants and commensals. mDNA enrichment using a selection of short fragments and single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) library preparation can improve pathogen yield but also increases background noise. Since nucleotide representation at mDNA fragment ends is biased by enzymatic digestion in vivo, we hypothesized that analysis of 5' and 3' mDNA fragment end motifs in enriched ssDNA libraries could improve pathogen detection.
METHODS: We performed deep metagenomic sequencing of size-selected ssDNA libraries from 38 plasma samples, including 20 samples from 5 sepsis patients, 18 samples from 6 patients without infection, and 6 no-template controls. Across these samples, we compared observed-to-expected ratios for end motifs in mDNA fragments from candidate pathogens and contaminants. For each candidate pathogen, we evaluated the accuracy of combining end motifs with microbial abundance for detection of infection.
RESULTS: mDNA fragments from infection-causing pathogens were biased in the nucleotide motifs at both fragment ends compared with contaminants, with the highest enrichment observed in the GG dinucleotide at the 3' end (P < 0.0001). Integrating microbial abundance with end motif features improved differentiation between clinically significant pathogens and corresponding noise from the same microbes in noninfection samples. For Staphylococcus infections, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve for the combination model was higher than than that for microbial abundance alone (0.892 vs 0.431, respectively; P = 0.018).
CONCLUSIONS: mDNA end motif analysis improves signal-to-noise ratio beyond microbial abundance alone and improves pathogen detection in plasma metagenomic sequencing.

articles.title: Urine as a liquid allograft biopsy: emerging technologies for noninvasive monitoring in kidney transplantation.
articles.journal: Current opinion in nephrology and hypertension
articles.authors: El Fekih R, Akalin E
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Long-term kidney allograft survival remains limited by immune and nonimmune injury, while conventional surveillance tools are constrained by delayed detection, limited specificity, or invasiveness. Urine provides an accessible window into the allograft, containing inflammatory mediators, cells, extracellular vesicles, nucleic acids, proteins, peptides, and metabolites reflecting intra-graft processes.
RECENT FINDINGS: Over the past two decades, urinary biomarkers have evolved from single-analyte discovery to molecular signatures matched to kidney biopsy findings. Urinary CXCL9/CXCL10, urinary-cell mRNA, extracellular-vesicle transcriptomics, donor-derived cell-free DNA, proteomics, and metabolomics provide complementary measures of allograft injury and have demonstrated encouraging diagnostic performance. Although some remain limited by variable specificity, analytical standardization, reproducibility, or insufficient prospective validation, others have undergone multicenter validation, assay standardization, and progression toward clinical implementation.
SUMMARY: Urinary biomarkers are unlikely to replace biopsy with a single universal test. Their greatest potential lies in context-specific applications, including risk stratification, surveillance, biopsy triage, differential diagnosis, prognostication, and treatment-response monitoring. High negative predictive value across several platforms may support reducing unnecessary biopsies. Clinical translation will depend on standardized, transferable assays, external validation in representative populations, clearly defined contexts of use, and evidence that biomarker-guided strategies improve patient and allograft outcomes.

articles.title: Birth and long-term health outcomes of intrauterine offspring after local methotrexate treatment for heterotopic pregnancy: A retrospective study and focused literature review.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Chen Q, Wan S, Li Q et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To report birth outcomes and long-term intellectual and physical development follow-up data of intrauterine offspring after local methotrexate (MTX) injection for heterotopic pregnancy (HP), and to summarize relevant published cases.
METHODS: We included 29 patients with HP involving uncommon ectopic implantation sites who underwent transvaginal ultrasound-guided local MTX injection to treat the ectopic gestation (2006-2023). We evaluated birth outcomes and the intellectual and physical development in offspring aged 4-17 years, and conducted a focused review of published cases from 1990 to 2025 via PubMed.
RESULTS: Pregnancy outcomes were available for 27 of 29 patients. Twenty-four women delivered 26 live-born offspring, including 23 without and three with congenital anomalies (congenital heart disease, hypospadias, and multiple craniofacial and limb abnormalities, respectively). Matched comparative analyses included 11 preschool-aged, eight school-aged, and seven adolescent offspring. Across the cognitive, anthropometric, blood pressure, and laboratory outcomes assessed, three between-group differences showed nominal P-values of below 0.05, involving preschool uric acid, school-age systolic blood pressure, and adolescent blood urea nitrogen. Among these, the systolic blood pressure difference was accompanied by high-normal blood pressure or hypertension in some offspring in the MTX group. None of the three differences remained statistically significant after Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction. After the exclusion of overlapping observations, the focused literature review identified 14 independent live-born offspring from previously reported cases, of whom two had congenital anomalies.
CONCLUSION: Most live-born offspring following local MTX treatment for HP had no congenital anomalies, and no long-term offspring outcome comparison remained statistically significant after FDR correction. However, congenital anomalies were reported in both our cohort and the published literature, and the small sample size and limited evidence preclude firm conclusions regarding long-term safety.

articles.title: High-throughput simultaneous determination of 51 herbicide residues in drinking water by online solid-phase extraction coupled with ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry.
articles.journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
articles.authors: Zhong Z, Wang K, Lin Q et al.
articles.abstract: An online solid-phase extraction coupled with ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (online SPE-UPLC-MS/MS) method was developed for the simultaneous determination of 51 herbicides, including triazines, sulfonylureas, amides, and phenylureas, in drinking water. Water samples were filtered through a 0.22 µm hydrophilic polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) membrane, adjusted to pH 6, enriched on an Oasis hydrophilic-lipophilic balance (HLB) online solid-phase extraction (SPE) column with 0.1% formic acid in water as the loading solution, and separated on an ACQUITY UPLC HSS T3 column using 0.1% formic acid in water-acetonitrile. Detection was performed in positive electrospray ionization (ESI+) and multiple reaction monitoring (MRM) mode. The method showed good linearity for all analytes, with correlation coefficients greater than 0.995. The limits of detection and quantification were 0.146-0.833 ng L-1 and 0.487-2.778 ng L-1, respectively. Mean recoveries at 5, 10, and 50 ng L-1 ranged from 68.0% to 118.9%, with intra-day and inter-day RSDs of 0.2-9.5% and 1.0-19.9%, respectively. Matrix effects were weak for forty-seven compounds, moderate for three, and strong for one. The method was successfully applied to 84 real samples from 28 water treatment plants in southeastern China. Overall detection rates decreased from raw water to finished water and tap water, with triazines and amides as the predominant detected classes. This analytical method provides reliable technical support for drinking water quality surveillance and health risk assessment.

articles.title: TMEFF2 is associated with trophoblast dysfunction in missed abortion.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Liu J, Zhang P, Li J et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Missed abortion (MA) is a common complication of early pregnancy, and its pathogenesis remains incompletely understood. Abnormal trophoblast proliferation and migration are associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, including MA. This study aimed to compare TMEFF2 expression in chorionic villous tissue between women with MA and those with normal early pregnancy and to evaluate the association between TMEFF2 and proliferation-related metabolic activity and migration in HTR-8/SVneo cells.
METHODS: The study included 21 women with MA and 21 women with normal early pregnancy. Hematoxylin and eosin staining was performed to evaluate the histomorphological features of chorionic villi. TMEFF2 expression was evaluated by immunohistochemistry and Western blotting. In HTR-8/SVneo cells, TMEFF2 was overexpressed or knocked down, and changes in TMEFF2 expression were assessed by real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction and Western blotting. Cell Counting Kit-8, wound-healing, and Transwell migration assays were used to assess proliferation-related metabolic activity and migration.
RESULTS: TMEFF2 expression was significantly higher in the chorionic villous tissue from women with MA than in tissue from controls. In HTR-8/SVneo cells, TMEFF2 overexpression was associated with reduced proliferation-related metabolic activity and migration, whereas TMEFF2 knockdown showed the opposite pattern.
CONCLUSION: TMEFF2 is upregulated in chorionic villous tissue from women with MA and is associated with reduced proliferation-related metabolic activity and migration in HTR-8/SVneo cells in vitro. These findings provide preliminary evidence of an association between TMEFF2 and MA.

articles.title: Utility of Artificial Intelligence in Diagnosing Image-Based Vaginal Pathology.
articles.authors: Shekar A, Shalom DF, Reddy M et al.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Artificial intelligence (AI) tools are increasingly used by patients for health-related concerns before formal medical evaluation. However, data evaluating the diagnostic performance of these AI models for vaginal pathology are limited.
OBJECTIVES: The objectives of this study were to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of publicly available AI models for image-based identification of vaginal pathology and compare their performance with expert physician review.
STUDY DESIGN: This diagnostic‑accuracy study assessed 25 deidentified clinical images representing various vaginal conditions. Four publicly accessible AI models (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, and Grok) and 2 board-certified urogynecology and reconstructive pelvic surgery physicians independently provided top 3 and top 1 diagnoses, malignancy identification, diagnostic confidence (0-100%), and triage recommendations using a standardized prompt.
RESULTS: Experts achieved top 3 diagnostic accuracy of 84% and top 1 accuracy of 66%. AI systems demonstrated variable performance, with mean top 3 accuracy of 51.8% and a mean top 1 accuracy of 32.5%. ChatGPT and Gemini achieved the highest AI performance (68% and 68% top 3 accuracy; 44% and 52% top 1 accuracy, respectively). In malignant cases (n=3), the correct diagnosis was included in the top 3 in 83.5% of evaluations across both groups, with AI slightly more likely to rank malignancy first. AI systems recommended urgent evaluation more frequently than experts (77% vs 22%).
CONCLUSIONS: Publicly available AI models demonstrate moderate accuracy in identifying vaginal pathology from images but perform below expert clinicians. While some models approach expert performance in detecting malignancy, they tend to over-recommend urgent care, highlighting a limited but evolving role for patient-facing AI in image-based triage.

articles.title: Data Sharing in Autism Research: Case Studies From the United States and the United Kingdom and Recommendations for Practice.
articles.journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
articles.authors: Grant A, Ellis R, Axbey H et al.
articles.abstract: Data sharing has become common in Autism research. In the context of a history of eugenics, additional risks are present, including re-identification, misinterpretation and deficit-framing of Autism. We, a group of community members and researchers, aimed to (a) describe our 'opt-in' data-sharing approach in two Community-Based Participatory Research studies based in the United States (AASPIRE Outcomes Project) and the United Kingdom (Autism from Menstruation to Menopause; AM2M), (b) report on how many people opted to data share and (c) co-develop recommendations for ethical data sharing in Autism research. In the AASPIRE Outcomes Project, 680 of 870 (78.2%) participants opted to share quantitative survey data, with no differences by demographic, disability, or health characteristics. In AM2M, 36 of 100 (36.0%) participants opted to share longitudinal qualitative data, with significant variation when controlling for family-wise error rate by menopause status (p = .007). We provide recommendations for ethical data sharing in Autism research, directed at governments, policy makers, research funders, data repositories, ethics boards and researchers. We favour approaches that centre autonomy and dignity, including, 'opt-in' data-sharing consent models and Autistic community participation. We hope that these recommendations will balance data-sharing benefits with strong protections for Autistic research participants.Lay AbstractData sharing is when people's information from a study are anonymised (names taken out) and shared in an online library. Other researchers can use this data to answer new research questions at reduced cost.Some funders say researchers must share data. However, some Autistic people worry this could be bad for Autistic people. One solution is letting research participants decide if they want to share their answers. This is called 'opt-in' data sharing.We are a neurodiverse group of Autism researchers and community members. We had three goals:1. Share how we handled data sharing in studies in the United States and the United Kingdom;2. Say how many people agreed to data share3. Make recommendations for ethical data sharing in Autism research.We had concerns about data sharing, including not keeping participants' identities private and researchers doing studies that were dehumanising or used deficit views of Autism. For this reason, the U.S. study decided not to share interview data, and both studies used separate data-sharing information…

articles.title: Oral-gut-vaginal microbiota crosstalk with host immunity and metabolism in pregnancy disorders.
articles.authors: Ge Y, Weng H, Chen G et al.
articles.abstract: Pregnancy represents a critical stage in which both maternal and fetal health are of paramount importance. This review systematically examines the temporal dynamics of maternal microbial communities across multiple anatomical niches-including the vaginal, intestinal, and oral ecosystems-during pregnancy, and explores their profound connections with gestational health. We highlight the specific associations between site-specific microbial dysbiosis and adverse outcomes such as preterm birth, gestational diabetes, and preeclampsia. In addition, we delineate the mechanisms by which the immune microenvironment at the maternal-fetal interface maintains dynamic equilibrium under microbial regulation, and underscores the role of microbial metabolites as transgenerational signaling molecules critical for fetal development. Furthermore, we dissect the pathological disruption of the "microbiota-immune-metabolism" network in pregnancy-related disorders and evaluate the potential of targeted strategies-including probiotic supplementation and nutritional interventions-to restore microbial homeostasis and improve maternal and neonatal outcomes. Finally, we emphasize the contribution of breast milk microbiota and immune components to offspring immune programming and outline future translational research directions, aiming to provide a scientific foundation for microbiota-based monitoring and early intervention in pregnancy health.

articles.title: Comparative performance of three HPV DNA detection assays for cervical cancer screening in Algeria.
articles.authors: Masdoua N, Boublenza L, Zatla I et al.
articles.abstract: Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) is the principal etiological driver of cervical cancer, making accurate HPV detection central to contemporary screening strategies. This study compared three molecular assays-INNO-LiPA HPV Genotyping Extra, Cobas 4800 HPV, and Amplicor HPV-using overlapping cervical-sample subsets from Algerian women at increased risk of cervical disease. Among the 94 specimens tested by both INNO-LiPA and Cobas, HR-HPV was detected in 54.3% and 29.8%, respectively; INNO-LiPA also identified HPV16 and HPV18 more frequently. In the 18-specimen subset tested by all three assays, HR-HPV positivity was 27.8% with INNO-LiPA, 33.3% with Cobas, and 50.0% with Amplicor. Pairwise agreement ranged from weak to substantial (κ=0.116-0.667), and discordance was significantly associated with multiple HPV infections (OR=5.88, 95% CI 1.29-26.85; p=0.012). HR-HPV positivity was more frequent in specimens with abnormal cytology, with the strongest association observed for INNO-LiPA (OR=4.9, 95% CI 1.5-15.9; p=0.005). Using the study-defined composite reference classification, INNO-LiPA showed higher sensitivity (93%) but lower specificity (62%) than Cobas (71% and 88%, respectively). These findings demonstrate substantial assay-dependent variation in HR-HPV detection and highlight the value of detailed genotyping for epidemiological investigation, while supporting the use of clinically validated HR-HPV assays for screening applications.

articles.title: The impact of parity on postpartum recovery and perinatal outcomes among obese women.
articles.authors: Elçin AB, Çakır D
articles.abstract: Maternal obesity is associated with adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes and may affect postpartum recovery; however, the role of parity remains unclear. This study evaluated the relationship between maternal and neonatal outcomes and postpartum recovery quality by parity in obese women. This descriptive and correlational study included 128 women (64 primiparous, 64 multiparous) with body mass index ≥30 kg/m². Data were collected using standardized forms and the Obstetric Quality of Recovery Scale. No significant difference was found between groups in total recovery scores (p>0.05), although multiparous women had higher scores in current recovery perception (p<0.05). Mode of delivery, neonatal intensive care unit admission, and oxygen requirement were associated with recovery outcomes. Regular antenatal care was identified as a significant predictor, although the regression model explained only a limited proportion of the variance. Parity was not an independent determinant of overall recovery; maternal and neonatal factors appear to play a more important role. L'obésité maternelle est associée à des issues maternelles et néonatales défavorables et peut affecter la récupération post-partum ; toutefois, le rôle de la parité reste incertain. Cette étude a évalué la relation entre les issues maternelles et néonatales et la qualité de la récupération post-partum en fonction de la parité chez les femmes obèses. Cette étude descriptive et corrélationnelle a inclus 128 femmes (64 primipares, 64 multipares) présentant un indice de masse corporelle ≥ 30 kg/m². Les données ont été recueillies à l'aide de formulaires standardisés et de l'échelle de qualité de la récupération obstétricale. Aucune différence significative n'a été observée entre les groupes concernant les scores totaux de récupération (p > 0,05), bien que les femmes multipares aient obtenu des scores plus élevés concernant leur perception de la récupération actuelle (p < 0,05). Le mode d'accouchement, l'admission en unité de soins intensifs néonatals et les besoins en oxygène étaient associés aux issues de récupération. Un suivi prénatal régulier a été identifié comme un facteur prédictif significatif, bien que le modèle de régression n'explique qu'une faible proportion de la variance. La parité n'était pas un déterminant indépendant de la récupération globale; les facteurs maternels et néonataux semblent jouer un rôle plus important.

articles.title: Interventions to prevent suicide and suicidal thoughts or behaviours in the perinatal period: a global mixed-methods systematic review.
articles.authors: Fernandez Turienzo C, Erpolat YD, De Backer K et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Suicide is a leading cause of maternal death during the perinatal period. While routine enquiry and identification is widely recommended, evidence on comprehensive interventions remains limited. This review evaluated global evidence on the effectiveness of interventions for perinatal suicide, associated thoughts and behaviours, and key implementation features.
METHODS: We conducted a mixed-methods systematic review using the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology. We searched eight databases and other sources from inception to December 3, 2025, for global evidence across all income settings without language restrictions. We included studies evaluating interventions, programmes or strategies reporting on our primary outcome: perinatal suicide or suicidal thoughts or behaviours (including ideation, self-harm, attempts) during pregnancy or one year after birth. Data were extracted and appraised for methodological quality. Meta-analysis was not possible due to clinical and methodological heterogeneity; data were synthesised using a convergent integrated approach. PROSPERO: CRD42025625903.
FINDINGS: We screened 27,045 records; 19 records representing nine studies were included: three randomised controlled trials, one secondary analysis of a randomised controlled trial, one non-randomised controlled trial, one quasi-experimental study, one cross-sectional descriptive study, one economic modelling, and one qualitative study. Studies were conducted between 2011 and 2025 in North America, Europe and Asia and included 3613 participants from at risk or disadvantaged populations across eight studies, plus a simulated cohort of 1000. We found trials of indirect clinical interventions targeting parenting or attachment did not reduce suicidality, whereas task-shared behavioural activation psychotherapy targeting depressive drivers, was associated with an 80% reduction in odds of suicidal ideation at three months in a secondary trial analysis. System or community-level strategies in three trials and the modelling were associated with reduced suicide or suicidal ideation by integrating routine screening within multidisciplinary pathways that ensured immediate linkage to care. Informal or crisis support mechanisms facilitated immediate access and worked as protective buffers against self-harm in two feasibility and qualitative studies; faith practices helped counter barriers to formal care while…
FUNDING: The National Institute for Health and Care Research.

articles.title: Maternal and neonatal outcomes of Kielland's rotational forceps-assisted vaginal births in a tertiary care center.
articles.authors: Naseef P, Leps C, Almoi E et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rates of second-stage Cesarean section (CS) have increased substantially, contributing to higher maternal morbidity and long-term risks in future pregnancies, including repeat CS and placenta accreta spectrum. Reducing unnecessary second-stage CS is therefore an important goal in modern obstetric care. Fetal malposition, particularly occiput transverse and posterior positions, is a key cause of labor dystocia and operative delivery. While several interventions exist, their success is variable. Kielland's rotational forceps can facilitate vaginal birth and potentially avoid CS, but their use has declined due to safety concerns and limited training, leaving a gap in contemporary evidence comparing outcomes with other delivery methods.
OBJECTIVE: To compare maternal and neonatal outcomes between rotational and nonrotational forceps use in a tertiary care setting.
STUDY DESIGN: A retrospective cohort study was conducted of all forceps-assisted births at a tertiary care hospital in Toronto, between January 2014 and December 2021. Maternal outcomes included postpartum hemorrhage defined as estimated blood loss of 500 mL or more, and significant obstetric anal sphincter injuries defined as 3B, 3C and fourth degree perineal lacerations. Neonatal outcomes included Apgar scores, cord blood gases, need for resuscitation, and neonatal head trauma.
RESULTS: Among 1606 forceps-assisted births, 26 (1.6%) required Kielland's rotational forceps. Episiotomy was universal in the rotational group (n=26/26, 100%) compared with 90.1% (n=1423/1580) in the nonrotational group. Significant OASIS occurred less frequently with rotational forceps (7.6%, n=2/26 vs 10.8%, n=172/1580), while rates of PPH were comparable (26.9%, n=7/26 vs 28.8%, n=456/1580). No major PPH (≥1000 mL) or shoulder dystocia occurred in the rotational group. Low 1-minute Apgar scores (<7) were more common in the rotational group (26.9%, n=7/26 vs 14%, n=227/1580), but all infants achieved scores ≥7 at 5 minutes. No cases of cephalohematoma, subgaleal hematoma, or intracranial hemorrhage occurred in the…
CONCLUSION: Kielland's rotational forceps are a safe alternative to second-stage CS when performed by experienced operators. Their use was not associated with excess major maternal morbidity or significant neonatal trauma, in comparison to nonrotational forceps. Our data support efforts to transfer these skills to trainees and larger studies are needed to confirm these single institution findings.

articles.title: Fluctuating Methylation-based ctDNA Detection in NSCLC Surveillance: Implications for Serial Monitoring and Specificity.
articles.authors: Cho JM, Clark G, Bogardus M et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) addresses key limitations of traditional radiographic and tissue-based screening by providing a noninvasive alternative for the surveillance of NSCLC. In our study, we aim to evaluate trends in the performance of a commercially available methylation-based ctDNA test, characterize patient factors associated with fluctuating ctDNA positivity, and evaluate the clinical implications of serial monitoring.
METHODS: This retrospective observational cohort study included patients who underwent lung resection or stereotactic body radiation therapy for NSCLC followed by posttreatment ctDNA testing from 2024 to 2025. The primary outcomes include patient- and tumor-related risk factors associated with ctDNA positivity. A subgroup analysis of the ctDNA-positive group evaluated clinical events and genomic profiling that may influence transient ctDNA positivity.
RESULTS: Of the 85 patients studied, 17 (20%) had at least one positive ctDNA test. Both ctDNA-positive and negative groups had similar patient and tumor-related features. Ten (59%) patients with a positive result subsequently tested negative, and 11 (65%) had a ctDNA tumor fraction near the limit of detection (LOD) without radiographic recurrence. No consistent associations were found with timing, adjuvant therapy, inflammatory markers, or tumor genomics. Three patients with ctDNA fractions above the limit of detection had confirmed recurrence; none in the ctDNA-negative group had disease recurrence.
CONCLUSIONS: Although the utility of serial ctDNA testing is promising for NSCLC surveillance, isolated low-level positivity may not warrant clinical action. We observe frequent low-level, transient ctDNA positivity without radiographic evidence of recurrence, suggesting limitations in assay specificity and need for trend-based interpretation instead of isolated testing.

articles.title: Personalizing postpartum cardiovascular prevention after preeclampsia: Is routine statin therapy justified in normotensive survivors? A critical narrative review.
articles.journal: International journal of cardiology. Cardiovascular risk and prevention
articles.ta: Int J Cardiol Cardiovasc Risk Prev
articles.authors: Naja S
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preeclampsia is a pregnancy-related cardiovascular risk-enhancing factor associated with increased lifetime cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk. However, long-term cardiovascular risk varies according to postpartum blood pressure, metabolic health, and development of conventional cardiovascular risk factors.
CURRENT CLINICAL RECOMMENDATIONS: Current guidelines recognize preeclampsia as a risk-enhancing factor to support cardiovascular risk assessment and shared decision-making regarding lipid-lowering therapy. However, preeclampsia alone is not an indication for routine statin therapy, and no postpartum low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) target is recommended solely on the basis of previous preeclampsia.
EVIDENCE GAP: Existing evidence is derived mainly from observational studies involving heterogeneous populations. Few studies have evaluated women who remain normotensive with favorable metabolic profiles, and no completed randomized trial has demonstrated that postpartum statin therapy improves long-term cardiovascular outcomes.
MAIN ARGUMENT: Lifelong cardiovascular surveillance is warranted after preeclampsia, but routine statin therapy for all survivors is not supported. Lipid-lowering therapy should be individualized according to overall cardiovascular risk.
FUTURE DIRECTIONS: Future studies should identify high-risk phenotypes, validate postpartum risk prediction tools such as PREVENT, and determine whether selected women benefit from targeted statin therapy.

articles.title: Changing Global Modelled Excess Incidence of Type 2 Diabetes Among Women with Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome, 1990-2023: A Risk-Translation Study.
articles.authors: Miao P, Jin Y, Lu J
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To estimate modelled excess type 2 diabetes (T2D) incidence associated with polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), previously termed polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), examine benchmark-year changes and geographic heterogeneity, and assess dependence on transported cohort associations.
METHODS: Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 inputs for women aged 20-49 years in 204 locations were combined with a US BMI-matched/adjusted hazard ratio (HR) of 1.47 and a baseline prevalence-allocation odds ratio of 2.41. Fixed risk parameters were applied to six benchmark years during 1990-2023, with five-factor Shapley decomposition. Conditional model uncertainty intervals (MUIs) used 10,000 Monte Carlo draws; alternative cohort effects, input dependence and exclusion of ages 20-24 were examined separately.
RESULTS: The 2023 country-age model estimated 78,075 annual excess cases (95% conditional MUI 67,645-88,983), or 15.3 per 10,000 T2D-free women with PMOS. This interval is conditional on the selected US source-effect distribution and simulation assumptions; it excludes between-cohort structural uncertainty. Excluding ages 20-24 yielded 69,070 cases (59,711-78,948). Benchmark estimates increased from 27,950 cases in 1990 to 77,874 in 2023, a 178.6% increase. Population growth and background T2D incidence accounted for 41.3% and 34.9% of the modelled net increase. Alternative cohort HRs generated 78,075-345,335 cases, while globally shared input ranks widened the primary-source MUI to 46,444-122,357.
CONCLUSION: These conditional risk-translation scenarios describe how population inputs and selected BMI-matched/adjusted associations generate excess T2D incidence. They do not identify the total PMOS-associated burden across adiposity pathways or causally attributable events. Geographical variation and effect uncertainty require local calibration before surveillance or prevention applications.

articles.title: Effect of group-based training interventions on mothers' knowledge about menstruation in the selected districts of Jimma zone: A controlled quasi-experimental study.
articles.authors: Olika AK, Debelew GT, Birhanu Z et al.
articles.abstract: Menstrual health plays an important role in adolescent development; however, many girls in resource-constrained settings enter menarche with inadequate knowledge due to restricted access to information and the influence of prevailing social and cultural norms. Strengthening mothers' knowledge may provide an indirect but effective approach for improving menstrual awareness among adolescent girls. In Ethiopia, little evidence exists regarding interventions specifically designed to improve maternal knowledge of menstruation. This study therefore assessed the impact of group-based training on mothers' knowledge, aiming to enhance understanding and dispel misconceptions. A quasi-experimental controlled study was conducted in Omo Nada and Shabe Sombo districts of Jimma Zone, Ethiopia, among 390 mothers of adolescent girls aged 10 to 19 years. One district received the intervention, while the other served as a comparison area. The intervention group participated in six structured sessions on menstrual health and hygiene, whereas the comparison group received routine health education. Data were collected using pre-tested questionnaires at baseline and endline and analyzed using multilevel mixed-effects logistic regression models to account for clustering within villages and kebeles. Following the intervention, the proportion of mothers with adequate menstrual knowledge increased from 46.7% to 99.5% in the intervention group. After adjusting for potential confounders and clustering effects, mothers in the intervention area were more than seven times as likely to have adequate menstrual knowledge compared with those in the comparison area (AOR = 7.55, 95% CI: 4.69-12.16). The findings suggest that a group-based, mother-focused educational intervention was associated with substantial improvements in maternal knowledge of menstruation. Such interventions may contribute to improving menstrual health literacy among mothers and, ultimately, support better menstrual health outcomes for adolescent girls.

articles.title: Uniform PLGA Nanorods Loaded with Curcumin: Statistical Optimization, Cellular Cytotoxicity and in vivo Pharmacokinetics.
articles.authors: Liu L, Liao Z, Liu H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Curcumin (CUR), a promising natural anticancer agent, faces challenges in clinical application due to poor water solubility, instability, and low bioavailability. Encapsulating CUR in biodegradable poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) nanoparticles can overcome these limitations. Although physicochemical properties of nanoparticles have crucial effects on drug fate in vivo, the role of particle shape remains understudied due to the difficulty in preparing non-spherical drug-loaded polymeric particles, especially in the nanosized range.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to prepare uniform CUR-loaded PLGA nanoparticles with spherical shape (CUR-NSs) and rod shape (CUR-NRs) using the two-step premix membrane emulsification technique, and to investigate the influence of particle shape on drug release, blood biocompatibility, cellular uptake, tumor cytotoxicity, and in vivo pharmacokinetics.
METHODS: An orthogonal experimental design was utilized to optimize the formulation to obtain uniform rod-shaped nanoparticles with high degree of deformation. Particle morphology and size were characterized by scanning electron microscopy, while drug loading and encapsulation efficiency were determined by high-performance liquid chromatography. In vitro drug release and blood biocompatibility were evaluated by dynamic dialysis and hemolysis assay, respectively. Cellular uptake was evaluated by confocal laser scanning microscopy and flow cytometry, while cytotoxicity was assessed using the MTT assay. Finally, the in vivo pharmacokinetic behavior of CUR-NSs and CUR-NRs was investigated in Sprague-Dawley rats following intravenous administration.
RESULTS: Orthogonal optimization enabled successful preparation of CUR-NRs with a high aspect ratio and nanoscale minor axis. Both CUR-NSs and CUR-NRs showed sustained release of CUR and low hemolytic activity. At the cellular level, CUR-NSs exhibited enhanced cellular uptake and stronger cytotoxicity against ID8 ovarian cancer cells. However, following intravenous administration, CUR-NRs significantly prolonged systemic circulation and improved CUR bioavailability, with an area under the concentration-time curve (AUC) of 1403.63 ± 223.53 μg/L·min, approximately 9.8-fold…
CONCLUSION: This study provides a foundation for developing CUR-loaded PLGA nanorods as effective delivery vehicles, highlighting that nanoparticle shape is a critical parameter that should be fully considered in the rational design of drug delivery systems.

articles.title: Management of a Tubo-Ovarian Abscess: A Single-Centre Retrospective Cohort Study of Clinical Outcomes and Factors Associated With Failure of First-Line Medical Therapy.
articles.authors: Satouf A
articles.abstract:
