OBJECTIVE: To describe the clinical characteristics, antibiotic management, and outcomes of a consecutive cohort of women admitted with tubo-ovarian abscess (TOA) and to determine the factors associated with failure of first-line medical therapy.
DESIGN AND SETTING: This is a retrospective cohort study, with the setting of the Gynaecology Department at the University Hospitals of Leicester, United Kingdom.
POPULATION: A total of 61 women who had a working diagnosis of TOA were identified during the study period; 14 (23%) were excluded when an alternative final diagnosis was made, and a further three women were excluded due to incomplete outcome documentation, so 44 women with a confirmed diagnosis of TOA remained for analysis.
METHODS: Demographic data, together with the microbiological, radiological, antibiotic, and procedural data, were systematically extracted from clinical records and coded. The outcomes were compared between women whose abscess resolved with antibiotics alone and those who required radiological or surgical drainage, using Fisher's exact test for categorical variables and the Mann-Whitney U test for continuous variables.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: These are the success of first-line antibiotic therapy, need for image-guided or surgical drainage, and length of hospital stay (LOS).
RESULTS: Median age was 41 years (IQR: 33.5-51), and median BMI was 28 kg/m² (IQR: 24-32.5). Among the 44 women with complete documented treatment outcomes, antibiotics alone were successful in 31 (70.5%), while 13 (29.5%) required further treatment with image-guided drainage or surgery. Procedures included image-guided drainage (n = 2), laparoscopic drainage or definitive laparoscopic surgery (n = 5), laparoscopic surgery converted to laparotomy (n = 3), and primary laparotomy (n = 3). A prior history of pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) (62% vs 3%, p < 0.001), previous admission with TOA (46% vs 13%, p = 0.043), and an abscess diameter >6.5 cm (64% vs 25%, p = 0.033) were each significantly more common among women whose medical management failed. LOS…
CONCLUSIONS: First-line antibiotic therapy resolved TOA in approximately 7 of 10 women with a documented treatment outcome in this cohort, which is in keeping with contemporary published series. Recurrent disease, a prior history of PID, and larger abscess diameter identify women at higher risk of failing medical therapy and may help target earlier senior/multidisciplinary review and consideration of early drainage.

articles.title: Beyond Layer Count at Caesarean Delivery: A Focused Clinical Review and Trial-Design Framework for Endometrium-Sparing Uterine Closure.
articles.authors: Puttakul W, Kantathavorn N, Chotichavanrattanakun K et al.
articles.abstract: Debate about uterine closure at Caesarean delivery often centers on layer count, although scar healing also depends on tissue handling, suture technique and material, operative context, and maternal factors. Layers describe anatomical repair planes, not the number of individual stitches. This focused clinical review asks whether true anatomical three-layer endometrium-sparing closure improves clinically meaningful scar outcomes compared with an optimized two-layer endometrium-sparing repair. We classified evidence as direct, near-direct, closely related, or indirect, without pooling biologically non-equivalent techniques. No completed head-to-head trial was identified. The closest randomized evidence evaluates a standardized closure package and suggests improved 6-month scar morphology relative to traditional double-layer closure; it does not test the independent benefit of a third anatomical layer. Component-level findings support precise reporting of endometrial handling, myometrial apposition, locking, bite geometry, tension, and suture material. Maternal and obstetric risk factors must also be considered; nutritional effects on uterine niche formation remain insufficiently established. Current evidence neither identifies a universally superior layer count nor demonstrates prevention of Caesarean scar pregnancy or placenta accreta spectrum by a particular closure strategy. We propose a trial comparing two fully specified, optimized endometrium-sparing packages with equivalent surgeon training and fidelity monitoring, blinded standardized imaging, symptom and reproductive outcomes, and prospective assessment of safety, feasibility, and maternal, operator, and center factors. This framework separates plausible healing mechanisms from demonstrated clinical benefit and defines the comparison needed to determine whether an anatomical third layer adds value.

articles.title: Development of a predictive model for histological chorioamnionitis in patients with preterm premature rupture of membranes: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Zhang J, Wu H, Zheng F et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study is to explore the risk factors for histological chorioamnionitis (HC) and to develop a preliminary clinical prediction model among women with preterm premature rupture of membranes (PPROM) during inpatient expectant management.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study consecutively enrolled women with singleton PPROM at 28 + 0 ∼ 36 + 6 weeks of gestation who delivered at Hangzhou Women's Hospital between December 2022 and October 2025. Clinical and laboratory data recorded from admission to delivery were extracted. Univariate analysis was followed by multivariable logistic regression. Candidate predictors were selected on clinical plausibility and statistical significance. A binary logistic regression model was fitted, and apparent discriminative performance was summarized with a receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve.
RESULTS: A total of 306 women were included (HC group, n = 152; control group, n = 154). In the multivariable model, vaginal examinations (VE), antibiotic beginning time (ABT), reproductive tract pathogens (RTP), white blood cell count (WBC), and C-reactive protein (CRP) remained independently associated with HC. The fitted model was z = 1.874 × ln(VE) + 1.051 × ln(ABT) + 2.378 × ln(WBC) + 0.821 × ln(CRP) + 0.846 × RTP (0 or 1) -11.054. The apparent area under the ROC curve (AUC) was 0.901 (95% confidence interval (CI) [0.864-0.934]); the optimism-corrected AUC after bootstrap internal validation was 0.894, and calibration was adequate (Hosmer-Lemeshow P = 0.409; Brier score 0.128).
CONCLUSIONS: VE, ABT, RTP, WBC, and CRP were identified as independent risk factors for HC in patients with PPROM. The resulting model is a preliminary risk-stratification tool intended for use during inpatient management. It requires external validation in independent populations and an admission-only predictor version before clinical implementation. It is not intended for prediction at the time of admission.

articles.title: Serum testosterone and uric acid: Key biomarkers for predicting response to drospirenone/ethinyl estradiol tablets (II) in adolescents polycystic ovary syndrome.
articles.journal: Therapeutic advances in endocrinology and metabolism
articles.authors: Chen X, Teng Y, He Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adolescent polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) poses diagnostic and management challenges. Although combined oral contraceptives (COCs) can improve symptoms, treatment response varies.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the efficacy of drospirenone/ethinyl estradiol tablets (II) (DRSP/EE (II)) and explore predictors of therapeutic response.
DESIGN: Single-center retrospective study.
METHODS: Adolescents with PCOS and healthy controls were retrospectively included. Among patients treated with DRSP/EE (II), clinical, biochemical, and sex-hormone indices were assessed at baseline and at 3 and 6 months, including total testosterone (TT), sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG), free androgen index (FAI), uric acid (UA), and lipid profile. Binary logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with treatment response, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were used to assess discriminative performance.
RESULTS: The PCOS group had higher androgen levels and lower SHBG than controls. TT and FAI decreased significantly after 3 and 6 months of DRSP/EE (II), while SHBG increased. Triglycerides, total cholesterol, LDL-C, and HDL-C increased. Responders had higher baseline TT (2.03±0.59 vs. 1.55±0.46 nmol/L; FDR P=0.009) and lower UA (314.43±61.33 vs. 372.16±77.16 μmol/L; FDR P=0.023) than non-responders. Multivariable logistic regression showed that TT (OR=6.893; P=0.004) and UA (OR=0.984; P=0.002) were independently associated with treatment response. ROC analyses showed AUCs of 0.716 for TT and 0.713 for UA, while the combined model yielded an AUC of 0.815, with 87.8% sensitivity and 75.0% specificity.
CONCLUSION: DRSP/EE (II) effectively improves hyperandrogenism in adolescent PCOS but may worsen lipid profiles. Baseline TT and UA are promising predictors of clinical response and may facilitate individualized management.

articles.title: National perioperative outcomes of sacrocolpopexy versus colporrhaphy with apical suspension for pelvic organ prolapse: A retrospective cohort study (2008-2021).
articles.authors: Sebai T, Toutounji K, Abdul Khalek J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pelvic organ prolapse (POP) affects up to 40% of women and often requires surgical repair, which can result in unfavorable outcomes.
OBJECTIVES: We compared perioperative outcomes of anteroposterior colporrhaphy with apical suspension versus minimally invasive sacrocolpopexy (SCP), hypothesizing differences in outcomes between the two approaches.
DESIGN: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (ACS-NSQIP) database from 2008 to 2021, including 15,015 women aged 18-89 years.
METHODS: Patients who underwent colporrhaphy with apical suspension (n=6,906) were compared to those who underwent laparoscopic or robotic SCP (n=8,109). We recorded baseline demographics and comorbidities. Primary outcomes included overall complications, infections, urinary tract infections (UTIs), unplanned readmissions, and length of hospital stay. Multivariable logistic regression and 1:1 propensity score matching were used to adjust for confounding factors.
RESULTS: Patients undergoing SCP were younger and healthier at baseline. After adjustment, colporrhaphy was associated with significantly higher odds of any complication (adjusted OR 1.34), minor complications (OR 1.42), infections (OR 1.35), UTIs (OR 1.57), and prolonged hospital stay >2 days (OR 1.49). After propensity score matching, rates of complications remained higher in the colporrhaphy group: Overall complications (8.5% vs. 6.5%), infections (6.7% vs. 5.0%), and UTIs (5.6% vs. 3.6%) (all p<0.001). Severe complications, reoperation, and mortality rates were low and similar between groups.
CONCLUSION: Minimally invasive SCP may be associated with more favorable short-term perioperative outcomes than colporrhaphy with apical suspension, supporting its consideration in appropriately selected patients.

articles.title: NSUN2 siRNA combined with cisplatin promotes ferroptosis and inhibits the proliferation of cervical cancer cells by downregulating GOLPH3 expression.
articles.authors: Zhong J, Hong L, Zhou X et al.
articles.abstract: Cisplatin resistance presents a major obstacle to effective treatment of cervical cancer (CC). Inducing ferroptosis represents a promising strategy to overcome cisplatin resistance. Thus, we aim to investigate the regulatory role of GOLPH3 in ferroptosis and its underlying mechanisms. Gene and protein expression were detected using RT-qPCR and western blot. CCK-8 and colony formation assays were used for cell viability and proliferation measurement. Lipid peroxidation levels were detected using the C11-BODIPY fluorescent probe via flow cytometry, and MDA content was measured by a commercial kit. RIP and MeRIP assays were applied to validate RNA-protein binding and m⁵C modification, respectively. Our results showed that GOLPH3 knockdown enhanced erastin- or cisplatin-induced ferroptosis in CC cells, and GOLPH3 knockdown-induced ferroptosis in cisplatin-treated CC cells was reversed by Fer-1, indicating that GOLPH3 knockdown inhibits cell proliferation via promoting ferroptosis. Besides, GOLPH3 depletion suppressed the AKT/GSK3β/NRF2 pathway, thereby enhancing ferroptosis. Furthermore, NSUN2 mediated m⁵C modification of GOLPH3 mRNA and recruited ALYREF to enhance its stability. NSUN2 knockdown downregulated GOLPH3 expression. Furthermore, NSUN2 knockdown augmented cisplatin-induced growth inhibition of parental and cisplatin-resistant CC cells through enhanced ferroptosis, whereas GOLPH3 overexpression reversed this effect. In conclusion, our findings suggest that NSUN2 may stabilize GOLPH3 mRNA via m⁵C modification in an ALYREF-dependent manner, which may activate the AKT/GSK3β/NRF2 pathway to inhibit ferroptosis and potentially contribute to cisplatin resistance in CC.

articles.title: Reproductive History, Biological Indicators, and Pain Vulnerability in Aging Women: A Multi-Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Zhang W, Wang Z, Wang X et al.
articles.abstract: Chronic pain disproportionately affects women, yet the relationship between female reproductive history and long-term pain vulnerability remains insufficiently understood. Using three population-based cohorts from the UK, China, and the US, we evaluated associations between reproductive factors and pain-related phenotypes in aging women. Endogenous reproductive milestones showed nonlinear associations with pain risk. Specifically, both earlier and later ages at menarche and menopause, as well as shorter and longer reproductive lifespans, were linked to higher pain vulnerability. Childbirth-related characteristics, such as higher parity, earlier age at first birth, and longer interbirth intervals, were also associated with increased pain vulnerability. Reproductive surgeries and exogenous hormone use were consistently associated with pain phenotypes, with timing-dependent effects. In the UK Biobank, reproductive factors showed both shared and site-specific associations across seven chronic pain sites. These reproductive-pain associations were amplified among women with higher adiposity, greater socioeconomic deprivation, a history of depression or anxiety, and hypertension. Exploratory mediation analyses implicated inflammatory, hormonal, and metabolic indicators as potential biological correlates of several reproductive-chronic pain associations. Together, these findings highlight reproductive history as an important life-course factor associated with pain vulnerability and provide insights for future studies investigating mechanisms and risk stratification of chronic pain in women.

articles.title: Matrix Softness and Fluid Shear Force Act Through TRPV4 to Promote Ovarian Cancer Stemness.
articles.authors: Lei Z, Du J, Zhang B et al.
articles.abstract: Matrix stiffness and fluid shear force are key mechanical cues in ovarian cancer microenvironment that can impact cancer stemness, tumorigenicity and metastasis. However, the molecular identity of related mechanosensors is unclear. In the present study, we used 3D soft fibrin gel to enrich ovarian cancer stem cell (OCSC)-like cells. Matrix softness increased the expression of a mechanosensitive Ca2+-permeable TRPV4 channel in these cells. TRPV4 stimulated the cell growth, increased the expression of OCSC markers, and promoted the growth of tumor xenografts in mice. Atomic force microscope measurement of patients' samples and spatial transcriptome analysis demonstrated that softer tumor regions had higher TRPV4 expression. Light-induced photolysis of 3D CarHc hydrogel, which rapidly dissipates the gel stiffness, elicited a TRPV4-mediated Ca2+ transient in the gel-encapsulated cells. Furthermore, TRPV4 activity promoted its own expression via NFAT and AP1, forming a positive feedback loop. Matrix softness also acted through integrin β3 to stimulate TRPV4. In addition, fluid shear force directly stimulated TRPV4, elevated the expression of OCSC markers, and promoted transwell migration in vitro and peritoneal tumor metastasis in vivo. Taken together, we conclude that soft matrix and fluid shear both act though TRPV4 to promote cancer stemness, consequently aggravating ovarian cancer malignancy.

articles.title: Terminal AZF deletions may predict micro-TESE failure in men with sY254/sY255 deletions: a next-generation sequencing study.
articles.authors: Zhang H, Li WN, Zeng SC et al.
articles.abstract: Patients carrying azoospermia factor c (AZFc) deletions present with different phenotypes, ranging from severe oligozoospermia to non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA). We used next-generation sequencing (NGS) to investigate whether cryptic structural variations within the Y chromosome contribute to this phenotypic heterogeneity. We retrospectively analyzed 297 infertile men with sY254 and sY255 deletions, including 224 with severe oligozoospermia and 73 with NOA between January 2023 and January 2025 at the Reproductive and Genetic Hospital of CITIC-Xiangya, Changsha, China. Microdissection testicular sperm extraction (micro-TESE) was performed only in the NOA subgroup, with a successful sperm retrieval rate of 50.7% (37 of 73 men). To delineate the structural complexity of AZFc, NGS was performed on a subset of 76 patients. This approach distinguished canonical b2/b4 deletions from rarer non-canonical rearrangements, including terminal deletions and duplication-containing variants. Compared with the severe oligozoospermia group, the NOA group exhibited significantly smaller testicular volumes and lower estradiol (E2) and inhibin B (INHB) levels. In addition, they exhibited higher follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) and luteinizing hormone (LH) levels. Across the NGS subgroup, b2/b4 deletions were the predominant pattern in all phenotypic groups. Terminal AZF deletions were observed only in sperm-negative NOA patients and were absent in severe oligozoospermia and sperm-positive NOA groups. Routine endocrine markers reflected overall testicular dysfunction but did not discriminate micro-TESE outcomes within the NOA subgroup. In this cohort, terminal AZF deletions were confined to sperm-negative cases. This raises the preliminary, hypothesis-generating possibility that detailed NGS-based structural characterization may provide additional prognostic information beyond standard sequence-tagged site-polymerase chain reaction (STS-PCR). However, given the small sample size and the single-center retrospective design, these findings must be interpreted with caution.

articles.title: Toward a Cross-Pathway Susceptibility Profile for Urinary Tract Infection After Pelvic Floor Reconstruction.
articles.authors: Pop-Lodromanean D, Grigore N, Hașegan A et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Urinary tract infection (UTI) is a frequent early complication after pelvic floor reconstruction. This study examined whether perioperative UTI is associated primarily with the surgical approach or with recurring patient-, disease-, and care-related factors.
METHODS: Medical records were retrospectively reviewed for 376 women treated with pelvic floor reconstructive surgery from 2020 through 2025. According to the principal reconstructive procedure, the cohort was divided into three surgical strata: mesh-based sacrospinous fixation accompanied by transobturator tape (TOT) or tension-free vaginal tape (TVT) insertion; combined anterior and posterior colporrhaphy with a midurethral sling; and anterior and posterior colporrhaphy performed without an associated sling procedure. The study endpoint was a symptomatic urinary tract infection confirmed by urine culture during the initial hospital admission. Associations between candidate predictors and infection were estimated separately within each surgical stratum. Stratum-level effect estimates were then integrated using a DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model to obtain pooled odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals. Cross-stratum variability was quantified through Cochran's Q test and the I2 statistic.
RESULTS: Of the 376 women included, 71 experienced a symptomatic, culture-confirmed infection during the perioperative period, producing an overall event rate of 18.9%. The proportion of affected patients varied numerically among the three reconstructive pathways, although no statistically significant difference was observed in the unadjusted comparison. When risk estimates were synthesized across surgical strata, higher odds of infection were observed in postmenopausal women, patients older than 63 years, those with grade III-IV pelvic organ prolapse, women with morbid obesity, patients requiring bladder catheterization for more than 3 days, and those undergoing hysterectomy during the same…
CONCLUSIONS: Perioperative urinary tract infection after pelvic floor reconstructive surgery appears to reflect a multifactorial susceptibility profile, influenced mainly by patient characteristics, prolapse severity, and prolonged catheterization rather than procedure type alone. These findings support individualized risk assessment and reduced unnecessary catheter use. However, differences in baseline characteristics between surgical groups preclude concluding that the procedures carry equivalent infectious risk.

articles.title: Profiles of emotion regulation difficulties in the transition to menopause: a latent profile analysis.
articles.authors: Brandão T
articles.abstract: The menopausal transition is associated with heightened psychological vulnerability, yet individual differences in emotion regulation (ER) during this period remain poorly understood. This study applied latent profile analysis to identify distinct ER difficulty profiles in women during menopause transition and examined attachment anxiety and avoidance as predictors of profile membership. A sample of 455 women aged 40-60 years at different stages of the menopausal transition (late reproductive, perimenopausal, and postmenopausal) participated in this cross-sectional study. Four profiles were identified: High ER Difficulties (11.2%), Moderate ER Difficulties (48.1%), Emotional Clarity Deficit (11.4%), and Low ER Difficulties (29.2%). Profiles differed significantly on depression, anxiety, stress, menopause-specific somatic and psychological symptoms, and personal burnout (all p < .001, with large effects), with one key exception: the Emotional Clarity Deficit profile did not differ from the Low ER profile on any outcome despite presenting the highest lack of emotional clarity scores in the solution. Attachment anxiety and avoidance both predicted membership in the High and Moderate ER profiles, whereas only attachment avoidance uniquely predicted the Emotional Clarity Deficit profile. These findings provide initial person-centered evidence of ER heterogeneity in the menopausal transition. The Emotional Clarity Deficit profile, which was statistically associated with attachment avoidance, represents a configuration not captured by severity-based approaches; however, its clinical significance and stability remain to be established through replication in independent samples and longitudinal research.

articles.title: Hysteroscopy for Suspected Uterine Malignant Tumor: A Nationwide Survey of Practice Patterns and Oncologic Concerns Among Gynecologic Oncology Institutions in Japan.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.authors: Sakai K, Takashima A, Nagasaka K et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Hysteroscopy for suspected endometrial cancer (EC) remains controversial because of concerns about transtubal tumor cell dissemination. However, its potential utility has been reported for diagnostic evaluation when a definitive diagnosis cannot be established by conventional endometrial sampling and as part of fertility-sparing treatment. In Japan, hysteroscopic surgery for EC and atypical endometrial hyperplasia (AEH) is not yet covered by national health insurance. We investigated current practice and perceptions among gynecologic oncology institutions in Japan.
METHODS: A web-based questionnaire developed by the Japan Society for Hysteroscopy was distributed to members of the Japan Society of Gynecologic Oncology between May and June 2024. It addressed the use of diagnostic, inpatient operative, and office operative hysteroscopy for suspected EC, during fertility-sparing treatment, and for differentiating corpus from cervical origin, together with reasons for reluctance and views on insurance coverage. One response per institution was analyzed.
RESULTS: Responses from 205 institutions were analyzed. For suspected EC, 31.2% of institutions never performed diagnostic hysteroscopy, 49.8% performed it selectively but reluctantly, and 19.0% performed it actively or routinely; the figures for inpatient operative hysteroscopy were similar (37.1%, 43.9%, and 19.0%). The main reason for reluctance was concern about peritoneal dissemination (69.7%). Diagnostic hysteroscopy was used during fertility-sparing treatment by 33.2% of institutions and for differentiating corpus from cervical origin by 13.7%. Overall, 62.4% of institutions desired insurance coverage of hysteroscopic surgery for EC and AEH, rising to 91.5% among those actively using hysteroscopy.
CONCLUSIONS: Hysteroscopy for suspected EC is used cautiously and heterogeneously in Japan, reflecting concern about oncologic safety. Standardized safety protocols, Japanese outcome data, and an appropriate reimbursement framework are needed.

articles.title: Efficacy of SGLT2 Inhibitors With or Without Metformin Compared With Metformin Alone in Women With Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.authors: Mohamed AA, Feteih M, Ahmed ME et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), recently redefined as polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), is a common endocrine disorder of reproductive-age women. Metformin remains first-line therapy, whereas sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors have emerged for their cardiometabolic effects. This study compared SGLT2 inhibitors, alone or with metformin, versus metformin alone in PMOS.
METHODS: We performed a PRISMA-guided systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials from PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane CENTRAL and Embase. Two reviewers independently screened, extracted data, assessed risk of bias (Cochrane RoB 2) and rated certainty using GRADE. Continuous outcomes were pooled as mean differences (MD) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) under a random-effects model; heterogeneity was assessed with I2.
RESULTS: Five trials (292 women) were included. SGLT2 inhibitors did not differ significantly from metformin in body weight (MD = -2.06 kg; 95% CI -5.79 to 1.68) or BMI (MD = -0.34 kg/m2; 95% CI -0.78 to 0.10), or most hormonal, glycemic and anthropometric outcomes. However, they significantly reduced triglycerides (MD = -0.21 mmol/L; 95% CI -0.38 to -0.05) and diastolic blood pressure (MD = -1.79 mmHg; 95% CI -2.57 to -1.01), with a small increase in systolic blood pressure (MD = 0.97 mmHg; 95% CI 0.11-1.83). Certainty of evidence ranged from low to high.
CONCLUSION: SGLT2 inhibitors, alone or with metformin, did not differ significantly from metformin across most metabolic and endocrine outcomes, with modest benefits on triglycerides and diastolic blood pressure. Metformin remains first-line therapy; SGLT2 inhibitors may be considered in selected patients pending larger trials.

articles.title: Use of transvaginal and transabdominal cerclage in the Nordic countries: A survey of incidences and indications.
articles.authors: Hoffmann CH, Hansen LK, Lantto A et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Clinical guidelines for cervical cerclage vary in terms of indications and patient management. In this study, we investigated the incidence, indications, surgical techniques, timing of placement, and peri- and postoperative care for both transvaginal and transabdominal cerclage use in the Nordic countries.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: This study was a cross-sectional survey. An electronic questionnaire was developed and distributed via an electronic data capture system (REDCap) to an obstetrician from all birth units in Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, and Sweden. The primary outcome was the reported incidence of transvaginal cerclage, both history- and ultrasound-indicated, and of transabdominal cerclage.
RESULTS: The estimated incidence per 100 000 births of history-indicated transvaginal cerclage was 231 in DK, 70 in FI, 140 in IS, 133 in NO, and 166 in SE. For ultrasound-indicated transvaginal cerclage, the estimated incidence per 100 000 births was 166 in DK, 21 in FI, 140 in IS, 17 in NO, and 59 in SE. For transabdominal cerclage, the estimated incidence was 63 in DK, 7 in FI, 28 in IS, 31 in NO, and 18 in SE.
CONCLUSIONS: There is substantial variation in the use of cervical cerclage between the Nordic countries. We advocate for a harmonized Nordic model of cerclage care to ensure equitable and consistent practice across countries, coupled with a Nordic research collaboration network that can drive knowledge generation and implementation across the region.

articles.title: Genetic variants in recurrent euploid pregnancy loss.
articles.authors: Aminbeidokhti M, Halstead M, Rodriguez-Escriba M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL) affects ~ 5% of couples. Known causes of RPL include aneuploidies and unbalanced chromosome rearrangements, however the genetic basis of losses with normal karyotype and chromosomal microarray analysis remains unclear. We hypothesized that deleterious variants in genes essential for early development, including genes previously associated only with neonatal lethal disorders, contribute to RPL.
METHODS: Genome sequencing was performed on 118 families with unexplained, euploid RPL; 95% lacked major fetal structural anomalies on ultrasound. A tiered variant prioritization pipeline integrated model organism, human population databases, essential developmental pathways, and fetal transcriptomic profiles. Rare variants (allele frequency ≤ 0.1%) were assessed and confirmed by orthogonal methods. Parental samples were analyzed for mosaicism.
RESULTS: Pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants were identified in 18 families (15.3%) across 17 genes. These include six families with DHCR7, PIEZO1, PIGV, PRF1, SLC12A3, and SMN1 biallelic variants; two cases with ALAS2 and IKBKG hemizygous variants; and four pregnancies with heterozygous alterations inherited from affected parents with MYH3 and TNNI3 variants, and from asymptomatic parents with SCN5A and FLT4 variants. Additionally, four families had presumed de novo heterozygous variants in the EFTUD2, HNRNPK, FGFR2, and KAT6A genes (associated with autosomal dominant conditions), while two exhibited parental germline mosaicism in the FGFR2 and PORCN genes. Variants of uncertain significance were detected in 12 families (10.2%) across the ABCB7, CLPB, CRB2, FBN1, FLT4, GJA1, LYST, MAGED2, PTPN14, RNF213, TLR8, and VPS35L genes. Of 28 genes with plausible variants, 13 genes were previously implicated in perinatal lethality, whereas 15 were novel candidates. Overall, variants in candidate genes were inherited in 80% of families. Four additional families (3.4%) had biallelic ultra-rare variants in genes, which are involved in fundamental developmental pathways but not yet linked to human disease, pointing to a possible role in prenatal…
CONCLUSIONS: Genome sequencing revealed plausible monogenic etiologies for unexplained euploid pregnancy loss, providing new insights into the biology of early human lethality, phenotypic spectra, recurrence risks, and inheritance patterns. These findings support expanding RPL diagnostics beyond karyotyping and chromosomal microarray analysis.

articles.title: The future of maternal mortality measurement: implications of reduced DHS availability.
articles.authors: Ahmed SMA, Cresswell JA, Aujla M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Demographic and Health Surveys (DHS) have historically filled key data gaps in global maternal mortality monitoring. Amid uncertainty regarding funding and their future availability, this study evaluates the potential impact of reduced DHS data availability on United Nations maternal mortality estimates.
METHODS: We conducted a modelling analysis using the UN Maternal Mortality Estimation Inter-Agency Group's BMat model to assess the contribution of DHS data to maternal mortality estimates. We compared three scenarios: [1] exclusion of all DHS data [2], exclusion of DHS conducted since 2015, and [3] a counterfactual with the "status quo" including all eligible data sources. Changes in 2023 maternal mortality ratio (MMR) and uncertainty intervals were evaluated globally, regionally, and nationally.
RESULTS: DHS contributed 21% of all country-year data and were the sole source of data in 23 countries. Excluding all DHS data led to a 15% reduction in the point estimate of the global MMR and a 70% increase in uncertainty. The post-2015 exclusion scenario resulted in a 10% global MMR reduction. These effects were most pronounced in countries and regions lacking alternative data sources (e.g., sub-Saharan Africa and Oceania regions). The exclusion narrowed uncertainty intervals in a few cases, mainly where DHS estimates were less consistent with other national data sources.
CONCLUSIONS: A sustained reduction in the availability of DHS data would substantially affect global maternal mortality estimation, particularly in data-scarce and high-burden settings. The findings highlight the urgent need to strengthen sustainable national data systems, including civil registration and vital statistics and health management information systems.

articles.title: Maternal BMI modulates cord plasma NT-proBNP in gestational diabetes linking cardiac stress to insulin-cortisol crosstalk.
articles.authors: Tocantins C, Rieder A, Strutz J et al.
articles.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is an increasingly prevalent pregnancy disorder associated with adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes, including an increased risk of early-onset cardiovascular disease in infants. GDM is associated with cardiac structural and functional changes as early as in utero. However, pathways linking maternal metabolic status to fetal cardiac stress remain poorly defined. We investigated N-teminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) in umbilical cord plasma (UCP) as a candidate biomarker of fetal cardiac stress, together with additional cardiac, endocrine and endothelial biomarkers to identify novel links between fetal cardiac health and maternal and fetal metabolic, inflammatory and hormonal characteristics. UCP from 82 term pregnancies (57 controls, 25 GDM) was analyzed for NT-proBNP and complementary cardiac, endocrine, and endothelial markers. Associations with maternal metabolic parameters, neonatal outcomes, and other UCP parameters were assessed using correlation, regression, and mediation analyses, adjusted for gestational age and neonatal sex. NT-proBNP levels were elevated in the cord plasma of GDM pregnancies, specifically in the presence of increased maternal pre-pregnancy BMI. Across the cohort, NT-proBNP was further associated with maternal BMI at delivery, fasting glucose levels, placental weight, and neonatal C-peptide, while inversely associated with cord plasma cortisol. Mediation analyses identified a significant indirect association involving neonatal C-peptide and suggested a potential mediating role of NT-proBNP in the association between maternal pre-pregnancy BMI and cord plasma cortisol. These findings suggest that NT-proBNP may reflect fetal cardiac load in GDM and is associated with maternal metabolic status and fetal insulin secretion. The inverse association between NT-proBNP and cortisol raises the possibility of an interplay between natriuretic peptide signaling and glucocorticoid regulation, pointing towards a potential cardiac-endocrine adaptation to intrauterine metabolic stress. While these observations deserve further investigation, they provide new insights into cardiovascular programming.

articles.title: Exploring strategies for accepting and continuing unintended pregnancies in the context of Iran's pro-natalist policies: a qualitative study.
articles.authors: Kohan S, Mokhtari F, Kolahdouzan SA et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Unintended pregnancy is a major reproductive health challenge. Although it often ends in abortion, its consequences can persist for an extended period. On the other hand, continuation of these pregnancies can also have multiple complications for maternal and child health. The cultural, social, and legal context of each country influences both the outcomes and the process of accepting such pregnancies. Therefore, this qualitative study aimed to identify strategies for accepting and continuing unintended pregnancies in Iran, a country characterized by pro-natalist policies and legal-religious restrictions on abortion.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This qualitative study employed a content analysis approach in 2025 in Isfahan, Iran, with participants including women who had experienced unintended pregnancy, their spouses, and health care providers and policymakers. Participants were selected through purposive sampling with maximum variation, and recruitment continued until data saturation was achieved. After obtaining informed consent, data were collected using in-depth, semi-structured individual interviews and field notes. Data analysis was conducted following the conventional content analysis method proposed by Graneheim and Lundman. All interviews were transcribed verbatim, meaningful units were identified and coded, and through constant comparison and categorization, subcategories and main categories were generated.
RESULTS: A total of 17 mothers who had experienced unintended pregnancy, 5 spouses, and 7 healthcare providers, and 4 policymakers participated in this study. Analysis of the interviews generated 2,115 codes,…
CONCLUSION: The findings indicate that promoting maternal and child health among women experiencing unintended pregnancies requires interventions at three levels: family, community, and the health system. At the family level, improving couple relationships, strengthening family foundations, supporting mothers' social roles and activities, and engaging men can create a supportive environment for the continuation of unintended pregnancies. At the community level, revising laws, providing financial support, coordinating non-governmental organizations, and leveraging the potential of online networks are essential to support pregnant women. The health system can also contribute through policymaking to promote planned pregnancies and provide long-term, continuous counseling services for women who have experienced unintended pregnancies.

articles.title: Maternal - fetal outcomes and risk factors of uterine rupture in the setting of pregnant women with scarred versus unscarred uterus: a systematic review and meta - analysis.
articles.authors: Wang Y, Chen Y, Chen M et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare risk factors and outcomes of uterine rupture among patients with a scarred versus an unscarred uterus.
METHODS: In this meta - analysis, we analyzed studies published in PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (ICTRP), and Clinical Trials. gov that appeared in our search from inception to 18/03/2024.
RESULT: This study included a total of 15 studies (1 prospective study and 14 retrospective studies). It comprised 914 cases of patients with scarred uterus and 468 cases of patients with unscarred uterus. Among the 914 scarred uterus cases, 861 (94.2%) were due to prior cesarean section, and the remaining 53 (5.8%) were attributable to other uterine surgeries. The meta - analysis demonstrated that the rates of perinatal mortality, hysterectomy, and postpartum hemorrhage were higher in women with unscarred uterine rupture than in scarred group. Although maternal mortality was also elevated in the unscarred group, the difference did not reach statistical significance. Additionally, compared with scarred uterine rupture, cases of unscarred uterine rupture were more frequently associated with advanced maternal age, oxytocin use, induction of labor, and malpresentation.
CONCLUSION: Compared to patients with scarred uterine rupture, unscarred uterine rupture is associated with significantly higher risks of perinatal mortality, hysterectomy, and postpartum hemorrhage. Additionally, advanced maternal age, a higher incidence of oxytocin, induction of labor, and malpresentation were associated with rupture in the unscarred uterus group. These factors should be taken seriously. Early identification of relevant risk factors is crucial to avoid potential obstetric emergencies, prevent diagnostic delays, and allow timely surgical intervention to improve maternal and neonatal outcomes.

articles.title: Hugo RAS versus da Vinci Xi for robot-assisted simple hysterectomy in endometrial cancer: a concurrent-period comparison of operative efficiency, cost structure, and the cost of early adoption.
articles.authors: Sakamoto I, Nozaki T, Fukada N et al.
articles.abstract: Assessing a newly introduced robotic platform is complicated by calendar-time confounding and early institutional experience. We compared Hugo robotic-assisted surgery (RAS) with da Vinci Xi for robot-assisted simple hysterectomy in endometrial cancer, restricting the primary analysis to their concurrent-use period. This single-centre retrospective cohort comprised 219 patients with clinical stage I disease operated between May 2018 and November 2025; procedures with lymphadenectomy or sentinel lymph node biopsy were excluded to standardise surgical content. The primary concurrent-period analysis included 67 procedures (da Vinci Xi 37, Hugo RAS 30), and cost data were analysable for 61. The adjusted mean difference in total operative time was 16.3 min (95% confidence interval [CI] 6.0-26.6), decreasing to 6.1 min (95% CI - 0.7 to 13.0) in an exploratory analysis excluding the first ten Hugo RAS procedures. Adjusted ratios for recorded consumable and operative costs were 0.808 and 0.923, respectively. These estimates compare early Hugo RAS use with established da Vinci Xi use; the exploratory exclusion cannot isolate learning from platform effects or predict steady-state performance. The findings apply to simple hysterectomy without nodal assessment and do not establish comparative safety, oncologic equivalence, or overall economic superiority.

articles.title: Target trial emulation of effectiveness of COVID-19 mRNA vaccination during pregnancy in four European countries.
articles.authors: Mercadé-Besora N, Raventós B, Trinh NT et al.
articles.abstract: Evidence on real-world effectiveness of COVID-19 vaccination during pregnancy remains limited. Using health data from the UK, Sweden, Spain, and Norway, we emulated two target trials to estimate vaccine effectiveness (VE) of mRNA COVID-19 vaccines administered during pregnancy against COVID-19 infection, hospitalisation, and admission to an Intensive Care Unit (ICU). The first trial compares initiation of a primary (two-dose) vaccination with unvaccinated, and the second compares the receipt of a first booster (third dose) with unboosted after primary vaccination. Pregnant women receiving a first or booster vaccination were matched weekly to comparable unexposed pregnant women. A total of 62,061 and 41,096 pregnant women were included in the first and second trial, respectively. Meta-analysis across the four databases showed a VE for primary vaccination of 26·2% (95% CI 16·2-35·1) against infection and 55·6% (95% CI 44·1-64·8) against hospitalisation. For boosters, the VE was 33.6% (95% CI 1·6-56·6) against infection and 34·1% (95% CI 0·6-56·4) against hospitalisation. ICU admission outcomes were too rare to analyse. In this work, we show that primary and first-booster mRNA vaccination during pregnancy is associated to a lower risk of COVID-19-related hospitalisation, while protection against infection is more modest and heterogeneous across databases.

articles.title: Health worker perspectives on the screening and management of hypertensive disorders and diabetes in pregnancy in Uganda: a cross-sectional survey.
articles.authors: Tibaijuka L, Jacquemyn Y, Lugobe HM et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) and diabetes in pregnancy (DIP) are leading contributors to maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality in sub-Saharan Africa, yet effective management depends on health workers having the knowledge, attitudes, and practices to screen, diagnose, and treat these conditions. Evidence on these provider-level factors remains limited in Uganda.
METHODS: We conducted a descriptive cross-sectional survey among health workers in Uganda (November-December 2025), disseminating a structured questionnaire on HDP and DIP knowledge, attitudes, practices, prescribing, and task shifting via WhatsApp-based Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, Child, and Adolescent Health (RMNCAH) networks and professional association platforms, hosted on REDCap. We analysed data in STATA 17 using descriptive statistics and comparisons across health worker groups.
RESULTS: Of the 690 eligible health workers, 577 completed the survey (83.5%). Midwives comprised the largest group (341, 59.1%) and most worked in public facilities (425, 73.7%). Knowledge and protocol integration were substantially stronger for HDP than DIP: CPD attendance was 70.9% for HDP versus 36.4% for DIP, self-reported protocol familiarity was 90.1% versus 38.6%, and routine BP screening was near-universal (538, 93.2%) while only 122 (21.1%) always screened for diabetes in pregnancy. Correct oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) thresholds were identified by only 186 (32.2%). Attitudes reflected strong support for patient involvement in treatment decisions and consistent treatment targets, with moderate confidence in guideline-based adjustments (279, 48.4%). Prescribing prioritised affordability (438, 75.9%) and reliable drug supply (473, 82.0%). Task shifting was widely accepted for basic functions including BP measurement (538, 93.2%) and lifestyle counselling (514, 89.1%), but less so for algorithm-based prescribing (170, 29.5%). Cadre differences were consistent across domains:…
CONCLUSIONS: Health workers in Uganda demonstrate substantially stronger knowledge, attitudes, and practices for HDP than for DIP, with consistent cadre-related differences. Under-recognition of DIP likely contributes to missed opportunities for timely intervention. Targeted CPD on DIP, wider protocol dissemination, and system-level support for diabetes screening are urgently needed. Leveraging existing RMNCAH networks offers a practical pathway for integrating DIP into routine antenatal care.

articles.title: Fragmentia-AI lymphoma: a cfDNA language model for lymphoma detection using ultra-low-pass WGS.
articles.authors: Dai Y, Zhong X, Bao H et al.
articles.abstract: Lymphomas are biologically and clinically heterogeneous malignancies. While liquid biopsies using circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) offer a non-invasive alternative, current methods typically require expensive deep sequencing. We developed Fragmentia-AI™ Lymphoma, a transformer-based genomic language model that enables lymphoma detection using ultra-low-pass whole-genome sequencing (ULP-WGS). The model integrates a genomic language model backbone with attention-based multiple instance learning to identify mutation-independent, malignancy-associated signals directly from raw cfDNA sequences. The model was trained on 389 samples (189 lymphoma, 200 healthy) and evaluated in an independent validation cohort of 190 lymphoma patients and 200 healthy controls. The model demonstrated robust diagnostic performance in the validation cohort, achieving an AUC of 0.944, with a sensitivity of 0.842 at 98% specificity and an F1 score of 0.904. Read-depth titration analysis showed sustained performance at sequencing depths as low as 0.01x, representing a substantial reduction compared with standard cfDNA mutation-based approaches. Attention-based fragment prioritization indicated that predictions were driven by fragmentomic signatures, including GC-content bias and altered fragment-size distributions characteristic of malignant cfDNA. These findings support the feasibility of a mutation-independent approach that may inform future lymphoma detection and monitoring strategies.

articles.title: KRAS and endometriosis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: The Journal of international medical research
articles.authors: Obadiah AA, Mgbeke O, Adeleye AS et al.
articles.abstract: BackgroundEndometriosis is a chronic gynecological condition affecting approximately 10% of women of reproductive age worldwide. Accumulating molecular evidence suggests that endometriotic lesions harbor somatic oncogenic mutations, including activating mutations in the KRAS gene. However, the prevalence of KRAS mutations across endometriosis subtypes and their clinical significance remain poorly defined.ObjectivesThis systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to estimate the prevalence of somatic KRAS mutations in endometriosis, characterize variant allele frequencies, and evaluate associations with clinical outcomes, including recurrence, infertility, and malignant transformation.MethodsA comprehensive search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Web of Science/Scopus was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 guidelines (International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews: CRD420261303629). Eligible studies included observational designs and molecular sequencing reports on endometriotic tissue. Pooled prevalence was estimated using a random-effects meta-analysis (DerSimonian-Laird model), with heterogeneity assessed using Cochran's Q and I2 statistics.ResultsSeven studies were included, covering deep infiltrating, ovarian, and superficial peritoneal endometriosis subtypes. The pooled KRAS mutation prevalence was 48% (95% confidence interval: 38%-58%), with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 77%). Mutations were most frequent in deep infiltrating and ovarian lesions (50%-55%) compared with that in superficial peritoneal disease (∼30%-35%). Variant allele fractions were consistently low (<20%), reflecting clonal epithelial expansion. KRAS-positive patients demonstrated greater disease extent and surgical complexity, though associations with pain, infertility, and recurrence were not statistically significant.ConclusionPreliminary evidence suggests that KRAS mutations are common in endometriosis; however, findings should be interpreted cautiously owing to substantial study heterogeneity and limited available data. KRAS may hold biological significance as a biomarker; however, current evidence is insufficient to support routine clinical use.

articles.title: Understanding family planning progress in Malawi: a mixed-methods case study.
articles.authors: Alhassan N, Chifungo C, Memon ZA et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Over the last three decades, Malawi has achieved remarkable progress in family planning. Modern contraceptive prevalence rate increased from 7% in 1992 to 66% in 2024. From a country where family planning was banned in the 1960s, Malawi is now one of the best performing countries in contraceptive access and equity in sub-Saharan Africa.
OBJECTIVE: This study examined the drivers of Malawi’s family planning progress from 1992 to 2024. We comprehensively examined policy, programme, financing, community, household, couple and individual-level drivers of Malawi’s accelerated progress in modern contraceptive use and equity.
METHODS: We relied on a mixed-methods case study approach that combined data from a narrative literature review, secondary analysis of Malawi Demographic and Health Surveys, policy and programme review and primary qualitative data. The narrative literature, policy and programme reviews examined the broader policy and socio-economic drivers that accelerated contraceptive use. The quantitative analysis decomposed the contribution of factors responsible for the modern contraceptive prevalence rate change between 2005 and 2016. The qualitative data provided contextual insights from key national stakeholders and community members on key factors influencing contraceptive use. The results from these data sources were integrated and synthesised to provide a comprehensive understanding of the drivers of contraceptive use and equity in Malawi.
RESULTS: The synthesis of results across the different data sources showed four essential drivers of Malawi’s progress in family planning. These were (1) creation of an enabling family planning policy environment through effective formulation and implementation of policies and programmes, (2) effective demand creation interventions that increased knowledge of family planning methods and addressed misinformation, (3) improved supply of contraceptive services via community outreach mechanisms and deployment of trained health workers at the local level and (4) socio-economic progress and increased women’s…
CONCLUSION: The results highlight important lessons and family planning best practices that can be implemented in low-and middle-income countries experiencing slow progress in modern contraceptive use. Malawi’s training and deployment of a lower cadre of health workers to provide injectables can be used to bridge inequalities in contraceptive access in countries with limited health human resources.

articles.title: Lao PDR's achievements in family planning: a mixed-methods study.
articles.authors: Chanthavilay P, Sengchaleun V, Pabouriboune P et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The use of modern contraceptives and family planning (FP) services has increased globally; however, progress varies across countries and regions. The current research aims to examine the key socioecological determinants driving the demand for and utilisation of modern contraceptive methods in the Lao People’s Democratic Republic (Lao PDR), providing insights into the factors that facilitate contraceptive uptake.
METHODOLOGY: We employed a mixed-methods analytical approach including: (1) a systematic literature review to synthesise existing evidence, (2) quantitative analysis of secondary data to identify demographic and behavioural trends, (3) a desk review of relevant policies and programmes to evaluate the policy landscape and (4) community-based qualitative design to explore sociocultural and contextual factors supporting FP uptake.
RESULTS: Modern contraceptive prevalence rate (mCPR) rose steadily from 38.6% in 2005 to 56.3% in 2017, associated with education, household wealth, contraceptive knowledge and age at first sex, alongside marked geographic and ethnic disparities that persisted throughout. Policy analysis identified three programmatic phases: foundation-building (1988–2005), scale-up aligned with the Millennium Development Goals (2005–2015) and an equity-focused phase emphasising adolescent health (2015–present). Qualitative findings revealed five interconnected themes driving FP progress in Lao PDR: political commitment, financing sustainability, health systems strengthening, community-driven demand generation and women’s reproductive agency. While strong policy commitment and expanded service delivery have improved access, donor dependency, geographic barriers for rural and ethnic minority populations and persistent gender-based decision-making constraints continue to limit equitable contraceptive use.
CONCLUSION: Lao PDR’s FP success reflects the simultaneous alignment of political will, financing structures, service delivery and shifting social norms. Sustaining and extending these gains will require a structured domestic financing transition, strengthened commodity supply and workforce systems, expansion of youth-friendly services into rural and ethnic minority areas and continued investment in gender-transformative community engagement to translate increased spousal communication into genuine shared decision-making.

articles.title: How Bolivia became a positive outlier in family planning: an in-depth mixed-methods case study.
articles.authors: Cardona C, Andersen L, Branisa B et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bolivia made remarkable progress in increasing modern contraceptive use among all women of reproductive age, achieving an exponential annual growth rate exceeding 5% between 1989 and 2016—from 8% to 32.4%. Based on a systematic, criteria-based country selection process implemented by the Exemplars in Global Health coalition, Bolivia was identified as a case for in-depth analysis of progress in family planning. In this study, we aimed to identify the socioeconomic, demographic, political, programmatic and health system factors that have contributed to Bolivia’s success in family planning.
METHODS: We employed a mixed-methods analytical approach, incorporating results from: (1) a systematic literature review, (2) quantitative analysis of secondary data, (3) a desk review of policies and programmes and (4) qualitative analysis of primary data. This study summarises the findings from these four analyses.
RESULTS: Bolivia’s progress in family planning outcomes is the result of a multifaceted approach emphasising political commitment, community engagement, health system strengthening and innovative service delivery mechanisms. Key initiatives such as the Universal Maternal and Child Health Insurance and the Revolving Fund for Contraceptives were instrumental in improving the accessibility of family planning services. These efforts ensured a steady supply of contraceptives and reduced financial barriers for marginalised populations particularly in rural and underserved areas.
CONCLUSION: Bolivia’s success in family planning since 1989 has been driven by strong political commitment and policy reforms that created a supportive sexual and reproductive health policy landscape. This, combined with the contributions of non-governmental organisations, has improved access to family planning services. Despite these advancements, service gaps persist for adolescents and marginalised groups, highlighting the need for continued investment in education and healthcare. This study provides valuable insights for enhancing contraceptive use and meeting family planning needs in similar global contexts.

articles.title: Drivers of increased voluntary modern contraceptive use in Kenya: a mixed-methods analysis.
articles.authors: Ontiri S, Oenga D, Chabeda S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: An analysis of 130 countries identified Kenya as one of six nations that significantly increased both its modern contraceptive prevalence rate (mCPR) and family planning (FP) demand satisfied with modern methods between 1994 and 2020. This study aimed to identify the major socio-ecological determinants that contributed to increased use of modern contraceptives in Kenya and to provide an in-depth, contextualised understanding of the specific policies, strategies and programmes implemented by Kenya to achieve this remarkable success.
METHODS: This mixed-methods study combined quantitative analysis of nationally representative datasets, a systematic review of peer-reviewed and grey literature, policy, programme and financial analysis of government and donor initiatives, and qualitative research including key informant interviews and focus group discussions. Data were analysed thematically and triangulated across sources to identify drivers of FP progress, assess trends in mCPR and method mix, and contextualise findings.
RESULTS: Findings revealed that Kenya surpassed its 2020 modern contraceptive rate target of 58%, more than doubled the use of modern contraception (from 27% in 1993 to 61% in 2020), and significantly reduced the unmet need for modern FP (from 36% in 1993 to 14% in 2020). Five major themes emerged as the key drivers of Kenya’s performance: (1) strong political commitment, (2) supportive donor and domestic financing, (3) incremental expansions in service delivery and infrastructure, (4) community engagement programmes and (5) increased women’s empowerment.
CONCLUSION: Lessons learnt from Kenya’s progress on FP may inform policy and programme decisions in other low- and middle-income countries.

articles.title: A synthesis of six countries' successes in increasing modern contraceptive uptake at scale: a mixed-methods study.
articles.authors: St-Onge Ahmad S, Memon ZA, Samuel K et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Data on facilitators to increase family planning (FP) services uptake in low- and middle-income countries is limited. This paper synthesises cross-cutting findings from six country mixed-methods case studies identified within the FP Exemplars FP project. We aimed to derive broader insights from analyses of policies, quantitative trends and contextual factors from 1994 to 2020 in Bolivia, Lao People’s Democratic Republic (PDR), Kenya, Malawi, Senegal and Sierra Leone.
METHODS: Drawing on the results, we compare drivers of change in modern contraceptive prevalence rate (mCPR); use the Oaxaca-Blinder decomposition and risk factor analysis to measure relative contributions of knowledge of individual FP methods to mCPR growth; map key developments occurring during and 5 years preceding maximum mCPR growth intervals (MGIs) and examine the association between official development assistance (ODA) and mCPR using Spearman’s rank correlation.
RESULTS: Compound mCPR annual change rates were 1.12% for Bolivia, 3.20% for Lao PDR, 3.98% for Kenya, 5.32% for Senegal, 5.44% for Malawi and 10.76% for Sierra Leone. Top drivers of mCPR increase were mean modern methods known of FP (MMK) and education. In Lao PDR, MMK was associated with mCPR in 2005 and 2012. Knowledge of implants was the strongest mCPR growth driver in Kenya, Malawi, Senegal and Sierra Leone. The MGI in Bolivia was 1998–2003, Kenya 2010–2015, Malawi 2009–2014, Senegal 2012–2017, Sierra Leone 2008–2013 and Lao PDR 1995–2000. During these time periods, we found that creation of laws, policies and programmes and international commitments played a role in all case countries, while product introduction, supply chain management, service integration, mass media, community-level initiatives, donor/domestic financing and institutional/structural changes played a role in some and mixed evidence for the role of ODA in mCPR growth.
CONCLUSION: Donor funding is important but insufficient for mCPR growth; country-level commitments through legislation, structural changes and targeted programming are key to achieving FP progress.

articles.title: PREGNANCY OUTCOMES IN A CONTEMPORARY COHORT OF WOMEN WITH REPAIRED TETRALOGY OF FALLOT.
articles.authors: Franch MJA, Pijuan-Domenech A, Ródenas-Alesina E et al.
articles.abstract: Most women with repaired Tetralogy of Fallot (rTOF) now reach reproductive age, but pregnancy outcomes in contemporary cohorts, particularly after pulmonary valve replacement (PVR), remain uncertain. The aim of this study as to assess maternal cardiac, obstetric and neonatal outcomes in a contemporary cohort of women with rTOF. We retrospectively included all pregnancies in women with rTOF followed at a tertiary referral center for complex congenital heart disease (CHD) and high-risk pregnancy between 2013 and 2024. A total of 44 pregnancies in 32 women with rTOF were included, resulting in 45 live births. Severe PR was present in 43% of pregnancies, and 40% had undergone prior PVR. Maternal cardiac events occurred in 6.8%: 2 cases of supraventricular arrhythmias and 1 case of thrombosis on an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) lead. Among women with prior PVR, transvalvular gradients increased transiently during pregnancy and returned to baseline postpartum. Mean gestational age was 38 weeks, vaginal birth was preferred and cesarean section was performed in 18% of pregnancies. The most frequent adverse obstetric and neonatal outcomes were low birth weight (22%) and preterm birth (11%), both associated with lower pre-pregnancy right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF) possibly reflecting impaired uteroplacental perfusion related to right ventricular dysfunction. In conclusion, in this contemporary cohort, pregnancy in women with rTOF was associated with low risk of maternal cardiac events, mainly supraventricular arrhythmias. However, low birth weight and preterm birth remained frequent and were associated with lower pre-pregnancy RVEF, underscoring the importance of specialized cardio-obstetric follow-up.

articles.title: Cutaneous Manifestations of the Menopausal Transition - Part 1: Epidemiology, Biology, Diagnosis and Workup.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology
articles.authors: Kim U, Gangal A, Li Y et al.
articles.abstract: Menopause represents a physiologic transition characterized by the cessation of ovarian follicular estrogen synthesis and subsequent alterations in the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis, with broad systemic and cutaneous consequences. This review (Part 1) provides a comprehensive overview of the epidemiology, pathogenesis, diagnosis, and clinical evaluation of dermatologic manifestations associated with perimenopause and menopause. We summarize key hormonal changes, including declining estrogen and dynamic androgen shifts, and their downstream effects on skin structure and function through nuclear and membrane-associated estrogen receptor signaling pathways. The impact of estrogen deficiency across major cutaneous compartments-including the epidermis, dermis, hair follicle unit, sebaceous glands, vasculature, pigmentary system, and immune milieu-is examined, with emphasis on mechanisms underlying xerosis, impaired barrier function, dermal atrophy, alopecia, vasomotor instability, dyschromia, delayed wound healing, and vulvovaginal dermatoses. Dermatology-specific examination findings, limited utility of routine hormonal testing, and specific laboratory workup in patients with atypical or rapid-onset cutaneous hyperandrogenism are covered. This review equips clinicians with a mechanistic understanding of menopause-associated skin changes to support accurate diagnosis, appropriate workup, and informed management.

articles.title: The challenge of Adenomyosis across the ART journey: insights from the Naples Workshop group.
articles.authors: Cozzolino M, Di Spiezio Sardo A, Exacoustos C et al.
articles.abstract: Adenomyosis is increasingly recognized in women of reproductive age and may adversely affect fertility, assisted reproductive technology (ART) outcomes, and pregnancy. However, its optimal management in women seeking pregnancy remains uncertain, with substantial heterogeneity in diagnostic criteria, disease phenotypes, and available therapeutic evidence. This narrative review, informed by the multidisciplinary discussion of the Naples Workshop on Adenomyosis and ART (10th-12th October 2025), critically examines the available evidence on adenomyosis throughout the ART journey. Available evidence is critically synthesized, with multidisciplinary clinical perspectives incorporated where appropriate, to identify practical clinical considerations, areas of uncertainty, and priorities for future research. The review is structured into three sections according to the phase of adenomyosis management during the ART timeline: (i) before ART, including diagnosis, ovarian reserve assessment and potential pre-treatment; (ii) during ART, including embryo transfer strategies; (iii) after ART, addressing pregnancy-related risks, antenatal surveillance, delivery, and postpartum management. This expert narrative review integrates available evidence with multidisciplinary clinical expertise to provide practical considerations for patient management while identifying areas of uncertainty and priorities for future research. Overall, management should be individualized according to disease phenotype, symptoms, reproductive potential, previous ART history, and coexisting conditions, while several commonly proposed interventions still require confirmation in well-designed prospective studies.

articles.title: Effects of letrozole on oocyte-associated ultrastructure and follicular gene expression in a mouse model of polycystic ovary syndrome.
articles.journal: The international journal of biochemistry & cell biology
articles.authors: Khourmehr H, Ghasemian F, Gharabadian S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) impairs follicular development and ovarian function. This study investigated the effects of letrozole on follicular development, gene expression, and oocyte-associated ultrastructure in an estradiol valerate (EV)-induced mouse model of PCOS.
METHODS: Thirty female NMRI mice were assigned to control (n = 5) and EV-treated (40 mg/kg, intramuscularly; n = 25) groups. After 60 days, five PCOS mice were used for model validation; the remaining mice were allocated to untreated PCOS and letrozole groups (0.5, 1.0, or 1.5 mg/kg; n = 5/group) treated for five days. Serum testosterone, estradiol, LH, and FSH were measured in control and PCOS mice. Histology, RT-qPCR (Gdf9, Bcl2, and Bax), and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) were performed.
RESULTS: Compared with controls, PCOS mice had higher testosterone, estradiol, and LH levels (2.1-, 2.2-, and 1.8-fold, respectively; p < 0.05), while FSH was unchanged. At letrozole (1.5 mg/kg) group, letrozole increased Gdf9 and Bcl2 and decreased Bax expression versus untreated PCOS mice (p < 0.0001). TEM, conducted only in untreated PCOS and letrozole (1.5 mg/kg) groups, showed that the mitochondrial matrix-to-total area ratio increased from 60% to 90% (p < 0.001), while mean zona pellucida thickness decreased from 0.56 ± 0.16-0.47 ± 0.05 μm (p < 0.05). TEM revealed differences in mitochondrial morphology, smooth endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus, zona pellucida, and vesicular bodies between the two groups.
CONCLUSION: Letrozole was associated with changes in follicular development, gene expression, and oocyte-associated ultrastructure. Functional oocyte competence and dose-dependent ultrastructural effects remain unestablished.

articles.title: Genetic Diagnoses and Postnatal Outcomes in a Prenatal Cohort of Arthrogryposis Multiplex Congenita.
articles.authors: Haizler-Cohen L, O'Brien D, Field E et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Describe genetic diagnoses and characterize postnatal outcomes in a prenatal cohort of arthrogryposis multiplex congenita (AMC) evaluated at a quaternary fetal center.
METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of pregnancies referred between 2014 and 2026 for contractures involving ≥ 2 body areas. We categorized cases into three groups using the Hall classification. Demographics, prenatal imaging, genetic results, autopsy findings, and postnatal outcomes were collected.
RESULTS: Ninety-four pregnancies were included: 15 with isolated arthrogryposis, 32 with arthrogryposis and systemic anomalies excluding the central nervous system (CNS), and 47 with arthrogryposis and CNS involvement or fetal akinesia deformation sequence (FADS). Genetic findings in our cohort included 18 aneuploidies, 3 copy number variants and 25 single gene disorders. Of pregnancies with non-diagnostic cytogenetic findings that underwent next-generation sequencing (NGS), 50% (24/48) had a molecular diagnosis. Neonates with FADS had notably poor outcomes, including high mortality (86%, 6/7) and failed intubation (50%, 3/6) rates. Of neonates with isolated arthrogryposis, 77% (10/13) survived but frequently required respiratory or feeding support, orthopedic surgery, ambulation assistance and had neurodevelopmental delays.
CONCLUSIONS: AMC is genetically heterogeneous with frequent underlying single gene disorders, supporting the use of NGS in prenatal diagnosis. Neonatal morbidity and mortality remain high, particularly with FADS.

articles.title: Symptom, not solution: Digital contraceptives, structural ambivalence, and the cracks in contraceptive care.
articles.authors: Klim C
articles.abstract: Digital contraceptive technologies are increasingly promoted as solutions to persistent problems in contraceptive care, including user dissatisfaction and limited pharmaceutical innovation. Drawing on qualitative workshops with contraceptive users in Australia, this article interrogates this solutionist framing by exploring how digital contraceptives are understood and evaluated in relation to everyday experiences of contraceptive care. Although participants recognised certain benefits, they frequently described these technologies as inadequate or disappointing solutions. Rather than treating their responses as matters of individual preference or technical failure, I show how dissatisfaction with digital contraceptives reflects broader structural critiques of contraceptive care. What appear as 'emergent frictions' in the form of cost, usability, security, and design are, in fact, symptomatic of 'embedded fractures', including gendered responsibility, fragmented educational infrastructures, the commodification of care, and political precarity. By reframing participants' ambivalence as a response to structural conditions rather than to discrete technologies, the article re-situates digital contraception within the broader landscape of contraceptive care and challenges solutionist approaches to future improvements.
